#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Per-column categorical analyses for envoy-analyze
##
## Analyses: top values, category dominance, group summaries, Cramer's V.
##
## Reads:  input_file delim COL_COUNT COL_NAMES COL_TYPE COL_UNIQUE
##         NUM_COL_INDEXES NUM_COL_NAMES CAT_COL_INDEXES CAT_COL_NAMES
##         MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE MAX_GROUPS MAX_GROUP_NUM_COLS
##         AWK_ISMISSING
## Writes: ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

run_categorical_analyses () {
    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}" != "categorical" ]]; then
            continue
        fi

        local col_name="${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}"

        # Single-pass: compute unique count, top 5 values, dominance, and entropy
        local cat_combined
        cat_combined=$(awk -F"$delim" -v col="$i" "$AWK_ISMISSING"'
            function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
            NR>1{
                v=trim($col)
                if(ismissing(v)) next
                total++
                count[v]++
            }
            END{
                if(total==0){print "0|0|0|0.0000|"; exit}
                # Find unique count, top value, and entropy in one loop
                uniq=0; top=0; topval=""; ent=0
                for(k in count){
                    uniq++
                    if(count[k]>top){top=count[k]; topval=k}
                    p=count[k]/total
                    if(p>0) ent -= p*log(p)/log(2)
                }
                printf "%d|%d|%d|%.4f|%s\n", total, uniq, top, ent, topval
                # Sort values by count descending for top-5 (shell sort in awk)
                n=0
                for(k in count){n++; vals[n]=k; cnts[n]=count[k]}
                # Simple selection of top 5
                for(t=1; t<=5 && t<=n; t++){
                    best=t
                    for(j=t+1; j<=n; j++){
                        if(cnts[j]>cnts[best]) best=j
                    }
                    if(best!=t){
                        tmp=vals[t]; vals[t]=vals[best]; vals[best]=tmp
                        tmp=cnts[t]; cnts[t]=cnts[best]; cnts[best]=tmp
                    }
                    printf "%d %s\n", cnts[t], vals[t]
                }
            }
        ' "$input_file")

        # Parse first line: stats
        local cat_stats_line
        cat_stats_line=$(head -n 1 <<< "$cat_combined")
        local cat_total unique_count cat_top cat_entropy cat_topval
        IFS='|' read -r cat_total unique_count cat_top cat_entropy cat_topval <<< "$cat_stats_line"

        COL_UNIQUE[$((i-1))]="$unique_count"

        if [[ -n "$cat_total" && "$cat_total" -gt 0 ]]; then
            local top_share
            local _ts100=$(( cat_top * 10000 / cat_total ))
            top_share="$(( _ts100 / 100 )).$(printf '%02d' $(( _ts100 % 100 )))"
            add_item "Category dominance: $col_name" "Top share: ${top_share}% (value: ${cat_topval})
Entropy (bits): ${cat_entropy}" "ADVANCED" "dominance"
        fi

        # Parse remaining lines: top values
        local top_lines
        top_lines=$(tail -n +2 <<< "$cat_combined")
        local top_body="Unique values: $unique_count"$'\n'"Top values:"$'\n'
        if [[ -n "$top_lines" ]]; then
            local count value
            while read -r count value; do
                top_body+="  $value: $count"$'\n'
            done <<< "$top_lines"
        else
            top_body+="  (none)"$'\n'
        fi
        add_item "Top values: $col_name" "${top_body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "top_values"
    done
}

run_group_summaries () {
    if [[ ${#NUM_COL_INDEXES[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        return
    fi
    # ENV-126: skip per-group awks when group_summary kind is filtered out.
    _will_keep_kind group_summary || return 0

    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}" != "categorical" ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        local unique_count="${COL_UNIQUE[$((i-1))]}"
        if [[ -z "$unique_count" || "$unique_count" -eq 0 || "$unique_count" -gt "$MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE" ]]; then
            if [[ -n "$unique_count" && "$unique_count" -gt "$MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE" ]]; then
                echo "Warning: column '${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}' has $unique_count unique values, exceeding MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE=$MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE; skipping group summary" >&2
            fi
            continue
        fi

        local num_cols=()
        local num_names=()
        local n
        if [[ ${#NUM_COL_INDEXES[@]} -gt "$MAX_GROUP_NUM_COLS" ]]; then
            echo "Warning: ${#NUM_COL_INDEXES[@]} numeric columns available but group summary limited to MAX_GROUP_NUM_COLS=$MAX_GROUP_NUM_COLS for column '${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}'" >&2
        fi
        for ((n=0; n<${#NUM_COL_INDEXES[@]} && n<MAX_GROUP_NUM_COLS; n++)); do
            num_cols+=("${NUM_COL_INDEXES[$n]}")
            num_names+=("${NUM_COL_NAMES[$n]}")
        done

        if [[ ${#num_cols[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
            continue
        fi

        local num_cols_list num_names_list
        num_cols_list=$(IFS=,; echo "${num_cols[*]}")
        num_names_list=$(IFS='|'; echo "${num_names[*]}")

        local group_lines
        group_lines=$(awk -F"$delim" -v cat_col="$i" -v num_cols="$num_cols_list" -v num_names="$num_names_list" "$AWK_ISMISSING"'
            function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
            function isnum(x){ return (x ~ /^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$/) }
            BEGIN{ split(num_cols, cols, ","); split(num_names, names, "|") }
            NR>1 {
                cat=trim($cat_col)
                if (ismissing(cat)) next
                count[cat]++
                for (i=1;i<=length(cols);i++) {
                    c=cols[i]
                    v=trim($(c))
                    if (isnum(v)) {
                        sum[cat,i]+=v
                        n[cat,i]++
                    }
                }
            }
            END{
                for (c in count) {
                    printf "%s|%d", c, count[c]
                    for (i=1;i<=length(cols);i++) {
                        if (n[c,i]>0) printf "|%.4f", (sum[c,i]/n[c,i])
                        else printf "|"
                    }
                    print ""
                }
            }
        ' "$input_file" | sort -t'|' -k2,2nr)

        local total_groups
        total_groups=$(printf "%s\n" "$group_lines" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        if [[ "$total_groups" -gt "$MAX_GROUPS" ]]; then
            echo "Warning: column '${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}' has $total_groups groups but only showing top MAX_GROUPS=$MAX_GROUPS" >&2
            group_lines=$(printf "%s\n" "$group_lines" | head -n "$MAX_GROUPS")
        fi

        if [[ -n "$group_lines" ]]; then
            local body="" group count rest
            while IFS='|' read -r group count rest; do
                body+="$group (n=$count): "
                local -a means
                IFS='|' read -r -a means <<< "$rest"
                local m val label
                for ((m=0; m<${#num_names[@]}; m++)); do
                    val="${means[$m]:-}"
                    label="${num_names[$m]}"
                    if [[ -n "$val" ]]; then
                        body+="$label=$val"
                    else
                        body+="$label=n/a"
                    fi
                    if (( m < ${#num_names[@]}-1 )); then
                        body+="; "
                    fi
                done
                body+=$'\n'
            done <<< "$group_lines"

            add_item "Group summary: ${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}" "${body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "group_summary"
        fi
    done
}

run_cramers_v () {
    # ENV-126: skip the NAjc2b2Aj categorical-pair awk when cramers_v isn't kept.
    _will_keep_kind cramers_v || return 0
    CAT_COL_INDEXES=()
    CAT_COL_NAMES=()
    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}" == "categorical" ]]; then
            local uq="${COL_UNIQUE[$((i-1))]}"
            if [[ -n "$uq" && "$uq" -gt 1 && "$uq" -le "$MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE" ]]; then
                CAT_COL_INDEXES+=("$i")
                CAT_COL_NAMES+=("${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}")
            elif [[ -n "$uq" && "$uq" -gt "$MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE" ]]; then
                echo "Warning: column '${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}' has $uq unique values, exceeding MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE=$MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE; excluded from Cramer's V" >&2
            fi
        fi
    done

    if [[ ${#CAT_COL_INDEXES[@]} -lt 2 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    local cramer_body=""
    local cramer_found=0
    local ci cj
    for ((ci=0; ci<${#CAT_COL_INDEXES[@]}-1 && ci<4; ci++)); do
        for ((cj=ci+1; cj<${#CAT_COL_INDEXES[@]} && cj<5; cj++)); do
            local cramer_v
            cramer_v=$(awk -F"$delim" -v c1="${CAT_COL_INDEXES[$ci]}" -v c2="${CAT_COL_INDEXES[$cj]}" "$AWK_ISMISSING"'
                function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
                NR>1{
                    v1=trim($c1); v2=trim($c2)
                    if(ismissing(v1)) next
                    if(ismissing(v2)) next
                    n++
                    joint[v1,v2]++
                    row_total[v1]++
                    col_total[v2]++
                    if(!seen_r[v1]){seen_r[v1]=1; nr++}
                    if(!seen_c[v2]){seen_c[v2]=1; nc++}
                }
                END{
                    if(n==0||nr<2||nc<2){print "NA"; exit}
                    chi2=0; low_exp=0; total_cells=0
                    for(key in joint){
                        split(key, parts, SUBSEP)
                        r=parts[1]; c=parts[2]
                        obs=joint[key]
                        exv=row_total[r]*col_total[c]/n
                        total_cells++
                        if(exv<5) low_exp++
                        if(exv>0) chi2+=(obs-exv)*(obs-exv)/exv
                    }
                    k=(nr<nc? nr : nc)
                    v=sqrt(chi2/(n*(k-1)))
                    if(total_cells>0 && low_exp > total_cells*0.2)
                        printf "%.6f|WARNING", v
                    else
                        printf "%.6f", v
                }
            ' "$input_file")
            # Strip warning flag for display
            local cramer_warn=""
            if [[ "$cramer_v" == *"|WARNING" ]]; then
                cramer_warn=" (warning: >20% expected frequencies <5)"
                cramer_v="${cramer_v%%|*}"
            fi
            if [[ "$cramer_v" != "NA" ]]; then
                local strength=""
                if float_cmp "$cramer_v" ">=" "0.3"; then
                    strength="strong"
                elif float_cmp "$cramer_v" ">=" "0.15"; then
                    strength="moderate"
                else
                    strength="weak"
                fi
                if float_cmp "$cramer_v" ">=" "0.15"; then
                    cramer_body+="${CAT_COL_NAMES[$ci]} vs ${CAT_COL_NAMES[$cj]}: V=$cramer_v ($strength association)${cramer_warn}"$'\n'
                    cramer_found=1
                fi
            fi
        done
    done
    if [[ $cramer_found -eq 1 ]]; then
        add_item "Categorical associations (Cramer's V)" "${cramer_body%$'\n'}" "ADVANCED" "cramers_v"
    fi
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_compare.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=f50e1c2d04abccda29eead823d5dedd9e018df90eefbcee222dc3521cdd76898===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Cross-dataset comparison for envoy-analyze
##
## Compares summary statistics across multiple CSV/TSV files, producing
## side-by-side tables and rankings.
##
## Reads:  compare_files forced_delim AWK_ISMISSING
## Writes: cleanup_files
##         ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

# Extract per-column stats from a single file.
# Output: tab-separated lines:  col_name \t mean \t std \t min \t max \t median \t cv
_compare_extract_stats () {
    local file="$1"
    local file_delim="$2"

    awk -F"$file_delim" "$AWK_ISMISSING"'
    function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
    function isnum(x){ return (x ~ /^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$/) }
    NR==1{
        for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) col[i]=trim($i)
        ncols=NF
        next
    }
    {
        for(i=1;i<=ncols;i++){
            v=trim($i)
            if(ismissing(v)) continue
            if(!isnum(v)) { text[i]++; total[i]++; continue }
            total[i]++
            num[i]++
            vn=v+0
            # Welford online
            delta=vn-wm[i]
            n1=num[i]
            delta_n=delta/n1
            wm2[i]+=delta*delta_n*(n1-1)
            wm[i]+=delta_n
            if(n1==1||vn<mn[i]) mn[i]=vn
            if(n1==1||vn>mx[i]) mx[i]=vn
            # Store values for median (up to 50K)
            if(num[i]<=50000) { vals[i,num[i]]=vn }
        }
    }
    END{
        for(i=1;i<=ncols;i++){
            n=num[i]+0; t=total[i]+0
            if(t>0 && n/t < 0.80) continue  # skip non-numeric columns
            if(n==0) continue
            mean=wm[i]
            m2=wm2[i]/n; if(m2<0) m2=0
            std=sqrt(m2)
            cv=(mean!=0? (std/(mean<0?-mean:mean))*100 : 0)
            # Compute median via insertion sort on stored values
            # Simple selection for median
            mid=int((n+1)/2)
            # Shell sort the values
            h=1; while(h<n) h=3*h+1
            while(h>1){
                h=int(h/3)
                for(j=h+1;j<=n;j++){
                    tmp=vals[i,j]; k=j
                    while(k>h && vals[i,k-h]>tmp){
                        vals[i,k]=vals[i,k-h]; k-=h
                    }
                    vals[i,k]=tmp
                }
            }
            if(n%2==1) median=vals[i,mid]
            else median=(vals[i,mid]+vals[i,mid+1])/2
            printf "%s\t%.6f\t%.6f\t%g\t%g\t%.6f\t%.2f\n", col[i], mean, std, mn[i], mx[i], median, cv
        }
    }
    ' "$file"
}

# Main entry point for cross-dataset comparison.
# Called from envoy-analyze when --compare is active.
run_cross_dataset_comparison () {
    local nfiles=${#compare_files[@]}
    if [[ $nfiles -lt 2 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    # Extract stats from each file
    # _CMP_DATA[fileindex] = multiline output from _compare_extract_stats
    local -a _CMP_DATA=()
    local -a _CMP_LABELS=()
    local fi_idx

    for ((fi_idx=0; fi_idx<nfiles; fi_idx++)); do
        local cfile="${compare_files[$fi_idx]}"
        [[ -f "$cfile" ]] || err "Compare file not found: $cfile"

        # Detect delimiter for this file
        local cdelim
        if [[ -n "$forced_delim" ]]; then
            cdelim="$forced_delim"
        else
            cdelim="$(detect_delim "$cfile")"
        fi

        # BOM strip
        strip_bom "$cfile"
        local cfile_clean="$_STRIP_BOM_RESULT"

        # CSV preprocess if needed
        if needs_csv_preprocess "$cfile_clean"; then
            local ctmp
            ctmp="$(mktemp -t mda-cmp-tsv.XXXXXX)"
            cleanup_files+=("$ctmp")
            csv_to_tsv "$cfile_clean" "$cdelim" > "$ctmp"
            cfile_clean="$ctmp"
            cdelim=$'\t'
        fi

        _CMP_DATA[$fi_idx]="$(_compare_extract_stats "$cfile_clean" "$cdelim")"
        # Label = basename without extension
        local label
        label="$(basename "$cfile")"
        label="${label%.*}"
        _CMP_LABELS[$fi_idx]="$label"
    done

    # Collect all column names that appear in ALL files
    local -A col_in_files
    local -a all_cols=()
    for ((fi_idx=0; fi_idx<nfiles; fi_idx++)); do
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r cname _rest; do
            [[ -z "$cname" ]] && continue
            col_in_files["$cname"]=$(( ${col_in_files["$cname"]:-0} + 1 ))
        done <<< "${_CMP_DATA[$fi_idx]}"
    done
    for cname in "${!col_in_files[@]}"; do
        if [[ "${col_in_files[$cname]}" -eq "$nfiles" ]]; then
            all_cols+=("$cname")
        fi
    done

    if [[ ${#all_cols[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        add_item "Cross-dataset comparison" "No shared numeric columns found across datasets." "DIAGNOSTIC" "compare"
        return
    fi

    # Build comparison table for each shared column
    local col
    for col in "${all_cols[@]}"; do
        local table_body=""
        # Header row
        local header="Dataset"
        header+=$'\t'"Mean"$'\t'"Std"$'\t'"Min"$'\t'"Max"$'\t'"Median"$'\t'"CV%"
        table_body+="$header"$'\n'

        local -a means=()
        local -a labels_for_rank=()
        for ((fi_idx=0; fi_idx<nfiles; fi_idx++)); do
            local row
            # NB: no early `exit` in awk. Under `set -euo pipefail`, an awk that
            # exits before consuming all of `echo`'s output can leave `echo` with
            # SIGPIPE (141); pipefail then propagates that and `set -e` aborts the
            # whole comparison Aje28094Aj a timing-dependent failure that flaked on Alpine.
            # Column names are unique in the stats payload, so match the first row
            # without closing the pipe early.
            row=$(echo "${_CMP_DATA[$fi_idx]}" | awk -F'\t' -v c="$col" '$1==c && !seen{print; seen=1}')
            if [[ -z "$row" ]]; then continue; fi
            local rmean rstd rmin rmax rmedian rcv
            IFS=$'\t' read -r _ rmean rstd rmin rmax rmedian rcv <<< "$row"
            table_body+="${_CMP_LABELS[$fi_idx]}"$'\t'"$rmean"$'\t'"$rstd"$'\t'"$rmin"$'\t'"$rmax"$'\t'"$rmedian"$'\t'"$rcv"$'\n'
            means+=("$rmean")
            labels_for_rank+=("${_CMP_LABELS[$fi_idx]}")
        done

        add_item "Cross-dataset comparison: $col" "${table_body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "compare"

        # Ranking by mean (ascending = lowest wins)
        if [[ ${#means[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
            local rank_body=""
            # Build sortable pairs
            local rank_lines=""
            for ((ri=0; ri<${#means[@]}; ri++)); do
                rank_lines+="${means[$ri]}"$'\t'"${labels_for_rank[$ri]}"$'\n'
            done
            local rank_num=0
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r rmean rlabel; do
                [[ -z "$rlabel" ]] && continue
                rank_num=$((rank_num + 1))
                rank_body+="#${rank_num} ${rlabel} (mean: ${rmean})"$'\n'
            done <<< "$(printf "%s" "$rank_lines" | sort -g)"

            add_item "Dataset ranking: $col" "Ranked by mean (ascending):
${rank_body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "compare_rank"
        fi
    done

    # Overall comparison summary
    local summary_body
    summary_body="Compared ${nfiles} datasets across ${#all_cols[@]} shared numeric column(s).
Datasets: $(printf "%s, " "${_CMP_LABELS[@]}" | sed 's/, $//')
Columns compared: $(printf "%s, " "${all_cols[@]}" | sed 's/, $//')"

    add_item "Comparison summary" "$summary_body" "GOOD" "compare_summary"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_correlation.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=c217b37ee259819b98aab1fcc073de3944fa7b40543aa162044653eba1aaf5e2===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Cross-column correlation analyses for envoy-analyze
##
## Analyses: correlation matrix, strongest pairs, linear regression,
## pairwise completeness, outlier co-occurrence, column correlation strength.
##
## Reads:  input_file delim NUM_COL_INDEXES NUM_COL_NAMES
##         COL_MEAN COL_STD MAX_CORR_COLS
##         AWK_ISMISSING
## Writes: CORR_VALUES corr_cols corr_names _CORR_PAIR_LINES
##         ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

run_correlation_analyses () {
    local corr_numeric_count=${#NUM_COL_INDEXES[@]}
    # ENV-125: _correlation_dimension_summary's footer needs to know how
    # many columns existed before the MAX_CORR_COLS cap so it can report
    # any drops alongside the summed count.
    local corr_numeric_count_full=$corr_numeric_count
    corr_cols=()
    corr_names=()
    CORR_VALUES=()

    if [[ "$corr_numeric_count" -lt 2 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    # ENV-126: skip the whole correlation pipeline (matrix + pairs +
    # regression + pairwise + outlier-cooccurrence + dimension summary)
    # when none of its kinds are kept. The matrix awk is the costliest
    # single computation in envoy-analyze for wide datasets, so this is
    # the biggest filter-skip win available.
    #
    # Dependency: `run_suggested_drops` (kind=drop_suggest) reads the
    # CORR_VALUES globals to suggest dropping high-correlation columns.
    # If that kind is kept we still need the matrix even if no
    # correlation-kind output is requested.
    if ! _will_keep_kind corr_matrix \
       && ! _will_keep_kind corr_pairs \
       && ! _will_keep_kind regression \
       && ! _will_keep_kind pairwise_complete \
       && ! _will_keep_kind outlier_cooccur \
       && ! _will_keep_kind corr_strength \
       && ! _will_keep_kind drop_suggest; then
        return
    fi

    if [[ "$corr_numeric_count" -gt "$MAX_CORR_COLS" ]]; then
        echo "Warning: $corr_numeric_count numeric columns found but correlation matrix limited to MAX_CORR_COLS=$MAX_CORR_COLS; columns $((MAX_CORR_COLS+1))-${corr_numeric_count} dropped" >&2
    fi

    local i j
    for ((i=0; i<corr_numeric_count && i<MAX_CORR_COLS; i++)); do
        corr_cols+=("${NUM_COL_INDEXES[$i]}")
        corr_names+=("${NUM_COL_NAMES[$i]}")
    done

    _correlation_matrix
    _correlation_strongest_pairs
    _correlation_regression
    _correlation_pairwise_completeness
    _correlation_outlier_cooccurrence
    _correlation_dimension_summary
}

_correlation_matrix () {
    local i j idx nc=${#corr_cols[@]}

    CORR_VALUES=()

    # Build comma-separated column index list for awk
    local cols_csv=""
    for ((i=0; i<nc; i++)); do
        cols_csv+="${corr_cols[$i]},"
    done

    # Single-pass: compute pairwise-correct correlations
    # Uses per-pair sums instead of pre-computed means/stds, so missing
    # values in one pair don't affect other pairs' statistics.
    local corr_raw
    corr_raw=$(awk -F"$delim" -v cols_csv="$cols_csv" -v nc="$nc" '
        function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
        function isnum(x){ return (x ~ /^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$/) }
        BEGIN{ split(cols_csv, cols, ",") }
        NR==1{next}
        {
            for(i=1; i<=nc; i++){
                v[i]=trim($cols[i])
                ok[i]=isnum(v[i])
            }
            for(i=1; i<=nc; i++){
                if(!ok[i]) continue
                vi=v[i]+0
                for(j=i+1; j<=nc; j++){
                    if(!ok[j]) continue
                    vj=v[j]+0
                    pn[i,j]++
                    sx[i,j]+=vi; sy[i,j]+=vj
                    sxx[i,j]+=vi*vi; syy[i,j]+=vj*vj
                    sxy[i,j]+=vi*vj
                }
            }
        }
        END{
            for(i=1; i<=nc; i++){
                for(j=i+1; j<=nc; j++){
                    nn=pn[i,j]+0
                    if(nn<2){printf "NA\n"; continue}
                    mx=sx[i,j]/nn; my=sy[i,j]/nn
                    vx=sxx[i,j]/nn - mx*mx
                    vy=syy[i,j]/nn - my*my
                    cov=sxy[i,j]/nn - mx*my
                    if(vx>0 && vy>0){
                        r=cov/sqrt(vx*vy)
                        if(r>1) r=1; if(r<-1) r=-1
                        printf "%.4f\n", r
                    } else {
                        printf "NA\n"
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    ' "$input_file")

    # Fill CORR_VALUES from the single-pass output
    # Read all lines into an array first to avoid per-pair process spawns
    local -a _corr_lines=()
    while IFS= read -r _cl; do
        _corr_lines+=("$_cl")
    done <<< "$corr_raw"

    local pair_idx=0
    local r
    for ((i=0; i<nc; i++)); do
        for ((j=0; j<nc; j++)); do
            idx=$((i*nc+j))
            if (( i == j )); then
                CORR_VALUES[$idx]="1.0000"
            elif (( j < i )); then
                local sym=$((j*nc+i))
                CORR_VALUES[$idx]="${CORR_VALUES[$sym]}"
            else
                CORR_VALUES[$idx]="${_corr_lines[$pair_idx]}"
                pair_idx=$((pair_idx+1))
            fi
        done
    done

    # Build matrix display
    local matrix=" "$'\t'
    local name
    for name in "${corr_names[@]}"; do
        matrix+="$name"$'\t'
    done
    matrix=${matrix%$'\t'}
    matrix+=$'\n'

    for ((i=0; i<${#corr_cols[@]}; i++)); do
        local line="${corr_names[$i]}"
        for ((j=0; j<${#corr_cols[@]}; j++)); do
            idx=$((i*${#corr_cols[@]}+j))
            line+=$'\t'"${CORR_VALUES[$idx]}"
        done
        matrix+="$line"$'\n'
    done

    local matrix_body
    matrix_body=$(printf "%s" "$matrix" | column -t -s$'\t' 2>/dev/null || printf "%s" "$matrix")
    local corr_numeric_count=${#NUM_COL_INDEXES[@]}
    if [[ "$corr_numeric_count" -gt "$MAX_CORR_COLS" ]]; then
        matrix_body+=$'\n'"(Note: showing first $MAX_CORR_COLS numeric columns)"
    fi

    add_item "Correlation matrix" "${matrix_body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "corr_matrix"
}

_correlation_strongest_pairs () {
    local i j idx r abs
    local pair_lines=""

    for ((i=0; i<${#corr_cols[@]}; i++)); do
        for ((j=i+1; j<${#corr_cols[@]}; j++)); do
            idx=$((i*${#corr_cols[@]}+j))
            r="${CORR_VALUES[$idx]}"
            if [[ "$r" == "NA" ]]; then
                continue
            fi
            abs="${r#-}"
            pair_lines+="$abs"$'\t'"$r"$'\t'"${corr_names[$i]}"$'\t'"${corr_names[$j]}"$'\n'
        done
    done

    # Store for reuse by regression
    _CORR_PAIR_LINES="$pair_lines"

    if [[ -n "$pair_lines" ]]; then
        local top_pairs
        top_pairs=$(printf "%s" "$pair_lines" | sort -nr | awk 'NR<=5')
        local pairs_body=""
        local abs r a b
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r abs r a b; do
            pairs_body+="$a vs $b: r=$r"$'\n'
        done <<< "$top_pairs"
        add_item "Strongest correlations" "${pairs_body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "corr_pairs"
    fi
}

_correlation_regression () {
    local pair_lines="$_CORR_PAIR_LINES"
    if [[ -z "$pair_lines" ]]; then
        return
    fi

    local reg_body=""
    local reg_count=0
    local abs r col_a col_b
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r abs r col_a col_b; do
        if [[ "$r" == "NA" ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        if ! float_cmp "$abs" ">=" "0.5"; then
            continue
        fi
        local idx_a="" idx_b="" ci
        for ((ci=0; ci<${#corr_names[@]}; ci++)); do
            if [[ "${corr_names[$ci]}" == "$col_a" ]]; then
                idx_a="${corr_cols[$ci]}"
            fi
            if [[ "${corr_names[$ci]}" == "$col_b" ]]; then
                idx_b="${corr_cols[$ci]}"
            fi
        done
        if [[ -z "$idx_a" || -z "$idx_b" ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        local mean_a="${COL_MEAN[$((idx_a-1))]}"
        local mean_b="${COL_MEAN[$((idx_b-1))]}"
        local std_a="${COL_STD[$((idx_a-1))]}"
        local std_b="${COL_STD[$((idx_b-1))]}"
        if [[ -n "$std_a" ]] && float_cmp "$std_a" ">" "0"; then
            local slope intercept r2
            slope=$(awk -v r="$r" -v sy="$std_b" -v sx="$std_a" 'BEGIN{printf "%.6f", r*(sy/sx)}')
            intercept=$(awk -v my="$mean_b" -v sl="$slope" -v mx="$mean_a" 'BEGIN{printf "%.4f", my - sl*mx}')
            r2=$(awk -v r="$r" 'BEGIN{printf "%.4f", r*r}')
            reg_body+="$col_b = ${slope} * $col_a + ${intercept}  (r=$r, RAjc2b2Aj=$r2)"$'\n'
            reg_count=$((reg_count+1))
            if [[ $reg_count -ge 5 ]]; then
                break
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$(printf "%s" "$pair_lines" | sort -nr | awk 'NR<=5')"
    if [[ -n "$reg_body" ]]; then
        add_item "Linear regression (top pairs)" "${reg_body%$'\n'}" "ADVANCED" "regression"
    fi
}

_correlation_pairwise_completeness () {
    local nc=${#corr_cols[@]}
    if [[ $nc -lt 2 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    # Limit to first 6 columns
    local limit=$((nc < 6 ? nc : 6))

    # Build comma-separated column index list
    local cols_csv=""
    for ((i=0; i<limit; i++)); do
        cols_csv+="${corr_cols[$i]},"
    done

    # Single-pass: compute pairwise completeness for all pairs
    local pcomp_raw
    pcomp_raw=$(awk -F"$delim" -v cols_csv="$cols_csv" -v nc="$limit" "$AWK_ISMISSING"'
        function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
        BEGIN{ split(cols_csv, cols, ",") }
        NR==1{next}
        {
            total++
            for(i=1; i<=nc; i++) miss[i]=ismissing(trim($cols[i]))
            for(i=1; i<nc; i++){
                for(j=i+1; j<=nc; j++){
                    if(miss[i] || miss[j]) inc[i,j]++
                }
            }
        }
        END{
            for(i=1; i<nc; i++){
                for(j=i+1; j<=nc; j++){
                    if(total==0) printf "100.00\n"
                    else printf "%.2f\n", (total-inc[i,j]+0)/total*100
                }
            }
        }
    ' "$input_file")

    local paircomp_body=""
    local paircomp_found=0
    local pair_idx=0
    local ci cj
    for ((ci=0; ci<limit-1; ci++)); do
        for ((cj=ci+1; cj<limit; cj++)); do
            pair_idx=$((pair_idx+1))
            local pcomp
            pcomp=$(sed -n "${pair_idx}p" <<< "$pcomp_raw")
            if float_cmp "$pcomp" "<" "100"; then
                paircomp_body+="${corr_names[$ci]} vs ${corr_names[$cj]}: ${pcomp}% complete"$'\n'
                paircomp_found=1
            fi
        done
    done
    if [[ $paircomp_found -eq 1 ]]; then
        add_item "Pairwise completeness" "${paircomp_body%$'\n'}" "ADVANCED" "pairwise_complete"
    fi
}

_correlation_outlier_cooccurrence () {
    local nc=${#corr_cols[@]}
    if [[ $nc -lt 2 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    # Limit: ci<4, cj<5
    local limit_i=$((nc-1 < 4 ? nc-1 : 4))
    local limit_j=$((nc < 5 ? nc : 5))

    # Collect valid pairs and their Q1/Q3 boundaries
    local pairs_csv="" pair_names_i=() pair_names_j=()
    local pair_count=0
    local ci cj
    for ((ci=0; ci<limit_i; ci++)); do
        for ((cj=ci+1; cj<limit_j; cj++)); do
            local col_ci="${corr_cols[$ci]}"
            local col_cj="${corr_cols[$cj]}"
            local q1_a="${COL_Q1[$((col_ci-1))]:-}"
            local q3_a="${COL_Q3[$((col_ci-1))]:-}"
            local q1_b="${COL_Q1[$((col_cj-1))]:-}"
            local q3_b="${COL_Q3[$((col_cj-1))]:-}"
            if [[ -z "$q1_a" || "$q1_a" == "n/a" || -z "$q1_b" || "$q1_b" == "n/a" ]]; then
                continue
            fi
            pairs_csv+="${col_ci},${col_cj},${q1_a},${q3_a},${q1_b},${q3_b};"
            pair_names_i+=("${corr_names[$ci]}")
            pair_names_j+=("${corr_names[$cj]}")
            pair_count=$((pair_count+1))
        done
    done

    if [[ $pair_count -eq 0 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    # Single-pass: compute outlier co-occurrence for all pairs
    local cooccur_raw
    cooccur_raw=$(awk -F"$delim" -v pairs_csv="$pairs_csv" -v npairs="$pair_count" '
        function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
        function isnum(x){ return (x ~ /^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$/) }
        BEGIN{
            split(pairs_csv, pairs, ";")
            for(p=1; p<=npairs; p++){
                split(pairs[p], pp, ",")
                pc1[p]=pp[1]; pc2[p]=pp[2]
                q1a[p]=pp[3]; q3a[p]=pp[4]; q1b[p]=pp[5]; q3b[p]=pp[6]
                iqr1[p]=q3a[p]-q1a[p]; lo1[p]=q1a[p]-1.5*iqr1[p]; hi1[p]=q3a[p]+1.5*iqr1[p]
                iqr2[p]=q3b[p]-q1b[p]; lo2[p]=q1b[p]-1.5*iqr2[p]; hi2[p]=q3b[p]+1.5*iqr2[p]
            }
        }
        NR>1{
            for(p=1; p<=npairs; p++){
                v1=trim($pc1[p]); v2=trim($pc2[p])
                o1=(isnum(v1) && (v1+0<lo1[p] || v1+0>hi1[p]))
                o2=(isnum(v2) && (v2+0<lo2[p] || v2+0>hi2[p]))
                if(o1) out1[p]++
                if(o2) out2[p]++
                if(o1 && o2) both[p]++
            }
        }
        END{
            for(p=1; p<=npairs; p++){
                printf "%d|%d|%d\n", out1[p]+0, out2[p]+0, both[p]+0
            }
        }
    ' "$input_file")

    local cooccur_body=""
    local cooccur_found=0
    local p=0
    while IFS='|' read -r o1 o2 oboth; do
        if [[ "$oboth" -gt 0 ]]; then
            cooccur_body+="${pair_names_i[$p]} vs ${pair_names_j[$p]}: $oboth rows where both are outliers (${o1} in ${pair_names_i[$p]}, ${o2} in ${pair_names_j[$p]})"$'\n'
            cooccur_found=1
        fi
        p=$((p+1))
    done <<< "$cooccur_raw"
    if [[ $cooccur_found -eq 1 ]]; then
        add_item "Outlier co-occurrence" "${cooccur_body%$'\n'}" "ADVANCED" "outlier_cooccur"
    fi
}

_correlation_dimension_summary () {
    if [[ ${#corr_cols[@]} -lt 3 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    # ENV-125: this is a "how connected is each column to the rest"
    # heuristic, not a dimensional decomposition. Output framing was
    # softened in v0.6 ("Correlation dimension summary" / "Rank N:")
    # but still implied a dimension count it could not deliver. Path A
    # rewrites the body to use neutral `<col>: connectedness=<v>`
    # entries sorted descending, and drops the dimension framing.
    local strength_body
    strength_body=$(awk -v ncols="${#corr_cols[@]}" -v corr_vals="$(printf "%s," "${CORR_VALUES[@]}")" -v col_names="$(IFS='|'; echo "${corr_names[*]}")" '
        BEGIN{
            split(corr_vals, cv, ",")
            split(col_names, names, "|")
            n=ncols
            for(i=0;i<n;i++){
                colsum=0
                for(j=0;j<n;j++){
                    if(i==j) continue
                    idx=i*n+j+1
                    r=cv[idx]+0
                    if(r<0) r=-r
                    colsum+=r
                }
                strength[i]=colsum
            }
            for(i=0;i<n;i++) order[i]=i
            for(i=0;i<n-1;i++) for(j=i+1;j<n;j++){
                if(strength[order[i]]<strength[order[j]]){
                    t=order[i]; order[i]=order[j]; order[j]=t
                }
            }
            print "Sum of |r| with other numeric columns; higher = more linearly related to the rest. Not a PCA / variance-explained metric."
            for(i=0;i<n;i++){
                idx=order[i]
                printf "%s: connectedness=%.3f\n", names[idx+1], strength[idx]
            }
        }
    ')

    # Footer: how many columns were actually summed and how many were
    # dropped by the MAX_CORR_COLS cap (the cap is announced upstream
    # in run_correlation_analyses but the summed count belongs here).
    local n_summed=${#corr_cols[@]}
    local footer="---"$'\n'"Summed across $n_summed numeric column(s)."
    if [[ "${corr_numeric_count_full:-0}" -gt "$n_summed" ]]; then
        local dropped=$(( corr_numeric_count_full - n_summed ))
        footer+=" $dropped further numeric column(s) dropped by MAX_CORR_COLS=$MAX_CORR_COLS."
    fi

    add_item "Column correlation strength" "$strength_body"$'\n'"$footer" "ADVANCED" "corr_strength"
}

===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_csv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=0309a3153474cd370144ee93e7e1e07d0cd0d7ca7b6160af4d89c41c8badb46e===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## CSV preprocessing for envoy-analyze
##
## Provides RFC 4180-compliant CSV-to-TSV conversion. Handles:
##   - Quoted fields with embedded delimiters
##   - Escaped quotes ("" inside quoted fields)
##   - Embedded newlines inside quoted fields (replaced with literal \n)
##   - UTF-8 BOM stripping
##
## The preprocessor runs once before analysis, producing a clean TSV file
## where no field contains a tab. All downstream AWK blocks continue to
## work unchanged with -F"\t".
##
## Reads:  (function arguments only)
## Writes: _STRIP_BOM_RESULT
################################################################################

# Strip UTF-8 BOM if present (EF BB BF).
# Works on a temp copy so the original file is never modified.
# Sets _STRIP_BOM_RESULT to the working file path (temp copy if BOM was
# found, or the original path if no BOM was present).
strip_bom () {
    local file="$1"
    local first3
    first3=$(head -c 3 "$file" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    if [[ "$first3" == "efbbbf" ]]; then
        local tmp
        tmp=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mda-bom.XXXXXX")
        cleanup_files+=("$tmp")
        tail -c +4 "$file" > "$tmp"
        _STRIP_BOM_RESULT="$tmp"
    else
        _STRIP_BOM_RESULT="$file"
    fi
}

# Fast check: does the file contain any double-quote characters?
# If not, no RFC 4180 preprocessing is needed.
needs_csv_preprocess () {
    local file="$1"
    grep -q '"' "$file"
}

# Convert CSV (with quoting) to clean TSV.
# Args: input_file delimiter
# Output: TSV to stdout
csv_to_tsv () {
    local file="$1"
    local delim="$2"
    awk -v delim="$delim" '
    BEGIN {
        OFS = "\t"
        state = 0   # 0=start-of-field, 1=in-quoted, 2=in-unquoted
        field = ""
        ncols = 0
        row = 0
    }
    {
        line = $0
        len = length(line)
        i = 1
        while (i <= len) {
            ch = substr(line, i, 1)
            if (state == 0) {
                # Start of a new field
                if (ch == "\"") {
                    state = 1
                    field = ""
                    i++
                } else if (ch == delim) {
                    # Empty unquoted field
                    fields[++ncols] = field
                    field = ""
                    i++
                } else {
                    state = 2
                    field = ch
                    i++
                }
            } else if (state == 1) {
                # Inside a quoted field
                if (ch == "\"") {
                    # Check for escaped quote ""
                    if (i < len && substr(line, i+1, 1) == "\"") {
                        field = field "\""
                        i += 2
                    } else {
                        # End of quoted field
                        state = 0
                        fields[++ncols] = field
                        field = ""
                        i++
                        # Skip the delimiter after the closing quote
                        if (i <= len && substr(line, i, 1) == delim) {
                            i++
                            state = 0
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    field = field ch
                    i++
                }
            } else if (state == 2) {
                # Inside an unquoted field
                if (ch == delim) {
                    fields[++ncols] = field
                    field = ""
                    state = 0
                    i++
                } else {
                    field = field ch
                    i++
                }
            }
        }
        # End of physical line
        if (state == 1) {
            # Still inside a quoted field Aje28094Aj embedded newline
            field = field "\\n"
        } else {
            # End of record
            if (state == 2 || state == 0) {
                fields[++ncols] = field
            }
            # Emit the record as TSV (replace any tabs in field values with spaces)
            row++
            for (f = 1; f <= ncols; f++) {
                gsub(/\t/, " ", fields[f])
                if (f > 1) printf "\t"
                printf "%s", fields[f]
            }
            printf "\n"
            # Reset for next record
            ncols = 0
            field = ""
            state = 0
            delete fields
        }
    }
    END {
        # Handle last record if file does not end with newline
        if (ncols > 0 || field != "") {
            fields[++ncols] = field
            for (f = 1; f <= ncols; f++) {
                gsub(/\t/, " ", fields[f])
                if (f > 1) printf "\t"
                printf "%s", fields[f]
            }
            printf "\n"
        }
    }
    ' "$file"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_format.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=e6ee123a498d2874f981aea5602f90b47c3f6176dda194d4f9b764c0023db721===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Output formatting for envoy-analyze
##
## Renders analysis items in plain, JSON, CSV, or TSV format.
##
## Reads:  ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS output_format
##         COLOR_ENABLED VERSION
## Writes: (none Aje28094Aj pure output)
################################################################################

# ENV-065: isolated helper Aje28094Aj only call when COLOR_ENABLED=1 and format=plain.
_colorize_tag () {
    local tag="$1"
    local c=""
    case "$tag" in
        GOOD)       c='\033[32m' ;;  # green
        ADVANCED)   c='\033[36m' ;;  # cyan
        DIAGNOSTIC) c='\033[33m' ;;  # yellow
        NOISY)      c='\033[90m' ;;  # bright black (grey)
        *)          printf '%s' "$tag"; return ;;
    esac
    printf '%b%s\033[0m' "$c" "$tag"
}

format_output () {
    local -a selected=("$@")
    local item_count=${#ITEM_TITLES[@]}

    case "$output_format" in
        plain)
            for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
                if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                    echo "Skipping invalid selection: $id" >&2
                    continue
                fi
                if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then
                    echo "Skipping out-of-range selection: $id" >&2
                    continue
                fi
                local idx=$((id-1))
                local title="${ITEM_TITLES[$idx]}"
                local body="${ITEM_BODIES[$idx]}"
                local tag="${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}"

                local tag_display="$tag"
                if [[ "${COLOR_ENABLED:-0}" -eq 1 ]]; then
                    tag_display="$(_colorize_tag "$tag")"
                fi
                printf "%d. [%s] %s\n" "$id" "$tag_display" "$title"
                if [[ -n "$body" ]]; then
                    printf "%s\n" "$body" | sed 's/^/   /'
                fi
                printf "\n"
            done
            ;;
        json)
            # ENV-064: stable envelope. schema_version is additive-evolution
            # only Aje28094Aj new optional fields can be added without a bump; removing
            # or retyping fields bumps to 2.0. See docs/json-schema.md.
            printf '{"schema_version":"1.0","envoy_analyze_version":"%s","items":[' "${VERSION:-unknown}"
            local first=1
            for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
                if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                    continue
                fi
                if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then
                    continue
                fi
                local idx=$((id-1))
                local title body tag kind
                title=$(json_escape "${ITEM_TITLES[$idx]}")
                body=$(json_escape "${ITEM_BODIES[$idx]}")
                tag=$(json_escape "${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}")
                kind=$(json_escape "${ITEM_KINDS[$idx]:-generic}")
                if [[ $first -eq 0 ]]; then
                    printf ","
                fi
                printf '{"id":%d,"tag":"%s","kind":"%s","title":"%s","body":"%s"}' "$id" "$tag" "$kind" "$title" "$body"
                first=0
            done
            printf ']}\n'
            ;;
        csv)
            printf "id,tag,title,body\n"
            for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
                if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                    continue
                fi
                if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then
                    continue
                fi
                local idx=$((id-1))
                printf "%s,%s,%s,%s\n" "$id" "$(escape_csv "${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}")" "$(escape_csv "${ITEM_TITLES[$idx]}")" "$(escape_csv "${ITEM_BODIES[$idx]}")"
            done
            ;;
        tsv)
            printf "id\ttag\ttitle\tbody\n"
            for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
                if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                    continue
                fi
                if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then
                    continue
                fi
                local idx=$((id-1))
                printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n" "$id" "$(escape_tsv "${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}")" "$(escape_tsv "${ITEM_TITLES[$idx]}")" "$(escape_tsv "${ITEM_BODIES[$idx]}")"
            done
            ;;
        markdown)
            for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
                if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                    echo "Skipping invalid selection: $id" >&2
                    continue
                fi
                if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then
                    echo "Skipping out-of-range selection: $id" >&2
                    continue
                fi
                local idx=$((id-1))
                local title="${ITEM_TITLES[$idx]}"
                local body="${ITEM_BODIES[$idx]}"
                local tag="${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}"

                printf "## %d. [%s] %s\n\n" "$id" "$tag" "$title"
                if [[ -n "$body" ]]; then
                    # Check if body looks tabular (contains tab-separated lines)
                    if [[ "${body%%$'\n'*}" == *$'\t'* ]]; then
                        # Render as markdown table
                        local first_line=1
                        while IFS= read -r line; do
                            local md_line
                            md_line="| $(echo "$line" | sed 's/\t/ | /g') |"
                            printf "%s\n" "$md_line"
                            if [[ $first_line -eq 1 ]]; then
                                local col_count
                                col_count=$(echo "$line" | awk -F'\t' '{print NF}')
                                local sep="|"
                                local c
                                for ((c=0; c<col_count; c++)); do
                                    sep+=" --- |"
                                done
                                printf "%s\n" "$sep"
                                first_line=0
                            fi
                        done <<< "$body"
                    else
                        printf "%s\n" "$body"
                    fi
                fi
                printf "\n"
            done
            ;;
        html)
            _format_html_output "${selected[@]}"
            ;;
        *)
            err "Unknown output format: $output_format"
            ;;
    esac
}

html_escape () {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s//&/&amp;}"
    s="${s//</&lt;}"
    s="${s//>/&gt;}"
    s="${s//\"/&quot;}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

# Generate an inline SVG sparkline bar chart from a body that contains
# numeric distribution data (histogram-style lines like "  [0.0, 5.0)  Aje29688e29688e29688e29688Aj 12").
# Falls back gracefully if no histogram data found.
_html_sparkline_svg () {
    local body="$1"
    local vals=()
    local max_val=0
    # Extract histogram bucket counts from lines like "Bin N (range): COUNT ####"
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        local count=""
        # Match "): COUNT #" pattern from histogram bins
        count=$(echo "$line" | sed -n 's/.*): *\([0-9][0-9]*\) *#.*/\1/p' || true)
        if [[ -n "$count" && "$count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            vals+=("$count")
            if (( count > max_val )); then
                max_val=$count
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$body"

    if [[ ${#vals[@]} -eq 0 || $max_val -eq 0 ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    local svg_w=$(( ${#vals[@]} * 8 ))
    if (( svg_w < 40 )); then svg_w=40; fi
    if (( svg_w > 200 )); then svg_w=200; fi
    local svg_h=50
    local bar_w=$(( svg_w / ${#vals[@]} ))
    if (( bar_w < 4 )); then bar_w=4; fi

    printf '<svg width="%d" height="%d" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="vertical-align:middle">' "$svg_w" "$svg_h"
    local i
    for ((i=0; i<${#vals[@]}; i++)); do
        local v="${vals[$i]}"
        local bar_h=$(( v * (svg_h - 2) / max_val ))
        if (( bar_h < 1 && v > 0 )); then bar_h=1; fi
        local x=$(( i * bar_w ))
        local y=$(( svg_h - bar_h ))
        printf '<rect x="%d" y="%d" width="%d" height="%d" fill="#4a90d9" rx="1"/>' "$x" "$y" "$((bar_w - 1))" "$bar_h"
    done
    printf '</svg>'
    return 0
}

_format_html_output () {
    local -a selected=("$@")
    local item_count=${#ITEM_TITLES[@]}
    local title_text="EnvoyAnalyze Report"

    # HTML document header
    cat <<'HTMLHEAD'
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<title>EnvoyAnalyze Report</title>
<style>
  * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
  body {
    font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    background: #f8f9fa; color: #212529; line-height: 1.5; padding: 2rem;
    max-width: 960px; margin: 0 auto;
  }
  h1 { font-size: 1.6rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; color: #1a1a2e; }
  h2 { font-size: 1.15rem; margin: 1.5rem 0 0.5rem; color: #2c3e50; border-bottom: 1px solid #dee2e6; padding-bottom: 0.25rem; }
  .tag { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 0.1rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 3px; margin-right: 0.5rem; vertical-align: middle; }
  .tag-GOOD { background: #d4edda; color: #155724; }
  .tag-ADVANCED { background: #d1ecf1; color: #0c5460; }
  .tag-DIAGNOSTIC { background: #fff3cd; color: #856404; }
  .tag-NOISY { background: #e2e3e5; color: #6c757d; }
  .item { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #dee2e6; border-radius: 6px; padding: 1rem 1.2rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; }
  .item-header { font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }
  .item-body { white-space: pre-wrap; font-family: "SFMono-Regular", Consolas, "Liberation Mono", Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; color: #495057; }
  table.data { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; margin: 0.5rem 0; font-size: 0.85rem; }
  table.data th, table.data td { border: 1px solid #dee2e6; padding: 0.3rem 0.6rem; text-align: left; }
  table.data th { background: #e9ecef; font-weight: 600; }
  .anomaly { color: #dc3545; font-weight: 600; }
  .correlation-strong { color: #28a745; font-weight: 600; }
  .sparkline { margin: 0.25rem 0; }
  .summary-stats { background: #e9ecef; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem; }
  .footer { margin-top: 2rem; padding-top: 1rem; border-top: 1px solid #dee2e6; color: #6c757d; font-size: 0.8rem; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
HTMLHEAD

    printf '<h1>EnvoyAnalyze Report</h1>\n'

    # Summary statistics section
    local total_items=${#selected[@]}
    local good_count=0
    local advanced_count=0
    local noisy_count=0
    local diag_count=0
    for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
        if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then continue; fi
        if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then continue; fi
        local idx=$((id-1))
        case "${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}" in
            GOOD) good_count=$((good_count+1)) ;;
            ADVANCED) advanced_count=$((advanced_count+1)) ;;
            NOISY) noisy_count=$((noisy_count+1)) ;;
            DIAGNOSTIC) diag_count=$((diag_count+1)) ;;
        esac
    done

    printf '<div class="summary-stats">\n'
    printf '<strong>Summary:</strong> %d items' "$total_items"
    if (( good_count > 0 )); then printf ' &mdash; <span class="tag tag-GOOD">GOOD: %d</span>' "$good_count"; fi
    if (( advanced_count > 0 )); then printf ' <span class="tag tag-ADVANCED">ADVANCED: %d</span>' "$advanced_count"; fi
    if (( noisy_count > 0 )); then printf ' <span class="tag tag-NOISY">NOISY: %d</span>' "$noisy_count"; fi
    if (( diag_count > 0 )); then printf ' <span class="tag tag-DIAGNOSTIC">DIAGNOSTIC: %d</span>' "$diag_count"; fi
    printf '\n</div>\n'

    # Each analysis item
    for id in "${selected[@]}"; do
        if ! [[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then continue; fi
        if (( id < 1 || id > item_count )); then continue; fi
        local idx=$((id-1))
        local title="${ITEM_TITLES[$idx]}"
        local body="${ITEM_BODIES[$idx]}"
        local tag="${ITEM_TAGS[$idx]}"
        local kind="${ITEM_KINDS[$idx]}"

        local escaped_title
        escaped_title=$(html_escape "$title")

        printf '<div class="item">\n'
        printf '<h2><span class="tag tag-%s">%s</span> %d. %s</h2>\n' "$tag" "$tag" "$id" "$escaped_title"

        if [[ -n "$body" ]]; then
            # Check if body is tabular (tab-separated)
            if [[ "${body%%$'\n'*}" == *$'\t'* ]]; then
                printf '<table class="data">\n'
                local first_line=1
                while IFS= read -r line; do
                    if [[ $first_line -eq 1 ]]; then
                        printf '<tr>'
                        while IFS=$'\t' read -r cell; do
                            local ecell
                            ecell=$(html_escape "$cell")
                            printf '<th>%s</th>' "$ecell"
                        done <<< "$(echo "$line" | tr '\t' '\n')"
                        printf '</tr>\n'
                        first_line=0
                    else
                        printf '<tr>'
                        while IFS=$'\t' read -r cell; do
                            local ecell
                            ecell=$(html_escape "$cell")
                            # Color-code anomaly items
                            if [[ "$kind" == "anomaly" ]] && echo "$cell" | grep -qiE 'outlier|anomal'; then
                                printf '<td class="anomaly">%s</td>' "$ecell"
                            else
                                printf '<td>%s</td>' "$ecell"
                            fi
                        done <<< "$(echo "$line" | tr '\t' '\n')"
                        printf '</tr>\n'
                    fi
                done <<< "$body"
                printf '</table>\n'
            else
                # Non-tabular body: render as pre-formatted text
                # Apply color coding for correlations and anomalies
                local escaped_body
                escaped_body=$(html_escape "$body")

                # Color strong correlations (r >= 0.70)
                if [[ "$kind" == "corr_pairs" ]]; then
                    escaped_body=$(echo "$escaped_body" | sed -E 's/(r=0\.[7-9][0-9])/<span class="correlation-strong">\1<\/span>/g; s/(r=1\.00)/<span class="correlation-strong">\1<\/span>/g; s/(r=-0\.[7-9][0-9])/<span class="correlation-strong">\1<\/span>/g; s/(r=-1\.00)/<span class="correlation-strong">\1<\/span>/g')
                fi

                # Color anomaly markers
                if [[ "$kind" == "anomaly" ]]; then
                    escaped_body=$(echo "$escaped_body" | sed -E 's/(outlier[s]?)/<span class="anomaly">\1<\/span>/gi')
                fi

                printf '<div class="item-body">%s</div>\n' "$escaped_body"

                # Add sparkline SVG for histogram/sparkline kinds
                if [[ "$kind" == "histogram" || "$kind" == "sparkline" ]]; then
                    local svg=""
                    svg=$(_html_sparkline_svg "$body" 2>/dev/null) || true
                    if [[ -n "$svg" ]]; then
                        printf '<div class="sparkline">%s</div>\n' "$svg"
                    fi
                fi
            fi
        fi

        printf '</div>\n'
    done

    # Footer
    printf '<div class="footer">Generated by EnvoyAnalyze v%s &mdash; %s</div>\n' "$VERSION" "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    printf '</body>\n</html>\n'
}

===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_helpers.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=73c0ebaec9f30df6762bce0d5954490006a52a6aac31e703025e8a0b9423ca4e===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Helper functions for envoy-analyze
##
## String utilities, escaping, delimiter detection, and common helpers.
##
## Reads:  (varies per helper; inputs are function arguments)
##         emit_summary kind_filter analysis_list (read by _will_keep_kind)
## Writes: AWK_ISMISSING (module-level definition)
################################################################################

err () {
    echo "envoy-analyze: error: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

warn () {
    echo "envoy-analyze: warning: $*" >&2
}

################################################################################
## ENV-126: filter-aware computation gate
##
## Returns 0 (true) iff the caller should compute / report items of `kind`.
## A `run_*` analysis function should call this early and `return 0` on a
## false answer to skip its expensive work. Output for any *un*-filtered
## run is byte-identical to the no-skip pipeline.
##
## Conservative-by-default: if any signal makes us uncertain whether the
## kind would be kept, we say yes. Skipping is purely an optimisation;
## a false negative prints stale data, which is the worst-case failure.
##
## Skip-eligible scenarios:
##   - User passed `--kinds K1,K2,...` and `kind` is not in the list.
##
## Always-run scenarios (anything that could need every kind's globals):
##   - `EF_FILTER_SKIP=0` escape hatch (regression-test toggle).
##   - `--summary` is on Aje28094Aj `run_summary_verdict` reads from every kind.
##   - `--analysis-list 1,2,...` (selecting by item id requires all
##     items to exist before the post-pass picker runs).
##   - `--mode benchmark|monitor` Aje28094Aj modes rewrite tags after analyses
##     run; without knowing the post-rewrite tag we can't safely skip.
################################################################################
_will_keep_kind () {
    local kind="$1"
    # Escape hatch.
    [[ "${EF_FILTER_SKIP:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
    # --summary needs everything (run_summary_verdict reads from every kind).
    [[ "${emit_summary:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
    # Numeric `--analysis-list` picks items by id post-hoc.
    [[ -n "${analysis_list:-}" ]] && return 0
    # No --kinds filter Aje28692Aj keep everything (tag-only filters and mode
    # rewrites operate over the full kind set; skipping the awks here
    # would mask items the user might still want).
    [[ -z "${kind_filter:-}" ]] && return 0
    # --kinds is set: skip iff the kind is not listed.
    local k
    for k in ${kind_filter//,/ }; do
        [[ "$kind" == "$k" ]] && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

normalize_list () {
    echo "$1" | tr ',' ' ' | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//'
}

trim () {
    echo "$1" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//'
}

detect_delim () {
    local file="$1"
    local header
    header=$(head -n 1 "$file")
    if [[ "$header" == *$'\t'* ]]; then
        echo $'\t'
    elif [[ "$header" == *'|'* ]]; then
        echo '|'
    elif [[ "$header" == *';'* ]] && [[ "$header" != *','* ]]; then
        echo ';'
    elif [[ "$header" == *':'* ]] && [[ "$header" != *','* ]]; then
        echo ':'
    else
        echo ','
    fi
}

# Shared AWK function for missing value detection.
# Inject into AWK blocks with: awk "$AWK_ISMISSING" '...'
AWK_ISMISSING='function ismissing(v) {
    return (v=="" || v=="NA" || v=="N/A" || v=="null" || v=="NULL" || v=="NaN" || v=="nan" || v=="None" || v=="none" || v=="-" || v=="." || v=="#N/A")
}'

json_escape () {
    awk 'BEGIN{ORS=""; first=1}
        {
            gsub(/\\/, "\\\\");
            gsub(/"/, "\\\"");
            gsub(/\t/, "\\t");
            gsub(/\r/, "");
            if (!first) printf "\\n";
            printf "%s", $0;
            first=0;
        }' <<< "$1"
}

escape_csv () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\r'/}"
    v="${v//$'\n'/\\n}"
    v="${v//\"/\"\"}"
    printf '"%s"' "$v"
}

escape_tsv () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\r'/}"
    v="${v//$'\n'/\\n}"
    v="${v//$'\t'/ }"
    printf "%s" "$v"
}

# Case-insensitive match of a name against a comma-separated list.
# Usage: _name_in_csv_list_ci "zip_code" "zip_code,id,total"
_name_in_csv_list_ci () {
    local needle="${1,,}"
    local csv="$2"
    local old_ifs="$IFS"
    IFS=',' read -ra _items <<< "$csv"
    IFS="$old_ifs"
    local v
    for v in "${_items[@]}"; do
        # Trim whitespace
        v="${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        if [[ "${v,,}" == "$needle" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

list_contains () {
    local needle="$1"
    shift
    local v
    for v in "$@"; do
        if [[ "$v" == "$needle" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# Float comparison.
# Usage: float_cmp "3.14" ">=" "2.0"  (operators: > >= < <= == !=)
#
# ENV-164: implementation rewritten to delegate to awk. The previous
# bash-arithmetic version scaled by 1e6 and overflowed any value above
# ~9.2e12 (signed-64-bit max / 1e6) Aje28094Aj a column of nanosecond timestamps,
# financial cents, or large IDs would silently produce wrong comparison
# results. It also rejected scientific notation (`1e-05`) with
# "value too great for base", which awk routinely produces from
# `printf %g`. The awk delegation handles both: numbers go through
# awk's IEEE-754 double conversion (~15-17 significant digits, scientific
# notation native), and the per-call awk fork is acceptable because
# float_cmp is called O(columns) per analyze run, not in tight loops.
float_cmp () {
    local a="$1" op="$2" b="$3"
    awk -v a="$a" -v b="$b" -v op="$op" '
        BEGIN {
            af = a + 0
            bf = b + 0
            if (op == ">")  exit !(af >  bf)
            if (op == ">=") exit !(af >= bf)
            if (op == "<")  exit !(af <  bf)
            if (op == "<=") exit !(af <= bf)
            if (op == "==") exit !(af == bf)
            if (op == "!=") exit !(af != bf)
            exit 1
        }
    '
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=520642c404161a4e82f6853db3aa7abb3cf5064061997a4c42ec34daac5d4192===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Per-column numeric analyses for envoy-analyze (optimized: combined single-pass)
##
## Analyses: summary stats, histogram, sparkline, anomaly detection,
## distribution shape, CV, mode, normality, precision, trend detection,
## bimodality, Benford's Law, monotonicity.
##
## Each numeric column is analyzed in ONE awk pass over the input file (plus
## a sort + small awk for percentiles). Previously required ~10 awk passes
## per column.
##
## Reads:  input_file delim COL_COUNT COL_NAMES COL_TYPE
##         COL_MEAN COL_STD COL_SKEW COL_KURT COL_MIN COL_MAX
##         COL_NUMERIC COL_TEXT
##         ROW_COUNT SPARK_SAMPLES
##         AWK_ISMISSING BENFORD_CRIT BENFORD_ALPHA
## Writes: _NUM_P05 _NUM_Q1 _NUM_P50 _NUM_Q3 _NUM_P95 cleanup_files
##         ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

# Percentile values set by anomaly detection for use by shape analysis
_NUM_P05="n/a"
_NUM_Q1="n/a"
_NUM_P50="n/a"
_NUM_Q3="n/a"
_NUM_P95="n/a"

########################################
## Combined single-pass awk for one numeric column. Emits 9 fixed-order
## lines parsed by run_numeric_analyses; body in lib/awk/numeric_combined.awk
## (ENV-123). Args: col min max mean std skip tmp_vals.
_numeric_combined_awk () {
    local col="$1" cmin="$2" cmax="$3" cmean="$4" cstd="$5" skip="$6" tmp_vals="$7"

    awk -F"$delim" \
        -v col="$col" -v mn="$cmin" -v mx="$cmax" \
        -v mean="$cmean" -v std="$cstd" -v skip="$skip" \
        -v maxn="$SPARK_SAMPLES" -v tmpfile="$tmp_vals" \
        -v benford_crit="${BENFORD_CRIT:-15.507}" \
        -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/awk/numeric_combined.awk" \
        "$input_file"
}

########################################
## Percentile computation from sorted values.
## Sets _NUM_P05..P95 globals and emits the anomaly item.
## Args: tmp_vals col_name z_count z_vals
##
_numeric_percentiles () {
    local tmp_vals="$1" col_name="$2" z_count="$3" z_vals="$4"

    _NUM_P05="n/a"; _NUM_Q1="n/a"; _NUM_P50="n/a"; _NUM_Q3="n/a"; _NUM_P95="n/a"

    local p05="n/a" q1="n/a" p50="n/a" q3="n/a" p95="n/a"
    local iqr_body="Q1: n/a
Q3: n/a
IQR: n/a
Outliers: 0
Samples: none"

    if [[ -s "$tmp_vals" ]]; then
        local tmp_sorted
        tmp_sorted="$(mktemp -t mda-sorted.XXXXXX)"
        cleanup_files+=("$tmp_sorted")
        sort -n "$tmp_vals" > "$tmp_sorted"
        local iqr_stats
        iqr_stats=$(awk '
            function quantile(p, idx, lo, hi, frac) {
                idx=(n-1)*p+1
                lo=int(idx)
                hi=lo+1
                if (hi>n) hi=n
                frac=idx-lo
                return a[lo] + frac*(a[hi]-a[lo])
            }
            {a[NR]=$1}
            END{
                n=NR
                if (n==0) {print ""; exit}
                p05=quantile(0.05)
                q1=quantile(0.25)
                p50=quantile(0.50)
                q3=quantile(0.75)
                p95=quantile(0.95)
                iqr=q3-q1
                low=q1-1.5*iqr
                high=q3+1.5*iqr
                for(i=1;i<=n;i++){
                    if(a[i]<low || a[i]>high){
                        count++
                        if(count<=5) samples[count]=a[i]
                    }
                }
                printf "%.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %d", p05, q1, p50, q3, p95, iqr, count+0
                for(i=1;i<=count && i<=5;i++) printf "|%s", samples[i]
            }
        ' "$tmp_sorted")

        if [[ -n "$iqr_stats" ]]; then
            local out_count out_vals iqr
            read -r p05 q1 p50 q3 p95 iqr out_count <<< "${iqr_stats%%|*}"
            out_vals=""
            if [[ "$iqr_stats" == *"|"* ]]; then
                out_vals=${iqr_stats#*|}
            fi
            iqr_body="Q1: $q1
Q3: $q3
IQR: $iqr
Outliers: $out_count
Samples: ${out_vals:-none}"
        fi
    fi

    _NUM_P05="$p05"; _NUM_Q1="$q1"; _NUM_P50="$p50"; _NUM_Q3="$q3"; _NUM_P95="$p95"

    add_item "Anomaly detection: $col_name" "Z-score outliers (|z|>3): $z_count
Samples: ${z_vals:-none}

IQR outliers (1.5x):
$iqr_body" "NOISY" "anomaly"
}

########################################
## Main entry point: loop numeric columns, emit all analysis items.
##
run_numeric_analyses () {
    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        local col_name="${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}"
        local col_type="${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}"

        # ENV-135: per-column progress tick on the slowest stage. The
        # global gate `_ENV135_SHOW_PROGRESS` is set in envoy-analyze
        # right before this is called.
        if [[ "${_ENV135_SHOW_PROGRESS:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
            envoy_progress_tick "$i" "$COL_COUNT" "stats: $col_name"
        fi

        if [[ "$col_type" != "numeric" ]]; then
            continue
        fi

        local min="${COL_MIN[$((i-1))]}"
        local max="${COL_MAX[$((i-1))]}"
        local mean="${COL_MEAN[$((i-1))]}"
        local std="${COL_STD[$((i-1))]}"
        local col_skew="${COL_SKEW[$((i-1))]}"
        local col_kurt="${COL_KURT[$((i-1))]}"

        ## 1. Summary stats
        # ENV-132: when the column was classified as numeric but had any
        # non-numeric rows, the mean / std are computed over the numeric
        # subset only. Surface that subset's size inline so the user
        # doesn't read "Mean: 45" without realising 20% of rows were
        # silently dropped. The 0% case (clean numeric column) renders
        # exactly as before Aje28094Aj no annotation noise.
        local _excluded="${COL_TEXT[$((i-1))]:-0}"
        local summary_body="Min: $min
Max: $max
Mean: $mean
Std: $std"
        if [[ "${_excluded:-0}" -gt 0 ]]; then
            local _total_rows=$(( ${COL_NUMERIC[$((i-1))]:-0} + _excluded ))
            local _pct
            if [[ "$_total_rows" -gt 0 ]]; then
                local _p100=$(( ${COL_NUMERIC[$((i-1))]:-0} * 10000 / _total_rows ))
                _pct="$(( _p100 / 100 )).$(printf '%02d' $(( _p100 % 100 )))"
            else
                _pct="0.00"
            fi
            summary_body+=$'\n'"Note: $_excluded non-numeric value(s) excluded from mean/std (${_pct}% numeric)"
        fi
        add_item "Summary stats: $col_name" "$summary_body" "GOOD" "summary"

        ## 2. Run combined single-pass awk
        local tmp_vals
        tmp_vals="$(mktemp -t mda-vals.XXXXXX)"
        cleanup_files+=("$tmp_vals")

        local skip=$(( (ROW_COUNT + SPARK_SAMPLES - 1) / SPARK_SAMPLES ))

        local combined
        combined=$(_numeric_combined_awk "$i" "$min" "$max" "$mean" "$std" "$skip" "$tmp_vals")

        # Parse all 9 fixed-order lines into variables
        local _L=()
        while IFS= read -r _cl; do
            _L+=("$_cl")
        done <<< "$combined"

        local hist_data="${_L[0]:-}"
        local spark_data="${_L[1]:-}"
        local mode_data="${_L[2]:-}"
        local prec_data="${_L[3]:-}"
        local benf_data="${_L[4]:-}"
        local mono_data="${_L[5]:-}"
        local bimod_data="${_L[6]:-}"
        local zout_data="${_L[7]:-}"
        local trend_data="${_L[8]:-}"

        ## 3. Histogram
        if [[ -n "$hist_data" ]]; then
            local hist_body=""
            local bin_spec hbin hstart hend hcount bar
            IFS=';' read -r -a hist_bins <<< "$hist_data"
            for bin_spec in "${hist_bins[@]}"; do
                IFS='|' read -r hbin hstart hend hcount <<< "$bin_spec"
                bar=""
                if [[ "$hcount" -gt 0 ]]; then
                    bar=$(printf "%0.s#" $(seq 1 $((hcount>20?20:hcount))))
                fi
                hist_body+="Bin $hbin ($hstart - $hend): $hcount $bar"$'\n'
            done
            add_item "Histogram: $col_name" "${hist_body%$'\n'}" "GOOD" "histogram"
        fi

        ## 4. Sparkline
        if [[ -n "$spark_data" && "$ROW_COUNT" -gt 0 ]]; then
            add_item "Sparkline: $col_name" "Samples: $spark_data" "GOOD" "sparkline"
        fi

        ## 5. Anomaly detection + percentiles (sort tmpfile, compute IQR)
        local z_count="${zout_data%%|*}"
        local z_vals=""
        if [[ "$zout_data" == *"|"* ]]; then
            z_vals="${zout_data#*|}"
        fi

        _numeric_percentiles "$tmp_vals" "$col_name" "$z_count" "$z_vals"
        COL_Q1[$((i-1))]="$_NUM_Q1"
        COL_Q3[$((i-1))]="$_NUM_Q3"

        ## 6. Distribution shape (uses percentiles set by step 5)
        add_item "Distribution shape: $col_name" "Skewness: ${col_skew}
Kurtosis (excess): ${col_kurt}
P05: ${_NUM_P05}
P25: ${_NUM_Q1:-n/a}
P50: ${_NUM_P50}
P75: ${_NUM_Q3:-n/a}
P95: ${_NUM_P95}" "ADVANCED" "shape"

        ## 7. CV (pure math, no file I/O)
        if float_cmp "$mean" "!=" "0"; then
            local cv
            cv=$(awk -v s="$std" -v m="$mean" 'BEGIN{if(m<0) m=-m; printf "%.2f", (s/m)*100}')
            local cv_interp="high variability"
            if float_cmp "$cv" "<" "15"; then
                cv_interp="low variability"
            elif float_cmp "$cv" "<" "30"; then
                cv_interp="moderate variability"
            fi
            add_item "Coefficient of variation: $col_name" "CV: ${cv}%
Mean: $mean
Std: $std
Interpretation: $cv_interp" "ADVANCED" "cv"
        fi

        ## 8. Mode
        local mode_val mode_count mode_uniq
        IFS='|' read -r mode_val mode_count mode_uniq <<< "$mode_data"
        if [[ "$mode_val" != "n/a" && "$mode_count" -gt 1 ]]; then
            add_item "Mode: $col_name" "Mode: $mode_val (appears $mode_count times)
Unique values: $mode_uniq" "ADVANCED" "mode"
        fi

        ## 9. Normality (pure math, no file I/O)
        local norm_desc
        local abs_skew="${col_skew#-}"
        if float_cmp "$abs_skew" "<" "0.5" && float_cmp "$col_kurt" ">" "-1" && float_cmp "$col_kurt" "<" "1"; then
            norm_desc="approximately normal"
        elif float_cmp "$abs_skew" ">=" "0.5" && float_cmp "$abs_skew" "<" "1"; then
            norm_desc="moderately skewed"
        elif float_cmp "$abs_skew" ">=" "1"; then
            norm_desc="highly skewed"
        else
            norm_desc="unknown shape"
        fi
        if float_cmp "$col_kurt" ">" "2"; then
            norm_desc+=", heavy-tailed (leptokurtic)"
        elif float_cmp "$col_kurt" "<" "-1"; then
            norm_desc+=", light-tailed (platykurtic)"
        fi
        local skew_dir=""
        if float_cmp "$col_skew" ">" "0.5"; then
            skew_dir="right-skewed"
        elif float_cmp "$col_skew" "<" "-0.5"; then
            skew_dir="left-skewed"
        else
            skew_dir="symmetric"
        fi
        add_item "Normality: $col_name" "Shape: $norm_desc
Direction: $skew_dir
Skewness: $col_skew
Excess kurtosis: $col_kurt" "ADVANCED" "normality"

        ## 10. Precision
        local prec_total prec_int prec_dec prec_maxdp prec_avgdp
        IFS='|' read -r prec_total prec_int prec_dec prec_maxdp prec_avgdp <<< "$prec_data"
        local prec_type="integer"
        if [[ "$prec_dec" -gt 0 ]]; then
            if [[ "$prec_int" -eq 0 ]]; then
                prec_type="decimal"
            else
                prec_type="mixed (${prec_int} integer, ${prec_dec} decimal)"
            fi
        fi
        add_item "Numeric precision: $col_name" "Type: $prec_type
Max decimal places: $prec_maxdp
Avg decimal places: $prec_avgdp" "ADVANCED" "precision"

        ## 11. Trend
        if [[ "$trend_data" != "NA" ]]; then
            local trend_desc abs_trend="${trend_data#-}"
            if float_cmp "$abs_trend" "<" "0.3"; then
                trend_desc="no trend"
            elif float_cmp "$abs_trend" "<" "0.7"; then
                trend_desc="moderate trend"
            else
                trend_desc="strong trend"
            fi
            if float_cmp "$trend_data" ">" "0.3"; then
                trend_desc+=" (increasing)"
            elif float_cmp "$trend_data" "<" "-0.3"; then
                trend_desc+=" (decreasing)"
            fi
            add_item "Trend: $col_name" "Spearman rho vs row order: $trend_data
$trend_desc" "ADVANCED" "trend"

            ## ENV-057: oscillation detection. Count sign changes in first
            ## differences of sequential numeric values. If the ratio of
            ## sign-changes to transitions exceeds 0.6, report as oscillating.
            local osc_data
            osc_data=$(awk -v col="$i" -F"$delim" "$AWK_ISMISSING"'
                function isnum(x){ return (x ~ /^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$/) }
                NR==1{next}
                {
                    v = $col
                    gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", v)
                    if (ismissing(v) || !isnum(v)) next
                    if (have_prev) {
                        diff = v - prev
                        if (have_prev_diff && prev_diff != 0 && diff != 0) {
                            if ((prev_diff > 0) != (diff > 0)) changes++
                            transitions++
                        }
                        prev_diff = diff
                        have_prev_diff = 1
                    }
                    prev = v
                    have_prev = 1
                }
                END {
                    if (transitions < 5) { print "NA"; exit }
                    ratio = changes / transitions
                    printf "%d|%d|%.3f\n", changes, transitions, ratio
                }' "$input_file")
            if [[ -n "$osc_data" && "$osc_data" != "NA" ]]; then
                local osc_changes osc_trans osc_ratio
                IFS='|' read -r osc_changes osc_trans osc_ratio <<< "$osc_data"
                if float_cmp "$osc_ratio" ">=" "0.6"; then
                    add_item "Oscillation: $col_name" "Sign-change ratio: $osc_ratio ($osc_changes / $osc_trans transitions)
Column alternates direction frequently Aje28094Aj consider treating as oscillating rather than trending." "ADVANCED" "oscillation"
                fi
            fi
        fi

        ## 12. Bimodality
        local bimod_flag bimod_peaks bimod_h1 bimod_h2
        IFS='|' read -r bimod_flag bimod_peaks bimod_h1 bimod_h2 <<< "$bimod_data"
        if [[ "$bimod_flag" == "YES" ]]; then
            add_item "Bimodality: $col_name" "Bimodal: YES
Peaks detected: $bimod_peaks
Peak heights: $bimod_h1, $bimod_h2
A valley between peaks drops below 50% of the smaller peak." "ADVANCED" "bimodality"
        fi

        ## 13. Benford's Law
        if [[ "$benf_data" != "INSUFFICIENT" ]]; then
            local benford_body="" benford_chi2=""
            local -a benford_parts
            IFS='|' read -r -a benford_parts <<< "$benf_data"
            local part
            for part in "${benford_parts[@]}"; do
                if [[ "$part" =~ ^[0-9]+: ]]; then
                    local digit obs exp
                    IFS=':' read -r digit obs exp <<< "$part"
                    benford_body+="Digit $digit: observed ${obs}%, expected ${exp}%"$'\n'
                fi
            done
            local n_parts=${#benford_parts[@]}
            local benford_verdict="${benford_parts[$((n_parts-2))]}"
            benford_chi2="${benford_parts[$((n_parts-1))]}"
            add_item "Benford's Law: $col_name" "${benford_body}Chi-squared: $benford_chi2 (df=8, critical=${BENFORD_CRIT:-15.507}, alpha=${BENFORD_ALPHA:-0.05})
Result: $benford_verdict ($(if [[ "$benford_verdict" == "PASS" ]]; then echo "distribution follows Benford's Law"; else echo "deviation from Benford's Law detected"; fi))" "ADVANCED" "benford"
        fi

        ## 14. Monotonicity
        local mono_n mono_asc mono_desc mono_eq mono_pairs
        IFS='|' read -r mono_n mono_asc mono_desc mono_eq mono_pairs <<< "$mono_data"
        if [[ "$mono_n" != "NA" && "$mono_pairs" -gt 0 ]]; then
            local asc_pct desc_pct mono_label
            # Compute percentage with 1 decimal using bash integer math (scaled by 10)
            local _a10=$(( mono_asc * 1000 / mono_pairs ))
            asc_pct="$(( _a10 / 10 )).$(( _a10 % 10 ))"
            local _d10=$(( mono_desc * 1000 / mono_pairs ))
            desc_pct="$(( _d10 / 10 )).$(( _d10 % 10 ))"
            mono_label="not sorted"
            if [[ "$mono_asc" -eq "$mono_pairs" ]]; then
                mono_label="perfectly sorted (ascending)"
            elif [[ "$mono_desc" -eq "$mono_pairs" ]]; then
                mono_label="perfectly sorted (descending)"
            elif float_cmp "$asc_pct" ">=" "90"; then
                mono_label="nearly sorted (ascending, ${asc_pct}%)"
            elif float_cmp "$desc_pct" ">=" "90"; then
                mono_label="nearly sorted (descending, ${desc_pct}%)"
            fi
            if [[ "$mono_label" != "not sorted" ]]; then
                add_item "Monotonicity: $col_name" "$mono_label
Ascending pairs: $mono_asc/$mono_pairs (${asc_pct}%)
Descending pairs: $mono_desc/$mono_pairs (${desc_pct}%)
Equal pairs: $mono_eq" "ADVANCED" "monotonicity"
            fi
        fi
    done
}
