#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Profile management for envoy-analyze
##
## Save and load analysis selection profiles.
##
## Reads:  (function arguments only Aje28094Aj name + dir)
## Writes: (none Aje28094Aj file I/O to profile directory)
################################################################################

load_profile () {
    local name="$1"
    local dir="$2"
    local file="$dir/$name.profile"
    [[ -f "$file" ]] || err "Profile not found: $file"
    cat "$file"
}

save_profile () {
    local name="$1"
    local dir="$2"
    local list="$3"
    if [[ ! "$name" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ ]]; then
        err "Invalid profile name: '$name' (use only alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores)"
    fi
    if ! mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
        err "Cannot create profile directory: $dir"
    fi
    if ! echo "$list" > "$dir/$name.profile"; then
        err "Cannot write profile: $dir/$name.profile"
    fi
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_quality.sh===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Data quality and diagnostic analyses for envoy-analyze
##
## Analyses: zero-variance columns, data quality score, suggested drops,
## noisy items (duplicates, sample rows, row lengths, common chars).
##
## Reads:  input_file delim COL_COUNT COL_NAMES COL_TYPE
##         COL_STD COL_MIN COL_MAX COL_MISSING ROW_COUNT
##         CORR_VALUES corr_cols corr_names
## Writes: dup_count
##         ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

run_zero_variance () {
    local zero_body=""
    local i
    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}" != "numeric" ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        local std="${COL_STD[$((i-1))]}"
        local min="${COL_MIN[$((i-1))]}"
        local max="${COL_MAX[$((i-1))]}"
        if [[ -n "$std" ]] && float_cmp "$std" "==" "0"; then
            zero_body+="${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}: std=0, min=$min, max=$max"$'\n'
        fi
    done

    if [[ -n "$zero_body" ]]; then
        add_item "Zero-variance numeric columns" "${zero_body%$'\n'}" "DIAGNOSTIC" "zero_variance"
    fi
}

run_quality_score () {
    # Pre-compute dup_count (also used by noisy items)
    dup_count=$(awk 'NR>1{if(seen[$0]++) dup++} END{print dup+0}' "$input_file")

    local quality_score=100
    local quality_issues=""

    # Missing data penalty
    local total_cells=$((ROW_COUNT * COL_COUNT))
    local total_missing=0
    local i
    for ((i=0; i<COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        total_missing=$((total_missing + ${COL_MISSING[$i]:-0}))
    done
    if [[ $total_cells -gt 0 ]]; then
        local missing_pct missing_penalty
        local _mp100=$(( total_missing * 10000 / total_cells ))
        missing_pct="$(( _mp100 / 100 )).$(printf '%02d' $(( _mp100 % 100 )))"
        # penalty = int(pct * 1.5), capped at 25
        # _mp100 = pct * 100, so pct * 1.5 = _mp100 * 15 / 1000
        missing_penalty=$(( _mp100 * 15 / 1000 ))
        if [[ $missing_penalty -gt 25 ]]; then missing_penalty=25; fi
        quality_score=$((quality_score - missing_penalty))
        if [[ "$total_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
            quality_issues+="Missing values: ${missing_pct}% of cells (-${missing_penalty} points)"$'\n'
        fi
    fi

    # Duplicate rows penalty
    if [[ "$dup_count" -gt 0 && "$ROW_COUNT" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local dup_pct dup_penalty
        local _dp100=$(( dup_count * 10000 / ROW_COUNT ))
        dup_pct="$(( _dp100 / 100 )).$(printf '%02d' $(( _dp100 % 100 )))"
        dup_penalty=$(( _dp100 / 100 ))
        if [[ $dup_penalty -gt 15 ]]; then dup_penalty=15; fi
        quality_score=$((quality_score - dup_penalty))
        quality_issues+="Duplicate rows: $dup_count (${dup_pct}%, -${dup_penalty} points)"$'\n'
    fi

    # Zero-variance penalty
    local zv_count=0
    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}" == "numeric" ]]; then
            local std_val="${COL_STD[$((i-1))]}"
            if [[ -n "$std_val" ]] && float_cmp "$std_val" "==" "0"; then
                zv_count=$((zv_count+1))
            fi
        fi
    done
    if [[ $zv_count -gt 0 ]]; then
        local zv_penalty=$((zv_count * 5))
        if [[ $zv_penalty -gt 15 ]]; then
            zv_penalty=15
        fi
        quality_score=$((quality_score - zv_penalty))
        quality_issues+="Zero-variance columns: $zv_count (-${zv_penalty} points)"$'\n'
    fi

    # Low row count penalty
    if [[ "$ROW_COUNT" -lt 10 ]]; then
        local low_penalty=10
        quality_score=$((quality_score - low_penalty))
        quality_issues+="Low row count: $ROW_COUNT rows (-${low_penalty} points)"$'\n'
    fi

    # Single-column penalty
    if [[ "$COL_COUNT" -lt 2 ]]; then
        local col_penalty=10
        quality_score=$((quality_score - col_penalty))
        quality_issues+="Single column (-${col_penalty} points)"$'\n'
    fi

    if [[ $quality_score -lt 0 ]]; then
        quality_score=0
    fi

    local quality_grade="Excellent"
    if [[ $quality_score -lt 90 ]]; then quality_grade="Good"; fi
    if [[ $quality_score -lt 70 ]]; then quality_grade="Fair"; fi
    if [[ $quality_score -lt 50 ]]; then quality_grade="Poor"; fi

    local quality_body="Score: ${quality_score}/100 ($quality_grade)
Rows: $ROW_COUNT | Columns: $COL_COUNT | Cells: $total_cells"
    if [[ -n "$quality_issues" ]]; then
        quality_body+=$'\n'"Issues:"$'\n'"${quality_issues%$'\n'}"
    else
        quality_body+=$'\n'"No issues detected."
    fi
    add_item "Data quality score" "$quality_body" "GOOD" "quality_score"
}

run_suggested_drops () {
    local drop_body=""
    local drop_found=0
    local i

    for ((i=1; i<=COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        local col_name="${COL_NAMES[$((i-1))]}"
        local reasons=""

        # Zero variance
        if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$((i-1))]}" == "numeric" ]]; then
            local std_val="${COL_STD[$((i-1))]}"
            local mean_val="${COL_MEAN[$((i-1))]}"
            if [[ -n "$std_val" ]] && float_cmp "$std_val" "==" "0"; then
                reasons+="zero variance; "
            elif [[ -n "$std_val" && -n "$mean_val" ]]; then
                # Near-constant: CV < 1%
                local cv_check
                cv_check=$(awk -v s="$std_val" -v m="$mean_val" 'BEGIN{
                    if(m<0) m=-m; if(m>0) printf "%.4f", s/m*100; else print 0
                }')
                if [[ -z "$reasons" ]] && float_cmp "$cv_check" ">" "0" && float_cmp "$cv_check" "<" "1"; then
                    reasons+="near-constant (CV=${cv_check}%); "
                fi
            fi
        fi

        # High missing (>50%)
        local miss="${COL_MISSING[$((i-1))]}"
        if [[ -n "$miss" && "$miss" -gt 0 && "$ROW_COUNT" -gt 0 ]]; then
            local miss_ratio miss_pct
            local _mr100=$(( miss * 100 / ROW_COUNT ))
            miss_ratio="$(( _mr100 / 100 )).$(printf '%02d' $(( _mr100 % 100 )))"
            if float_cmp "$miss_ratio" ">" "0.50"; then
                miss_pct="$(( _mr100 ))"
                reasons+="${miss_pct}% missing; "
            fi
        fi

        if [[ -n "$reasons" ]]; then
            drop_body+="$col_name: ${reasons%; }"$'\n'
            drop_found=1
        fi
    done

    # Duplicate columns (limit to first 15 columns for performance) Aje28094Aj single awk pass
    local max_dup_check=$((COL_COUNT < 15 ? COL_COUNT : 15))
    if [[ $max_dup_check -ge 2 ]]; then
        local dup_raw
        dup_raw=$(awk -F"$delim" -v ncols="$max_dup_check" '
            NR>1{
                for(i=1; i<ncols; i++){
                    for(j=i+1; j<=ncols; j++){
                        if(!diff[i,j] && $i!=$j) diff[i,j]=1
                    }
                }
            }
            END{
                for(i=1; i<ncols; i++){
                    for(j=i+1; j<=ncols; j++){
                        if(!diff[i,j]) printf "%d,%d\n", i, j
                    }
                }
            }
        ' "$input_file")
        if [[ -n "$dup_raw" ]]; then
            local ci cj
            while IFS=',' read -r ci cj; do
                drop_body+="${COL_NAMES[$((cj-1))]}: duplicate of ${COL_NAMES[$((ci-1))]}"$'\n'
                drop_found=1
            done <<< "$dup_raw"
        fi
    fi

    # Perfectly correlated pairs (r > 0.99)
    if [[ "${#CORR_VALUES[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local ci cj
        for ((ci=0; ci<${#corr_cols[@]}; ci++)); do
            for ((cj=ci+1; cj<${#corr_cols[@]}; cj++)); do
                local idx=$((ci*${#corr_cols[@]}+cj))
                local r="${CORR_VALUES[$idx]}"
                if [[ "$r" == "NA" ]]; then
                    continue
                fi
                local abs_r
                abs_r="${r#-}"
                if float_cmp "$abs_r" ">" "0.99"; then
                    drop_body+="${corr_names[$cj]}: nearly perfectly correlated with ${corr_names[$ci]} (r=$r)"$'\n'
                    drop_found=1
                fi
            done
        done
    fi

    if [[ $drop_found -eq 1 ]]; then
        add_item "Suggested column drops" "${drop_body%$'\n'}" "DIAGNOSTIC" "drop_suggest"
    fi
}

run_noisy_items () {
    add_item "Duplicate rows" "Duplicate rows: $dup_count" "NOISY" "noisy"

    # Single-pass: collect first 3 rows, last 3 rows, line length extremes, and common chars
    local noisy_raw
    noisy_raw=$(awk '
        NR==1{next}
        {
            row++
            l=length($0)
            if(min_len=="" || l<min_len) min_len=l
            if(l>max_len) max_len=l
            if(row<=3) first[row]=$0
            # Keep circular buffer for last 3
            last_buf[row%3]=$0
            last_count=row
            for(i=1;i<=l;i++){
                c=substr($0,i,1)
                if(c==","||c=="\t"||c=="\r"||c==" ") continue
                chars[c]++
            }
        }
        END{
            # Section 1: first rows
            for(i=1;i<=3 && i<=last_count;i++) print first[i]
            print "---SECTION---"
            # Section 2: last rows
            if(last_count>=3){
                for(i=last_count-2;i<=last_count;i++) print last_buf[i%3]
            } else {
                for(i=1;i<=last_count;i++) print first[i]
            }
            print "---SECTION---"
            # Section 3: line lengths
            printf "%d %d\n", min_len+0, max_len+0
            print "---SECTION---"
            # Section 4: common chars (all, to be sorted externally)
            for(c in chars) printf "%d\t%s\n", chars[c], c
        }
    ' "$input_file")

    # Parse sections
    local section=0 first_rows="" last_rows="" line_lengths="" char_lines=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == "---SECTION---" ]]; then
            section=$((section+1))
            continue
        fi
        case $section in
            0) first_rows+="$line"$'\n' ;;
            1) last_rows+="$line"$'\n' ;;
            2) line_lengths="$line" ;;
            3) char_lines+="$line"$'\n' ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$noisy_raw"

    add_item "Sample rows (first 3)" "${first_rows%$'\n'}" "NOISY" "noisy"
    add_item "Sample rows (last 3)" "${last_rows%$'\n'}" "NOISY" "noisy"

    local min_len max_len
    read -r min_len max_len <<< "$line_lengths"
    add_item "Row length extremes" "Min row length: $min_len
Max row length: $max_len" "NOISY" "noisy"

    local common_chars chars_body
    common_chars=$(printf "%s" "${char_lines%$'\n'}" | sort -nr | head -n 5)
    chars_body=""
    if [[ -n "$common_chars" ]]; then
        local count ch
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r count ch; do
            chars_body+="$ch: $count"$'\n'
        done <<< "$common_chars"
    else
        chars_body="(none)"
    fi
    add_item "Most common characters" "${chars_body%$'\n'}" "NOISY" "noisy"
}

===FILE: analyze/lib/_summary.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=34076f243fcd351e17151009fc56ae0b6b0d672f4a625111fb8e7ac96cd57390===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Summary/verdict output for envoy-analyze
##
## Synthesizes a natural-language summary from analysis results.
##
## Reads:  COL_NAMES COL_TYPE COL_MEAN COL_MISSING COL_COUNT ROW_COUNT
##         NUM_COL_NAMES
##         ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS
##         _CORR_PAIR_LINES threshold_specs
## Writes: ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

run_summary_verdict () {
    local findings=()

    # 1. Dataset size
    findings+=("Dataset: ${ROW_COUNT} rows, ${COL_COUNT} columns")

    # 2. Column with lowest and highest mean
    if [[ ${#NUM_COL_NAMES[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
        local lo_name="" lo_mean="" hi_name="" hi_mean=""
        local i
        for ((i=0; i<COL_COUNT; i++)); do
            [[ "${COL_TYPE[$i]}" != "numeric" ]] && continue
            local m="${COL_MEAN[$i]}"
            [[ -z "$m" || "$m" == "NA" ]] && continue
            if [[ -z "$lo_mean" ]] || float_cmp "$m" "<" "$lo_mean"; then
                lo_mean="$m"
                lo_name="${COL_NAMES[$i]}"
            fi
            if [[ -z "$hi_mean" ]] || float_cmp "$m" ">" "$hi_mean"; then
                hi_mean="$m"
                hi_name="${COL_NAMES[$i]}"
            fi
        done
        if [[ -n "$lo_name" && "$lo_name" != "$hi_name" ]]; then
            findings+=("Lowest mean: '$lo_name' ($lo_mean); Highest mean: '$hi_name' ($hi_mean)")
        fi
    fi

    # 3. Strongest correlation
    if [[ -n "${_CORR_PAIR_LINES:-}" ]]; then
        local best_pair
        best_pair=$(printf "%s" "$_CORR_PAIR_LINES" | sort -nr | awk 'NR==1')
        if [[ -n "$best_pair" ]]; then
            local _abs _r _a _b
            IFS=$'\t' read -r _abs _r _a _b <<< "$best_pair"
            findings+=("Strongest correlation: $_a vs $_b (r=$_r)")
        fi
    fi

    # 4. Count outliers from anomaly items
    local total_outliers=0
    local outlier_cols=""
    for ((i=0; i<${#ITEM_KINDS[@]}; i++)); do
        if [[ "${ITEM_KINDS[$i]}" == "anomaly" ]]; then
            local body="${ITEM_BODIES[$i]}"
            # Extract z-score count from "Z-score outliers (|z|>3): N"
            local zcount="0"
            local zline
            zline=$(echo "$body" | grep "Z-score outliers" || true)
            if [[ -n "$zline" ]]; then
                zcount=$(echo "$zline" | sed 's/.*): //' | tr -cd '0-9')
                [[ -z "$zcount" ]] && zcount=0
            fi
            if [[ "$zcount" -gt 0 ]]; then
                total_outliers=$((total_outliers + zcount))
                local cname="${ITEM_TITLES[$i]#Anomaly detection: }"
                outlier_cols+="$cname ($zcount), "
            fi
        fi
    done
    if [[ $total_outliers -gt 0 ]]; then
        findings+=("Outliers: $total_outliers z-score outlier(s) in ${outlier_cols%, }")
    fi

    # 5. Trend detection
    for ((i=0; i<${#ITEM_KINDS[@]}; i++)); do
        if [[ "${ITEM_KINDS[$i]}" == "trend" ]]; then
            local body="${ITEM_BODIES[$i]}"
            if [[ "$body" == *"strong trend"* ]]; then
                local cname="${ITEM_TITLES[$i]#Trend: }"
                local rho
                rho=$(echo "$body" | grep "Spearman rho" | sed 's/.*: //' || true)
                if [[ -n "$rho" ]]; then
                    local dir="increasing"
                    if float_cmp "$rho" "<" "0"; then
                        dir="decreasing"
                    fi
                    findings+=("Strong trend: '$cname' is $dir (rho=$rho)")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done

    # 6. Quality score
    for ((i=0; i<${#ITEM_KINDS[@]}; i++)); do
        if [[ "${ITEM_KINDS[$i]}" == "quality_score" ]]; then
            local score_line
            score_line="${ITEM_BODIES[$i]%%$'\n'*}"
            findings+=("Quality: $score_line")
            break
        fi
    done

    # 7. Missing data
    local total_missing=0
    for ((i=0; i<COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        total_missing=$((total_missing + ${COL_MISSING[$i]:-0}))
    done
    if [[ $total_missing -gt 0 ]]; then
        findings+=("Missing data: $total_missing missing value(s) across dataset")
    fi

    # 8. Threshold results
    if [[ ${#threshold_specs[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        local tpass=0 tfail=0
        for ((i=0; i<${#ITEM_KINDS[@]}; i++)); do
            if [[ "${ITEM_KINDS[$i]}" == "threshold" ]]; then
                if [[ "${ITEM_TAGS[$i]}" == "GOOD" ]]; then
                    tpass=$((tpass + 1))
                else
                    tfail=$((tfail + 1))
                fi
            fi
        done
        if [[ $tfail -gt 0 ]]; then
            findings+=("Thresholds: $tfail of $((tpass+tfail)) check(s) FAILED")
        else
            findings+=("Thresholds: All $tpass check(s) passed")
        fi
    fi

    # Build body
    local body="Key findings:"
    local f
    for f in "${findings[@]}"; do
        body+=$'\n'"- $f"
    done

    add_item "Analysis summary" "$body" "GOOD" "verdict"
}

===FILE-ESC: analyze/lib/_threshold.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=57afa8dc4fab677e55533b5a14dfe8d0468f6244d32115f1dafeea9398bb6b61===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Threshold alerting for envoy-analyze
##
## Checks column statistics against user-defined thresholds and emits
## PASS/FAIL verdicts. Sets threshold_exit_code=1 if any threshold fails.
##
## Reads:  threshold_specs COL_NAMES COL_COUNT
##         COL_TYPE COL_MEAN COL_MIN COL_MAX
## Writes: threshold_exit_code
##         ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)
################################################################################

# Parse a threshold spec like "column_name>100" or "column name<=0.5"
# Sets: _THRESH_COL _THRESH_OP _THRESH_VAL
_parse_threshold_spec () {
    local spec="$1"
    _THRESH_COL=""
    _THRESH_OP=""
    _THRESH_VAL=""

    # Try operators in order of length (longest first to avoid partial match)
    local op
    for op in ">=" "<=" "!=" "==" ">" "<"; do
        if [[ "$spec" == *"$op"* ]]; then
            _THRESH_COL="${spec%%"$op"*}"
            _THRESH_VAL="${spec#*"$op"}"
            _THRESH_OP="$op"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# Find column index (0-based) by name (case-insensitive)
# Sets _THRESH_COL_IDX or returns 1 if not found
_THRESH_COL_IDX=-1
_find_threshold_col () {
    local target="$1"
    local target_lower="${target,,}"
    _THRESH_COL_IDX=-1
    local i
    for ((i=0; i<COL_COUNT; i++)); do
        local name_lower="${COL_NAMES[$i],,}"
        if [[ "$name_lower" == "$target_lower" ]]; then
            _THRESH_COL_IDX=$i
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# Check a single threshold against summary stats (mean, min, max).
# Returns result text via _THRESH_CHECK_RESULT and sets _THRESH_CHECK_PASS (0=pass, 1=fail)
_THRESH_CHECK_RESULT=""
_THRESH_CHECK_PASS=0

_check_threshold () {
    local col_idx="$1"
    local op="$2"
    local threshold="$3"
    local col_name="${COL_NAMES[$col_idx]}"

    _THRESH_CHECK_RESULT=""
    _THRESH_CHECK_PASS=0

    if [[ "${COL_TYPE[$col_idx]}" != "numeric" ]]; then
        _THRESH_CHECK_RESULT="Column '$col_name' is not numeric Aje28094Aj threshold check skipped."
        _THRESH_CHECK_PASS=1
        return
    fi

    local mean="${COL_MEAN[$col_idx]}"
    local min="${COL_MIN[$col_idx]}"
    local max="${COL_MAX[$col_idx]}"

    if [[ -z "$mean" || "$mean" == "NA" ]]; then
        _THRESH_CHECK_RESULT="Column '$col_name' has no numeric data."
        _THRESH_CHECK_PASS=1
        return
    fi

    # Check mean, min, max against the threshold
    local mean_pass min_pass max_pass
    mean_pass=$(awk -v v="$mean" -v t="$threshold" -v op="$op" 'BEGIN{
        if(op==">")  exit !(v>t)
        if(op==">=") exit !(v>=t)
        if(op=="<")  exit !(v<t)
        if(op=="<=") exit !(v<=t)
        if(op=="==") exit !(v==t)
        if(op=="!=") exit !(v!=t)
        exit 1
    }' && echo "PASS" || echo "FAIL")

    min_pass=$(awk -v v="$min" -v t="$threshold" -v op="$op" 'BEGIN{
        if(op==">")  exit !(v>t)
        if(op==">=") exit !(v>=t)
        if(op=="<")  exit !(v<t)
        if(op=="<=") exit !(v<=t)
        if(op=="==") exit !(v==t)
        if(op=="!=") exit !(v!=t)
        exit 1
    }' && echo "PASS" || echo "FAIL")

    max_pass=$(awk -v v="$max" -v t="$threshold" -v op="$op" 'BEGIN{
        if(op==">")  exit !(v>t)
        if(op==">=") exit !(v>=t)
        if(op=="<")  exit !(v<t)
        if(op=="<=") exit !(v<=t)
        if(op=="==") exit !(v==t)
        if(op=="!=") exit !(v!=t)
        exit 1
    }' && echo "PASS" || echo "FAIL")

    local overall="PASS"
    # For > and >= thresholds: check that min satisfies (strongest test)
    # For < and <= thresholds: check that max satisfies (strongest test)
    # For == and !=: check mean
    case "$op" in
        ">"  |">=") [[ "$min_pass" == "FAIL" ]] && overall="FAIL" ;;
        "<"  |"<=") [[ "$max_pass" == "FAIL" ]] && overall="FAIL" ;;
        "==" |"!=") [[ "$mean_pass" == "FAIL" ]] && overall="FAIL" ;;
    esac

    _THRESH_CHECK_RESULT="Threshold: $col_name $op $threshold
Mean: $mean ($mean_pass)
Min:  $min ($min_pass)
Max:  $max ($max_pass)
Verdict: $overall"

    if [[ "$overall" == "FAIL" ]]; then
        _THRESH_CHECK_PASS=1
    else
        _THRESH_CHECK_PASS=0
    fi
}

# ENV-027: boolean composition for threshold expressions.
#
# Grammar:
#   expr   := term (OR term)*
#   term   := factor (AND factor)*
#   factor := '(' expr ')' | atom
#   atom   := column op value
#
# Tokenize to _THRESH_TOKENS (one token per element). AND/OR are emitted in
# canonical upper case. Parentheses are separate tokens. Conditions are kept
# whole (column, operator, and value merged) so existing _parse_threshold_spec
# can handle them as before.
_tokenize_threshold_expr () {
    _THRESH_TOKENS=()
    local expr="$1"
    local len=${#expr}
    local i=0
    local cur=""
    _push_cur () {
        local c="${cur#"${cur%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        c="${c%"${c##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        if [[ -n "$c" ]]; then
            case "${c,,}" in
                and) _THRESH_TOKENS+=("AND") ;;
                or)  _THRESH_TOKENS+=("OR") ;;
                *)   _THRESH_TOKENS+=("$c") ;;
            esac
        fi
        cur=""
    }
    while (( i < len )); do
        local ch="${expr:i:1}"
        case "$ch" in
            '(')
                _push_cur
                _THRESH_TOKENS+=("(")
                ;;
            ')')
                _push_cur
                _THRESH_TOKENS+=(")")
                ;;
            ' '|$'\t')
                # Whitespace alone doesn't split a condition like "a>1"; we
                # decide word boundaries based on context. To tokenize AND/OR
                # reliably, treat whitespace as a soft boundary: if the
                # accumulated text (case-insensitive) is exactly "and" or "or"
                # when we hit whitespace, flush. Otherwise accumulate the
                # whitespace too so "col name > 5" stays one token.
                case "${cur,,}" in
                    "and"|"or")
                        _push_cur
                        ;;
                    *)
                        cur+="$ch"
                        ;;
                esac
                # If the next non-space content starts the AND/OR keyword,
                # flush so "a>1 AND b>2" tokenizes as [a>1, AND, b>2].
                local j=$((i + 1))
                while (( j < len )) && [[ "${expr:j:1}" == " " || "${expr:j:1}" == $'\t' ]]; do
                    j=$((j + 1))
                done
                # Peek the next 3-4 chars for AND / OR followed by space/paren/EOF
                local peek3="${expr:j:3}"
                local peek2="${expr:j:2}"
                local after3="${expr:j+3:1}"
                local after2="${expr:j+2:1}"
                if [[ "${peek3,,}" == "and" && ( "$after3" == " " || "$after3" == $'\t' || "$after3" == "(" || -z "$after3" ) ]]; then
                    _push_cur
                fi
                if [[ "${peek2,,}" == "or" && ( "$after2" == " " || "$after2" == $'\t' || "$after2" == "(" || -z "$after2" ) ]]; then
                    _push_cur
                fi
                ;;
            *)
                cur+="$ch"
                ;;
        esac
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    _push_cur
}

# Evaluate a condition atom. Takes the token string, populates
# _THRESH_ATOM_PASS (0=pass, 1=fail) and _THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL.
_eval_threshold_atom () {
    local spec="$1"
    _THRESH_ATOM_PASS=1
    _THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL=""
    if ! _parse_threshold_spec "$spec"; then
        _THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL="Invalid condition syntax: '$spec'"
        return
    fi
    if ! _find_threshold_col "$_THRESH_COL"; then
        _THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL="Column '$_THRESH_COL' not found"
        return
    fi
    _check_threshold "$_THRESH_COL_IDX" "$_THRESH_OP" "$_THRESH_VAL"
    _THRESH_ATOM_PASS="$_THRESH_CHECK_PASS"
    _THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL="$_THRESH_CHECK_RESULT"
}

# Recursive-descent parser/evaluator over _THRESH_TOKENS using a cursor.
# Sets _THRESH_EVAL_PASS (0=pass, 1=fail). Collects per-atom detail lines
# into _THRESH_EVAL_DETAIL.
_THRESH_CUR=0
_THRESH_EVAL_PASS=1
_THRESH_EVAL_DETAIL=""
_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR=""

_thresh_peek () {
    _THRESH_PEEK="${_THRESH_TOKENS[$_THRESH_CUR]:-}"
}
_thresh_consume () {
    _THRESH_CUR=$((_THRESH_CUR + 1))
}

# Returns pass/fail via _THRESH_EVAL_PASS on each call
_parse_expr () {
    _parse_term
    [[ -n "$_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR" ]] && return
    local left="$_THRESH_EVAL_PASS"
    while :; do
        _thresh_peek
        [[ "$_THRESH_PEEK" == "OR" ]] || break
        _thresh_consume
        _parse_term
        [[ -n "$_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR" ]] && return
        # OR: pass if either side passes
        if [[ "$left" == "0" || "$_THRESH_EVAL_PASS" == "0" ]]; then
            left=0
        else
            left=1
        fi
    done
    _THRESH_EVAL_PASS="$left"
}

_parse_term () {
    _parse_factor
    [[ -n "$_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR" ]] && return
    local left="$_THRESH_EVAL_PASS"
    while :; do
        _thresh_peek
        [[ "$_THRESH_PEEK" == "AND" ]] || break
        _thresh_consume
        _parse_factor
        [[ -n "$_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR" ]] && return
        # AND: pass only if both sides pass
        if [[ "$left" == "0" && "$_THRESH_EVAL_PASS" == "0" ]]; then
            left=0
        else
            left=1
        fi
    done
    _THRESH_EVAL_PASS="$left"
}

_parse_factor () {
    _thresh_peek
    if [[ "$_THRESH_PEEK" == "(" ]]; then
        _thresh_consume
        _parse_expr
        [[ -n "$_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR" ]] && return
        _thresh_peek
        if [[ "$_THRESH_PEEK" != ")" ]]; then
            _THRESH_EVAL_ERROR="Expected ')' at token position $_THRESH_CUR"
            return
        fi
        _thresh_consume
        return
    fi
    if [[ -z "$_THRESH_PEEK" || "$_THRESH_PEEK" == "AND" || "$_THRESH_PEEK" == "OR" || "$_THRESH_PEEK" == ")" ]]; then
        _THRESH_EVAL_ERROR="Expected condition at token position $_THRESH_CUR, got '$_THRESH_PEEK'"
        return
    fi
    _eval_threshold_atom "$_THRESH_PEEK"
    if [[ -z "$_THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL" || "$_THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL" == Invalid* || "$_THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL" == Column*not\ found ]]; then
        _THRESH_EVAL_ERROR="$_THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL"
        _thresh_consume
        return
    fi
    _THRESH_EVAL_DETAIL+="${_THRESH_ATOM_DETAIL}"$'\n\n'
    _THRESH_EVAL_PASS="$_THRESH_ATOM_PASS"
    _thresh_consume
}

# Main entry point: run all threshold checks.
run_threshold_checks () {
    if [[ ${#threshold_specs[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        return
    fi

    local pass_count=0
    local fail_count=0
    local spec

    for spec in "${threshold_specs[@]}"; do
        # Reset parser state
        _THRESH_CUR=0
        _THRESH_EVAL_PASS=1
        _THRESH_EVAL_DETAIL=""
        _THRESH_EVAL_ERROR=""

        _tokenize_threshold_expr "$spec"
        if [[ ${#_THRESH_TOKENS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
            add_item "Threshold check: $spec" "Empty threshold expression" "DIAGNOSTIC" "threshold"
            threshold_exit_code=1
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
            continue
        fi

        _parse_expr
        if [[ -n "$_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR" ]]; then
            add_item "Threshold check: $spec" "Threshold parse error: $_THRESH_EVAL_ERROR
Expression: '$spec'
Supported syntax: column>value, column<=value, etc.
Compose with AND / OR / parentheses, e.g. '(a>1 OR b>1) AND c<10'" "DIAGNOSTIC" "threshold"
            threshold_exit_code=1
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
            continue
        fi

        local tag="GOOD"
        if [[ "$_THRESH_EVAL_PASS" != "0" ]]; then
            tag="DIAGNOSTIC"
            threshold_exit_code=1
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        fi

        local verdict="PASS"
        [[ "$_THRESH_EVAL_PASS" != "0" ]] && verdict="FAIL"
        add_item "Threshold check: $spec" "Expression: $spec
Verdict: $verdict

Per-condition detail:
${_THRESH_EVAL_DETAIL}" "$tag" "threshold"
    done

    # Summary item
    local total=$((pass_count + fail_count))
    local summary_tag="GOOD"
    if [[ $fail_count -gt 0 ]]; then
        summary_tag="DIAGNOSTIC"
    fi
    add_item "Threshold summary" "$pass_count/$total checks passed, $fail_count failed" "$summary_tag" "threshold_summary"
}
===END===

# lib/awk/ Aje28094Aj Standalone awk programs

Introduced by [ENV-123](../../../tickets/archive/ENV-123.md) (2026-04-24). Holds awk programs that are too large or stylistically too rich to live as inline heredocs inside `lib/_*.sh`.

## Why a separate directory

Inline awk heredocs in bash have well-known maintenance issues: editor syntax highlighters treat the body as a string, `awk -W lint` cannot run on an embedded program, and parse errors cite an offset *inside the heredoc* rather than the source line. Splitting the program into its own `.awk` file fixes all three with no build-system overhead Aje28094Aj bash invokes it via `awk -f`.

The trade-off (one extra path lookup per invocation) is negligible: each program is invoked once per column, not once per row.

## Contents

| File | Caller | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `numeric_combined.awk` | `lib/_numeric.sh::_numeric_combined_awk` | Single-pass per-column numeric analysis: histogram, sparkline, mode, precision, Benford's Law, monotonicity, bimodality, z-score outliers, Spearman trend. Emits 9 fixed-order lines parsed by `run_numeric_analyses`. |

## Contract

Every `*.awk` here:

1. **Receives all dynamic values via `-v`.** No bash interpolation in the program body. The header comment lists each `-v` parameter (`col`, `mn`, `mx`, Aje280a6Aj) so callers know what to pass.
2. **Initialises every BEGIN-time variable it touches in END.** `awk -W lint` (gawk's pedantic mode) is run against the file in [`tests/test_module_contracts.sh::test_awk_files_pass_lint`](../../tests/test_module_contracts.sh) with all `-v` args supplied; the test asserts zero warnings on empty input.
3. **Stays self-contained.** No `awk -e prelude.awk -f main.awk` chains. If a helper is shared, the duplication is acceptable for now (we have one file).
4. **Outputs a fixed format** documented in the file's header so the caller's parser can stay simple Aje28094Aj see `numeric_combined.awk`'s "Line 0: HISTOGRAM Aje280a6Aj" through "Line 8: TREND" comments.

## Testing

- [`tests/test_module_contracts.sh::test_awk_files_pass_lint`](../../tests/test_module_contracts.sh) gates lint cleanliness.
- The behavioural correctness of `numeric_combined.awk` is covered by the pre-existing 81-test [`tests/test_correctness.sh`](../../tests/test_correctness.sh) and the broader 327-test suite Aje28094Aj the ENV-123 extract is a pure move, so any behaviour change would surface there.
- Performance: [`tests/bench_large_dataset.sh`](../../tests/bench_large_dataset.sh) (10k rows, ENV-024 threshold 10 s) measures end-to-end. The post-extract baseline is ~4.4 s Aje28094Aj same envelope as pre-extract.
===END===

# numeric_combined.awk Aje28094Aj single-pass per-column numeric analysis.
#
# Computes nine analyses in one pass over the input file: histogram,
# sparkline, mode, precision, Benford's Law, monotonicity, bimodality,
# z-score outliers, and Spearman trend. Emits nine fixed-order lines on
# stdout which `_numeric.sh`'s `run_numeric_analyses` parses into the
# final report items.
#
# Extracted from an inline bash heredoc in ENV-123 (2026-04-24). No
# behaviour change Aje28094Aj the awk body is byte-identical; only the quoting
# / interpolation wrapper moved out. Bash dynamic values reach this
# program exclusively through `-v` flags:
#
#   -v col           1-based column index
#   -v mn,mx         min, max from the summary stats phase
#   -v mean,std      mean, stddev from the summary stats phase
#   -v skip          sparkline sampling stride (rows per sample)
#   -v maxn          sparkline max samples ($SPARK_SAMPLES)
#   -v tmpfile       path to write numeric values for percentile sort
#   -v benford_crit  chi-square critical value ($BENFORD_CRIT)
#
# The delimiter (`-F"$delim"`) and input file path are supplied by the
# invoking bash wrapper, as is the output destination (stdout).

function trim(t){ gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", t); return t }
function isnum(x){ return (x ~ /^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$/) }

# Initialise everything the END block touches so `awk -W lint -f Aje280a6Aj </dev/null`
# is silent. Awk would happily treat these as 0/"" anyway, but explicit init
# documents intent and lets gawk's lint pass on empty input.
BEGIN {
    # Initialise everything the END block touches so gawk's `--lint`
    # is silent on empty input. Awk would happily treat these as 0/""
    # anyway; explicit init documents intent and lets CI run lint as
    # part of the structural test (see tests/test_module_contracts.sh).
    n = 0; row = 0; num_row = 0; spark = ""; spark_n = 0
    prev_vn = 0
    prec_total = 0; prec_integer = 0; prec_decimal = 0
    prec_maxdp = 0; prec_sumdp = 0
    benford_total = 0
    mono_asc = 0; mono_desc = 0; mono_eq = 0
    zcount = 0
    # Histogram and bimodality bins (5 + 10 fixed indices).
    for (_i = 0; _i < 5; _i++) hcount[_i] = 0
    for (_i = 0; _i < 10; _i++) bcount[_i] = 0
    # Benford's first-significant-digit buckets.
    for (_i = 1; _i <= 9; _i++) benford[_i] = 0
    # Declare mode_count as an array so the END-block `for (k in
    # mode_count)` doesn't trip gawk's "for loop on untyped variable"
    # lint when there is no data to populate it.
    mode_count["__init"] = 0; delete mode_count["__init"]
}

NR==1{next}
{
    row++
    v=trim($col)
    is_num=isnum(v)

    # Sparkline sampling (uses numeric-row count for even spacing)
    if(is_num && num_row++ % skip == 0 && spark_n < maxn){
        vn_s=v+0
        if(mx==mn) sidx=4
        else sidx=int((vn_s-mn)/(mx-mn)*7)
        if(sidx<0) sidx=0; if(sidx>7) sidx=7
        spark = spark substr(" .:-=+*#", sidx+1, 1)
        spark_n++
    }

    if(!is_num) next
    vn=v+0
    n++

    # Value extraction for percentile sorting
    print vn > tmpfile

    # Trend: store values and row indices for Spearman
    tval[n]=vn; trow[n]=row

    # Histogram (5 bins)
    if(mn!=mx){
        hidx=int((vn-mn)/(mx-mn)*5)
        if(hidx>=5) hidx=4
        hcount[hidx]++
    }

    # Mode (count occurrences)
    mode_count[v]++

    # Precision
    prec_total++
    if(v ~ /\./){
        prec_decimal++
        split(v, dp_parts, ".")
        dp=length(dp_parts[2])
        if(dp>prec_maxdp) prec_maxdp=dp
        prec_sumdp+=dp
    } else {
        prec_integer++
    }

    # Benford (first significant digit)
    if(vn!=0){
        s=v; gsub(/^-/, "", s); gsub(/^0+\./, "0.", s)
        for(k=1;k<=length(s);k++){
            ch=substr(s,k,1)
            if(ch>="1" && ch<="9"){benford[ch+0]++; benford_total++; break}
        }
    }

    # Monotonicity
    if(n>1){
        if(vn>prev_vn) mono_asc++
        else if(vn<prev_vn) mono_desc++
        else mono_eq++
    }
    prev_vn=vn

    # Bimodality (10 bins)
    if(mn!=mx){
        bidx=int((vn-mn)/(mx-mn)*10)
        if(bidx>=10) bidx=9
        bcount[bidx]++
    }

    # Z-score outliers
    if(std+0>0){
        z=(vn-mean)/std
        if(z<-3 || z>3){
            zcount++
            if(zcount<=5) zvals[zcount]=vn
        }
    }
}
END{
    ## Line 0: HISTOGRAM (semicolon-separated bins, each pipe-delimited)
    if(mn!=mx){
        for(i=0;i<5;i++){
            bstart=mn + (mx-mn)/5*i
            bend=bstart + (mx-mn)/5
            if(i>0) printf ";"
            printf "%d|%.4f|%.4f|%d", i+1, bstart, bend, hcount[i]+0
        }
    }
    printf "\n"

    ## Line 1: SPARKLINE
    printf "%s\n", spark

    ## Line 2: MODE (pipe-separated: val|count|unique)
    maxc=0; uniq=0
    for(k in mode_count){
        uniq++
        if(mode_count[k]>maxc){maxc=mode_count[k]; maxv=k}
    }
    printf "%s|%d|%d\n", (maxc>0? maxv : "n/a"), maxc, uniq

    ## Line 3: PRECISION (pipe-separated: total|int|dec|maxdp|avgdp)
    printf "%d|%d|%d|%d|%.1f\n", prec_total, prec_integer+0, prec_decimal+0, prec_maxdp+0, (prec_decimal>0? prec_sumdp/prec_decimal : 0)

    ## Line 4: BENFORD (original pipe-separated format)
    if(benford_total<20){
        printf "INSUFFICIENT\n"
    } else {
        split("30.1 17.6 12.5 9.7 7.9 6.7 5.8 5.1 4.6", expected, " ")
        chi2=0
        for(d=1;d<=9;d++){
            obs=(benford[d]+0)/benford_total*100
            exv=expected[d]+0
            chi2 += (obs-exv)*(obs-exv)/exv
            printf "%d:%.1f:%.1f|", d, obs, exv
        }
        if(chi2<benford_crit) printf "PASS|%.2f\n", chi2
        else printf "FAIL|%.2f\n", chi2
    }

    ## Line 5: MONOTONICITY (pipe-separated: n|asc|desc|eq|pairs)
    pairs=n-1
    if(n<2) printf "NA|0|0|0|0\n"
    else printf "%d|%d|%d|%d|%d\n", n, mono_asc+0, mono_desc+0, mono_eq+0, pairs

    ## Line 6: BIMODALITY (pipe-separated: flag|peaks|h1|h2)
    if(n>=10 && mn!=mx){
        np=0
        for(i=0;i<10;i++){
            c=bcount[i]+0
            prev_c=(i>0? bcount[i-1]+0 : 0)
            next_c=(i<9? bcount[i+1]+0 : 0)
            min_peak = n * 0.005
            if(min_peak < 1) min_peak = 1
            if(c >= min_peak && c >= prev_c && c >= next_c && (c > prev_c || c > next_c)){
                np++
                peaks[np]=i; peakh[np]=c
            }
        }
        if(np>=2){
            p1=1; p2=2
            if(peakh[2]>peakh[1]){p1=2; p2=1}
            for(k=3;k<=np;k++){
                if(peakh[k]>peakh[p1]){p2=p1; p1=k}
                else if(peakh[k]>peakh[p2]) p2=k
            }
            lo=peaks[p1]; hi=peaks[p2]
            if(lo>hi){tmp=lo; lo=hi; hi=tmp}
            valley=peakh[p1]
            for(i=lo+1;i<hi;i++){
                if(bcount[i]+0 < valley) valley=bcount[i]+0
            }
            thresh=(peakh[p1]<peakh[p2]? peakh[p1] : peakh[p2]) * 0.5
            if(valley < thresh) printf "YES|%d|%d|%d\n", np, peakh[p1], peakh[p2]
            else printf "NO|%d|0|0\n", np
        } else {
            printf "NO|%d|0|0\n", np
        }
    } else {
        printf "NO|0|0|0\n"
    }

    ## Line 7: Z-SCORE OUTLIERS (pipe-separated: count|v1, v2, ...)
    printf "%d", zcount+0
    if(zcount>0){
        printf "|"
        for(i=1;i<=zcount && i<=5;i++) printf "%s%s", zvals[i], (i<zcount && i<5?", ":"")
    }
    printf "\n"

    ## Line 8: TREND (Spearman rank correlation)
    if(n<3){
        printf "NA\n"
    } else {
        # Shell sort to compute ranks (O(n^3/2) vs O(n^2) bubble)
        for(i=1;i<=n;i++) order[i]=i
        h=1; while(h<n) h=3*h+1
        while(h>1){
            h=int(h/3)
            for(i=h+1;i<=n;i++){
                tmp=order[i]; j=i
                while(j>h && tval[order[j-h]]>tval[tmp]){
                    order[j]=order[j-h]; j-=h
                }
                order[j]=tmp
            }
        }
        for(i=1;i<=n;i++) rank[order[i]]=i
        # Handle ties
        i=1
        while(i<=n){
            j=i
            while(j<=n && tval[order[j]]==tval[order[i]]) j++
            avg=(i+j-1)/2.0
            for(k=i;k<j;k++) rank[order[k]]=avg
            i=j
        }
        # Spearman correlation
        for(i=1;i<=n;i++){sr+=rank[i]; srr+=trow[i]}
        mr=sr/n; mrr=srr/n
        for(i=1;i<=n;i++){
            d1=rank[i]-mr; d2=trow[i]-mrr
            cov+=d1*d2; v1+=d1*d1; v2+=d2*d2
        }
        if(v1>0 && v2>0) printf "%.6f\n", cov/sqrt(v1*v2)
        else printf "NA\n"
    }
}

# Handoff Aje28094Aj EnvoyAnalyze/profiles

Storage directory for saved envoy-analyze selection profiles. Profiles are created with `--save NAME` and loaded with `--profile NAME`.

## Format

Each profile is a plain text `.profile` file containing a comma-delimited list of analysis item numbers (e.g., `1,2,3,5,9`).

## Notes

# Handoff Aje28094Aj EnvoyAnalyze/samples

## Overview

Sample CSV datasets for testing and demonstrating envoy-analyze and envoy-browse.

## Files

- `trees.csv` Aje28094Aj R "trees" dataset (31 rows, 4 numeric columns: Index, Girth, Height, Volume)
- `anscombe.csv` Aje28094Aj Anscombe's quartet (categorical "data" column + numeric x/y)
- `biostats.csv` Aje28094Aj Small biostats sample (mixed categorical + numeric: Name, Sex, Age, Height, Weight)
- `edge.csv` Aje28094Aj Synthetic edge cases (5 rows: zero-variance column, missing values)
- `known.csv` Aje28094Aj Known-answer dataset (x=1..10, y=10x, constant=5) for correctness tests
- `missing.csv` Aje28094Aj Missing value edge cases (10 rows, 4 cols; all 12 missing forms: empty, NaN, null, None, NULL, NA, N/A, #N/A, nan, none, `-`, `.`)
- `numeric_edge.csv` Aje28094Aj Numeric edge cases (5 rows: x, neg=-x, sci=10x scientific, big=1Mx); hand-calculated: mean(x)=3, corr(x,neg)=-1, corr(x,sci)=1
- `bimodal.csv` Aje28094Aj Distribution tests (20 rows: bimodal column with two clusters, skewed column, Benford-distributed column)
- `quoted.csv` Aje28094Aj RFC 4180 CSV quoting (embedded commas, escaped quotes, embedded newlines, empty quoted fields)
- `large_vals.csv` Aje28094Aj Welford's algorithm verification (10 rows near 1e9 with small variance; proves naive formula fails)
- `known_benford.csv` Aje28094Aj 200 rows; `benford` column drawn log-uniform (chiAjc2b2Aj = 2.68, PASS) and `uniform` column drawn uniform (chiAjc2b2Aj = 51.02, FAIL). Used by `test_known_values_extended.sh` (ENV-124).
- `known_categorical.csv` Aje28094Aj 60 rows, three categorical columns. Hand-computed Cramer's V(device, os) = 0.7643; sparse cells trip the expected-frequency-<5 warning. (ENV-124)
- `known_spearman.csv` Aje28094Aj 15 rows. `x` strict ascending, `y = xAjc2b2Aj`, `z = -x`, `noisy` = `x` with one adjacent-pair swap. Spearman Ajcf81Aj values: x = +1.0, z = -1.0, noisy = 0.996429 (pins tie-handling). (ENV-124)
- `known_bimodal_seeded.csv` Aje28094Aj 50 rows, two well-separated clusters (~10 / ~90). Detector reports YES with peak heights 24, 22. (ENV-124)

## Notes

- All files have a header row as required by envoy-analyze
- `edge.csv` is used for regression tests (correlation bounds, zero-variance, missingness)
- `known.csv` is used by `test_correctness.sh` for exact value verification
- `missing.csv`, `numeric_edge.csv`, `bimodal.csv`, `quoted.csv`, `large_vals.csv` added in v0.7

# EnvoyAnalyze/schemas/ HANDOFF

## Purpose
Machine-readable JSON Schema definitions describing the stable `--json` output contract for EnvoyAnalyze commands (ENV-064).

## Contents
- `envoy-analyze-output.json` Aje28094Aj JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for every `--json` payload emitted by `envoy-analyze`. The human-readable companion lives at `../docs/json-schema.md`.

## Usage
Consumers can validate piped output against this schema, e.g.:

```
envoy-analyze --json ... | jq . | ajv validate -s schemas/envoy-analyze-output.json
```

## Stability
This schema is part of the v1.0 stability contract (tracked by ENV-097). Breaking changes require a major bump in the suite version per the versioning policy (ENV-096).
===END===

# Handoff Aje28094Aj EnvoyAnalyze/tests

- 2026-06-15: Extended dashboard alias smoke coverage to assert `envoy-browse --help` documents `--title`.
- 2026-06-15: Added `test_dashboard_alias.sh` smoke coverage for the new dashboard alias.
## Overview

Test suite for EnvoyAnalyze (envoy-analyze + envoy-browse). Uses a shared bash test harness (`helpers.sh`) with `run_test`, `assert_contains`, `assert_not_contains`, `assert_exit_zero`, and `print_summary`.

## Structure

- `helpers.sh` Aje28094Aj shared harness, defines `run_mda()`, color output, counters
- `test_mda.sh` Aje28094Aj 31 tests for envoy-analyze (correlations, filters, shape, matrix alignment, version, CV, normality, precision, Benford, trend, regression, quality score, PCA, monotonicity, suggested drops, formats, profiles, delimiter, stdin)
- `test_mdx.sh` Aje28094Aj 18 tests for envoy-browse (help output, key docs, no-input rejection, bad-flag, --all, --debug, TUI edge cases, unit tests)
- `test_correctness.sh` Aje28094Aj 81 known-answer tests across 8 datasets
- `test_csv_parsing.sh` Aje28094Aj 11 CSV preprocessing tests (BOM, quoting, embedded newlines)
- `test_performance.sh` Aje28094Aj 3 performance regression tests (1K/5K rows, wide datasets)
- `test_diverse_data.sh` Aje28094Aj 17 tests (negative numbers, scientific notation, missing values, large datasets)
- `run_tests.sh` Aje28094Aj runner, executes all `test_*.sh` files with `bash` explicitly

## Running

```bash
bash run_tests.sh          # run all tests
bash test_mda.sh           # run envoy-analyze tests only
bash test_mdx.sh           # run envoy-browse tests only
```

## Notes

- Test files must have execute permission (`chmod +x`) to be picked up by `run_tests.sh`
- envoy-browse tests are limited to non-interactive checks (help, exit codes) since the TUI requires a TTY

===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/_compute_known_truths.py===
===META: mode=644 sha256=d8282033c61de6b41959142d7a4d1816e2ae03130e80b3bf106f5f70f36dd600===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate synthetic datasets and the hand-calculated answers that
``test_known_values_extended.sh`` asserts against (ENV-124).

Usage::

    python3 tests/_compute_known_truths.py --emit samples
    python3 tests/_compute_known_truths.py --print

The first form (re)generates the CSV samples under ``samples/``; the second
prints the truth table the test references. Both modes are deterministic
(seeded), so the next person can verify or regenerate without asking what
the expected values "ought to be".
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
import random
import statistics
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SAMPLES = ROOT / "samples"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Datasets

def _benford_value(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    """Draw a single Benford-distributed positive integer.

    P(first digit = d) = log10(1 + 1/d). We sample uniformly in log space
    over a couple of orders of magnitude and round to an integer; that
    yields the Benford distribution exactly.
    """
    return int(round(10 ** (rng.uniform(0, 4))))


def make_benford(seed: int = 1) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """200 rows. ``benford`` column drawn from log-uniform Aje28692Aj first digits
    follow Benford. ``uniform`` column drawn from uniform(1, 1000) Aje28692Aj first
    digits do NOT follow Benford. Truth table records the exact chi-square
    statistic for each."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rows = []
    for _ in range(200):
        b = _benford_value(rng)
        u = rng.randint(1, 9999)
        rows.append({"benford": b, "uniform": u})

    expected = [30.1, 17.6, 12.5, 9.7, 7.9, 6.7, 5.8, 5.1, 4.6]

    def chi2(values: list[int]) -> float:
        nonzero = [v for v in values if v != 0]
        first = [int(str(abs(v)).lstrip("0").lstrip(".")[0]) for v in nonzero
                 if str(abs(v)).lstrip("0").lstrip(".")]
        first = [d for d in first if 1 <= d <= 9]
        n = len(first)
        if n < 20:
            return -1.0
        counts = Counter(first)
        s = 0.0
        for d in range(1, 10):
            obs = counts.get(d, 0) / n * 100
            ex = expected[d - 1]
            s += (obs - ex) ** 2 / ex
        return s

    truth = {
        "benford_chi2": round(chi2([r["benford"] for r in rows]), 2),
        "uniform_chi2": round(chi2([r["uniform"] for r in rows]), 2),
    }
    return rows, truth


def make_categorical(seed: int = 2) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """60 rows. ``device`` and ``os`` are correlated (phoneAje28694AjiOS/Android,
    laptopAje28694AjmacOS/Linux/Windows). ``country`` is low-cardinality (3 values)
    so its Cramer's V vs ``device`` is small but computable, and the
    expected-frequency warning fires if the cell count is too low."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rows = []
    cells = [
        ("phone", "iOS", 12),
        ("phone", "Android", 14),
        ("laptop", "macOS", 8),
        ("laptop", "Linux", 9),
        ("laptop", "Windows", 11),
        ("phone", "Linux", 1),
        ("phone", "Windows", 2),
        ("laptop", "iOS", 1),
        ("laptop", "Android", 2),
    ]
    countries = ["US", "UK", "DE"]
    for d, o, n in cells:
        for _ in range(n):
            rows.append({"device": d, "os": o,
                         "country": rng.choice(countries)})
    rng.shuffle(rows)

    # Cramer's V for device vs os (hand calc).
    contingency: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = Counter()
    for r in rows:
        contingency[(r["device"], r["os"])] += 1
    devices = sorted({r["device"] for r in rows})
    oses = sorted({r["os"] for r in rows})
    n = len(rows)
    row_totals = {d: sum(contingency[(d, o)] for o in oses) for d in devices}
    col_totals = {o: sum(contingency[(d, o)] for d in devices) for o in oses}
    # Match envoy-analyze's awk (lib/_categorical.sh::run_cramers_v): only
    # iterate observed-cell combinations (`for key in joint`), not all
    # row*col combinations. Zero-observation cells are skipped on both
    # sides Aje28094Aj keeps the truth table aligned with what the tool reports.
    chi2 = 0.0
    for (d, o), obs in contingency.items():
        exp = row_totals[d] * col_totals[o] / n
        if exp > 0:
            chi2 += (obs - exp) ** 2 / exp
    k = min(len(devices), len(oses)) - 1
    cramers_v = math.sqrt(chi2 / (n * k))

    truth = {
        "n": n,
        "cramers_v_device_os": round(cramers_v, 4),
        "device_unique": len(devices),
        "os_unique": len(oses),
        "country_unique": 3,
    }
    return rows, truth


def make_spearman(seed: int = 3) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """15 rows. ``x`` increasing, ``y`` is x squared with a small noise
    floor Aje28094Aj pure-monotonic so Spearman Ajcf81Aj is exactly 1.0 by ranks. ``z`` is
    the negative monotonic of x Aje28692Aj Ajcf81Aj = -1.0. ``noisy`` is x with a single
    rank inversion swapped in to give a known partial Ajcf81Aj."""
    xs = list(range(1, 16))
    ys = [v * v for v in xs]
    zs = [-v for v in xs]
    noisy = list(xs)
    # Single adjacent swap at positions 7,8 (0-indexed): values 8 and 9
    # become 9 and 8. Spearman Ajcf81Aj for n=15 with one adjacent inversion:
    # sum d_i^2 = 1+1 = 2 Aje28692Aj Ajcf81Aj = 1 - 6*2 / (15 * (15^2 - 1)) = 1 - 12/3360
    # = 1 - 0.0035714... = 0.996429.
    noisy[7], noisy[8] = noisy[8], noisy[7]
    rows = [{"x": x, "y": y, "z": z, "noisy": n}
            for x, y, z, n in zip(xs, ys, zs, noisy)]
    truth = {
        "spearman_x_y": 1.000000,
        "spearman_x_z": -1.000000,
        "spearman_x_noisy": round(1 - 6 * 2 / (15 * (15**2 - 1)), 6),
    }
    return rows, truth


def make_bimodal_seeded(seed: int = 4) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """50 rows drawn from two well-separated normal-ish clusters: 25 rows
    near 10 (peak A), 25 rows near 90 (peak B). Designed so the bimodality
    detector's 10-bin histogram puts A in bin 0-1 and B in bin 8-9 with a
    clean valley near 0 in the middle bins."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rows = []
    for _ in range(25):
        rows.append({"v": round(rng.gauss(10, 3), 2)})
    for _ in range(25):
        rows.append({"v": round(rng.gauss(90, 3), 2)})
    rng.shuffle(rows)
    values = [r["v"] for r in rows]
    truth = {
        "n": len(values),
        "min": round(min(values), 2),
        "max": round(max(values), 2),
        "expect_bimodal": True,
    }
    return rows, truth


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Emit / print

def _write_csv(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    if not rows:
        path.write_text("")
        return
    cols = list(rows[0].keys())
    lines = [",".join(cols)]
    for r in rows:
        lines.append(",".join(str(r[c]) for c in cols))
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


GENERATORS = {
    "known_benford.csv": make_benford,
    "known_categorical.csv": make_categorical,
    "known_spearman.csv": make_spearman,
    "known_bimodal_seeded.csv": make_bimodal_seeded,
}


def cmd_emit(target: Path) -> None:
    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for filename, gen in GENERATORS.items():
        rows, truth = gen()
        _write_csv(target / filename, rows)
        print(f"wrote {target / filename}: {len(rows)} rows; truth={truth}")


def cmd_print() -> None:
    for filename, gen in GENERATORS.items():
        _, truth = gen()
        print(f"{filename}:")
        for k, v in truth.items():
            print(f"    {k} = {v}")


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--emit", nargs="?", const=str(SAMPLES),
                        help="Write CSV samples (defaults to samples/)")
    parser.add_argument("--print", action="store_true",
                        help="Print the truth table the tests reference")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.emit:
        cmd_emit(Path(args.emit))
    elif args.print:
        cmd_print()
    else:
        parser.print_help()
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
===END===
===FILE: analyze/tests/bench_large_dataset.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=79359ebaa5a25b12a47f10d7eceb7cb2dd6c5751968fe7199e11b4a1528b1668===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Benchmark: envoy-analyze on large datasets (ENV-024)
##
## Generates a synthetic CSV with a mix of numeric, categorical, and sparse
## columns, then times a full --all analysis. Produces baselines that can
## back a regression test.
##
## Usage:
##   bash bench_large_dataset.sh                    # default: 10k + 100k
##   bash bench_large_dataset.sh --rows 10000       # single size
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
MDA_SCRIPT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/envoy-analyze"

SIZES=(10000 100000)
SEED=1337

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --rows) SIZES=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
        --seed) SEED="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

# Default regression thresholds (seconds)
BENCH_MAX_10K="${BENCH_MAX_10K:-10}"
BENCH_MAX_100K="${BENCH_MAX_100K:-60}"

# Generate a synthetic CSV.
# Columns: id (numeric, unique), region (categorical low card), score (numeric),
#          timestamp (numeric), label (categorical high card), note (sparse text)
gen_csv () {
    local rows="$1" path="$2" seed="$3"
    awk -v rows="$rows" -v seed="$seed" 'BEGIN{
        srand(seed)
        regions[0]="us-east"; regions[1]="us-west"; regions[2]="eu"; regions[3]="apac"
        printf "id,region,score,timestamp,label,note\n"
        for (i=1; i<=rows; i++){
            r=regions[int(rand()*4)]
            s=int(rand()*1000) + 1
            t=1700000000 + int(rand()*86400*365)
            lbl="lbl_" int(rand()*500)
            nt=""
            if (rand() < 0.20) nt="obs_" int(rand()*10000)
            printf "%d,%s,%d,%d,%s,%s\n", i, r, s, t, lbl, nt
        }
    }' > "$path"
}

echo "Large-dataset benchmark for envoy-analyze (ENV-024)"
echo "==================================================="
echo "Seed: $SEED"
echo ""

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t envanalyze_bench.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

any_over=0

for rows in "${SIZES[@]}"; do
    csv="$TMP/synth_${rows}.csv"
    echo "--- $rows rows ---"
    gen_t0=$(date +%s.%N)
    gen_csv "$rows" "$csv" "$SEED"
    gen_t1=$(date +%s.%N)
    gen_dur=$(awk -v a="$gen_t0" -v b="$gen_t1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", b-a}')
    bytes=$(wc -c <"$csv")
    echo "  generated ${bytes} bytes in ${gen_dur}s"

    # Measure wall time via bash builtin. Memory sampling is optional and
    # only runs if /usr/bin/time is available (not present in minimal containers).
    sec=""
    peak=""
    TIMEFORMAT='%R'
    if command -v /usr/bin/time >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        out_file="$TMP/time_${rows}.out"
        /usr/bin/time -v -o "$out_file" bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all "$csv" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        wall=$(awk -F': ' '/Elapsed \(wall clock\)/ {print $2}' "$out_file")
        peak=$(awk -F': ' '/Maximum resident set size/ {print $2}' "$out_file")
        sec=$(awk -v t="$wall" 'BEGIN{
            n = split(t, p, ":")
            if (n==2) { print p[1]*60 + p[2] }
            else if (n==3) { print p[1]*3600 + p[2]*60 + p[3] }
            else { print t }
        }')
    else
        sec=$({ time bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all "$csv" > /dev/null 2>&1 ; } 2>&1)
    fi

    if [[ -n "$sec" ]]; then
        echo "  analyze:      ${sec} s"
        [[ -n "$peak" ]] && echo "  peak RSS:     ${peak} KB"

        # Regression check
        local_threshold="$BENCH_MAX_10K"
        [[ "$rows" -ge 100000 ]] && local_threshold="$BENCH_MAX_100K"
        if awk -v v="$sec" -v t="$local_threshold" 'BEGIN{exit !(v>t)}'; then
            echo "  FAIL: analyze time ${sec}s exceeds threshold ${local_threshold}s"
            any_over=1
        else
            echo "  OK: under threshold ${local_threshold}s"
        fi
    else
        echo "  FAIL: could not measure analyze time"
        any_over=1
    fi
    echo ""
done

if [[ $any_over -eq 1 ]]; then
    exit 1
fi
echo "All size points under thresholds."
exit 0
===END===
===FILE: analyze/tests/helpers.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=dc402864e16174ed3521334744840bc311e6eddcfb3358a17e9d31c46e9d33a6===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Test Helpers for EnvoyAnalyze (envoy-analyze)
################################################################################

MDA_SCRIPT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/envoy-analyze"
SAMPLES_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/samples"

TESTS_RUN=0
TESTS_PASSED=0
TESTS_FAILED=0
FAILED_NAMES=()

if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    RED='\033[0;31m'
    YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
    NC='\033[0m'
else
    GREEN='' RED='' YELLOW='' NC=''
fi

assert_contains () {
    local haystack="$1"
    local needle="$2"
    local msg="${3:-output should contain string}"
    if [[ "$haystack" == *"$needle"* ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    looking for: '$needle'"
        echo "    in:          '$haystack'"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_not_contains () {
    local haystack="$1"
    local needle="$2"
    local msg="${3:-output should not contain string}"
    if [[ "$haystack" != *"$needle"* ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    should not find: '$needle'"
        echo "    in:              '$haystack'"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_exit_zero () {
    local code="$1"
    local msg="${2:-command should succeed (exit 0)}"
    if [[ "$code" -eq 0 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    exit code: $code"
        return 1
    fi
}

run_mda () {
    bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "$@"
}

run_test () {
    local description="$1"
    local func="$2"
    TESTS_RUN=$((TESTS_RUN + 1))

    # Capture the test subshell's exit code without triggering the
    # caller's `set -e`. Half of EnvoyAnalyze's test files top with
    # `set -euo pipefail`; a bare `( ... ); result=$?` would let
    # `set -e` fire on a failing subshell BEFORE `result=$?` runs,
    # aborting the entire run. Putting the subshell in an
    # `|| result=$?` list suppresses `set -e` for that step and
    # captures the real exit status. The default `result=0` covers
    # the success branch (where `||` short-circuits).
    local result=0
    ( set -e; "$func" ) || result=$?

    if [[ $result -eq 0 ]]; then
        TESTS_PASSED=$((TESTS_PASSED + 1))
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}PASS${NC}: $description"
    else
        TESTS_FAILED=$((TESTS_FAILED + 1))
        FAILED_NAMES+=("$description")
        echo -e "  ${RED}FAIL${NC}: $description (exit $result)"
    fi
}

print_summary () {
    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    echo "Results: $TESTS_PASSED/$TESTS_RUN passed, $TESTS_FAILED failed"
    if [[ $TESTS_FAILED -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Failed tests:${NC}"
        for name in "${FAILED_NAMES[@]}"; do
            echo "  - $name"
        done
        echo "========================================"
        return 1
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}All tests passed.${NC}"
        echo "========================================"
        return 0
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

    [[ -f "$test_file" ]] || continue

#!/bin/bash
# ENV-067: --benford-alpha flag selects chi-squared critical value
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

SAMPLE="$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv"

test_default_alpha () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --all "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || true
    # Body should mention the default alpha and critical value
    if [[ "$out" == *"Benford"* ]]; then
        assert_contains "$out" "alpha=0.05" "default Benford alpha should be 0.05"
        assert_contains "$out" "critical=15.507" "default critical should be 15.507"
    else
        # trees.csv has only 31 rows so Benford may hit INSUFFICIENT; try a larger sample
        return 0
    fi
}

test_alpha_001 () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --benford-alpha 0.01 --all "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || true
    if [[ "$out" == *"Benford"* ]]; then
        assert_contains "$out" "alpha=0.01" "alpha=0.01 should appear in body"
        assert_contains "$out" "critical=20.090" "alpha=0.01 => critical 20.090"
    else
        return 0
    fi
}

test_alpha_0001 () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --benford-alpha 0.001 --all "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || true
    if [[ "$out" == *"Benford"* ]]; then
        assert_contains "$out" "alpha=0.001" "alpha=0.001 should appear in body"
        assert_contains "$out" "critical=26.125" "alpha=0.001 => critical 26.125"
    else
        return 0
    fi
}

test_alpha_invalid () {
    local out code=0
    out=$(run_mda --benford-alpha 0.5 "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: invalid alpha should exit non-zero"; return 1; }
    assert_contains "$out" "--benford-alpha must be" "error message should list accepted values"
}

test_alpha_missing_arg () {
    local out code=0
    out=$(run_mda --benford-alpha 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: missing alpha should exit non-zero"; return 1; }
}

run_test "ENV-067 default alpha reports 0.05 / 15.507" test_default_alpha
run_test "ENV-067 --benford-alpha 0.01 maps to 20.090" test_alpha_001
run_test "ENV-067 --benford-alpha 0.001 maps to 26.125" test_alpha_0001
run_test "ENV-067 invalid alpha rejected with clear message" test_alpha_invalid
run_test "ENV-067 missing alpha value rejected" test_alpha_missing_arg

print_summary
===END===

#!/bin/bash
# ENV-065: ANSI colour in plain output with NO_COLOR and --color support
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

SAMPLE="$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv"

test_color_always_emits_escapes () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --color always --good "$SAMPLE")
    assert_contains "$out" $'\033[' "--color always should emit ANSI escapes"
}

test_color_never_strips_escapes () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --color never --good "$SAMPLE")
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\033['* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --color never must not emit ANSI escapes"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_no_color_env_wins () {
    # NO_COLOR overrides --color always
    local out
    out=$(NO_COLOR=1 run_mda --color always --good "$SAMPLE")
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\033['* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: NO_COLOR must override --color always"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_color_auto_pipe_is_monochrome () {
    # When stdout is a pipe (not a TTY), auto resolves to no colour
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --color auto --good "$SAMPLE" | cat)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\033['* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --color auto over pipe should be monochrome"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_json_never_has_ansi () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --color always --format json "$SAMPLE")
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\033['* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: JSON output must never contain ANSI escapes"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_csv_never_has_ansi () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --color always --format csv "$SAMPLE")
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\033['* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: CSV output must never contain ANSI escapes"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_color_invalid () {
    local out code=0
    out=$(run_mda --color sometimes "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: invalid --color value must error"; return 1; }
    assert_contains "$out" "--color must be" "error message should list accepted values"
}

run_test "ENV-065 --color always emits ANSI" test_color_always_emits_escapes
run_test "ENV-065 --color never strips ANSI" test_color_never_strips_escapes
run_test "ENV-065 NO_COLOR overrides --color always" test_no_color_env_wins
run_test "ENV-065 auto over pipe is monochrome" test_color_auto_pipe_is_monochrome
run_test "ENV-065 JSON never has ANSI" test_json_never_has_ansi
run_test "ENV-065 CSV never has ANSI" test_csv_never_has_ansi
run_test "ENV-065 invalid --color value rejected" test_color_invalid

print_summary
===END===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: --numeric-columns / --categorical-columns (ENV-025)
##           --missing-values (ENV-026)
##           --threshold AND/OR composition (ENV-027)
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "=== Column Overrides / Missing Values / Threshold Composition ==="

TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
_FIXTURE="$TMPDIR/env025_fixture.csv"

_write_fixture () {
    cat > "$_FIXTURE" <<'EOF'
zip_code,age,status
90210,25,active
10001,32,UNKNOWN
78701,NA,inactive
60601,45,active
30303,28,active
EOF
}

# ENV-025 ---------------------------------------------------------------

test_numeric_columns_override () {
    _write_fixture
    local out
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all --numeric-columns age "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "age: numeric" "age should still be numeric"
}

test_categorical_columns_forces_categorical () {
    _write_fixture
    local out
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all --categorical-columns zip_code "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "zip_code: categorical (forced" "zip_code should be forced categorical"
}

test_numeric_columns_unknown_errors () {
    _write_fixture
    local out code=0
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --numeric-columns nonexistent "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ "$code" -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: unknown column should fail"; return 1; }
    assert_contains "$out" "unknown column" "should report unknown column"
}

test_numeric_and_categorical_overlap_errors () {
    _write_fixture
    local out code=0
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --numeric-columns age --categorical-columns age "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ "$code" -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: overlap should fail"; return 1; }
    assert_contains "$out" "cannot appear in both" "should reject overlapping column"
}

test_override_case_insensitive () {
    _write_fixture
    local out
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all --categorical-columns ZIP_CODE "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "zip_code: categorical (forced" "match should be case-insensitive"
}

# ENV-026 ---------------------------------------------------------------

test_missing_values_custom_list () {
    _write_fixture
    local out
    # "UNKNOWN" and "inactive" together account for 2 rows of `status`.
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all --missing-values "UNKNOWN,inactive" "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "status: 2 missing" "should treat UNKNOWN and inactive as missing"
}

test_missing_values_case_insensitive () {
    _write_fixture
    local out
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all --missing-values "unknown" --missing-values-case-insensitive "$_FIXTURE" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "status: 1 missing" "case-insensitive should match UNKNOWN"
}

test_missing_empty_always_missing () {
    # Even with a custom list, empty string must still count as missing.
    local fix="$TMPDIR/env026_empty.csv"
    cat > "$fix" <<'EOF'
a,b
1,X
,X
EOF
    local out
    out=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --all --missing-values "zzz" "$fix" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "a: 1 missing" "empty string should remain missing"
    rm -f "$fix"
}

===FILE: analyze/tests/test_completions.sh===

#!/bin/bash
# ENV-062: bash completions syntax + basic behaviour
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

COMPDIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/completions"
ENVOY_ANALYZE_COMP="$COMPDIR/envoy-analyze.bash"
ENVOY_BROWSE_COMP="$COMPDIR/envoy-browse.bash"

test_envoy_analyze_syntax () {
    bash -n "$ENVOY_ANALYZE_COMP" || {
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: envoy-analyze.bash fails syntax check"
        return 1
    }
}

test_envoy_browse_syntax () {
    bash -n "$ENVOY_BROWSE_COMP" || {
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: envoy-browse.bash fails syntax check"
        return 1
    }
}

# Drive the completion function in a subshell and capture COMPREPLY.
_run_completion () {
    local script="$1"
    local -a words=( "${@:2}" )
    local cword=$(( ${#words[@]} - 1 ))
    bash -c '
        source "$1"
        shift
        COMP_WORDS=("$@")
        COMP_CWORD=$(( $# - 1 ))
        # Call the right handler based on the command name
        case "${COMP_WORDS[0]}" in
            envoy-analyze) _envoy_analyze_complete ;;
            envoy-browse)  _envoy_browse_complete ;;
        esac
        printf "%s\n" "${COMPREPLY[@]}"
    ' _comp "$script" "${words[@]}"
}

test_envoy_analyze_flag_completion () {
    local out
    out=$(_run_completion "$ENVOY_ANALYZE_COMP" envoy-analyze --)
    assert_contains "$out" "--format" "completion should include --format"
    assert_contains "$out" "--help" "completion should include --help"
    assert_contains "$out" "--head" "completion should include --head (ENV-063)"
    assert_contains "$out" "--color" "completion should include --color (ENV-065)"
    assert_contains "$out" "--benford-alpha" "completion should include --benford-alpha (ENV-067)"
}

test_envoy_analyze_format_values () {
    local out
    out=$(_run_completion "$ENVOY_ANALYZE_COMP" envoy-analyze --format "")
    assert_contains "$out" "plain" "--format should offer plain"
    assert_contains "$out" "json" "--format should offer json"
    assert_contains "$out" "html" "--format should offer html"
}

test_envoy_analyze_color_values () {
    local out
    out=$(_run_completion "$ENVOY_ANALYZE_COMP" envoy-analyze --color "")
    assert_contains "$out" "auto" "--color should offer auto"
    assert_contains "$out" "always" "--color should offer always"
    assert_contains "$out" "never" "--color should offer never"
}

test_envoy_browse_flag_completion () {
    local out
    out=$(_run_completion "$ENVOY_BROWSE_COMP" envoy-browse --)
    assert_contains "$out" "--all" "envoy-browse completion should include --all"
    assert_contains "$out" "--no-timeout" "envoy-browse completion should include --no-timeout"
}

run_test "ENV-062 envoy-analyze.bash passes bash -n" test_envoy_analyze_syntax
run_test "ENV-062 envoy-browse.bash passes bash -n" test_envoy_browse_syntax
run_test "ENV-062 envoy-analyze flag list includes new flags" test_envoy_analyze_flag_completion
run_test "ENV-062 --format offers enumerated values" test_envoy_analyze_format_values
run_test "ENV-062 --color offers enumerated values" test_envoy_analyze_color_values
run_test "ENV-062 envoy-browse flag list" test_envoy_browse_flag_completion

print_summary
===END===

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=helpers.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

################################################################################
## Known-answer numerical correctness tests
##
## Uses samples/known.csv:
##   x = 1,2,...,10  (uniform integers)
##   y = 10,20,...,100  (y = 10x, perfect linear)
##   constant = 5,5,...,5  (zero variance)
##
## Hand-calculated expected values:
##   x: mean=5.500000, std=2.872281, skew=0.000000, min=1, max=10
##   y: mean=55.000000, std=28.722813, min=10, max=100
##   corr(x,y) = 1.0000
##   regression: y = 10.0*x + 0.0  (RAjc2b2Aj=1.0000)
##   x percentiles: P05=1.4500, Q1=3.2500, P50=5.5000, Q3=7.7500, P95=9.5500
##   x: perfectly sorted ascending
##   constant: zero-variance, std=0
################################################################################

test_mean_exact () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds summary "$SAMPLES_DIR/known.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "Mean: 5.500000" "x mean should be 5.500000"
    assert_contains "$output" "Mean: 55.000000" "y mean should be 55.000000"
}

test_histogram_bin_sum () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds histogram "$SAMPLES_DIR/known.csv")
    # All 10 values of x should be distributed across the 5 bins, summing to 10
    local total=0
    while read -r line; do
        local count
        count=$(echo "$line" | sed 's/.*: //' | awk '{print $1}')
        if [[ "$count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            total=$((total + count))
        fi
    done < <(echo "$output" | grep "Bin.*Histogram: x" -A5 | grep "^Bin")
    # Alternative: get histogram for x specifically
    local hist_x
    hist_x=$(echo "$output" | sed -n '/Histogram: x/,/^[0-9]*\./p' | head -6)
    local bin_sum=0
    while read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == Bin* ]]; then
            local c
            c=$(echo "$line" | sed 's/.*): //' | awk '{print $1}')
            bin_sum=$((bin_sum + c))
        fi
    done <<< "$hist_x"
    if [[ "$bin_sum" -ne 10 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: histogram bins for x should sum to 10, got $bin_sum"
        return 1
    fi
}

    local output

    # CV = std/|mean| * 100 = 2.8723/5.5 * 100 Aje28988Aj 52.22%

test_positive_skewness () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds shape "$SAMPLES_DIR/bimodal.csv" 2>&1)
    local skew
    skew=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: skewed" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    if [[ -z "$skew" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: could not extract skewness for skewed column"
        return 1
    fi
    # The skewed column has heavy right tail, skewness should be positive
    local positive
    positive=$(awk -v s="$skew" 'BEGIN{print (s>0)? "yes" : "no"}')
    if [[ "$positive" != "yes" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: skewed column should have positive skewness, got $skew"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_pipe_delimiter_detection () {

    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-pipe.XXXXXX)
    printf 'a|b|c\n1|2|3\n4|5|6\n' > "$tmp"
    local output
    output=$(run_mda "$tmp")
    assert_contains "$output" "Delimiter: |" "pipe delimiter should be detected"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

################################################################################
## Deep correctness tests Aje28094Aj exact values across all datasets
##
## These tests verify that computed statistical values are numerically correct,
## not just that the output contains certain keywords.
################################################################################

# --- missing.csv: statistics computed with missing values excluded ---
# value column non-missing: {100, 200, 300, 1200, -50} (5 of 10 rows)
#   mean = 1750/5 = 350, pop_std = sqrt(970000/5) = 440.454311

    assert_contains "$shape_val" "P75: 300.0000" "missing.csv value Q3 should be 300.0000"
}

test_missing_value_skewness () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds shape "$SAMPLES_DIR/missing.csv")
    local skew
    skew=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: value" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    # Right-skewed: {-50, 100, 200, 300, 1200} has positive skewness
    local positive
    positive=$(awk -v s="$skew" 'BEGIN{print (s>0)? "yes" : "no"}')
    if [[ "$positive" != "yes" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: missing.csv value column should have positive skewness, got $skew"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$output" "Skewness: 1.242859" "missing.csv value skewness should be 1.242859"
}

    assert_contains "$anomaly_val" "Outliers: 1" "missing.csv value should have 1 IQR outlier"
    assert_contains "$anomaly_val" "1200" "missing.csv value IQR outlier should be 1200"
}
