# --- bimodal.csv: distribution shape exactness ---

test_bimodal_skewed_skewness_exact () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds shape "$SAMPLES_DIR/bimodal.csv" 2>&1)
    local skew
    skew=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: skewed" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    # Fibonacci-like sequence: heavily right-tailed
    # Exact value from envoy-analyze: should be a large positive number
    if [[ -z "$skew" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: could not extract skewness for skewed column"
        return 1
    fi
    # Skewness should be > 1.0 (strongly right-skewed)
    local strong
    strong=$(awk -v s="$skew" 'BEGIN{print (s>1.0)? "yes" : "no"}')
    if [[ "$strong" != "yes" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: skewed column should have skewness > 1.0, got $skew"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_bimodal_symmetric_skewness () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds shape "$SAMPLES_DIR/bimodal.csv" 2>&1)
    local skew
    skew=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: bimodal" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    # bimodal column: {10,11,12,13,14,10,11,12,13,14,50,51,52,53,54,50,51,52,53,54}
    # Mean Aje28988Aj 32, positive skew due to gap
    if [[ -z "$skew" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: could not extract skewness for bimodal column"
        return 1
    fi
    # Skewness should be near 0 or slightly positive (two symmetric clusters)
    local bounded
    bounded=$(awk -v s="$skew" 'BEGIN{print (s>-1.0 && s<1.0)? "yes" : "no"}')
    if [[ "$bounded" != "yes" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: bimodal column skewness should be between -1 and 1, got $skew"
        return 1
    fi
}

# --- delimiter detection ---

test_semicolon_delimiter () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-semi.XXXXXX)
    printf 'a;b;c\n1;2;3\n4;5;6\n' > "$tmp"
    local output
    output=$(run_mda "$tmp")
    assert_contains "$output" "Delimiter: semicolon" "semicolon delimiter should be detected"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_tab_delimiter () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-tab.XXXXXX)
    printf 'a\tb\tc\n1\t2\t3\n4\t5\t6\n' > "$tmp"
    local output
    output=$(run_mda "$tmp")
    assert_contains "$output" "Delimiter: tab" "tab delimiter should be detected"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

===FILE: analyze/tests/test_csv_parsing.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=965556d81bde015ed64a923b303b19f78128b3bb3102782539fe5da456d878a0===
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=helpers.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

CSV_LIB="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/lib/_csv.sh"
cleanup_files=()  # required by _csv.sh

source "$CSV_LIB"

################################################################################
## CSV preprocessing tests
################################################################################

test_bom_stripping () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-bom.XXXXXX)
    cleanup_files+=("$tmp")
    # Write a file with BOM followed by "hello"
    printf '\xEF\xBB\xBFname,value\na,1\n' > "$tmp"
    strip_bom "$tmp"
    local result_file="$_STRIP_BOM_RESULT"
    local first3
    first3=$(head -c 3 "$result_file" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    if [[ "$first3" == "efbbbf" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: BOM should have been stripped"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        return 1
    fi
    # Original file should NOT be modified
    local orig_first3
    orig_first3=$(head -c 3 "$tmp" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    if [[ "$orig_first3" != "efbbbf" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: original file should not be modified"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$(cat "$result_file")" "name,value" "content should be intact after BOM strip"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_no_bom_passthrough () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-nobom.XXXXXX)
    cleanup_files+=("$tmp")
    printf 'name,value\na,1\n' > "$tmp"
    strip_bom "$tmp"
    # When no BOM, _STRIP_BOM_RESULT should point back to the original file
    if [[ "$_STRIP_BOM_RESULT" != "$tmp" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: no-BOM file should return original path, got $_STRIP_BOM_RESULT"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$(cat "$_STRIP_BOM_RESULT")" "name,value" "file without BOM should be unchanged"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_needs_csv_preprocess_yes () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf '"Smith, John",100\n' > "$tmp"
    if ! needs_csv_preprocess "$tmp"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: file with quotes should need preprocessing"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_needs_csv_preprocess_no () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf 'Smith,100\nJohn,200\n' > "$tmp"
    if needs_csv_preprocess "$tmp"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: file without quotes should not need preprocessing"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_csv_quoted_comma () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf 'name,value\n"Smith, John",100\n' > "$tmp"
    local result
    result=$(csv_to_tsv "$tmp" ",")
    assert_contains "$result" "Smith, John" "comma inside quotes should be preserved"
    assert_not_contains "$result" '"' "quotes should be stripped"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_csv_escaped_quotes () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf 'name,note\nAlice,"has ""quotes"""\n' > "$tmp"
    local result
    result=$(csv_to_tsv "$tmp" ",")
    assert_contains "$result" 'has "quotes"' "escaped quotes should become single quotes"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_csv_embedded_newline () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf 'name,note\nAlice,"line one\nline two"\n' > "$tmp"
    local result
    result=$(csv_to_tsv "$tmp" ",")
    # Embedded newline replaced with literal \n, so it fits in one TSV row
    local line_count
    line_count=$(echo "$result" | wc -l)
    if [[ "$line_count" -ne 2 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: embedded newline should produce 2 output lines (header + data), got $line_count"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_csv_empty_quoted_field () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf 'a,b\n"",value\n' > "$tmp"
    local result
    result=$(csv_to_tsv "$tmp" ",")
    # First field should be empty (just a tab before "value")
    local data_line
    data_line=$(echo "$result" | tail -1)
    if [[ "$data_line" != $'\t'"value" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: empty quoted field should produce empty string, got: '$data_line'"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_csv_mixed_quoting () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t test-csv.XXXXXX)
    printf 'a,b,c\nunquoted,"quoted, with comma",123\n' > "$tmp"
    local result
    result=$(csv_to_tsv "$tmp" ",")
    local data_line
    data_line=$(echo "$result" | tail -1)
    # Should have 3 tab-separated fields
    local field_count
    field_count=$(echo "$data_line" | awk -F'\t' '{print NF}')
    if [[ "$field_count" -ne 3 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: mixed quoting should produce 3 fields, got $field_count"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$data_line" "quoted, with comma" "quoted field with comma should be intact"
    rm -f "$tmp"
}

test_quoted_csv_full_pipeline () {
    # Run envoy-analyze on our quoted.csv sample and verify it parses correctly
    local output
    output=$(run_mda "$SAMPLES_DIR/quoted.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "Rows: 6" "quoted.csv should have 6 data rows"
    assert_contains "$output" "Columns: 4" "quoted.csv should have 4 columns"
    assert_contains "$output" "Delimiter: tab" "preprocessed CSV should use tab delimiter"
}

test_missing_expanded_forms () {
    # Run envoy-analyze on missing.csv and verify expanded missing detection
    local output
    output=$(run_mda "$SAMPLES_DIR/missing.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "value: 5 missing" "value column should have 5 missing (empty, NaN, null, NULL, .)"
    assert_contains "$output" "score: 5 missing" "score column should have 5 missing (empty, N/A, nan, none, -)"
}

########################################
## Run all CSV parsing tests
##

run_test "BOM stripping" test_bom_stripping
run_test "no-BOM passthrough" test_no_bom_passthrough
run_test "needs_csv_preprocess detects quotes" test_needs_csv_preprocess_yes
run_test "needs_csv_preprocess skips clean files" test_needs_csv_preprocess_no
run_test "CSV quoted comma preserved" test_csv_quoted_comma
run_test "CSV escaped quotes (\"\")" test_csv_escaped_quotes
run_test "CSV embedded newline" test_csv_embedded_newline
run_test "CSV empty quoted field" test_csv_empty_quoted_field
run_test "CSV mixed quoting" test_csv_mixed_quoting
run_test "quoted CSV full pipeline" test_quoted_csv_full_pipeline
run_test "expanded missing value forms" test_missing_expanded_forms

print_summary
===END===

create_negative_csv () {
    local f="$TMPDIR_TEST/negative.csv"
    cat > "$f" <<'EOF'
id,value,balance
1,-10.5,100
2,-20.3,-200
3,-5.7,50
4,-100.0,-500
5,-0.1,0
6,15.2,-75
7,-33.3,250
8,0,-1000
9,-99.9,999
10,-42.0,-42
EOF
    echo "$f"
}

create_scientific_csv () {
    local f="$TMPDIR_TEST/scientific.csv"
    cat > "$f" <<'EOF'
id,measurement,large_value,small_value
1,1.5e10,1e6,1.2e-3
2,2.3e10,2e6,3.4e-3
3,3.1e10,3e6,5.6e-3
4,4.7e10,4e6,7.8e-3
5,5.0e10,5e6,9.0e-3
6,6.2e10,6e6,1.1e-2
7,7.8e10,7e6,2.2e-2
8,8.4e10,8e6,3.3e-2
9,9.9e10,9e6,4.4e-2
10,1.0e11,1e7,5.5e-2
EOF
    echo "$f"
}

create_missing_csv () {
    local f="$TMPDIR_TEST/missing_vals.csv"
    cat > "$f" <<'EOF'
name,score,grade,notes
Alice,95,A,good
Bob,,B,
Charlie,87,A,excellent
,72,,needs work
Eve,NA,C,
Frank,91,A,great
Grace,,B,
Heidi,NaN,A,outstanding
Ivan,88,,
Judy,None,B,average
Kate,78,C,
Leo,#N/A,,
Mallory,65,D,poor
Nancy,-,B,
Oscar,.,A,
EOF
    echo "$f"
}

create_large_csv () {
    local f="$TMPDIR_TEST/large.csv"
    # Generate 150 rows programmatically
    echo "id,x,y,category" > "$f"
    local i=1
    while [ "$i" -le 150 ]; do
        # Simple deterministic values: x cycles, y = x*2 + noise, category alternates
        local x=$((i % 50 + 1))
        local y=$((x * 2 + (i % 7) - 3))
        local cat
        case $((i % 3)) in
            0) cat="alpha" ;;
            1) cat="beta" ;;
            2) cat="gamma" ;;
        esac
        echo "$i,$x,$y,$cat" >> "$f"
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    echo "$f"
}

===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/test_empty_input.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=4b670fb2615d279ef09b08854a2aa254954a674ab7b9697bb9805a189e4a27d0===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: empty / header-only stdin handling (ENV-129)
##
## Regression cover: before ENV-129, running `envoy-analyze < /dev/null`
## or any upstream pipeline that produced zero bytes crashed with
##   line 701: COL_NAMES[$((col_idx-1))]: unbound variable
## because the empty-stdin guard only fired when stdin was a TTY.
##
## The fix adds a post-header-read check: if COL_COUNT is 0 the input
## had no header, if ROW_COUNT is 0 the input had only a header. Both
## cases exit non-zero with a user-readable message that does NOT leak
## the internal "unbound variable" text.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "=== Empty-Input Handling (ENV-129) ==="

_check_empty_input () {
    local desc="$1" input="$2" expected_needle="$3"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(printf '%s' "$input" | bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $desc Aje28094Aj expected non-zero exit, got 0"
        echo "    output: $output"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$output" "$expected_needle" "$desc Aje28094Aj user-friendly message" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$output" "unbound variable" "$desc Aje28094Aj no 'unbound variable' leak" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$output" "COL_NAMES" "$desc Aje28094Aj no 'COL_NAMES' leak" || return 1
    return 0
}

test_empty_stdin_dev_null () {
    # envoy-analyze < /dev/null  Aje28094Aj the original ticket repro.
    local output rc=0
    output=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" < /dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: /dev/null stdin Aje28094Aj expected non-zero exit, got 0"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$output" "Input contained no data" "user-friendly message" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$output" "unbound variable" "no unbound-variable leak" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$output" "COL_NAMES" "no COL_NAMES leak" || return 1
}

test_empty_stdin_zero_bytes () {
    # Zero bytes on a pipe (`printf '' | envoy-analyze`).
    _check_empty_input "zero-byte pipe" "" "Input contained no data"
}

test_header_only_no_rows () {
    # Header line present, zero data rows. Previously rendered a bogus
    # "Rows: 0" dashboard; now exits non-zero with a clear message.
    _check_empty_input "header-only pipe" "col1,col2"$'\n' "no data rows"
}

test_header_only_tsv () {
    # Same path for a TSV header to make sure the delimiter-detection
    # branch takes the same guard.
    _check_empty_input "header-only TSV" $'a\tb\tc\n' "no data rows"
}

test_empty_file_arg () {
    # Empty file passed as a path argument also hits the same code path.
    local f
    f=$(mktemp)
    local output rc=0
    output=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "$f" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$f"
    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: empty file arg Aje28094Aj expected non-zero exit, got 0"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$output" "Input contained no data" "user-friendly message" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$output" "unbound variable" "no unbound-variable leak" || return 1
}

test_valid_data_still_works () {
    # Regression guard: a real dataset still parses and exits 0.
    local output rc=0
    output=$(bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "$SAMPLES_DIR/anscombe.csv" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "valid dataset should succeed"
    assert_contains "$output" "Rows:" "valid dataset should render stats"
}

run_test "empty stdin via < /dev/null" test_empty_stdin_dev_null
run_test "empty stdin via zero-byte pipe" test_empty_stdin_zero_bytes
run_test "header-only CSV pipe" test_header_only_no_rows
run_test "header-only TSV pipe" test_header_only_tsv
run_test "empty file passed as argument" test_empty_file_arg
run_test "valid dataset still works" test_valid_data_still_works

print_summary

===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/test_filter_skip_correctness.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=807be92a34a47987e0800f3f0da598c7773f64e870c8a2be38fb8c077162b678===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: filter-aware computation skip preserves output byte-identically
## (ENV-126).
##
## The optimisation gates `run_correlation_analyses`, `run_cramers_v`, and
## `run_group_summaries` behind a `_will_keep_kind` check. The whole point is
## that the user-visible output of any filtered run is unchanged: skipping is
## a *performance* optimisation, not a behaviour change.
##
## These tests run the same filtered command twice Aje28094Aj once with the default
## `EF_FILTER_SKIP=1` (skip enabled) and once with the escape-hatch
## `EF_FILTER_SKIP=0` (skip disabled) Aje28094Aj and assert the two outputs match.
## Any divergence means the gate is dropping work that the un-skipped
## pipeline produces, which is the regression we care about catching.
##
## The escape hatch lives in `lib/_helpers.sh::_will_keep_kind`; it always
## returns 0 (true) when `EF_FILTER_SKIP=0` is exported.
################################################################################
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "Filter-Skip Correctness Tests (ENV-126)"
echo "========================================"

# Pick a sample with enough columns to exercise correlation, group summaries,
# and Cramer's V Aje28094Aj biostats has mixed numeric+categorical columns.
DATASET="$SAMPLES_DIR/biostats.csv"

# Strict byte-identical check: for runs with no `--kinds` filter active,
# every gate in `_will_keep_kind` short-circuits to true, so the skip
# path computes exactly what the no-skip path computes.
_diff_skipped_vs_unskipped () {
    local desc="$1"
    shift
    local args=("$@")
    local skipped unskipped
    skipped=$(EF_FILTER_SKIP=1 bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "${args[@]}" "$DATASET" 2>&1) \
        || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: skipped run failed for: $desc"; return 1; }
    unskipped=$(EF_FILTER_SKIP=0 bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "${args[@]}" "$DATASET" 2>&1) \
        || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: unskipped run failed for: $desc"; return 1; }
    if [[ "$skipped" != "$unskipped" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $desc Aje28094Aj skipped vs unskipped output differs"
        diff <(echo "$skipped") <(echo "$unskipped") | head -20 | sed 's/^/    /'
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Content-only check: for `--kinds X` runs the skip path may renumber
# items (skipped analyses don't add to ITEM_TITLES, so survivors get
# lower numbers) and may suppress stderr warnings that came from the
# now-skipped functions. Both are intentional. The kept items'
# *bodies* must still match line-for-line modulo those leading number
# prefixes.
_compare_kept_item_bodies () {
    local desc="$1"
    shift
    local args=("$@")
    local skipped unskipped
    # Only stdout for this comparison; stderr warnings from skipped
    # functions are expected to differ.
    skipped=$(EF_FILTER_SKIP=1 bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "${args[@]}" "$DATASET" 2>/dev/null) \
        || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: skipped run failed for: $desc"; return 1; }
    unskipped=$(EF_FILTER_SKIP=0 bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" "${args[@]}" "$DATASET" 2>/dev/null) \
        || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: unskipped run failed for: $desc"; return 1; }
    # Strip leading "N. " item numbers so renumbering doesn't show up
    # as a difference, and drop blank lines.
    local strip_skipped strip_unskipped
    strip_skipped=$(echo "$skipped" | sed -E 's/^[0-9]+\. //' | grep -v '^$' | sort)
    strip_unskipped=$(echo "$unskipped" | sed -E 's/^[0-9]+\. //' | grep -v '^$' | sort)
    if [[ "$strip_skipped" != "$strip_unskipped" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $desc Aje28094Aj kept-item bodies differ"
        diff <(echo "$strip_skipped") <(echo "$strip_unskipped") | head -20 | sed 's/^/    /'
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

test_default_run_unchanged () {
    # No filters Aje28094Aj both runs should do the same work.
    _diff_skipped_vs_unskipped "default run (no filters)"
}

test_good_filter_unchanged () {
    _diff_skipped_vs_unskipped "--good filter" --good
}

test_all_filter_unchanged () {
    _diff_skipped_vs_unskipped "--all filter" --all
}

test_kinds_corr_only_unchanged () {
    # Skip path drops nothing here (corr is requested) but Cramer's V and
    # group_summary would be skipped Aje28094Aj the kept items must still match.
    _compare_kept_item_bodies "--kinds corr_matrix,corr_pairs" --kinds corr_matrix,corr_pairs
}

test_kinds_threshold_only_unchanged () {
    # Monitor-mode shape: narrow --kinds with no correlation work required.
    # Skip path drops correlation entirely; the kept items (quality_score,
    # col_types) must still come out identical.
    _compare_kept_item_bodies "--kinds quality_score,col_types" --kinds quality_score,col_types
}

test_kinds_drop_suggest_unchanged () {
    # Regression: drop_suggest reads CORR_VALUES from run_correlation_analyses.
    # The skip gate must still run correlation when drop_suggest is kept,
    # so the high-correlation column shows up in the suggestion.
    _compare_kept_item_bodies "--kinds drop_suggest" --kinds drop_suggest
}

test_tags_advanced_unchanged () {
    _diff_skipped_vs_unskipped "--tags ADVANCED" --tags ADVANCED
}

test_summary_unchanged () {
    # --summary forces _will_keep_kind to always say yes. Both runs do the
    # full pipeline; output must match.
    _diff_skipped_vs_unskipped "--summary" --summary
}

test_mode_monitor_unchanged () {
    # --mode rewrites tags after analyses run; the gate forces full
    # computation when a non-explore mode is set, so output is identical.
    _diff_skipped_vs_unskipped "--mode monitor" --mode monitor
}

test_kinds_cramers_v_unchanged () {
    # cramers_v is gated separately. Asserting parity on kept-item bodies
    # covers the categorical-pair awk skip path.
    _compare_kept_item_bodies "--kinds cramers_v" --kinds cramers_v
}

test_drop_suggest_finds_high_corr_column () {
    # Direct regression for the dependency we discovered during
    # implementation: edge.csv has a `measure` column highly correlated
    # with another. With skip enabled, drop_suggest must still see
    # CORR_VALUES populated.
    local out
    out=$(EF_FILTER_SKIP=1 bash "$MDA_SCRIPT" --kinds drop_suggest "$SAMPLES_DIR/edge.csv" 2>&1) \
        || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: edge.csv drop_suggest run failed"; return 1; }
    assert_contains "$out" "measure" "drop_suggest must still flag high-corr column under skip"
}

run_test "default run byte-identical" test_default_run_unchanged
run_test "--good byte-identical" test_good_filter_unchanged
run_test "--all byte-identical" test_all_filter_unchanged
run_test "--tags ADVANCED byte-identical" test_tags_advanced_unchanged
run_test "--summary byte-identical" test_summary_unchanged
run_test "--mode monitor byte-identical" test_mode_monitor_unchanged
run_test "--kinds corr_matrix,corr_pairs kept items match" test_kinds_corr_only_unchanged
run_test "--kinds quality_score,col_types kept items match" test_kinds_threshold_only_unchanged
run_test "--kinds drop_suggest preserves CORR dep" test_kinds_drop_suggest_unchanged
run_test "--kinds cramers_v kept items match" test_kinds_cramers_v_unchanged
run_test "drop_suggest finds high-corr col under skip (edge.csv)" test_drop_suggest_finds_high_corr_column

print_summary
===END===
===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/test_float_cmp.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=e23bd53527e7c819cbbbad5a31f743805d2d13a0b8fed9d04fa1014ad3e6f14e===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for ENV-164 Aje28094Aj float_cmp delegates to awk; no integer overflow,
##                     no scientific-notation rejection
##
## Pre-ENV-164, `float_cmp` (in `lib/_helpers.sh`) scaled values by 1e6
## and compared via bash arithmetic. That had two latent bugs:
##
##   1. Any value above ~9.2e12 (signed-64-bit max / 1e6) overflowed
##      during the scale step. A column of nanosecond timestamps,
##      financial cents, or large primary-key IDs silently produced
##      wrong comparison results Aje28094Aj driving wrong threshold flags,
##      wrong CV / correlation classifications, wrong quality scores.
##
##   2. Scientific notation (`1e-05`, `2.5e7`) was rejected with
##      `value too great for base` because `10#1e-05` is not valid in
##      bash's base-10 arithmetic. awk routinely produces scientific
##      notation from `printf %g` for very small or very large numbers,
##      so a column whose mean rounded outside `[1e-4, 1e6]` could
##      abort the analyze pipeline mid-run.
##
## After the fix, float_cmp is a one-line wrapper around an awk BEGIN
## block. We pin the new behaviour:
##   - Old overflow case (13-digit ints) now compares correctly.
##   - Scientific notation in either operand works.
##   - Negatives, decimals, and equality remain correct.
##   - Invalid operator returns rc=1 (matches old behaviour).
##   - Bash drift guard: the production source no longer contains the
##     `10#${a_int:-0}` overflow-prone scaling line.
################################################################################

set -u

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
EA_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
HELPERS="$EA_DIR/lib/_helpers.sh"

[[ -r "$HELPERS" ]] || { echo "FATAL: $HELPERS missing"; exit 1; }

# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$HELPERS"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
_pass () { PASS=$((PASS+1)); printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
_fail () { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf '  FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2; if [[ -n "${2:-}" ]]; then printf '    %s\n' "$2" >&2; fi; }

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "ENV-164: float_cmp via awk (no overflow, no scientific rejection)"
echo "========================================"

###############################################################################
# Section A Aje28094Aj overflow regression (the audit's headline)
###############################################################################

# A1: 13-digit ints near the bash-arith overflow boundary.
if float_cmp 9999999999999 ">" 8999999999999; then
    _pass "13-digit > 13-digit (was BUG: bash arith overflowed signed-64)"
else
    _fail "13-digit comparison still wrong"
fi
if float_cmp 9999999999999 "<" 9999999999999.1; then
    _pass "13-digit < 13-digit + small fraction"
else
    _fail "13-digit fractional comparison wrong"
fi

# A2: equal large-int comparison.
if float_cmp 9999999999999 "==" 9999999999999; then
    _pass "13-digit == 13-digit equal"
else
    _fail "13-digit equality wrong"
fi

# A3: 14-15 digit ints (well past the old overflow). At ~16-17 digits
#     IEEE-754 doubles lose precision and adjacent integers round
#     together; we don't pin behaviour past the double's mantissa.
if float_cmp 99999999999999 ">" 99999999999990; then
    _pass "14-digit > 14-digit"
else
    _fail "14-digit comparison wrong"
fi

###############################################################################
# Section B Aje28094Aj scientific notation
###############################################################################

# B1: `1e-05` / `1e-04` round-trip without aborting the pipeline.
if float_cmp 1e-05 "<" 1e-04; then
    _pass "1e-05 < 1e-04 (scientific notation)"
else
    _fail "1e-05 < 1e-04 wrong (should be true)"
fi
if float_cmp 1e-04 "<" 1e-05; then
    _fail "1e-04 < 1e-05 wrong (should be false)"
else
    _pass "1e-04 < 1e-05 correctly false"
fi

# B2: large positive scientific notation.
if float_cmp 2.5e7 ">" 2e7; then
    _pass "2.5e7 > 2e7"
else
    _fail "2.5e7 > 2e7 wrong"
fi

# B3: mixed scientific + plain decimal.
if float_cmp 1e3 "==" 1000; then
    _pass "1e3 == 1000 (mixed forms)"
else
    _fail "1e3 == 1000 wrong"
fi

###############################################################################
# Section C Aje28094Aj old-behaviour regressions (decimals, negatives, ops)
###############################################################################

if float_cmp 3.14 ">" 2.0; then _pass "3.14 > 2.0"; else _fail "3.14 > 2.0 wrong"; fi
if float_cmp -3.14 "<" 0; then _pass "-3.14 < 0"; else _fail "-3.14 < 0 wrong"; fi
if float_cmp -3.14 ">" -3.15; then _pass "-3.14 > -3.15"; else _fail "-3.14 > -3.15 wrong"; fi
if float_cmp 3.14 "==" 3.140; then _pass "3.14 == 3.140 (trailing-zero invariance)"; else _fail "3.14 == 3.140 wrong"; fi
if float_cmp 5 ">=" 5; then _pass "5 >= 5"; else _fail "5 >= 5 wrong"; fi
if float_cmp 5 "<=" 5; then _pass "5 <= 5"; else _fail "5 <= 5 wrong"; fi
if float_cmp 0 "!=" 1; then _pass "0 != 1"; else _fail "0 != 1 wrong"; fi
if ! float_cmp 0 "!=" 0; then _pass "0 != 0 correctly false"; else _fail "0 != 0 wrong"; fi

# Invalid operator Aje28692Aj rc=1 (legacy behaviour).
float_cmp 1 "??" 2; rc=$?
if [[ "$rc" -eq 1 ]]; then
    _pass "invalid operator returns rc=1"
else
    _fail "invalid operator rc unexpected: $rc"
fi

###############################################################################
# Section D Aje28094Aj drift guard
###############################################################################

# D1: source no longer contains the overflow-prone `10#${a_int:-0} * 1000000`.
if grep -qF '10#${a_int:-0} * 1000000' "$HELPERS"; then
    _fail "drift: lib/_helpers.sh still has the overflow-prone scaling line"
else
    _pass "drift: overflow-prone bash-arith scaling is gone"
fi

# D2: source delegates to awk.
if grep -qE 'awk -v a=' "$HELPERS"; then
    _pass "drift: float_cmp delegates to awk"
else
    _fail "drift: awk delegation missing"
fi

###############################################################################

echo ""
echo "========================================"
printf 'Results: %d/%d passed, %d failed\n' "$PASS" "$((PASS+FAIL))" "$FAIL"
if [[ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "========================================"
    exit 1
fi
echo "All tests passed."
echo "========================================"
===END===

===META: mode=755 sha256=771c63d333e84d92bcd8776b0de2760e159c581dcbeb9f0534e65243c808e76f===
#!/bin/bash
# ENV-064: JSON output envelope + schema validation
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

_has_jq=0
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && _has_jq=1

_produce_json () {
    local file="$1"
    run_mda --format json --all "$file"
}

test_envelope_has_schema_version () {
    local out
    out=$(_produce_json "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" '"schema_version":"1.0"' "schema_version present"
    assert_contains "$out" '"envoy_analyze_version":' "tool version present"
    assert_contains "$out" '"items":[' "items array present"
}

test_item_has_required_keys () {
    local out
    out=$(_produce_json "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    # Every item must carry id, tag, kind, title, body
    for key in '"id":' '"tag":' '"kind":' '"title":' '"body":'; do
        assert_contains "$out" "$key" "items should include $key"
    done
}

test_multiple_samples_envelope () {
    for s in trees.csv anscombe.csv missing.csv; do
        local f="$SAMPLES_DIR/$s"
        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
        local out
        out=$(_produce_json "$f")
        assert_contains "$out" '"schema_version":"1.0"' "$s: envelope missing"
    done
}

test_jq_structural_check () {
    if [[ $_has_jq -ne 1 ]]; then
        echo "  (skipping Aje28094Aj jq not installed)"
        return 0
    fi
    local out
    out=$(_produce_json "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    # schema_version is "1.0"
    local sv
    sv=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.schema_version')
    [[ "$sv" == "1.0" ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: jq schema_version=$sv"; return 1; }
    # At least one item
    local n
    n=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq '.items | length')
    (( n > 0 )) || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: items array is empty"; return 1; }
    # Every item has required keys
    local missing
    missing=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq '[.items[] | (has("id") and has("tag") and has("kind") and has("title") and has("body"))] | all')
    [[ "$missing" == "true" ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: some item is missing required keys"; return 1; }
    # Tag values are valid
    local bad_tags
    bad_tags=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq '[.items[] | .tag | select(. != "GOOD" and . != "ADVANCED" and . != "DIAGNOSTIC" and . != "NOISY")] | length')
    [[ "$bad_tags" == "0" ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: invalid tag values"; return 1; }
}

test_schema_file_valid_json () {
    local schema
    schema="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/schemas/envoy-analyze-output.json"
    [[ -f "$schema" ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: schema file missing: $schema"; return 1; }
    if [[ $_has_jq -eq 1 ]]; then
        jq '.' "$schema" >/dev/null || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: schema is not valid JSON"; return 1; }
    fi
}

run_test "ENV-064 envelope has schema_version / version / items" test_envelope_has_schema_version
run_test "ENV-064 each item has required keys" test_item_has_required_keys
run_test "ENV-064 envelope present across multiple samples" test_multiple_samples_envelope
run_test "ENV-064 jq structural validation" test_jq_structural_check
run_test "ENV-064 schemas/envoy-analyze-output.json is valid JSON" test_schema_file_valid_json

print_summary
===END===
===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/test_known_values_extended.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=24fe72849338a26b2e8092334e924d1bfe8ef6358ff4bc71dfcf616b640c2b80===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: known-answer correctness on synthetic datasets (ENV-124)
##
## The pre-existing `test_correctness.sh` covers the core summary stats and
## `samples/known.csv`'s perfect-linear case in depth. This file extends
## that coverage to the four computations that the original suite only
## smoke-tested:
##
##   1. Benford's Law chi-squared on a Benford-drawn sample (PASS) AND a
##      uniform-drawn sample (FAIL) Aje28094Aj pins both the formula and the data.
##   2. Cramer's V on hand-computed contingency tables, plus the
##      expected-frequency-<5 warning for sparse cells.
##   3. Spearman rho on non-trivial inputs: a square-monotonic +1.0, a
##      negative-monotonic Aje28892Aj1.0, and a single-adjacent-swap value (15-row,
##      Ajcf81Aj = 0.996429) that catches off-by-one errors in the rank tie code.
##   4. Bimodality detection on a seeded two-cluster distribution where
##      both peak heights are independently verifiable.
##
## Truth values come from `_compute_known_truths.py` (see that file's
## docstring). Re-run `python3 tests/_compute_known_truths.py --print` to
## regenerate the truth table.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "Known-Answer Extended Tests (ENV-124)"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## Benford's Law Aje28094Aj exact chi-squared values
################################################################################

test_benford_pass_chi2_exact () {
    # known_benford.csv `benford` column: 200 rows drawn from a log-uniform
    # distribution (matches Benford). Hand-computed chiAjc2b2Aj = 2.68; well under
    # the 15.507 critical value, so the analysis must report PASS.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds benford "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_benford.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" "Chi-squared: 2.68" "benford column chiAjc2b2Aj should be 2.68" || return 1
    # PASS verdict appears on the same item.
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS (distribution follows Benford" "benford column should PASS the chiAjc2b2Aj test"
}

test_benford_fail_chi2_exact () {
    # known_benford.csv `uniform` column: 200 rows from uniform(1, 9999)
    # Aje28692Aj first digits do NOT follow Benford. Hand-computed chiAjc2b2Aj = 51.02,
    # well above critical Aje28692Aj FAIL.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds benford "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_benford.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" "Chi-squared: 51.02" "uniform column chiAjc2b2Aj should be 51.02" || return 1
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL (deviation from Benford" "uniform column should FAIL the chiAjc2b2Aj test"
}

################################################################################
## Cramer's V Aje28094Aj exact contingency-table values
################################################################################

test_cramers_v_device_os_exact () {
    # known_categorical.csv: device(2) Ajc397Aj os(5) contingency, hand-computed
    # V Aje28988Aj 0.7643 (matches the awk's "iterate observed cells only"
    # implementation in lib/_categorical.sh::run_cramers_v).
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds cramers_v "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_categorical.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" "device vs os: V=0.764" "device vs os V should be ~0.764" || return 1
    # The strong-association label must accompany V > 0.5.
    assert_contains "$out" "strong association" "V=0.764 should be labelled strong association"
}

test_cramers_v_low_expected_warning () {
    # device Ajc397Aj os has cells with expected frequency < 5 (the rare
    # phoneAje28694AjLinux / laptopAje28694AjiOS combinations) Aje28692Aj the >20% low-expected
    # warning fires.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds cramers_v "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_categorical.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" "expected frequencies <5" "low-expected warning should fire on sparse cells"
}

################################################################################
## Spearman rho Aje28094Aj three known values on non-trivial 15-row data
################################################################################

test_spearman_perfect_increasing () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds trend "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_spearman.csv")
    # x and y (= xAjc2b2Aj) both strictly monotonic in row order Aje28692Aj Ajcf81Aj = +1.0.
    assert_contains "$out" "Trend: x" "x trend item should be present" || return 1
    assert_contains "$out" "Spearman rho vs row order: 1.000000" "Ajcf81Aj for x should be 1.000000"
}

test_spearman_perfect_decreasing () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds trend "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_spearman.csv")
    # z = -x Aje28692Aj strict reverse monotonic Aje28692Aj Ajcf81Aj = -1.0.
    if ! [[ "$out" == *"Trend: z"* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: z trend item missing"; return 1
    fi
    # Pull out the line that follows "Trend: z" and assert its rho.
    local zblock
    zblock=$(awk '/Trend: z$/,/Trend: noisy$/' <<< "$out")
    assert_contains "$zblock" "Spearman rho vs row order: -1.000000" "Ajcf81Aj for z should be -1.000000"
}

test_spearman_single_adjacent_swap () {
    # `noisy` column: 1..15 with positions 8,9 swapped. Sum of dAjc2b2Aj = 2,
    # so Ajcf81Aj = 1 - 6Ajc2b7Aj2 / (15 Ajc2b7Aj (15Ajc2b2Aj-1)) = 0.996429. This pins the tie-handling
    # path in the awk Spearman impl Aje28094Aj any off-by-one in rank averaging
    # would shift this number.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds trend "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_spearman.csv")
    local nblock
    nblock=$(awk '/Trend: noisy$/,0' <<< "$out")
    assert_contains "$nblock" "Spearman rho vs row order: 0.996429" "Ajcf81Aj for noisy should be exactly 0.996429"
}

################################################################################
## Bimodality Aje28094Aj verifiable peak heights
################################################################################

test_bimodality_yes_on_seeded_two_clusters () {
    # known_bimodal_seeded.csv: 25 values clustered around 10, 25 around
    # 90. The 10-bin histogram puts ~24 in bin 0 and ~22 in bin 9 with a
    # clean valley. Detector must flag YES with two peaks.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds bimodality "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_bimodal_seeded.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" "Bimodal: YES" "seeded two-cluster data should be flagged bimodal" || return 1
    assert_contains "$out" "Peaks detected: 2" "should detect exactly 2 peaks"
}

test_bimodality_peak_heights_match_seed () {
    # Truth: with seed=4, peak heights are 24 and 22 (the 25 values per
    # cluster spread over a few bins each, leaving 24/22 in the dominant
    # bins). Hard-coded because the dataset is deterministic.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --kinds bimodality "$SAMPLES_DIR/known_bimodal_seeded.csv")
    assert_contains "$out" "Peak heights: 24, 22" "peak heights should match the seeded distribution"
}

################################################################################
## Sabotage smoke Aje28094Aj make sure these tests would actually catch a bug
##
## The point of known-answer tests is that they fail when the underlying
## formula breaks. We can't sabotage the production code from here, but
## we can sanity-check that our assertions are tight enough to fail
## against a *different* dataset Aje28094Aj proving they aren't substring-matching
## something benign.
################################################################################

test_assertions_are_dataset_specific () {
    # Run the tool on a different dataset (anscombe) and confirm none of
    # the very-specific strings the tests above look for appear there.
    # This is the "would my test pass for the wrong reasons?" check.
    local out
    out=$(run_mda "$SAMPLES_DIR/anscombe.csv" 2>&1)
    assert_not_contains "$out" "Chi-squared: 2.68" "Benford 2.68 must not appear in unrelated dataset" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$out" "Chi-squared: 51.02" "Benford 51.02 must not appear in unrelated dataset" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$out" "Spearman rho vs row order: 0.996429" "Spearman 0.996429 must not appear in unrelated dataset" || return 1
    assert_not_contains "$out" "Peak heights: 24, 22" "Bimodality 24,22 must not appear in unrelated dataset"
}

################################################################################
## Truth-generator script must remain runnable Aje28094Aj guards against drift
################################################################################

test_truth_generator_runs () {
    # If the helper script breaks (Python syntax error, missing module,
    # whatever) someone can't regenerate the samples. Catch that at CI
    # rather than at next change.
    local out rc=0
    out=$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/_compute_known_truths.py" --print 2>&1) || rc=$?
    [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || {
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: truth-generator script crashed (rc=$rc)"
        echo "$out" | head -10 | sed 's/^/    /'
        return 1
    }
    assert_contains "$out" "benford_chi2 = 2.68" "truth-generator output should pin Benford chiAjc2b2Aj" || return 1
    assert_contains "$out" "cramers_v_device_os = 0.7643" "truth-generator output should pin Cramer's V" || return 1
    assert_contains "$out" "spearman_x_noisy = 0.996429" "truth-generator output should pin Spearman Ajcf81Aj"
}

run_test "benford pass chiAjc2b2Aj = 2.68" test_benford_pass_chi2_exact
run_test "benford fail chiAjc2b2Aj = 51.02" test_benford_fail_chi2_exact
run_test "cramers V (device vs os) = 0.764" test_cramers_v_device_os_exact
run_test "cramers V low-expected-frequency warning" test_cramers_v_low_expected_warning
run_test "spearman Ajcf81Aj = +1.000000 (strict monotonic)" test_spearman_perfect_increasing
run_test "spearman Ajcf81Aj = -1.000000 (reverse monotonic)" test_spearman_perfect_decreasing
run_test "spearman Ajcf81Aj = 0.996429 (single adjacent swap)" test_spearman_single_adjacent_swap
run_test "bimodality YES on seeded 2-cluster data" test_bimodality_yes_on_seeded_two_clusters
run_test "bimodality peak heights match seed" test_bimodality_peak_heights_match_seed
run_test "assertions are dataset-specific (sabotage smoke)" test_assertions_are_dataset_specific
run_test "truth-generator script remains runnable" test_truth_generator_runs

print_summary
===END===

#!/bin/bash

test_list_items_shows_menu () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --list-items "$SAMPLE" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "ID" "menu has a header"
    assert_contains "$out" "KIND" "menu lists the kind column"
    assert_contains "$out" "TITLE" "menu lists the title column"
    assert_contains "$out" "Dataset overview" "menu includes the overview item"
}

    local out
    out=$(run_mda --list-items "$SAMPLE" 2>/dev/null)
    # The overview item is always suggested Aje28692Aj row 1 carries the '*' marker.
    assert_contains "$out" "*" "suggested items are marked"
}

    local out
    out=$(run_mda --list-items "$SAMPLE" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "summary" "summary analyses are listed"
    assert_contains "$out" "col_types" "column-type analysis is listed"
}

test_list_items_in_help () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --help 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "--list-items" "help documents --list-items"
}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=helpers.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

test_strongest_correlations_has_pairs () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" --good)
    assert_contains "$output" "Strongest correlations" "should include correlation header"
    assert_contains "$output" "Girth (in) vs Volume(ft^3): r=" "should include specific correlation pair"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "vs : r=" "correlation pairs should not be empty"
}

test_tags_filter_advanced () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --tags ADVANCED "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "[ADVANCED]" "should emit ADVANCED items"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "[GOOD]" "should filter out GOOD items when only ADVANCED"
}

test_kinds_filter_shape () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds shape "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "Distribution shape: Index" "should include shape items"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Summary stats: Index" "should exclude non-shape items"
}

test_zero_variance_and_missing_rank () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds zero_variance "$SAMPLES_DIR/edge.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "Zero-variance numeric columns" "should include zero-variance header"
    assert_contains "$output" "constant: std=0" "should flag constant column"

    output=$(run_mda --kinds missing_rank "$SAMPLES_DIR/edge.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "Most missing columns" "should include missing-rank header"
    assert_contains "$output" "measure: 2 missing" "should report missing counts"
}

test_skewness_differs_per_column () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds shape "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    # Extract skewness values Aje28094Aj each column should have a different value
    local skew_index skew_girth skew_height
    skew_index=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: Index" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    skew_girth=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: Girth" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    skew_height=$(echo "$output" | grep -A1 "Distribution shape: Height" | grep "Skewness:" | awk '{print $2}')
    # Index is uniform (1..31), skewness should be ~0
    assert_contains "$skew_index" "0.000000" "Index skewness should be ~0 (uniform)"
    # Girth and Height should differ from each other and from Index
    if [[ "$skew_index" == "$skew_girth" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: Index and Girth skewness should differ ($skew_index vs $skew_girth)"
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ "$skew_girth" == "$skew_height" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: Girth and Height skewness should differ ($skew_girth vs $skew_height)"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_correlation_bounded () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds corr_pairs "$SAMPLES_DIR/edge.csv")
    # Correlation should be between -1 and 1, never exceed those bounds
    local r_val
    r_val=$(echo "$output" | grep "id vs measure" | sed 's/.*r=//')
    if awk -v r="$r_val" 'BEGIN{exit !(r > 1.0 || r < -1.0)}'; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: correlation $r_val exceeds [-1,1] bounds"
        return 1
    fi
    assert_contains "$output" "id vs measure: r=" "should include correlation pair"
}

test_correlation_matrix_alignment () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds corr_matrix "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    # Column names with spaces should stay intact in the matrix header
    assert_contains "$output" "Girth (in)" "matrix should preserve column name with spaces"
    assert_contains "$output" "Height (ft)" "matrix should preserve column name with spaces"
    # Should NOT have broken fragments like standalone "(in)" as a column
    assert_not_contains "$output" $'\n'"   (in)" "column name should not be split across columns"
}

test_correlation_matrix_header_alignment () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds corr_matrix "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    # Header row should be indented past the row-label column
    # The first data row starts with "Index" followed by values
    # The header should NOT start with a column name at position 0
    local header_line
    header_line=$(echo "$output" | grep "Index.*Girth" | head -1)
    # Header line should have leading whitespace (blank row-label column)
    if [[ "$header_line" == [A-Za-z]* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: matrix header should be indented (has blank row-label column)"
        echo "    got: '$header_line'"
        return 1
    fi
}

}

test_corr_strength () {
    # ENV-125: the old "Correlation dimension summary" / "Rank N:" /
    # "Total dimensions: N" framing implied a dimensional decomposition
    # the metric (sum of |r|) cannot deliver. Path A reframed it as
    # "Column correlation strength" with `<col>: connectedness=<v>`
    # entries plus an explicit "not a PCA" disclaimer.
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --kinds corr_strength "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "Column correlation strength" "renamed item title"
    assert_contains "$output" "connectedness=" "neutral per-column connectedness label"
    assert_contains "$output" "Not a PCA" "explicit disclaimer about the metric"
    assert_contains "$output" "Summed across" "footer reports summed-column count"
    # Old framing must be gone.
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Correlation dimension summary" "old title removed"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Rank1:" "old Rank N: labels removed"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Total dimensions:" "misleading dimension count removed"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Principal component" "no PCA label"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "PC1:" "no PC1 label"
}

test_corr_strength_constant_column_last () {
    # ENV-125: a constant column has zero variance, so |r| with every
    # other column is undefined Aje28692Aj treated as 0; sum of |r| is 0 too. It
    # must rank last in the connectedness order. samples/known.csv has
    # exactly such a column (header `constant`, all rows = 5).
    local output constant_line
    output=$(run_mda --kinds corr_strength "$SAMPLES_DIR/known.csv")
    if ! grep -q "Column correlation strength" <<< "$output"; then
        # known.csv's numeric column count may be < 3 in some configs;
        # if no item was emitted skip the check rather than fail.
        return 0
    fi
    constant_line=$(grep -E "^[[:space:]]*constant:" <<< "$output" | head -1)
    if [[ -z "$constant_line" ]]; then
        # No `constant` column in this fixture revision Aje28094Aj skip silently.
        return 0
    fi
    assert_contains "$constant_line" "connectedness=0.000" \
        "constant column should sum |r|=0 with every other column"
}

#!/bin/bash

test_mode_benchmark_promotes_cv () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --mode benchmark --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$output" "Coefficient of variation" "benchmark mode should promote CV to GOOD"
}

test_mode_benchmark_promotes_anomaly () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --mode benchmark --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$output" "Anomaly detection" "benchmark mode should promote anomaly to GOOD"
}

test_mode_monitor_promotes_trend () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --mode monitor --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$output" "Trend:" "monitor mode should promote trend to GOOD"
}

test_mode_monitor_demotes_histogram () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --mode monitor --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Histogram:" "monitor mode should demote histogram from GOOD"
}

test_mode_monitor_demotes_sparkline () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mda --mode monitor --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Sparkline:" "monitor mode should demote sparkline from GOOD"
}

test_mode_explore_unchanged () {
    local output_default output_explore
    output_default=$(run_mda --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    output_explore=$(run_mda --mode explore --tags GOOD "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ "$output_default" != "$output_explore" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --mode explore should produce identical output to no mode"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_mode_invalid () {
    local code=0
    run_mda --mode bogus "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" 2>/dev/null || code=$?
    if [[ $code -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: invalid mode should error"
        return 1
    fi
}

    local output
    output=$(run_mda --mode benchmark --compare "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" --tags GOOD 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$output" "Cross-dataset comparison" "benchmark + compare should show comparison as GOOD"
}

===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/test_module_contracts.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=6a9357208068299240750262216bb24595b60a31333bfac60bac202ab9cbcdba===
#!/bin/bash
# ENV-066: enforce that every lib/*.sh module declares the globals it touches
# in a `## Reads:` / `## Writes:` header block. The registry in _globals.sh
# remains authoritative; this static check keeps the headers and the registry
# in sync.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

LIB_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/lib"

# Modules that must declare their contract. _globals.sh is excluded Aje28094Aj it IS
# the contract.
_lib_modules () {
    local f
    for f in "$LIB_DIR"/_*.sh; do
        [[ "$(basename "$f")" == "_globals.sh" ]] && continue
        printf '%s\n' "$f"
    done
}

# Collect "## Reads:" + "## Writes:" declared names for a module into a single
# whitespace-separated string. Handles multi-line blocks (continuation lines
# that don't start a new header). Strips trailing notes in parentheses.
_declared_globals () {
    local file="$1"
    awk '
        /^## Reads:/  { inblk=1; sub(/^## Reads:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; next }
        /^## Writes:/ { inblk=1; sub(/^## Writes:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; next }
        /^##[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z]/ { inblk=0; next }
        /^##[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/ && inblk {
            sub(/^##[[:space:]]+/, "")
            print
            next
        }
        /^##$/ || /^##[[:space:]]*$/ { inblk=0; next }
        /^[^#]/ { exit }
    ' "$file" | tr '()' '  ' | tr -s ' \n' ' '
}

# ENV-128: extract a single header section ("Reads", "Writes", or "Allowlist")
# from the top-of-file comment block, supporting multi-line continuations.
# Returns space-separated names with `(via FN)` annotations preserved so the
# caller can decide whether to accept indirection.
_extract_section () {
    local file="$1" section="$2"
    awk -v want="$section" '
        # Start the wanted section.
        $0 ~ "^## " want ":" {
            inblk=1
            sub("^## " want ":[[:space:]]*", "")
            print
            next
        }
        # Any other top-level header line ends the current block. The
        # `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_ -]*:` shape requires a trailing colon
        # so a continuation line like `##         COL_MEAN COL_STD`
        # is not mistaken for a new section header.
        /^## [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_ -]*:/ { inblk=0; next }
        # Continuation: indented body line under the active section.
        /^##[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/ && inblk {
            sub(/^##[[:space:]]+/, "")
            print
            next
        }
        /^##$/ || /^##[[:space:]]*$/ { inblk=0; next }
        /^[^#]/ { exit }
    ' "$file"
}

# ENV-128: tokenise an `## Reads:` / `## Writes:` block into raw entries,
# preserving `(via FN)` annotations as `NAME(via=FN)`. Convention: a
# `(via FN)` clause applies to every name on the SAME LINE preceding it
# (e.g. `## Writes: ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS (via add_item)`
# tags all four). Names on continuation lines without an annotation are
# treated as direct.
_tokenise_section () {
    local file="$1" section="$2"
    _extract_section "$file" "$section" \
        | awk '
            {
                line = $0
                # First pass: collect names on this line, then look for a
                # `(via FN)` clause to retroactively tag them.
                line_names_n = 0
                tail = line
                while (tail != "") {
                    sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", tail)
                    if (tail == "") break
                    if (substr(tail, 1, 1) == "(") {
                        end = index(tail, ")")
                        if (end == 0) break
                        clause = substr(tail, 2, end - 2)
                        tail = substr(tail, end + 1)
                        # Anchor on `via FN` Aje28094Aj other prose like
                        # "(function arguments only)" is dropped.
                        if (match(clause, /^[[:space:]]*via[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*/)) {
                            sub(/^[[:space:]]*via[[:space:]]+/, "", clause)
                            sub(/[[:space:]].*$/, "", clause)
                            for (i = 0; i < line_names_n; i++) {
                                line_names[i] = line_names[i] "(via=" clause ")"
                            }
                        }
                        continue
                    }
                    if (match(tail, /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*/)) {
                        name = substr(tail, RSTART, RLENGTH)
                        tail = substr(tail, RSTART + RLENGTH)
                        line_names[line_names_n++] = name
                        continue
                    }
                    tail = substr(tail, 2)
                }
                for (i = 0; i < line_names_n; i++) print line_names[i]
            }
        '
}

# ENV-128: extract names from a section, dropping any `(via FN)` annotation.
# Names like "function" or "arguments" that appear in prose like
# "(function arguments only)" still come through here as plain words; the
# caller filters them via _important_names_in_module / _is_important_name.
_section_names () {
    _tokenise_section "$1" "$2" | sed -E 's/\(via=[^)]+\)$//'
}

# ENV-128: look up the via-function for a tokenised name (returns empty if
# the entry has no `(via=FN)` annotation).
_section_via () {
    local entry="$1"
    [[ "$entry" == *"(via="* ]] || { echo ""; return; }
    local rest="${entry#*(via=}"
    echo "${rest%)}"
}

# ENV-128: filter a single name through the same `_important_names_in_module`
# regex so we only enforce the contract on names that look like cross-module
# globals. Names like "function" / "arguments" / "varies" / "none" Aje28094Aj common
# inside parenthetical prose in the headers Aje28094Aj are dropped here.
_is_important_name () {
    local n="$1"
    [[ "$n" =~ ^(COL_[A-Z_]+|CORR_[A-Z_]+|corr_[a-z_]+|ITEM_[A-Z_]+|NUM_COL_[A-Z_]+|CAT_COL_[A-Z_]+|MAX_[A-Z_]+|SPARK_[A-Z_]+|BENFORD_[A-Z_]+|COLOR_[A-Z_]+|SAMPLE_[A-Z_]+|AWK_[A-Z_]+|threshold_[a-z_]+|cleanup_files|dup_count|ROW_COUNT|COL_COUNT|input_file|delim|VERSION|_NUM_P05|_NUM_Q1|_NUM_P50|_NUM_Q3|_NUM_P95|_STRIP_BOM_RESULT|_CORR_PAIR_LINES|output_format|forced_delim|compare_files|kind_filter|analysis_list|summary_mode)$ ]]
}

# ENV-128: returns 0 if the module body references NAME as a read.
# Recognises:
#   * `$NAME`, `${NAME}`, `${NAME[Aje280a6Aj]}` Aje28094Aj standard parameter expansion
#   * Bare `NAME` inside arithmetic contexts (`(( Aje280a6Aj ))`, `$(( Aje280a6Aj ))`,
#     array index `${arr[NAME]}`) Aje28094Aj bash dereferences automatically there
#   * Bare `NAME` inside `[[ NAME -gt 0 ]]` and similar
# Excludes references on lines that are pure `local`/`declare` declarations.
_module_reads_name () {
    local file="$1" name="$2"
    # Strip pure local/declare lines first so a function-scoped
    # `local COL_MEAN=...` doesn't masquerade as a global read.
    local body
    body=$(grep -vE "^[[:space:]]*(local|declare|readonly)[[:space:]]+([^=]+[[:space:]])?${name}([[:space:]=]|$)" "$file")
    # Standard $NAME / ${NAME / ${NAME[ forms. Use an explicit boundary
    # class instead of `\b` (busybox grep -E does not support `\b`).
    grep -qE "(\\\$\\{?${name}([^A-Za-z0-9_]|\$)|\\\$\\{${name}\\[)" <<< "$body" && return 0
    # Arithmetic / test contexts where bare NAME is dereferenced. Match a
    # word-boundary occurrence on a line that contains `((` or `[[` to
    # keep the pattern conservative Aje28094Aj line-of-code references to a bare
    # identifier elsewhere (e.g. as a command name) shouldn't count.
    # Bracket expressions (`[(]`, `[[]`) keep the line selector portable:
    # busybox grep -E treats `\(` as a group, not a literal paren. `[(][(]`
    # also covers the `((` inside `$((`.
    #
    # Materialise the selected lines into a variable instead of piping
    # `grep Aje280a6Aj | grep -q`: under `set -o pipefail` the pipe form fails
    # spuriously Aje28094Aj `grep -q` exits 0 on first match, the upstream `grep`
    # is killed by SIGPIPE (141), pipefail surfaces 141, and `&& return 0`
    # is skipped, so a referenced name is mis-reported as unreferenced.
    # This is timing-dependent (early matches in long modules trigger it),
    # which made it flake intermittently on Alpine CI. Same fix as
    # _module_writes_name below.
    local arith
    arith=$(grep -E "[(][(]|[[][[]" <<< "$body")
    grep -qE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${name}([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" <<< "$arith" && return 0
    return 1
}

# ENV-128: returns 0 if the module body assigns NAME (`NAME=`, `NAME[Aje280a6Aj]=`,
# `NAME+=`). Excludes `local NAME=` and `declare NAME=` so function-local
# assignments don't count as global writes.
#
# Implementation note: we materialise the filtered body into a single
# variable before greping for the assignment, instead of `grep -v | grep
# -q`.  Under `set -o pipefail` the latter form FAILS spuriously: `grep
# -q` exits 0 on first match, the upstream `grep -v` is killed by
# SIGPIPE and reports exit 141, pipefail surfaces 141, and the helper
# returns "no assignment found" even when the assignment exists.  CI
# under mawk/bash hit this where local under gawk/bash didn't because
# of buffer-flush timing differences.
_module_writes_name () {
    local file="$1" name="$2" body
    body=$(grep -vE "^[[:space:]]*(local|declare|readonly)[[:space:]]" "$file")
    grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*${name}([[:space:]]*\\+?=|\\[)" <<<"$body"
}

# ENV-128: returns 0 if the module body calls FN (as command word).
_module_calls_fn () {
    local file="$1" fn="$2"
    grep -qE "(^|[[:space:]\\(])${fn}([[:space:]\\(]|$)" "$file"
}

# Names that look like cross-module globals. Non-exhaustive but covers the
# invariants the registry tracks: COL_*, CORR_*, corr_*, ITEM_*, NUM_COL_*,
# CAT_COL_*, MAX_*, SPARK_*, BENFORD_*, COLOR_*, SAMPLE_*, AWK_*,
# threshold_*, cleanup_files, dup_count, ROW_COUNT, COL_COUNT, add_item, input_file, delim, VERSION.
_important_names_in_module () {
    local file="$1"
    # Candidate names: references and assignments of interesting identifiers.
    local candidates
    candidates=$(awk 'body || /^[^#]/ { body=1; print }' "$file" | \
        grep -oE '(\$\{?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*|^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]*[+]?=|^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\[)' | \
        sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/\$\{?//; s/[[:space:]]*\+?=$//; s/\[$//' | \
        grep -E '^(COL_[A-Z_]+|CORR_[A-Z_]+|corr_[a-z_]+|ITEM_[A-Z_]+|NUM_COL_[A-Z_]+|CAT_COL_[A-Z_]+|MAX_[A-Z_]+|SPARK_[A-Z_]+|BENFORD_[A-Z_]+|COLOR_[A-Z_]+|SAMPLE_[A-Z_]+|AWK_[A-Z_]+|threshold_[a-z_]+|cleanup_files|dup_count|ROW_COUNT|COL_COUNT|input_file|delim|VERSION|_NUM_P05|_NUM_Q1|_NUM_P50|_NUM_Q3|_NUM_P95|_STRIP_BOM_RESULT|_CORR_PAIR_LINES|output_format|forced_delim|compare_files)$' | \
        sort -u)
    # Filter out names that are declared `local` somewhere in the file Aje28094Aj those
    # are function-scoped and not cross-module globals.
    local name
    while IFS= read -r name; do
        [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
        if grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*local[[:space:]]+([^=]+[[:space:]])?${name}([[:space:]=]|$)" "$file"; then
            continue
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "$name"
    done <<< "$candidates"
}

# Registry of known cross-module names (authoritative).
_registry_names () {
    # Allowed because the registry explicitly documents them. A tiny permit list
    # to keep the static check from false-failing on things like `COL_UNIQUE`
    # being read inside a for-loop index (it IS declared).
    cat <<'EOF'
COL_TYPE COL_NUMERIC COL_TEXT COL_MEAN COL_STD COL_SKEW COL_KURT COL_MIN COL_MAX COL_UNIQUE COL_MISSING COL_NAMES COL_COUNT
CORR_VALUES corr_cols corr_names _CORR_PAIR_LINES
ITEM_TITLES ITEM_BODIES ITEM_TAGS ITEM_KINDS
NUM_COL_INDEXES NUM_COL_NAMES CAT_COL_INDEXES CAT_COL_NAMES
MAX_CORR_COLS MAX_GROUP_UNIQUE MAX_GROUPS MAX_GROUP_NUM_COLS
SPARK_SAMPLES
BENFORD_CRIT BENFORD_ALPHA
COLOR_ENABLED
SAMPLE_NOTE
AWK_ISMISSING
threshold_specs threshold_exit_code
cleanup_files dup_count
ROW_COUNT input_file delim forced_delim output_format compare_files
VERSION
_NUM_P05 _NUM_Q1 _NUM_P50 _NUM_Q3 _NUM_P95
_STRIP_BOM_RESULT
add_item
EOF
}

test_each_module_has_contract_headers () {
    local f
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        if ! grep -q '^## Reads:' "$f"; then
            echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") missing '## Reads:' header"
            return 1
        fi
        if ! grep -q '^## Writes:' "$f"; then
            echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") missing '## Writes:' header"
            return 1
        fi
    done < <(_lib_modules)
}

test_all_referenced_globals_in_registry () {
    # For each module: everything it references (of the important-name class)
    # should appear in the module's own Reads/Writes OR the registry.
    local registry
    registry="$(_registry_names | tr '\n' ' ')"
    local f failures=0
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        local declared
        declared="$(_declared_globals "$f" | tr '()' '  ' | tr -s ' ')"
        local name
        while IFS= read -r name; do
            [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
            # Registry check (authoritative)
            if [[ " $registry " == *" $name "* ]]; then
                continue
            fi
            # Module-declared fallback
            if [[ " $declared " == *" $name "* ]]; then
                continue
            fi
            echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") touches undeclared global '$name'"
            failures=$((failures+1))
        done < <(_important_names_in_module "$f")
    done < <(_lib_modules)
    [[ $failures -eq 0 ]] || return 1
}

# ENV-128: every name listed under `## Reads:` must actually be referenced
# in the module body. Catches stale entries and typos in the header (e.g.
# declared `COL_MEAN` while the body reads `COL_MEANS`).
test_declared_reads_referenced () {
    local f failures=0
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        local entry name via
        while IFS= read -r entry; do
            [[ -z "$entry" ]] && continue
            name="${entry%%(*}"
            via=$(_section_via "$entry")
            _is_important_name "$name" || continue
            if [[ -n "$via" ]]; then
                # Annotated `(via FN)`: indirection is allowed iff the
                # module actually calls FN.
                if ! _module_calls_fn "$f" "$via"; then
                    echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") declares '## Reads: $name (via $via)' but doesn't call $via"
                    failures=$((failures+1))
                fi
                continue
            fi
            if ! _module_reads_name "$f" "$name"; then
                echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") declares '## Reads: $name' but doesn't reference \$$name"
                failures=$((failures+1))
            fi
        done < <(_tokenise_section "$f" "Reads")
    done < <(_lib_modules)
    [[ $failures -eq 0 ]] || return 1
}

# ENV-128: every name listed under `## Writes:` must actually be assigned in
# the module body, OR be reachable through a `(via FN)` indirection. Catches
# typos like `## Writes: dup_count` while the body writes to `dup_counts`.
test_declared_writes_assigned () {
    local f failures=0
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        local entry name via
        while IFS= read -r entry; do
            [[ -z "$entry" ]] && continue
            name="${entry%%(*}"
            via=$(_section_via "$entry")
            _is_important_name "$name" || continue
            if [[ -n "$via" ]]; then
                if ! _module_calls_fn "$f" "$via"; then
                    echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") declares '## Writes: $name (via $via)' but doesn't call $via"
                    failures=$((failures+1))
                fi
                continue
            fi
            if ! _module_writes_name "$f" "$name"; then
                echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") declares '## Writes: $name' but doesn't assign $name"
                failures=$((failures+1))
            fi
        done < <(_tokenise_section "$f" "Writes")
    done < <(_lib_modules)
    [[ $failures -eq 0 ]] || return 1
}

# ENV-128: union of all module Reads/Writes must be a subset of the registry
# in lib/_globals.sh. Adding a new cross-module global without registering
# it is now a hard failure.
test_registry_completeness () {
    local registry_text
    registry_text=$(< "$LIB_DIR/_globals.sh")
    local f entry name failures=0
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        local section
        for section in Reads Writes; do
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
                [[ -z "$entry" ]] && continue
                name="${entry%%(*}"
                _is_important_name "$name" || continue
                # The registry comments names like `# COL_MEAN=()` or
                # mentions them in prose. A simple word-boundary substring
                # check is enough Aje28094Aj false matches against random comment
                # text cost nothing here.
                if ! grep -qE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${name}([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" "$LIB_DIR/_globals.sh"; then
                    echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") $section: '$name' is not listed in lib/_globals.sh"
                    failures=$((failures+1))
                fi
            done < <(_tokenise_section "$f" "$section")
        done
    done < <(_lib_modules)
    [[ $failures -eq 0 ]] || return 1
}

# ENV-128 sabotage test: drop a copy of a real module into a tempdir with a
# deliberate Reads/Writes mismatch and confirm the new assertions fail with
# a useful message. Pins the contract end-to-end so a future `s/COL_MEAN/-/`
# refactor can't quietly weaken the check.
test_sabotage_typo_detected () {
    local tmpd
    tmpd=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/env128_sabotage.XXXXXX")
    # Use _correlation.sh as the victim Aje28094Aj it has a rich Reads list with
    # COL_MEAN, so renaming it to COL_MEANS in the body simulates the
    # exact typo class the ticket calls out.
    cp "$LIB_DIR/_correlation.sh" "$tmpd/_correlation.sh"
    sed -i 's/\$COL_MEAN\b/$COL_MEANS/g; s/\${COL_MEAN\b/${COL_MEANS/g' "$tmpd/_correlation.sh"

    # Run the per-name read check against just the sabotaged copy. We
    # inline the loop body rather than override `_lib_modules` because
    # the existing function declarations are seen by the test runner's
    # subshell only after this test function definition was parsed Aje28094Aj
    # function-level overrides in a subshell don't propagate across the
    # call boundary the way `local -n` would.
    local out=""
    local entry name via
    while IFS= read -r entry; do
        [[ -z "$entry" ]] && continue
        name="${entry%%(*}"
        via=$(_section_via "$entry")
        _is_important_name "$name" || continue
        if [[ -n "$via" ]]; then
            _module_calls_fn "$tmpd/_correlation.sh" "$via" || \
                out+="declares '## Reads: $name (via $via)' but doesn't call $via in $tmpd/_correlation.sh"$'\n'
            continue
        fi
        if ! _module_reads_name "$tmpd/_correlation.sh" "$name"; then
            out+="$(basename "$tmpd/_correlation.sh") declares '## Reads: $name' but doesn't reference \$$name"$'\n'
        fi
    done < <(_tokenise_section "$tmpd/_correlation.sh" "Reads")

    rm -rf "$tmpd"

    if [[ "$out" != *"COL_MEAN"* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: sabotage test did not flag the COL_MEAN/COL_MEANS swap"
        echo "    test output: $out"
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ "$out" != *"_correlation.sh"* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: sabotage error message must name the offending file"
        echo "    test output: $out"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_registry_file_exists () {
    [[ -f "$LIB_DIR/_globals.sh" ]] || {
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: _globals.sh missing"
        return 1
    }
    grep -q 'Global Variable Registry' "$LIB_DIR/_globals.sh" || {
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: _globals.sh lacks registry header"
        return 1
    }
}

################################################################################
## ENV-123: standalone awk programs in lib/awk/ must pass `awk -W lint`
##
## The `_numeric_combined_awk` body was extracted to
## `lib/awk/numeric_combined.awk` so editors and lint can see it. This
## test gates the file against gawk's `--lint` so any future edit that
## introduces an uninitialized read or untyped for-loop is caught at CI
## time rather than on first column-with-no-data.
################################################################################

test_awk_files_pass_lint () {
    local awk_dir="$LIB_DIR/awk"
    if [[ ! -d "$awk_dir" ]]; then
        # No standalone awk programs yet Aje28094Aj vacuously pass.
        return 0
    fi
    # gawk-only check; if /usr/bin/awk is mawk or similar, skip cleanly.
    # Materialised (no `| grep -q` under pipefail Aje28094Aj see _module_reads_name).
    local awk_version
    awk_version=$(awk --version 2>&1 || true)
    if ! grep -qiE "^GNU Awk|^awk version.*GNU" <<< "$awk_version"; then
        echo "  (skipping: gawk not available Aje28094Aj using ${awk_version%%$'\n'*})"
        return 0
    fi
    local f rc=0
    for f in "$awk_dir"/*.awk; do
        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
        local out
        # Pass dummy values for every -v that the program uses, so lint
        # doesn't flag the parameters as uninitialized. The program itself
        # is responsible for initialising any other variables in BEGIN.
        # Filter out gawk's `data file '-' is empty` notice Aje28094Aj that warns
        # only that we passed `</dev/null` to satisfy the data-file slot,
        # which has no bearing on the script's lint-cleanliness.
        out=$(awk -W lint \
            -v col=1 -v mn=0 -v mx=1 -v mean=0 -v std=1 \
            -v skip=1 -v maxn=10 -v tmpfile=/dev/null \
            -v benford_crit=15.507 \
            -f "$f" </dev/null 2>&1 >/dev/null \
            | grep -vE "warning: data file \`-' is empty" || true)
        if [[ -n "$out" ]]; then
            echo "  ASSERT FAILED: $(basename "$f") emits lint warnings:"
            printf '    %s\n' "$out"
            rc=1
        fi
    done
    return $rc
}

run_test "ENV-066 every lib/*.sh has Reads:/Writes: header" test_each_module_has_contract_headers
run_test "ENV-066 referenced globals are in registry or declared" test_all_referenced_globals_in_registry
run_test "ENV-066 _globals.sh registry exists" test_registry_file_exists
run_test "ENV-128 declared Reads names are referenced in body" test_declared_reads_referenced
run_test "ENV-128 declared Writes names are assigned in body" test_declared_writes_assigned
run_test "ENV-128 module Reads/Writes are listed in lib/_globals.sh" test_registry_completeness
run_test "ENV-128 sabotage: COL_MEAN -> COL_MEANS typo detected" test_sabotage_typo_detected
run_test "ENV-123 standalone awk files pass gawk --lint" test_awk_files_pass_lint

print_summary
===END===

test_compare_no_early_exit_in_pipe () {
    # Regression guard: under `set -euo pipefail`, an awk that exits before
    # consuming all of a piped `echo` can leave `echo` with SIGPIPE (141),
    # which pipefail+set -e turn into a comparison-aborting failure. That flaked
    # the "compare same file" test on Alpine. Keep the match-row awk free of an
    # early `exit` so the upstream pipe always drains.
    local lib="$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/_compare.sh"
    if grep -nE 'echo .*\| *awk[^|]*exit' "$lib"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: _compare.sh pipes echo into an early-exit awk (SIGPIPE/pipefail hazard)"
        return 1
    fi
}
