===FILE-ESC: analyze/tests/test_numeric_exclusions.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=58d21a6898ca5da01683246567d59f8dfdaefd83de66531d3e6f7dba27317c09===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Numeric-column exclusion visibility (ENV-132)
##
## When envoy-analyze classifies a column as numeric (Aje289a5Aj80% of values parse
## as numbers, the remaining Aje289a4Aj20% are non-numeric), the mean/std are
## computed from the numeric subset only and the rest are silently dropped.
## Pre-ENV-132 the user had no way to tell.
##
## This test asserts:
##   1. A clean (100% numeric) column produces no exclusion annotation.
##   2. An 80/20 column produces a "Note: N non-numeric value(s) excluded"
##      line in the Summary stats item.
##   3. --strict on a clean column exits 0; --strict on the 80/20 column
##      exits 1 with a message naming the dirty column.
################################################################################

set -u
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ANALYZE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../envoy-analyze"

pass=0
fail=0
fail_msgs=()

_check () {
    local name="$1" cond="$2" details="${3:-}"
    if [[ "$cond" == "1" ]]; then
        pass=$((pass + 1))
    else
        fail=$((fail + 1))
        fail_msgs+=("$name${details:+: $details}")
    fi
}

sandbox=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$sandbox"' EXIT

# Build the fixtures fresh so the test is self-contained.
cat >"$sandbox/clean.csv" <<'EOF'
id,score
1,10
2,20
3,30
4,40
5,50
EOF

cat >"$sandbox/dirty.csv" <<'EOF'
id,score
a,10
b,20
c,30
d,40
e,50
f,60
g,70
h,80
i,broken
j,broken
EOF

##############################################################################
# 1. Clean column Aje28692Aj no Note line
##############################################################################
out=$(bash "$ANALYZE" --all "$sandbox/clean.csv" 2>&1)
_check "clean column shows Mean" \
    "$([[ "$out" == *"Mean: "* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
_check "clean column produces NO non-numeric Note line" \
    "$([[ "$out" != *"non-numeric value"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"

##############################################################################
# 2. 80/20 column Aje28692Aj exclusion annotation in Summary stats
##############################################################################
out=$(bash "$ANALYZE" --all "$sandbox/dirty.csv" 2>&1)
_check "dirty column still classified numeric (Mean shows)" \
    "$([[ "$out" == *"Mean: 45"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
_check "dirty column shows non-numeric exclusion count" \
    "$([[ "$out" == *"2 non-numeric value(s) excluded"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)" \
    "expected 'Note: 2 non-numeric value(s) excluded' in: $(echo "$out" | grep -A2 'Summary stats')"
_check "dirty column shows numeric percentage" \
    "$([[ "$out" == *"80.00% numeric"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"

##############################################################################
# 3. --strict
##############################################################################
bash "$ANALYZE" --strict "$sandbox/clean.csv" >/dev/null 2>&1
rc=$?
_check "--strict on clean column exits 0" \
    "$([[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "rc=$rc"

err=$(bash "$ANALYZE" --strict "$sandbox/dirty.csv" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
rc=$?
_check "--strict on dirty column exits non-zero" \
    "$([[ $rc -ne 0 ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "rc=$rc"
_check "--strict error mentions the dirty column name" \
    "$([[ "$err" == *"score"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "$err"
_check "--strict error mentions the non-numeric count" \
    "$([[ "$err" == *"2 non-numeric"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "$err"

total=$((pass + fail))
echo ""
echo "Results: $pass/$total passed, $fail failed"
if (( fail > 0 )); then
    printf '  - %s\n' "${fail_msgs[@]}" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "All tests passed."
===END===
===FILE: analyze/tests/test_performance.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=c0b94a18ee1529994dfb1edd8cc8d320632940edc2946015dbe074503f894133===
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=helpers.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

################################################################################
## Performance regression tests
##
## Verifies envoy-analyze completes within time limits on generated datasets.
## Skip with: MDA_SKIP_PERF=1
################################################################################

if [[ "${MDA_SKIP_PERF:-0}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo "Performance tests skipped (MDA_SKIP_PERF=1)"
    exit 0
fi

generate_csv () {
    local rows="$1"
    local cols="$2"
    local output="$3"
    awk -v rows="$rows" -v cols="$cols" '
    BEGIN {
        srand(42)
        for (c=1; c<=cols; c++) {
            if (c>1) printf ","
            printf "col%d", c
        }
        print ""
        for (r=1; r<=rows; r++) {
            for (c=1; c<=cols; c++) {
                if (c>1) printf ","
                printf "%d", r*c + int(rand()*100)
            }
            print ""
        }
    }' > "$output"
}

test_perf_1k_rows () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t perf-1k.XXXXXX.csv)
    generate_csv 1000 5 "$tmp"
    local start end elapsed
    start=$(date +%s)
    run_mda "$tmp" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
    end=$(date +%s)
    elapsed=$((end - start))
    rm -f "$tmp"
    if [[ "$elapsed" -gt 10 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: 1K rows should complete in <10s, took ${elapsed}s"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_perf_5k_rows () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t perf-5k.XXXXXX.csv)
    generate_csv 5000 5 "$tmp"
    local start end elapsed
    start=$(date +%s)
    run_mda "$tmp" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
    end=$(date +%s)
    elapsed=$((end - start))
    rm -f "$tmp"
    if [[ "$elapsed" -gt 30 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: 5K rows should complete in <30s, took ${elapsed}s"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_perf_wide () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -t perf-wide.XXXXXX.csv)
    generate_csv 500 20 "$tmp"
    local start end elapsed
    start=$(date +%s)
    run_mda "$tmp" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
    end=$(date +%s)
    elapsed=$((end - start))
    rm -f "$tmp"
    if [[ "$elapsed" -gt 10 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: 500 rows x 20 cols should complete in <10s, took ${elapsed}s"
        return 1
    fi
}

########################################
## Run all performance tests
##

run_test "1K rows 5 cols in <10s" test_perf_1k_rows
run_test "5K rows 5 cols in <30s" test_perf_5k_rows
run_test "500 rows 20 cols in <10s" test_perf_wide

print_summary
===END===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: ENV-135 progress indicator in envoy-analyze.
##
## Mirrors EnvoyExtract/tests/test_progress.sh but for the per-column
## stats stage. The shared helper at lib/envoy_progress.sh is the same
## code path; we re-test here to pin the analyze-side wiring.
################################################################################
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

EA="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/envoy-analyze"
SAMPLE="$SAMPLES_DIR/biostats.csv"

# Wrapper that suppresses the unrelated awk/gawk warnings so progress
# parsing works even with mawk in CI.
_run_ea () {
    ENVOY_ANALYZE_SUPPRESS_AWK_WARNING=1 "$@"
}

################################################################################
## --progress emits per-column lines on stderr (non-TTY path)
################################################################################

test_progress_per_column_lines () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(_run_ea bash "$EA" --progress "$SAMPLE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "analyze should still succeed with --progress"
    # `[n/N] stats: <colname>` is the per-column tick format.
    if ! grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\] stats: ' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --progress should emit '[n/N] stats: <col>' lines"
        echo "  stderr (first 200): $(printf '%s' "$err" | head -c 200)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## TTY mode uses CR for in-place updates
################################################################################

test_progress_uses_cr_on_tty () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 _run_ea bash "$EA" --progress "$SAMPLE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "analyze should still succeed with TTY-forced progress"
    if [[ "$err" != *$'\r'* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: TTY progress should contain a CR for in-place updates"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Suppression knobs
################################################################################

test_no_progress_suppresses () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 _run_ea bash "$EA" --no-progress "$SAMPLE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\] stats:' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --no-progress should suppress ticks"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_envoy_no_progress_beats_progress () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1 _run_ea bash "$EA" --progress "$SAMPLE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\] stats:' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1 should beat --progress"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_envoy_quiet_suppresses () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 _run_ea bash "$EA" --quiet --progress "$SAMPLE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\] stats:' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --quiet should suppress progress"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_default_non_tty_silent () {
    # No flag and no forced TTY Aje28692Aj biostats.csv (5 columns) should be silent.

test_below_threshold_silent_on_tty () {
    # biostats.csv has 5 columns Aje28094Aj below the 20-column auto threshold.
    # On a forced TTY without --progress, no ticks should appear.
    local err rc=0
    err=$(ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 _run_ea bash "$EA" "$SAMPLE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\] stats:' <<< "$err"; then

        return 1
    fi
}

    local with without
    with=$(_run_ea bash "$EA" --progress "$SAMPLE" 2>/dev/null)
    without=$(_run_ea bash "$EA" --no-progress "$SAMPLE" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ "$with" != "$without" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --progress altered stdout payload"
        return 1
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash
# ENV-063: --head N / --sample N / --seed flags
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

SAMPLE="$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv"  # 31 rows

test_head_n_rows () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --head 10 "$SAMPLE")
    assert_contains "$out" "Rows: 10" "--head 10 should analyse 10 rows"
    assert_contains "$out" "Sampling: (first 10 of 31 rows)" "banner should note sampling"
}

test_sample_deterministic () {
    local a b
    a=$(run_mda --sample 10 --seed 42 "$SAMPLE" | grep -E '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.')
    b=$(run_mda --sample 10 --seed 42 "$SAMPLE" | grep -E '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.')
    if [[ "$a" != "$b" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --sample with the same seed must be deterministic"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_sample_banner () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --sample 10 --seed 42 "$SAMPLE")
    assert_contains "$out" "Sampling: (random sample 10 of 31 rows, seed=42)" "banner must note sample + seed"
}

test_head_and_sample_mutually_exclusive () {
    local out code=0
    out=$(run_mda --head 5 --sample 5 "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --head + --sample should error"; return 1; }
    assert_contains "$out" "mutually exclusive" "error message should be explicit"
}

test_invalid_n_rejected () {
    local out code=0
    out=$(run_mda --head abc "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --head abc should error"; return 1; }
    out=$(run_mda --head 0 "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --head 0 should error"; return 1; }
    out=$(run_mda --sample -1 "$SAMPLE" 2>&1) || code=$?
    [[ $code -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --sample -1 should error"; return 1; }
}

test_stdin_head () {
    local out
    out=$(cat "$SAMPLE" | run_mda --head 5)
    assert_contains "$out" "Rows: 5" "--head works over stdin"
}

test_head_json_has_banner () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mda --head 10 --format json "$SAMPLE")
    assert_contains "$out" "first 10 of 31 rows" "JSON overview item should note sampling"
}

run_test "ENV-063 --head N limits to N data rows" test_head_n_rows
run_test "ENV-063 --sample N with --seed is deterministic" test_sample_deterministic
run_test "ENV-063 --sample banner includes seed" test_sample_banner
run_test "ENV-063 --head and --sample are mutually exclusive" test_head_and_sample_mutually_exclusive
run_test "ENV-063 invalid N values rejected" test_invalid_n_rejected

test_threshold_pass () {

test_threshold_fail () {
    local output code=0

    output=$(run_mda --threshold "Index>50" "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" --all 2>/dev/null) || code=$?
    assert_contains "$output" "FAIL" "should show FAIL verdict"
    if [[ $code -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: threshold should fail with exit code 1"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_threshold_exit_code_pass () {
    local code=0
    run_mda --threshold "Index>0" "$SAMPLES_DIR/trees.csv" --all 2>/dev/null || code=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$code" "exit code should be 0 on pass"
}

test_threshold_exit_code_fail () {
    local code=0

        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: exit code should be 1 on fail, got $code"
        return 1
    fi
}

    fi

===META: mode=644 sha256=2687a67e08f6cdc0960a23bc87babb649599579fd6c6afb6455d367daff132a8===
# bash completion for glean Aje28094Aj source this file, or drop it in
# /etc/bash_completion.d/ (the installer does this).
_glean_complete () {
    local cur prev words cword
    _init_completion 2>/dev/null || {
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"; prev="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}"
        cword=$COMP_CWORD
    }

    local verbs="run inject source control uncontrol instances export import log restore ls show rm stats triage doctor help"
    local ws="${GLEAN_WORKSPACE:-${GLEAN_HOME:-$HOME/.glean}}"

    # First word: complete the verb.
    if [[ $cword -eq 1 ]]; then
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$verbs" -- "$cur") )
        return
    fi

    local verb="${COMP_WORDS[1]}"
    case "$verb" in
        show|stats|rm|delete|drop)
            # complete dataset names from the active store (rm also offers flags)
            case "$cur" in
                -*) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "-f --yes --purge --no-purge --keep-captures --help" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
            esac
            local ds
            ds="$(cd "$ws/datasets" 2>/dev/null && ls -1 *.tsv 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\.tsv$//')"
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$ds" -- "$cur") ) ;;
        restore)
            local caps
            caps="latest $(cd "$ws/captures" 2>/dev/null && ls -1d c* 2>/dev/null)"
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$caps" -- "$cur") ) ;;
        control|uncontrol|import|export)
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -o default -- "$cur") ) ;;   # paths
        run|inject)
            case "$cur" in
                -*) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "--silent --min-confidence --plugin-dir --async --sync --help" -- "$cur") ) ;;
                *)  COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -c -- "$cur") ) ;;    # a command to run
            esac ;;
        *) COMPREPLY=() ;;
    esac
}
complete -F _glean_complete glean
===END===

# Proposal 0001 Aje28094Aj Rename Envoy to **Glean** and rebuild as a minimal single-binary tool

- **Status:** Draft (for discussion)
- **Date:** 2026-07-04
- **Branch:** `claude/extraction-feature-naming-2d16xi`
- **Author:** scoped with Claude
- **Supersedes:** the three-binary `envoy-*` product shape

---

## 1. Summary

Retire the **Envoy** suite (three binaries, ~55 subcommands, satellite tools, and a
3,500-file scenario corpus) and replace it with a single rebranded tool, **Glean**,
built fresh in a new `glean/` tree. Glean keeps only the one workflow the product is
actually about:

> **Pipe command output in Aje28692Aj auto-detect its format Aje28692Aj present it as a clean, typed dataset Aje28692Aj optionally analyze it.**

This is today's `envoy-capture inject` path, promoted to be *the* product.

Confirmed decisions driving this proposal:

1. **Rename the binaries *and* rebrand** Aje28094Aj `envoy-*` Aje28692Aj `glean`. Not a doc-only reskin.
2. **Keep all 198 extract strategies** Aje28094Aj the "throw anything at it" auto-detect breadth is the value.
3. **Keep analyze** Aje28094Aj statistics stay in-tool.
4. **New tree** Aje28094Aj build `glean/` fresh from the one path rather than mutating the `Envoy*` trees in place.

---

## 2. Why

The current repo has accreted far past its core. The scenario we care about Aje28094Aj
auto-capture-format + present-dataset Aje28094Aj is a single path through three binaries:

| Today | Lines / surface |
|---|---|
| `envoy-capture` | 347 lines, **40 subcommands** |
| `envoy-extract` | 794 lines, 198 strategies, ~40 flags, 6 subcommands |
| `envoy-analyze` | 1,411 lines, ~9 analysis modes |
| satellites | `envoy-browse`, `envoy-filedb`, `envoy-tnt` |
| `scenarios/` | 3,575 files (3,269 "Generic") Aje28094Aj most of the repo by file count |

Most of `envoy-capture`'s 40 verbs (`goto`/`next`/`prev`/`home`, `watch`, `process`,
`scripts`, `results`, `merge`, `search`, `tag`/`untag`, `register`, `archive`,
`push`/`pull`, `gc`, `verify`, `destroy`, Aje280a6Aj) are navigation, lifecycle, and
git-plumbing surface that the core scenario never touches. Cutting to the one path
removes the maintenance surface without removing the product.

**Why a fresh tree, not a mutation:** the cut commands share library code with the
kept path, so "delete 50 verbs" means tracing shared internals Aje28094Aj slow and error-prone.
Adding ~6 verbs to a clean tree that reuses the extract engine and the tidy-melt
presenter is far cleaner than deleting 50 from the existing one.

---

## 3. The name

**Glean** Aje28094Aj to gather what's worth keeping from a field of raw material. It describes
what auto-detection actually does: *purposeful selection* of structure from noisy
command output (strategy dispatch + confidence scoring), as opposed to Sift's passive
"let it fall through a mesh." Short, lowercase, four letters, types fast as a CLI
prefix, no known collision with an existing terminal tool, and it passes the tagline
test with no explanation: **"Glean turns command output into data."**

---

## 4. Target command surface

One binary, `glean`. The pipe *is* the capture; auto-detect *is* the extract; `show`
*is* the present. No `init` Aje28094Aj the workspace auto-creates on first use.

```bash
# THE core verb Aje28094Aj capture + auto-detect + present into a typed dataset
free -m | glean                 # routed by detected type Aje28692Aj dataset 'free'
df -h   | glean
cat metrics.txt | glean --silent

glean ls                        # list datasets: name, type, rows, cleanliness
glean show free                 # present one dataset as a tidy table
glean triage                    # low-confidence / unmatched bucket
glean stats free                # statistics on a dataset (survivor of envoy-analyze)

glean doctor                    # dependency / environment check
glean help
```

That is the entire surface: **default verb + 5 subcommands + doctor/help.**

### 4.1 Command mapping (Envoy Aje28692Aj Glean)

| Glean | Replaces | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `glean` (default, stdin) | `envoy-capture inject` | extract Aje28692Aj classify Aje28692Aj route Aje28692Aj record, in one step |
| `glean ls` | `envoy-capture dataset` / `list` | list datasets with cleanliness score |
| `glean show <name>` | `envoy-capture show` + tidy present | one dataset as a tidy table |
| `glean triage` | `envoy-capture triage` | unmatched / low-confidence rows |
| `glean stats <name>` | `envoy-analyze` (core modes) | stats / summary / correlation / anomaly kept; browse UI dropped |
| `glean doctor` | `envoy-capture doctor` | dependency + wiring check |
| *(none)* | `init` | implicit Aje28094Aj auto-create workspace on first `glean` |

### 4.2 Explicitly dropped

`run`, `watch`, `process`/`reprocess`, `scripts`, `results`, `goto`/`next`/`prev`/`home`,
`search`, `log`, `diff`, `merge`, `rename`, `tag`/`tags`/`untag`, `register`/`unregister`,
`dirs`, `archive`/`archives`, `push`/`pull`, `gc`, `verify`, `destroy`, `export`, and the
satellites `envoy-browse` / `envoy-filedb` / `envoy-tnt`.

The `envoy-extract` engine is **kept in full** (all 198 strategies) but is no longer a
user-facing binary Aje28094Aj it becomes the internal auto-detect library behind `glean`. Its
power-user flags (`--strategy`, `--min-confidence`, `--rename`, `--chain`, Aje280a6Aj) may be
exposed as advanced flags on the default verb; default UX stays flagless.

## 5a. Store model (added after the git-core directive)

The user's "git core" directive expanded the store requirements beyond a simple
capture-commit. The model, built in stages:

- **Row Aje28692Aj source traceability.** Every dataset row carries a globally-unique,
  **visible** `#N` index (first column). `glean source <#N>` maps it back to the
  exact captured input that produced it (`provenance.tsv` Aje28692Aj `captures/<id>/output.txt`).
- **Global store by default.** Captures go to `$GLEAN_HOME` (or `~/.glean`) so a
  user need not be in any particular directory. `GLEAN_WORKSPACE` is an explicit
  override. A shared, group-writable `GLEAN_HOME` supports multiple users; a
  `mkdir` lock + double-checked `git init` serialise concurrent writers.
- **Controlled directories** *(Stage B)*. `glean control <dir>` marks a directory
  as its own capture instance; commands run within it (or a subdir) route there,
  and the commit's context includes the directory's contents. Resolution walks up
  from CWD to find a controlling instance, else falls back to the global store.
- **Export / import** *(Stage C)*. Bundle an instance (datasets + capture commits)
  into a portable file, import it into another repository, and browse it there
  with the same `ls`/`show`/`log`/`source`/`restore`.

Status: **Stages A, B, C all done.** Stage A Aje28094Aj global store, per-row provenance,
multi-user lock (verified under 8-way concurrency). Stage B Aje28094Aj `control`/`instances`/
`uncontrol`, CWD walk-up resolution, directory-context snapshots. Stage C Aje28094Aj
`export`/`import` via `git bundle` (datasets + capture log + per-row provenance
survive the move). Verified end-to-end by `glean/tests/smoke.sh` (27 checks).

## 6. The rename plane

Renaming the binaries touches nearly every file. Inventory of what must move together
so CI stays green:

- **Binary + prefix:** `envoy-capture`/`-extract`/`-analyze` Aje28692Aj `glean`; all internal
  `envoy_*` lib source names and sourced paths.
- **Env vars:** `CAPTURE_INJECT_MIN_CONFIDENCE`, `CAPTURE_INJECT_VARIANT_OVERLAP`, and
  siblings Aje28692Aj `GLEAN_*`. Provide a one-release compatibility shim that reads the old
  names with a deprecation warning.
- **Man pages:** regenerate via the generator (CI enforces drift-free man pages); one
  `glean.1` replaces six.
- **Completions:** one `glean.*` set replaces the per-tool completions.
- **Packaging / install:** `install.sh`, `packaging/`, `pyproject.toml`, `VERSION`
  wiring, `release.sh`.
- **CI gates that will fail if not updated in-step:**
  - `Handoff Check` Aje28094Aj every top-level dir needs `HANDOFF.md`; the new `glean/` dir must ship one in its first commit.
  - New-top-level-dir rule Aje28094Aj `glean/` needs `HANDOFF.md` **and** `CHANGELOG.md` in the same commit as its first tracked file.
  - Man-page drift test.
  - The three subproject CHANGELOG enforcement Aje28094Aj retired along with the `Envoy*` dirs.
- **Docs / README:** rewrite the three-stage "Capture Aje28692Aj Extract Aje28692Aj Analyze" framing into
  the single-tool `glean` story; keep the pipeline as an internal concept.

## 7. Phased plan

Each phase is independently reviewable; the repo stays shippable between phases.

**Phase 0 Aje28094Aj Proposal & sign-off** (this document).

**Phase 1 Aje28094Aj New tree skeleton.** Aje29c85Aj *Done Aje28094Aj see `glean/`.* Entry point implements the
default verb (`| glean`) plus `ls`/`show`/`triage`/`doctor`/`help`, wiring the real
extract engine via `--emit-meta`, tidy-melt present, and a minimal flat-TSV store.
`glean/tests/smoke.sh` passes; the new dir ships `HANDOFF.md` + `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Phase 2 Aje28094Aj Carry the engine.** Aje29c85Aj *Done.* Vendored `EnvoyExtract`'s entry point +
`lib/` + all 202 strategies + `tools/` + tests + samples under **`glean/extract/`**, and
the cross-suite shared libs (`envoy_*.sh`) under **`glean/lib/`** (the engine's `../lib`),
via `glean/tools/sync-extract.sh` (re-syncable from an upstream checkout;
`VENDOR.json` records the source SHA). Full vendored suite green: **216/216 test files,
1103 assertions, 0 failed**. `glean` resolves the vendored engine first. Two fixes found
along the way: an upstream test portability bug (hardcoded `EnvoyExtract/` path Aje28692Aj resolved
relative to the test dir), and a first-cut layout error (engine at `lib/extract/` left its
`../lib` at `lib/lib` and under-vendored the shared libs + `tools/` Aje28094Aj corrected to the
`extract/` + `lib/` layout above).

> **Layout amendment to Ajc2a7Aj5:** the engine lives at top-level `glean/extract/` (not
> `glean/lib/extract/`) so its `../lib` resolves cleanly to `glean/lib/`, matching how the
> engine finds its shared libs upstream. Future components (capture/present/analyze) follow
> the same top-level pattern.

**Phase 3 Aje28094Aj The verbs + git core.** *In progress.* `ls`, `show`, `triage`, `doctor`,
`log`, `restore`, and `run` implemented; tidy-melt presenter ported. The **git core is
done**: the workspace is a git repo, every capture is one commit tagged `capture-<id>`,
`glean run` captures a binary's output as a commit and `glean restore` brings it back up
(a deliberate simplification of EnvoyCapture's per-run + `__dataset`/`__results`/`__scripts`
orphan-branch store down to one linear commit-per-capture history).
*Remaining:* `stats` (vendor envoy-analyze under `glean/analyze/`) and schema
reconciliation (union columns instead of the `.v2` variant split).

**Phase 4 Aje28094Aj Rename plane.** Aje29c85Aj *Done.* glean's own surface is entirely `GLEAN_*`;
shipped `glean/README.md`, `glean/completions/glean.bash`, `glean/man/glean.1`, and
`glean/install.sh` (installs in place + drops completion/man, `--uninstall`). Fixed a
symlink-safety bug (glean now resolves its real dir via `GLEAN_ROOT` so it finds its
vendored trees when run through a PATH symlink). The melt/transform was also imported
from source (`glean/transform/melt.sh` via `tools/sync-melt.sh`) rather than hand-copied.

**Phase 5 Aje28094Aj Retire Envoy.** *Superseded by the standalone-repo split (2026-07-05):*
`glean` was extracted into its own repository instead of hard-cutting the `Envoy*`
trees in place, so the vendored trees here are already canonical. Removing the
`Envoy*` trees, satellites, and their CI gates is now a task in the upstream Envoy
monorepo, not this repo Aje28094Aj out of scope here.

## 8. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cut commands share library code with the kept path | Fresh tree copies only what the kept path needs; nothing to untangle |
| Users/scripts depend on `envoy-*` names or env vars | Env-var compat shim for one release; document the rename; keep `envoy-*` as thin deprecated wrappers for one release if desired |
| Strategy suite regresses when relocated | Move tests with sources in Phase 2; gate the phase on a green suite |
| Losing history/value in `scenarios/` | Archive to a sibling repo, don't delete (open question 6.4) |
| Man-page / HANDOFF / CHANGELOG CI gates fail mid-migration | Phase boundaries chosen so each lands its required docs in the same commit |

---

## 9. Non-goals

- No change to the extraction *strategies* themselves or their detection behavior.
- No new analysis capability Aje28094Aj analyze is carried, not extended.
- Not removing git-based storage; only the user-facing plumbing verbs around it.
- Not a rewrite in another language Aje28094Aj this stays Bash + the existing engine.

---

2. **Advanced extract flags** on the default verb (`--strategy`, `--min-confidence`,
   `--chain`) Aje28094Aj expose now, or keep the surface flagless until asked?
3. **Analyze scope** Aje28094Aj keep all core modes (stats/summary/correlation/anomaly) or trim
   to `stats`/`summary` only?
4. ~~**`scenarios/` / `web/` / `tickets/`**~~ **Resolved: archive** to a sibling repo (do not delete).
5. **Repo identity** Aje28094Aj new `glean` repo, or rebrand this repo in place and prune?

## 11. Success criteria

- A single `glean` binary implements the full scenario end-to-end: `cmd | glean`,
  `ls`, `show`, `triage`, `stats`.
- All 198 strategies pass their suite in the new tree.
- One man page, one completion set, green CI (Handoff Check, man-page drift, changelog).

- README tells one story: *Glean turns command output into data.*

batch-jobs, bpftrace, brew-outdated-sparse, btrfs-balance-status,

lists Aje28094Aj output byte-identical to r2, reviewer standards sharpened.

**Done this round:** batch-jobs REMOVED from the corpus per the reviewer
("REMOVE THIS ONE" Aje28094Aj the input is an error message, not data). Corpus
3706 Aje28692Aj 3705.

**Refined guidance folded into open rounds:**

  ("most info missing"), ansible-v ("[core 2.17.1] one column"),
  apachectl-S ("info is in the column headers"), apachebench (connection-

# Design note 0002 Aje28094Aj Tidy-first output, and spreadsheet-style names for nameless columns

- **Status:** Adopted
- **Date:** 2026-07-09
- **Branch:** `claude/project-state-assessment-5x589r`
- **Author:** scoped with Claude
- **Relates to:** [docs/columnar-specs-engine.md](columnar-specs-engine.md) (the migration
  machinery this note reframes the *goal* of)

---

## 1. Summary

Two connected decisions:

1. **Judge output on its own tidy/meaningful merits Aje28094Aj not on byte-fidelity to a
   bespoke parser.** For most of this project the yardstick was "does the generic
   parser reproduce the hand-written per-tool parser's bytes exactly?" That yardstick
   makes the bespoke the source of truth and caps generic coverage at whatever the
   bespokes already did. We drop it. The question is now simply: *is the emitted table
   tidy (one row per record, columns cleanly separated, values intact) and usable?*

2. **Name genuinely-nameless columns `A,B,CAje280a6Aj,Z,AA,BB,CCAje280a6Aj` instead of `c1,c2,c3Aje280a6Aj`.**
   Same information, better affordance (details in Ajc2a7Aj3).

Neither decision changes how any input is *parsed*. They change what we *measure* and
how we *label*. The practical payoff is that the ~12 generic parsers plus positional
labels already produce tidy, usable output for the overwhelming majority of tools, so
the bespoke-per-tool count can keep falling without chasing byte-parity.

---

## 2. Why drop byte-fidelity as the goal

The `columnar-specs` migration (doc 0001-era work, see the engine note) drove the
strategy count 407 Aje28692Aj ~374 by re-expressing bespoke parsers as one-line declarative
specs, each verified **byte-identical** to the bespoke before retiring it. That
discipline was correct *for a migration* Aje28094Aj it guaranteed no output changed. But as a
long-term goal it has a ceiling: it treats the bespoke as ground truth, so a generic
parser can never be judged *better* than the bespoke, only *equal*. A close audit put
the clean 1:1 ceiling at ~374 (173 strategies are generic multi-tool parsers that
can't be migrated 1:1 without regressing *other* tools; 158 have no corpus input to
verify against; the rest each need a bespoke engine feature).

The reframe: a tidy table with positional columns is a *good* result even when no
bespoke exists and even when it differs from the bespoke's bytes. Measuring against
"tidy + usable" instead of "byte-identical" removes the ceiling Aje28094Aj the generic parsers
are allowed to be the answer.

### Goldens change role, not existence

We keep both golden sets (`extract/tests/golden/`, `tests/corpus/expected/`), but their
job changes from **spec** to **regression snapshot**. They no longer encode "the
bespoke's exact bytes are correct"; they encode "this is the current output Aje28094Aj tell me
precisely if it moves." When we *intend* to improve output we regenerate them
(`run.sh --update-golden`, `verify_strategy_outputs.sh --update`); when output moves and
we *didn't* intend it, that diff is a caught bug. This note's own change exercised that:
the `c1Aje28692AjA` rename surfaced as a clean header-only diff on exactly 224 corpus + 17
extract goldens, which is how we proved it touched *only* labels and nothing else.

---

## 3. Nameless columns: `A,B,C` over `c1,c2,c3`

When a source genuinely has no column names (e.g. `aa-unconfined`, `ssh-keygen -l`,
`pacman -Qm`), glean must still label the columns it split out. It used to emit
`c1,c2,c3Aje280a6Aj`. It now emits `A,B,CAje280a6Aj,Z,AA,BB,CCAje280a6Aj` (repeated-letter convention past 26).

The information content is identical. The difference is affordance:

- `c1` reads as an **apologetic internal placeholder** Aje28094Aj "we tried to name this and
  failed." It looks like a leaked implementation detail.
- `A` reads as the **universal spreadsheet convention** Aje28094Aj every user already knows it
  means "unnamed column, in position 1; name it yourself if you want." It signals
  *intended positional labeling*, not *failed naming*.

Implementation: one helper, `_col_letter <1-based index>`, in `extract/lib/_helpers.sh`
(1Aje28692AjA Aje280a6Aj 26Aje28692AjZ, 27Aje28692AjAA, 28Aje28692AjBB Aje280a6Aj; self-tested through AAA), wired into the six generic
parsers that mint nameless labels (`aligned-columns`, `colon-fields`, `line-records`,
`text-lines`, `psql-table` header-fallback, `structured/tsv`), the five
`columnar-specs` `@line` specs, and 14 single-column columnar bespokes. Mawk-safe,
POSIX-ish, no new dependency.

---

## 4. What the re-score shows Aje28094Aj and what it *doesn't*

A crude tidiness scorer (`score_one.sh`) classifies each tool's generic-mode output as
MEANINGFUL / GENERIC / BLOB / PARTIAL / EMPTY, where "generic" meant a column labeled
`cN`/`entryN`/a bare number. Re-scoring all 1040 corpus tools before vs after the
rename:

| Category   | Before (`c1,c2`) | After (`A,B,C`) |
|------------|:---:|:---:|
| MEANINGFUL | 780 | 1013 |
| GENERIC    | 148 | 7   |
| BLOB       | 92  | 0   |
| PARTIAL    | 19  | 19  |
| EMPTY      | 1   | 1   |

Transition matrix: **141 GENERICAje28692AjMEANINGFUL, 92 BLOBAje28692AjMEANINGFUL, 807 unchanged, zero
regressions.**

**Read this honestly.** The 233-tool flip is *largely a labeling artifact*: the scorer
defined "meaningful" as "the label isn't `cN`," so renaming `cN`Aje28692Aj`A` mechanically
reclassifies those columns without changing a single value. What the flip actually
reveals is that the metric was really measuring *"does glean emit an apologetic
placeholder,"* not *"are these columns semantically named."* Removing the placeholder
makes the metric go green Aje28094Aj which is a fair signal that the placeholder was the thing
making the output *look* unfinished, but **not** a claim that 233 tools gained semantic
column names. (The 7 tools still scoring GENERIC emit *bare-numeric* keys from a
different path Aje28094Aj `json` array-flattening and `indented-hierarchy` Aje28094Aj outside this
change's scope.)

---

## 5. The trustworthy signal: an LLM-judge pass

Because the mechanical score can't tell "positionally labeled but tidy" from
"semantically named," we ran an independent LLM-judge validation over a deterministic
21-tool sample drawn from the tools that actually exercise the nameless-column path.
Three blind judges rated each on two orthogonal axes Aje28094Aj **tidy** (one row per record,
clean split, values intact) and **usable** (could a user work with this table).
Aggregate: **13/21 tidy, 15/21 usable.**

The decisive finding is *why* the other cases fell short: **every** shortfall is an
orthogonal, pre-existing parser-routing issue that has nothing to do with column
labels Aje28094Aj

- colon `key : value` blocks routed to `text-lines` instead of `colon-fields`
  (`chage-l`, `redis-info-memory`),
- a separator token kept as its own noise column (`docker-port`'s `->`,
  `getsebool-a`'s `-->`, `ip-netns-list`'s `(id: N)`),
- space-separated numeric blobs left unsplit (`proc-stat`),
- tree hierarchy flattened (`poetry-show-tree`), and ragged keyword fields (`tc-class`).

None of these are caused Aje28094Aj or cured Aje28094Aj by the `c1Aje28692AjA` rename; they are the genuine
remaining parser-quality tail. Where the split *is* sensible, the judges confirmed the
positional `A,B,C` output is fully usable (`gsutil-du`, `jq`, `pacman-Qm`,
`ssh-keygen-l`, `rustup-toolchain`, `vault-policy-list`, Aje280a6Aj).

So: the rename is a **pure affordance win** (same tidy structure, conventional labels,
zero regressions), and it usefully *separates* the "is it labeled well" question from
the "is it parsed well" question Aje28094Aj the latter being where the real work remains.

---

## 6. Consequences / direction

1. **Stop chasing byte-parity.** Generic parsers + positional labels are an acceptable
   answer on their own merits. Retire bespokes when the generic output is tidy and
   usable, not only when it is byte-identical.
2. **Goldens are snapshots.** Regenerate freely on intended improvements; treat any
   *unintended* diff as a bug. The scorer is a coarse guard; goldens catch value-level
   drift the scorer can't.
3. **The real backlog is parser routing, not labeling.** The judge pass names the
   concrete tail: colon-block routing, separator-as-noise-column, numeric-blob
   splitting, tree modeling. These are the "meaningful" gaps worth closing next Aje28094Aj and
   they are exactly the cases doc `HANDOFF.md`'s parse-wrong clusters already track.
4. **`A,B,C` is now the house convention** for any nameless column; use `_col_letter`
   rather than inventing a placeholder.
===END===

# The `columnar-specs` engine Aje28094Aj how it works & how to add a tool

`extract/strategies/delimited/columnar-specs.sh` is a **data-driven columnar
parser**. Instead of a ~50-line bespoke `.sh` strategy per tool, each tool it
handles is **one declarative spec line** describing how to turn that command's
tabular text output into `entryN.field value` records. One engine, many tools.

> **Keep this document current.** Whenever you add a new transform or engine
> feature to support a strategy, update the relevant section here (the spec
> format table, the transform list, or the capability/limitation notes) in the
> same change. This is a required doc, like `CHANGELOG.md` and `HANDOFF.md`.

## Dataset identity Aje28094Aj the engine reports the matched tool name

`glean` names a dataset after the **reporting strategy**. To keep each migrated
tool its own dataset (so `mount | glean` Aje28692Aj dataset `mount`, not `columnar-specs`,
and two different tools never collide into one dataset), `strategy_detect` sets
the global `_STRATEGY_REPORT_NAME` to the matched spec's tool name. The engine
(`extract/lib/_discovery.sh`) uses it for the dispatch winner, the `matched`
list, and the `STRAT-<name>` record label, falling back to the file's strategy
name when unset (it clears the global before each strategy's detect so a name
never leaks to the next). This must be set in `strategy_detect` (parent shell),
not `strategy_extract` (which runs in a command-substitution subshell, so its
globals would not propagate).

> `free` intentionally stays bespoke: it is the smoke suite's canonical
> end-to-end example (reconciliation, provenance, variants), and migrating it Aje28094Aj
> though byte-identical on its sample Aje28094Aj perturbs those `glean`-level tests.

## Why it exists

Dozens of tools emit the same *shape* Aje28094Aj a header row (or none) followed by
rows of whitespace- or pipe-delimited columns. Writing a hand-rolled awk
strategy for each is repetitive and grows the strategy count. The engine
absorbs that whole family: adding a tool is a one-line spec, and the tidy output
is **byte-for-byte identical** to the bespoke it replaces (verified at migration
time Aje28094Aj see *Verification* below).

## The spec format

Each entry of the `_COLUMNAR_SPECS` array is a single TAB-separated string
(written with `$'Aje280a6Aj\tAje280a6Aj'`):

```
name <TAB> detect <TAB> header_marker <TAB> delim <TAB> absorb <TAB> minreq <TAB> cols [<TAB> total [<TAB> rowre [<TAB> prefix]]]
```

| # | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `name` | tool name, used only as the record label region |
| 2 | `detect` | `;`-separated tokens that must **all** be present for this spec to match the input (see *Detection*) |
| 3 | `header_marker` | skip every line up to **and including** the first line containing this substring (drops preamble + header row). `-` = headerless (start at line 1). Must not be empty. |
| 4 | `delim` | `ws` (split on whitespace) or `pipe` (split on `|`, trim each cell) |
| 5 | `absorb` | 0-based index of the column that soaks up overflow tokens (joined with `_`) when a row has more tokens than columns (`ws` only); `-1` = none |
| 6 | `minreq` | minimum token count for a row to be accepted (lets trailing columns be optional) |
| 7 | `cols` | comma-separated output column names, each optionally carrying a transform (see *Transforms*) |
| 8 | `total` | optional; `1` (default) appends a `total_entries N` record, `0` omits it Aje28094Aj match whatever the bespoke did |
| 9 | `rowre` | optional **per-row accept regex**: a row is processed only if its raw line matches this bash regex. The engine's per-row structural guard, for outputs with footer/note lines that survive the `minreq` filter (e.g. gsutil `TOTAL:`, grafana's trailing note, a `--- ---` rule row). Empty Aje28792Aj every row past the header. To use `rowre` with the default total, set field 8 to `1` explicitly. |
| 10 | `prefix` | optional record-name prefix (default `entry`). Some bespokes label records `jobN` (crontab) / `commitN` (git-log) instead of `entryN` Aje28094Aj set this to match byte-for-byte. To use it, fill fields 8 and 9 explicitly. |

### Detection (field 2)

`detect` tokens are split on `;`. **All** must be satisfied for the spec to
match:

- a **plain token** is a substring that must appear anywhere in the input;
- a token written `re:PATTERN` requires **at least one line** to match the bash
  regex `PATTERN`. A single `re:` token keeps its spaces (it is not split on
  whitespace), so `re:^[^[:space:]]+ on .* type ` is one pattern.

**JSON guard.** Before any spec is tried, the engine declines inputs that
`_is_json` classifies as JSON Aje28094Aj which includes any text whose first non-blank
line starts with `[` or `{`. So a tool whose output opens with a bracketed
section header (e.g. `php -m`'s `[PHP Modules]`) can **not** be detected by
`columnar-specs` and must stay bespoke. (Symptom: `strategy_extract` works when
the file is sourced alone but the engine reports "No fields extracted", because
the standalone shell lacks `_is_json`.)

Detection is **input-level, not per-row.** Beyond the `rowre` accept guard, the
engine has no per-cell structural guard Aje28094Aj every non-blank row past the header with `Aje289a5Aj minreq` tokens becomes an
entry. If a tool's output contains footer/notes lines that would wrongly parse
(e.g. a `TOTAL:` summary, a "Restart Aje280a6Aj" note), a flat spec cannot yet exclude
them Aje28094Aj those tools await a per-row guard transform (see *Limitations*).

**Detection must be specific.** Because every input is tried against every spec
(first match wins in generic mode), a too-greedy `detect` will *steal* other
tools' inputs. Two real examples that the corpus golden run (`tests/corpus/run.sh
--golden`, the collision detector) caught as FAILs:

- `re:^([^|]*[|]){9}` ("Aje289a5Aj9 pipes") wrongly matched wide bordered SQL tables;
  fixed by keying on ipmitool's unique sensor-status field
  `re:[|] *(ok|na|nc|cr) *[|]`.
- `re: @ [0-9]` (grafana plugin `name @ version`) wrongly matched CPU-info files
  (`Aje280a6Aj CPU @ 2.80GHz`); fixed by keying on grafana's header `installed plugins`.

Note a structural limitation: `re:` means **"at least one line matches"**, which
is *weaker* than the guard many bespokes use ("**every** non-blank line matches
this shape"). Tools whose only signature is a shape shared with other tools Aje28094Aj
e.g. `composer show`'s `vendor/pkg version description`, which collides with
`docker images`, `go list -m`, `apt list`, crictl/nerdctl image lists Aje28094Aj cannot be
told apart by a one-line detect and **stay bespoke** until an *all-lines-match*
detect mode is added. Attempting `composer-show` as a spec hijacked 13 other
tools; it was reverted.

### Row handling (fields 3Aje28093Aj6)

1. Blank lines are skipped.
2. Until `header_marker` is seen, lines are skipped (unless headerless `-`).
3. `pipe` rows must contain `|`; cells are split on `|` and trimmed.
   `ws` rows are split on runs of whitespace.
4. Rows with fewer than `minreq` tokens are skipped.
5. `ws` + `absorb Aje289a5Aj 0` + (tokens > cols): the absorb column soaks the surplus
   tokens, **joined with `_`** (e.g. goose-status folds a multi-word timestamp
   `2026-01-10 12:00:00 +0000` Aje28692Aj `2026-01-10_12:00:00_+0000`).

### Transforms (field 7 column suffixes)

| Column syntax | Effect |
|---|---|
| `name` | always emit the token verbatim |
| `~name` | **separator**: consume a token slot (keeping later columns aligned) but emit nothing Aje28094Aj e.g. mount's `on`/`type` literals |
| `name@opt` | emit only if the cell is non-empty (optional trailing column) |
| `name@unwrap` | strip one layer of surrounding `()`/`[]`/`{}`/`""` Aje28094Aj e.g. `(rw,relatime)` Aje28692Aj `rw,relatime` |
| `name@between@L@R` | emit the substring between the first `L` and the next `R` (empty Aje28792Aj skip) Aje28094Aj e.g. ss `users:(("sshd",Aje280a6Aj))` Aje28692Aj `sshd` |
| `name@rest` | **terminal** column: soaks every remaining token from its slot, joined with **single spaces** (verbatim internal spacing, unlike `absorb`'s `_`) Aje28094Aj e.g. arp-scan's `vendor` = `Raspberry Pi Foundation`. No column may follow it. |
| `name@line` | **sole-column** mode: the value is the whole **trimmed** line (no tokenizing) Aje28094Aj for single-column list outputs (module lists, cfg dumps). Use `cols` = one `@line` column; `delim`/`absorb`/`minreq` are ignored for the value. Combine with `header_marker` and `rowre` to drop headers / sub-section lines. |

## Recipe: migrate a bespoke into a spec

0. **Check where the bespoke lives first.** A strategy under
   `strategies/delimited/` or `strategies/structured/` is a **generic multi-tool parser**, not a
   per-tool bespoke Aje28094Aj it wins *other* corpus inputs too (e.g. `getconf` also
   tidies `docker-diff` and `nats-stream-ls`). Migrating one 1:1 reproduces only
   its own input and silently regresses the others (the golden run catches it as
   failures on *unrelated* tools). Do **not** migrate generic strategies.
1. **Probe** the bespoke's output to learn its columns and edge cases:
   `mig.sh probe <name>` (dev harness; shows raw + tidy).
2. **Read** the bespoke `.sh` for any per-row filtering or value cleanup Aje28094Aj if it
   does something the transforms above can't express, this tool is *not yet*
   migratable (add a transform first, or defer).
3. **Write** a spec line and add it to `_COLUMNAR_SPECS`.
4. **Verify byte-identical** against the bespoke, comparing record *content*
   (the `STRAT-<name>:N` label differs by design): `mig.sh check <name>` Aje28692Aj
   must print `IDENTICAL`.
5. **Retire** the bespoke (`git rm extract/strategies/<cat>/<name>.sh`) and
   remove any dedicated `extract/tests/test_strategy_<name>.sh` (or repoint it at
   `columnar-specs`, as `mount` did).
6. **Run the gate** and fix regressions:
   - `tests/corpus/run.sh --golden` Aje28094Aj catches detection collisions and
     generic-mode output changes. Where generic mode now (correctly) routes a
     tool through `columnar-specs` and the output improved, **regenerate** that
     tool's golden (`run.sh --update-golden` or write the single file) and
     confirm the new output is the better one.
   - `extract/tests/run_tests.sh`, `tests/smoke.sh`, `transform/tests/test_melt.sh`.

The `mig.sh` harness lives in the scratchpad (dev-only, not shipped).

## Recipe: add a new transform to the engine

1. Add the parsing/emit logic in `columnar-specs.sh` (`_cs_apply` for a
   per-column transform; the row loop in `strategy_extract` for row-level
   behavior; `_cs_matches` for detection features).
2. Keep it **mawk-safe / POSIX-ish bash** Aje28094Aj no gawk-only features (CI covers this).
3. Add at least one migrated tool that exercises it, verified byte-identical.
4. **Update this document** Aje28094Aj add the transform to the table above and note any
   new spec-field semantics.
5. Run the full gate.

## Capabilities & limitations (current)

**Handles:** header-skip or headerless tables; whitespace or pipe delimiters;
positional column maps; one overflow-absorb column; a terminal space-preserving
`@rest` column; optional trailing columns via `minreq`; a per-row accept guard
(`rowre`); the `~sep`, `@opt`, `@unwrap`, `@between`, `@rest` transforms; per-spec
`total_entries` control; substring and regex (`re:`) input detection.

**Does not yet handle** (tools needing these stay bespoke until the feature
lands Aje28094Aj ranked by how many tools each would unlock):

- **all-lines-match detect** Aje28094Aj require *every* non-blank data line to match a
  shape (not just one). Needed to safely migrate tools whose signature is a
  shape shared with others (`composer-show`, and much of the package/image-list
  family) without hijacking them.
- **transpose / `vertical`** Aje28094Aj first field on each line becomes the field *name*
  (key/value outputs folded into one wide record).
- **line prefix strip** Aje28094Aj an `@line` variant that strips a leading token/prefix
  (go-list keeps only the first token; cabal-freeze strips `constraints:`; the
  tree tools `systemd-cgls`/`fwupdmgr` strip box-drawing `Aje2949ce29480Aj` characters).
- **`delim=tab`** Aje28094Aj tab as a first-class delimiter (space-containing 2Aje28093Aj3 col
  tables, e.g. the `git-*` family).
- **`@default@<val>`** Aje28094Aj placeholder for a missing optional column.
- **mid-row multi-token column** Aje28094Aj a fixed-width value with internal spaces that
  is *not* the last column (e.g. nodetool's `145.23 GiB` load); `@rest` only
  covers the terminal column, `absorb` joins with `_`.
- **stateful / continuation rows** Aje28094Aj values inherited from a previous row
  (`fuser -v`), or mixed record shapes in one output (`aws s3 ls` objects vs
  `PRE` prefixes).
- **`@split@<delim>`**, **`@keyword`** Aje28094Aj split one token into two columns; locate
  a value by a preceding keyword.

## Tools currently migrated into the engine

zypper-search, buildah-containers, lsmem, ss-tulnp, smartctl-attributes, mount,
iostat-d, rabbitmqctl-list-queues, goose-status, ipmitool-sensor,
dpkg-get-selections, gsutil-ls-l, grafana-cli-plugins, bq-ls, arp-scan,
rustc-cfg, apache2ctl-modules, dub-list, lstopo-no-graphics, lshw-network,
route-6, snap-connections, networkctl-lldp, memcached-stats,
es-cat-allocation, bundle-list, nethogs, slabtop, objdump-headers,
iptables-save, ldconfig-p, perf-top, turbostat, traceroute, crontab,
git-remote, w-sessions, dpkg-list, tar-listing, beegfs.
(See `_COLUMNAR_SPECS` for the authoritative list.)

# glean/extract Aje28094Aj the extract engine

This directory holds glean's extract engine + all strategies. `glean` runs it
in-process (via the `--emit-meta` contract) to auto-detect the format of captured
output.

The engine sources cross-suite shared libraries (version, progress, pager, Aje280a6Aj)
from its sibling `../lib` Aje28094Aj i.e. **`glean/lib/`**.

**This is first-party glean code Aje28094Aj edit it here.** The tree was originally
imported from the Envoy suite's `EnvoyExtract/` project, but it is now maintained
in this repo directly; there is no live upstream sync. Add a new format-detection
strategy under `strategies/` with its sample + golden fixtures, then run the suite:

```bash
bash glean/extract/tests/run_tests.sh     # strategy + engine suite
```

`tools/new_strategy.sh` and `tools/review_strategy.sh` scaffold and check a new
strategy.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `envoy-extract` | engine entry point (invoked internally by `glean`) |
| `lib/` | engine libraries (dispatch, format, postprocess, Aje280a6Aj) |
| `strategies/` | the 200+ format-detection strategies |
| `tools/` | strategy-authoring helpers (`new_strategy.sh`, `review_strategy.sh`) |
| `samples/` | sample inputs used by the strategy tests |
| `tests/` | the strategy + engine test suite (`bash tests/run_tests.sh`) |
| `../lib/` (`glean/lib/`) | shared suite libs the engine sources via `../lib` |
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/envoy-extract===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
##                         Multi-Format Extractor
################################################################################
## Version 4.2
## Developed by SageCor Solutions, Annapolis Junction, MD
################################################################################
##
## Description: Use various strategies to extract field names and values from
##      the supplied file or stdin. Auto-detects data formats (JSON, YAML, CSV,
##      syslog, benchmark output, etc.) and outputs structured key/value fields.
##
################################################################################
##
## Usage: envoy-extract [COMMAND] [OPTIONS] [FILE] [FIELD-LIST]
##        cat file | envoy-extract [OPTIONS] [FIELD-LIST]
##
################################################################################
##
## Author: Martin J. Gallagher
##
################################################################################
##
## See CHANGELOG.md for version history.
##
################################################################################

set -eo pipefail
# ENV-115: nounset catches undefined-variable bugs at first read (typos in
# side-channel globals, missing defaults, uninitialised state) rather than
# silently expanding to "". Side-channel init lives at the top of each
# owning lib module. Strategies see `set -u` too; plugin authors should
# guard optional reads with `${VAR:-default}`.
set -o nounset

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
STRATEGIES_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/strategies"
# Declarative tool->strategy routing table (see _discovery.sh for the format).
HINTS_FILE="${MFE_HINTS_FILE:-$SCRIPT_DIR/hints.tsv}"
if [[ -r "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_version.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_version.sh"
elif [[ -r "${ENVOY_HOME:-}/lib/envoy_version.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "${ENVOY_HOME}/lib/envoy_version.sh"
fi
if declare -F envoy_suite_version >/dev/null; then
    VERSION="$(envoy_suite_version "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
else
    VERSION="0.0.0+unknown"
fi

########################################
## MODULE LOADING
##

source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_log.sh"
# ENV-137: shared typo / suggestion helpers (best-effort).
if [[ -r "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_suggest.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_suggest.sh"
elif [[ -r "${ENVOY_HOME:-}/lib/envoy_suggest.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "${ENVOY_HOME}/lib/envoy_suggest.sh"
fi
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_helpers.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_techniques.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_format.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_postprocess.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_discovery.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_interactive.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_validate.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_autotune.sh"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_dispatch.sh"

# ENV-143: shared pager helper.  Tolerate missing file (partial dev checkout).
if [[ -r "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_pager.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_pager.sh"
elif [[ -r "${ENVOY_HOME:-}/lib/envoy_pager.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "${ENVOY_HOME}/lib/envoy_pager.sh"
fi
if ! declare -F envoy_maybe_page >/dev/null; then
    envoy_maybe_page() { cat; }
    envoy_pager_disable() { :; }
    envoy_pager_active() { return 1; }
fi

# ENV-135: shared progress helper. Tolerate a missing file (partial dev
# checkout) by stubbing no-op shims so callers don't have to defend
# against the absence.
if [[ -r "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/envoy_progress.sh" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091

    envoy_progress_tick() { :; }

# ENV-154: suite-wide config layer.  Loaded before flag parsing so

########################################
## USAGE
##

usage () {
    printf 'Multi-Format Extractor (envoy-extract) v%s\n\n' "$VERSION"
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: envoy-extract [COMMAND] [OPTIONS] [FILE] [FIELD-LIST]
       cat file | envoy-extract [OPTIONS] [FIELD-LIST]

Auto-detect data formats and extract structured key/value fields.
Output defaults to JSON when piped, or a numbered table in the terminal.

Commands:
  extract                 Extract fields from a file or stdin (default)
  explain                 Show which strategies match and why (dry-run)
  list                    List available strategies
  search [KEYWORD ...]    Search strategies by name/description/technique/category
                          --category <cat>        Limit to one category
                          --case-sensitive        Match literally (default: insensitive)
                          Multiple keywords use AND semantics.
                          No keywords lists all strategies.
  validate [FILE]         Validate a strategy file, or all strategies
  validate-strategies     Run each strategy's detect() against its declared
                          sample file. Reports strategies whose self-confidence
                          is below the threshold.
                          --threshold N           Pass/fail cutoff (default 75)
                          --strategy NAME | -s NAME
                                                  Validate only this strategy
  stream                  Stream mode: read stdin line-by-line, output JSON Lines
  batch                   Batch mode: read file paths from stdin, output JSON Lines

Basic Options:
  -h, --help              Show this help message
  -V, --version           Show version number
  -s, --strategy NAME     Run only the named strategy
  -f, --format FMT        Output format: json, json-nested, csv, tsv, plain, yaml, xml

Output Control:
  --count                 Output only the number of fields extracted
  --names                 Output only field names (no values)
  --sort                  Sort output fields alphabetically by name
  -r, --raw               Emit raw extracted fields without formatting
  --output FILE           Write output to FILE instead of stdout
  -q, --quiet             Suppress output; exit 0 if fields found, 1 otherwise
  -i, --interactive       Interactively select which fields to include
  --progress              Emit per-strategy progress to stderr (auto on
                          TTY Aje289a5Aj20 strategies; ENV-135)
  --no-progress           Disable progress (also: ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1)

Filtering & Selection:
  --min-confidence N      Skip strategies with confidence below N (0-100)
  --first-match           Stop after first strategy produces output
  --max-strategies N      Limit number of strategies that produce output
  --delimiter DELIM       Set custom field delimiter for output (overrides strategy default)
                          Examples: '=>', '::', '|', ' -> '
  --field-pattern REGEX   Only include fields whose names match REGEX
  --exclude-field NAME    Exclude fields with this exact name (repeatable)
  --rename 'old=new,...'  Rename fields after extraction
  --no-dedup              Skip deduplication of fields across strategies
  --aggregate             Compute count/min/max/sum/avg for numeric fields
  --generic               Use only the generic format strategies (delimited/structured)
  --no-hints              Skip the declarative hints.tsv tool-routing table

Advanced:
  -c                      Output a fully-qualified command line for replay
  --replay SPEC           Replay a previously exported extraction (format: strategy_name@version,
                          e.g. 'colons@1.0'; use -c to generate a replay spec)
  --chain 'A|B'           Chain strategies: output of A feeds into B
  --plugin-dir DIR        Additional strategy directory
  --auto-tune             Auto-adjust confidence threshold; rank best strategy
                          (results reported via --verbose or --debug flags)
  --max-input-size N      Max input size in bytes (default: 50MB)
  --emit-meta             Print the winning strategy + confidence to stderr as
                          one line: __EXTRACT_META__<TAB>strategy<TAB>confidence

Debug & Development:
  -d, --debug             Show strategy matching details and field provenance
  -v, --verbose           Show extraction summary and per-strategy field counts
  --profile               Show per-strategy timing on stderr

Arguments:
  FILE                    Input file to parse (reads stdin if omitted)
  FIELD-LIST              Comma-delimited list of field numbers or names

Examples:
  envoy-extract config.json                         Extract all fields (auto-detect)
  envoy-extract -s yaml config.yml                  Use a specific strategy
  envoy-extract -f csv data.json                    Output as CSV
  cat server.log | envoy-extract                    Read from stdin
  envoy-extract list                                Show available strategies
  envoy-extract -d mystery-file.txt                 Debug: see which strategies match
  envoy-extract stream -s syslog < app.log          Stream line-by-line as JSON Lines
  find logs/ -name "*.log" | envoy-extract batch    Process multiple files at once

Batch Options:
  --batch-summary           After batch processing, emit a summary JSON object
                            with totals, strategy usage, and common fields.
                            Requires --batch (or batch subcommand).

Pager (ENV-143):
  --no-pager                Disable auto-paging of `list` and `--validate-all`
                            output even on a TTY.
  ENVOY_NO_PAGER=1          Suite-wide pager disable.
  PAGER                     Override pager command (default: less -FRX).
EOF
}

            _OPT_min_confidence="$2"; shift 2 ;;

            _OPT_count=1; shift ;;

        --sort)
            _OPT_sort=1; shift ;;
        --first-match)
            _OPT_first_match=1; shift ;;

            _OPT_max_strategies="$2"; shift 2 ;;

            _OPT_delimiter="$2"; shift 2 ;;

            _OPT_field_pattern="$2"; shift 2 ;;

            [[ $# -lt 2 ]] && _log_error "--exclude-field requires an argument" && exit 1
            _OPT_exclude_fields+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
        --category)
            [[ $# -lt 2 ]] && _log_error "--category requires an argument" && exit 1
            _OPT_search_category="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --case-sensitive)
            _OPT_search_case_sensitive=1; shift ;;
        --threshold)
            [[ $# -lt 2 ]] && _log_error "--threshold requires an argument" && exit 1
            [[ "$2" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { _log_error "--threshold requires a number (0-100)"; exit 1; }
            _OPT_self_validate_threshold="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --record-boundary)
            [[ $# -lt 2 ]] && _log_error "--record-boundary requires a regex argument" && exit 1
            _OPT_record_boundary="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --)
            shift; break ;;
        -*)
            _log_error "Unknown option: $1"
            _log_info "Run 'envoy-extract --help' for usage information."
            exit 1 ;;
        *)
            break ;;
    esac
done

# ENV-043: minimal interactive strategy browser Aje28094Aj a REPL over search_strategies

    [[ -t 0 ]] && echo "Commands: <keyword> ... to search, 'cat <name>' for category, 'show <name>' for details, 'q' or Ctrl-D to quit"
    [[ -t 0 ]] && echo ""
    while :; do
        [[ -t 0 ]] && printf 'extract> '
        IFS= read -r _line || break
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue

           && _envoy_arg_looks_like_typo "$1"; then

            exit 2

        # Suggest common file-extension completions for the typo'd path case.
        if [[ -f "${1}.log" ]]; then
            _log_info "Did you mean: ${1}.log?"
        elif [[ -f "${1}.txt" ]]; then
            _log_info "Did you mean: ${1}.txt?"
        elif [[ -f "${1}.json" ]]; then
            _log_info "Did you mean: ${1}.json?"

        exit 1
    fi

# Parse any remaining flags that appeared after the file argument

            _log_error "Unknown option after filename: $1"

            fields="$1"; shift ;;

########################################
## INPUT READING

text=""
if [[ -n "$file" ]]; then
    # Check file size before reading
    _file_size=$(wc -c < "$file")
    if [[ $_file_size -gt $_OPT_max_input_size ]]; then
        _log_error "Input file is too large (${_file_size} bytes, max ${_OPT_max_input_size}). Try --stream for large inputs."
        exit 1
    fi
    text=$(<"$file")
elif [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
    # Read from stdin, capping at max_input_size + 1 to detect oversized input
    # without exhausting memory on very large streams.
    # ENV-182: pre-fix we did `text=$(head -c $((N+1)))` then checked
    # `${#text} > N`. `$(...)` strips trailing newlines, so an input of
    # exactly N+1 bytes ending in newline(s) shrank to Aje289a4Aj N and slipped
    # past the cap. We now cache the raw byte count from the stage
    # file (BEFORE the trailing-newline-strip) and check against
    # _text_byte_len, while keeping the in-memory $text for downstream
    # consumers.
    _raw_stage=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/envoy-extract-stage.XXXXXX") || {
        _log_error "Could not stage stdin"
        exit 1
    }
    head -c $((_OPT_max_input_size + 2)) > "$_raw_stage"
    _text_byte_len=$(wc -c < "$_raw_stage" | tr -d ' ')
    text=$(<"$_raw_stage")
    rm -f "$_raw_stage" 2>/dev/null
    # ENV-182 introduced this empty-input gate, but the original form
    # required BOTH `-z "$text"` AND `_text_byte_len -eq 0`.  An input
    # like `echo "" | envoy-extract` sends a single newline byte:
    # `text=$(<file)` strips trailing newlines so `$text` is empty but
    # `_text_byte_len=1`, the AND condition is false, processing
    # continues, and the user sees the downstream "warning: No fields
    # extracted." with exit 0 instead of the documented "error: No
    # data received on stdin." with exit 1.  Treat any whitespace-only
    # stdin as no-data; this also subsumes the strict empty-buffer
    # case (text="" and byte-len 0).
    if [[ -z "${text//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
        _log_error "No data received on stdin."
        exit 1
    fi
    _text_len=${#text}
    if [[ "$_text_byte_len" -gt $_OPT_max_input_size ]]; then
        _log_error "Input is too large (>${_OPT_max_input_size} bytes). Try --stream for large inputs."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    _log_error "No input file provided and no data on stdin."
    _log_info "Run 'envoy-extract --help' for usage information."
    exit 1
fi

# Binary file detection: compare file size with byte count of read text.
# Binary detection: bash strips NUL bytes when reading via $(<file), so a
# byte-count mismatch indicates binary content. Also strips trailing newlines
# which can account for several bytes in normal text files.
# Use tr to count NUL-free bytes for a direct comparison.
# _file_size already set by the size guard above.
if [[ -n "$file" && -f "$file" ]]; then
    _clean_bytes=$(tr -d '\0' < "$file" | wc -c)
    if [[ $((_file_size - _clean_bytes)) -gt 0 ]]; then
        _log_warn "Input appears to be a binary file, skipping extraction."
        exit 0
    fi
fi

# Normalise alternate line terminators to \n so record splitting Aje28094Aj which keys on
# \n throughout Aje28094Aj sees every logical line. Covers Windows CRLF, bare-CR (classic
# Mac), vertical-tab / form-feed page breaks, and the Unicode line separators
# NEL (U+0085), LS (U+2028) and PS (U+2029). Without this, a capture that uses any
# of these instead of \n collapses to a single physical line and no rows are found.
# Gated on such a byte being present, so it is a true no-op for ordinary \n input.
# Order matters: strip CRLF's trailing CR first, then map any remaining bare CR /
# VT / FF, then the multibyte separators Aje28094Aj so CRLF never becomes a blank line.
#
# VT is context-sensitive: when the input ALREADY has real \n lines, a VT is not
# a line break at all Aje28094Aj it's a stray control byte INSIDE a cell (`disk\vfailure`)
# and becomes a SPACE, keeping the row whole. Only in a \n-less capture (VT as
# the sole line separator Aje28094Aj the adversarial breaker this block was built for)
# does VT map to \n.
if [[ "$text" == *$'\r'* || "$text" == *$'\013'* || "$text" == *$'\014'* \
      || "$text" == *$'\302\205'* || "$text" == *$'\342\200\250'* || "$text" == *$'\342\200\251'* ]]; then
    local_vt_to=$'\n'
    [[ "$text" == *$'\n'* ]] && local_vt_to=' '
    text="$(printf '%s' "$text" | sed 's/\r$//' | tr '\r\013\014' $'\n'"${local_vt_to}"$'\n' \
            | sed $'s/\302\205/\\\n/g; s/\342\200\250/\\\n/g; s/\342\200\251/\\\n/g')"
    unset local_vt_to
fi


# Normalise exotic Unicode horizontal spaces to ASCII space so column splitting
# Aje28094Aj which keys on runs of 0x20 Aje28094Aj sees the alignment the terminal showed. Covers
# NBSP (U+00A0, also used as locale thousands grouping Aje28094Aj a SINGLE space inside a
# number survives the 2+-space column rule, so "1 234,56" stays one cell while
# NBSP-padded column gaps still split), narrow NBSP (U+202F), medium math space
# (U+205F), the U+2000Aje28093AjU+200A quad/en/em/thin/hair family, and the ideographic
# space (U+3000) CJK tables pad with. Gated on such a byte being present; the
# U+2028/29 line separators were already mapped to \n above, and curly quotes
# (U+2018-201D) fall outside the mapped ranges.
if [[ "$text" == *$'\302\240'* || "$text" == *$'\342\200'* || "$text" == *$'\342\201\237'* \
      || "$text" == *$'\343\200\200'* ]]; then
    text="$(printf '%s' "$text" | LC_ALL=C sed $'s/\302\240/ /g; s/\342\200[\200-\212]/ /g; s/\342\200\257/ /g; s/\342\201\237/ /g; s/\343\200\200/ /g')"
fi

# Delete ZERO-WIDTH SPACE (U+200B) Aje28094Aj invisible in the terminal, so it can only
# corrupt: a header token carrying one (`userAje2808bAjname`) prints as one word but
# compares unequal to its plain form and pollutes the melted field name. Only
# ZWSP is dropped; ZWNJ/ZWJ (U+200C/D) are orthographically REAL (Farsi
# half-space, emoji family joins) and stay. Gated on the byte pair.
if [[ "$text" == *$'\342\200\213'* ]]; then
    text="$(printf '%s' "$text" | LC_ALL=C sed $'s/\342\200\213//g')"
fi

# Normalise FULLWIDTH digits (U+FF10Aje28093AjFF19, CJK tables: `Ajefbc98efbc90Aj`) and the fullwidth
# colon (U+FF1A) to their ASCII forms so numeric-contrast header detection and
# `key: value` splitting see them the way a reader does. Gated on the FF-block
# lead bytes being present.
if [[ "$text" == *$'\357\274'* ]]; then
    text="$(printf '%s' "$text" | LC_ALL=C sed $'s/\357\274\220/0/g; s/\357\274\221/1/g; s/\357\274\222/2/g; s/\357\274\223/3/g; s/\357\274\224/4/g; s/\357\274\225/5/g; s/\357\274\226/6/g; s/\357\274\227/7/g; s/\357\274\230/8/g; s/\357\274\231/9/g; s/\357\274\232/:/g')"
fi

# Strip ANSI/VT escape sequences (colored output: ls --color, gh, git, kubectl,
# systemctl status dots, terraform plan, npm/cargo, Aje280a6Aj) so a color code can never
# split or pollute a data cell. Gated on an ESC byte being present, so it is a
# true no-op Aje28094Aj no subprocess Aje28094Aj for the overwhelming majority of inputs that carry
# none. Matches the ECMA-48 CSI form (ESC [ params intermediates final) plus the
# OSC form (ESC ] Aje280a6Aj BEL) and bare two-byte escapes.
if [[ "$text" == *$'\033'* ]]; then
    text="$(printf '%s' "$text" | sed $'s/\033\\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]//g; s/\033\\][^\007]*\007//g; s/\033[@-Z\\\\-_]//g')"
fi

# Strip terminal-bell and backspace control bytes (BEL \a, BS \b) Aje28094Aj decoration
# or erase intent, never data; leaving them embeds invisible bytes in a cell.
# Runs AFTER the ANSI strip: BEL terminates an OSC sequence, so deleting it
# first would orphan `ESC]Aje280a6AjBEL` sequences the OSC rule needs intact. Gated on
# presence, a no-op otherwise.
if [[ "$text" == *$'\007'* || "$text" == *$'\010'* ]]; then
    text="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '\007\010')"
fi

# LEADING-CHROME strip Aje28094Aj lines a capture drags in ABOVE the data (reviewer
# round R3). Only the LEADING run of a block with >=2 remaining lines is
# touched, each form gated to leading-only so real content is never lost:
#   * `$ command` shell-prompt echoes (`$ amass intel -org Aje280a6Aj`);
#   * `WARNING:`/`ERROR:`/`NOTICE:` stderr noise when no later line starts
#     the same way (apk's cache warning);
#   * `NAME ********Aje280a6Aj` banner rules (ansible's `PLAY RECAP ****`).
_lc_strip () {
    local _in="$1" _out="" _body="" _l _lead=1 _n=0
    local _drop_warn=1
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        _n=$((_n + 1))
        [[ $_n -le 1 ]] && continue
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^(WARNING|ERROR|NOTICE): ]] && _drop_warn=0
    done <<< "$_in"
    _n=0
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        if [[ $_lead -eq 1 ]]; then
            if [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then :
            elif [[ "$_l" =~ ^\$\ [A-Za-z] ]]; then continue
            elif [[ $_drop_warn -eq 1 && "$_l" =~ ^(WARNING|ERROR|NOTICE): ]]; then continue
            elif [[ "$_l" =~ \*{6,}[[:space:]]*$ && "$_l" =~ ^[A-Z] ]]; then continue
            elif [[ "$_l" =~ ^[A-Z][a-z]+([[:space:]]+[a-z]+){2,}$ ]] && \
                 [[ "$_l" =~ [[:space:]](of|the|to|in|for|with|and|on|at|by|from|is|are)[[:space:]] ]]; then
                # prose title ("List of devices attached") Aje28094Aj Titlecase word +
                # lowercase words incl. a function word, no colon/digits
                continue
            else _lead=0
            fi
        fi
        _body+="$_l"$'\n'
        [[ -n "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && _n=$((_n + 1))
    done <<< "$_in"
    if [[ $_n -ge 2 && "$_body" != "$_in"$'\n' ]]; then
        printf '%s' "${_body%$'\n'}"
    else
        printf '%s' "$_in"
    fi
}
# Interspersed `== section ==` banner lines (apptainer inspect's
# `== labels ==` / `== runscript ==`) are pure section decoration Aje28094Aj drop a
# line delimited by EXACTLY-two-equals runs (`== word ==`). Longer runs
# (`=== SET ===`, `====== JOB MAP ======`) are GROUP-LABEL banners that the
# embedded-table / kv-under-group parsers legitimately consume, so the
# exact-`==` shape is the discriminator. Gated on the byte pair.
if [[ "$text" == *'== '* ]]; then
    _banner_out=""
    while IFS= read -r _bl; do
        if [[ "$_bl" =~ ^[[:space:]]*==[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9][^=]*[[:space:]]+==[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        _banner_out+="$_bl"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    text="${_banner_out%$'\n'}"
fi

case "$text" in
    '$ '*|WARNING:*|ERROR:*|NOTICE:*|*'******'*|List\ *|Ran\ *)
        text="$(_lc_strip "$text")" ;;
    [A-Z]*)
        # prose-title first line Aje28094Aj cheap pre-check before the full pass
        _lc_first="${text%%$'\n'*}"
        if [[ "$_lc_first" =~ ^[A-Z][a-z]+([[:space:]]+[a-z]+){2,}$ ]]; then
            text="$(_lc_strip "$text")"
        fi
        ;;
esac

# Metadata for strategy interface enrichment
_STATE_filename="${file:-}"
_STATE_encoding_hint=""
if [[ -n "$file" ]]; then
    case "${file##*.}" in
        json|yaml|yml|xml|csv|tsv|ini|toml|hcl) _STATE_encoding_hint="utf-8" ;;
    esac
fi

# Cache for clean_text: strategies that need date/paren normalization call
# clean_text() which now uses a cached result after the first call.
_CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE=""
_CLEAN_TEXT_DONE=0

########################################
## EXPLAIN MODE (dry-run)
##

if [[ $_OPT_explain -eq 1 ]]; then
    run_explain_mode
    exit 0
fi

########################################
## STRATEGY EXECUTION
##

# ENV-135: arm progress before the strategy loop. Translate the CLI
# tri-state into the env-var contract envoy_progress_init reads. -1 (auto)
# leaves both knobs unset so the helper applies its TTY + threshold
# defaults; explicit on/off forces the matching knob.
case "$_OPT_progress" in
    1) export ENVOY_PROGRESS_OPT_IN=1; unset ENVOY_PROGRESS_DISABLE ;;
    0) export ENVOY_PROGRESS_DISABLE=1; unset ENVOY_PROGRESS_OPT_IN ;;
    *) : ;;
esac
[[ "$_OPT_quiet" -eq 1 ]] && export ENVOY_QUIET=1
envoy_progress_init

# Dispatch to chain or auto strategy runner
if [[ -n "$_OPT_chain" ]]; then
    run_chain_strategies
else
    run_auto_strategies
fi
# Clear any in-place progress line so the field-table output below starts
# on a clean stderr.
envoy_progress_done

# ENV-200: opt-in winner metadata to stderr, so a single extract run yields both
# the data (stdout) and the winning strategy + confidence (no second `explain`
# pass). Format: a single line `__EXTRACT_META__<TAB>strategy<TAB>confidence`.
if [[ $_OPT_emit_meta -eq 1 ]]; then
    printf '__EXTRACT_META__\t%s\t%s\n' "${_WINNER_NAME:-}" "${_WINNER_CONF:-0}" >&2
fi

########################################
## POST-PROCESSING
##
run_postprocess

## OUTPUT
##
run_output_mode

# glean extract Aje28094Aj declarative tool hints
#
# One row routes a recognized tool's output to an existing strategy, replacing
# a per-tool parser script. Consulted by the engine before strategy
# auto-detection (disable with --no-hints). First matching row wins.
#
# Format (TAB-separated):
#   tool <TAB> match-type <TAB> pattern <TAB> strategy
#
#   tool        dataset/report name for the match (the tool's identity);
#               a family row may cover several tools with one shared name
#   match-type  prefix   Aje28094Aj first non-blank input line starts with pattern
#               contains Aje28094Aj pattern appears anywhere in the input
#               regex    Aje28094Aj input matches the bash ERE pattern (anchor ^ = start
#               of the whole input)
#   strategy    usually a generic strategy (strategies/delimited/ or
#               strategies/structured/); a bespoke target acts as detection
#               routing and is skipped under --generic
#
