#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Helper functions for envoy-extract
##
## Pure-bash utility functions used by strategies and the engine.
## Dependencies: none (standalone)
################################################################################

# ENV-115: initialise clean_text cache slots at source time so nounset in
# envoy-extract doesn't trip when a caller (e.g. stream mode) reaches
# clean_text() before _dispatch.sh's extract-path init runs.
_CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE="${_CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE:-}"
_CLEAN_TEXT_DONE="${_CLEAN_TEXT_DONE:-0}"
_CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT="${_CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT:-}"
_STRIPPED_LINE="${_STRIPPED_LINE:-}"
_FIELD_NAME="${_FIELD_NAME:-}"
_FIELD_VALUE="${_FIELD_VALUE:-}"

# Strip STRAT-name:N<tab> prefix from a line. Result in _STRIPPED_LINE.
strip_strat_prefix () {
    _STRIPPED_LINE="$1"
    case "$_STRIPPED_LINE" in
        STRAT-*$'\t'*) _STRIPPED_LINE="${_STRIPPED_LINE#*$'\t'}" ;;
    esac
}

# Strategy helper: check if text looks like JSON (starts with { or [).
# Available to strategies for quick rejection.
_is_json () {
    case "$1" in
        '{'*|'['*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# Return 0 if the text repeats two or more DISTINCT top-level (unindented) "key:"
# names Aje28094Aj the signature of a multi-record output (git log's Author/Date per
# commit, blank-line-separated records, multi-response HTTP headers). Single-record
# scalar formats (a YAML mapping, /proc/stat, a colon key/value listing) have
# unique top-level keys. The "two or more distinct" threshold avoids misfiring on
# a single record that merely nests one duplicate name (e.g. a WARC response whose
# `Content-Type` appears at both the WARC and HTTP layers). Generic scalar
# strategies use this to decline true multi-record input so it reaches the
# dedicated per-record strategy (which emits entry<N>/record<N> groups the capture
# tidy melt renders one row per record), instead of flattening every record into
# one wide row with duplicate columns.
_has_repeated_top_keys () {
    local _n
    _n=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -oE '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*:' | sort | uniq -d | grep -c .)
    [[ "$_n" -ge 2 ]]
}

# Strategy helper: extract a value from text by grep pattern.
# Usage: _extract_value "$text" "grep_pattern" "field_name"
# Appends "field_name value" to $result if found.
# NOTE: Spaces in extracted values are replaced with underscores to ensure
# single-token values in the "field_name value" output format. Strategy authors
# should be aware of this normalization when extracting multi-word values.
_extract_value () {
    local _ev_text="$1" _ev_pattern="$2" _ev_field="$3"
    local _ev_line _ev_value
    while IFS= read -r _ev_line; do
        if [[ "$_ev_line" == *"$_ev_pattern"* ]]; then
            # Extract value: everything after last colon or equals, trimmed
            _ev_value="${_ev_line##*: }"
            if [[ "$_ev_value" == "$_ev_line" ]]; then
                _ev_value="${_ev_line##*=}"
            fi
            # Trim whitespace
            while [[ "$_ev_value" == " "* ]]; do _ev_value="${_ev_value# }"; done
            while [[ "$_ev_value" == *" " ]]; do _ev_value="${_ev_value% }"; done
            # Replace spaces with underscores
            _ev_value="${_ev_value// /_}"
            if [[ -n "$_ev_value" ]]; then
                result+="${_ev_field} ${_ev_value}"$'\n'
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$_ev_text"
    return 1
}

# Trim leading and trailing whitespace (spaces and tabs) from $1. Result in _TRIMMED.
_trim () {
    _TRIMMED="$1"
    while [[ "$_TRIMMED" == [' '$'\t']* ]]; do _TRIMMED="${_TRIMMED#[' '$'\t']}"; done
    while [[ "$_TRIMMED" == *[' '$'\t'] ]]; do _TRIMMED="${_TRIMMED%[' '$'\t']}"; done
}

# Trim + replace spaces with underscores. Result in _CLEANED.
_clean_field () {
    _trim "$1"
    _CLEANED="${_TRIMMED// /_}"
}

# Count non-empty lines in $1. Result in _LINE_COUNT.
_count_lines () {
    _LINE_COUNT=0
    local _cl_line
    while IFS= read -r _cl_line; do
        [[ -n "$_cl_line" ]] && _LINE_COUNT=$((_LINE_COUNT + 1))
    done <<< "$1"
}

# Parse a "name value" line into _FIELD_NAME and _FIELD_VALUE globals.
_parse_field_line () {
    _FIELD_NAME="${1%% *}"
    _FIELD_VALUE="${1#* }"
}

# Clean and normalize text for extraction.
# Consolidates date-fix and parentheses-fix that were previously duplicated
# in every strategy. Result in _CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT (no subshell needed).
# Caching: after first call, returns cached result from _CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE.
clean_text () {
    local input="$1"

    # Return cached result if available
    if [[ $_CLEAN_TEXT_DONE -eq 1 ]]; then
        _CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT="$_CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE"
        return
    fi

    # Pure-bash replacements (no sed forks)
    # Date pattern: " Mon 01 12:30:45 2024" -> "Mon_01_12_30_45_2024"
    local _date_re=' ([A-Za-z]{3}) ([0-9]{2}) ([0-9]{2}):([0-9]{2}):([0-9]{2}) ([0-9]{4})'
    # Paren pattern: spaces inside () -> underscores
    local _paren_re
    _paren_re='[(][^) ]*[ ]'

    local result="" _line
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        # Date normalization (only lines with colons)
        if [[ "$_line" == *":"* ]]; then
            while [[ "$_line" =~ $_date_re ]]; do
                local _dm="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
                local _dr="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}_${BASH_REMATCH[2]}_${BASH_REMATCH[3]}_${BASH_REMATCH[4]}_${BASH_REMATCH[5]}_${BASH_REMATCH[6]}"
                _line="${_line/$_dm/$_dr}"
            done
        fi
        # Parentheses space normalization (only lines with parens)
        if [[ "$_line" == *"("* ]]; then
            while [[ "$_line" =~ $_paren_re ]]; do
                local _pm="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
                local _pr="${_pm% }_"
                _line="${_line/$_pm/$_pr}"
            done
        fi
        result+="$_line"$'\n'
    done <<< "$input"
    result="${result%$'\n'}"

    _CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE="$result"
    _CLEAN_TEXT_DONE=1
    _CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT="$result"
}

# _col_letter <1-based index> Aje28094Aj spreadsheet-style label for a nameless column:
# 1->A .. 26->Z, 27->AA, 28->BB, 29->CC ... (repeated-letter convention).
# Used by the generic parsers to name headerless columns A,B,C instead of c1,c2.
_col_letter () {
    local i="$1" reps rem ch out="" k
    reps=$(( (i - 1) / 26 + 1 )); rem=$(( (i - 1) % 26 ))
    printf -v ch '%b' "\\$(printf '%03o' $(( 65 + rem )))"
    for (( k = 0; k < reps; k++ )); do out="${out}${ch}"; done
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

# _list_explode Aje28094Aj pivot a flat "key value" record that has EXACTLY ONE indexed
# list field (keys `<prefix>.<N>` or `<prefix>.<N>.<sub>`, N a 0-based integer)
# into one record per element, repeating the scalar (non-list) keys. Reads the
# pair lines on stdin, writes the (possibly transformed) pairs on stdout.
# Passthrough unchanged when there is not exactly one indexed list or it has
# fewer than 2 elements. Lets json/yaml render a list-of-records (avro schema
# `fields`, amtool `Peers`) as tidy rows instead of one wide `field.0.* field.1.*`
# row whose duplicate leaf names collide in the melt.
_list_explode () {
    mawk '
    {
        key = $1; val = ""
        if (length($0) > length(key) + 1) val = substr($0, length(key) + 2)
        K[NR] = key; V[NR] = val; n = NR
    }
    END {
        np = 0
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            k = K[i]
            # A list key needs a NON-EMPTY named prefix before its `.N`; a bare
            # `.0`/`.1` (empty prefix Aje28094Aj a jq array-boundary artifact in
            # multi-array JSON like kubectl config) is not a real named list.
            if (match(k, /\.[0-9]+(\.|$)/) && RSTART > 1) {
                pre = substr(k, 1, RSTART - 1)
                rest = substr(k, RSTART + 1)
                idx = rest; sub(/\..*$/, "", idx)
                sfx = ""
                if (rest ~ /\./) { sfx = rest; sub(/^[0-9]+\./, "", sfx) }
                PRE[i] = pre; IDX[i] = idx + 0; SFX[i] = sfx; ISLIST[i] = 1
                if (!(pre in seenpre)) { seenpre[pre] = 1; np++; onlypre = pre }
            } else { ISLIST[i] = 0 }
        }
        maxidx = -1; has_subkey = 0; nscalar = 0
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            if (!ISLIST[i]) { nscalar++; continue }
            if (np == 1 && PRE[i] == onlypre) {
                if (IDX[i] > maxidx) maxidx = IDX[i]
                if (SFX[i] != "") has_subkey = 1
            }
        }
        # Explode a list of RECORDS (elements carry sub-keys) always; a list of
        # bare SCALARS only when it DOMINATES the record (element count >= the
        # number of scalar sibling keys). This keeps a kv snapshot with a small
        # incidental list (a config tags list, npm maintainers) as one wide row,
        # while a record whose content IS the list (amtool Peers, skopeo Tags)
        # becomes one row per element.
        nelem = maxidx + 1
        if (np != 1 || maxidx < 1 || (!has_subkey && nelem < nscalar)) {
            for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print K[i] " " V[i]
        } else {
            entry = 0
            for (e = 0; e <= maxidx; e++) {
                entry++
                for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!ISLIST[i]) print "entry" entry "." K[i] " " V[i]
                for (i = 1; i <= n; i++)
                    if (ISLIST[i] && PRE[i] == onlypre && IDX[i] == e) {
                        if (SFX[i] == "") print "entry" entry "." PRE[i] " " V[i]
                        else print "entry" entry "." PRE[i] "." SFX[i] " " V[i]
                    }
            }
            print "total_entries " entry
        }
    }'
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=126ca4bf8accef13d075e8b0d0a71804702796793d17508a46491000ecad4314===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Interactive field selection for envoy-extract
##
## TUI-based field picker with keyboard navigation.
## Dependencies: _helpers.sh (strip_strat_prefix)
################################################################################

# Return the Nth value (0-indexed) from a newline-delimited string.
# Result in _NTH_RESULT (no subshell needed).
_interactive_get_nth () {
    local list="$1" n="$2" i=0
    while IFS= read -r val; do
        if [[ $i -eq $n ]]; then _NTH_RESULT="$val"; return; fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "$list"
    _NTH_RESULT="0"
}

# Toggle the Nth value in a newline-delimited "0"/"1" string.
# Result in _TOGGLE_RESULT (no subshell needed).
_interactive_toggle_nth () {
    local list="$1" n="$2" i=0
    _TOGGLE_RESULT=""
    while IFS= read -r val; do
        if [[ $i -eq $n ]]; then
            if [[ "$val" == "1" ]]; then val="0"; else val="1"; fi
        fi
        _TOGGLE_RESULT+="$val"$'\n'
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "$list"
    _TOGGLE_RESULT="${_TOGGLE_RESULT%$'\n'}"
}

# Set all values in a newline-delimited string to a given value.
# Result in _SETALL_RESULT (no subshell needed).
_interactive_set_all () {
    local count="$1" val="$2" i
    _SETALL_RESULT=""
    for ((i=0; i<count; i++)); do
        _SETALL_RESULT+="$val"$'\n'
    done
    _SETALL_RESULT="${_SETALL_RESULT%$'\n'}"
}

# Interactive field selector. Sets _SELECTED_FIELDS (comma-separated field numbers).
_interactive_select () {
    local input="$1"

    # Build parallel arrays of field names (newline-delimited)
    local field_count=0
    local field_names=""
    local selected=""

    while IFS= read -r _iline; do
        [[ -z "$_iline" ]] && continue
        strip_strat_prefix "$_iline"
        local _fname="${_STRIPPED_LINE%% *}"
        field_names+="$_fname"$'\n'
        selected+="1"$'\n'
        field_count=$((field_count + 1))
    done <<< "$input"

    field_names="${field_names%$'\n'}"
    selected="${selected%$'\n'}"

    if [[ $field_count -eq 0 ]]; then
        _SELECTED_FIELDS=""
        return
    fi

    # Check for TTY -- if not a terminal, warn and select all
    if ! [ -e /dev/tty ]; then
        _log_warn "--interactive ignored: not a terminal (selecting all fields)"
        _SELECTED_FIELDS=""
        local _j
        for ((_j=1; _j<=field_count; _j++)); do
            if [[ -n "$_SELECTED_FIELDS" ]]; then _SELECTED_FIELDS+=","; fi
            _SELECTED_FIELDS+="$_j"
        done
        return
    fi

    local cursor=0
    local done_flag=0

    # Save terminal state
    local _saved_stty
    _saved_stty=$(stty -g </dev/tty 2>/dev/null)
    stty -echo -icanon min 1 </dev/tty 2>/dev/null

    while [[ $done_flag -eq 0 ]]; do
        # Render
        {
            printf '\033[H\033[2J'
            printf 'Select fields (SPACE=toggle, a=all, n=none, ENTER=confirm, q=cancel):\n\n'
            local _i=0
            while IFS= read -r _fn; do
                _interactive_get_nth "$selected" "$_i"
                local _sel="$_NTH_RESULT"
                local _marker="[ ]"
                if [[ "$_sel" == "1" ]]; then _marker="[x]"; fi
                local _cursor_marker="  "
                if [[ $_i -eq $cursor ]]; then _cursor_marker="> "; fi
                printf '%s%s %2d  %s\n' "$_cursor_marker" "$_marker" "$((_i + 1))" "$_fn"
                _i=$((_i + 1))
            done <<< "$field_names"
            printf '\n'
        } >/dev/tty

        # Read key from /dev/tty
        local key=""
        IFS= read -rsn1 key </dev/tty

        case "$key" in
            $'\x1b')
                # Escape sequence -- read CSI
                local _seq="" _code=""
                # Use stty timeout for escape sequence bytes
                stty min 0 time 1 </dev/tty 2>/dev/null
                IFS= read -rsn1 _seq </dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true
                if [[ "$_seq" == "[" ]]; then
                    IFS= read -rsn1 _code </dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true
                    case "$_code" in
                        A) if [[ $cursor -gt 0 ]]; then cursor=$((cursor - 1)); fi ;;
                        B) if [[ $cursor -lt $((field_count - 1)) ]]; then cursor=$((cursor + 1)); fi ;;
                    esac
                fi
                # Restore blocking read
                stty min 1 time 0 </dev/tty 2>/dev/null
                ;;
            ' ')
                _interactive_toggle_nth "$selected" "$cursor"; selected="$_TOGGLE_RESULT"
                ;;
            'a')
                _interactive_set_all "$field_count" "1"; selected="$_SETALL_RESULT"
                ;;
            'n')
                _interactive_set_all "$field_count" "0"; selected="$_SETALL_RESULT"
                ;;
            ''|$'\n')
                done_flag=1
                ;;
            'q')
                stty "$_saved_stty" </dev/tty 2>/dev/null
                printf '\033[H\033[2J' >/dev/tty
                exit 1
                ;;
        esac
    done

    # Restore terminal
    stty "$_saved_stty" </dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    printf '\033[H\033[2J' >/dev/tty

    # Build comma-separated field numbers for selected items
    _SELECTED_FIELDS=""
    local _j=0
    while IFS= read -r _sval; do
        if [[ "$_sval" == "1" ]]; then
            if [[ -n "$_SELECTED_FIELDS" ]]; then _SELECTED_FIELDS+=","; fi
            _SELECTED_FIELDS+="$((_j + 1))"
        fi
        _j=$((_j + 1))
    done <<< "$selected"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/lib/_postprocess.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=41bce7f11f2236676540c75df0bbf4f7de7b03c223e682895bc2dae23e6414a0===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Post-processing functions for envoy-extract
##
## Accumulate, deduplicate, rename, aggregate, and filter extracted fields.
## Dependencies: _helpers.sh (strip_strat_prefix, _clean_field, _count_lines)
################################################################################

# Accumulate strategy output into the global output variable.
store () {
    local input="$1"
    local label="$2"

    # Number each line and prefix with strategy label (pure bash, no forks)
    local _n=0
    while IFS= read -r _sline; do
        [[ -z "$_sline" ]] && continue
        _n=$((_n + 1))
        output+="${label}:${_n}	${_sline}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$input"
}

# Deduplicate output across strategies.
# When multiple strategies extract the same field name+value, keep only the first.
# Sort-based O(n log n) approach using SOH (0x01) as the record delimiter.
# Format: fieldpart SOH lineno SOH origline
# Sort by fieldpart (col 1 only), dedup, restore insertion order by lineno (col 2).
deduplicate_output () {
    local input="$1"
    [[ -z "$input" ]] && return

    local _n=0 _formatted=""
    while IFS= read -r _dline; do
        [[ -z "$_dline" ]] && continue
        _n=$((_n + 1))
        local _fpart
        case "$_dline" in
            *$'\t'*) _fpart="${_dline#*$'\t'}" ;;
            *)       _fpart="$_dline" ;;
        esac
        _formatted+="${_fpart}"$'\x01'"${_n}"$'\x01'"${_dline}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$input"

    # Sort by fieldpart (SOH col 1), dedup, restore order by lineno (SOH col 2)
    printf '%s' "$_formatted" \
        | sort -t$'\x01' -k1,1 -u \
        | sort -t$'\x01' -k2,2 -n \
        | while IFS=$'\x01' read -r _fpart _lno _orig; do
            echo "$_orig"
          done
}

# Apply field renames to output.
# Renames only the field name portion (after STRAT prefix tab, before first space).
apply_renames () {
    local input="$1"
    local renames="$2"

    # Build a sed script for O(n) rename application.
    # Each rename pair becomes a sed substitution on the field name portion
    # (the part between the tab and the first space).
    #
    # ENV-172: read the comma-separated rename list into an array
    # (`read -r -a`) instead of `for pair in $renames`. The legacy form
    # word-split on `,` correctly (IFS=','), but ALSO glob-expanded the
    # unquoted variable against CWD, so a `--rename 'a=*'` would
    # resolve `*` to whatever filenames were sitting around.
    #
    # ENV-172 (sed escapes): the pattern-side class previously was
    # `[.[\/*^$]` Aje28094Aj covered `.`, `[`, `\`, `/`, `*`, `^`, `$` but
    # missed `]` (would close the char class). The replacement-side
    # class `[\/&]` covered `/` and `&` but missed `\`. A field name
    # containing `]` or a replacement containing a literal backslash
    # produced a malformed sed script and aborted the pipeline.
    local _renames_arr=()
    IFS=',' read -r -a _renames_arr <<< "$renames"
    local _sed_script=""
    local pair
    for pair in "${_renames_arr[@]}"; do
        local old_name="${pair%%=*}"
        local new_name="${pair#*=}"
        [[ -z "$old_name" || -z "$new_name" ]] && continue
        # Pattern-side: escape every BRE metacharacter PLUS `]`. The
        # bracket class `[].[\/*^$]` lists `]` first (so it's a
        # literal not the closer), then `.`, `[`, `\`, `/`, `*`, `^`,
        # `$`. The pre-fix class `[.[\/*^$]` missed `]` Aje28094Aj a field
        # name containing `]` produced a malformed sed script.
        local _eo _en
        _eo="$(printf '%s' "$old_name" | sed 's/[].[\/*^$]/\\&/g')"
        # Replacement-side: escape `\`, `/`, and `&`. Pre-fix `\` was
        # NOT in the class (the class was `[\/&]` which is `/` and `&`
        # only), so a new_name containing a literal backslash produced
        # an invalid sed substitution.
        _en="$(printf '%s' "$new_name" | sed 's/[\\/&]/\\&/g')"
        _sed_script+="s/	${_eo} /	${_en} /;"
    done

    if [[ -z "$_sed_script" ]]; then
        echo "$input"
        return
    fi

    echo "$input" | sed "$_sed_script"
}

# Aggregate numeric fields: compute count/min/max/sum/avg.
# Uses a single awk call -- float arithmetic makes pure-bash impractical here.
aggregate_output () {
    local input="$1"

    echo "$input" | awk '/^$/ { next } {
        # Extract field portion (after STRAT prefix tab)
        idx = index($0, "\t")
        if (idx > 0) {
            rest = substr($0, idx + 1)
        } else {
            rest = $0
        }

        # Split into name and value
        n = split(rest, parts, " ")
        if (n < 2) next
        name = parts[1]
        value = parts[2]

        # Check if value is numeric
        if (value + 0 == value && value != "") {
            if (!(name in count)) {
                order[++order_n] = name
            }
            count[name]++
            sum[name] += value
            if (!(name in min_v) || value + 0 < min_v[name] + 0) min_v[name] = value
            if (!(name in max_v) || value + 0 > max_v[name] + 0) max_v[name] = value
        }
    }
    END {
        for (i = 1; i <= order_n; i++) {
            name = order[i]
            if (count[name] > 1) {
                printf "%s_count %d\n", name, count[name]
                printf "%s_min %s\n", name, min_v[name]
                printf "%s_max %s\n", name, max_v[name]
                printf "%s_sum %s\n", name, sum[name]
                printf "%s_avg %.2f\n", name, sum[name] / count[name]
            }
        }
    }'
}

# Filter output to only include fields matching a regex pattern.
# Operates on STRAT-prefixed lines; extracts field name from after the tab.
# Result replaces $output in-place (caller passes/receives via global).
apply_field_pattern () {
    local input="$1"
    local pattern="$2"
    [[ -z "$input" || -z "$pattern" ]] && { echo "$input"; return; }

    local _result="" _fpline _fpclean _fpname
    while IFS= read -r _fpline; do
        [[ -z "$_fpline" ]] && continue
        # Extract field name: strip STRAT prefix, then take first word
        case "$_fpline" in
            *$'\t'*) _fpclean="${_fpline#*$'\t'}" ;;
            *)       _fpclean="$_fpline" ;;
        esac
        _fpname="${_fpclean%% *}"
        if [[ "$_fpname" =~ $pattern ]]; then
            _result+="$_fpline"$'\n'
        fi
    done <<< "$input"
    printf '%s' "${_result%$'\n'}"
}

# Filter output to exclude fields with exact name matches.
# _OPT_exclude_fields array must be set by caller.
apply_exclude_fields () {
    local input="$1"
    [[ -z "$input" ]] && { echo "$input"; return; }
    [[ ${#_OPT_exclude_fields[@]} -eq 0 ]] && { echo "$input"; return; }

    # Build a lookup string for O(1) matching
    local _excl_lookup=$'\n'
    local _ef
    for _ef in "${_OPT_exclude_fields[@]}"; do
        _excl_lookup+="$_ef"$'\n'
    done

    local _result="" _efline _efclean _efname
    while IFS= read -r _efline; do
        [[ -z "$_efline" ]] && continue
        case "$_efline" in
            *$'\t'*) _efclean="${_efline#*$'\t'}" ;;
            *)       _efclean="$_efline" ;;
        esac
        _efname="${_efclean%% *}"
        if [[ "$_excl_lookup" == *$'\n'"$_efname"$'\n'* ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        _result+="$_efline"$'\n'
    done <<< "$input"
    printf '%s' "${_result%$'\n'}"
}

# Filter raw output by field numbers or names and strip STRAT prefix.
# Supports: "1,3,5" (numeric), "hostname,cpu_count" (names), or mixed.
# Returns clean "name value" lines for format functions.
filter_fields () {
    local input="$1"
    local field_filter="$2"

    # Build lookup string from comma-separated field specs
    local _wanted=$'\n'"${field_filter//,/$'\n'}"$'\n'

    # Determine if filter is purely numeric
    local _is_numeric=1
    if [[ ! "$field_filter" =~ ^[0-9,]+$ ]]; then
        _is_numeric=0
    fi

    local _n=0
    while IFS= read -r _fline; do
        [[ -z "$_fline" ]] && continue
        _n=$((_n + 1))

        # Strip STRAT prefix
        strip_strat_prefix "$_fline"
        local _clean="$_STRIPPED_LINE"
        local _fname="${_clean%% *}"

        if [[ $_is_numeric -eq 1 ]]; then
            # Check by line number
            [[ "$_wanted" == *$'\n'"$_n"$'\n'* ]] || continue
        else
            # Check by field name (or number for mixed)
            local _match=0
            if [[ "$_wanted" == *$'\n'"$_n"$'\n'* ]]; then
                _match=1
            elif [[ "$_wanted" == *$'\n'"$_fname"$'\n'* ]]; then
                _match=1
            fi
            [[ $_match -eq 1 ]] || continue
        fi
        echo "$_clean"
    done <<< "$input"
}

===FILE: extract/lib/_techniques.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=97f56efa1523f280279420774ea8f441935a6f726c926d96c3a89cad5f3c7237===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Shared extraction technique functions for envoy-extract
##
## Pure-bash utility functions used by generic (technique-tagged) strategies.
## Requires bash 4.0+.
##
## Globals set (no subshell forks):
##   _TECH_STRIPPED   result of _tech_strip_leading
##   _TECH_KEY_VALID  result of _tech_validate_key (0=invalid, 1=valid)
##   _TECH_BLOCKS     result of _tech_split_blocks (null-delimited blocks)
##
## Dependencies: _helpers.sh (_clean_field -> $_CLEANED)
################################################################################

# Strip leading spaces and optional "* " bullet prefix from a string.
# Result stored in $_TECH_STRIPPED (no subshell fork).
_tech_strip_leading () {
    _TECH_STRIPPED="$1"
    while [[ "$_TECH_STRIPPED" == " "* ]]; do
        _TECH_STRIPPED="${_TECH_STRIPPED# }"
    done
    case "$_TECH_STRIPPED" in
        "* "*) _TECH_STRIPPED="${_TECH_STRIPPED#\* }" ;;
    esac
}

# Validate a field key. Sets $_TECH_KEY_VALID=1 if valid, 0 if not.
# Rules: non-empty, length <= 50, does not start with a digit.
_tech_validate_key () {
    _TECH_KEY_VALID=0
    [[ -z "$1" ]] && return
    [[ ${#1} -gt 50 ]] && return
    case "$1" in
        [0-9]*) return ;;
    esac
    _TECH_KEY_VALID=1
}

# Extract key: value pairs from text (colon-delimited).
# Emits "field value" lines to stdout.
# Usage: _tech_kv_colon "$text" "$prefix"
#   $prefix: dot-prefix for output keys (e.g. "record1" -> "record1.key value")
#            pass "" for no prefix.
# Skips: empty lines, keys >50 chars, digit-start keys, URL values (http://, https://).
_tech_kv_colon () {
    local _tkc_text="$1"
    local _tkc_prefix="$2"
    local _tkc_line _tkc_key _tkc_value
    while IFS= read -r _tkc_line; do
        [[ -z "$_tkc_line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_tkc_line" != *":"* ]] && continue
        _tech_strip_leading "$_tkc_line"
        _tkc_line="$_TECH_STRIPPED"
        _tkc_key="${_tkc_line%%:*}"
        _tkc_value="${_tkc_line#*: }"
        # If no space after colon, take everything after the colon
        if [[ "$_tkc_value" == "$_tkc_line" ]]; then
            _tkc_value="${_tkc_line#*:}"
        fi
        _tech_validate_key "$_tkc_key"
        [[ $_TECH_KEY_VALID -eq 0 ]] && continue
        # Skip URL values (http://, https://, and // protocol-relative URLs)
        [[ "$_tkc_value" == "http://"* || "$_tkc_value" == "https://"* || "$_tkc_value" == "//"* ]] && continue
        _clean_field "$_tkc_key";   _tkc_key="$_CLEANED"
        _clean_field "$_tkc_value"; _tkc_value="$_CLEANED"
        [[ -z "$_tkc_key" || -z "$_tkc_value" ]] && continue
        if [[ -n "$_tkc_prefix" ]]; then
            echo "${_tkc_prefix}.${_tkc_key} ${_tkc_value}"
        else
            echo "${_tkc_key} ${_tkc_value}"
        fi
    done <<< "$_tkc_text"
}

# Extract key=value pairs from text (equals-delimited).
# Emits "field value" lines to stdout.
# Usage: _tech_kv_equals "$text" "$prefix"
# Skips: ==, +=, != comparisons; empty/invalid keys.
_tech_kv_equals () {
    local _tke_text="$1"
    local _tke_prefix="$2"
    local _tke_line _tke_key _tke_value
    while IFS= read -r _tke_line; do
        [[ -z "$_tke_line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_tke_line" != *"="* ]] && continue
        # Skip comparison operators
        [[ "$_tke_line" == *"=="* || "$_tke_line" == *"+="* || "$_tke_line" == *"!="* ]] && continue
        _tech_strip_leading "$_tke_line"
        _tke_line="$_TECH_STRIPPED"
        _tke_key="${_tke_line%%=*}"
        _tke_value="${_tke_line#*=}"
        _tech_validate_key "$_tke_key"
        [[ $_TECH_KEY_VALID -eq 0 ]] && continue
        _clean_field "$_tke_key";   _tke_key="$_CLEANED"
        _clean_field "$_tke_value"; _tke_value="$_CLEANED"
        [[ -z "$_tke_key" || -z "$_tke_value" ]] && continue
        if [[ -n "$_tke_prefix" ]]; then
            echo "${_tke_prefix}.${_tke_key} ${_tke_value}"
        else
            echo "${_tke_key} ${_tke_value}"
        fi
    done <<< "$_tke_text"
}

# Split text into blank-line-separated blocks.
# Result stored in $_TECH_BLOCKS as SOH ($'\x01') delimited segments.
# SOH (ASCII 0x01) is used instead of null to be safe in bash string variables.
# Callers iterate blocks:
#   local _remaining="$_TECH_BLOCKS"
#   while [[ -n "$_remaining" ]]; do
#       local _block="${_remaining%%$'\x01'*}"
#       [[ "$_remaining" == *$'\x01'* ]] && _remaining="${_remaining#*$'\x01'}" || _remaining=""
#       # process $_block
#   done
_tech_split_blocks () {
    _TECH_BLOCKS=""
    local _tsb_current="" _tsb_line
    while IFS= read -r _tsb_line; do
        if [[ -z "$_tsb_line" ]]; then
            if [[ -n "$_tsb_current" ]]; then
                if [[ -n "$_TECH_BLOCKS" ]]; then
                    _TECH_BLOCKS+=$'\x01'"$_tsb_current"
                else
                    _TECH_BLOCKS="$_tsb_current"
                fi
                _tsb_current=""
            fi
        else
            if [[ -n "$_tsb_current" ]]; then
                _tsb_current+=$'\n'"$_tsb_line"
            else
                _tsb_current="$_tsb_line"
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$1"
    # Flush final block (no trailing blank line)
    if [[ -n "$_tsb_current" ]]; then
        if [[ -n "$_TECH_BLOCKS" ]]; then
            _TECH_BLOCKS+=$'\x01'"$_tsb_current"
        else
            _TECH_BLOCKS="$_tsb_current"
        fi
    fi
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/lib/_validate.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=eedfbeb8396b10865b11ecf1cfa968691e8d10de7031ec2fb77047d6462be800===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Strategy validation for envoy-extract
##
## Validate strategy files for required functions, metadata headers,
## sample paths, naming conventions, and version format.
## Dependencies: _log.sh, _discovery.sh (read_strategy_metadata, build_strategy_list)
################################################################################

# Validate a single strategy file.
# Prints PASS/FAIL lines to stdout. Returns 0 if all checks pass, 1 otherwise.
validate_strategy () {
    local filepath="$1"
    local _v_errors=0

    if [[ ! -f "$filepath" ]]; then
        echo "FAIL: File not found: $filepath"
        return 1
    fi

    local fname="${filepath##*/}"
    fname="${fname%.sh}"

    # Check 1: Required metadata headers
    read_strategy_metadata "$filepath"

    if [[ -n "$_META_NAME" ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has ## Name: header ($_META_NAME)"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Missing ## Name: header"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    if [[ -n "$_META_DESCRIPTION" ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has ## Description: header"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Missing ## Description: header"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    if [[ "$_META_VERSION" != "0" ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has ## Version: header ($_META_VERSION)"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Missing ## Version: header"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    if [[ "$_META_PRIORITY" != "99" ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has ## Priority: header ($_META_PRIORITY)"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Missing ## Priority: header (defaulting to 99)"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    # Check 2: Version format (N.N)
    if [[ "$_META_VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Version format is valid"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Version format should be N.N (got: $_META_VERSION)"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    # Check 3: Filename matches ## Name: header
    if [[ -n "$_META_NAME" ]]; then
        if [[ "$_META_NAME" == "$fname" ]]; then
            echo "PASS: Filename matches ## Name: header"
        else
            echo "FAIL: Filename '$fname' does not match ## Name: '$_META_NAME'"
            _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
        fi
    fi

    # Check 4: Required functions exist (must be actual function definitions,
    # not comments or strings containing the function name)
    local _v_has_detect=0 _v_has_extract=0
    local _v_line _v_trimmed
    while IFS= read -r _v_line; do
        # Strip leading whitespace for matching
        _v_trimmed="${_v_line#"${_v_line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        # Skip comment lines
        case "$_v_trimmed" in '#'*) continue ;; esac
        case "$_v_trimmed" in
            'strategy_detect'*'()'*|'strategy_detect '*'('*|'function strategy_detect'*) _v_has_detect=1 ;;
            'strategy_extract'*'()'*|'strategy_extract '*'('*|'function strategy_extract'*) _v_has_extract=1 ;;
        esac
    done < "$filepath"

    if [[ $_v_has_detect -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has strategy_detect function"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Missing strategy_detect function"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    if [[ $_v_has_extract -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has strategy_extract function"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Missing strategy_extract function"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    # Check 5: ## Sample: header and path exists
    local _v_sample=""
    local _v_n=0
    while IFS= read -r _v_line; do
        _v_n=$((_v_n + 1))
        [[ $_v_n -gt 15 ]] && break
        case "$_v_line" in
            '## Sample: '*)
                _v_sample="${_v_line#'## Sample: '}"
                break
                ;;
        esac
    done < "$filepath"

    if [[ -n "$_v_sample" ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Has ## Sample: header ($_v_sample)"
        # Check if sample path exists relative to samples dir
        local _v_samples_dir="${SCRIPT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}/samples"
        if [[ -f "$_v_samples_dir/$_v_sample" ]]; then
            echo "PASS: Sample file exists"
        else
            echo "WARN: Sample file not found: $_v_sample"
        fi
    else
        echo "WARN: Missing ## Sample: header"
    fi

    # Check 6: Syntax check (bash -n)
    if bash -n "$filepath" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "PASS: Syntax check (bash -n)"
    else
        echo "FAIL: Syntax error detected by bash -n"
        _v_errors=$((_v_errors + 1))
    fi

    # Check 7: _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE is set in strategy_detect
    local _v_has_confidence=0
    while IFS= read -r _v_line; do
        case "$_v_line" in
            *'_STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE='*) _v_has_confidence=1; break ;;
        esac
    done < "$filepath"
    if [[ $_v_has_confidence -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Sets _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE in detect"
    else
        echo "WARN: Does not set _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE (will default to 50)"
    fi

    # Check 8: Helper function naming convention (_strat_* required)
    local _v_bad_helpers=0
    while IFS= read -r _v_line; do
        # Match function definitions: word ()
        case "$_v_line" in
            strategy_detect*|strategy_extract*) continue ;;
            _strat_*'()'*|_strat_*'('*) continue ;;
            *'() {'*|*'()'*)
                # Extract function name
                local _v_fn="${_v_line%%(*}"
                _v_fn="${_v_fn# }"
                _v_fn="${_v_fn% }"
                case "$_v_fn" in
                    strategy_detect|strategy_extract) ;;
                    _strat_*) ;;
                    *)
                        if [[ $_v_bad_helpers -eq 0 ]]; then
                            echo "WARN: Helper function '$_v_fn' does not use _strat_* naming convention"
                        fi
                        _v_bad_helpers=$((_v_bad_helpers + 1))
                        ;;
                esac
                ;;
        esac
    done < "$filepath"
    if [[ $_v_bad_helpers -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "PASS: Helper function naming convention (_strat_*)"
    fi

    if [[ $_v_errors -gt 0 ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Validate all strategies in all strategy directories.
# Prints a summary report. Returns 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail.
validate_all_strategies () {
    local strategy_dirs=("$STRATEGIES_DIR")
    [[ -d "${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.mfe/strategies" ]] && strategy_dirs+=("${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.mfe/strategies")
    [[ -n "${_OPT_plugin_dir:-}" && -d "${_OPT_plugin_dir:-}" ]] && strategy_dirs+=("$_OPT_plugin_dir")

    local sorted_list
    sorted_list=$(build_strategy_list "${strategy_dirs[@]}")

    if [[ -z "$sorted_list" ]]; then
        _log_error "No strategies found."
        return 1
    fi

    local _va_total=0 _va_pass=0 _va_fail=0
    while IFS='|' read -r _priority _version strategy_file; do
        [[ -z "$strategy_file" ]] && continue
        _va_total=$((_va_total + 1))
        local sname="${strategy_file##*/}"
        sname="${sname%.sh}"
        echo "--- Validating: $sname ($strategy_file)"
        if validate_strategy "$strategy_file"; then
            _va_pass=$((_va_pass + 1))
        else
            _va_fail=$((_va_fail + 1))
        fi
        echo ""
    done <<< "$sorted_list"

    echo "========================================"
    echo "Validation: $_va_total strategies, $_va_pass passed, $_va_fail failed"
    echo "========================================"

    if [[ $_va_fail -gt 0 ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# ENV-018: self-validation. Run each strategy's detect() against its declared
# ## Sample: file and report strategies whose self-confidence is below the
# threshold (default 75). Miscalibrated strategies indicate either a wrong
# sample, a buggy detector, or inflated confidence scoring.
#
# Honors globals:
#   _OPT_self_validate_threshold  (int, default 75)
#   _OPT_self_validate_strategy   (string, filter to one strategy name)
#
# Returns 0 if all strategies meet the threshold, 1 otherwise.
self_validate_strategies () {
    local threshold="${_OPT_self_validate_threshold:-75}"
    local filter="${_OPT_self_validate_strategy:-}"

    local strategy_dirs=("$STRATEGIES_DIR")
    [[ -d "${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.mfe/strategies" ]] && strategy_dirs+=("${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.mfe/strategies")
    [[ -n "${_OPT_plugin_dir:-}" && -d "${_OPT_plugin_dir:-}" ]] && strategy_dirs+=("$_OPT_plugin_dir")

    local sorted_list
    sorted_list=$(build_strategy_list "${strategy_dirs[@]}")
    if [[ -z "$sorted_list" ]]; then
        _log_error "No strategies found."
        return 1
    fi

    # Sample paths in ## Sample: headers are relative to the EnvoyExtract root
    # (they already include the "samples/" prefix).
    local envoy_extract_root="${SCRIPT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"

    local total=0 pass=0 below=0 no_sample=0 missing_file=0
    local -a _below_lines=()
    local -a _no_sample_lines=()
    local -a _missing_file_lines=()

    printf "Self-validation: running each strategy's detect() against its declared sample\n"
    printf "Threshold: %d\n\n" "$threshold"
    printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "STRATEGY" "CONF" "SAMPLE" "VERDICT"
    printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "--------" "----" "------" "-------"

    while IFS='|' read -r _priority _version strategy_file; do
        [[ -z "$strategy_file" ]] && continue
        local name="${strategy_file##*/}"
        name="${name%.sh}"
        [[ -n "$filter" && "$name" != "$filter" ]] && continue
        total=$((total + 1))

        # Look up the ## Sample: header
        local sample=""
        local _line _n=0
        while IFS= read -r _line; do
            _n=$((_n + 1))
            [[ $_n -gt 20 ]] && break
            case "$_line" in
                '## Sample: '*) sample="${_line#'## Sample: '}"; break ;;
            esac
        done < "$strategy_file"

        if [[ -z "$sample" ]]; then
            no_sample=$((no_sample + 1))
            _no_sample_lines+=("$name")
            printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "$name" "-" "(no sample)" "SKIP"
            continue
        fi

        local sample_path="$envoy_extract_root/$sample"
        if [[ ! -f "$sample_path" ]]; then
            missing_file=$((missing_file + 1))
            _missing_file_lines+=("$name: $sample")
            printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "$name" "-" "$sample" "MISSING"
            continue
        fi

        # Source the strategy and invoke detect() against the sample.
        # Run in a subshell so a strategy's state changes don't leak.
        local conf
        conf=$(
            set +e
            unset -f strategy_detect strategy_extract 2>/dev/null
            source "$strategy_file" >/dev/null 2>&1
            if ! type -t strategy_detect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "-1"
                exit 0
            fi
            local text
            text=$(cat "$sample_path")
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=50
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON=""
            if ! strategy_detect "$text" "$(basename "$sample_path")" "" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "0"
                exit 0
            fi
            # Clamp
            [[ "$_STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE" -lt 0 ]] && _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
            [[ "$_STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE" -gt 100 ]] && _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=100
            echo "$_STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE"
        )
        # Strip anything but the first line/integer
        conf="${conf%%$'\n'*}"

        if [[ "$conf" == "-1" ]]; then
            printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "$name" "-" "$sample" "NO-DETECT-FN"
            continue
        fi

        if [[ "$conf" -ge "$threshold" ]]; then
            pass=$((pass + 1))
            printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "$name" "$conf" "$sample" "PASS"
        else
            below=$((below + 1))
            _below_lines+=("$name (conf $conf, sample $sample)")
            printf "  %-22s %-8s %-30s %s\n" "$name" "$conf" "$sample" "BELOW"
        fi
    done <<< "$sorted_list"

    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    printf "Self-validation: %d total, %d pass, %d below threshold, %d no sample, %d missing file\n" \
        "$total" "$pass" "$below" "$no_sample" "$missing_file"
    echo "========================================"

    if [[ $below -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo "Below threshold ($threshold):"
        local _line
        for _line in "${_below_lines[@]}"; do
            echo "  - $_line"
        done
    fi
    if [[ $missing_file -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo "Missing sample files:"
        for _line in "${_missing_file_lines[@]}"; do
            echo "  - $_line"
        done
    fi

    # Exit 1 if any strategy fell below threshold or has a missing sample file.
    if [[ $below -gt 0 || $missing_file -gt 0 ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Handoff Aje28094Aj EnvoyExtract/samples

## Status: Complete (~281 files)

Sample input files organized by strategy for testing and documentation. All 126 strategies have sample data (1-3 files each), plus edge-case samples for dedup verification and robustness testing.

Sample input files for the `jsonl` strategy (JSON Lines format Aje28094Aj one JSON object per line).

- `basic.jsonl` Aje28094Aj Simple JSONL with name/age/city fields

# Handoff -- EnvoyExtract/strategies

## Status: Active (178 strategies, v4.0)

Individual strategy files for the Multi-Format Extractor. Each file defines `strategy_detect()` and `strategy_extract()` functions, plus metadata headers (`## Name:`, `## Description:`, `## Version:`, `## Priority:`). Strategies are organized into 17 categorized subdirectories.

## Directory Structure

| Subdirectory | Count | Description |
|-------------|-------|-------------|
| `benchmark/` | 42 | Performance/benchmarking tool output (incl. HPC: OSU, HPCG, NPB, IMB, IOR, b_eff) |
| `build/` | 16 | Build/test/CI tool output |
| `config/` | 11 | Configuration file formats |
| `container/` | 6 | Docker/Kubernetes tool output |
| `delimited/` | 7 | Delimiter-based text formats |
| `filesystem/` | 4 | HPC parallel filesystem output (Lustre, GPFS, BeeGFS, NFS) |
| `gpu/` | 3 | GPU/accelerator monitoring (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi, CUDA deviceQuery) |
| `hardware/` | 9 | Cluster/hardware inventory (lscpu, lspci, numactl, ibstat, dmidecode, hwloc, ethtool, lshw, xpu-smi) |
| `hpc/` | 10 | HPC schedulers & MPI (Slurm, PBS, LSF, SGE, Flux, HTCondor, MPI profiling, Darshan) |
| `logging/` | 6 | Log file formats |
| `misc/` | 5 | Miscellaneous formats |
| `network/` | 7 | Network/HTTP tool output |
| `profiling/` | 11 | Profiling tool output (VTune, gprof, perf report, TAU, LIKWID, etc.) |
| `scientific/` | 13 | Scientific data formats (HDF5, NetCDF, PDB, FITS, VTK, GROMACS, LAMMPS, VASP, Gaussian, AMBER, NAMD, CP2K, QE) |
| `security/` | 6 | Security scanning/crypto tool output |
| `structured/` | 9 | Structured data formats (JSON, YAML, etc.) |
| `system/` | 13 | System monitoring/info tool output |

## Adding a Strategy

1. Create `<name>.sh` with `## Name:`, `## Description:`, `## Version:` headers
2. Define `strategy_detect($text)` -- return 0 if applicable
3. Define `strategy_extract($text)` -- output `fieldname value` lines
4. `clean_text` from `envoy-extract` is available after sourcing

===META: mode=644 sha256=00a3138c04cab84b357f598376148fde4419538f8f14dff237dab45511ac2e13===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: dotnet-list-package
## Description: Extract package references from `dotnet list package` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/dotnet-list-package/basic.txt

# `dotnet list package` prints a "Top-level Package / Requested / Resolved"
# table where each package row is marked with "> ". Each ">" row is one record
# with package/requested/resolved fields.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    if [[ "$text" == *"Top-level Package"* && "$text" == *"Resolved"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line s pkg req res rest
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Trim leading whitespace, then require the "> " row marker.
        s="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ "$s" == "> "* ]] || continue
        s="${s#> }"
        s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        pkg="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; rest="${s#"$pkg"}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        req="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"; rest="${rest#"$req"}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        res="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"
        [[ -z "$pkg" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.package ${pkg}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.requested ${req}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.resolved ${res}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/build/go-list.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=21dc1862f1bb8c842d43b05c94764f3e9ff8aefc90be0c3566837a6e54e0470f===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: go-list
## Description: Extract module paths from `go list -m all` output (main module + dependencies)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/go-list/basic.txt

# `go list -m all` prints the main module on the first line (path only, no
# version), then one dependency per line as "<path> <version>" (version like
# v1.9.1). Every non-blank line is one module; the single-column value is the
# module path (first token), which is unique per row.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local first="" nb=0 versioned=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        if [[ $nb -eq 1 ]]; then
            first="$line"
            # Main module: a single bare path token containing both '.' and '/'.
            [[ "$first" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+$ && "$first" == *.*/* ]] || return 1
            continue
        fi
        # Dependency lines: "<path> <version>" with a v-prefixed semantic version.
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+\ v[0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*$ ]]; then
            versioned=$((versioned + 1))
        else
            return 1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $versioned -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local path="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${path}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: go-mod-why
## Description: Extract the import path chain from `go mod why` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/go-mod-why/basic.txt

# `go mod why` prints "# <module>" comment headers followed by the import path
# chain, one package path per line. Each non-comment path line is one record
# (single column, the path itself).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local first="" nb=0 line ok=1
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        [[ $nb -eq 1 ]] && first="$line"
        # Comment headers, or single-token import paths containing '/'. Anything
        # with embedded whitespace (a real table row) disqualifies.
        if [[ "$line" == "#"* ]]; then
            continue
        elif [[ "$line" == *[[:space:]]* || "$line" != */* ]]; then
            ok=0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $nb -eq 0 ]] && return 1
    # Require the leading "# <module>" header that opens go mod why output.
    if [[ $ok -eq 1 && "$first" == "# "* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line s
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue
        s="$line"
        s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        s="${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$s" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${s}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: mix-deps
## Description: Extract dependencies from Elixir `mix deps` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/mix-deps/basic.txt

# `mix deps` lists each dependency as a "* name version (Hex package) (mix)"
# bullet, followed by indented continuation lines ("locked at ...", "ok").
# Only the bullet lines are records; the single field is the dependency name.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: hex-package bullets with a "locked at" lockfile continuation.
    [[ "$text" == *"(Hex package)"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"locked at "* ]] || return 1
    local deps=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^\*[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+[[:space:]] ]] && deps=$((deps + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $deps -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Only bullet lines; skip "locked at ..." / "ok" continuation lines.
        [[ "$line" =~ ^\*[[:space:]]+([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+) ]] || continue
        local name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${name}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: pnpm-why
## Description: Extract dependency lines from `pnpm why` tree output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/pnpm-why/basic.txt

# `pnpm why` prints a project banner ("<name>@<ver> <path>"), a "dependencies:"
# header, then a Unicode tree of "<name> <version>" nodes. Each dependency node
# is one record; the cleaned value strips the leading tree glyphs (single
# column).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # A "dependencies:" section drawn with box tree glyphs.
    if [[ "$text" == *"dependencies:"* && ( "$text" == *"Aje2949cAj"* || "$text" == *"Aje29494Aj"* ) ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line s
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Skip section headers ("dependencies:", "devDependencies:").
        [[ "$line" == *: && "$line" != *" "* ]] && continue
        # Skip the project banner: "<name>@<ver> <path>".
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+@[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+/ ]] && continue
        # Strip leading non-alphanumeric bytes (tree glyphs + spaces).
        s="$line"
        while [[ -n "$s" && "$s" != [A-Za-z0-9]* ]]; do s="${s#?}"; done
        s="${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$s" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${s}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: sbt-dependencytree
## Description: Extract dependencies from `sbt dependencyTree` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/sbt-dependencytree/basic.txt

# `sbt dependencyTree` prefixes every line with "[info]"; the root project is a
# bare "[info] <org>:<name>:<ver>" line and each dependency is drawn with a
# "+-" tree marker ("[info]   +-<org>:<name>:<ver>"). Only the "+-" dependency
# lines are records; the cleaned value is the coordinate after the marker
# (single column).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # NB: no _is_json guard Aje28094Aj sbt's "[info]"-prefixed lines start with '[' and
    # would be mis-flagged as a JSON array. The "[info] ... +-" signature below
    # is specific enough on its own.
    if [[ "$text" == *"[info]"* && "$text" == *"+-"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line s
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Only dependency lines carry the "+-" marker.
        [[ "$line" != *"+-"* ]] && continue
        s="${line##*+-}"
        s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        s="${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$s" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${s}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/cloud/kubectl-get-all.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=8bddd4f2dc3624f9921c30e9bcbb366f23e62807fbc83c5a58a15f9240ee106a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: kubectl-get-all
## Description: Parse `kubectl get all` multi-section output Aje28094Aj one record per resource kind
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/kubectl-get-all/basic.txt

# `kubectl get all` prints one section per resource kind, each led by a "NAME ..."
# header and separated by blank lines:
#   NAME  READY STATUS ...        (pods)
#   pod/web-...  1/1 Running ...
#   <blank>
#   NAME  TYPE  CLUSTER-IP ...     (services)
#   service/... ...
# One record per section (resource kind): its kind, the number of resources, and
# their names. Section headers and blank lines are skipped.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"pod/"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"service/"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"NAME"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
        function flush(){
            if (open){
                e++
                print "entry" e ".kind " (kind==""?"-":kind)
                print "entry" e ".count " cnt
                print "entry" e ".names " (names==""?"-":names)
            }
            open=0; kind=""; cnt=0; names=""
        }
        {
            if ($1=="NAME") { flush(); open=1; next }   # section header
            if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next
            if (!open) next
            name=$1
            k=name; sub(/\/.*$/,"",k)                   # kind: text before first /
            rn=name; sub(/^[^\/]*\//,"",rn)             # resource name: after first /
            if (kind=="") kind=k
            cnt++
            names=names (names==""?"":"_") rn
        }
        END{ flush(); if(e>0) print "total_entries " e }
    '
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: docker-ps
## Description: Extract container information from docker ps output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/docker-ps/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    # First non-empty line is the `docker ps` header: starts with CONTAINER and
    # carries the ps-specific COMMAND column. Requiring COMMAND avoids hijacking
    # `docker stats` (CONTAINER Aje280a6Aj CPU %/MEM Aje280a6Aj) and `buildah containers`
    # (CONTAINER Aje280a6Aj BUILDER/IMAGE ID Aje280a6Aj) Aje28094Aj those have no COMMAND column and are
    # tidied fine by the generic aligned-columns parser.
    local first_line=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        first_line="$_line"
        break
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ "$first_line" == "CONTAINER"* && "$first_line" == *"COMMAND"* ]]
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # Get the header line to find column positions
    local header_line=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        header_line="$_line"
        break
    done <<< "$text"

    # Find column start positions from the header
    # Docker ps uses fixed-width columns aligned by header words
    local col_names=()
    local col_starts=()

    _strat_docker_ps_parse_columns "$header_line"

    # Process each data row
    local row_num=0
    local line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line_num=$((line_num + 1))
        [[ $line_num -eq 1 ]] && continue  # skip header
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        row_num=$((row_num + 1))
        local prefix="container${row_num}"

        local i
        for ((i=0; i<${#col_names[@]}; i++)); do
            local col_name="${col_names[$i]}"
            local start="${col_starts[$i]}"
            local end=""
            if [[ $((i + 1)) -lt ${#col_names[@]} ]]; then
                end="${col_starts[$((i + 1))]}"
            fi

            local val
            if [[ -n "$end" ]]; then
                local _len=$((end - start))
                val="${line:$((start - 1)):$_len}"
            else
                val="${line:$((start - 1))}"
            fi

            # Trim leading/trailing whitespace
            while [[ "$val" == " "* ]]; do val="${val# }"; done
            while [[ "$val" == *" " ]]; do val="${val% }"; done
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue

            # Normalize column name
            col_name=$(_strat_docker_ps_normalize_col "$col_name")
            result+="${prefix}.${col_name} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

_strat_docker_ps_parse_columns () {
    local header="$1"
    col_names=()
    col_starts=()

    # Known docker ps column headers (multi-word headers)
    # "CONTAINER ID" is a two-word header
    local remaining="$header"
    local pos=1

    # Find each header's position
    local offset=0
    while [[ -n "$remaining" ]]; do
        # Skip leading spaces
        local stripped="$remaining"
        while [[ "$stripped" == " "* ]]; do stripped="${stripped# }"; done
        local spaces_skipped=$(( ${#remaining} - ${#stripped} ))
        offset=$((offset + spaces_skipped))
        remaining="$stripped"

        [[ -z "$remaining" ]] && break

        # Try to match a known two-word header first
        local matched=0
        if [[ "$remaining" == "CONTAINER ID"* ]]; then
            col_names+=("CONTAINER_ID")
            col_starts+=($((offset + 1)))
            local hdr="CONTAINER ID"
            remaining="${remaining#$hdr}"
            offset=$((offset + ${#hdr}))
            matched=1
        fi

        if [[ $matched -eq 0 ]]; then
            # Single-word header
            read -ra _arr <<< "$remaining"
            local word="${_arr[0]}"
            [[ -z "$word" ]] && break
            col_names+=("$word")
            col_starts+=($((offset + 1)))
            remaining="${remaining#$word}"
            offset=$((offset + ${#word}))
        fi
    done
}

_strat_docker_ps_normalize_col () {
    local col="$1"
    # Replace spaces with underscores
    col="${col// /_}"
    # Lowercase manually
    local _result=""
    local _i
    for ((_i=0; _i<${#col}; _i++)); do
        local _c="${col:$_i:1}"
        case "$_c" in
            A) _c=a ;; B) _c=b ;; C) _c=c ;; D) _c=d ;; E) _c=e ;;
            F) _c=f ;; G) _c=g ;; H) _c=h ;; I) _c=i ;; J) _c=j ;;
            K) _c=k ;; L) _c=l ;; M) _c=m ;; N) _c=n ;; O) _c=o ;;
            P) _c=p ;; Q) _c=q ;; R) _c=r ;; S) _c=s ;; T) _c=t ;;
            U) _c=u ;; V) _c=v ;; W) _c=w ;; X) _c=x ;; Y) _c=y ;;
            Z) _c=z ;;
        esac
        _result+="$_c"
    done
    echo "$_result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: cassandra-nodetool-tpstats
## Description: Extract thread-pool rows from `nodetool tpstats`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/cassandra-nodetool-tpstats/basic.txt

# `nodetool tpstats` starts with a thread-pool table:
#   Pool Name   Active  Pending  Completed  Blocked  All time blocked
#   ReadStage        0        0    1204853        0                 0
# followed by unrelated "Latencies ... dropped message types" and
# "Message type / Dropped" blocks. Emit ONE record per pool row (the 6-column
# rows whose last five columns are integers); the trailing blocks are ignored
# because they never form a 6-token row with five numeric fields.

_ctp_sanitize_val () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Signature: the distinctive thread-pool header columns.
    [[ "$text" == *"Pool Name"* ]]        || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Completed"* ]]        || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"All time blocked"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line ok i
    local -a t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#t[@]} -eq 6 ]] || continue
        ok=1
        for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            [[ "${t[$i]}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { ok=0; break; }
        done
        [[ $ok -eq 1 ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.pool_name $(_ctp_sanitize_val "${t[0]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.active ${t[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.pending ${t[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.completed ${t[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.blocked ${t[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.all_time_blocked ${t[5]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=11d451b45081352c23aadc5c992db72c4f1cbd56b36a8d38db090a59cd087671===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: clickhouse-processlist
## Description: Extract rows from a ClickHouse PrettyCompact Unicode box table
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/clickhouse-processlist/basic.txt

# ClickHouse's PrettyCompact format draws a Unicode box table. Column names live
# in the top border line and each data row is delimited by vertical bars:
#   Aje2948ce29480AjuserAje29480e294ace29480Ajquery_idAje29480e294ace29480AjaddressAje29480e294ace29480AjelapsedAje29480e294ace29480Ajread_rowsAje29480e294ace29480Ajmemory_usageAje29480e29490Aj
#   Aje29482Aj default Aje29482Aj 9f3c... Aje29482Aj 10.0.0.5:41022 Aje29482Aj 0.145 Aje29482Aj 120340 Aje29482Aj 33554432 Aje29482Aj
#   
# Generic table parsers mangle the box-drawing characters, so we handle it here.

# Box-drawing characters (UTF-8).
_CH_BAR=$'Aje29482Aj'    # Aje29482Aj  cell separator
_CH_TL=$'Aje2948cAj'     # Aje2948cAj  top-left
_CH_TR=$'Aje29490Aj'     # Aje29490Aj  top-right
_CH_TD=$'Aje294acAj'     # Aje294acAj  top tee (column split in header)
_CH_DASH=$'Aje29480Aj'   # Aje29480Aj  horizontal fill
_CH_BL=$'Aje29494Aj'     # Aje29494Aj  bottom-left
_CH_ML=$'Aje2949cAj'     # Aje2949cAj  mid-left

_ch_trim () {
    # Trim leading/trailing whitespace; echo result.
    local s="$1"
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    s="${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

_ch_sanitise () {
    # Collapse whitespace runs to single underscores. Used for column HEADERS,
    # where the whole label becomes a field NAME.
    local s
    s="$(_ch_trim "$1")"
    s="${s//$'\t'/ }"
    while [[ "$s" == *"  "* ]]; do s="${s//  / }"; done
    printf '%s' "${s// /_}"
}

_ch_value () {
    # Sanitise a data cell VALUE: trim edges and map tabs to underscores, but
    # PRESERVE spaces (the engine keeps everything after the first space intact).
    local s
    s="$(_ch_trim "$1")"
    printf '%s' "${s//$'\t'/_}"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    # Distinctive signature: a top-border line and a bar-delimited data line.
    local has_border=0 has_bar=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "$_CH_TL"* ]] && has_border=1
        [[ "$line" == "$_CH_BAR"* ]] && has_bar=1
        [[ $has_border -eq 1 && $has_bar -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local -a cols=()
    local ncols=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Header: top border line carries the column names.
        if [[ "$line" == "$_CH_TL"* ]]; then
            local hdr="$line"
            hdr="${hdr//$_CH_TL/}"
            hdr="${hdr//$_CH_TR/}"
            # Split on the top tee to isolate each column label.
            local IFS_save="$IFS"
            local rest="$hdr" seg
            cols=()
            while [[ "$rest" == *"$_CH_TD"* ]]; do
                seg="${rest%%$_CH_TD*}"
                rest="${rest#*$_CH_TD}"
                seg="${seg//$_CH_DASH/}"
                cols+=("$(_ch_sanitise "$seg")")
            done
            rest="${rest//$_CH_DASH/}"
            cols+=("$(_ch_sanitise "$rest")")
            IFS="$IFS_save"
            ncols=${#cols[@]}
            continue
        fi

        # Skip other border lines (mid/bottom).
        [[ "$line" == "$_CH_ML"* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "$_CH_BL"* ]] && continue

        # Data row: bar-delimited cells.
        if [[ "$line" == "$_CH_BAR"* ]]; then
            local row="${line//$_CH_BAR/|}"
            row="${row#|}"
            row="${row%|}"
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            local idx=0 cell field rest2="$row"
            while :; do
                cell="${rest2%%|*}"
                field="${cols[$idx]:-col$((idx + 1))}"
                [[ -z "$field" ]] && field="col$((idx + 1))"
                result+="entry${entry}.${field} $(_ch_value "$cell")"$'\n'
                idx=$((idx + 1))
                [[ "$rest2" == *"|"* ]] || break
                rest2="${rest2#*|}"
            done
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: mariadb-innodb-status
## Description: Extract stable InnoDB metrics from SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/mariadb-innodb-status/basic.txt

# `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS` prints sectioned free-form text with labelled
# numbers (`History list length 42`, `OS WAIT ARRAY INFO: reservation count N`,
# `Trx id counter N`, ...). Pull a set of stable labelled metrics into ONE wide
# record (`entry1.<metric> value`).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"INNODB MONITOR OUTPUT"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"TRANSACTIONS"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"History list length"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line fields=0

    _emit () { # $1=field  $2=value
        [[ -n "$2" ]] || return 0
        result+="entry1.$1 $2"$'\n'
        fields=$((fields + 1))
    }

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "$line" in
            "History list length "*)
                _emit history_list_length "${line##* }" ;;
            *"reservation count "*)
                _emit reservation_count "${line##* }" ;;
            *"signal count "*)
                _emit signal_count "${line##* }" ;;
            "Trx id counter "*)
                _emit trx_id_counter "${line##* }" ;;
        esac
        # `RW-shared spins A, rounds B, OS waits C`
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^RW-shared[[:space:]]spins[[:space:]][0-9]+,[[:space:]]rounds[[:space:]]([0-9]+) ]]; then
            _emit rw_shared_rounds "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        fi
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^RW-excl[[:space:]]spins[[:space:]][0-9]+,[[:space:]]rounds[[:space:]]([0-9]+) ]]; then
            _emit rw_excl_rounds "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $fields -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=64b0494613d7650bb33a2ef8207dd6f790d8685d28365fb2e15a99099c3936d7===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: alias-list
## Description: Shell `alias name='command'` listings Aje28094Aj name/command columns, quotes and the `alias ` keyword stripped
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/alias-list/basic.txt

# `alias ll='ls -alF'` is an assignment whose key carries a constant `alias `
# keyword and whose value is a (usually single-quoted) command. aligned-columns
# would shred the command on its internal spaces (`ls`/`-alF` in separate
# columns) and keep the redundant `alias` token as column A; equals would keep
# the `alias_` prefix glued to the name. Neither is what the value is: a name
# mapped to a command string. This owns the shape and emits exactly that.

# True only when EVERY non-empty line is `alias <name>=<value>` Aje28094Aj a listing, not
# prose that happens to contain the word "alias".
_al_is_alias_list () {
    local text="$1" line seen=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Leading whitespace tolerated (some shells indent), then `alias `.
        local s="$line"
        while [[ "$s" == " "* || "$s" == $'\t'* ]]; do s="${s#?}"; done
        [[ "$s" == "alias "* ]] || return 1
        local rest="${s#alias }"
        # Must be `name=value` with a non-empty name that looks like an
        # identifier (shell alias names: letters, digits, _, -, ., and the
        # handful of punctuation aliases like `..`).
        [[ "$rest" == *"="* ]] || return 1
        local name="${rest%%=*}"
        [[ -n "$name" ]] || return 1
        [[ "$name" == *" "* ]] && return 1   # a space in the name = not an alias def
        seen=$((seen + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $seen -ge 1 ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _al_is_alias_list "$text" || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    return 0
}

# Strip one layer of matching outer quotes from $1 -> _AL_UNQUOTE
_al_unquote () {
    local v="$1"
    if [[ ${#v} -ge 2 ]]; then
        local a="${v:0:1}" b="${v: -1}"
        if [[ ( "$a" == "'" && "$b" == "'" ) || ( "$a" == '"' && "$b" == '"' ) ]]; then
            v="${v:1:${#v}-2}"
        fi
    fi
    _AL_UNQUOTE="$v"
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local s="$line"
        while [[ "$s" == " "* || "$s" == $'\t'* ]]; do s="${s#?}"; done
        [[ "$s" == "alias "* ]] || continue
        local rest="${s#alias }"
        [[ "$rest" == *"="* ]] || continue
        local name="${rest%%=*}" cmd="${rest#*=}"
        [[ -n "$name" ]] || continue
        _al_unquote "$cmd"; cmd="$_AL_UNQUOTE"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$cmd" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.command ${cmd}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/aligned-columns.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=7da724dbc9701d97a8a3ab615f087e34a45f7b0524a32aa5999ef47f88d2b130===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: aligned-columns
## Description: Extract fields from whitespace-aligned columnar output (ps, df, mount, etc.)
## Version: 3.1
## Priority: 55
## Sample: samples/aligned-columns/basic.txt

# Count a line's 2-space-gap segments Aje28094Aj the columns a fixed-width header defines
# (a multi-word cell like "Best Rate MB/s" is ONE segment; only a >=2-space gap
# starts a new one).
_ac_seg () {
    local l="$1" n=0 i=0 L
    l="${l#"${l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; L=${#l}
    while (( i < L )); do
        while (( i < L )) && [[ "${l:i:1}" == " " ]]; do ((i++)); done
        (( i >= L )) && break
        ((n++))
        while (( i < L )) && ! { [[ "${l:i:1}" == " " ]] && [[ "${l:i+1:1}" == " " ]]; }; do ((i++)); done
    done
    printf '%s' "$n"
}

# Is the token a value (number/size/%/time/version Aje28094Aj anything starting with a
# digit)? A header label never does.
_ac_is_value () { [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9] ]]; }

# Echo the block with leading preamble removed: an `ls -l` "total <n>" line, or
# short banner/preamble lines with <2 columns (e.g. `apt list`'s "ListingAje280a6Aj"),
# but only when a real (>=2 column) table follows.
_ac_body () {
    local text="$1" _l _tk out="" started=0 has_table=0

    # AUDIT-REPORT chrome (aureport family): `====` rule lines are never
    # data; a 1-2 token line DIRECTLY ABOVE a rule is the report title; a
    # single `# label label Aje280a6Aj` line among the first lines is the real
    # header wearing a comment marker Aje28094Aj strip the marker. Sequentially
    # numbered `N.` first tokens on every data row are row numbers (the
    # melt's `n` column already carries that) Aje28094Aj strip them.
    if [[ "$text" == *$'\n'====* ]]; then
        local _ar_lines=() _ar_i
        while IFS= read -r _l; do _ar_lines+=("$_l"); done <<< "$text"
        # drop rules + the title above the first rule
        local _ar_out=() _ar_hash=-1 _ar_hashes=0
        for ((_ar_i = 0; _ar_i < ${#_ar_lines[@]}; _ar_i++)); do
            _l="${_ar_lines[$_ar_i]}"
            if [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*={4,}[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
                # title directly above the FIRST rule (<=2 tokens, no colon)
                if [[ ${#_ar_out[@]} -ge 1 ]]; then
                    local _ar_last="${_ar_out[$(( ${#_ar_out[@]} - 1 ))]}"
                    local _ar_lt=(); read -ra _ar_lt <<< "$_ar_last"
                    [[ ${#_ar_lt[@]} -le 2 && ! "$_ar_last" == *:* && "$_ar_last" =~ ^[A-Z] ]] && unset '_ar_out[$(( ${#_ar_out[@]} - 1 ))]'
                    _ar_out=("${_ar_out[@]}")
                fi
                continue
            fi
            [[ "$_l" == "# "* ]] && { _ar_hashes=$((_ar_hashes + 1)); _ar_hash=${#_ar_out[@]}; }
            _ar_out+=("$_l")
        done
        # exactly one `# Aje280a6Aj` line within the first 3 kept lines Aje28692Aj header
        if [[ $_ar_hashes -eq 1 && $_ar_hash -ge 0 && $_ar_hash -le 2 ]]; then
            _ar_out[$_ar_hash]="${_ar_out[$_ar_hash]#\# }"
        fi
        # sequential `N.` first tokens on every line after the header
        local _ar_seq=1 _ar_want=1 _ar_started=0
        for ((_ar_i = _ar_hash >= 0 ? _ar_hash + 1 : 1; _ar_i < ${#_ar_out[@]}; _ar_i++)); do
            [[ -z "${_ar_out[$_ar_i]//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
            _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "${_ar_out[$_ar_i]}"
            [[ "${_tk[0]:-}" == "${_ar_want}." ]] || { _ar_seq=0; break; }
            _ar_want=$((_ar_want + 1)); _ar_started=1
        done
        if [[ $_ar_seq -eq 1 && $_ar_started -eq 1 && $_ar_want -ge 3 ]]; then
            for ((_ar_i = _ar_hash >= 0 ? _ar_hash + 1 : 1; _ar_i < ${#_ar_out[@]}; _ar_i++)); do
                [[ -z "${_ar_out[$_ar_i]//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
                local _ar_rest="${_ar_out[$_ar_i]#*.}"
                _ar_rest="${_ar_rest# }"
                _ar_out[$_ar_i]="$_ar_rest"
            done
        fi
        text="$(printf '%s\n' "${_ar_out[@]}")"
    fi

    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "$_l"
        [[ ${#_tk[@]} -ge 2 ]] && { has_table=1; break; }
    done <<< "$text"

    # The modal (most common) token count of the block Aje28094Aj used to spot leading
    # banner lines that are much wider than the table that follows (`w`'s
    # load-average line, numastat's title). Only lines wider by >=3 tokens are
    # banners; a leading line with FEWER tokens can be a group-header row
    # (vmstat) and must stay.
    local _modal=0
    if [[ $has_table -eq 1 ]]; then
        local _mc=() _mn=0
        while IFS= read -r _l; do
            [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
            _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "$_l"
            _mc+=("${#_tk[@]}"); _mn=$((_mn + 1)); [[ $_mn -ge 40 ]] && break
        done <<< "$text"
        local _a _b _k _best=0
        for _a in "${_mc[@]}"; do
            _k=0; for _b in "${_mc[@]}"; do [[ "$_b" -eq "$_a" ]] && _k=$((_k + 1)); done
            [[ $_k -gt $_best ]] && { _best=$_k; _modal=$_a; }
        done
        # A banner is only recognisable against a real consensus: most of the
        # block (>=65%) must share the modal count, or a wide first line is
        # just one more ragged row (samtools flagstat), not chrome.
        [[ $_best -lt 2 || $(( _best * 100 / _mn )) -lt 65 ]] && _modal=0
    fi

    # A section title Aje28094Aj the FIRST line, ending with `:`, set off by a blank
    # line before the table ("Current machine states:", `vagrant status`) Aje28094Aj
    # is chrome, not data. Identified by lookahead here, dropped in the loop.
    local _title="" _prev="" _seenfirst=0
    if [[ $has_table -eq 1 ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r _l; do
            if [[ $_seenfirst -eq 0 ]]; then
                [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
                _seenfirst=1; _prev="$_l"; continue
            fi
            [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" && "$_prev" =~ :[[:space:]]*$ ]] && _title="$_prev"
            break
        done <<< "$text"
    fi

    # A title banner in front of a FIXED-WIDTH table (STREAM's "STREAM version
    # 5.10", blender's "Blender 4.2.0 Benchmark", kdiskmark's "KDiskMark 3.1.4")
    # Aje28094Aj a leading single-column line (seg<2) or decorated rule, followed by an
    # ALL-LABEL header over NUMERIC data. Both the all-label header and the
    # numeric data are required so this never eats a real header that happens to
    # be single-segment ("Installed Packages" over version rows Aje28094Aj dnf-list) or a
