                                at|on|from|via|dev|to|of|by|for) _sc_isword=1 ;;
                            esac
                            if [[ $_sc_isword -eq 1 ]]; then
                                [[ -n "$_sc_name" && -n "$_sc_val" ]] && _sc_res+="entry${_sc_e}.${_sc_name} ${_sc_val}"$'\n'
                                _sc_name="${_sc_tk[$_sc_i]}"; _sc_val=""
                            else
                                _sc_val+="${_sc_val:+ }${_sc_tk[$_sc_i]}"
                            fi
                        done
                        [[ -n "$_sc_name" && -n "$_sc_val" ]] && _sc_res+="entry${_sc_e}.${_sc_name} ${_sc_val}"$'\n'
                    done
                    if [[ $_sc_e -gt 0 ]]; then
                        _sc_res+="total_entries ${_sc_e}"$'\n'
                        echo "$_sc_res"; return 0
                    fi
                fi
            fi
        fi
    fi

    # HEADERLESS PHRASE MERGE: with no header to say otherwise, the TRAILING
    # pair of columns holding the SAME two lowercase words on every row
    # ("not confined" split into C/D Aje28094Aj aa-unconfined) is one status phrase,
    # not two columns. Trailing-only: a constant mid-table word pair is a
    # real pair of columns that happens to be constant (`ls -l`'s owner and
    # group, masscan's "open port"), so only the LAST pair may merge. Both
    # cells pure lowercase alpha, identical down the whole table, every row
    # full-width.
    local _pm_join=()
    if [[ "$mode" == HL && ${#headers[@]} -ge 3 && ${#lines[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
        local _pm_c _pm_l _pm_vals _pm_first _pm_ok
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#headers[@]}; i++)); do _pm_join[$i]=0; done
        _pm_c=$(( ${#headers[@]} - 1 ))
        _pm_ok=1; _pm_first=""
        for ((_pm_l = startidx; _pm_l < ${#lines[@]}; _pm_l++)); do
            _pm_vals=(); read -ra _pm_vals <<< "${lines[$_pm_l]}"
            [[ ${#_pm_vals[@]} -eq ${#headers[@]} ]] || { _pm_ok=0; break; }
            local _pm_pair="${_pm_vals[$((_pm_c - 1))]} ${_pm_vals[$_pm_c]}"
            [[ "${_pm_vals[$((_pm_c - 1))]}" =~ ^[a-z]+$ && "${_pm_vals[$_pm_c]}" =~ ^[a-z]+$ ]] || { _pm_ok=0; break; }
            [[ -z "$_pm_first" ]] && _pm_first="$_pm_pair"
            [[ "$_pm_pair" != "$_pm_first" ]] && { _pm_ok=0; break; }
        done
        [[ $_pm_ok -eq 1 ]] && _pm_join[$_pm_c]=1
    fi

    # Emit each data line as an indexed group (entry<N>.<field>) so the tidy melt
    # renders one row per line with shared columns.
    local result="" entry=0 li
    for ((li = startidx; li < ${#lines[@]}; li++)); do
        local values; values=(); read -ra values <<< "${lines[$li]}"
        # Apply the phrase merges (right-to-left so indices stay valid).
        if [[ ${#_pm_join[@]} -gt 0 && ${#values[@]} -eq ${#headers[@]} ]]; then
            for ((i = ${#headers[@]} - 1; i >= 1; i--)); do
                [[ "${_pm_join[$i]:-0}" -eq 1 ]] || continue
                values[$((i - 1))]="${values[$((i - 1))]} ${values[$i]}"
                values=("${values[@]:0:$i}" "${values[@]:$((i + 1))}")
            done
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local _ncols=${#headers[@]}
        if [[ ${#_pm_join[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
            _ncols=0
            for ((i = 0; i < ${#headers[@]}; i++)); do
                [[ "${_pm_join[$i]:-0}" -eq 1 ]] || _ncols=$((_ncols + 1))
            done
        fi
        for ((i = 0; i < _ncols; i++)); do
            local name; name="$(_col_letter $((i + 1)))"
            [[ ${#_pm_join[@]} -eq 0 || $_ncols -eq ${#headers[@]} ]] && name="${headers[$i]}"
            local value="${values[$i]:-}"
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
            # Last column absorbs any extra trailing tokens.
            if [[ $i -eq $((_ncols - 1)) && ${#values[@]} -gt $_ncols ]]; then
                local j
                for ((j = i + 1; j < ${#values[@]}; j++)); do value+="_${values[$j]}"; done
            fi
            result+="entry${entry}.${name} ${value}"$'\n'
        done
    done

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: asciigraph
## Description: Line charts (asciigraph) Aje28094Aj recover the axis labels + series values from the plot's footer, dropping the graphics
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 46
## Sample: samples/asciigraph/basic.txt

# asciigraph renders a braille/box-drawing line chart with a numeric footer:
#
#    120 Aje294a4Aj                     Aje295ade29480e29480Aj
#    ...
#     20 Aje294a4Aj
#        00:00   04:00   08:00   12:00   16:00   20:00
#   req/s  18      44      61      85     102     118
#
# The plot body is graphics; the DATA is the bottom pair Aje28094Aj an x-axis label row
# and a `<series> v v v Aje280a6Aj` value row. This drops the graphics and emits one row
# per point: the axis label and the series value. (reviewer: "extract the
# values, not the graphics".)

# A series footer line: a leading label token then >=3 numeric tokens. Sets
# _AG_LABEL and the _AG_VALS array.
_ag_series () {
    local line="$1"
    local -a t=(); read -ra t <<< "$line"
    [[ ${#t[@]} -ge 4 ]] || return 1
    local i nums=0
    for ((i = 1; i < ${#t[@]}; i++)); do
        [[ "${t[$i]}" =~ ^-?[0-9][0-9.]*$ ]] || return 1
        nums=$((nums + 1))
    done
    # the label token must NOT be numeric (it names the series)
    [[ "${t[0]}" =~ ^-?[0-9] ]] && return 1
    _AG_LABEL="${t[0]}"; _AG_VALS=("${t[@]:1}"); _AG_NUM=$nums
    return 0
}

# y-axis tick glyph asciigraph draws: `Aje294a4Aj` (U+2524) / `Aje294bcAj` (U+253C). Their UTF-8
# lead bytes mark a plot line.
_ag_is_plot () {
    local l="$1"
    [[ "$l" == *$'\342\224\244'* || "$l" == *$'\342\224\274'* ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line plot=0 series=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        _ag_is_plot "$line" && plot=$((plot + 1))
        _ag_series "$line" && series=1
    done <<< "$text"
    # >=2 plot lines AND a numeric series footer Aje28094Aj the asciigraph signature.
    [[ $plot -ge 2 && $series -eq 1 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local -a lines=(); local line
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do lines+=("$line"); done <<< "$text"

    # Find the LAST series line; the nearest non-blank, non-plot line above it is
    # the x-axis label row.
    local n=${#lines[@]} i sidx=-1
    for ((i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--)); do
        if _ag_series "${lines[$i]}"; then sidx=$i; break; fi
    done
    [[ $sidx -lt 0 ]] && { echo ""; return 0; }
    _ag_series "${lines[$sidx]}"
    local label="$_AG_LABEL"; local -a vals=("${_AG_VALS[@]}")

    local aidx=-1
    for ((i = sidx - 1; i >= 0; i--)); do
        [[ -z "${lines[$i]//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _ag_is_plot "${lines[$i]}" && break
        aidx=$i; break
    done
    local -a axis=()
    [[ $aidx -ge 0 ]] && read -ra axis <<< "${lines[$aidx]}"

    local result="" entry=0 k
    for ((k = 0; k < ${#vals[@]}; k++)); do
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        [[ $k -lt ${#axis[@]} ]] && result+="entry${entry}.x ${axis[$k]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.${label} ${vals[$k]}"$'\n'
    done
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/delimited/block-records.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=d161f586b9e7911641db73c73ceccdd414248a1c12e625b2e518b16e76015d83===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: block-records
## Description: Split input on blank lines into records, extract key:value and key=value fields
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 40
## Sample: samples/blank-line-records/basic.txt

# Merges blank-line-records and repeated-blocks. Detects either:
#   (a) 2+ blank lines separating blocks with key:value/key=value patterns, or
#   (b) 1+ blank line where the same field name appears in multiple blocks.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=60

    # Reject JSON-like input
    _is_json "$1" && return 1

    # Must have at least one blank line separating blocks
    local blank_count=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && blank_count=$((blank_count + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $blank_count -lt 1 ]] && return 1

    # Must have key: value or key=value patterns
    [[ "$text" =~ (^|$'\n')\ *[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_\ -]*[:=] ]] || return 1

    # Condition (a): 2+ blank lines is sufficient
    if [[ $blank_count -ge 2 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Condition (b): same field name appears in 2+ blocks (repeated-blocks criterion)
    local _unique_names="" _total=0 _unique=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        if [[ "$_line" =~ ^[\ ]*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_\ -]*): ]]; then
            local _name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            while [[ "$_name" == " "* ]]; do _name="${_name# }"; done
            while [[ "$_name" == *" " ]]; do _name="${_name% }"; done
            _total=$((_total + 1))
            case "|${_unique_names}|" in
                *"|${_name}|"*) ;;
                *) _unique=$((_unique + 1)); _unique_names="${_unique_names}|${_name}" ;;
            esac
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $_total -gt $_unique && $_unique -ge 1 ]] && return 0

    # Also check for equals-delimited fields (key=value) from repeated-blocks patterns
    _unique_names="" _total=0 _unique=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        if [[ "$_line" =~ ^[\ ]*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_\ -]*)= ]]; then
            local _name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            while [[ "$_name" == " "* ]]; do _name="${_name# }"; done
            while [[ "$_name" == *" " ]]; do _name="${_name% }"; done
            _total=$((_total + 1))
            case "|${_unique_names}|" in
                *"|${_name}|"*) ;;
                *) _unique=$((_unique + 1)); _unique_names="${_unique_names}|${_name}" ;;
            esac
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $_total -gt $_unique && $_unique -ge 1 ]] && return 0

    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local record_num=0

    _tech_split_blocks "$text"

    local _remaining="$_TECH_BLOCKS"
    while [[ -n "$_remaining" ]]; do
        local _block="${_remaining%%$'\x01'*}"
        [[ "$_remaining" == *$'\x01'* ]] && _remaining="${_remaining#*$'\x01'}" || _remaining=""
        [[ -z "$_block" ]] && continue
        record_num=$((record_num + 1))
        local _prefix="record${record_num}"
        result+="$(_tech_kv_colon "$_block" "$_prefix")"$'\n'
        result+="$(_tech_kv_equals "$_block" "$_prefix")"$'\n'
    done

    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=f976b92bdb97ab2bfb89e4542fe9e7ded12955e2616f27b1065b5240266da131===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: box-table
## Description: Unicode box-drawing tables (Aje29482Aj cells, Aje29480e294bce295adAj borders) Aje28094Aj mysql/psql unicode, rich, tabulate, duckdb, gum, pdm, glow, many modern CLIs
## Version: 2.0
## Priority: 34
## Sample: samples/box-table/basic.txt

# Modern Rust/Python CLIs render tables with Unicode box-drawing:
#
#   Aje295ade29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e294ace29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e295aeAj   Aje2948fe29481e29481e29481e29481e294b3e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29493Aj   Aje29594e29590e29590e29590e29590e295a6e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29597Aj    id Aje29482Aj name    Aje29482Aj v
#   Aje29482Aj name     Aje29482Aj version Aje29482Aj   Aje29483Aj id Aje29483Aj name  Aje29483Aj   Aje29591Aj id Aje29591Aj name  Aje29591Aj   Aje29480e29480e29480e29480e294bce29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e294bce29480e29480e29480Aj
#   Aje2949ce29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e294bce29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e294a4Aj   Aje294a3e29481e29481e29481e29481e2958be29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e294abAj   Aje295a0e29590e29590e29590e29590e295ace29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e295a3Aj     1 Aje29482Aj django  Aje29482Aj 5
#   Aje29482Aj django   Aje29482Aj 5.0.6   Aje29482Aj   Aje29483Aj  1 Aje29483Aj djangoAje29483Aj   Aje29591Aj  1 Aje29591Aj djangoAje29591Aj     2 Aje29482Aj flask   Aje29482Aj 3
#   Aje295b0e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e294b4e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e29480e295afAj   Aje29497e29481e29481e29481e29481e294bbe29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e29481e2949bAj   Aje2959ae29590e29590e29590e29590e295a9e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e29590e2959dAj
#
# Same shape as psql-table's ASCII box, just different glyphs. The cell divider
# is one of the vertical box glyphs (Aje29482Aj Aje29483Aj Aje29591Aj Aje29486Aj Aje280a6Aj); border/rule rows are runs of a
# horizontal glyph (Aje29480Aj Aje29481Aj Aje29590Aj) with corner/joint glyphs, and some tools frame an
# ASCII `--- ` dash rule inside the box (csvlook). Rows may or may not carry an
# outer border (psql `linestyle unicode` has interior `Aje29482Aj` only). We normalise the
# verticals to `|`, drop the rules, and emit one record per data row. Sources:
# mysql/psql unicode, duckdb, rich/textual, python `tabulate`
# (fancy_grid/rounded/double/presto), polars, csvlook, gum, glow, pdm. ASCII
# `+`/`-`/`|` tables stay with psql-table; this fires only when a box rule and a
# box-cell row coexist.

# Normalise every vertical cell divider (light/heavy/double/dotted) to ASCII '|'.
_box_norm () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//Aje29482Aj/|}"; v="${v//Aje29483Aj/|}"; v="${v//Aje29591Aj/|}"
    v="${v//Aje29486Aj/|}"; v="${v//Aje29487Aj/|}"; v="${v//Aje2948aAj/|}"; v="${v//Aje2948bAj/|}"; v="${v//Aje2958eAj/|}"; v="${v//Aje2958fAj/|}"
    _BOX_NORM="$v"
}

_box_trim () { local v="$1"; while [[ "$v" == " "* ]]; do v="${v# }"; done; while [[ "$v" == *" " ]]; do v="${v% }"; done; _BOX_TRIM="$v"; }

# Strip every box-drawing glyph (borders, corners, joints of all weights) plus
# spaces. A pure rule/border line reduces to empty.
_box_strip () {
    local s="$1"
    # verticals
    s="${s//Aje29482Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29483Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29591Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29486Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29487Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2948aAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2948bAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2958eAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2958fAj/}"
    # horizontals
    s="${s//Aje29480Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29481Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29590Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2958cAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2958dAj/}"; s="${s//Aje29484Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29485Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29488Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29489Aj/}"
    # light corners/joints
    s="${s//Aje2948cAj/}"; s="${s//Aje29490Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29494Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29498Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2949cAj/}"; s="${s//Aje294a4Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje294acAj/}"; s="${s//Aje294b4Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje294bcAj/}"
    # heavy corners/joints
    s="${s//Aje2948fAj/}"; s="${s//Aje29493Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29497Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2949bAj/}"; s="${s//Aje294a3Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje294abAj/}"; s="${s//Aje294b3Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje294bbAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2958bAj/}"
    # double corners/joints
    s="${s//Aje29594Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29597Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2959aAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2959dAj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a0Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a3Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a6Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a9Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295acAj/}"
    # rounded + tabulate mixed joints
    s="${s//Aje295adAj/}"; s="${s//Aje295aeAj/}"; s="${s//Aje295b0Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295afAj/}"
    s="${s//Aje29592Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29595Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29598Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2959bAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2959eAj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a1Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a4Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a7Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295aaAj/}"
    s="${s//Aje29593Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29596Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje29599Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje2959cAj/}"; s="${s//Aje2959fAj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a2Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a5Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295a8Aj/}"; s="${s//Aje295abAj/}"
    s="${s// /}"
    _BOX_STRIP="$s"
}

# Split a box row into _BOX_CELLS: normalise verticals to '|', drop any outer
# '|', split on the interior '|'s. Handles both bordered (Aje29482Aj a Aje29482Aj b Aje29482Aj) and
# interior-only (a Aje29482Aj b Aje29482Aj c) rows.
_box_split () {
    _box_norm "$1"; _box_trim "$_BOX_NORM"
    local row="$_BOX_TRIM"
    # Strip the outer dividers only when the row is BRACKETED (a '|' at both
    # ends). An interior-only row with an empty leading/trailing cell (psql
    # `linestyle unicode`: "Aje29482Aj value Aje280a6Aj" where the first column is blank) keeps
    # its edge '|' so the empty cell is not silently dropped.
    [[ "$row" == "|"* && "$row" == *"|" ]] && { row="${row#|}"; row="${row%|}"; }
    _BOX_CELLS=()
    local rest="$row" cell
    while [[ "$rest" == *"|"* ]]; do
        cell="${rest%%|*}"; rest="${rest#*|}"
        _box_trim "$cell"; _BOX_CELLS+=("$_BOX_TRIM")
    done
    _box_trim "$rest"; _BOX_CELLS+=("$_BOX_TRIM")
}

# A rule/border line: a pure box rule (only box glyphs + spaces, carrying a
# horizontal run), OR a framed ASCII dash rule (`Aje29482Aj --- Aje29482Aj --- Aje29482Aj`, csvlook).
_box_is_rule () {
    local l="$1"
    _box_strip "$l"
    if [[ -z "$_BOX_STRIP" ]]; then
        [[ "$l" == *Aje29480Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29481Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29590Aj* || "$l" == *Aje2958cAj* || "$l" == *Aje2958dAj* \
           || "$l" == *Aje29484Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29485Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29488Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29489Aj* ]]
        return
    fi
    # framed dash rule: has a vertical divider and every split cell is dash-only.
    [[ "$l" == *Aje29482Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29483Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29591Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29486Aj* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$l" == *-* ]] || return 1
    _box_split "$l"
    [[ ${#_BOX_CELLS[@]} -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    local _c
    for _c in "${_BOX_CELLS[@]}"; do
        [[ "$_c" == *-* ]] || return 1
        local s="${_c//-/}"; s="${s//:/}"; s="${s// /}"
        [[ -z "$s" ]] || return 1
    done
    return 0
}

# A data/header row: carries a vertical box divider and is not a pure rule.
_box_is_row () {
    local l="$1"
    [[ "$l" == *Aje29482Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29483Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29591Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29486Aj* || "$l" == *Aje29487Aj* \
       || "$l" == *Aje2948aAj* || "$l" == *Aje2948bAj* || "$l" == *Aje2958eAj* || "$l" == *Aje2958fAj* ]] || return 1
    _box_is_rule "$l" && return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="unicode box-drawing table (Aje29482Aj/Aje29483Aj/Aje29591Aj cells + Aje29480Aj/Aje29481Aj/Aje29590Aj borders)"
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local _line _saw_rule=0 _saw_cell=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "${_line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if _box_is_rule "$_line"; then _saw_rule=1
        elif _box_is_row "$_line"; then _saw_cell=1; fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $_saw_rule -eq 1 && $_saw_cell -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _line
    # modal cell count across box rows (rules excluded)
    local counts=()
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _box_is_row "$_line" || continue
        _box_split "$_line"; counts+=("${#_BOX_CELLS[@]}")
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ ${#counts[@]} -lt 2 ]] && return
    local modal=0 best=0 a b k
    for a in "${counts[@]}"; do
        k=0; for b in "${counts[@]}"; do [[ "$b" -eq "$a" ]] && k=$((k + 1)); done
        [[ $k -gt $best ]] && { best=$k; modal=$a; }
    done
    [[ $modal -lt 1 ]] && return

    local col_names=() num_cols=0 have_header=0 _c name i val
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _box_is_row "$_line" || continue
        _box_split "$_line"
        [[ ${#_BOX_CELLS[@]} -ne $modal ]] && continue
        if [[ $have_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            for _c in "${_BOX_CELLS[@]}"; do
                name="$_c"; name="${name//./}"; name="${name// /_}"
                while [[ "$name" == *__* ]]; do name="${name//__/_}"; done
                name="${name#_}"; name="${name%_}"
                [[ -z "$name" ]] && name="$(_col_letter $((${#col_names[@]} + 1)))"
                col_names+=("$name")
            done
            num_cols=${#col_names[@]}; have_header=1; continue
        fi
        # Skip a duckdb/clickhouse "type row" Aje28094Aj the line of column types printed
        # under the names, before the header/data separator rule (every cell is a
        # bare SQL type keyword). Only the row immediately after the header.
        if [[ $entry -eq 0 ]]; then
            local _allty=1 _tc
            for _tc in "${_BOX_CELLS[@]}"; do
                case "${_tc%%(*}" in
                    varchar|char|text|string|blob|bytea|uuid|json|jsonb|xml|bool|boolean|bit \
                    |int|integer|tinyint|smallint|bigint|hugeint|int2|int4|int8|serial \
                    |float|float4|float8|double|real|decimal|numeric|number \
                    |date|time|timestamp|timestamptz|datetime|interval|enum|array|map|struct) : ;;
                    *) _allty=0; break ;;
                esac
            done
            [[ $_allty -eq 1 ]] && continue
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i = 0; i < num_cols; i++)); do
            val="${_BOX_CELLS[$i]}"; _box_trim "$val"; val="$_BOX_TRIM"
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${col_names[$i]} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/bracket-log.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=39559713d73a23e5e1b8fc317275f47b98053691da341b1ae11cd6f8838995a6===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: bracket-log
## Description: Log lines prefixed with a [bracketed] timestamp/tag (dmesg, kernel ring buffer, many app logs)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 48
## Sample: samples/bracket-log/dmesg.txt

# Matches lines shaped like `[<tag>] <message>` Aje28094Aj dmesg / kernel ring buffer
# (`[    0.000000] Linux version Aje280a6Aj`), and app logs that lead with a bracketed
# timestamp or level. Tidied to one row per line: (timestamp, message).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    local nonblank=0 bracketed=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        # leading (optional ws) '[', some content, ']', then a space + message
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*\[[^]]+\][[:space:]]+[^[:space:]] ]] && bracketed=$((bracketed + 1))
        [[ $nonblank -ge 40 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $nonblank -lt 2 ]] && return 1
    # Strong majority of lines must be bracket-prefixed.
    [[ $(( bracketed * 100 / nonblank )) -lt 80 ]] && return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*\[[^]]+\][[:space:]]+[^[:space:]] ]] || continue

        # timestamp/tag = text between the first '[' and ']'
        local ts="${_l#*[}"; ts="${ts%%]*}"
        # message = everything after the first ']'
        local msg="${_l#*]}"
        # trim surrounding whitespace
        ts="${ts#"${ts%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; ts="${ts%"${ts##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        msg="${msg#"${msg%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; msg="${msg%"${msg##*[![:space:]]}"}"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.timestamp ${ts}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$msg" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.message ${msg}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/colon-fields.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=f87d912db6abe7c7f6df48538b0cd31723074d0ee0363e5160abae8549ad4f09===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: colon-fields
## Description: Colon-delimited records (/etc/passwd, /etc/group, getent, fstab-ish) Aje28692Aj one row per line
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 48
## Sample: samples/colon-fields/basic.txt

# Classic colon-delimited tables: `root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash`. Distinct from
# the `colons` key:value parser (single ` : ` per line) Aje28094Aj here the colon is a field
# DELIMITER packed several-per-token. The discriminator: the first whitespace token
# carries >=3 colons (>=4 packed fields), which a stray timestamp like `10:15:42`
# (2 colons) never does, so mpstat/sar-style tables are not misread as colon records.

_cf_first_colons () {
    # Colons in the first whitespace-delimited token of "$1" -> _CF_N.
    local tok="${1#"${1%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # ltrim
    tok="${tok%%[[:space:]]*}"               # first token
    local nc="${tok//[^:]/}"
    _CF_N=${#nc}
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *'{'* || "$text" == *'":'* ]] && return 1

    local nb=0 ok=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        _cf_first_colons "$_l"
        [[ $_CF_N -ge 3 ]] && ok=$((ok + 1))
        [[ $nb -ge 60 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $nb -ge 1 && $(( ok * 100 / nb )) -ge 60 ]] || return 1

    # Decline a uniform identifier list: every line sharing the SAME first
    # colon-field is a scheme prefix on one opaque identifier (ARNs "arn:aws:Aje280a6Aj",
    # URIs), not per-record colon fields (passwd/group, whose first field is the
    # varying record key). Splitting an ARN into arn|aws|service|Aje280a6Aj is wrong Aje28094Aj it
    # is a single value Aje28094Aj so let a one-column list parser take it instead.
    local _f1="" _same=1 _seen=0 _l2
    while IFS= read -r _l2; do
        [[ -z "${_l2//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local _pre="${_l2%%:*}"
        if [[ $_seen -eq 0 ]]; then _f1="$_pre"; _seen=1
        elif [[ "$_pre" != "$_f1" ]]; then _same=0; break; fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $_seen -eq 1 && $_same -eq 1 && $nb -ge 2 ]] && return 1

    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local rest="$_l" i=0 field
        while [[ "$rest" == *:* ]]; do
            field="${rest%%:*}"
            rest="${rest#*:}"
            i=$((i + 1))
            result+="entry${entry}.$(_col_letter "$i") ${field}"$'\n'
        done
        i=$((i + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.$(_col_letter "$i") ${rest}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/colon-pairs.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=56ff915a0aa330fd7ba5e64f03c52767373606b7624f8576318df5767bfad705===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: colon-pairs
## Description: Inline "Label: value  Label: value" status lines (mysqladmin status, memcached/redis one-liners)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 11
## Sample: samples/colon-pairs/basic.txt

# The one-line status format: several "Label: value" pairs run together on a
# single line, labels possibly multi-word:
#
#   Uptime: 58234  Threads: 3  Slow queries: 2  Queries per second avg: 2.223
#
# One record per line. Split on ": " boundaries; a value is the first
# whitespace token after the colon, and any remaining words before the next
# colon belong to the NEXT label ("2  Opens" -> value 2, next label Opens).

_cp_pairs_on_line () {
    # Count ": " pairs that look like "word: token"
    local l="$1" n=0
    while [[ "$l" == *": "* ]]; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        l="${l#*: }"
    done
    printf '%s' "$n"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local line lines=0 good=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        lines=$((lines + 1))
        [[ $lines -gt 4 ]] && return 1        # a STATUS one-liner block, not a document
        # Need >=4 inline pairs on the line, and the line must not START with
        # indentation (yaml/colons documents) nor contain " = " (kv blocks).
        [[ "$line" == [[:space:]]* || "$line" == *" = "* ]] && return 1
        [[ "$(_cp_pairs_on_line "$line")" -ge 4 ]] && good=$((good + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $good -ge 1 && $good -eq $lines ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line entry=0 fields=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" != *": "* ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        # Walk "label: value rest..." Aje28094Aj value is the first token after the
        # colon; leftover words accumulate into the next label.
        local rest="$line" label value seg
        label="${rest%%: *}"
        rest="${rest#*: }"
        while :; do
            if [[ "$rest" == *": "* ]]; then
                seg="${rest%%: *}"           # "<value> <next label words>"
                rest="${rest#*: }"
                value="${seg%%[[:space:]]*}"
                local next="${seg#"$value"}"
                next="${next#"${next%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
                result+="entry${entry}.${label// /_} ${value}"$'\n'
                fields=$((fields + 1))
                label="$next"
            else
                result+="entry${entry}.${label// /_} ${rest}"$'\n'
                fields=$((fields + 1))
                break
            fi
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $fields -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/colons.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=112479909d1e36c9517a44d6385afeae2d15ec723672d2a0a935db1de0a0064a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: colons
## Description: Extract field:value pairs from colon-delimited data
## Version: 1.1
## Priority: 60
## Sample: samples/colons/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=35
    # NOTE: no repeated-top-key guard here. `colons` is the last-resort fallback
    # (priority 60) Aje28094Aj a dedicated record strategy (e.g. block-records, p40) always
    # outranks it for real multi-record input, so the guard is unnecessary. It
    # also must keep accepting repeated-key input so `--aggregate` can compute
    # count/min/max/sum/avg over repeated numeric fields.
    # Apply if input contains lines with colons (but not just URLs or timestamps)
    # Use variable for regex: (^|newline) to match any line start
    local _nl=$'\n'
    # A real `key: value` line: optional indent, a label, a colon, then whitespace
    # or end of line. Requiring whitespace after the colon avoids matching colons
    # inside timestamps/values (e.g. `date`'s `10:15:42`) as a key.
    local _re="(^|${_nl})[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_ -]*:([[:space:]]|${_nl}|$)"
    # Bracketed keys Aje28094Aj Android getprop's `[ro.product.model]: [Pixel 8]`.
    local _bre="(^|${_nl})\[[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\]:([[:space:]]|${_nl}|$)"
    [[ "$text" =~ $_re || "$text" =~ $_bre ]] || return 1

    # Require key:value lines to be a real fraction of the content, not a lone
    # stray colon in otherwise free text (e.g. a single `usage:` line inside
    # `strings` output). Below ~40% this isn't colon-delimited data Aje28094Aj let the
    # last-resort line-records catch it as a one-column list instead.
    #
    # `#` comment banners are excluded from BOTH sides of that ratio: they are
    # not data, strategy_extract already drops them (no colon, or an empty
    # value), and counting them in the denominator buries the real pairs. `perf
    # bench sched` prints three banner lines over a single `Total time:` pair Aje28094Aj
    # 25% with the banners, 100% without, and only the pair is data.
    local _kv=0 _nb=0 _l
    local _line_re="^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_ -]*:([[:space:]]|$)"
    local _bline_re="^[[:space:]]*\[[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\]:([[:space:]]|$)"
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "${_l#"${_l%%[![:space:]]*}"}" == "#"* ]] && continue
        _nb=$((_nb + 1))
        [[ "$_l" =~ $_line_re || "$_l" =~ $_bline_re ]] && _kv=$((_kv + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $_nb -gt 0 && $(( _kv * 100 / _nb )) -ge 40 ]]
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Clean text (dates, parentheses) -- cached by engine after first call
    clean_text "$text"; text="$_CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT"

    # Collapse spaces around colons and extract "key: value" lines
    # Skip lines where the "key" portion is too long (>50 chars) or empty
    local result=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Skip empty lines
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Must contain a colon
        [[ "$line" != *":"* ]] && continue

        # Extract key (everything before first colon) and value (everything after)
        local key value

        # Strip leading "* " bullet markers and spaces
        local _stripped="$line"
        if [[ "$_stripped" == "* "* ]]; then
            _stripped="${_stripped#\* }"
        fi
        while [[ "$_stripped" == " "* ]]; do _stripped="${_stripped# }"; done

        key="${_stripped%%:*}"
        value="${_stripped#*: }"
        # If no space after colon, strip just the colon
        if [[ "$value" == "$_stripped" ]]; then
            value="${_stripped#*:}"
        fi

        # Bracketed kv (`[ro.product.model]: [Pixel 8]`): the brackets are
        # chrome Aje28094Aj unwrap both sides, keeping the whole value (spaces intact).
        if [[ "$key" =~ ^\[([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)\]$ ]]; then
            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            while [[ "$value" == " "* ]]; do value="${value# }"; done
            while [[ "$value" == *" " ]]; do value="${value% }"; done
            [[ "$value" =~ ^\[(.*)\]$ ]] && value="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        fi

        # Skip if key is empty, too long, or looks like a non-field line
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        [[ ${#key} -gt 50 ]] && continue

        # Skip lines that look like URLs (value starts with //)
        [[ "$value" == //* ]] && continue

        # Skip lines where key starts with a digit
        [[ "$key" =~ ^[0-9] ]] && continue

        # Trim the key's surrounding whitespace (column-alignment padding, e.g.
        # `Battery #1     :`) BEFORE turning inner spaces into underscores, then
        # collapse any runs so the field name is clean (`Battery_#1`, not
        # `Battery_#1____`).
        key="${key#"${key%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        key="${key%"${key##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        key="${key// /_}"
        while [[ "$key" == *__* ]]; do key="${key//__/_}"; done
        key="${key#_}"
        key="${key%_}"

        # Trim edges of value; spaces inside the value are preserved (the engine
        # keeps everything after the first space as the value).
        while [[ "$value" == " "* ]]; do value="${value# }"; done
        while [[ "$value" == *" " ]]; do value="${value% }"; done

        # Skip if value is empty
        [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

        result+="${key} ${value}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/columnar-specs.sh===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: columnar-specs
## Description: Data-driven columnar parser Aje28094Aj one spec per tool (detect + column map) instead of a bespoke strategy each
## Version: 1.1
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/columnar-specs/basic.txt

# A single engine that replaces many near-identical per-tool columnar strategies.
# Full reference (spec format, transforms, how to add a tool / a transform):
#   docs/columnar-specs-engine.md   Aje28094Aj keep it current when you extend the engine.
# Each tool is one TAB-separated spec line instead of a ~50-line .sh file:
#
#   name <TAB> detect1;detect2;Aje280a6Aj <TAB> header_marker <TAB> delim <TAB> absorb <TAB> minreq <TAB> col,col,Aje280a6Aj
#
#   detect*       Aje28094Aj substrings that must ALL appear in the input for this spec
#   header_marker Aje28094Aj skip every line up to and INCLUDING the first line containing
#                   this (drops preamble + header/rule row); `-` = headerless.
#                   (Must not be empty Aje28094Aj `read` collapses consecutive TAB fields.)
#   delim         Aje28094Aj "ws" (whitespace tokens) or "pipe" (split on `|`, trim cells)
#   absorb        Aje28094Aj 0-based index of the column that soaks up overflow tokens when
#                   a row has more tokens than columns (ws only); -1 = none
#   minreq        Aje28094Aj minimum token count for a row to be accepted (lets trailing
#                   columns be optional, e.g. ss `Process`)
#   detect tokens may be plain substrings (must appear anywhere) or `re:PATTERN`
#     (at least one line must match the bash regex PATTERN) Aje28094Aj the latter gives the
#     precision a substring can't, e.g. mount's `<dev> on <mp> type <fs>` shape.
#   colN          Aje28094Aj output field name, optionally with a transform:
#                     name                 always emit
#                     ~name                structural separator token (e.g. mount
#                                          `on`/`type`): consume a token, emit nothing
#                     name@opt             emit only if the cell is non-empty
#                     name@unwrap          strip one layer of surrounding ()/[]/{}/""
#                                          e.g. mount `(rw,relatime)` Aje28692Aj `rw,relatime`
#                     name@between@L@R     emit the substring between the first L
#                                          and the next R (empty Aje28792Aj skip); e.g.
#                                          ss `users:(("sshd",Aje280a6Aj))` Aje28692Aj `sshd`
#
# On a match the engine REPORTS the matched tool name (via `_STRATEGY_REPORT_NAME`,
# set in `strategy_detect`), not "columnar-specs" Aje28094Aj so `glean` names the dataset
# per-tool (mount -> dataset `mount`, not `columnar-specs`) and different tools
# don't collide into one dataset. The tidy output (melted by tool) is identical to
# the retired bespokes Aje28094Aj verified byte-for-byte at migration time.

_COLUMNAR_SPECS=(
  $'zypper-search\t| Name ;| Summary ;| Type\t-+-\tpipe\t-1\t4\tstatus,name,summary,type'

  $'lsmem\tRANGE;REMOVABLE;BLOCK\tRANGE\tws\t-1\t5\trange,size,state,removable,block'
  $'ss-tulnp\tState;Local;Process\tRecv-Q\tws\t5\t5\tstate,recv_q,send_q,local,peer,process@between@users:(("@"\t0'
  $'smartctl-attributes\tATTRIBUTE_NAME;RAW_VALUE;WHEN_FAILED\tATTRIBUTE_NAME\tws\t-1\t10\tid,attribute_name,flag,value,worst,thresh,type,updated,when_failed,raw_value'
  $'mount\tre:^[^[:space:]]+ on .* type \t-\tws\t-1\t6\tdevice,~on,mount_point,~type,fstype,options@unwrap'
  $'iostat-d\ttps;kB_read/s\tDevice\tws\t-1\t6\tdevice,tps,kb_read_s,kb_wrtn_s,kb_read,kb_wrtn'
  $'rabbitmqctl-list-queues\tListing queues for vhost\tListing queues for vhost\tws\t-1\t3\tname,messages,consumers'

  $'gsutil-ls-l\tgs://\t-\tws\t-1\t3\tsize,timestamp,url\t1\tgs://'

  $'memcached-stats\tre:^STAT \t-\tws\t-1\t3\t~stat,key,value'

  $'turbostat\tBzy_MHz\t-\tws\t-1\t10\tCore,CPU,Avg_MHz,Busy_pct,Bzy_MHz,TSC_MHz,IRQ,PkgTmp,PkgWatt,RAMWatt\t1\t^[0-9]'
  $'traceroute\ttraceroute to\thops max\tws\t-1\t4\thop,host,~ip,rtt1@opt,~m1,rtt2@opt,~m2,rtt3@opt,~m3'
  $'git-remote\t(fetch);(push)\t-\tws\t-1\t3\tremote,url,direction@unwrap'
  $'w-sessions\tLOGIN@;JCPU;PCPU;WHAT\tTTY\tws\t-1\t8\tuser,tty,from,login,idle,jcpu,pcpu,what@rest'
  $'dpkg-list\tDesired=Unknown\t+++-\tws\t-1\t5\tstatus,name,version,arch,description@rest'
  $'tar-listing\tre:^[-dlbcps][-rwxsStT]{9} +[^ ]+/[^ ]+ +[0-9]+ +[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} \t-\tws\t-1\t6\tpermissions,owner,size,date,~time,path@rest'

# Split a spec string into the globals used by detect/extract. Field 7 (total) is
# optional: 1 (default) emits a `total_entries` record, 0 omits it Aje28094Aj some bespokes
# emit it, some don't, and migration must match byte-for-byte.
_cs_parse () {
    local IFS=$'\t'; local -a p=()
    read -ra p <<< "$1"
    _CS_NAME="${p[0]}"; _CS_DETECT="${p[1]}"; _CS_HDR="${p[2]}"
    _CS_DELIM="${p[3]}"; _CS_ABSORB="${p[4]}"; _CS_MINREQ="${p[5]}"; _CS_COLS="${p[6]}"
    _CS_TOTAL="${p[7]:-1}"
    # Field 9 (optional): a per-row ACCEPT regex. When set, a row is processed
    # only if its raw line matches Aje28094Aj the engine's per-row structural guard, for
    # outputs with footer/note lines that survive the minreq filter (e.g.
    # gsutil `TOTAL:`, grafana trailing note). Empty Aje28792Aj every row past the header.
    _CS_ROWRE="${p[8]:-}"
    # Field 10 (optional): record-name prefix (default "entry"). Some bespokes
    # label records `jobN`/`commitN`/Aje280a6Aj instead of `entryN`; match byte-for-byte.
    _CS_PREFIX="${p[9]:-entry}"
}

# A ws-delim spec with a FIXED column layout (no `absorb` overflow sink and no
# terminal `@rest` column) can only faithfully map a row whose token count is at
# most its column count Aje28094Aj any extra tokens are silently DROPPED, and worse, when
# the real table is WIDER than the spec, its first `ncols` tokens get mapped onto
# the wrong names (turbostat -q's 20-column output mis-labelled by the 10-column
# `turbostat` spec: SMI->PkgTmp, POLL->PkgWatt, Aje280a6Aj, 10 columns lost). Since no
# fixed-layout spec can legitimately rely on that drop (a genuinely multi-token
# trailing column would already need @rest/absorb), a spec whose data rows carry
# MORE tokens than it has columns is being misapplied Aje28094Aj decline so a generic
# parser (tsv / aligned-columns) can take the full width. Returns 0 (overflow Aje28692Aj
# decline) only for ws specs with no absorb and no @rest; every other spec shape
# returns 1 (no objection). Uses the already-parsed _CS_* globals.
_cs_row_overflow () {
    local text="$1"
    [[ "$_CS_DELIM" == "ws" ]] || return 1
    [[ "${_CS_ABSORB:--1}" -ge 0 ]] && return 1
    local -a cols=(); IFS=',' read -ra cols <<< "$_CS_COLS"
    local ncols=${#cols[@]} _ci
    [[ $ncols -le 1 ]] && return 1                 # @line / single-col: never overflows
    for ((_ci=0; _ci<ncols; _ci++)); do [[ "${cols[$_ci]}" == *"@rest" ]] && return 1; done
    local _l past=0 wide=0 seen=0
    [[ -z "$_CS_HDR" || "$_CS_HDR" == "-" ]] && past=1
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ $past -eq 0 ]]; then [[ "$_l" == *"$_CS_HDR"* ]] && past=1; continue; fi
        [[ -n "$_CS_ROWRE" && ! "$_l" =~ $_CS_ROWRE ]] && continue
        local -a _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "$_l"
        [[ ${#_tk[@]} -lt "${_CS_MINREQ:-$ncols}" ]] && continue
        seen=$((seen + 1))
        [[ ${#_tk[@]} -gt $ncols ]] && wide=$((wide + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    # Decline only when the OVERWHELMING majority of accepted rows are wider than
    # the layout Aje28094Aj a lone ragged row shouldn't lose the spec its normal input.
    [[ $seen -ge 2 && $((wide * 100 / seen)) -ge 80 ]]
}

# Does the text match this spec's detect tokens (all present)? A plain token is a
# substring anywhere; a `re:PATTERN` token requires >=1 line to match the regex.
_cs_matches () {
    local text="$1" det="$2" IFS=';' tok
    local -a toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$det"
    for tok in "${toks[@]}"; do
        [[ -z "$tok" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$tok" == re:* ]]; then
            local pat="${tok#re:}" _l hit=0
            while IFS= read -r _l; do [[ "$_l" =~ $pat ]] && { hit=1; break; }; done <<< "$text"
            [[ $hit -eq 1 ]] || return 1
        else
            [[ "$text" == *"$tok"* ]] || return 1
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local spec
    for spec in "${_COLUMNAR_SPECS[@]}"; do
        _cs_parse "$spec"
        if _cs_matches "$text" "$_CS_DETECT"; then
            # A fixed-layout spec that would silently drop columns on a wider
            # table declines here (see _cs_row_overflow) so a generic full-width
            # parser wins instead.
            _cs_row_overflow "$text" && continue
            _CS_MATCHED="$spec"
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            # Report the matched TOOL name (not the shared "columnar-specs") so
            # the engine names the dataset per-tool. Runs in the parent shell
            # (unlike strategy_extract, which is a command-substitution subshell).
            _STRATEGY_REPORT_NAME="$_CS_NAME"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

_cs_trim () { local s="$1"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; s="${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"; printf '%s' "$s"; }

# Apply a column's transform. Sets _CS_OUT to the (possibly transformed) value and
# _CS_SKIP=1 when an @opt/@between column should be dropped. Uses globals (not a
# command-substitution) so the caller sees _CS_SKIP Aje28094Aj a subshell would lose it.
_CS_OUT=""; _CS_SKIP=0
_cs_apply () {  # $1=raw value, $2=colspec (name@Aje280a6Aj)
    local raw="$1" spec="$2"; _CS_SKIP=0; _CS_OUT="$raw"
    [[ "$spec" != *"@"* ]] && return          # plain column: always emit raw
    local IFS='@'; local -a c=(); read -ra c <<< "$spec"
    local xform="${c[1]:-}"
    case "$xform" in
        opt) [[ -z "$raw" ]] && _CS_SKIP=1 ;;
        unwrap)
            case "$raw" in
                "("*")") _CS_OUT="${raw#(}"; _CS_OUT="${_CS_OUT%)}" ;;
                "["*"]") _CS_OUT="${raw#[}"; _CS_OUT="${_CS_OUT%]}" ;;
                "{"*"}") _CS_OUT="${raw#\{}"; _CS_OUT="${_CS_OUT%\}}" ;;
                '"'*'"') _CS_OUT="${raw#\"}"; _CS_OUT="${_CS_OUT%\"}" ;;
            esac ;;
        between)
            local L="${c[2]:-}" R="${c[3]:-}" out=""
            if [[ "$raw" == *"$L"* ]]; then local t="${raw#*"$L"}"; out="${t%%"$R"*}"; fi
            [[ -z "$out" ]] && _CS_SKIP=1
            _CS_OUT="$out" ;;
    esac
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local spec="${_CS_MATCHED:-}"
    if [[ -z "$spec" ]]; then
        local s
        for s in "${_COLUMNAR_SPECS[@]}"; do
            _cs_parse "$s"; _cs_matches "$text" "$_CS_DETECT" && { spec="$s"; break; }
        done
        [[ -z "$spec" ]] && { echo ""; return 0; }
    fi
    _cs_parse "$spec"
    local -a cols=(); IFS=',' read -ra cols <<< "$_CS_COLS"
    local ncols=${#cols[@]}
    local minreq="${_CS_MINREQ:-$ncols}"
    # index of the terminal @rest column (soaks remaining tokens, space-joined), or -1
    local rest_idx=-1 _ci
    for ((_ci=0; _ci<ncols; _ci++)); do [[ "${cols[$_ci]}" == *"@rest" ]] && rest_idx=$_ci; done
    # @line: a sole column capturing the whole TRIMMED line verbatim (no tokenizing).
    # For single-column list outputs (module lists, cfg dumps, cgroup trees).
    local line_mode=0
    [[ $ncols -eq 1 && "${cols[0]}" == *"@line" ]] && line_mode=1

    local result="" entry=0 line past=0 _cs_hdr_line=""
    [[ -z "$_CS_HDR" || "$_CS_HDR" == "-" ]] && past=1
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ $past -eq 0 ]]; then
            [[ "$line" == *"$_CS_HDR"* ]] && { past=1; _cs_hdr_line="$line"; }
            continue
        fi
        # A mid-stream repeat of the header line (watch/interval re-prints the
        # whole table every cycle) is chrome, not a data row.
        [[ -n "$_cs_hdr_line" && "$line" == "$_cs_hdr_line" ]] && continue
        # per-row accept guard (field 9): skip rows whose raw line doesn't match
        [[ -n "$_CS_ROWRE" && ! "$line" =~ $_CS_ROWRE ]] && continue
        # @line mode: emit the whole trimmed line as the sole column (no tokenizing)
        if [[ $line_mode -eq 1 ]]; then
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            result+="${_CS_PREFIX}${entry}.${cols[0]%%@*} $(_cs_trim "$line")"$'\n'
            continue
        fi
        local -a tok=()
        if [[ "$_CS_DELIM" == "pipe" ]]; then
            [[ "$line" == *"|"* ]] || continue
            local IFSbak="$IFS"; IFS='|'; read -ra tok <<< "$line"; IFS="$IFSbak"
            local i; for ((i=0; i<${#tok[@]}; i++)); do tok[$i]="$(_cs_trim "${tok[$i]}")"; done
        else
            read -ra tok <<< "$line"
        fi
        [[ ${#tok[@]} -lt $minreq ]] && continue

        # Assign tokens to columns.
        local -a vals=()
        if [[ "$_CS_DELIM" == "ws" && $rest_idx -ge 0 ]]; then
            # @rest column: takes every remaining token from its slot, joined with
            # single spaces (verbatim internal spacing, unlike absorb's `_`). It is
            # terminal Aje28094Aj no columns follow it.
            local i; for ((i=0; i<rest_idx; i++)); do vals+=("${tok[$i]:-}"); done
            local r="${tok[$rest_idx]:-}" k
            for ((k=rest_idx+1; k<${#tok[@]}; k++)); do r="$r ${tok[$k]}"; done
            vals+=("$r")
        elif [[ "$_CS_DELIM" == "ws" && "$_CS_ABSORB" -ge 0 && ${#tok[@]} -gt $ncols ]]; then
            local extra=$(( ${#tok[@]} - ncols )) i ti=0
            for ((i=0; i<ncols; i++)); do
                if [[ $i -eq $_CS_ABSORB ]]; then
                    local j v="${tok[$ti]}"; ti=$((ti+1))
                    for ((j=0; j<extra; j++)); do v="${v}_${tok[$ti]}"; ti=$((ti+1)); done
                    vals+=("$v")
                else
                    vals+=("${tok[$ti]:-}"); ti=$((ti+1))
                fi
            done
        else
            local i; for ((i=0; i<ncols; i++)); do vals+=("${tok[$i]:-}"); done
        fi

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local i fname
        for ((i=0; i<ncols; i++)); do
            # ~name = structural separator: it consumed a token slot (keeping later
            # columns aligned) but is never emitted.
            [[ "${cols[$i]}" == "~"* ]] && continue
            _cs_apply "${vals[$i]}" "${cols[$i]}"
            [[ "$_CS_SKIP" -eq 1 ]] && continue
            fname="${cols[$i]%%@*}"
            result+="${_CS_PREFIX}${entry}.${fname} ${_CS_OUT}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 && "${_CS_TOTAL:-1}" != "0" ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/count-percent-label.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=72f5b4c0a2533bc2dc0a0e0cb2a107fbec63008658bb9a3229c06282802b8f9a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: count-percent-label
## Description: `N (P%) description` alignment/mapping summaries (bowtie2, HISAT2, STAR) -> count/percent/label rows
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 42
## Sample: samples/count-percent-label/basic.txt

# Read-alignment tools report a nested tally where every line is a count, an
# optional share of its parent, and a description:
#
#   1000000 reads; of these:
#     1000000 (100.00%) were paired; of these:
#       45231 (4.52%) aligned concordantly 0 times
#       889012 (88.90%) aligned concordantly exactly 1 time
#   98.14% overall alignment rate
#
# A flat line list keeps all three facts welded into one cell, so neither the
# counts nor the percentages can be sorted or summed. The tidy shape splits them:
# `count`, `percent`, `label` Aje28094Aj the reviewer's "separate the numbers, percentages
# and text into three separate columns".
#
# Indentation encodes nesting, but it is presentation, not data: the label text
# already says what each row counts, so rows are emitted flat in file order.
#
# Three line forms are accepted, and EVERY non-blank line must be one of them:
#   `N (P%) text`   -> count, percent, label
#   `N text`        -> count, "",      label
#   `P% text`       -> "",    percent, label
# The parenthesised form is the signature: at least two lines must carry it, so
# ordinary counted lists (`uniq -c`, `wc -l` tables) are left to line-records.

_cpl_re_np='^[[:space:]]*([0-9][0-9,]*)[[:space:]]+\(([0-9]+\.?[0-9]*%)\)[[:space:]]+(.+)$'
_cpl_re_n='^[[:space:]]*([0-9][0-9,]*)[[:space:]]+([^0-9(].*)$'
_cpl_re_p='^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+\.?[0-9]*%)[[:space:]]+(.+)$'

# Classify "$1" -> _CPL_COUNT, _CPL_PCT, _CPL_LABEL, _CPL_PAREN (1 if `N (P%)`).
# Returns 1 when the line is none of the three forms.
_cpl_split () {
    local l="$1"
    _CPL_COUNT=""; _CPL_PCT=""; _CPL_LABEL=""; _CPL_PAREN=0
    if [[ "$l" =~ $_cpl_re_np ]]; then
        _CPL_COUNT="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        _CPL_PCT="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        _CPL_LABEL="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
        _CPL_PAREN=1
    elif [[ "$l" =~ $_cpl_re_p ]]; then
        _CPL_PCT="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        _CPL_LABEL="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    elif [[ "$l" =~ $_cpl_re_n ]]; then
        _CPL_COUNT="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        _CPL_LABEL="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    else
        return 1
    fi
    _CPL_LABEL="${_CPL_LABEL%"${_CPL_LABEL##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    [[ -n "$_CPL_LABEL" ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1

    local line nb=0 paren=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _cpl_split "$line" || return 1
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        [[ $_CPL_PAREN -eq 1 ]] && paren=$((paren + 1))
    done <<< "$text"

    # >=2 `N (P%)` lines is the discriminator; a plain counted list has none.
    [[ $nb -ge 3 && $paren -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local line result="" entry=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _cpl_split "$line" || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.count ${_CPL_COUNT:--}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.percent ${_CPL_PCT:--}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.label ${_CPL_LABEL}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/dashed-sections.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=1f20c1707d82699e3ac847b9a0716ed1aa88aa372e2eb46fa28afd9f8ac05191===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: dashed-sections
## Description: "--- Section ---" banners over aligned label/value lines Aje28094Aj one record per section
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/dashed-sections/basic.txt

# The LVM-display family shape (lvdisplay, vgdisplay, pvdisplay, and any
# report that groups aligned label/value pairs under dashed banners):
#
#   --- Logical volume ---
#   LV Path                /dev/vg0/lv_root
#   LV Name                lv_root
#   --- Segments ---
#   Logical extents 0 to 51198:
#
# One entry per banner; each body line splits on the FIRST run of 2+ spaces
# into label/value. The banner text itself is kept as entryN.section so
# records of different kinds stay distinguishable after the melt.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local line saw_banner=0 body=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        local t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        if [[ "$t" =~ ^---\ [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\ ]*\ ---$ ]]; then
            saw_banner=1
            continue
        fi
        # A body line after a banner: label, 2+ spaces, value.
        if [[ $saw_banner -eq 1 && "$t" == *"  "* && -n "${t%%  *}" ]]; then
            body=$((body + 1))
            if [[ $body -ge 2 ]]; then
                _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=82
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line entry=0 fields=0
    local key val t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        t="${t%"${t##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$t" =~ ^---\ ([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\ ]*)\ ---$ ]]; then
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            result+="entry${entry}.section ${key// /_}"$'\n'
            fields=$((fields + 1))
            continue
        fi
        [[ $entry -eq 0 ]] && continue
        # Split on the first 2+-space run; a line with no such run is a
        # label-only line (kept with an empty value, like `lvdisplay -m`'s
        # "LV Creation host, time server1, Aje280a6Aj" wrap).
        if [[ "$t" == *"  "* ]]; then
            key="${t%%  *}"
            val="${t#"$key"}"
            val="${val#"${val%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        else
            key="$t"
            val=""
        fi
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        key="${key// /_}"
        key="${key//$'\t'/_}"
        val="${val//$'\t'/_}"
        result+="entry${entry}.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
        fields=$((fields + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $fields -gt 0 && $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/diffstat.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=8e2fb531f6c42d4585c164e098e6ed8fc96d3f6ce4c8bc070f976ddd2e3bf4f4===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: diffstat
## Description: diffstat blocks (path | N +++--- per file, files-changed summary) Aje28094Aj git diff/stash/show --stat
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/diffstat/basic.txt

# The diffstat format every git --stat variant (and diffstat(1)) prints:
#
#    src/app.py | 12 ++++++------
#    README.md  |  4 ++++
#    4 files changed, 40 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
#
# One record per file line; the summary line becomes scalar fields the melt
# repeats onto every row. A log that carries commit headers (git log --stat)
# belongs to git-log-stat, not here Aje28094Aj inputs with `commit <sha>` lines are
# declined.

_diffstat_file_line () {
    # " path | 12 ++++----"  /  " img.png | Bin 0 -> 4096 bytes"
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([^|[:space:]][^|]*[^|[:space:]])[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*([0-9]+|Bin[^|]*)([[:space:]]+[+-]+)?[[:space:]]*$ ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local line hits=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^commit[[:space:]][0-9a-f]{7,} ]] && return 1
        _diffstat_file_line "$line" && hits=$((hits + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $hits -ge 2 && "$text" == *" changed"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line entry=0 summary=""
    local file changes graph
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _diffstat_file_line "$line"; then
            file="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            changes="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            graph="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
            graph="${graph#"${graph%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            result+="entry${entry}.file ${file}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.changes ${changes// /_}"$'\n'
            [[ -n "$graph" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.graph ${graph}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi
        # " 4 files changed, 40 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)"
        if [[ "$line" =~ ([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+files?\ changed ]]; then
            summary+="files_changed ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
            [[ "$line" =~ ([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+insertions?\(\+\) ]] && summary+="insertions ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
            [[ "$line" =~ ([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+deletions?\(-\) ]] && summary+="deletions ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="${summary}total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/delimited/dot-leader-kv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=b36c282dc74f83227e58702d3195beb789e5876e4d028b2f01feb9a7bcf7488a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: dot-leader-kv
## Description: `label: ......... value` / `label ........: value` reports where dot leaders separate key from value
## Version: 1.1
## Priority: 15
## Sample: samples/dot-leader-kv/basic.txt
## Sample: samples/dot-leader-kv/leader-before-colon.txt

# Reports like artillery / some benchmark summaries align a value to the right
# with a run of dot leaders: `http.codes.200: ............ 120488`. The dots are
# a delimiter, not data. block-records / colons mangle these (the leaders end up
# glued to the value, or the row is split on the dots). This owns the shape:
# key before the colon, value after the dot run, one row per metric.
#
# The leaders sit on either side of the colon depending on the tool. gpg --card-status
# and hashcat --status pad the *key* out to a fixed width instead, putting the dots
# before the colon: `Reader ...........: Yubico`. Same shape, same delimiter, so both
# orderings are handled here. In a block of that second kind the padding is only
# sometimes dots -- `Signature counter : 42` lines up with spaces -- so once the
# block is recognised, colon-separated lines without leaders are taken too, rather
# than dropping those rows.

# A dot-leader line, in either ordering:
#   A  `label: ....... value`   -- colon first, leaders before the value
#   B  `label .......: value`   -- leaders pad the key, colon last
# Sets _DL_KEY / _DL_VAL on success, and _DL_FORM to A or B.
_dl_match () {
    local line="$1"
    local _re_a='^[[:space:]]*([^:]+):[[:space:]]*\.\.\.+[[:space:]]*(.+)$'
    local _re_b='^[[:space:]]*([^:]*[^.:[:space:]])[[:space:]]*\.+[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(.+)$'
    if [[ "$line" =~ $_re_a ]]; then
        _DL_FORM=A
    elif [[ "$line" =~ $_re_b ]]; then
        _DL_FORM=B
    else
        return 1
    fi
    _DL_KEY="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    _DL_VAL="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    # Trim trailing whitespace from the value.
    while [[ "$_DL_VAL" == *" " ]]; do _DL_VAL="${_DL_VAL% }"; done
    # A value that is itself only dots is not a value.
    [[ "$_DL_VAL" =~ ^\.*$ ]] && return 1
    return 0
}

# A plain `label: value` line. Only used to pick up the unpadded stragglers in a
# block already recognised as form B -- never on its own, or this would swallow
# every colon-bearing line in the corpus.
_dl_match_plain () {
    local line="$1"
    local _re='^[[:space:]]*([^:]*[^.:[:space:]])[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]+(.+)$'
    [[ "$line" =~ $_re ]] || return 1
    _DL_KEY="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    _DL_VAL="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    while [[ "$_DL_VAL" == *" " ]]; do _DL_VAL="${_DL_VAL% }"; done
    [[ "$_DL_VAL" =~ ^\.*$ ]] && return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line hits=0 form_b=0
    local -A seen_keys=()
    local repeated=0 key
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        _dl_match "$line" || continue
        hits=$((hits + 1))
        [[ "$_DL_FORM" == B ]] && form_b=1
        key="$_DL_KEY"
        while [[ "$key" == *"." || "$key" == *" " ]]; do key="${key%[. ]}"; done
        [[ -n "${seen_keys[$key]:-}" ]] && repeated=1
        seen_keys[$key]=1
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $hits -ge 3 ]] || return 1
    # A key that repeats means these are grouped records, not one flat key/value
    # list -- hashcat --benchmark repeats `Speed.#1` / `Hashmode` once per hash
    # mode, and a record parser keeps that grouping where flattening would lose
    # it. Only form B can reach such blocks, so leave them to the record parsers.
    [[ $form_b -eq 1 && $repeated -eq 1 ]] && return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line

    # Does this block use form B? If so its unpadded `label: value` lines are
    # part of the same aligned block and are kept.
    local form_b=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        if _dl_match "$line" && [[ "$_DL_FORM" == B ]]; then form_b=1; break; fi
    done <<< "$text"

    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        if ! _dl_match "$line"; then
            [[ $form_b -eq 1 ]] || continue
            _dl_match_plain "$line" || continue
        fi
        local key="$_DL_KEY"
        # Form B pads the key out with dots; they are delimiter, not name.
        while [[ "$key" == *"." ]]; do key="${key%.}"; done
        # Trim trailing space off the key too.
        while [[ "$key" == *" " ]]; do key="${key% }"; done
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.key ${key}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.value ${_DL_VAL}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/embedded-table.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=1410cd1c2969353f9b01075f5179be662241caf56e74dcd11b117cee4baf3594===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: embedded-table
## Description: Reports with one dominant aligned table amid prose/kv preamble and footnotes
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 37
## Sample: samples/embedded-table/basic.txt

# The REPORT shape: free prose or `Key: value` preamble, ONE dominant
# whitespace-aligned table (labelly header + consistent data rows), optional
# trailing footnotes/kv Aje28094Aj smartctl -a, mdadm --detail, benchmark write-ups,
# backup job reports:
#
#   Backup Job Report
#   Job Name:   nightly-full
#
#   Volume       Files      Size       Status
#   vol-daily    122045     18.4 GB    OK
#   ...
#
#   Elapsed:    01:42:18
#
# aligned-columns can't take these (the preamble defeats its banner rules and
# block-records claims the blank-separated blocks first, welding everything
# into kv mush). This strategy finds the LARGEST table window and extracts
# only it; everything outside the window is report chrome.
#
# A table window: a HEADER line Aje28094Aj >=3 tokens, digit-free, every token
# alphanumeric-bearing, none ending in ':' (a kv label) Aje28094Aj followed by >=3
# consecutive non-blank lines each with >= the header's token count and >=1
# digit-bearing token (data, not prose). And the window must be EMBEDDED:
# >=2 non-blank lines outside it Aje28094Aj a bare table stays with aligned-columns.

# Does a SHORT data row (fewer tokens than the header) still belong to this
# table? Only if every token positionally aligns to a distinct header column in
# increasing order Aje28094Aj a genuine blank interior cell (bundle-outdated's sidekiq
# row with an empty `Requested`), not a prose footnote that merely has a digit.
# Column boundaries mirror the extractor's midpoint model. $1=header line,
# $2=data line. Returns 0 when aligned.
_et_row_aligns () {
    local hline="$1" dline="$2"
    # Header token start columns.
    local -a hs=() he=()
    local i c inw=-1 n=${#hline}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${hline:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$c" != ' ' && "$c" != $'\t' ]]; then
            [[ $inw -lt 0 ]] && { inw=$i; hs+=("$i"); }
        elif [[ $inw -ge 0 ]]; then he+=($((i - 1))); inw=-1; fi
    done
    [[ $inw -ge 0 ]] && he+=($((n - 1)))
    local ncols=${#hs[@]}
    [[ $ncols -lt 3 ]] && return 1
    # Midpoint boundary opening each column c (>=1); col 0 opens at 0.
    local -a bnd=(0)
    for ((i = 1; i < ncols; i++)); do
        bnd+=($(( (${he[$((i - 1))]} + ${hs[$i]} + 1) / 2 )))
    done
    # Bucket each data token's start into a column; require strictly increasing
    # distinct columns and a left-aligned first token (column 0).
    local dn=${#dline} prev=-1 tok=0 first=1
    inw=-1
    for ((i = 0; i <= dn; i++)); do
        c="${dline:$i:1}"
        if [[ $i -lt $dn && "$c" != ' ' && "$c" != $'\t' ]]; then
            if [[ $inw -lt 0 ]]; then
                inw=$i
                # column for a token starting at inw
                local col=0 k
                for ((k = 0; k < ncols; k++)); do
                    [[ $inw -ge ${bnd[$k]} ]] && col=$k
                done
                [[ $first -eq 1 && $col -ne 0 ]] && return 1
                first=0
                [[ $col -le $prev ]] && return 1
                prev=$col
                tok=$((tok + 1))
            fi
        else
            inw=-1
        fi
    done
    [[ $tok -ge 3 ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

# Find the best window. Sets _ET_START (header line index, 0-based over
# non-blank-preserved raw lines), _ET_LEN (data row count), _ET_COLS.
_et_scan () {
    local text="$1"
    local -a _lines=()
    local _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do _lines+=("$_l"); done <<< "$text"
    _ET_START=-1; _ET_LEN=0; _ET_COLS=0
    local i j n=${#_lines[@]} nonblank=0
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        [[ -n "${_lines[$i]//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
    done
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        _l="${_lines[$i]}"
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_l" =~ [0-9] ]] && continue
        local -a hk=(); read -ra hk <<< "$_l"
        [[ ${#hk[@]} -lt 3 ]] && continue
        local t ok=1
        for t in "${hk[@]}"; do
            # a label: alphanumeric-bearing, starts alnum-or-bracket (a diff
            # hunk's `+use` line must not read as a header), no kv colon
            [[ "$t" =~ [A-Za-z0-9] && "$t" != *: && "$t" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9\[] ]] || { ok=0; break; }
        done
        [[ $ok -eq 0 ]] && continue
        # The header must open a section: preceded by a blank line, the start
        # of input, or a NARROWER line (a title, kv or section label Aje28094Aj fewer
        # tokens). A same-or-wider data row directly above means this "header"
        # is really a row inside a bigger table (prlimit's all-caps rows).
        if [[ $i -gt 0 && -n "${_lines[$((i - 1))]//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
            local -a pv=(); read -ra pv <<< "${_lines[$((i - 1))]}"
            if [[ ${#pv[@]} -ge ${#hk[@]} ]]; then
                # Aje280a6Ajunless that wider line is banner chrome, not a data row: a
                # data row's tokens all lead with alphanumerics, a `=== SECTION
                # ===` banner's don't.
                local _pvrow=1 t3
                for t3 in "${pv[@]}"; do [[ "$t3" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9] ]] || { _pvrow=0; break; }; done
                [[ $_pvrow -eq 1 ]] && continue
            fi
        fi
        # count consecutive data rows: >= the header's token count, digit-
        # bearing (data, not prose), and not a SENTENCE (ends in '.')
        local rows=0
        for ((j = i + 1; j < n; j++)); do
            local dl="${_lines[$j]}"
            [[ -z "${dl//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && break
            local -a dk=(); read -ra dk <<< "$dl"
            # A row with fewer tokens than the header is admitted ONLY when its
            # tokens positionally align to distinct header columns Aje28094Aj a blank
            # interior cell (bundle-outdated's sidekiq), not a prose footnote.
            # The FIRST row must be full-width, though: it anchors the window as
            # a genuine table. A header whose token count is inflated by
            # multi-word column labels (spec-cpu's doubled `Ref. Run Time Rate`)
            # makes EVERY data row "short" Aje28094Aj that is aligned-columns' positional
            # multi-word-header case, not an embedded table.
            if [[ ${#dk[@]} -lt ${#hk[@]} ]]; then
                [[ $rows -eq 0 ]] && break
                _et_row_aligns "$_l" "$dl" || break
            fi
            [[ "$dl" =~ [0-9] ]] || break
            [[ "$dl" =~ \.$ ]] && break
            rows=$((rows + 1))
        done
        # The window must CLOSE the section too: the line after the last row
        # must be blank, EOF, or narrower. A same-width non-matching row right
        # after (a digit-free data row like `worker stopped - -`) means the
        # window TRUNCATED a bigger table Aje28094Aj that table isn't ours.
        local nxt=$((i + rows + 1))
        if [[ $nxt -lt $n && -n "${_lines[$nxt]//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
            local -a nk=(); read -ra nk <<< "${_lines[$nxt]}"
            [[ ${#nk[@]} -ge ${#hk[@]} ]] && continue
        fi
        if [[ $rows -ge 3 && $rows -gt $_ET_LEN ]]; then
            _ET_START=$i; _ET_LEN=$rows; _ET_COLS=${#hk[@]}
        fi
    done
    [[ $_ET_START -lt 0 ]] && return 1
    # Embedded means real chrome around it: >=2 non-blank lines OUTSIDE.
    [[ $(( nonblank - _ET_LEN - 1 )) -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    # And the chrome must contain at least one PROSE/banner line Aje28094Aj >=3 tokens,
    # >=2 of them alphanumeric-bearing, and NOT `key: value`-shaped (no ` : `
    # and no colon-suffixed first token). A report whose chrome is ALL kv
    # (mdadm --detail's `Version : 1.2` block, nvidia-smi -q) is fully
    # representable by the kv-capable parsers (indented-hierarchy,
    # block-records) Aje28094Aj table AND fields Aje28094Aj and taking only the table would LOSE
    # the fields. Prose and footnotes, by contrast, no parser can use.
    local _pr=0
    local -a _hk2=(); read -ra _hk2 <<< "${_lines[$_ET_START]}"
    local _hnorm="${_hk2[*]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        [[ $i -ge $_ET_START && $i -le $((_ET_START + _ET_LEN)) ]] && continue
        _l="${_lines[$i]}"
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local -a pk=(); read -ra pk <<< "$_l"
        # A chrome line token-identical to the window's header is a SECTION
        # repeat Aje28094Aj this is a multi-section table (faillock's per-user blocks,
        # ps/top page reprints) that aligned-columns' resume logic already
        # collects in full; taking one window would DROP the other sections.
        [[ "${pk[*]}" == "$_hnorm" ]] && return 1
        # Aje280a6Ajand a chrome line whose tokens are a SUBSET of the header's is a
        # sibling section's slightly-narrower header (yugabyte's Tablet
        # Servers table without the Role column) Aje28094Aj same multi-section story.
        if [[ ${#pk[@]} -ge 3 && ${#pk[@]} -le ${#_hk2[@]} ]]; then
            local _sub=1 _st _st2 _hit2
            for _st in "${pk[@]}"; do
                _hit2=0
                for _st2 in "${_hk2[@]}"; do [[ "$_st" == "$_st2" ]] && { _hit2=1; break; }; done
                [[ $_hit2 -eq 0 ]] && { _sub=0; break; }
            done
            [[ $_sub -eq 1 ]] && return 1
        fi
        [[ "$_l" == *" : "* ]] && continue
        [[ ${#pk[@]} -lt 3 ]] && continue
        [[ "${pk[0]}" == *: ]] && continue
        # Prose is WORDS: digit-bearing chrome is data from another section
        # (faillock's second table, readelf's offset banner), and box-drawing
        # glyphs mark tree rows (findmnt submounts) Aje28094Aj neither is the prose
        # preamble/footnote evidence this strategy exists for.
        [[ "$_l" =~ [0-9] ]] && continue
        [[ "$_l" == *$'\342\224'* || "$_l" == *$'\342\225'* ]] && continue
        local _pa=0 t2
        for t2 in "${pk[@]}"; do [[ "$t2" =~ [A-Za-z0-9] ]] && _pa=$((_pa + 1)); done
        [[ $_pa -ge 2 ]] && { _pr=1; break; }
    done
    [[ $_pr -eq 1 ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="report with one dominant embedded aligned table"
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    _et_scan "$text" || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=76
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    _et_scan "$text" || { echo ""; return 0; }
    local -a _lines=()
    local _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do _lines+=("$_l"); done <<< "$text"

    # Column boundaries from the header's printed token positions, split at the
    # MIDPOINT of each inter-label gap (the vertical-line treatment) Aje28094Aj so a
    # multi-word cell anywhere in the row (`18.4 GB` under Size, `active sync`
    # under State) stays in ITS column instead of shifting everything after it,
    # and right-aligned numbers that start left of their label still land home.
    local hline="${_lines[$_ET_START]}"
    local -a headers=() h_start=() h_end=()
    local i c in_word=-1 n=${#hline}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${hline:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$c" != ' ' && "$c" != '	' ]]; then
            [[ $in_word -lt 0 ]] && { in_word=$i; h_start+=("$i"); }
        elif [[ $in_word -ge 0 ]]; then
            h_end+=($((i - 1))); headers+=("${hline:$in_word:$((i - in_word))}"); in_word=-1
        fi
    done
    [[ $in_word -ge 0 ]] && { h_end+=($((n - 1))); headers+=("${hline:$in_word:$((n - in_word))}"); }
    local ncols=${#headers[@]}
    for ((i = 0; i < ncols; i++)); do headers[$i]="${headers[$i]//./_}"; done
    local -a col_lo=(0) col_hi=()
    for ((i = 1; i < ncols; i++)); do
        local b=$(( (${h_end[$((i - 1))]} + ${h_start[$i]} + 1) / 2 ))
        col_hi+=("$b"); col_lo+=("$b")
    done
    col_hi+=(99999)

    local result="" entry=0 j
    for ((j = _ET_START + 1; j <= _ET_START + _ET_LEN; j++)); do
        local row="${_lines[$j]}"
        local rlen=${#row}
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local lo=0 b
        for ((i = 0; i < ncols; i++)); do
            if [[ $i -lt $((ncols - 1)) ]]; then
                b=${col_hi[$i]}
                # A boundary landing INSIDE a token means that cell overflows
                # its printed column (`zstd-19` under a 4-char `Tool` label,
                # `Reallocated_Sector_Ct` past ATTRIBUTE_NAME's span): snap the
                # cut right to the token's end so the cell stays whole.
                while [[ $b -gt 0 && $b -lt $rlen && "${row:$b:1}" != ' ' && "${row:$((b - 1)):1}" != ' ' ]]; do
                    b=$((b + 1))
                done
            else
                b=$rlen
            fi
            [[ $lo -ge $rlen ]] && break
            [[ $b -gt $rlen ]] && b=$rlen
            local value="${row:$lo:$((b - lo))}"
            lo=$b
            value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            # collapse inner alignment padding runs to one space
            while [[ "$value" == *'  '* ]]; do value="${value//  / }"; done
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${headers[$i]} ${value}"$'\n'
        done
    done
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
