===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/equals.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=553ddebcefd0ca24fb69a37f3ef7441dfa7a95144e4d26ea8c35b25965fa1001===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: equals
## Description: Extract field=value pairs from equals-delimited data
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 65
## Sample: samples/equals/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=35
    # Apply if input contains lines with equals signs that look like assignments
    # Skip lines that look like code (==, +=, !=)
    # Use while-read so ^ anchors match per-line (not start of entire string)
    local _det_line
    while IFS= read -r _det_line; do
        # Tight assignment: `KEY=value` (env vars, systemctl show, `git config
        # --list`'s dotted keys `user.name=Aje280a6Aj`). The key allows `.` so dotted
        # config keys match.
        [[ "$_det_line" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.\ -]*=[^=] ]] && return 0
        # Space-padded assignment with a rich key: `KEY(ctx) = value`,
        # `KEY(env: X) = value` (ansible-config dump). Requires ` = ` so it does
        # not fire on prose that merely contains a lone '='.
        [[ "$_det_line" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_().:\ -]*\ =\ [^=] ]] && return 0
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Clean text (dates, parentheses) -- cached by engine after first call
    clean_text "$text"; text="$_CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT"

    local result=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Skip empty lines
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Must contain = but not == (comparison) or += or !=
        [[ "$line" != *"="* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == *"=="* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == *"+="* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == *"!="* ]] && continue

        # Extract key (before first =) and value (after first =)
        local key value

        # Strip leading spaces and bullet markers
        local _stripped="$line"
        while [[ "$_stripped" == " "* ]]; do _stripped="${_stripped# }"; done
        if [[ "$_stripped" == "* "* ]]; then
            _stripped="${_stripped#\* }"
        fi

        key="${_stripped%%=*}"
        value="${_stripped#*=}"

        # Skip if key is empty or too long
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        [[ ${#key} -gt 50 ]] && continue

        # Skip lines where key starts with a digit
        [[ "$key" =~ ^[0-9] ]] && continue

        # Clean up key and value
        key="${key// /_}"
        key="${key#_}"
        key="${key%_}"

        while [[ "$value" == " "* ]]; do value="${value# }"; done
        while [[ "$value" == *" " ]]; do value="${value% }"; done

        # Skip if value is empty
        [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

        result+="${key} ${value}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: fixed-width
## Description: Fixed-width column format with header/separator
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 30
## Sample: samples/fixed-width/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=65

    # Reject JSON-like input
    _is_json "$1" && return 1

    # Decline `+---+` box tables Aje28094Aj psql-table's box parser owns those.
    local _bxl
    while IFS= read -r _bxl; do
        [[ "$_bxl" == *"+"* && "$_bxl" == *"---"* ]] || continue
        [[ "$_bxl" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[-+[:space:]]+$ ]] && return 1
    done <<< "$text"

    # Must have a separator line of dashes with gaps (scan line by line)
    local _det_line
    while IFS= read -r _det_line; do
        if [[ "$_det_line" =~ ^[-]+(\ +[-]+)+ ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    return 1
}

_strat_fw_find_columns () {
    # Given a separator line like "-------  --------  --------   -----"
    # return column start:end positions
    local sep_line="$1"
    local positions=""
    local i=0
    local len=${#sep_line}
    local in_dash=0
    local col_start=0

    while [[ $i -lt $len ]]; do
        local ch="${sep_line:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$ch" == "-" ]]; then
            if [[ $in_dash -eq 0 ]]; then
                col_start=$i
                in_dash=1
            fi
        else
            if [[ $in_dash -eq 1 ]]; then
                # End of a dash column
                if [[ -n "$positions" ]]; then
                    positions+="|"
                fi
                positions+="${col_start}:${i}"
                in_dash=0
            fi
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done

    # Handle last column if line ends with dashes
    if [[ $in_dash -eq 1 ]]; then
        if [[ -n "$positions" ]]; then
            positions+="|"
        fi
        positions+="${col_start}:${i}"
    fi

    echo "$positions"
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # Find the separator line
    local sep_line=""
    local header_line=""
    local sep_line_num=0
    local line_num=0
    local prev_line=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line_num=$((line_num + 1))
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[-]+(\ +[-]+)+ ]]; then
            sep_line="$line"
            sep_line_num=$line_num
            header_line="$prev_line"
            break
        fi
        prev_line="$line"
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ -z "$sep_line" ]] && return

    # Get column positions from separator
    local col_positions
    col_positions=$(_strat_fw_find_columns "$sep_line")

    # Parse column positions into arrays
    local col_starts=""
    local col_ends=""
    local num_cols=0
    local old_ifs="$IFS"
    IFS='|'
    local pos_entries
    read -ra pos_entries <<< "$col_positions"
    IFS="$old_ifs"

    local p
    for p in "${pos_entries[@]}"; do
        [[ -z "$p" ]] && continue
        local cs="${p%%:*}"
        local ce="${p##*:}"
        col_starts="${col_starts}${cs} "
        col_ends="${col_ends}${ce} "
        num_cols=$((num_cols + 1))
    done

    # Extract header names using column positions
    local headers=""
    local ci=0
    local starts_arr
    local ends_arr
    read -ra starts_arr <<< "$col_starts"
    read -ra ends_arr <<< "$col_ends"

    for ((ci=0; ci<num_cols; ci++)); do
        local cs=${starts_arr[$ci]}
        local ce=${ends_arr[$ci]}
        local clen=$((ce - cs))
        local hdr="${header_line:$cs:$clen}"
        # Trim whitespace and replace spaces with underscores
        while [[ "$hdr" == " "* ]]; do hdr="${hdr# }"; done
        while [[ "$hdr" == *" " ]]; do hdr="${hdr% }"; done
        hdr="${hdr// /_}"
        if [[ -n "$headers" ]]; then
            headers+=" "
        fi
        headers+="$hdr"
    done

    local headers_arr
    read -ra headers_arr <<< "$headers"

    # Extract data rows (lines after separator)
    local row_num=0
    local past_sep=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ $past_sep -eq 0 ]]; then
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[-]+(\ +[-]+)+ ]]; then
                past_sep=1
            fi
            continue
        fi

        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        row_num=$((row_num + 1))

        for ((ci=0; ci<num_cols; ci++)); do
            local cs=${starts_arr[$ci]}
            local ce=${ends_arr[$ci]}
            local hdr="${headers_arr[$ci]}"
            local val

            if [[ $ci -eq $((num_cols - 1)) ]]; then
                # Last column: take from start to end of line
                val="${line:$cs}"
            else
                local clen=$((ce - cs))
                val="${line:$cs:$clen}"
            fi

            # Trim edges; spaces inside the value are preserved (the engine keeps
            # everything after the first space as the value).
            while [[ "$val" == " "* ]]; do val="${val# }"; done
            while [[ "$val" == *" " ]]; do val="${val% }"; done
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue

            result+="row${row_num}.${hdr} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/grouped-list.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=fb5978e0a6cc04092ef6af9ebe8a3ec272920690cc023483857543e6da1b5f48===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: grouped-list
## Description: Single-token group labels over indented single-token members (asdf list: tool over its versions)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 49
## Sample: samples/grouped-list/basic.txt

# asdf and similar version managers print each tool as an unindented label with
# its installed versions indented beneath, the active one flagged `*`:
#
#   nodejs
#    *20.14.0
#     22.4.1
#   python
#     3.11.9
#    *3.12.4
#
# A flat line list (line-records) loses the toolAje28692Ajversion grouping and keeps the
# `*` glued to the version. The tidy shape carries the label down: one row per
# member Aje28094Aj `group`, `value`, and a `current` flag when the `*` marks it.

# Leading-space count of $1 -> _GL_IND
_gl_indent () {
    local l="$1" i=0
    while [[ "${l:$i:1}" == ' ' || "${l:$i:1}" == $'\t' ]]; do i=$((i + 1)); done
    _GL_IND=$i
}

# A member line: indented, and its content (after an optional `*` marker) is a
# SINGLE token. Sets _GL_VAL / _GL_CUR. A group label: unindented single token.
_gl_classify () {   # $1 = raw line -> _GL_KIND (G|M|X), _GL_VAL, _GL_CUR
    local l="$1"
    _GL_KIND=X; _GL_VAL=""; _GL_CUR=""
    [[ -z "${l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && return
    _gl_indent "$l"
    local body="${l#"${l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"    # lstrip
    body="${body%"${body##*[![:space:]]}"}"    # rstrip
    if [[ $_GL_IND -eq 0 ]]; then
        # unindented label: a single bare token, no `*`, and NOT a colon-
        # suffixed section header (`inputs:` telegraf) Aje28094Aj that's a kv/list group,
        # not a version-manager tool label.
        [[ "$body" == *[[:space:]]* ]] && return
        [[ "$body" == "*"* ]] && return
        [[ "$body" == *: ]] && return
        _GL_VAL="$body"; _GL_KIND=G
    else
        local cur=""
        if [[ "$body" == "*"* ]]; then cur="*"; body="${body#\*}"; fi
        body="${body#"${body%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ "$body" == *[[:space:]]* ]] && return   # multi-token Aje28692Aj not a bare version
        [[ -z "$body" ]] && return
        # A member must look like a VERSION: single token, carries an ASCII
        # digit, and holds no `:` Aje28094Aj so a colon kv leaf (nodetool gossipinfo's
        # `generation:1718Aje280a6Aj`) and a word-only tree node (CJK hierarchy) stay
        # with indented-hierarchy / the flat list, not here.
        [[ "$body" == *:* ]] && return
        [[ "$body" =~ [0-9] ]] || return
        _GL_VAL="$body"; _GL_CUR="$cur"; _GL_KIND=M
    fi
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line groups=0 members=0 last_was_group=0 bad=0 any=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        any=1
        _gl_classify "$line"
        case "$_GL_KIND" in
            G) groups=$((groups + 1)); last_was_group=1 ;;
            M) members=$((members + 1)); last_was_group=0 ;;
            X) bad=1; break ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    # Every non-blank line must classify (no stragglers), with >=2 groups and
    # >=1 member per group on average Aje28094Aj the asdf signature, nothing looser.
    [[ $bad -eq 1 || $any -eq 0 ]] && return 1
    [[ $groups -ge 2 && $members -ge $groups ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=78
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 group="" line
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _gl_classify "$line"
        case "$_GL_KIND" in
            G) group="$_GL_VAL" ;;
            M)
                [[ -z "$group" ]] && continue
                entry=$((entry + 1))
                result+="entry${entry}.group ${group}"$'\n'
                result+="entry${entry}.value ${_GL_VAL}"$'\n'
                [[ -n "$_GL_CUR" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.current true"$'\n'
                ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/indented-colon-groups.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=bd8165c794b62e56c0bdb13a0ea615df4bf3b9b69122841b27704386909ad3f4===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: indented-colon-groups
## Description: `header:` lines over indented single-token members (cargo install/machete, ethtool caps) -> group/value rows
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 35
## Sample: samples/indented-colon-groups/basic.txt

# Some tools print an unindented header ending in a colon, then the items that
# belong to it indented beneath, one bare token per line:
#
#   cargo-audit v0.20.0:
#       cargo-audit
#   ripgrep v14.1.0:
#       rg
#
# A flat line list (text-lines / line-records) loses the header->item grouping
# and leaves each header stranded in its own row. The tidy shape carries the
# header down: one row per member, `group` + `value`.
#
# cargo-machete names the group as `crate -- /path/Cargo.toml:`. When EVERY
# header carries that ` -- ` split the group becomes two columns, `name` and
# `path`, so the crate and its manifest are addressable separately -- exactly
# what a reviewer asked for (crate, path, and one dependency per row).
#
# Kept off config / YAML / key:value output by three gates: members must be a
# SINGLE token (no whitespace) and carry no `key: value` colon pair, and the
# header's own text (before the trailing colon) must hold no `key: value`
# pair either. Preamble and footer lines are tolerated only at the very top
# and bottom -- any unclassifiable line in the middle rejects the block.

# Leading whitespace width of $1 -> _ICG_IND
_icg_indent () {
    local l="$1" i=0
    while [[ "${l:$i:1}" == ' ' || "${l:$i:1}" == $'\t' ]]; do i=$((i + 1)); done
    _ICG_IND=$i
}

# Classify a raw line -> _ICG_KIND (G group | M member | N noise), _ICG_BODY.
_icg_classify () {
    local l="$1"
    _ICG_KIND=N; _ICG_BODY=""
    [[ -z "${l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && return
    _icg_indent "$l"
    local body="${l#"${l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"    # lstrip
    body="${body%"${body##*[![:space:]]}"}"    # rstrip
    if [[ $_ICG_IND -eq 0 ]]; then
        # A group header: unindented, ends in ':', and the text before that
        # colon holds no `key: value` pair (so YAML/config mappings stay out).
        if [[ "$body" == *: && "${body%:}" != *": "* ]]; then
            _ICG_BODY="${body%:}"; _ICG_KIND=G
        fi
        return
    fi
    # A member: indented, a single token, no colon pair.
    [[ "$body" == *[[:space:]]* ]] && return
    [[ "$body" == *": "* ]] && return
    _ICG_BODY="$body"; _ICG_KIND=M
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line groups=0 members=0
    local order=""
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _icg_classify "$line"
        case "$_ICG_KIND" in
            G) order+="G"; groups=$((groups + 1)) ;;
            M) order+="M"; members=$((members + 1)) ;;
            N) order+="N" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    # Need real grouping: >=2 headers and at least one member each.
    [[ $groups -ge 2 && $members -ge $groups ]] || return 1
    # Noise (preamble/footer) only at the very ends -- never between groups.
    local core="${order#"${order%%[!N]*}"}"   # strip leading N run
    core="${core%"${core##*[!N]}"}"           # strip trailing N run
    [[ "$core" == *N* ]] && return 1
    # Every group must be followed by a member somewhere before the next group.
    [[ "$core" == G* ]] || return 1
    case "$core" in *GG*) return 1 ;; esac     # a header with no members of its own
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local line

    # Two-column group name only when EVERY member-bearing header carries the
    # ` -- ` split; otherwise a single `group` column, so a file never mixes the
    # two shapes. Headers with no members (a trailing footer line that happens
    # to end in a colon) do not count Aje28094Aj they emit nothing and must not veto the
    # split for the real groups above them.
    local split=1 saw_group=0 cur_group="" cur_split=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        _icg_classify "$line"
        case "$_ICG_KIND" in
            G)
                cur_group="$_ICG_BODY"
                [[ "$cur_group" == *" -- "* ]] && cur_split=1 || cur_split=0
                ;;
            M)
                [[ -n "$cur_group" ]] || continue
                saw_group=1
                [[ $cur_split -eq 1 ]] || split=0
                ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $saw_group -eq 1 ]] || split=0

    local result="" entry=0 gname="" gpath="" group=""
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        _icg_classify "$line"
        case "$_ICG_KIND" in
            G)
                group="$_ICG_BODY"
                if [[ $split -eq 1 ]]; then
                    gname="${group%% -- *}"
                    gpath="${group#* -- }"
                fi
                ;;
            M)
                [[ -n "$group" ]] || continue
                entry=$((entry + 1))
                if [[ $split -eq 1 ]]; then
                    result+="entry${entry}.name ${gname}"$'\n'
                    result+="entry${entry}.path ${gpath}"$'\n'
                else
                    result+="entry${entry}.group ${group}"$'\n'
                fi
                result+="entry${entry}.value ${_ICG_BODY}"$'\n'
                ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/delimited/indented-hierarchy.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=8b9109e238a2d1acfacd104b76a9917bce643c4d8277fbd8bc1ee3d0d84f0afd===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: indented-hierarchy
## Description: Indentation-based hierarchical data, flattened with dot notation
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 50
## Sample: samples/indented-hierarchy/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=65

    # Reject JSON-like input
    _is_json "$1" && return 1

    # Must have lines with increasing indentation (2+ space-indented lines)
    local indented_count=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        if [[ "$_line" == "  "* ]]; then
            indented_count=$((indented_count + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $indented_count -lt 2 ]] && return 1

    # Must have a non-indented line followed by indented lines
    [[ "${text:0:1}" != " " ]] || return 1

    # Must contain colons
    [[ "$text" == *":"* ]] || return 1

    return 0
}

_strat_ih_get_indent () {
    local line="$1"
    local stripped="$line"
    # Count leading spaces
    local count=0
    while [[ "$stripped" == " "* ]]; do
        stripped="${stripped# }"
        count=$((count + 1))
    done
    echo $count
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # Build arrays of path components at each indentation level
    # path_keys[0]="System_Information", path_keys[1]="BIOS_Information", etc.
    # We use indexed arrays
    local path_keys=""  # pipe-delimited: "level:key|level:key|..."
    local prev_indent=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        local indent
        indent=$(_strat_ih_get_indent "$line")

        # Strip leading whitespace
        local trimmed="$line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done

        [[ -z "$trimmed" ]] && continue

        # Check if this is a key: value line or a bare heading
        if [[ "$trimmed" == *":"* ]]; then
            local key="${trimmed%%:*}"
            local value="${trimmed#*:}"
            # Trim leading spaces from value
            while [[ "$value" == " "* ]]; do value="${value# }"; done

            # Trim key
            while [[ "$key" == " "* ]]; do key="${key# }"; done
            while [[ "$key" == *" " ]]; do key="${key% }"; done
            key="${key// /_}"
            # Trim value; spaces inside the value are preserved (the engine keeps
            # everything after the first space as the value).
            while [[ "$value" == *" " ]]; do value="${value% }"; done

            if [[ -n "$value" ]]; then
                # This is a key: value line -- emit with full path
                # Build path from path_keys for current indent level
                local path=""
                # Parse pipe-delimited entries
                local old_ifs="$IFS"
                IFS='|'
                local entries
                read -ra entries <<< "$path_keys"
                IFS="$old_ifs"
                local e
                for e in "${entries[@]}"; do
                    [[ -z "$e" ]] && continue
                    local elevel="${e%%:*}"
                    local ekey="${e#*:}"
                    if [[ $elevel -lt $indent ]]; then
                        if [[ -n "$path" ]]; then
                            path+="."
                        fi
                        path+="$ekey"
                    fi
                done
                if [[ -n "$path" ]]; then
                    result+="${path}.${key} ${value}"$'\n'
                else
                    result+="${key} ${value}"$'\n'
                fi
            else
                # Bare heading with colon but no value (e.g., "Section:")
                # Remove entries at this level or deeper
                local new_path_keys=""
                local old_ifs="$IFS"
                IFS='|'
                local entries
                read -ra entries <<< "$path_keys"
                IFS="$old_ifs"
                local e
                for e in "${entries[@]}"; do
                    [[ -z "$e" ]] && continue
                    local elevel="${e%%:*}"
                    if [[ $elevel -lt $indent ]]; then
                        if [[ -n "$new_path_keys" ]]; then
                            new_path_keys+="|"
                        fi
                        new_path_keys+="$e"
                    fi
                done
                if [[ -n "$new_path_keys" ]]; then
                    path_keys="${new_path_keys}|${indent}:${key}"
                else
                    path_keys="${indent}:${key}"
                fi
            fi
        else
            # Bare heading without colon
            local heading="$trimmed"
            while [[ "$heading" == " "* ]]; do heading="${heading# }"; done
            while [[ "$heading" == *" " ]]; do heading="${heading% }"; done
            heading="${heading// /_}"

            # Remove entries at this level or deeper
            local new_path_keys=""
            local old_ifs="$IFS"
            IFS='|'
            local entries
            read -ra entries <<< "$path_keys"
            IFS="$old_ifs"
            local e
            for e in "${entries[@]}"; do
                [[ -z "$e" ]] && continue
                local elevel="${e%%:*}"
                if [[ $elevel -lt $indent ]]; then
                    if [[ -n "$new_path_keys" ]]; then
                        new_path_keys+="|"
                    fi
                    new_path_keys+="$e"
                fi
            done
            if [[ -n "$new_path_keys" ]]; then
                path_keys="${new_path_keys}|${indent}:${heading}"
            else
                path_keys="${indent}:${heading}"
            fi
        fi

        prev_indent=$indent
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/labeled-inline-kv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=d551b490e009ec19058a85e95cc8982e2d703c7097d6fd0a61f33124d1fca2c0===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: labeled-inline-kv
## Description: Labeled inline key=value records Aje28094Aj "name: k=v, k=v, ..." (fio disk-stats/run-status/io-depths, ip -s)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 29
## Sample: samples/labeled-inline-kv/basic.txt

# Records of the form `<label>: <k=v>, <k=v>, Aje280a6Aj` Aje28094Aj a row label, a colon, then a
# comma-separated list of key=value pairs:
#
#   sda: ios=7411882/0, merge=0/0, ticks=1882044/0, in_queue=1883210, util=98.82%
#   READ: bw=482MiB/s (505MB/s), io=28.2GiB (30.3GB), run=60001-60001msec
#   IO depths : 1=0.1%, 2=0.1%, 4=0.1%, 8=0.1%, >=64=99.9%
#
# The label becomes a `name` column and each `k=v` a data column, so the whole
# block melts to one row per label. A leading section banner (`Disk stats
# (read/write):` Aje28094Aj a `label:` with no `k=v` after it) is skipped. Distinct from
# inline-kv (no label prefix, whitespace-separated) and colons (a single
# `key: value` per line): this needs a colon-label AND >=2 comma-separated
# `key=value` pairs after it.

# Echo the k=v part after the first colon of $1, or nothing if it isn't a record.
# A record: after the first ": " there are >=2 comma-separated parts each with '='.
_lik_kvpart () {
    local line="$1"
    [[ "$line" == *:* ]] || return 1
    local rest="${line#*:}"
    rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    [[ "$rest" == *=* ]] || return 1
    # split on comma; need >=2 parts, each containing '='
    local n=0 ok=1 part _oi="$IFS"
    IFS=','
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    set -- $rest
    IFS="$_oi"
    for part in "$@"; do
        [[ -z "${part//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        [[ "$part" == *=* ]] || { ok=0; break; }
    done
    [[ $ok -eq 1 && $n -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "$rest"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="labeled inline key=value records (name: k=v, k=v, ...)"
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Records must DOMINATE Aje28094Aj the whole block is `label: k=v, Aje280a6Aj` records, with at
    # most one non-record line (an optional leading section title like `Disk
    # stats (read/write):`). This keeps it off `key: value` snapshots (nmcli,
    # mdadm --examine) that merely contain one stray `label: k=v, k=v` line.
    local nonblank=0 records=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        _lik_kvpart "$_l" >/dev/null && records=$((records + 1))
        [[ $nonblank -ge 40 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $records -ge 1 && $records -ge $((nonblank - 1)) ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=82
    return 0
}

_lik_sanitize () {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s//[^A-Za-z0-9_]/_}"
    while [[ "$s" == *__* ]]; do s="${s//__/_}"; done
    s="${s#_}"; s="${s%_}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local kv; kv="$(_lik_kvpart "$_l")" || continue
        local label="${_l%%:*}"
        label="${label#"${label%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; label="${label%"${label##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${label}"$'\n'
        local part key val _oi="$IFS"
        IFS=','
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        set -- $kv
        IFS="$_oi"
        for part in "$@"; do
            part="${part#"${part%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; part="${part%"${part##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            [[ "$part" == *=* ]] || continue
            # Split on the LAST '=' so a key that itself contains '=' survives
            # (fio's `>=64=99.9%` Aje28692Aj key `>=64`, value `99.9%`); single-'=' pairs
            # (`ios=7411882/0`) are unaffected.
            key="$(_lik_sanitize "${part%=*}")"; val="${part##*=}"
            val="${val#"${val%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; val="${val%"${val##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            [[ -z "$key" || -z "$val" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/labeled-records.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=a849ce1bf6f8423c120a069dea105ba4b927de5a694399aaa1d2c6a3d8fe555e===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: labeled-records
## Description: One record per "label: prose" line (file, and similar per-line labelled output)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 40
## Sample: samples/labeled-records/basic.txt

# For output where EVERY line is `<single-token-label>: <prose value>` Aje28094Aj e.g.
# `file` output ("archive.tar.gz: gzip compressed data, Aje280a6Aj"). Each line is a
# distinct record, so this melts to one row per line with (name, value) columns.
#
# The single-token label + letter-initial value signature separates it from:
#   - key/value snapshots with numeric values (/proc/meminfo "MemTotal: 8173456 kB")
#   - status output with multi-word labels (hostnamectl "Static hostname: Aje280a6Aj")
# both of which are single-observation and handled by yaml/colons.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    local n=0 match=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        # single-token label (no space before the colon), then a value starting
        # with a letter (prose, not a number)
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+:[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z] ]] && match=$((match + 1))
        [[ $n -ge 40 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    # Every non-blank line must fit, and we need at least two records.
    [[ $n -ge 2 && $match -eq $n ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local key="${_l%%:*}" val="${_l#*:}"
        # trim
        key="${key#"${key%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; key="${key%"${key##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        val="${val#"${val%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; val="${val%"${val##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${key}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$val" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.value ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/line-records.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=9678c88b65ec0f12a4ce76f6d96f5b416d249b9532d9d74f1927cb901ca1ecc6===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: line-records
## Description: Last-resort Aje28094Aj each line is a record of whitespace-separated fields (value lists, single-line field dumps)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 96
## Sample: samples/line-records/basic.txt

# The catch-all for tabular-ish output nothing more specific claims: a single
# line of fields (date, /proc/loadavg, taskset, groups) or a consistent list of
# lines (dig +short, rpm -qa, brew list). Each line becomes one record with
# columns c1..cN. Priority 96 keeps it strictly last-resort Aje28094Aj every real parser
# runs first.

# A LEADING `# /path` line is a location banner (`# /home/Aje280a6Aj/ansible_collections`
# over the collection list), not a record. Narrow to a PATH content (`# /Aje280a6Aj`)
# so section titles (`# conda environments:`, `# Memory`, `# name`) that a
# real parser uses as a header are never stripped. Strategy-local: bespoke
# parsers (go mod why) read their own `# module` markers.
_lr_body () {
    local text="$1"
    if [[ "$text" == '# /'* ]]; then
        local _rest="${text#*$'\n'}"
        [[ -n "${_rest//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && { printf '%s' "$_rest"; return; }
    fi
    printf '%s' "$text"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    text="$(_lr_body "$text")"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    # Decline structured markup (JSON / quoted key-value) Aje28094Aj real parsers own it,
    # and this catch-all must not pollute the engine's multi-strategy merge.
    [[ "$text" == *'{'* || "$text" == *'":'* ]] && return 1

    local counts=() idx=0 hasnum=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        idx=$((idx + 1))
        local _tk; _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "$_l"
        counts+=("${#_tk[@]}")
        [[ "$_l" =~ [0-9] ]] && hasnum=1
        [[ $idx -ge 60 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    local n=${#counts[@]}
    [[ $n -lt 1 ]] && return 1

    if [[ $n -eq 1 ]]; then
        # single line: needs >=2 fields AND a number, so pure prose (e.g. "no
        # extractable content here") isn't carved into columns.
        [[ ${counts[0]} -ge 2 && $hasnum -eq 1 ]] || return 1
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
        return 0
    fi

    # Multi-line: a dominant modal column count means a consistent list/table
    # (git ls-files, git branch, strings, git status Aje280a6Aj). The consistency itself is
    # the structure signal, so no digit is required here Aje28094Aj but ragged prose (which
    # has no dominant column count) is still rejected.
    local mode=0 best=0 c d k
    for c in "${counts[@]}"; do
        k=0
        for d in "${counts[@]}"; do [[ "$d" -eq "$c" ]] && k=$((k + 1)); done
        [[ $k -gt $best ]] && { best=$k; mode=$c; }
    done
    [[ $mode -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    [[ $(( best * 100 / n )) -ge 60 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    text="$(_lr_body "$text")"
    local result="" entry=0 _l

    # COLON-STRUCTURED single-column lists (ARNs Aje28094Aj `arn:aws:ecs:region:
    # account:cluster/name`): every line space-free with the SAME colon
    # count >=2 means the colons are field separators, not punctuation.
    # Split them into columns instead of emitting one opaque cell.
    local _cs_ok=1 _cs_first=-1 _cs_n=0
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _cs_n=$((_cs_n + 1))
        # URLs (`https://host:port`) and bare time lists keep their colons:
        # require no `//` and an alpha-led first field.
        if [[ "$_l" == *" "* || "$_l" == *$'\t'* || "$_l" != *:*:* \
              || "$_l" == *//* || ! "$_l" =~ ^[A-Za-z] ]]; then _cs_ok=0; break; fi
        local _cs_only="${_l//[!:]/}"
        [[ $_cs_first -lt 0 ]] && _cs_first=${#_cs_only}
        [[ ${#_cs_only} -ne $_cs_first ]] && { _cs_ok=0; break; }
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $_cs_ok -eq 1 && $_cs_n -ge 2 && $_cs_first -ge 2 ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r _l; do
            [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            local _cs_i=0 _cs_part
            while [[ "$_l" == *:* ]]; do
                _cs_part="${_l%%:*}"; _l="${_l#*:}"
                _cs_i=$((_cs_i + 1))
                [[ -n "$_cs_part" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.$(_col_letter $_cs_i) ${_cs_part}"$'\n'
            done
            _cs_i=$((_cs_i + 1))
            [[ -n "$_l" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.$(_col_letter $_cs_i) ${_l}"$'\n'
        done <<< "$text"
        [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
        echo "$result"
        return 0
    fi

    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local _tk; _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "$_l"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local i
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#_tk[@]}; i++)); do
            result+="entry${entry}.$(_col_letter $((i + 1))) ${_tk[$i]}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/ping-report.sh===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ping-report
## Description: ping/arping reply streams Aje28094Aj one row per reply, summary chrome dropped
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 35
## Sample: samples/ping-report/ping.txt

# The ping family (`ping`, `ping6`, `arping`): a banner, repeated REPLY rows
# (`64 bytes from 93.184.216.34: icmp_seq=1 ttl=56 time=11.4 ms`,
# `60 bytes from 00:14:bf:Aje280a6Aj (192.168.1.1): index=0 time=1.234 msec`), then a
# `--- Aje280a6Aj statistics ---` footer with prose summaries. The replies are the
# dataset: one row each Aje28094Aj bytes, from, optional ip, then a column per k=v
# pair with a trailing bare unit token folded into the previous value. The
# banner/footer/summary lines are chrome and are dropped.

_pr_is_reply () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+\ bytes\ from\ [^[:space:]]+ && "$1" == *": "* && "$1" == *=* ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local _l nb=0 replies=0
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        _pr_is_reply "$_l" && replies=$((replies + 1))
        [[ $nb -ge 60 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $replies -ge 2 && $(( replies * 100 / nb )) -ge 40 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        _pr_is_reply "$_l" || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local toks=() t i
        read -ra toks <<< "$_l"
        result+="entry${entry}.bytes ${toks[0]}"$'\n'
        # toks[1]=bytes toks[2]=from toks[3]=<addr>[:]
        local _from="${toks[3]%:}"
        result+="entry${entry}.from ${_from}"$'\n'
        i=4
        # optional `(ip):` / `(ip)` token Aje28094Aj regex via a variable: a literal
        # `)` inside a bracket class confuses the [[ ]] parser inline.
        local _ip_re='^\(([^)]+)\):?$'
        if [[ "${toks[4]:-}" =~ $_ip_re ]]; then
            result+="entry${entry}.ip ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
            i=5
        fi
        local _lastkey=""
        for ((; i < ${#toks[@]}; i++)); do
            t="${toks[$i]}"
            if [[ "$t" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.+)$ ]]; then
                _lastkey="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                result+="entry${entry}.${_lastkey} ${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"$'\n'
            elif [[ -n "$_lastkey" && "$t" =~ ^[A-Za-z%/]+$ ]]; then
                # bare unit token (`ms`, `msec`) folds into the last value
                result="${result%$'\n'} ${t}"$'\n'
            fi
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: pipe-cells
## Description: Monitor rows like `PRC | sys 1.42s | user 3.18s |` Aje28094Aj a row label plus pipe-separated key/value cells (atop)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 31
## Sample: samples/pipe-cells/basic.txt

# atop and similar full-screen monitors print each resource group as a row:
#
#   PRC | sys    1.42s | user   3.18s | #proc    284 | #zombie    0 |
#   CPU | sys      14% | user     31% | irq       2% | idle    248% |
#
# a short row LABEL, then `|`-separated cells that are each a `key value` pair.
# The keys differ line to line, so a wide-per-line table is sparse mush and
# aligned-columns keeps the `|` glyphs as columns. The tidy shape is long:
# one row per cell Aje28094Aj group / key / value Aje28094Aj with the pipes gone. Distinct enough
# not to poach real pipe tables: the label sits OUTSIDE the pipes, the row ends
# in a pipe, and every cell is a two-token key/value (a data table's cells are
# lone values).

# A pipe-cells row: sets nothing, returns 0/1. `LABEL | k v | k v | Aje280a6Aj |`
_pc_row () {
    local line="$1"
    # Leading label: uppercase-led short token, then ` | `.
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9#_]{0,5}[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]] ]] || return 1
    # Must carry >=2 pipes and end (after trailing spaces) with a pipe.
    local t="${line%"${line##*[![:space:]]}"}"   # rstrip
    [[ "$t" == *"|" ]] || return 1
    local bars="${line//[^|]/}"
    [[ ${#bars} -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    # Every non-empty cell after the label must be a key/value (>=2 tokens).
    local rest="${line#*|}"
    local -a cells=(); IFS='|' read -ra cells <<< "$rest"
    # Count key/value cells (>=2 tokens). Empty cells (SWP's gap) and a single
    # lone-value cell (DSK's `sda` device name) are tolerated and skipped; a
    # real 2-/3-column pipe table has only lone-value cells and so scores 0.
    local seen=0 c
    for c in "${cells[@]}"; do
        local -a tk=(); read -ra tk <<< "$c"
        [[ ${#tk[@]} -ge 2 ]] && seen=$((seen + 1))
    done
    [[ $seen -ge 2 ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line hits=0
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _pc_row "$line" && hits=$((hits + 1))
        [[ $hits -ge 3 ]] && { _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80; return 0; }
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        _pc_row "$line" || continue
        local group="${line%%|*}"
        group="${group%"${group##*[![:space:]]}"}"      # rstrip
        group="${group#"${group%%[![:space:]]*}"}"      # lstrip
        local rest="${line#*|}"
        local IFS='|'; local -a cells=(); read -ra cells <<< "$rest"; unset IFS
        local c
        for c in "${cells[@]}"; do
            local -a tk=(); read -ra tk <<< "$c"
            [[ ${#tk[@]} -lt 2 ]] && continue
            local key="${tk[0]}" val="${tk[*]:1}"
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            result+="entry${entry}.group ${group}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.key ${key}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.value ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/pipe-table.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=78259411f54bc0f073c5cff8668d7b55c5a1c896937f55ca176779d3ec38bd18===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: pipe-table
## Description: GitHub-flavored markdown tables (| a | b | with a |---|---| rule) Aje28094Aj BenchmarkDotNet, doc-gen CLIs
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 33
## Sample: samples/pipe-table/basic.txt

# Markdown pipe tables Aje28094Aj the format many tools print (BenchmarkDotNet, glow,
# `column`-style doc generators, GitHub rendering):
#
#   | Method     | Mean      | Allocated |
#   |----------- |----------:|----------:|
#   | ParseSmall |  14.42 us |     512 B |
#   | ParseLarge | 448.21 us |   10248 B |
#
# Rows are wrapped in leading/trailing `Aje29482Aj`... no Aje28094Aj leading/trailing `|`, with a
# separator rule of `-`/`:`/`|`/space only. This is a distinct dialect from
# psql-table (`a | b` with a `---+---` rule and NO outer pipes): a pipe-table
# row is bracketed by `|` and its rule carries no `+` joints. We drop the rule,
# take the first row as the header, and emit one record per data row.

# A rule row: trimmed, made only of |, -, :, and spaces, and contains a '-'.
_pt_is_rule () {
    local l="$1"
    l="${l#"${l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; l="${l%"${l##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    [[ "$l" == *-* ]] || return 1
    local s="$l"; s="${s//|/}"; s="${s//-/}"; s="${s//:/}"; s="${s// /}"
    [[ -z "$s" ]]
}

# A table row: trimmed, starts and ends with '|', and has >=2 pipes (>=1 cell).
_pt_is_row () {
    local l="$1"
    l="${l#"${l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; l="${l%"${l##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    [[ "$l" == "|"*"|" ]] || return 1
    local rest="${l#|}"; [[ "$rest" == *"|"* ]]
}

_pt_trim () { local v="$1"; v="${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"; _PT_TRIM="$v"; }

# --- bare dialect: `a | b | c` rows with NO outer pipes and NO rule row ------
#
#   name | pattern | action
#   http | ^GET\|POST$ | allow
#
# A second pipe dialect many CLIs print: cells joined by ' | ' with no border
# pipes and no separator rule, where in-cell bars are protected by a backslash
# (`\|`) or double quotes (`"a|b"`). Detection is deliberately strict Aje28094Aj this
# shape is one stray '|' away from prose Aje28094Aj see _pt_bare_shape.

# Split a bare row into _PT_CELLS: '|' separates at top level; '\|' is a literal
# bar (escape dropped); a double-quoted span protects everything inside it
# (quotes kept Aje28094Aj they are cell content, stripping is the melt's call).
_pt_split_bare () {
    local row="$1"
    local cell="" i c inq=0 n=${#row}
    _PT_CELLS=()
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${row:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$c" == '\' && "${row:$((i + 1)):1}" == '|' ]]; then
            cell+='|'; i=$((i + 1))
        elif [[ "$c" == '"' ]]; then
            inq=$((1 - inq)); cell+='"'
        elif [[ "$c" == '|' && $inq -eq 0 ]]; then
            _pt_trim "$cell"; _PT_CELLS+=("$_PT_TRIM"); cell=""
        else
            cell+="$c"
        fi
    done
    _pt_trim "$cell"; _PT_CELLS+=("$_PT_TRIM")
}

# Is this text a bare pipe table? Yes only when EVERY non-blank line: does not
# start or end with '|' (that's the markdown/box dialects' territory), contains
# no `---+---` rule (psql-table's anchor), and splits (escape/quote-aware) into
# the SAME >=2 top-level cell count Aje28094Aj across >=3 lines. Sets _PT_BARE_COLS.
_pt_bare_shape () {
    local text="$1" _line lines=0 want=-1 _c
    _PT_BARE_COLS=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "${_line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _pt_trim "$_line"; _line="$_PT_TRIM"
        [[ "$_line" == "|"* || "$_line" == *"|" ]] && return 1
        [[ "$_line" == *"---+---"* ]] && return 1
        _pt_split_bare "$_line"
        [[ ${#_PT_CELLS[@]} -lt 2 ]] && return 1
        # A trimmed cell with an INTERNAL run of 2+ spaces isn't a table cell Aje28094Aj
        # it's a TUI gauge line (`CPU     45.2%  |####...|  user: Aje280a6Aj`) whose bars
        # merely look like pipes. Real bare-table cells are compact.
        for _c in "${_PT_CELLS[@]}"; do [[ "$_c" =~ [\ ]{2,} ]] && return 1; done
        if [[ $want -lt 0 ]]; then want=${#_PT_CELLS[@]}
        elif [[ ${#_PT_CELLS[@]} -ne $want ]]; then return 1; fi
        lines=$((lines + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $lines -ge 3 ]] || return 1
    _PT_BARE_COLS=$want
    return 0
}

# Split a `| a | b |` row into _PT_CELLS (inner cells, trimmed).
_pt_split () {
    local row="$1"
    _pt_trim "$row"; row="$_PT_TRIM"
    row="${row#|}"; row="${row%|}"
    _PT_CELLS=()
    local rest="$row" cell
    while [[ "$rest" == *"|"* ]]; do
        cell="${rest%%|*}"; rest="${rest#*|}"
        _pt_trim "$cell"; _PT_CELLS+=("$_PT_TRIM")
    done
    _pt_trim "$rest"; _PT_CELLS+=("$_PT_TRIM")
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="markdown pipe table (| a | b | rows + |---| rule)"
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local _line _saw_rule=0 _saw_row=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "${_line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if _pt_is_rule "$_line" && [[ "$_line" == *"|"* ]]; then _saw_rule=1
        elif _pt_is_row "$_line"; then _saw_row=1; fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $_saw_rule -eq 1 && $_saw_row -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    # No markdown rule Aje28094Aj try the bare ` a | b | c ` dialect (strict shape check).
    if _pt_bare_shape "$text"; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="bare pipe table (a | b rows, uniform cells, no rule)"
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Extract a bare pipe table: first line is the header Aje28094Aj unless one of its
# cells is digit-leading (`CPU1 Temp | 42 degrees C | ok`: a headerless sensor
# list where every line is data), in which case synthesize A,B,CAje280a6Aj names.
_pt_extract_bare () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _line
    local col_names=() have_header=0 _c name i val first=1
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "${_line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _pt_trim "$_line"; _line="$_PT_TRIM"
        _pt_split_bare "$_line"
        if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then
            first=0
            local _hl=0
            for _c in "${_PT_CELLS[@]}"; do [[ "$_c" == [0-9]* ]] && { _hl=1; break; }; done
            if [[ $_hl -eq 1 ]]; then
                for ((i = 0; i < ${#_PT_CELLS[@]}; i++)); do
                    col_names+=("$(_col_letter $((i + 1)))")
                done
                have_header=1
                # fall through: this first line is DATA, emit it below
            fi
        fi
        if [[ $have_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            for _c in "${_PT_CELLS[@]}"; do
                name="$_c"; name="${name//./}"; name="${name// /_}"
                while [[ "$name" == *__* ]]; do name="${name//__/_}"; done
                name="${name#_}"; name="${name%_}"
                [[ -z "$name" ]] && name="$(_col_letter $((${#col_names[@]} + 1)))"
                col_names+=("$name")
            done
            have_header=1; continue
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#col_names[@]}; i++)); do
            val="${_PT_CELLS[$i]:-}"
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${col_names[$i]} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _line
    # Which dialect won detection? A markdown table always carries a rule row;
    # re-check here (detect's globals don't survive into this subshell).
    local _has_rule=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _pt_is_rule "$_line" && [[ "$_line" == *"|"* ]] && { _has_rule=1; break; }
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $_has_rule -eq 0 ]]; then
        _pt_extract_bare "$text"
        return
    fi
    # modal cell count across non-rule pipe rows
    local counts=()
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _pt_is_row "$_line" || continue
        _pt_is_rule "$_line" && continue
        _pt_split "$_line"; counts+=("${#_PT_CELLS[@]}")
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ ${#counts[@]} -lt 2 ]] && return
    local modal=0 best=0 a b k
    for a in "${counts[@]}"; do
        k=0; for b in "${counts[@]}"; do [[ "$b" -eq "$a" ]] && k=$((k + 1)); done
        [[ $k -gt $best ]] && { best=$k; modal=$a; }
    done
    [[ $modal -lt 1 ]] && return

    local col_names=() num_cols=0 have_header=0 _c name i val
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _pt_is_row "$_line" || continue
        _pt_is_rule "$_line" && continue
        _pt_split "$_line"
        [[ ${#_PT_CELLS[@]} -ne $modal ]] && continue
        if [[ $have_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            for _c in "${_PT_CELLS[@]}"; do
                name="$_c"; name="${name//./}"; name="${name// /_}"
                while [[ "$name" == *__* ]]; do name="${name//__/_}"; done
                name="${name#_}"; name="${name%_}"
                [[ -z "$name" ]] && name="$(_col_letter $((${#col_names[@]} + 1)))"
                col_names+=("$name")
            done
            num_cols=${#col_names[@]}; have_header=1; continue
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i = 0; i < num_cols; i++)); do
            val="${_PT_CELLS[$i]}"; _pt_trim "$val"; val="$_PT_TRIM"
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${col_names[$i]} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/psql-table.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=ba30d3df5db25ebf8d079dca0b7632609b3082f21e934c8ed82f5dbbc0c2b538===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: psql-table
## Description: Pipe-delimited box tables with a ---+--- separator (psql, mysql \G-less output)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 35
## Sample: samples/psql-table/basic.txt

# Is a line a box-table separator? Only '-'/'=', '+', and spaces, with at least
# one '+' joint and a run of the rule char -- e.g. "----+----+----",
# "+----+----+", or airflow's equals rule "====+====+====".
_psql_is_separator () {
    local l="$1"
    [[ "$l" == *"+"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$l" =~ ^[-=+\ ]+$ ]] || return 1
    [[ "$l" == *"---"* || "$l" == *"==="* ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    # Walk lines keeping the previous line so we can confirm the row above the
    # separator carries a '|' column delimiter, and that at least one row below
    # does too. Only then is this a genuine pipe box table.
    local _prev="" _line _sep_hdr="" _saw_data=0 _hit_sep=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        if [[ $_hit_sep -eq 0 ]]; then
            if _psql_is_separator "$_line"; then
                [[ "$_prev" == *"|"* ]] || { _prev="$_line"; continue; }
                _hit_sep=1
            fi
        else
            [[ "$_line" == *"|"* ]] && { _saw_data=1; break; }
        fi
        _prev="$_line"
    done <<< "$text"

    if [[ $_hit_sep -eq 1 && $_saw_data -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Trim leading/trailing spaces from $1 -> _PSQL_TRIM
_psql_trim () {
    local v="$1"
    while [[ "$v" == " "* ]]; do v="${v# }"; done
    while [[ "$v" == *" " ]]; do v="${v% }"; done
    _PSQL_TRIM="$v"
}

# Split a box-table row into the global array _PSQL_CELLS (trimmed). Strips one
# outer '|' border on each side first, so `| a | b |` (mysql / aws --output table)
# and `a | b` (psql) both yield the same inner cells.
_psql_split () {
    local row="$1"
    _psql_trim "$row"; row="$_PSQL_TRIM"
    # Strip outer '|' borders only for a FULL box row (both ends piped, e.g.
    # `| a | b |` from mysql / aws --output table). A psql row has no leading '|',
    # so its trailing '|' denotes a genuine empty last column and must be kept.
    local _lead=0
    [[ "$row" == "|"* ]] && { row="${row#|}"; _lead=1; }
    [[ $_lead -eq 1 && "$row" == *"|" ]] && row="${row%|}"
    # Split on '|' EXCEPT a backslash-escaped '\|' Aje28094Aj SQL result cells legitimately
    # contain literal bars (regex alternations, `s1 || s2` concat expressions) and
    # psql-style renderers escape them as '\|'. A naive split shreds such a row
    # into extra cells, pushing it off the modal width so it's silently DROPPED.
    # The escape is table-encoding, so the emitted cell carries the bare '|'.
    _PSQL_CELLS=()
    local cell="" i c n=${#row}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${row:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$c" == '\' && "${row:$((i + 1)):1}" == '|' ]]; then
            cell+='|'; i=$((i + 1))
        elif [[ "$c" == '|' ]]; then
            _psql_trim "$cell"; _PSQL_CELLS+=("$_PSQL_TRIM"); cell=""
        else
            cell+="$c"
        fi
    done
    _psql_trim "$cell"
    _PSQL_CELLS+=("$_PSQL_TRIM")
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _line

    # Collect every '|'-bearing, non-separator row's cell count. A box table's
    # data/header rows share a modal cell count; a single-cell title banner
    # (`aws --output table`'s "DescribeInstances") and the `(N rows)` footer /
    # blanks / rules fall outside it and are dropped.
    local counts=() _n
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ "$_line" == *"|"* ]] || continue
        _psql_is_separator "$_line" && continue
        _psql_split "$_line"
        counts+=("${#_PSQL_CELLS[@]}")
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ ${#counts[@]} -lt 2 ]] && return

    local modal=0 best=0 a b k
    for a in "${counts[@]}"; do
        k=0; for b in "${counts[@]}"; do [[ "$b" -eq "$a" ]] && k=$((k + 1)); done
        [[ $k -gt $best ]] && { best=$k; modal=$a; }
    done
    [[ $modal -lt 1 ]] && return

    # First modal-width row is the header; the rest (modal width, non-continuation)
    # are data. A psql wrapped-cell continuation line has an empty first cell.
    local col_names=() num_cols=0 have_header=0 _c name i val
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ "$_line" == *"|"* ]] || continue
        _psql_is_separator "$_line" && continue
        _psql_split "$_line"
        [[ ${#_PSQL_CELLS[@]} -ne $modal ]] && continue    # skip title/odd rows

        if [[ $have_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            for _c in "${_PSQL_CELLS[@]}"; do
                name="$_c"; name="${name//./}"; name="${name// /_}"
                [[ -z "$name" ]] && name="$(_col_letter $((${#col_names[@]} + 1)))"
                col_names+=("$name")
            done
            num_cols=${#col_names[@]}
            have_header=1
            continue
        fi

        [[ -z "${_PSQL_CELLS[0]}" ]] && continue           # psql continuation row
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i = 0; i < num_cols; i++)); do
            val="${_PSQL_CELLS[$i]}"
            _psql_trim "$val"; val="$_PSQL_TRIM"
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${col_names[$i]} ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/quoted-fields.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=dd1cfdbb140b8e49275491f5d45341b05823c3edda188de2a8777fe591ba7a4d===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: quoted-fields
## Description: Space-delimited records with quoted/bracketed field grouping (access logs, quoted crontabs, audit logs)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/quoted-fields/basic.txt

# The access-log family Aje28094Aj space-separated positional fields where "Aje280a6Aj", 'Aje280a6Aj' and
# [Aje280a6Aj] group a multi-word value into ONE field:
#
#   10.0.0.1 - - [11/Jul/2026:09:15:42 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 5120 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (X11) Gecko"
#   2026-07-11 09:15:42 INFO  "started worker, id=3" pool=default
#   0 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/backup --dst "s3://bucket/path" --note "nightly, full"
#
# No header Aje28094Aj rows are positional, so columns are synthesised A,B,CAje280a6Aj. A grouping
# character is STRUCTURAL only at token start (start of line or after
# whitespace): `msg="retry scheduled"` keeps its mid-token quote literal, so
# logfmt lines and quoted CSV (quotes after commas) never form spans and stay
# with their own parsers. Detection requires EVERY line to carry at least one
# grouped span and a near-constant field count Aje28094Aj prose with an occasional quote
# varies too much to qualify.

# Split one line into _QF_FIELDS: whitespace-delimited tokens where a token
# BEGINNING with " ' or [ runs to its matching closer (spaces included), then to
# the next whitespace. _QF_QSPANS counts only the QUOTE-grouped tokens Aje28094Aj the
# detection signature. Brackets group (a [timestamp +0000] stays one field) but
# don't qualify a line by themselves, or every bracket-tag log and aligned table
# with a [SWAP]-style cell would match.
_strat_qf_split () {
    local line="$1"
    local i c field="" close="" len=${#line}
    _QF_FIELDS=()
    _QF_QSPANS=0
    i=0
    while [[ $i -lt $len ]]; do
        c="${line:$i:1}"
        # skip inter-field whitespace
        if [[ "$c" == " " || "$c" == $'\t' ]]; then i=$((i+1)); continue; fi
        field=""
        # grouped token?
        case "$c" in
            '"') close='"'; _QF_QSPANS=$((_QF_QSPANS + 1)) ;;
            "'") close="'"; _QF_QSPANS=$((_QF_QSPANS + 1)) ;;
            '[') close=']' ;;
            *)   close="" ;;
        esac
        if [[ -n "$close" ]]; then
            i=$((i+1))
            while [[ $i -lt $len ]]; do
                c="${line:$i:1}"
                [[ "$c" == "$close" ]] && { i=$((i+1)); break; }
                field+="$c"; i=$((i+1))
            done
        fi
        # continue the token to the next whitespace (covers [x]y and plain tokens)
        while [[ $i -lt $len ]]; do
            c="${line:$i:1}"
            [[ "$c" == " " || "$c" == $'\t' ]] && break
            field+="$c"; i=$((i+1))
        done
        _QF_FIELDS+=("$field")
    done
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local _line n=0 minf=0 maxf=0 f
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "${_line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        _strat_qf_split "$_line"
        f=${#_QF_FIELDS[@]}
        # DNS resource records (`name 300 IN TXT "v=spf1 Aje280a6Aj"`, space- or
        # tab-separated) carry quoted strings too Aje28094Aj they belong to dns-records.
        # Token pair (IN, <rr-type>) anywhere in the line is the tell.
        local _qi
        for ((_qi = 0; _qi + 1 < f; _qi++)); do
            if [[ "${_QF_FIELDS[$_qi]}" == "IN" ]]; then
                case "${_QF_FIELDS[$((_qi + 1))]}" in
                    A|AAAA|TXT|MX|CNAME|NS|SOA|PTR|SRV|CAA|DS|DNSKEY|RRSIG|NSEC) return 1 ;;
                esac
            fi
        done
        # every line: at least one QUOTE-grouped span and enough fields to be a
        # positional record (4-field lines like amixer's `control 'Master',0`
        # are too short to be this shape)
        [[ $_QF_QSPANS -ge 1 && $f -ge 5 ]] || return 1
        if [[ $n -eq 1 ]]; then minf=$f; maxf=$f
        else
            [[ $f -lt $minf ]] && minf=$f
            [[ $f -gt $maxf ]] && maxf=$f
        fi
        [[ $n -ge 30 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $n -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    # near-constant field count (ragged tails allowed, prose is far wider)
    [[ $((maxf - minf)) -le 2 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=78
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="space-delimited records, quoted/bracketed fields, constant field count"
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _line i val
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "${_line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _strat_qf_split "$_line"
        [[ ${#_QF_FIELDS[@]} -lt 1 ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#_QF_FIELDS[@]}; i++)); do
            val="${_QF_FIELDS[$i]}"
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.$(_col_letter $((i + 1))) ${val}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
