===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/semicolon-values.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=5b38390e33d79163978fc58f96370b574887d3139523c063f370bfb5710face1===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: semicolon-values
## Description: Semicolon-delimited records (fio --output-format=terse, European-locale CSV)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 13
## Sample: samples/semicolon-values/basic.txt

# Records delimited by `;` rather than `,`:
#
#   3;fio-3.36;randread;0;0;28221440;482104;123001;60001;...   (fio terse)
#   name;value;unit                                            (some exporters)
#
# fio's terse output is one `;`-delimited line of ~130 positional fields; other
# tools (European-locale CSV, some `--format` exporters) use `;` the way csv
# uses `,`. Mirrors the csv strategy: a consistent semicolon count across every
# non-blank line Aje28094Aj counted QUOTE-AWARE (a `;` inside "Aje280a6Aj" is data, the
# European-CSV case: `Schraube;"1.234,56";"12; nachbestellen"`). Two bands:
#   * dense (top-level count >=4, Ajc2b1Aj1 across lines) Aje28094Aj fio terse and friends;
#   * low (2-3) Aje28094Aj accepted only when EVERY line has the IDENTICAL top-level
#     count and there are >=2 lines, so prose with stray semicolons
#     ("o - Other; r - Repeater; Aje280a6Aj", which varies line to line) and a lone
#     legend line never qualify.
# If the first row is all-numeric there is no header (fio terse) Aje28094Aj synthesise
# A,B,CAje280a6Aj and keep it; otherwise the first row names the columns.

# Split one line on TOP-LEVEL semicolons into _SSV_CELLS (quote-aware: a quote
# is structural only at field start; "" inside a quoted field is an escaped
# quote; structural quotes are consumed, leftover quotes are data). Also sets
# _SSV_N to the top-level separator count.
_strat_ssv_split () {
    local line="$1"
    local i c field="" inq=0 atstart=1 len=${#line}
    _SSV_CELLS=(); _SSV_N=0
    i=0
    while [[ $i -lt $len ]]; do
        c="${line:$i:1}"
        if [[ $inq -eq 1 ]]; then
            if [[ "$c" == '"' ]]; then
                if [[ "${line:$((i+1)):1}" == '"' ]]; then field+='"'; i=$((i+2)); continue; fi
                inq=0; i=$((i+1)); continue
            fi
            field+="$c"; i=$((i+1)); continue
        fi
        if [[ "$c" == '"' && $atstart -eq 1 ]]; then inq=1; atstart=0; i=$((i+1)); continue; fi
        if [[ "$c" == ';' ]]; then
            _SSV_CELLS+=("$field"); _SSV_N=$((_SSV_N + 1))
            field=""; atstart=1; i=$((i+1)); continue
        fi
        [[ "$c" != " " && "$c" != $'\t' ]] && atstart=0
        field+="$c"; i=$((i+1))
    done
    _SSV_CELLS+=("$field")
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="consistent semicolon count across lines (quote-aware)"
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1

    local nonblank=0 first_sc=0 dense=1 _l sc
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        _strat_ssv_split "$_l"; sc=$_SSV_N
        [[ $sc -lt 2 ]] && return 1
        if [[ $nonblank -gt 1 ]]; then
            if [[ $first_sc -ge 4 && $sc -ge 4 ]]; then
                local d=$(( first_sc - sc )); [[ ${d#-} -le 1 ]] || return 1
            else
                [[ $sc -eq $first_sc ]] || return 1   # low band: exact match only
            fi
        else
            first_sc=$sc
        fi
        [[ $sc -lt 4 ]] && dense=0
        [[ $nonblank -ge 40 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $nonblank -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    # a single low-density line is not enough signal (a lone prose line with
    # two semicolons); the dense band keeps single-line acceptance (fio terse)
    [[ $dense -eq 0 && $nonblank -lt 2 ]] && return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=84
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Field names: the first row if it carries non-numeric labels, else synthetic.
    local header="" _nb=0
    local _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _nb=$((_nb + 1)); [[ -z "$header" ]] && header="$_l"
    done <<< "$text"

    local hcells; _strat_ssv_split "$header"; hcells=("${_SSV_CELLS[@]}")
    # A single line is always one record (no header can exist without data); a
    # multi-line block is headerless only when its first row is all-numeric.
    local _headerless=1 _hc
    if [[ $_nb -gt 1 ]]; then
        for _hc in "${hcells[@]}"; do
            _hc="${_hc#"${_hc%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; _hc="${_hc%"${_hc##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            [[ -z "$_hc" || "$_hc" =~ ^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?%?$ ]] || { _headerless=0; break; }
        done
    fi

    local headers=() _k
    if [[ $_headerless -eq 1 ]]; then
        for ((_k=1; _k<=${#hcells[@]}; _k++)); do headers+=("$(_col_letter "$_k")"); done
    else
        for _hc in "${hcells[@]}"; do
            _hc="${_hc#"${_hc%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; _hc="${_hc%"${_hc##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            _hc="${_hc// /_}"; _hc="${_hc//./_}"; _hc="${_hc#_}"; _hc="${_hc%_}"
            [[ -z "$_hc" ]] && _hc="$(_col_letter $((${#headers[@]} + 1)))"
            headers+=("$_hc")
        done
    fi

    local result="" rec=0 row=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        row=$((row + 1))
        [[ $row -eq 1 && $_headerless -eq 0 ]] && continue
        local values; _strat_ssv_split "$line"; values=("${_SSV_CELLS[@]}")
        rec=$((rec + 1))
        local j v name
        for ((j=0; j<${#headers[@]}; j++)); do
            name="${headers[$j]}"; v="${values[$j]:-}"
            v="${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            [[ -z "$name" || -z "$v" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${rec}.${name} ${v}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $rec -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${rec}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/syslog.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=3a05de586e2227a94c64c6298208eb9659d2249108adc0bb25af05d4449d239c===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: syslog
## Description: Extract fields from BSD/RFC 3164 syslog format log lines
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/syslog/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    # A syslog CAPTURE is syslog lines throughout Aje28094Aj require a majority of
    # non-blank lines to open with the BSD timestamp (Mon DD HH:MM:SS).
    # A status block that merely EMBEDS a few journal lines (systemctl
    # status's log tail) is not a syslog capture and belongs to other
    # parsers.
    local line total=0 hits=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        total=$((total + 1))
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Z][a-z]{2}\ [\ 0-9]{2}\ [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\  ]] && hits=$((hits + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $total -gt 0 && $((hits * 100 / total)) -ge 50 ]]
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local line_num=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Only process lines matching syslog format
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Z][a-z]{2}\ [\ 0-9]{2}\ [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\  ]] || continue

        line_num=$((line_num + 1))
        local prefix="line${line_num}"

        # Extract timestamp (first 15 chars: "Mon DD HH:MM:SS")
        local timestamp
        timestamp=$(_strat_syslog_get_timestamp "$line")
        result+="${prefix}.timestamp ${timestamp}"$'\n'

        # Extract hostname (word after timestamp)
        read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
        local hostname="${_arr[3]}"
        result+="${prefix}.hostname ${hostname}"$'\n'

        # Extract process and PID
        local process_part="${_arr[4]}"
        local process pid
        process="${process_part%%[*}"
        process="${process%:}"
        # Extract PID from brackets if present
        pid=""
        if [[ "$process_part" == *"["*"]"* ]]; then
            pid="${process_part#*[}"
            pid="${pid%%]*}"
        fi
        result+="${prefix}.process ${process}"$'\n'
        if [[ -n "$pid" ]]; then
            result+="${prefix}.pid ${pid}"$'\n'
        fi

        # Extract message (everything after process/pid field)
        local message
        message=$(_strat_syslog_get_message "$line")
        if [[ -n "$message" ]]; then
            result+="${prefix}.message ${message}"$'\n'
        fi

    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

_strat_syslog_get_timestamp () {
    local line="$1"
    # Extract "Mon DD HH:MM:SS" and replace spaces/colons with underscores
    read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
    local ts="${_arr[0]}_${_arr[1]}_${_arr[2]}"
    # Replace colons with underscores in timestamp
    ts="${ts//:/_}"
    echo "$ts"
}

_strat_syslog_get_message () {
    local line="$1"
    # Message is everything after the 5th field's colon/bracket
    # Remove timestamp (3 fields), hostname (1 field), process[pid]: (1 field)
    read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
    # Reconstruct message from field 5 onwards
    local msg=""
    local i
    for ((i=5; i<${#_arr[@]}; i++)); do
        if [[ -z "$msg" ]]; then
            msg="${_arr[$i]}"
        else
            msg="${msg} ${_arr[$i]}"
        fi
    done
    # Also check if field 4 has trailing content after ":"
    local field4="${_arr[4]}"
    if [[ "$field4" == *":" ]]; then
        # Colon is at end, message starts at field 5 (already handled)
        :
    elif [[ "$field4" == *"]:" ]]; then
        # PID bracket + colon at end, message starts at field 5 (already handled)
        :
    fi
    echo "$msg"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/text-lines.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=d440ef4fb6319f8a2689efa174dac0dbd6f31e414e846835d81423f63cd0e67b===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: text-lines
## Description: Absolute last resort Aje28094Aj each non-blank line becomes a one-column record (whole line)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 97
## Sample: samples/text-lines/basic.txt

# The final fallback, below even line-records (p96). When no columnar structure
# exists Aje28094Aj ragged, single-token-varying text like `strings` output or a plain
# list Aje28094Aj the honest tidy shape is one row per line, a single column holding the
# whole line. Runs only when everything more specific has declined.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    # Structured markup is owned by real parsers; never wrap it line-by-line.
    # A document is markup when it carries quoted-key `":` syntax, or when it
    # OPENS with a brace/bracket and CLOSES with the matching kind (a JSON /
    # array document). A `{` mid-line (a UUID in `vboxmanage list vms`, an
    # exabgp block opener) or a leading `[INFO]` tag is just text.
    [[ "$text" == *'":'* ]] && return 1

    local nb=0 first="" last="" _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        [[ $nb -eq 1 ]] && first="$_l"
        last="$_l"
        [[ $nb -ge 200 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ "$first" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[\{\[] ]]; then
        local _lt="${last%"${last##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ "$_lt" == *'}' || "$_lt" == *']' || "$_lt" == *','  ]] && return 1
    fi

    [[ $nb -ge 1 ]] || return 1

    # A lone single line is only a record when it reads like a status, not
    # prose: a single bare token (`getenforce`'s "Enforcing") or a short
    # phrase of <=3 tokens with no sentence-ending period ("gamemode is
    # active", "Signature Verified"). Anything longer ("no extractable
    # content here") is prose with no tabular structure and falls through
    # to nothing rather than a spurious 1-cell row.
    if [[ $nb -eq 1 ]]; then
        local trimmed="${first#"${first%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        trimmed="${trimmed%"${trimmed##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        local _tk; _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "$trimmed"
        [[ ${#_tk[@]} -gt 3 || "$trimmed" == *. ]] && return 1
    fi

    # Otherwise: >=2 non-blank lines Aje28094Aj one row per line, single column. Runs only
    # when every more-specific parser (incl. line-records) has declined.
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=55
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        # Trim surrounding whitespace but keep the line's own spaces.
        local v="$_l"
        v="${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$v" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${v}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/two-col-gap.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=ab3b0d6fd02296e9bfee694e09301ab547f929df9881e98853f6f03f54e699ff===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: two-col-gap
## Description: Two-column tables split by a 2+-space gap where the last column is free text
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 54
## Sample: samples/two-col-gap/basic.txt

# The "2-col table, free-text last column" shape (a long-documented gap class):
#
#   unit                 execstart
#   nginx.service        /usr/sbin/nginx -g 'daemon off; master_process on;'
#   app.service          /opt/app --flags "--a=1 --b=2,3"
#
# A single-token key column, a run of >=2 spaces, then a value column that
# freely contains SINGLE spaces (shell commands, JSON arrays, descriptions).
# aligned-columns can't take these: the value's word count varies per row, so
# no consistent grid exists Aje28094Aj it either declines (falling to line-records,
# which welds key and value into one cell) or grabs the first data row as a
# fake header. Splitting each line on its FIRST 2+-space run is exact here.
#
# Detection is deliberately strict Aje28094Aj every non-blank line must fit, and at
# least one value must actually contain a space (a plain 2-col table without
# spacey values stays with aligned-columns, which already handles it):
#   - >=3 non-blank lines, all UNINDENTED
#   - every line: single-token first cell, a 2+-space gap, non-empty rest
#   - no tabs (tsv territory), first cells not colon-labels (colons territory)

# Split $1 on its FIRST run of >=2 spaces -> _TCG_KEY / _TCG_VAL (val trimmed).
_tcg_split () {
    local line="$1"
    _TCG_KEY=""; _TCG_VAL=""
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([^[:space:]]+)[\ ]{2,}(.+)$ ]] || return 1
    _TCG_KEY="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    _TCG_VAL="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    _TCG_VAL="${_TCG_VAL%"${_TCG_VAL##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="2-col gap table (single-token key, free-text value)"
    local _l lines=0 spacey=0 colonish=0 vcounts=()
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_l" == [' 	']* ]] && return 1          # indented => not this shape
        [[ "$_l" == *'	'* ]] && return 1            # tabs => tsv territory
        _tcg_split "$_l" || return 1
        # The value must be ONE free-text column: a further 2+-space run inside
        # it means this is really a >=3-column aligned grid (zfs list, velero
        # get, any wide table) Aje28094Aj aligned-columns' shape, never ours.
        [[ "$_TCG_VAL" =~ [\ ]{2,} ]] && return 1
        lines=$((lines + 1))
        # Free-text evidence must come from a DATA row (line >=2) Aje28094Aj a 2-word
        # HEADER cell (`VOLUME NAME`, `CREATED AT`) over single-token values is
        # a plain 2-col table that aligned-columns already tidies perfectly.
        [[ $lines -ge 2 && "$_TCG_VAL" == *" "* ]] && spacey=$((spacey + 1))
        [[ "$_TCG_KEY" == *: ]] && colonish=$((colonish + 1))
        # Track each DATA value's word count Aje28094Aj a value column whose counts are
        # (near-)uniform at >=2 tokens (`a1b2c3d [main]` on every git-worktree
        # row, rpm -V's `c /etc/...`) is a single-space-aligned GRID whose words
        # are really separate columns; welding them would LOSE structure. Free
        # text varies word to word; grids don't.
        if [[ $lines -ge 2 ]]; then
            local _vt; _vt=(); read -ra _vt <<< "$_TCG_VAL"
            vcounts+=("${#_vt[@]}")
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $lines -ge 3 ]] || return 1
    # Modal-share grid test: if one >=2-token count covers >=2/3 of the data
    # rows, this is a grid with at most a ragged straggler (git-worktree-list's
    # `(detached HEAD)` row among `sha [branch]` rows) Aje28094Aj decline. Genuinely
    # free-text values (commands, JSON arrays) spread their counts wider, and
    # a modal count of 1 (mostly single-token values with a few multi-word
    # stragglers, getent-services style) is not a grid signal at all.
    if [[ ${#vcounts[@]} -ge 3 ]]; then
        local _a _b _k modal=0 best=0
        for _a in "${vcounts[@]}"; do
            _k=0; for _b in "${vcounts[@]}"; do [[ "$_b" -eq "$_a" ]] && _k=$((_k + 1)); done
            [[ $_k -gt $best ]] && { best=$_k; modal=$_a; }
        done
        [[ $modal -ge 2 && $((best * 100 / ${#vcounts[@]})) -ge 66 ]] && return 1
        # A multi-token ROW-1 value whose word count EQUALS the modal data count
        # is a single-space-aligned grid whose header names line up over the
        # value words (lsblk's `NAME  SIZE TYPE MOUNTPOINT` over `500G disk Aje280a6Aj`)
        # Aje28094Aj that's a real >=3-column table, aligned-columns' to keep.
        if [[ $modal -ge 2 ]]; then
            local _h1; _h1=""
            while IFS= read -r _l; do
                [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
                _h1="$_l"; break
            done <<< "$text"
            if _tcg_split "$_h1"; then
                local _ht; _ht=(); read -ra _ht <<< "$_TCG_VAL"
                [[ ${#_ht[@]} -eq $modal ]] && return 1
            fi
        fi
    fi
    # At least one free-text DATA value Aje28094Aj otherwise it's a plain 2-col grid
    # that aligned-columns already tidies; don't steal those.
    [[ $spacey -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    # Majority colon-suffixed keys is a `Label: value` block Aje28094Aj colons' shape.
    [[ $((colonish * 2)) -ge $lines ]] && return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=78
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _l
    # Header: row 1 when BOTH its cells are single tokens AND neither is
    # digit-leading Aje28094Aj a `127.0.0.1  localhost` or `ssh  22/tcp` first row is
    # DATA (getent hosts/services style headerless lists); otherwise
    # synthesize A/B.
    local k1="" v1="" have=0 hk="A" hv="B" first=1
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _tcg_split "$_l" || continue
        if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then
            first=0
            if [[ "$_TCG_VAL" != *" "* && "$_TCG_KEY" != [0-9]* && "$_TCG_VAL" != [0-9]* ]]; then
                hk="${_TCG_KEY//./_}"; hv="${_TCG_VAL//./_}"
                continue
            fi
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.${hk} ${_TCG_KEY}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.${hv} ${_TCG_VAL}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/unspaced-colon-kv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=97f52d0f51cae2190905c7438a5563355fcaa7e9e639c76202e8872dbacb18c2===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: unspaced-colon-kv
## Description: `Label:value` lines where the colon is a delimiter with no space after it (HammerDB TPC-C, Vuser logs) -> label/value rows
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 52
## Sample: samples/unspaced-colon-kv/basic.txt

# The `colons` parser (priority 60) requires whitespace AFTER the colon, because
# that is what tells a `key: value` pair apart from a colon living inside a value
# (`10:15:42`). Some tools never print that space:
#
#   TEST RESULT : System achieved 482100 NOPM from 1204882 TPM
#   Vuser 1:RAMPUP complete
#   Vuser 1:Test complete, Taking end AWR snapshot.
#
# Those fall through to the blob parser and land in one column, which is exactly
# the "the colons are delimiters, not values" complaint. This strategy owns that
# form: split each line at its FIRST colon into `label` and `value`.
#
# Labels repeat (`Vuser 1` three times above), so the output is records Aje28094Aj a real
# two-column table Aje28094Aj not a flat key/value map that would collapse them.
#
# Kept off everything else by gates that all must hold. Each one is here because
# it was caught stealing a tool that a better parser already owned:
#   * every non-blank line splits into a plausible label + non-empty value;
#   * labels start with a letter (so `10:15:42` and `2024-01-01T00:00:00` are
#     out, their "label" starting with a digit) and stay short;
#   * no line carries a `d:dd` clock pair or `://`, so timestamps and URLs are
#     out even when a letter leads the line;
#   * no line is indented Aje28094Aj YAML and nested config blocks are out;
#   * the first token never packs 3+ colons Aje28094Aj passwd/group records stay with
#     colon-fields (priority 48, which runs first anyway);
#   * every line contains whitespace SOMEWHERE. A whitespace-free line is one
#     identifier that happens to hold a colon, not a pair Aje28094Aj `redis-cli KEYS`
#     (`user:1001`), `rg --count` (`src/main.rs:12`), `jack_lsp`
#     (`system:capture_1`), image refs (`registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9`);
#   * no line contains a 2+ space run Aje28094Aj that gap is column alignment, so
#     `lsblk` (`sda        8:0   500G`), `vcpkg list` and `haproxy show servers`
#     stay with the column parsers;
#   * no value starts with `digits:` Aje28094Aj that is `file:LINE:text` grep output;
#   * no value starts with a colon Aje28094Aj `::` is IPv6 (`prefix ::1/128`) or a Python
#     test path (`test_auth.py::test_login`), not a delimiter;
#   * a MAJORITY of lines have no space after the colon. One unspaced banner
#     over a spaced block is still a `colons` document Aje28094Aj `nvme smart-log` prints
#     `Smart Log for NVME device:nvme0` above twenty `critical_warning : 0` rows;
#   * at least two DISTINCT labels. One label repeated on every line is a
#     namespace prefix, not a key Aje28094Aj `vllm:num_requests_running 12`. This mirrors
#     the uniform-identifier guard colon-fields already carries.

# Split "$1" at its first colon -> _UCK_LABEL, _UCK_VALUE. Returns 1 if the line
# is not a usable label/value pair.
_uck_split () {
    local l="$1"
    [[ "$l" == *:* ]] || return 1
    # A pair always has whitespace somewhere; a bare `user:1001` identifier does not.
    [[ "$l" == *[[:space:]]* ]] || return 1
    # A 2+ space run ANYWHERE is column alignment: the colon belongs to an
    # identifier in column 1 and the real delimiter is the gap. Keeps `vcpkg
    # list` (`fmt:x64-linux    10.2.1  Formatting library`) and `haproxy show
    # servers` (`... 10.0.2.1:8080 UP  L7OK/200`) with the column parsers.
    [[ "$l" == *"  "* ]] && return 1
    local label="${l%%:*}" value="${l#*:}"
    # A second colon straight after the first is `::`, not a delimiter.
    [[ "$value" == :* ]] && return 1
    # `file:LINE:text` Aje28094Aj grep/compiler diagnostics, owned by their own parsers.
    [[ "$value" =~ ^[0-9]+: ]] && return 1
    # rtrim label (`TEST RESULT :` -> `TEST RESULT`), trim value both ends
    label="${label%"${label##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    [[ -n "$label" && -n "$value" ]] || return 1
    [[ ${#label} -le 40 ]] || return 1
    [[ "$label" == [A-Za-z]* ]] || return 1
    # Letters, digits, spaces and mild punctuation only Aje28094Aj a label, not prose.
    [[ -z "${label//[A-Za-z0-9 ._#\/-]/}" ]] || return 1
    _UCK_LABEL="$label"; _UCK_VALUE="$value"
    return 0
}

# Colons in the first whitespace token of "$1" -> _UCK_N.
_uck_first_colons () {
    local tok="${1#"${1%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    tok="${tok%%[[:space:]]*}"
    local nc="${tok//[^:]/}"
    _UCK_N=${#nc}
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *'{'* || "$text" == *'":'* ]] && return 1

    local line nb=0 tight=0 labels=""
    # A clock is 1-2 digits, a colon, then EXACTLY two more digits Aje28094Aj the trailing
    # `[^0-9]` matters: without it `Vuser 1:482100` reads as the time `1:48`.
    local _clock_re='(^|[^0-9:])[0-9][0-9]?:[0-9][0-9]([^0-9]|$)'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Indented -> YAML / nested config, not this.
        [[ "$line" == [[:space:]]* ]] && return 1
        [[ "$line" == *"://"* ]] && return 1
        [[ "$line" =~ $_clock_re ]] && return 1
        _uck_first_colons "$line"
        [[ $_UCK_N -ge 3 ]] && return 1
        _uck_split "$line" || return 1
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        # An unspaced colon is the whole point Aje28094Aj `Label:value`, not `Label: value`.
        [[ "${line#*:}" == [[:space:]]* ]] || tight=$((tight + 1))
        case "$labels" in
            *"|${_UCK_LABEL}|"*) ;;
            *) labels+="|${_UCK_LABEL}|" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $nb -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    # Majority unspaced, and more than one distinct label.
    [[ $(( tight * 100 / nb )) -ge 60 ]] || return 1
    local distinct="${labels//[^|]/}"
    [[ $(( ${#distinct} / 2 )) -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local line result="" entry=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _uck_split "$line" || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.label ${_UCK_LABEL}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.value ${_UCK_VALUE}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/delimited/vertical-line.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=fefa87d3db0af21fa56acb6348869de28cd90656dc9c3f504272a07b6eb060bc===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: vertical-line
## Description: Extract data from tables with separator lines (---, ===, etc.)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 45
## Sample: samples/vertical-line/benchmark.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=70
    # Apply if input contains a separator line (--- or === repeated)
    [[ "$text" =~ (^|$'\n')[-=]{3,} ]] || return 1

    # Decline a `label: value` key/value block that merely carries a `===`/`---`
    # banner (aureport --summary, `duplicity collection-status`). vertical-line
    # would split the banner's title line into positional columns and shred the
    # values; the `colons` parser tidies these to one field per label. Examine the
    # lines below the FIRST separator (the data region) Aje28094Aj if most are `label: value`,
    # defer.
    local seen_sep=0 nb=0 kv=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        if [[ $seen_sep -eq 0 ]]; then
            [[ "$_l" =~ ^[-=]{3,} ]] && seen_sep=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nb=$((nb + 1))
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z][^:]*:[[:space:]] ]] && kv=$((kv + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $nb -ge 2 && $(( kv * 100 / nb )) -ge 60 ]] && return 1

    # Audit-report shape (aureport): a `# col col Aje280a6Aj` header line adjacent to
    # a `===` rule. aligned-columns strips that chrome and reads the real
    # header; splitting on the rule here would shred it.
    local _prev="" _cur
    while IFS= read -r _cur; do
        if [[ "$_cur" == "# "* && "$_prev" =~ ^[-=]{3,} ]] || \
           [[ "$_cur" =~ ^[-=]{3,} && "$_prev" == "# "* ]]; then
            return 1
        fi
        _prev="$_cur"
    done <<< "$text"
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Find the separator line number
    local separator_line_num=0
    local _line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _line_num=$((_line_num + 1))
        if [[ "$_line" =~ ^[-=]{3,} ]]; then
            separator_line_num=$_line_num
            break
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $separator_line_num -eq 0 ]] && return

    # Header is the line before the separator
    local header_num=$((separator_line_num - 1))
    [[ $header_num -lt 1 ]] && return

    local header_line=""
    _line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _line_num=$((_line_num + 1))
        if [[ $_line_num -eq $header_num ]]; then
            header_line="$_line"
            break
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ -z "$header_line" ]] && return

    # Find header word positions (start and end of each word)
    local h_starts; h_starts=()
    local h_ends; h_ends=()
    local in_word=0
    local i
    for ((i=0; i<${#header_line}; i++)); do
        local ch="${header_line:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$ch" != " " ]]; then
            if [[ $in_word -eq 0 ]]; then
                h_starts+=("$i")
                in_word=1
            fi
        else
            if [[ $in_word -eq 1 ]]; then
                h_ends+=($((i-1)))
                in_word=0
            fi
        fi
    done
    [[ $in_word -eq 1 ]] && h_ends+=($((${#header_line}-1)))

    local num_cols=${#h_starts[@]}
    [[ $num_cols -lt 1 ]] && return

    # Extract column names from header
    local col_names; col_names=()
    local c
    for ((c=0; c<num_cols; c++)); do
        local start=${h_starts[$c]}
        local end=${h_ends[$c]}
        col_names+=("${header_line:$start:$((end-start+1))}")
    done

    # Compute column boundaries using midpoints of inter-header gaps.
    # This correctly handles right-aligned data that extends beyond header text.
    local col_lo; col_lo=()
    local col_hi; col_hi=()
    col_lo=(0)
    for ((c=1; c<num_cols; c++)); do
        local prev_end=${h_ends[$((c-1))]}
        local this_start=${h_starts[$c]}
        local boundary=$(( (prev_end + this_start + 1) / 2 ))
        col_hi+=("$boundary")
        col_lo+=("$boundary")
    done
    col_hi+=(99999)

    # Get data lines (everything after the separator, skip blank lines)
    local data_lines=""
    _line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _line_num=$((_line_num + 1))
        [[ $_line_num -le $separator_line_num ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        if [[ -z "$data_lines" ]]; then
            data_lines="$_line"
        else
            data_lines+=$'\n'"$_line"
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ -z "$data_lines" ]] && return

    # For each data row, extract values using computed column boundaries and emit
    # an indexed record group (entry<N>.<column>) so the tidy melt renders one row
    # per data line instead of welding every cell into one wide record.
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))

        for ((c=0; c<num_cols; c++)); do
            local lo=${col_lo[$c]}
            local hi=${col_hi[$c]}

            # Clamp to row length
            [[ $lo -ge ${#row} ]] && continue
            local len=$((hi - lo))
            [[ $((lo + len)) -gt ${#row} ]] && len=$((${#row} - lo))

            local value="${row:$lo:$len}"
            # Trim surrounding whitespace; internal spaces are part of the value.
            while [[ "$value" == " "* ]]; do value="${value# }"; done
            while [[ "$value" == *" " ]]; do value="${value% }"; done
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

            local name="${col_names[$c]}"
            name="${name//./_}"   # '.' would break the tidy melt's group key split
            result+="entry${entry}.${name} ${value}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$data_lines"

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: btrfs-filesystem-show
## Description: Extract per-device rows from `btrfs filesystem show` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 27
## Sample: samples/btrfs-filesystem-show/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # `btrfs filesystem show` is distinctive: `Label:` + `uuid:` headers, a
    # `Total devices N FS bytes used ...` line, and `devid ... path /dev/...` rows.
    local has_label=0 has_total=0 has_devid=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "Label:"* && "$line" == *"uuid:"* ]] && has_label=1
        [[ "$line" == *"Total devices"* && "$line" == *"FS bytes used"* ]] && has_total=1
        [[ "$line" == *"devid"* && "$line" == *"path "* ]] && has_devid=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_label -eq 1 && $has_total -eq 1 && $has_devid -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Device rows look like: devid  1 size 931.51GiB used 420.00GiB path /dev/sda1
        [[ "$line" == *"devid"* && "$line" == *"path "* ]] || continue

        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        # Pull each field by position relative to its keyword.
        local devid="" size="" used="" path=""
        local i
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#f[@]}; i++)); do
            case "${f[$i]}" in
                devid) devid="${f[$((i + 1))]}" ;;
                size)  size="${f[$((i + 1))]}" ;;
                used)  used="${f[$((i + 1))]}" ;;
                path)  path="${f[$((i + 1))]}" ;;
            esac
        done
        [[ -n "$devid" && -n "$path" ]] || continue

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.devid ${devid}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.size ${size}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.used ${used}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.path ${path}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=66cc4923f26316b0b0d6ae331f72702aee6800ef3ed51287e3ad3f13e1379b30===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: fdisk
## Description: Extract disk partition table from fdisk -l output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/fdisk/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: a "Disk /dev/..." line AND a partition-table header containing
    # Device / Start / End / Sectors / Size / Type columns.
    local has_disk=0 has_header=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "Disk /dev/"* ]] && has_disk=1
        if [[ "$line" == "Device"* && "$line" == *Start* && "$line" == *End* \
              && "$line" == *Sectors* && "$line" == *Size* && "$line" == *Type* ]]; then
            has_header=1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_disk -eq 1 && $has_header -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local in_table=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Partition-table header marks the start of the data rows.
        if [[ "$line" == "Device"* && "$line" == *Start* && "$line" == *Type* ]]; then
            in_table=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_table -eq 1 ]] || continue
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Only partition rows (/dev/...) are data.
        [[ "$line" == /dev/* ]] || continue

        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        # f[0]=device; optional "*" boot flag; then start end sectors size id type...
        local device="${f[0]}"
        local idx=1
        local boot=""
        if [[ "${f[1]}" == "*" ]]; then
            boot="*"
            idx=2
        fi
        local start="${f[$idx]}"; idx=$((idx + 1))
        local end="${f[$idx]}";   idx=$((idx + 1))
        local sectors="${f[$idx]}"; idx=$((idx + 1))
        local size="${f[$idx]}";  idx=$((idx + 1))
        # skip Id column
        idx=$((idx + 1))
        # remaining tokens form the Type (may contain spaces)
        local type=""
        local i
        for ((i = idx; i < ${#f[@]}; i++)); do
            type+="${f[$i]} "
        done
        type="${type%" "}"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.device ${device}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.boot ${boot}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.start ${start}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.end ${end}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.sectors ${sectors}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.size ${size}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.type ${type}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=22c8072b08342130f80e909225ecd5b09ec8050ebaea015c008bc1cd2319a345===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: iostat-x
## Description: Extract per-device extended I/O stats from `iostat -x` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/iostat-x/basic.txt

# `iostat -x` prints a `Linux ...` banner, then an `avg-cpu:` block, then an
# extended per-device table headed by a `Device` line (no trailing colon) whose
# columns include r/s, w/s, rrqm/s and the extended-only aqu-sz. We emit one
# record per DEVICE row, ignoring the banner and the avg-cpu block.

# Turn a raw column header into a safe field name (word chars only).
_iostatx_field () {
    local c="$1"
    c="${c//%/pct_}"
    c="${c//\//_per_}"
    c="${c//-/_}"
    printf '%s' "$c" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_' '_' | sed 's/_\{1,\}/_/g; s/^_//; s/_$//'
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    # Require the avg-cpu block AND an extended Device header (aqu-sz + rrqm/s).
    [[ "$text" == *"avg-cpu:"* ]] || return 1
    # `aqu-sz` alone (without `rrqm/s`) is a reduced extended-mode column set
    # (e.g. `iostat -c -x`, a shorter field list) Aje28094Aj still `iostat -x`'s output,
    # just not every optional column. `aqu-sz` is distinctive enough on its own
    # to not misfire on a plain `iostat -d` Device table (which never has it).
    local line seen=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == Device* ]] || continue
        [[ "$line" == *"aqu-sz"* ]] && seen=1
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $seen -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0
    local -a cols=()
    local have_header=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        if [[ $have_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            [[ "$line" == Device* ]] || continue
            read -ra cols <<< "$line"
            have_header=1
            continue
        fi

        local -a vals=()
        read -ra vals <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#vals[@]} -lt 2 ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.device ${vals[0]}"$'\n'
        local i
        for ((i=1; i<${#cols[@]}; i++)); do
            local f; f=$(_iostatx_field "${cols[$i]}")
            [[ -z "$f" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${n}.${f} ${vals[$i]:-NONE}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: parted-print
## Description: Extract partition table (number/start/end/size/fs/name) from `parted print`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/parted-print/basic.txt

# `parted print` prints a Model:/Disk:/Partition Table: header block, then a
# "Number Start End Size File system Name Flags" table. One record per
# partition; the header block is skipped.

_parted_is_header_row () {
    [[ "$1" == "Number"* && "$1" == *Start* && "$1" == *End* \
       && "$1" == *Size* && "$1" == *"File system"* ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line saw_disk=0 saw_hdr=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "Disk /dev/"* ]] && saw_disk=1
        _parted_is_header_row "$line" && saw_hdr=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $saw_disk -eq 1 && $saw_hdr -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line in_table=0 i
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _parted_is_header_row "$line"; then
            in_table=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_table -eq 1 ]] || continue
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        read -ra _f <<< "$line"
        # _f[0]=Number _f[1]=Start _f[2]=End _f[3]=Size _f[4]=Filesystem,
        # remaining tokens = Name + Flags.
        [[ "${_f[0]:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
        local number="${_f[0]}" start="${_f[1]:-}" end="${_f[2]:-}"
        local size="${_f[3]:-}" fs="${_f[4]:-}"
        local name=""
        for ((i = 5; i < ${#_f[@]}; i++)); do
            [[ -n "$name" ]] && name+="_"
            name+="${_f[$i]}"
        done
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.number ${number}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.start ${start}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.end ${end}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.size ${size}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.fs ${fs}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: readelf-sections
## Description: Extract section headers from `readelf -S` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/readelf-sections/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: the readelf -S column header with the "[Nr]" index cell.
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == *"[Nr]"* && "$line" == *"Name"* \
              && "$line" == *"Type"* && "$line" == *"Address"* \
              && "$line" == *"Offset"* ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local trimmed="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        # Section rows start with a "[ N]" index cell.
        [[ "$trimmed" =~ ^\[[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\] ]] || continue
        # Pull the numeric index out of the brackets, keep the remainder.
        local nr="${trimmed#\[}"; nr="${nr%%\]*}"; nr="${nr//[[:space:]]/}"
        local rest="${trimmed#*\]}"
        read -ra f <<< "$rest"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 4 ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.nr ${nr}"$'\n'
        # The NULL section (index 0) has an empty Name, so the remainder has one
        # fewer token; shift the field mapping accordingly.
        if [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 5 ]]; then
            result+="entry${entry}.name ${f[0]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.type ${f[1]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.address ${f[2]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.offset ${f[3]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.size ${f[4]}"$'\n'
        else
            result+="entry${entry}.type ${f[0]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.address ${f[1]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.offset ${f[2]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.size ${f[3]}"$'\n'
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/filesystem/xfs-info.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=ff2614f2ac17adad4f75f669d533da109086ed3bab9e9e3f0b189d44d30b4475===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: xfs-info
## Description: Extract geometry fields from `xfs_info` (section `key=value` tokens)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/xfs-info/basic.txt

# `xfs_info` prints aligned sections (meta-data, data, naming, log, realtime),
# each with several `key=value` tokens spread across continuation lines, e.g.
#   meta-data=/dev/sda2   isize=512    agcount=4, agsize=6553600 blks
#            =            sectsz=512   attr=2, projid32bit=1
# Generic parsers can't cope with the aligned continuations and duplicate token
# names (bsize/sectsz/blocks recur per section). This emits ONE wide record with
# each token as a section-prefixed field, e.g. entry1.meta_data_isize 512.

_xfsinfo_field () {
    local s; s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
    local out="" i c
    for ((i=0; i<${#s}; i++)); do
        c="${s:$i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [a-z0-9_]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

_xfsinfo_sanitize_val () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v%,}"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # xfs_info signature: the meta-data section header plus its distinctive tokens.
    [[ "$text" == *"meta-data"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"isize="* ]]    || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"agcount="* ]]  || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line section leading tok key val field
    local -a toks
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        leading=""
        # A section-starting line begins in column 0; the section name is the run
        # of chars before the first '=' or whitespace (continuation lines are
        # indented and inherit the current section).
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[^[:space:]] ]]; then
            leading="${line%%[=[:space:]]*}"
            section="$(_xfsinfo_field "$leading")"
        fi
        read -ra toks <<< "$line"
        for tok in "${toks[@]}"; do
            [[ "$tok" == *"="* ]] || continue
            key="${tok%%=*}"
            val="${tok#*=}"
            [[ -n "$key" && "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z] ]] || continue
            [[ -n "${val%,}" ]] || continue
            if [[ "$key" == "$leading" ]]; then
                field="$section"
            else
                field="${section}_$(_xfsinfo_field "$key")"
            fi
            entry=1
            result+="entry1.${field} $(_xfsinfo_sanitize_val "$val")"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: zpool-status
## Description: Extract the vdev/device table from `zpool status` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 27
## Sample: samples/zpool-status/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # `zpool status` has a distinctive `pool:` header, a `config:` line, and a
    # device table whose header is exactly `NAME STATE READ WRITE CKSUM`.
    local has_pool=0 has_config=0 has_hdr=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"pool:"* ]] && has_pool=1
        [[ "$line" == "config:"* ]] && has_config=1
        if [[ "$line" == *"NAME"* && "$line" == *"STATE"* \
              && "$line" == *"READ"* && "$line" == *"WRITE"* \
              && "$line" == *"CKSUM"* ]]; then
            has_hdr=1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_pool -eq 1 && $has_config -eq 1 && $has_hdr -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local in_table=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # The `NAME STATE READ WRITE CKSUM` header opens the device table.
        if [[ "$line" == *"NAME"* && "$line" == *"STATE"* \
              && "$line" == *"READ"* && "$line" == *"WRITE"* \
              && "$line" == *"CKSUM"* ]]; then
            in_table=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_table -eq 1 ]] || continue
        # A blank line ends the table (before the trailing `errors:` block).
        [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && break

        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        # Each device row is: name state read write cksum
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 5 ]] || continue

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${f[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.state ${f[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.read ${f[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.write ${f[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.cksum ${f[4]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=5149a40a139b3ec0593c7332c2fad418bbe76416ddd96b96831806dd2b38405b===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: biosdecode
## Description: `biosdecode` SMBIOS entry-point block (address/length/counts snapshot)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/biosdecode/basic.txt

# `biosdecode` prints entry-point structures ("SMBIOS x.y present." followed by
# indented "Some Label <value>" detail lines). There is no colon separator, so
# generic key/value parsers cannot find the fields. This lifts the SMBIOS
# entry-point block into one wide record: the value is the first numeric / hex
# token on each indented line, the label is the words before it.

_bios_key () {
    local s="$1" out="" c i n=${#1}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${s:i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    while [[ "$out" == *__* ]]; do out="${out//__/_}"; done
    out="${out#_}"; out="${out%_}"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    # Distinctive: the "# biosdecode <ver>" banner or the SMBIOS present line
    # together with a "Structure Table" detail line.
    [[ "$text" == *"# biosdecode "* ]] || \
        { [[ "$text" == *"SMBIOS "*" present."* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"Structure Table "* ]]; } || return 1

    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line trimmed in_block=0 key val tok
    local -a toks

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        trimmed="${line//[[:space:]]/}"
        [[ -z "$trimmed" ]] && continue

        # SMBIOS entry-point header: capture the version, start the block.
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^SMBIOS[[:space:]]+([0-9][0-9.]*)[[:space:]]+present ]]; then
            result+="entry1.smbios_version ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
            in_block=1
            continue
        fi

        # A non-indented, non-blank line ends the SMBIOS block.
        if [[ "$line" != [[:space:]]* ]]; then
            [[ $in_block -eq 1 ]] && break
            continue
        fi

        [[ $in_block -eq 1 ]] || continue

        # Indented detail line: "Label words 0x1234." Aje28094Aj strip trailing period,
        # split at the first numeric/hex token.
        line="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        line="${line%.}"
        toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$line"
        key=""; val=""
        for tok in "${toks[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$tok" =~ ^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+$ || "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
                val="$tok"
                break
            fi
            [[ -n "$key" ]] && key+=" "
            key+="$tok"
        done
        [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
        key="$(_bios_key "$key")"
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        result+="entry1.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/hardware/decode-dimms.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=d63ae60d09e2c91655ba551d16901dee577cbbea548a5b6916af7b18e8f25c2f===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: decode-dimms
## Description: `decode-dimms` SPD EEPROM snapshot ("field <TAB> value" block)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/decode-dimms/basic.txt

# `decode-dimms` prints the SPD EEPROM contents as "Field name<TABs>value"
# lines under "---=== ... ===---" section banners. The tab alignment and the
# multi-word, multi-word values (e.g. "16 x 16 x 10 x 64") defeat generic
# key/value parsers. This lifts the whole SPD snapshot into one wide record.

_dimms_key () {
    local s="$1" out="" c i n=${#1}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${s:i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    while [[ "$out" == *__* ]]; do out="${out//__/_}"; done
    out="${out#_}"; out="${out%_}"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

_dimms_val () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/ }"
    while [[ "$v" == *"  "* ]]; do v="${v//  / }"; done
    v="${v# }"; v="${v% }"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    # Distinctive: the decode-dimms banner or the SPD EEPROM section title.
    [[ "$text" == *"decode-dimms"* || "$text" == *"SPD EEPROM Information"* ]] || return 1

    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line key val

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Only "field<TAB>value" data lines carry a tab.
        [[ "$line" == *$'\t'* ]] || continue
        # Skip section banners and the "# decode-dimms version" comment banner
        # (but keep real fields like "# of bytes written to SDRAM EEPROM").
        [[ "$line" == "# decode-dimms"* || "$line" == *"==="* ]] && continue

        key="${line%%$'\t'*}"
        val="${line#*$'\t'}"
        key="$(_dimms_key "$key")"
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        val="$(_dimms_val "$val")"
        [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
        result+="entry1.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: lspci-tv
## Description: Extract PCI device tree lines from lspci -tv output (one record per device)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/lspci-tv/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # lspci -tv tree: a root bus like "-[0000:00]-" (HEX bus address, no spaces)
    # plus branch glyphs (+- \-). The hex requirement rejects psql `\x` record
    # separators like "-[ RECORD 1 ]---+---".
    if [[ "$text" =~ \-\[[0-9a-fA-F]+(:[0-9a-fA-F]+)?\]- ]] \
       && { [[ "$text" == *"+-"* ]] || [[ "$text" == *"\\-"* ]]; }; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        # Single-column: whole tree line is the value (internal spaces preserved).
        result+="entry${n}.A ${line}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: lsusb-v
## Description: Extract descriptor fields from `lsusb -v` into one wide record
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/lsusb-v/basic.txt

# `lsusb -v` prints a large indented key/value block for a device descriptor:
#   `  bLength                18`
#   `  idVendor           0x8087 Intel Corp.`
# Flatten the descriptor into ONE wide record (`entry1.<field> value`). Repeated
# field names (they recur across nested descriptors) are suffixed _2, _3, ... so
# columns stay unique.

_lsusbv_name () {
    local s="$1" out="" c i n=${#1}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${s:i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    while [[ "$out" == *__* ]]; do out="${out//__/_}"; done
    out="${out#_}"; out="${out%_}"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}
_lsusbv_san () { local v="$1"; v="${v//$'\t'/_}"; printf '%s' "$v"; }

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Device Descriptor:"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"bLength"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"idVendor"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line key val san count fields=0
    declare -A seen=()
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Only indented `key value` lines (skip banners like "Device Descriptor:").
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)[[:space:]]+([^[:space:]].*)$ ]] || continue
        key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        val="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        san="$(_lsusbv_name "$key")"
        [[ -n "$san" ]] || continue
        count="${seen[$san]:-0}"
        count=$((count + 1))
        seen[$san]=$count
        [[ $count -gt 1 ]] && san="${san}_${count}"
        result+="entry1.${san} $(_lsusbv_san "$val")"$'\n'
        fields=$((fields + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $fields -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: rocm-smi-concise
## Description: Extract the GPU concise-info table from rocm-smi (skips banners)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 8
## Sample: samples/rocm-smi-concise/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    if [[ "$text" == *"ROCm System Management Interface"* ]] \
       || { [[ "$text" == *"AvgPwr"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"SCLK"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"PwrCap"* ]]; }; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Skip banner/rule lines and the column header.
        case "$line" in
            *=*) continue ;;
            GPU[[:space:]]*) continue ;;
        esac
        # Data rows begin with the GPU index (a number).
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9] ]] || continue

        read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#_arr[@]} -lt 10 ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        local p="entry${n}."
        result+="${p}gpu ${_arr[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}temp ${_arr[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}avgpwr ${_arr[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}sclk ${_arr[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}mclk ${_arr[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}fan ${_arr[5]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}perf ${_arr[6]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}pwrcap ${_arr[7]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}vram_pct ${_arr[8]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}gpu_pct ${_arr[9]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/hardware/smartctl-selftest.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=cac6d06553899aed742baef3fe1a10ac4247f6c5a199ea29300114c0da031411===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: smartctl-selftest
## Description: Extract the SMART self-test log table from smartctl -l selftest output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/smartctl-selftest/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    if [[ "$text" == *"Self-test log"* ]] \
       || { [[ "$text" == *"Test_Description"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"LBA_of_first_error"* ]]; }; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Data rows start with a "# N" test-number marker.
        [[ "$line" =~ ^#[[:space:]]*[0-9]+ ]] || continue

        # Fields are column-aligned; single spaces occur within a field
        # (e.g. "Extended offline") and 2+ spaces separate fields.
        local rest="$line"
        local -a cols=()
        while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
            # Trim leading whitespace.
            rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            [[ -z "$rest" ]] && break
            local seg
            if [[ "$rest" =~ ^([^[:space:]]([^[:space:]]|[[:space:]][^[:space:]])*) ]]; then
                seg="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            else
                seg="$rest"
            fi
            cols+=("$seg")
            rest="${rest:${#seg}}"
        done

        # cols: [# N] [Test_Description] [Status] [Remaining] [LifeTime] [LBA]
        [[ ${#cols[@]} -lt 6 ]] && continue

        # num from "# N".
        local num="${cols[0]##*[[:space:]]}"

        n=$((n + 1))
        local p="entry${n}."
        result+="${p}num ${num}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}test_description ${cols[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}status ${cols[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}remaining ${cols[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}lifetime ${cols[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}lba ${cols[5]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

# Changelog -- HPC Strategies

## 2026-03-31 (2 new Kubernetes resource monitoring strategies)
- Added `kubectl-top-nodes.sh` -- extracts node resource usage from `kubectl top nodes` (name, cpu_cores, cpu_pct, mem_bytes, mem_pct)
- Added `kubectl-top-pods.sh` -- extracts pod resource usage from `kubectl top pods` (namespace, name, cpu, memory); supports both namespaced and non-namespaced output
- Files: `kubectl-top-nodes.sh`, `kubectl-top-pods.sh`
- Samples: `samples/kubectl-top-nodes/sample1.txt`, `samples/kubectl-top-pods/sample1.txt`

## 2026-03-20 (Initial HPC strategies)
- Added `mpi-profile.sh` Aje28094Aj extracts MPI profiling data from mpiP summaries and Intel MPI statistics (comm_size, total_time, mpi_time, mpi_percent, callsite function breakdown)
- Added `mpi-ranklog.sh` Aje28094Aj parses multi-rank interleaved MPI output with rank prefixes (`[0]`, `[rank N]`, `[i,j]`, `Rank N:`), extracts num_ranks, per-rank line/error counts
- Added `mpi-display-map.sh` Aje28094Aj parses Open MPI `--display-map` output, extracts num_nodes, per-node process binding (rank, slot, binding)
- Added `darshan.sh` Aje28094Aj parses `darshan-parser` text output, extracts POSIX/MPI-IO/STDIO counters (bytes read/written, opens, reads, writes), totals, and metadata
- Files: `mpi-profile.sh`, `mpi-ranklog.sh`, `mpi-display-map.sh`, `darshan.sh`
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: csvlook
## Description: Extract rows from a csvlook / Markdown pipe table (skips the |---| separator row)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/csvlook/basic.txt

# `csvlook` renders a Markdown-style table: a header row of pipe-delimited column
# names, a "| --- | --- |" separator row, then one data row per record. The
# header names the fields; the separator row is skipped; each data row becomes a
# record.

# A markdown separator row is ENTIRELY `|`, `-`, `:` and spaces (every cell is
# `---`) Aje28094Aj and contains at least one dash. A data row with a lone `-` cell (e.g.
# an `aws --output table` box row "| ... | - | ... |") is NOT a separator.
_csvlook_is_sep () {
    local l="$1"
    [[ "$l" == *"-"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*\|[-:|[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*$ ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

_csvlook_cells () {
    # Splits one pipe-delimited row into the global array _CELLS, trimmed.
    local line="$1"
    while [[ "$line" == " "* ]]; do line="${line# }"; done
    [[ "$line" == "|"* ]] && line="${line#|}"
    while [[ "$line" == *" " ]]; do line="${line% }"; done
    [[ "$line" == *"|" ]] && line="${line%|}"
    local old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS='|'
    read -ra _CELLS <<< "$line"
    IFS="$old_ifs"
    local i c
    for ((i=0; i<${#_CELLS[@]}; i++)); do
        c="${_CELLS[$i]}"
        while [[ "$c" == " "* ]]; do c="${c# }"; done
        while [[ "$c" == *" " ]]; do c="${c% }"; done
        _CELLS[$i]="$c"
    done
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Must contain pipe rows and a dashed separator row.
    [[ "$text" == *"|"* ]] || return 1
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"|"* ]] || continue
        if _csvlook_is_sep "$line"; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local -a _CELLS headers
    local have_header=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"|"* ]] || continue
        # Separator row: cells are all dashes.
        if _csvlook_is_sep "$line"; then continue; fi
        _csvlook_cells "$line"
        if [[ $have_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            headers=("${_CELLS[@]}")
            have_header=1
            continue
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        local j name value
        for ((j=0; j<${#headers[@]}; j++)); do
            name="${headers[$j]}"
            value="${_CELLS[$j]:-}"
            name="${name// /_}"; name="${name//./_}"
            [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${entry}.${name} ${value}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/misc/git-log.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=71cc61d9db4d8ce1d78b68ea3f3f88441966c26f98133c8b424bbf63975144cb===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: git-log
## Description: Extract fields from git log output (full and oneline formats)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/git-log/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    # Detect full git log format: "commit <40-char hex>"
    if [[ "$text" =~ ^commit\ [0-9a-f]{40} ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    # Detect oneline format: "<7+ char hex> <message>"
    if [[ "$text" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,}\  ]]; then
        # Require >=2 lines, and guard against look-alikes: the hash must contain a
        # hex LETTER (not a pure-decimal size Aje28094Aj `gsutil du`), the line must not be
        # tab-delimited (`git for-each-ref` "<hash> commit\t<ref>"), and the message
        # must not be a `git lfs ls-files` "* <path>" status marker.
        local match_count=0
        while IFS= read -r _line; do
            if [[ "$_line" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,}\  ]]; then
                local _h="${_line%%[[:space:]]*}" _rest="${_line#* }"
                if [[ "$_h" =~ [a-f] && "$_line" != *$'\t'* && "$_rest" != "* "* && "$_rest" != "- "* ]]; then
                    match_count=$((match_count + 1))
                fi
            fi
            [[ $match_count -ge 2 ]] && return 0
        done <<< "$text"
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Check if this is full format or oneline format
    if [[ "$text" =~ ^commit\ [0-9a-f]{40} ]]; then
        _strat_git_log_extract_full "$text"
    else
        _strat_git_log_extract_oneline "$text"
    fi
}

_strat_git_log_extract_full () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local commit_num=0
    local current_hash=""
    local current_author=""
    local current_date=""
    local current_message=""
    local in_message=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^commit\ ([0-9a-f]{40}) ]]; then
            # Emit previous commit if we have one
            if [[ -n "$current_hash" ]]; then
                _strat_git_log_emit_commit "$commit_num" "$current_hash" "$current_author" "$current_date" "$current_message"
                result+="$_git_log_output"
            fi
            commit_num=$((commit_num + 1))
            current_hash="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            current_author=""
            current_date=""
            current_message=""
            in_message=0
            continue
        fi

        if [[ "$line" == "Author: "* ]]; then
            current_author="${line#Author: }"
            while [[ "$current_author" == " "* ]]; do current_author="${current_author# }"; done
            in_message=0
            continue
        fi

        if [[ "$line" == "Date: "* ]]; then
            current_date="${line#Date: }"
            while [[ "$current_date" == " "* ]]; do current_date="${current_date# }"; done
            in_message=0
            continue
        fi

        # Blank line after Date: signals start of message
        if [[ -z "$line" && -n "$current_date" && -z "$current_message" ]]; then
            in_message=1
            continue
        fi

        # Capture first non-empty indented message line
        if [[ $in_message -eq 1 && -z "$current_message" ]]; then
            local trimmed="$line"
            while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done
            if [[ -n "$trimmed" ]]; then
                current_message="${trimmed//$'\t'/_}"
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    # Emit last commit
    if [[ -n "$current_hash" ]]; then
        _strat_git_log_emit_commit "$commit_num" "$current_hash" "$current_author" "$current_date" "$current_message"
        result+="$_git_log_output"
    fi

    echo "$result"
}

# Helper to emit commit fields (uses global _git_log_output to avoid subshell)
_strat_git_log_emit_commit () {
    local num="$1" hash="$2" author="$3" date="$4" message="$5"
    local prefix="commit${num}"
    _git_log_output=""
    _git_log_output+="${prefix}.hash ${hash}"$'\n'
    if [[ -n "$author" ]]; then
        _git_log_output+="${prefix}.author ${author}"$'\n'
    fi
    if [[ -n "$date" ]]; then
        _git_log_output+="${prefix}.date ${date}"$'\n'
    fi
    if [[ -n "$message" ]]; then
        _git_log_output+="${prefix}.message ${message}"$'\n'
    fi
}

_strat_git_log_extract_oneline () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local commit_num=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        if ! [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,}\  ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        commit_num=$((commit_num + 1))
        local prefix="commit${commit_num}"
        local hash="${line%% *}"
        local message="${line#* }"
        message="${message//$'\t'/_}"
        result+="${prefix}.hash ${hash}"$'\n'
        result+="${prefix}.message ${message}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: restic
## Description: Extract snapshots from `restic snapshots` output (skips header rule + count footer)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/restic/basic.txt

# `restic snapshots` prints an "ID Time Host Tags Paths" header, a dashed rule,
# one row per snapshot, a second dashed rule, then an "N snapshots" footer. Only
# the rows between the two rules are data.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive restic header columns + a "snapshots" footer.
    [[ "$text" == *"ID"* && "$text" == *"Host"* && "$text" == *"Paths"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"snapshots"* ]] || return 1
    local line stripped
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        stripped="${line//-/}"
        if [[ -z "$stripped" && "$line" == *-* ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 in_data=0 line stripped
    local -a t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        stripped="${line//-/}"
        if [[ -z "$stripped" && "$line" == *-* ]]; then
            if [[ $in_data -eq 0 ]]; then in_data=1; else in_data=0; fi
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_data -eq 1 ]] || continue
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#t[@]} -ge 6 ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.id ${t[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.date ${t[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.time ${t[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.host ${t[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.tags ${t[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.paths ${t[5]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: terraform-plan-actions
## Description: Extract per-resource action lines from `terraform plan` ("# <resource> will be <action>")
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/terraform-plan-actions/basic.txt

# A `terraform plan` summary lists each affected resource on a
# "  # <resource> will be <action>" line, wrapped by a "Terraform will perform
# ..." intro and a "Plan: N to add, ..." footer. Only the "# ... will be ..."
# lines are data Aje28094Aj each becomes one record (resource + action) so the plan melts
# to one tidy row per resource. (The distinct name avoids colliding with the
# existing config/terraform-plan strategy, which targets the verbose diff form.)

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]].*[[:space:]]will[[:space:]]be[[:space:]] ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]].*[[:space:]]will[[:space:]]be[[:space:]] ]] || continue
        local body="$line"
        while [[ "$body" == " "* ]]; do body="${body# }"; done
        body="${body#\# }"
        local resource="${body%% will be *}"
        local action="${body#* will be }"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.resource ${resource}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.action ${action}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: arping
## Description: Extract ARP reply records from `arping` output (skips banner + stats footer)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/arping/basic.txt

# arping prints a banner ("ARPING <ip>"), one line per reply
# ("<N> bytes from <mac> (<ip>): index=<seq> time=<t> msec"), then a stats
# footer ("--- <ip> statistics ---", "<n> packets transmittedAje280a6Aj", "rtt Aje280a6Aj").
# Only the reply lines are data; the banner and footer are skipped. Each reply
# becomes a record with seq / from_ip / mac / time_msec (plus bytes).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local replies=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+\ bytes\ from\ [0-9A-Fa-f:]+\ \([0-9.]+\):\ index=[0-9]+\ time=[0-9.]+\ msec$ ]]; then
            replies=$((replies + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $replies -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+\ bytes\ from\ [0-9A-Fa-f:]+\ \([0-9.]+\):\ index=[0-9]+\ time=[0-9.]+\ msec$ ]] || continue
        local bytes="${line%% bytes*}"
        local rest="${line#* bytes from }"
        local mac="${rest%% *}"
        local ip="${rest#*\(}"; ip="${ip%%\)*}"
        local seq="${line##*index=}"; seq="${seq%% *}"
        local t="${line##*time=}"; t="${t%% *}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.seq ${seq}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.from_ip ${ip}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.mac ${mac}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.time_msec ${t}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.bytes ${bytes}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: haproxy-vv
## Description: Extract build/settings key-values from `haproxy -vv`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/haproxy-vv/basic.txt

# `haproxy -vv` prints a "HAProxy version ..." banner followed by "key = value"
# lines (build options + default settings). This is a key/value snapshot: emit a
# single wide record `entry1.<key> value` for every "key = value" line, then
# total_entries 1.

_hv_san () { local v="$1"; v="${v//$'\t'/_}"; printf '%s' "$v"; }
_hv_key () {
    local k="$1"
    k="${k#"${k%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # ltrim
    k="${k%"${k##*[![:space:]]}"}"   # rtrim
    k="${k//[[:space:]]/_}"
    k="${k//./_}"
    printf '%s' "$k"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"HAProxy version"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"="* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" n=0 line key val
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == *"="* ]] || continue
        key="$(_hv_key "${line%%=*}")"
        [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
        val="${line#*=}"
        val="${val#"${val%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        val="${val%"${val##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry1.${key} $(_hv_san "$val")"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ifstat
## Description: Extract per-interface throughput samples from `ifstat` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/ifstat/basic.txt

# `ifstat` prints a two-line header: interface names on the first line, then a
# `KB/s in  KB/s out` sub-header (two columns per interface), then one sample
# row per interval:
#     eth0                wlan0
#  KB/s in  KB/s out   KB/s in  KB/s out
#    12.45     3.21       0.98      0.12
# We emit one record per sample, with <iface>_in / <iface>_out columns.

# Safe field-name fragment (word chars only).
_ifstat_name () { printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_' '_' | sed 's/_\{1,\}/_/g; s/^_//; s/_$//'; }

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"KB/s in"* && "$text" == *"KB/s out"* ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0 idx=0
    local -a ifaces=()

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        idx=$((idx + 1))

        if [[ $idx -eq 1 ]]; then
            read -ra ifaces <<< "$line"
            continue
        fi
        [[ $idx -eq 2 ]] && continue   # KB/s in / KB/s out sub-header

        local -a vals=()
        read -ra vals <<< "$line"
        local ni=${#ifaces[@]}
        [[ $ni -eq 0 ]] && continue
        [[ ${#vals[@]} -lt $((2 * ni)) ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        local k
        for ((k=0; k<ni; k++)); do
            local nm; nm=$(_ifstat_name "${ifaces[$k]}")
            result+="entry${n}.${nm}_in ${vals[$((2*k))]}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${n}.${nm}_out ${vals[$((2*k+1))]}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
