===META: mode=644 sha256=2c08ea6cae8f4d597fdfb6b354570f5ca0b210bdb48f1db003695db927a0650a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: ip-maddr
## Description: Extract multicast addresses from `ip maddr show` interface blocks
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/ip-maddr/basic.txt

# `ip maddr` groups multicast addresses under interface blocks:
#   1:      lo
#           inet  224.0.0.251
#           inet6 ff02::1
#           link  33:33:00:00:00:01
# The header line is `<index>:<TAB><iface>` (iface only, no family token); each
# indented line is `<family> <address>` with family in {inet,inet6,link}. Emit
# one record per address line, carrying its interface, so the tidy melt renders
# one row per multicast address.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Signature: an interface header `<num>:<ws><name>` (exactly two tokens, the
    # second NOT a family keyword) AND an indented `<family> <address>` line whose
    # first token is inet/inet6/link with exactly two whitespace-separated tokens.
    local has_header=0 has_addr=0 line t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && continue
        read -ra _f <<< "$t"
        case "$t" in
            [0-9]*:*)
                if [[ ${#_f[@]} -eq 2 ]]; then
                    case "${_f[1]}" in
                        inet|inet6|link) ;;
                        *) has_header=1 ;;
                    esac
                fi
                ;;
        esac
        if [[ ${#_f[@]} -eq 2 ]]; then
            case "${_f[0]}" in
                inet|inet6|link) has_addr=1 ;;
            esac
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $has_header -eq 1 && $has_addr -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line t n=0 iface=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && continue
        read -ra _f <<< "$t"

        # Interface header: `<num>:<ws><iface>`
        case "$t" in
            [0-9]*:*)
                if [[ ${#_f[@]} -eq 2 ]]; then
                    case "${_f[1]}" in
                        inet|inet6|link) ;;
                        *) iface="${_f[1]}"; continue ;;
                    esac
                fi
                ;;
        esac

        # Address line: `<family> <address>`
        case "${_f[0]}" in
            inet|inet6|link) ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac
        [[ ${#_f[@]} -ge 2 ]] || continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.iface ${iface:-unknown}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.family ${_f[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.address ${_f[1]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ip-xfrm-state
## Description: Extract IPsec SAs (src/dst/proto) from `ip xfrm state`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/ip-xfrm-state/basic.txt

# `ip xfrm state` prints each SA as a "src <A> dst <B>" line followed by
# indented "proto ..."/"auth ..."/etc. lines. One record per SA.

_xfrm_is_sa () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^src\ [^[:space:]]+\ dst\ [^[:space:]]+ ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line saw_sa=0 saw_proto=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _xfrm_is_sa "$line" && saw_sa=1
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+proto\ (esp|ah|comp)\  ]] && saw_proto=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $saw_sa -eq 1 && $saw_proto -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local -a srcs=() dsts=() protos=()
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _xfrm_is_sa "$line"; then
            read -ra _s <<< "$line"
            # _s[0]=src _s[1]=<srcval> _s[2]=dst _s[3]=<dstval>
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            srcs[$entry]="${_s[1]:-}"
            dsts[$entry]="${_s[3]:-}"
            protos[$entry]=""
        elif [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+proto\  && $entry -ge 1 ]]; then
            read -ra _p <<< "$line"
            protos[$entry]="${_p[1]:-}"
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    local i
    for ((i = 1; i <= entry; i++)); do
        local src="${srcs[$i]}" dst="${dsts[$i]}" proto="${protos[$i]}"
        result+="entry${i}.src ${src}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${i}.dst ${dst}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${i}.proto ${proto}"$'\n'
    done
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: iperf3-intervals
## Description: Extract per-interval rows from `iperf3 -c` client output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/iperf3-intervals/basic.txt

# `iperf3 -c` prints a "Connecting to host" banner, a stream header, then one row
# per measurement interval:
#   [  5]   0.00-1.00   sec   112 MBytes   940 Mbits/sec    0    412 KBytes
# followed by a "- - -" separator and a summary block (sender/receiver rows).
# Signature: the "Bitrate" + "Interval" + "Transfer" column labels. Emit ONE
# record per interval row; skip the connect/header lines, the separator, and the
# sender/receiver summary rows.

_iperf3_sanitize () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # NB: iperf3 rows are prefixed with "[  5]" etc, so the generic _is_json
    # (which flags any text beginning with '[') would wrongly decline it Aje28094Aj the
    # Bitrate/Interval/Transfer signature below is specific enough on its own.
    [[ "$text" == *Bitrate* ]]  || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *Interval* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *Transfer* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line rest
    local -a t=()
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "["* ]] || continue                          # interval/summary rows
        [[ "$line" == *sender* || "$line" == *receiver* ]] && continue   # skip summary
        rest="${line#*]}"                                          # drop "[  5]" stream id
        read -ra t <<< "$rest"
        [[ "${t[1]}" == "sec" ]] || continue                       # data rows only
        [[ ${#t[@]} -ge 9 ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.interval $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[0]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.transfer $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[2]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.transfer_unit $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[3]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.bitrate $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[4]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.bitrate_unit $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[5]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.retr $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[6]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.cwnd $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[7]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.cwnd_unit $(_iperf3_sanitize "${t[8]}")"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: iptables-nat
## Description: Parse `iptables -t nat -L` rules (target prot opt source destination)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/iptables-nat/basic.txt

# `iptables -t nat -L` prints per-chain blocks:
#   Chain PREROUTING (policy ACCEPT)
#   target     prot opt source               destination
#   DNAT       tcp  --  anywhere             anywhere
#   ...
# One record per rule; the "Chain ..." headers and the "target prot opt ..."
# column headers are skipped.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"Chain "* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"target"*"prot"*"opt"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
        {
            if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next
            if ($1=="Chain") next
            if ($1=="target" && $2=="prot") next
            if (NF < 4) next
            target=$1; prot=$2; opt=$3; src=$4; dst=(NF>=5?$5:"-")
            e++
            print "entry" e ".target " target
            print "entry" e ".prot " prot
            print "entry" e ".opt " opt
            print "entry" e ".source " src
            print "entry" e ".destination " dst
        }
        END{ if(e>0) print "total_entries " e }
    '
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: iptables-nvL
## Description: Extract rule rows from `iptables -nvL` per-chain tables
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/iptables-nvL/basic.txt

# `iptables -nvL` prints one block per chain: a `Chain NAME (policy ...)` header,
# a column header `pkts bytes target prot opt in out source destination`, then
# one rule row per line. Emit ONE record per rule row. Keying on the `pkts bytes
# target` column header keeps this distinct from `iptables -nL`/`iptables-nat`
# (which have no pkts/bytes columns).

_iptnvl_san () { local v="$1"; v="${v//$'\t'/_}"; printf '%s' "$v"; }

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Chain "* ]] || return 1
    # The pkts/bytes/target column header is unique to -nvL (verbose) listings.
    [[ "$text" == *"pkts"*"bytes"*"target"*"prot"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 line
    local -a t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        case "$line" in
            Chain\ *) continue ;;              # chain header
            *pkts*bytes*target*) continue ;;   # column header
        esac
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        # Rule rows: pkts bytes target prot opt in out source destination (>=9).
        [[ ${#t[@]} -ge 9 ]] || continue
        [[ "${t[0]}" =~ ^[0-9] ]] || continue   # pkts is numeric
        [[ "${t[1]}" =~ ^[0-9] ]] || continue   # bytes is numeric
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.pkts ${t[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.bytes ${t[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.target ${t[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.prot ${t[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.opt ${t[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.in ${t[5]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.out ${t[6]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.source ${t[7]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.destination ${t[8]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: iwlist-scan
## Description: Extract wireless cells (address/essid) from `iwlist wlan0 scan`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/iwlist-scan/basic.txt

# `iwlist <iface> scan` prints "Cell NN - Address: <MAC>" blocks with indented
# ESSID/Quality/Channel lines beneath. One record per cell.

_iwlist_is_cell () {
    [[ "$1" =~ Cell\ [0-9]+\ -\ Address:\  ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _iwlist_is_cell "$line"; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

        if _iwlist_is_cell "$line"; then
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            addrs[$entry]="${line##*Address: }"

        result+="entry${i}.essid ${essid}"$'\n'

#!/bin/bash
## Name: mtr-report
## Description: Extract per-hop path statistics from an mtr report
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 17
## Sample: samples/mtr-report/basic.txt

# `mtr --report` prints a "HOST:" header followed by one row per hop:
#   1.|-- gateway   0.0%   10   1.2  1.4  1.1  2.3  0.4
# Columns after the host are: Loss% Snt Last Avg Best Wrst StDev.
# Priority 17 so it beats the generic tree-view (p50) on the "N.|--" marker.

_mtr_is_hop () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.\|--[[:space:]] ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local has_header=0 has_hop=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == HOST:* || "$line" == *"HOST:"*"Loss%"* ]] && has_header=1
        _mtr_is_hop "$line" && has_hop=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_header -eq 1 && $has_hop -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _mtr_is_hop "$line" || continue
        local trimmed="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        local hop="${trimmed%%.*}"
        local after="${trimmed#*|-- }"
        read -ra _a <<< "$after"
        # _a: host loss snt last avg best wrst stdev
        local host="${_a[0]}" loss="${_a[1]}" snt="${_a[2]}"
        local last="${_a[3]}" avg="${_a[4]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.hop ${hop}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.host ${host}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.loss ${loss}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.snt ${snt}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.last ${last}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.avg ${avg}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: netstat-s
## Description: Extract per-protocol counters from `netstat -s` grouped statistics
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/netstat-s/basic.txt

# `netstat -s` groups counters under protocol headers:
#   Ip:
#       Forwarding: 1
#       18274655 total packets received
#   Tcp:
#       9382 active connection openings
# Emit ONE record whose fields are the individual stats: each stat becomes a
# field named `<proto>_<sanitised description>` with the numeric count as value.
# capture's tidy melt renders this as a single wide key/value row.

# Sanitise a free-text description into a field-name fragment: lowercase,
# non-alphanumeric runs collapse to a single underscore, trim leading/trailing.
_netstat_s_slug () {
    printf '%s' "$1" | awk '{
        s=tolower($0); r=""; prev=0
        for(i=1;i<=length(s);i++){
            c=substr(s,i,1)
            if(c ~ /[a-z0-9]/){ r=r c; prev=0 }
            else if(prev==0){ r=r "_"; prev=1 }
        }
        gsub(/^_+/,"",r); gsub(/_+$/,"",r); print r
    }'
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Signature: a bare protocol group header (`Ip:`, `Tcp:`, ...) at column 0
    # AND an indented `<number> <description>` counter line under it.
    local has_group=0 has_counter=0 line t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "$line" in
            # Only genuine netstat -s protocol groups Aje28094Aj not any "word:" line (which
            # would wrongly grab `apt-cache policy`'s "curl:" package header).
            Ip:|Icmp:|IcmpMsg:|Tcp:|Udp:|UdpLite:|TcpExt:|IpExt:) has_group=1 ;;
        esac
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ "$line" == "$t" ]] && continue              # counter lines are indented
        case "$t" in
            [0-9]*" "*) has_counter=1 ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $has_group -eq 1 && $has_counter -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line t proto="" field val
    local count=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Protocol group header: unindented `<Name>:` with no value.
        case "$line" in
            [A-Za-z]*:)
                # unindented and ends in ':' with nothing after -> group header
                if [[ "${line:0:1}" != " " && "${line:0:1}" != $'\t' ]]; then
                    proto=$(_netstat_s_slug "${line%:}")
                    continue
                fi
                ;;
        esac

        # Only indented lines are counters.
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ "$line" == "$t" ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$proto" ]] && continue

        field=""; val=""
        case "$t" in
            [0-9]*" "*)
                # "<number> <description>"
                val="${t%% *}"
                field=$(_netstat_s_slug "${t#* }")
                ;;
            *": "*)
                # "<key>: <value>" Aje28094Aj keep only when value is a bare number
                local k="${t%%:*}" v="${t#*: }"
                case "$v" in
                    ""|*[!0-9]*) continue ;;           # non-numeric -> skip sub-headers
                    *) val="$v"; field=$(_netstat_s_slug "$k") ;;
                esac
                ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac

        [[ -z "$field" || -z "$val" ]] && continue
        count=$((count + 1))
        result+="entry1.${proto:+${proto}_}${field} ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=07e99edfaaad21f30cdeff231a220c251612122d1b6697f49b83a2d7818c65f2===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: nft-list-ruleset
## Description: Extract firewall rules from `nft list ruleset` nested table/chain output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/nft-list-ruleset/basic.txt

# `nft list ruleset` prints nested brace blocks:
#   table inet filter {
#       chain input {
#           type filter hook input priority filter; policy drop;
#           tcp dport 22 accept
#           ...
#       }
#   }
# Emit one record per actual RULE line Aje28094Aj the indented statements inside a chain,
# excluding the table/chain headers, the `type ... hook ... policy` declaration,
# and the closing braces. capture's tidy melt renders one row per rule.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Distinctive signature: a `table <family> <name> {` opener AND a
    # `chain <name> {` opener AND an nft `type ... hook ...` line.
    local has_table=0 has_chain=0 has_hook=0 line t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"      # strip leading whitespace
        case "$t" in
            "table "*"{"*) has_table=1 ;;
            "chain "*"{"*) has_chain=1 ;;
            "type "*" hook "*) has_hook=1 ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $has_table -eq 1 && $has_chain -eq 1 && $has_hook -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line t n=0
    local in_chain=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"      # strip leading whitespace
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && continue

        case "$t" in
            "table "*) continue ;;
            "chain "*"{"*) in_chain=1; continue ;;
            "type "*" hook "*) continue ;;         # chain type/hook/policy decl
            "}"*)  in_chain=0; continue ;;
            "{"*)  continue ;;
        esac
        [[ $in_chain -eq 1 ]] || continue

        # Whatever remains inside a chain block is a rule statement.
        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.rule ${t}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: nmap-sn
## Description: Extract discovered hosts (host/ip/latency) from `nmap -sn` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/nmap-sn/basic.txt

# `nmap -sn` host discovery prints a "Starting Nmap" banner, then one
# "Nmap scan report for <host> (<ip>)" line per host (each followed by a
# "Host is up (<lat> latency)." line), then a "Nmap done:" summary line.
# One record per host; banner and summary are skipped.

_nmapsn_is_report () {
    [[ "$1" == "Nmap scan report for "* ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line saw_report=0 saw_up=0 saw_ports=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _nmapsn_is_report "$line" && saw_report=1
        [[ "$line" == "Host is up"* ]] && saw_up=1
        # A PORT table means a full scan, not a -sn ping sweep Aje28094Aj that input
        # belongs to the nmap strategy.
        [[ "$line" == "PORT"*"STATE"* ]] && saw_ports=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $saw_report -eq 1 && $saw_up -eq 1 && $saw_ports -eq 0 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local -a hosts=() ips=() lats=()
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _nmapsn_is_report "$line"; then
            local target="${line#Nmap scan report for }"
            local host="$target" ip="$target"
            if [[ "$target" == *"("*")"* ]]; then
                host="${target%% (*}"
                ip="${target##*(}"; ip="${ip%)}"
            fi
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            hosts[$entry]="$host"
            ips[$entry]="$ip"
            lats[$entry]=""
        elif [[ "$line" == "Host is up"* && $entry -ge 1 ]]; then
            if [[ "$line" == *"("*"latency)"* ]]; then
                local lat="${line#*(}"
                lat="${lat%% *}"
                lats[$entry]="$lat"
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    local i
    for ((i = 1; i <= entry; i++)); do
        local host="${hosts[$i]}" ip="${ips[$i]}" lat="${lats[$i]}"
        result+="entry${i}.host ${host}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${i}.ip ${ip}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${i}.latency ${lat}"$'\n'
    done
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

## Priority: 8
## Sample: samples/nslookup_mx/basic.txt

# `nslookup -type=mx <domain>` prints the Server/Address banner, then one line

#!/bin/bash
## Name: nstat
## Description: Extract kernel network counters from `nstat` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/nstat/basic.txt

# `nstat` prints a `#kernel` header line then one row per metric:
#   IpInReceives   284719   0.0
# columns are Metric, value, rate. We emit one record per metric, skipping the
# `#kernel` line.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    # First non-empty line must be exactly `#kernel`.
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#kernel" ]] && return 0
        return 1
    done <<< "$text"

}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#kernel"* ]] && continue

        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 2 ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.metric ${f[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.value ${f[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.rate ${f[2]:-NONE}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ping
## Description: Extract per-reply records from ping output (seq, ttl, time, from)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/ping-reply/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive signature: an ICMP reply line carries BOTH "bytes from" and
    # "icmp_seq=" on the same line.
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == *"bytes from "* && "$line" == *"icmp_seq="* ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # One record per reply line (skip header / stats / summary lines).
        [[ "$line" == *"bytes from "* && "$line" == *"icmp_seq="* ]] || continue

        local from="" seq="" ttl="" time=""

        # from: token after "from ", trailing ':' stripped
        local after="${line#*bytes from }"
        from="${after%%:*}"
        # trim surrounding whitespace
        from="${from#"${from%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        from="${from%"${from##*[![:space:]]}"}"

        [[ "$line" =~ icmp_seq=([0-9]+) ]] && seq="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        [[ "$line" =~ ttl=([0-9]+) ]] && ttl="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        [[ "$line" =~ time=([0-9.]+) ]] && time="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        [[ -n "$seq" ]]  && result+="entry${entry}.seq ${seq}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$ttl" ]]  && result+="entry${entry}.ttl ${ttl}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$time" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.time ${time}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$from" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.from ${from}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=f8a199fc43c27db564bd0a67c3820cecd336b8d803800618cdb163fe7c7fc011===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: resolvectl-query
## Description: Parse `resolvectl query` answer into one wide record (name/addresses/link)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/resolvectl-query/basic.txt

# `resolvectl query NAME` prints the resolved addresses, then "-- ..." metadata
# lines:
#   example.com: 93.184.216.34                      -- link: eth0
#                2606:2800:220:1:248:1893:25c8:1946 -- link: eth0
#   -- Information acquired via protocol DNS in 24.1ms.
# This is a single observation (key/value snapshot): one wide record with the
# query name, the IPv4/IPv6 answers and the resolving link.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"-- link:"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Information acquired via protocol"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
        /-- link:/ {
            # Split off the "-- link: X" trailer.
            head=$0; sub(/[ \t]*--[ \t]*link:.*$/,"",head)
            lk=$0; sub(/^.*--[ \t]*link:[ \t]*/,"",lk); gsub(/[ \t]+/,"",lk)
            link=lk
            # head is either "name: address" (first) or "address" (continuation).
            if (head ~ /:[ \t]/ && head !~ /^[ \t]/) {
                nm=head; sub(/:.*$/,"",nm); gsub(/[ \t]+/,"",nm); name=nm
                addr=head; sub(/^[^:]*:[ \t]*/,"",addr); gsub(/[ \t]+/,"",addr)
                ipv4=addr
            } else {
                a=head; gsub(/[ \t]+/,"",a); ipv6=a
            }
        }
        END{
            print "entry1.name " (name==""?"-":name)
            print "entry1.address " (ipv4==""?"-":ipv4)
            print "entry1.address_ipv6 " (ipv6==""?"-":ipv6)
            print "entry1.link " (link==""?"-":link)
            print "total_entries 1"
        }
    '
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: rfkill-list
## Description: Extract radio devices and block states from `rfkill list` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/rfkill-list/basic.txt

# `rfkill list` prints one block per radio device:
#   0: phy0: Wireless LAN
#           Soft blocked: no
#           Hard blocked: no
# The header line is `<id>: <name>: <type>`; the indented lines carry the soft
# and hard block states. Emit one record per DEVICE with id/name/type/soft/hard
# so the tidy melt renders one row per device.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Signature: a device header `<id>: <name>: <type>` AND both a
    # "Soft blocked:" and a "Hard blocked:" indented line.
    local has_header=0 has_soft=0 has_hard=0 line t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        case "$t" in
            [0-9]*": "*": "*) has_header=1 ;;
            "Soft blocked:"*) has_soft=1 ;;
            "Hard blocked:"*) has_hard=1 ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $has_header -eq 1 && $has_soft -eq 1 && $has_hard -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line t n=0
    local id="" name="" type="" soft="" hard=""

    _rfkill_flush () {
        [[ -z "$id" ]] && return
        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.id ${id}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.name ${name:-unknown}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.type ${type}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.soft ${soft:-unknown}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.hard ${hard:-unknown}"$'\n'
    }

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && continue

        case "$t" in
            [0-9]*": "*": "*)
                _rfkill_flush
                id="${t%%:*}"
                local rest="${t#*: }"          # "name: type"
                name="${rest%%:*}"
                type="${rest#*: }"
                soft=""; hard=""
                ;;
            "Soft blocked:"*) soft="${t#*: }" ;;
            "Hard blocked:"*) hard="${t#*: }" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    _rfkill_flush

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ssh-keyscan
## Description: Extract host public-key records from ssh-keyscan output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/ssh-keyscan/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # ssh-keyscan lines: "<host> <keytype> <base64>", with "#"-comment lines.
    local n=0 line kt
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 3 ]] || continue
        kt="${f[1]}"
        case "$kt" in
            ssh-rsa|ssh-dss|ssh-ed25519|ecdsa-sha2-*|sk-ssh-ed25519@*|sk-ecdsa-*)
                n=$((n + 1)) ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $n -ge 2 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local line host keytype
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 3 ]] || continue
        keytype="${f[1]}"
        case "$keytype" in
            ssh-rsa|ssh-dss|ssh-ed25519|ecdsa-sha2-*|sk-ssh-ed25519@*|sk-ecdsa-*) : ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac
        host="${f[0]}"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.host ${host}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.keytype ${keytype}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: sslscan
## Description: Extract accepted/preferred cipher rows from sslscan output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/sslscan/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    if [[ "$text" == *"Supported Server Cipher"* ]] \
       || { [[ "$text" == *"Accepted"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"bits"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"TLS"* ]]; }; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Cipher rows: "Preferred|Accepted  <proto>  <bits> bits  <cipher>"
        case "$line" in
            Preferred[[:space:]]*|Accepted[[:space:]]*) : ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac

        read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
        # status proto bits "bits" cipher
        [[ ${#_arr[@]} -lt 5 ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        local p="entry${n}."
        result+="${p}status ${_arr[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}protocol ${_arr[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}bits ${_arr[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}cipher ${_arr[4]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: tcpdump-summary
## Description: Extract packet summaries from `tcpdump` line-summary output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/tcpdump-summary/basic.txt

# `tcpdump` (default summary mode) prints a `verbose output suppressed` banner
# and a `listening on ...` line, then one line per packet:
#   14:22:31.482910 IP 192.168.1.24.51234 > 93.184.216.34.443: Flags [S], ... length 0
# We emit one record per packet (time, src, dst, flags, length), skipping the
# banner / listening lines.

# Strip a Flags token like `[S.],` down to `S.`.
_tcpdump_flags () {
    local f="$1"
    f="${f#[}"; f="${f%%]*}"
    printf '%s' "${f:-NONE}"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"tcpdump: verbose output suppressed"* ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        # Packet lines begin with an HH:MM:SS timestamp.
        case "${f[0]}" in
            [0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]*) ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac

        local time="${f[0]}" src="" dst="" flags="NONE" length="NONE"
        local i=0
        # src / dst straddle the ">" arrow: <src> > <dst>:
        for ((i=0; i<${#f[@]}; i++)); do
            case "${f[$i]}" in
                ">")     src="${f[$((i-1))]}"; dst="${f[$((i+1))]%:}" ;;
                Flags)   flags=$(_tcpdump_flags "${f[$((i+1))]}") ;;
                length)  length="${f[$((i+1))]}" ;;
            esac
        done

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.time ${time}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.src ${src:-NONE}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.dst ${dst:-NONE}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.flags ${flags}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.length ${length}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=e5ab3935168251899705173b722b7a81f5f727de9394144643ce9788312f9a03===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: vnstat
## Description: Extract monthly traffic totals from `vnstat` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/vnstat/basic.txt

# `vnstat` (monthly view) prints a title, a `month rx | tx | total | avg. rate`
# header, a `----` rule, one row per month, another rule, and an `estimated`
# footer:
#    2026-05      42.18 GiB |    8.91 GiB |   51.09 GiB |  158.72 kbit/s
# We emit one record per real month row, skipping title / header / rule /
# estimated. Values (number + unit) have spaces collapsed to underscores.

# Collapse a whitespace-separated segment into a single underscore token.
_vnstat_val () {
    local -a t=()
    read -ra t <<< "$1"
    local out="" x
    for x in "${t[@]}"; do out="${out:+${out}_}${x}"; done
    printf '%s' "${out:-NONE}"
}

# Is the first token a YYYY-MM month stamp?
_vnstat_is_month () {
    local -a t=()
    read -ra t <<< "$1"
    case "${t[0]}" in
        [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"avg. rate"* && "$text" == *"estimated"* ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        _vnstat_is_month "$line" || continue

        local -a segs=()
        IFS='|' read -ra segs <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#segs[@]} -lt 4 ]] && continue

        local -a m=()
        read -ra m <<< "${segs[0]}"
        local month="${m[0]}"
        # rx is the rest of segment 0 after the month stamp.
        local rx=""; local i
        for ((i=1; i<${#m[@]}; i++)); do rx="${rx:+${rx}_}${m[$i]}"; done

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.month ${month}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.rx ${rx:-NONE}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.tx $(_vnstat_val "${segs[1]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.total $(_vnstat_val "${segs[2]}")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.rate $(_vnstat_val "${segs[3]}")"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: 7z
## Description: Extract file entries from `7z l` archive listings (skips header rule + totals footer)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/7z/basic.txt

# `7z l` prints a column header ("Date Time Attr Size Compressed Name"), a
# dashed rule, one row per archived file, a second dashed rule, then a totals
# footer ("<date> <time>  <size> <comp>  N files"). Only the rows between the two
# rules are data Aje28094Aj the header, rules, and footer are skipped so the count is
# exact.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive 7z listing header: Attr + Compressed + Name columns.
    [[ "$text" == *"Attr"* && "$text" == *"Compressed"* && "$text" == *"Name"* ]] || return 1
    # Must have a dashed rule line.
    local line stripped
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        stripped="${line//[- ]/}"
        if [[ -z "$stripped" && "$line" == *-* ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 in_data=0 line stripped
    local -a t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        stripped="${line//[- ]/}"
        if [[ -z "$stripped" && "$line" == *-* ]]; then
            if [[ $in_data -eq 0 ]]; then in_data=1; else in_data=0; fi
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_data -eq 1 ]] || continue
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#t[@]} -ge 6 ]] || continue
        local name="" i
        for ((i=5; i<${#t[@]}; i++)); do name+="${t[i]}_"; done
        name="${name%_}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.date ${t[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.time ${t[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.attr ${t[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.size ${t[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.compressed ${t[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: bundle-outdated
## Description: Extract outdated gems from `bundle outdated` output (skips fetch preamble + header)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/bundle-outdated/basic.txt

# `bundle outdated` prints a "Fetching gem metadata..." / "Resolving
# dependencies..." preamble, then a column header
# ("Gem  Current  Latest  Requested  Groups"), then one row per outdated gem.
# The preamble and header are noise; only the gem rows are data. Each gem becomes
# a record with its name and its current/latest versions.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: bundler's fetch preamble plus the Current/Latest header.
    [[ "$text" == *"Fetching gem metadata"* ]] || return 1
    local line has_header=0 rows=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == Gem*Current*Latest* ]]; then
            has_header=1
            continue
        fi
        # A gem row: name, then two version-looking tokens (start with a digit).
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+[[:space:]]+[0-9][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9][^[:space:]]* ]]; then
            rows=$((rows + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_header -eq 1 && $rows -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line name current latest
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == Gem*Current*Latest* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+[[:space:]]+[0-9][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9][^[:space:]]* ]] || continue
        # First three whitespace-separated tokens: name, current, latest.
        read -r name current latest _ <<< "$line"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.current ${current}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.latest ${latest}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: dbmate-status
## Description: Extract migrations from `dbmate status` output ([X]/[ ] lines; skips Applied/Pending footer)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/dbmate-status/basic.txt

# `dbmate status` prints one line per migration: "[X] <name>" (applied) or
# "[ ] <name>" (pending), followed by an "Applied: N / Pending: M" summary
# footer. Only the bracketed migration lines are data.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # NB: no _is_json guard here Aje28094Aj dbmate rows start with "[", which the naive
    # leading-bracket JSON check would misread as a JSON array.
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^\[[X\ ]\][[:space:]] ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^\[[X\ ]\][[:space:]] ]] || continue
        local flag="${line:1:1}" name status
        name="${line:4}"
        while [[ "$name" == " "* ]]; do name="${name# }"; done
        if [[ "$flag" == "X" ]]; then status="applied"; else status="pending"; fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.status ${status}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash

## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/flatpak-remotes/basic.txt

# `flatpak remotes` prints a "Name  Options" header then one remote per line as
# "<name>  <options>" (columns separated by runs of spaces). Each data row is

#!/bin/bash
## Name: liquibase-status
## Description: Extract pending changesets from `liquibase status` output (path::id::author)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/liquibase-status/basic.txt

# `liquibase status` prints an "N changesets have not been applied ..." header
# then one indented line per pending changeset of the form
# "<path>::<id>::<author>". The header is skipped; each "::"-delimited line
# becomes a record.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Require the liquibase status banner AND a `path::id::author` changeset line.
    # The banner keys this to liquibase Aje28094Aj a bare `::.*::` match would otherwise grab
    # IPv6 socket rows (ss/netstat `:::80  :::*`).
    [[ "$text" == *"not been applied"* || "$text" == *"changeset"* || "$text" == *"changeSet"* ]] || return 1
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" != *"["* && "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]:/]*/[^[:space:]]*::[^[:space:]:]+::[^[:space:]:]+ ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"::"*"::"* ]] || continue
        local body="$line"
        while [[ "$body" == " "* ]]; do body="${body# }"; done
        local path="${body%%::*}"
        local rest="${body#*::}"
        local id="${rest%%::*}"
        local author="${rest#*::}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.path ${path}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.id ${id}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.author ${author}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: unzip
## Description: Extract file entries from `unzip -l` listings (skips banner/header + rule + totals footer)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/unzip/basic.txt

# `unzip -l` prints an "Archive:  <name>" banner, a "Length Date Time Name"
# column header, a dashed rule, one row per archived file, a second dashed rule,
# then a totals footer ("<total>  N files"). Only the rows between the two rules
# are data.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive unzip -l banner + header columns.
    [[ "$text" == *"Archive:"* && "$text" == *"Length"* && "$text" == *"Name"* ]] || return 1
    local line stripped
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        stripped="${line//[- ]/}"
        if [[ -z "$stripped" && "$line" == *-* ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 in_data=0 line stripped
    local -a t
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        stripped="${line//[- ]/}"
        if [[ -z "$stripped" && "$line" == *-* ]]; then
            if [[ $in_data -eq 0 ]]; then in_data=1; else in_data=0; fi
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_data -eq 1 ]] || continue
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#t[@]} -ge 4 ]] || continue
        local name="" i
        for ((i=3; i<${#t[@]}; i++)); do name+="${t[i]}_"; done
        name="${name%_}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.length ${t[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.date ${t[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.time ${t[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: perf-counters
## Description: `perf stat` counter table Aje28692Aj one tidy row per counter (count, event)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 18
## Sample: samples/perf-counters/basic.txt

# `perf stat` prints a "Performance counter stats for '<cmd>'" banner followed by
# one line per counter:
#     8,412.33 msec task-clock            #    0.842 CPUs utilized
#        1,204      context-switches      #  143.121 /sec
# and a trailing "N seconds time elapsed" summary. Each counter line begins with
# a (comma-grouped) number and ends Aje28094Aj before any "#" annotation Aje28094Aj with the event
# identifier. Tidied to one row per counter: (count, event).

_pc_is_counter () {
    # Leading spaces, then a number (comma/dot ok), then whitespace. Excludes the
    # banner (starts with a letter) and blank lines.
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9,\.]*[[:space:]] ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"Performance counter stats for"* ]] || return 1
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _pc_is_counter "$line" && { _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86; return 0; }
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _pc_is_counter "$line" || continue
        # Drop the trailing "N seconds time elapsed" wall-clock summary.
        [[ "$line" == *"time elapsed"* ]] && continue
        # Keep only the counter portion, before any "#" annotation.
        local body="${line%%#*}"
        local toks; toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$body"
        local ntok=${#toks[@]}
        [[ $ntok -ge 2 ]] || continue
        local count="${toks[0]}"
        count="${count//,/}"
        local event="${toks[$((ntok - 1))]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.count ${count}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.event ${event}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: aureport
## Description: Extract audit events from `aureport` summary output (skips title + column header)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/aureport/basic.txt

# `aureport` prints a title line ("Authentication Report"), a "====" rule, a
# column header ("# date time acct host term exe success event"), another rule,
# then numbered event rows ("N. date time acct host term exe success event"). The
# title, rules, and header are noise; each numbered row becomes a record whose
# fields are the eight audit columns.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: the aureport column header plus numbered event rows.
    [[ "$text" =~ (^|$'\n')#[[:space:]]+date[[:space:]]+time ]] || return 1
    local line rows=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[[:space:]] ]]; then
            rows=$((rows + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $rows -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line rest
    local date time acct host term exe success event
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[[:space:]] ]] || continue
        # Drop the leading "N." record number, keep the eight columns.
        rest="${line#*.}"
        read -r date time acct host term exe success event _ <<< "$rest"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.date ${date}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.time ${time}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.acct ${acct}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.host ${host}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.term ${term}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.exe ${exe}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.success ${success}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.event ${event}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: fail2ban-status
## Description: Extract jail status from fail2ban-client status output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 10
## Technique: kv_colon
## Sample: samples/fail2ban-status/sample1.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # fail2ban-client status output contains "Number of jail" and "Jail list"
    # fail2ban-client status <jail> contains "Currently banned" and "Total banned"
    local has_jail=0
    local has_banned=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"Jail list"* || "$line" == *"Number of jail"* ]] && has_jail=1
        [[ "$line" == *"Currently banned"* || "$line" == *"Total banned"* ]] && has_banned=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_jail -eq 1 || $has_banned -eq 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local section=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local trimmed="$line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done
        # Remove leading "|- " or "`- " tree markers
        case "$trimmed" in
            "|- "*) trimmed="${trimmed#|- }" ;;
            "\`- "*) trimmed="${trimmed#\`- }" ;;
        esac

        # Track sections
        case "$trimmed" in
            "Status for the jail:"*|"Status")
                continue
                ;;
            *"Filter"*)
                section="filter"
                continue
                ;;
            *"Actions"*)
                section="actions"
                continue
                ;;
        esac

        # Parse key: value pairs
        if [[ "$trimmed" == *":"* ]]; then
            local key="${trimmed%%:*}"
            local val="${trimmed#*:}"
            while [[ "$val" == " "* ]]; do val="${val# }"; done
            while [[ "$val" == *" " ]]; do val="${val% }"; done
            # Normalize key
            key="${key// /_}"
            # Lowercase key
            key="${key,,}"
            [[ -z "$val" ]] && continue
            if [[ -n "$section" ]]; then
                result+="${section}.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
            else
                result+="${key} ${val}"$'\n'
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===

===META: mode=644 sha256=6d7ca4ddab3b541a63bc0e0793807dd4f2d9bb2e77207618b86d831448ba9b4c===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: gpg-card-status
## Description: `gpg --card-status` dotted "Field ....: value" snapshot
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/gpg-card-status/basic.txt

# `gpg --card-status` prints a fixed set of "Label <dots>: value" lines whose
# labels are padded with dots for alignment. A generic key/value parser keeps
# the trailing dots in the field name and can trip on values with spaces; this
# lifts the whole card into one wide record.

_gpgcs_key () {
    local s="$1" out="" c i n=${#1}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${s:i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    while [[ "$out" == *__* ]]; do out="${out//__/_}"; done
    out="${out#_}"; out="${out%_}"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

_gpgcs_val () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/ }"
    while [[ "$v" == *"  "* ]]; do v="${v//  / }"; done
    v="${v# }"; v="${v% }"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    # Distinctive: the dotted, colon-aligned card fields. Require several
    # dotted labels plus the OpenPGP-card-specific "Application ID" line.
    local line dotted=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z].*\.\.+[[:space:]]*: ]] && dotted=$((dotted + 1))
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $dotted -ge 4 ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Application ID"* ]] || return 1

    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line key val

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *:* ]] || continue
        key="${line%%:*}"
        val="${line#*:}"
        # Drop the alignment dots from the label.
        key="${key//./ }"
        key="$(_gpgcs_key "$key")"
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        val="$(_gpgcs_val "$val")"
        result+="entry1.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/security/gpg-list-keys.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=d0a8ddda0cfdf6acb7bf6b2624e29ae799dfd5a1aaf1fcc26e677a8c36a8ac41===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: gpg-list-keys
## Description: Extract a single key snapshot from `gpg --list-keys`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 19
## Sample: samples/gpg-list-keys/basic.txt

# `gpg --list-keys` prints a keyring block:
#   pub   rsa4096/3AA5C34371567BD2 2026-01-15 [SC]
#         <fingerprint>
#   uid   [ultimate] Alice Example <alice@example.com>
#   sub   rsa4096/42B317FD4BA89E7A 2026-01-15 [E]
# Emit one record summarising the primary key.

_gpg_is_pub () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^pub[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]/]+/[0-9A-Fa-f]{8,40}[[:space:]] ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _gpg_is_pub "$line"; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local keyid="" created="" uid=""
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ $entry -eq 0 ]] && _gpg_is_pub "$line"; then
            read -ra _a <<< "$line"
            local algo_key="${_a[1]}"
            keyid="${algo_key#*/}"
            created="${_a[2]}"
            entry=1
        elif [[ "$line" =~ ^uid[[:space:]] && -z "$uid" ]]; then
            uid="${line#uid}"
            uid="${uid#"${uid%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            # drop leading [validity] marker if present
            [[ "$uid" == \[*\]* ]] && uid="${uid#*] }"
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $entry -eq 1 ]]; then
        result+="entry1.type pub"$'\n'
        result+="entry1.keyid ${keyid}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$uid" ]] && result+="entry1.uid ${uid}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$created" ]] && result+="entry1.created ${created}"$'\n'
        result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    fi
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/security/keytool-list.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=5048af9a79c8ed308bd4c4ca027a5142ce6c3f8ed087739fa2fee9395b201689===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: keytool-list
## Description: Extract keystore entries from `keytool -list`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/keytool-list/basic.txt

# `keytool -list` prints a banner then one comma-separated line per keystore
# entry:
#   mykey, Mar 01 2024, PrivateKeyEntry, A1:B2:C3:...
# i.e. alias, date, entry-type, fingerprint. Emit ONE record per entry with the
# alias, date and type (the fingerprint is dropped). Rows are identified by the
# entry-type field so banner lines never match.

_kt_trim () {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    s="${s%"${s##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

_kt_sanitize_val () {
    local v; v="$(_kt_trim "$1")"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Signature: keystore banner plus at least one recognisable entry type.
    [[ "$text" == *"Keystore type"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"PrivateKeyEntry"* || "$text" == *"trustedCertEntry"* \
       || "$text" == *"SecretKeyEntry"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line typ alias date
    local -a f
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *,* ]] || continue
        IFS=',' read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 3 ]] || continue
        typ="$(_kt_trim "${f[2]}")"
        case "$typ" in
            PrivateKeyEntry|trustedCertEntry|SecretKeyEntry) ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac
        alias="$(_kt_sanitize_val "${f[0]}")"
        date="$(_kt_sanitize_val "${f[1]}")"
        [[ -z "$alias" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.alias ${alias}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.date ${date}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.type ${typ}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/security/nmap.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=825589fe58a79d7a6b7b22ffc34fc9e5b1b974fa397b796971b02a182739bf17===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: nmap
## Description: Extract fields from nmap scan output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 15
## Sample: samples/nmap/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    # Contains "Nmap scan report" or "PORT  STATE  SERVICE" header
    [[ "$text" == *"Nmap scan report"* ]] && return 0
    [[ "$text" =~ PORT[[:space:]]+STATE[[:space:]]+SERVICE ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local in_ports=0
    local port_num=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Extract host info: "Nmap scan report for example.com (93.184.216.34)"
        if [[ "$line" == *"Nmap scan report for"* ]]; then
            local host ip
            local after="${line#*report for }"
            # Try to extract host and IP from "for host (ip)" pattern
            if [[ "$after" == *"("*")"* ]]; then
                host="${after%% (*}"
                ip="${after#*(}"
                ip="${ip%%)*}"
            else
                host="$after"
                ip=""
            fi
            result+="host ${host}"$'\n'
            [[ -n "$ip" ]] && result+="ip ${ip}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi

        # Extract latency: "Host is up (0.023s latency)."
        if [[ "$line" == *"Host is up"* ]]; then
            if [[ "$line" == *"("*"latency)"* ]]; then
                local latency="${line#*(}"
                latency="${latency%% latency)*}"
                result+="latency ${latency}"$'\n'
            fi
            continue
        fi

        # Detect port table header
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^PORT[[:space:]]+STATE[[:space:]]+SERVICE ]]; then
            in_ports=1
            continue
        fi

        # Parse port lines: "22/tcp  open  ssh  OpenSSH 8.9"
        if [[ $in_ports -eq 1 ]]; then
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+/ ]]; then
                port_num=$((port_num + 1))
                read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
                local port="${_arr[0]}"
                local state="${_arr[1]}"
                local service="${_arr[2]}"
                # Version is everything from field 4 onward
                local version_str=""
                local i
                for ((i=3; i<${#_arr[@]}; i++)); do
                    if [[ -n "$version_str" ]]; then
                        version_str+="_"
                    fi
                    version_str+="${_arr[$i]}"
                done

                result+="port${port_num}.port ${port}"$'\n'
                result+="port${port_num}.state ${state}"$'\n'
                result+="port${port_num}.service ${service}"$'\n'
                [[ -n "$version_str" ]] && result+="port${port_num}.version ${version_str}"$'\n'
            else
                in_ports=0
            fi
        fi

        # Extract scan summary: "Nmap done: 1 IP scanned in 12.34 seconds"
        if [[ "$line" == *"Nmap done:"* ]]; then
            if [[ "$line" == *"scanned in "* ]]; then
                local scan_time="${line#*scanned in }"
                result+="scan_time ${scan_time}"$'\n'
            fi
        fi

    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: semanage-boolean
## Description: Extract SELinux booleans from `semanage boolean -l` output (name, state, description)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/semanage-boolean/basic.txt

# `semanage boolean -l` prints a header
# ("SELinux boolean  State  Default Description"), a blank line, then one row per
# boolean: "<name>  (<state> , <default>)  <description>". The header is skipped;
# each boolean becomes a record with its name, current state, and description.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: the "SELinux boolean" header plus "(on/off , on/off)" rows.
    [[ "$text" == *"SELinux boolean"* ]] || return 1
    local line rows=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+[[:space:]]+\((on|off)[[:space:]]*, ]]; then
            rows=$((rows + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $rows -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line name state rest desc
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+[[:space:]]+\((on|off)[[:space:]]*, ]] || continue
        name="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        # State is the first token inside the parentheses.
        rest="${line#*\(}"
        state="${rest%%[[:space:]]*,*}"
        state="${state%%[[:space:]]*}"
        # Description follows the closing paren.
        desc="${line#*\)}"
        # Trim leading/trailing whitespace, collapse spaces to underscores.
        desc="${desc#"${desc%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        desc="${desc%"${desc##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        desc="${desc//[[:space:]]/_}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.state ${state}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.description ${desc}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: sshd-t
## Description: Extract effective sshd config from `sshd -T` (lowercase `key value` per line)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/sshd-t/basic.txt

# `sshd -T` dumps the effective server config, one directive per line as
# "key value" (space-separated, all-lowercase key, NOT colon-delimited), e.g.
#   permitrootlogin no
#   ciphers chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com,aes256-gcm@openssh.com
# Generic key/value parsers mangle the comma-lists and mis-split the values, so
# this strategy emits ONE wide record: entry1.<key> <value> for every line.

# Known sshd directive names Aje28094Aj used only to make detection specific.
_sshdt_known=" port addressfamily listenaddress permitrootlogin pubkeyauthentication \
passwordauthentication challengeresponseauthentication kbdinteractiveauthentication \
usepam x11forwarding maxauthtries maxsessions clientaliveinterval clientalivecountmax \
loglevel ciphers macs kexalgorithms permitemptypasswords "

_sshdt_sanitize_val () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local line key nb=0 hits=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        key="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        # Every non-blank line must be a lowercase-alnum directive key followed by
        # a value. This immediately rejects df-h ("/dev/sda1 ...", "Filesystem ...").
        [[ "$key" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || return 1
        [[ "$line" == *[[:space:]]* ]] || return 1
        [[ "$_sshdt_known" == *" $key "* ]] && hits=$((hits + 1))
        nb=$((nb + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $nb -ge 6 && $hits -ge 3 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line key value
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        key="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        [[ "$key" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$ ]] || continue
        value="${line#"$key"}"
        value="$(_sshdt_sanitize_val "$value")"
        entry=1
        result+="entry1.${key} ${value}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: systemd-analyze-security
## Description: Parse `systemd-analyze security` setting table (NAME DESCRIPTION EXPOSURE)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/systemd-analyze-security/basic.txt

# `systemd-analyze security <unit>` prints a table of hardening settings, each
# row prefixed with a Aje29c93Aj/Aje29c97Aj glyph: NAME, a free-text DESCRIPTION, and an optional
# EXPOSURE number. It ends with an "Aje28692Aj Overall exposure level ..." summary line.
# One record per setting row; header and summary are skipped.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"Overall exposure level"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"EXPOSURE"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
        {
            if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next
            if ($0 ~ /NAME[ \t]+DESCRIPTION[ \t]+EXPOSURE/) next
            if ($0 ~ /Overall exposure/) next
            # Remaining rows are glyph-prefixed settings: glyph NAME DESC [EXPOSURE].
            if (NF < 3) next
            name=$2
            expo=""
            last=$NF
            if (last ~ /^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$/) { expo=last; hi=NF-1 } else { hi=NF }
            desc=""
            for(i=3;i<=hi;i++) desc=desc (i>3?"_":"") $i
            e++
            print "entry" e ".name " name
            print "entry" e ".description " (desc==""?"-":desc)
            print "entry" e ".exposure " (expo==""?"-":expo)
        }
        END{ if(e>0) print "total_entries " e }
    '
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/security/vault-status.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=5f86702e4415fa75a9a46d85bd1cdc093953de175e8ca797d6a2d4f17ea7d4e4===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: vault-status
## Description: Extract the aligned Key/Value snapshot from `vault status` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 18
## Sample: samples/vault-status/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Distinctive signature: a "Key   Value" header, a "--- -----" underline,
    # and Vault-specific keys such as "Seal Type". df-h.txt has none of these.
    local line hdr=0 sep=0 seal=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "$line" in
            "Key"[[:space:]]*"Value"*) hdr=1 ;;
        esac
        case "$line" in
            "---"[[:space:]]*"---"*) sep=1 ;;
        esac
        case "$line" in
            "Seal Type"[[:space:]]*) seal=1 ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $hdr -eq 1 && $sep -eq 1 && $seal -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Skip the "Key   Value" header and the "--- -----" underline.
        case "$line" in
            "Key"[[:space:]]*"Value"*) continue ;;
            "---"*) continue ;;
        esac
        # Split at the first run of 2+ spaces: everything before is the key
        # (may contain single spaces, e.g. "Seal Type"), the rest is the value.
        local key value
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^(.*[^[:space:]])[[:space:]][[:space:]]+(.*)$ ]]; then
            key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        else
            continue
        fi
        # Trim trailing whitespace on the value.
        value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        # Sanitise key into a field name ("Seal Type" -> Seal_Type).
        local field="${key// /_}"
        [[ -n "$field" ]] || continue
        result+="entry1.${field} ${value}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ -n "$result" ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===
