===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/csv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=54e90c7585cb4cf88eda906f1664cd2182ded4697597facfc74c90533bc0f18a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: csv
## Description: Extract field names and values from CSV files (comma-delimited with header row)
## Version: 2.0
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/csv/basic.csv

# Split one CSV line into _CSV_FIELDS, RFC-4180-style. A double quote is
# STRUCTURAL only at field start (start of line, right after a comma, or after
# only spaces since the comma) Aje28094Aj `3/4"` keeps its literal inch mark, while
# `"Cash, operating"` protects its comma. Inside a quoted field `""` is an
# escaped quote. Sets _CSV_OPEN=1 when the line ends inside an open quoted
# field (i.e. the logical record continues on the next physical line).
_strat_csv_split () {
    local line="$1" field="" in_quotes=0 at_start=1 i c
    _CSV_FIELDS=()
    _CSV_OPEN=0
    for ((i=0; i<${#line}; i++)); do
        c="${line:$i:1}"
        if [[ $in_quotes -eq 1 ]]; then
            if [[ "$c" == '"' ]]; then
                if [[ "${line:$((i+1)):1}" == '"' ]]; then
                    field+='"'
                    ((i++))
                else
                    in_quotes=0
                fi
            else
                field+="$c"
            fi
        elif [[ "$c" == '"' && $at_start -eq 1 ]]; then
            in_quotes=1
            at_start=0
        elif [[ "$c" == ',' ]]; then
            _CSV_FIELDS+=("$field")
            field=""
            at_start=1
        else
            field+="$c"
            [[ "$c" != " " ]] && at_start=0
        fi
    done
    _CSV_FIELDS+=("$field")
    _CSV_OPEN=$in_quotes
}

# Drop THOUSANDS-SEPARATOR commas Aje28094Aj a digit immediately before the comma and
# EXACTLY THREE digits immediately after (not a 4th) Aje28094Aj from comma-counting
# only. The "exactly three, not a fourth" requirement is what makes this
# precise: it matches a true grouping comma ("1,234", apt's "[1,234 kB]", a
# status line's "2,341 kB/s") while correctly leaving alone a plain field
# separator that merely happens to sit between two digit-ish tokens, e.g. a
# region id ending in a digit followed by an ungrouped 6-digit count
# ("eu-west-1,881204" Aje28094Aj "881" then a 4th digit "2" disqualifies it, so the
# comma stays a real separator). A genuine list/field separator followed by a
# space ("[mean, p95, p99]", "88201, 882.01") never matches at all. Sets
# _CSV_NOTH.
_csv_strip_thousands () {
    local s="$1" out="" i c prev grp after
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++)); do
        c="${s:$i:1}"
        if [[ "$c" == ',' ]]; then
            prev="${s:$((i - 1)):1}"
            grp="${s:$((i + 1)):3}"
            after="${s:$((i + 4)):1}"
            if [[ "$prev" =~ [0-9] && "$grp" =~ ^[0-9][0-9][0-9]$ && ! "$after" =~ [0-9] ]]; then
                continue
            fi
        fi
        out+="$c"
    done
    _CSV_NOTH="$out"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="consistent comma count across lines"

    # TAB-dominant input is tsv's: `aws Aje280a6Aj --output text` emits TAB fields
    # whose VALUES contain commas ("my-logs, prod"). When every non-blank
    # line carries tabs and the tab count is uniform and >= the comma
    # count, the tabs are the real delimiter Aje28094Aj decline so tsv claims it.
    local _td_l _td_n=0 _td_first=-1 _td_uniform=1 _td_tabs _td_commas=0
    while IFS= read -r _td_l; do
        [[ -z "${_td_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _td_n=$((_td_n + 1))
        local _td_only="${_td_l//[!$'\t']/}"
        _td_tabs=${#_td_only}
        local _td_conly="${_td_l//[!,]/}"
        [[ ${#_td_conly} -gt $_td_commas ]] && _td_commas=${#_td_conly}
        [[ $_td_first -lt 0 ]] && _td_first=$_td_tabs
        [[ $_td_tabs -ne $_td_first || $_td_tabs -eq 0 ]] && { _td_uniform=0; break; }
        [[ $_td_n -ge 10 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $_td_n -ge 2 && $_td_uniform -eq 1 && $_td_first -ge 1 \
          && $_td_first -ge $_td_commas ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    # Check first 5 non-empty lines for CSV characteristics
    local line_count=0
    local header_commas=0
    local with_commas=0
    local matching=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        # Ignore commas inside parenthesised groups Aje28094Aj those are not CSV field
        # separators (`mount` options `(rw,nosuid,nodev)`). And ignore
        # THOUSANDS-SEPARATOR commas anywhere (apt's `[1,234 kB]`, a status
        # line's `2,341 kB/s`) Aje28094Aj counting only real separator commas keeps
        # csv from claiming such lines just because embedded grouping
        # punctuation happens to produce a similar comma count line-to-line
        # (apt-get's download progress, whose only "consistency" came from
        # repeated `[N,NNN kB]` tags).
        local _sep="${_line//(*)/}"
        _csv_strip_thousands "$_sep"; _sep="$_CSV_NOTH"
        # Count only commas OUTSIDE quoted fields: a quoted value's embedded
        # commas ("1,234,567.89", "go,api,server") are data, not separators.
        # Without this, quoted CSV fails the consistency check below and falls
        # through to a worse parser.
        _strat_csv_split "$_sep"
        local c=$(( ${#_CSV_FIELDS[@]} - 1 ))
        if [[ $line_count -eq 0 ]]; then
            # First line must have commas
            [[ $c -eq 0 ]] && return 1
            # Decline colon-delimited "key: value" lines whose commas are just
            # prose inside the value (e.g. `file` output: "name: desc, more, ...").
            # A `: ` before the first comma means this belongs to colons, not csv.
            local _before="${_sep%%,*}"
            [[ "$_before" == *": "* ]] && return 1
            header_commas=$c
        fi
        if [[ $c -gt 0 ]]; then
            with_commas=$((with_commas + 1))
            local diff=$(( header_commas - c ))
            if [[ ${diff#-} -le 1 ]]; then
                matching=$((matching + 1))
            fi
        fi
        line_count=$((line_count + 1))
        [[ $line_count -ge 5 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $line_count -lt 2 ]] && return 1

    # Real CSV: most lines should have commas (allow at most 1 without)
    [[ $with_commas -lt $((line_count - 1)) ]] && return 1

    # Of lines with commas, most should have consistent counts
    local threshold=3
    if [[ $with_commas -lt 3 ]]; then
        threshold=$with_commas
    fi
    [[ $matching -ge $threshold ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Strip UTF-8 BOM if present (EF BB BF)
    local bom
    bom=$(printf '\xef\xbb\xbf')
    text="${text#"$bom"}"

    # Pre-process: join multi-line quoted fields. A line whose RFC-4180 parse
    # ends inside an OPEN quoted field continues on the next physical line.
    # (Counting raw quote parity here would misfire on literal mid-field quotes
    # Aje28094Aj `3/4",100` is a complete row, not a continuation.)
    local processed=""
    local pending=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ -n "$pending" ]]; then
            pending+=" ${line}"
            _strat_csv_split "$pending"
            if [[ $_CSV_OPEN -eq 0 ]]; then
                processed+="${pending}"$'\n'
                pending=""
            fi
        else
            _strat_csv_split "$line"
            if [[ $_CSV_OPEN -eq 1 ]]; then
                pending="$line"
            else
                processed+="${line}"$'\n'
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ -n "$pending" ]]; then
        processed+="${pending}"$'\n'
    fi
    # Remove empty lines
    local _cleaned=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        _cleaned+="$_line"$'\n'
    done <<< "$processed"
    text="$_cleaned"

    # Parse header row for field names
    local header=""
    local _first=1
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        if [[ $_first -eq 1 ]]; then
            header="$_line"
            _first=0
            break
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    # Split header quote-aware too Aje28094Aj `"Last, First",Dept` is two columns, and a
    # naive IFS=',' split would misalign every data row against it.
    local headers; headers=()
    _strat_csv_split "$header"
    headers=("${_CSV_FIELDS[@]}")

    # Headerless numeric CSV Aje28094Aj data loggers (fio --write_bw_log / --write_iops_log,
    # `sar -o` CSV, collectd) emit raw rows with no header. If the FIRST row's
    # fields are all numeric, there is no header (a real header carries
    # non-numeric column names): synthesise A,B,CAje280a6Aj and keep row 1 as data.
    local _headerless=1
    [[ ${#headers[@]} -lt 2 ]] && _headerless=0
    local _hf
    for _hf in "${headers[@]}"; do
        _hf="${_hf#"${_hf%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; _hf="${_hf%"${_hf##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$_hf" || "$_hf" =~ ^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?%?$ ]] || { _headerless=0; break; }
    done
    # DUAL-ROW SHAPE test Aje28094Aj a header names its columns, so somewhere row 1
    # must be LABEL-shaped over a differently-shaped value (`age` over `30`).
    # When every column has the SAME shape in rows 1 and 2 (both numeric /
    # both IP-ish / both long mixed strings) AND at least one column is
    # value-shaped, row 1 is data (`Simple mixer control 'Master',0` over
    # `Aje280a6Aj'Headphone',0` Aje28094Aj amixer). Pure label-over-label tables (all-text,
    # no value shapes anywhere) keep their header.
    if [[ $_headerless -eq 0 && ${#headers[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
        local _dr2="" _dri=0 _drl
        while IFS= read -r _drl; do
            [[ -z "$_drl" ]] && continue
            _dri=$((_dri + 1))
            [[ $_dri -eq 2 ]] && { _dr2="$_drl"; break; }
        done <<< "$text"
        if [[ -n "$_dr2" ]]; then
            _strat_csv_split "$_dr2"
            local _drv=("${_CSV_FIELDS[@]}")
            _csv_shape () {
                local v="$1"
                v="${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"
                if [[ "$v" =~ ^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?[a-zA-Z%]{0,4}$ ]]; then echo num
                elif [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then echo ip
                elif [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} || "$v" =~ ^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2} ]]; then echo date
                else echo str
                fi
            }
            if [[ ${#_drv[@]} -eq ${#headers[@]} ]]; then
                local _drj _drcontrast=0 _drvaluish=0 _drs1 _drs2
                for ((_drj = 0; _drj < ${#headers[@]}; _drj++)); do
                    _drs1="$(_csv_shape "${headers[$_drj]}")"
                    _drs2="$(_csv_shape "${_drv[$_drj]:-}")"
                    [[ "$_drs1" == str && "$_drs2" != str ]] && _drcontrast=1
                    [[ "$_drs1" != str ]] && _drvaluish=1
                done
                [[ $_drcontrast -eq 0 && $_drvaluish -eq 1 ]] && _headerless=1
            fi
        fi
    fi
    if [[ $_headerless -eq 1 ]]; then
        local _hn=${#headers[@]} _hk
        headers=()
        for ((_hk=1; _hk<=_hn; _hk++)); do headers+=("$(_col_letter "$_hk")"); done
    fi

    # Clean BOM and whitespace from header names
    local hi
    for ((hi=0; hi<${#headers[@]}; hi++)); do
        local _h="${headers[$hi]}"
        while [[ "$_h" == " "* || "$_h" == "	"* ]]; do _h="${_h#?}"; done
        while [[ "$_h" == *" " || "$_h" == *"	" ]]; do _h="${_h%?}"; done
        headers[$hi]="$_h"
    done

    # Process each data row. Each row is emitted as an indexed record group
    # (entry<N>.<column>) so the capture tidy melt renders one row per record
    # with shared columns Aje28094Aj rather than welding every row's cells into a single
    # wide record with duplicate column names (where the format layer would even
    # drop a later row's field that repeats an earlier row's value).
    local result=""
    local row_num=0
    local rec=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        row_num=$((row_num + 1))
        [[ $row_num -eq 1 && $_headerless -eq 0 ]] && continue  # skip header (unless headerless)
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Parse the line field by field (same RFC-4180 splitter as the header:
        # quotes structural only at field start, "" escapes, literal otherwise)
        local values; values=()
        _strat_csv_split "$line"
        values=("${_CSV_FIELDS[@]}")

        rec=$((rec + 1))
        local j
        for ((j=0; j<${#headers[@]}; j++)); do
            local name="${headers[$j]}"
            local value="${values[$j]:-}"
            # Clean up name and value
            name="${name// /_}"
            name="${name//\"/}"
            name="${name#_}"
            name="${name%_}"
            name="${name//./_}"   # '.' would break the tidy melt's group key split
            # NOTE: no blanket quote-strip on the value Aje28094Aj the splitter already
            # consumed the structural quotes, so any quote still present is
            # literal data (3/4" inch marks, escaped "" quotes).
            # Trim leading/trailing whitespace (the header fields are trimmed the
            # same way above) so a ", value" delimiter's space isn't turned into a
            # leading underscore by the space->underscore step below.
            while [[ "$value" == " "* || "$value" == "	"* ]]; do value="${value#?}"; done
            while [[ "$value" == *" " || "$value" == *"	" ]]; do value="${value%?}"; done
            [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${rec}.${name} ${value}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $rec -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${rec}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/dns-records.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=61a20f9c6454d523c8ca93c1eaa8286f3b857a1fd3faf55b97bf1152e7fb249c===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: dns-records
## Description: BIND-style resource-record lines (name ttl class type rdata) Aje28094Aj dig/drill answers, zone dumps
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 8
## Sample: samples/dns-records/basic.txt

# The standard DNS presentation format every BIND-family tool prints:
#
#   example.com.   3600  IN  MX   5 mail.example.com.
#   example.com.   3600  IN  A    93.184.216.34
#
# One record per RR line, in ANY section (ANSWER/AUTHORITY/ADDITIONAL Aje28094Aj dig
# +trace and drill outputs interleave them). `;`-comment lines are skipped.
# MX rdata splits into preference/exchange; TXT rdata drops the surrounding
# quotes; other types keep rdata verbatim as `value`.

_dnsrr_line () {
    # Matches an RR presentation line. Captures: name ttl class type rdata.
    [[ "$1" =~ ^([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.?)[[:space:]]+([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+(IN|CH|HS)[[:space:]]+([A-Z0-9]+)[[:space:]]+(.*)$ ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local line hits=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == \;* ]] && continue
        if _dnsrr_line "$line"; then
            hits=$((hits + 1))
            if [[ $hits -ge 2 ]]; then
                _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    # A single RR line still counts when a dig/drill section marker confirms it.
    if [[ $hits -ge 1 && "$text" == *";; ANSWER SECTION"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line entry=0
    local name ttl class type rdata
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == \;* ]] && continue
        _dnsrr_line "$line" || continue
        name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        ttl="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        class="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
        type="${BASH_REMATCH[4]}"
        rdata="${BASH_REMATCH[5]}"
        rdata="${rdata%"${rdata##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        rdata="${rdata//$'\t'/ }"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.ttl ${ttl}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.class ${class}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.type ${type}"$'\n'
        case "$type" in
            MX)
                if [[ "$rdata" =~ ^([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+(.+)$ ]]; then
                    result+="entry${entry}.preference ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
                    result+="entry${entry}.exchange ${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"$'\n'
                else
                    result+="entry${entry}.value ${rdata}"$'\n'
                fi ;;
            TXT)
                rdata="${rdata#\"}"; rdata="${rdata%\"}"
                result+="entry${entry}.value ${rdata}"$'\n' ;;
            *)
                result+="entry${entry}.value ${rdata}"$'\n' ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/exposition-format.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=4716a2b9d183a276b02d4de0ccb34e283220430425ebcd2fdaa9b8a4a7c6f5af===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: exposition-format
## Description: Extract metrics from Prometheus/OpenMetrics exposition format (# TYPE, # HELP, # UNIT, labels)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 25
## Sample: samples/prometheus/basic.txt

# Merges prometheus and openmetrics strategies. The OpenMetrics format is a
# strict superset of Prometheus text format. Detects either:
#   - Prometheus: any # TYPE lines (with optional data lines)
#   - OpenMetrics: # EOF marker, # UNIT lines, OM-specific type names, or _created metrics

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90

    # Reject JSON
    _is_json "$1" && return 1

    local found_type=0 found_eof=0 found_unit=0 found_data=0 found_om_type=0 found_created=0
    local _re_type='^# TYPE [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* '
    local _re_data='^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\{.*\} '
    local _re_bare='^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* [0-9]'

    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_line" == "# EOF" ]] && found_eof=1
        [[ "$_line" == "# UNIT "* ]] && found_unit=1
        if [[ "$_line" =~ $_re_type ]]; then
            found_type=1
            [[ "$_line" == *" info" || "$_line" == *" stateset" || "$_line" == *" unknown" ]] && found_om_type=1
        fi
        [[ "$_line" =~ $_re_data ]] && found_data=1
        [[ "$_line" =~ $_re_bare ]] && found_data=1
        [[ "$_line" == *"_created "* || "$_line" == *"_created{"* ]] && found_created=1
        # Early exit once we have enough signal
        [[ $found_type -eq 1 && $found_data -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    done <<< "$text"

    # Accept Prometheus format: # TYPE lines (with or without data)
    [[ $found_type -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    # Accept OpenMetrics-specific signals
    [[ $found_eof -eq 1 && $found_type -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    [[ $found_unit -eq 1 && $found_type -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    [[ $found_om_type -eq 1 ]] && return 0
    [[ $found_created -eq 1 && $found_type -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local metric_num=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Skip # EOF marker (OpenMetrics)
        [[ "$line" == "# EOF" ]] && continue

        # Parse # HELP lines: "# HELP metric_name Description text"
        if [[ "$line" == "# HELP "* ]]; then
            local rest="${line#\# HELP }"
            local hname="${rest%% *}"
            local hdesc="${rest#* }"
            [[ "$hdesc" == "$hname" ]] && hdesc=""
            [[ -n "$hname" && -n "$hdesc" ]] && result+="${hname}.help ${hdesc}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi

        # Parse # TYPE lines: "# TYPE metric_name type_string"
        if [[ "$line" == "# TYPE "* ]]; then
            local rest="${line#\# TYPE }"
            local tname="${rest%% *}"
            local ttype="${rest#* }"
            [[ "$ttype" == "$tname" ]] && ttype=""
            [[ -n "$tname" && -n "$ttype" ]] && result+="${tname}.type ${ttype}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi

        # Parse # UNIT lines (OpenMetrics): "# UNIT metric_name unit"
        if [[ "$line" == "# UNIT "* ]]; then
            local rest="${line#\# UNIT }"
            local uname="${rest%% *}"
            local uunit="${rest#* }"
            [[ "$uunit" == "$uname" ]] && uunit=""
            [[ -n "$uname" && -n "$uunit" ]] && result+="${uname}.unit ${uunit}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi

        # Skip other comment lines
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue

        # Parse data lines
        # Format: metric_name{label="val",label2="val2"} value [timestamp]
        # or:     metric_name value [timestamp]
        local mname="" labels="" mvalue=""

        if [[ "$line" == *"{"* ]]; then
            mname="${line%%\{*}"
            local after_brace="${line#*\{}"
            labels="${after_brace%%\}*}"
            local after_close="${line#*\} }"
            [[ "$after_close" == "$line" ]] && continue
            read -ra _varr <<< "$after_close"
            mvalue="${_varr[0]}"
        else
            read -ra _varr <<< "$line"
            [[ ${#_varr[@]} -lt 2 ]] && continue
            mname="${_varr[0]}"
            mvalue="${_varr[1]}"
        fi

        # Validate metric name starts with letter or underscore
        local _re_mname='^[a-zA-Z_]'
        [[ ! "$mname" =~ $_re_mname ]] && continue

        # Validate value looks numeric (or special float values)
        local _re_val='^[0-9eE.+\-]'
        case "$mvalue" in
            NaN|Inf|+Inf|-Inf) ;;
            *) [[ ! "$mvalue" =~ $_re_val ]] && continue ;;
        esac

        metric_num=$((metric_num + 1))
        result+="metric${metric_num}.name ${mname}"$'\n'
        result+="metric${metric_num}.value ${mvalue}"$'\n'
        # Split the label set into one label.<key> field per label so the
        # melted table gets a real column per label key (method, code, cpuAje280a6Aj)
        # instead of a single opaque labels blob.
        if [[ -n "$labels" ]]; then
            local _lbl_rest="$labels" _lbl_pair _lbl_key _lbl_val
            while [[ -n "$_lbl_rest" ]]; do
                _lbl_pair="${_lbl_rest%%,*}"
                if [[ "$_lbl_rest" == *,* ]]; then _lbl_rest="${_lbl_rest#*,}"; else _lbl_rest=""; fi
                _lbl_key="${_lbl_pair%%=*}"
                _lbl_val="${_lbl_pair#*=}"
                _lbl_val="${_lbl_val#\"}"; _lbl_val="${_lbl_val%\"}"
                [[ -z "$_lbl_key" || "$_lbl_key" == "$_lbl_pair" ]] && continue
                _lbl_key="${_lbl_key//[[:space:]]/}"
                result+="metric${metric_num}.label_${_lbl_key} ${_lbl_val}"$'\n'
            done
        fi

    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/go-struct.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=35f7191121f97aec5fad0fd7ada69e8f1a558ab09630a462368a09d73edc3c72===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: go-struct
## Description: Go struct dumps Aje28094Aj {Key:value Key:value ...} banners (helm/kustomize/kubectl version)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/go-struct/basic.txt

# The `%+v` rendering Go tools print for version/build info:
#   version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.15.2", GitCommit:"a1b2c3d4", GoVersion:"go1.22.4"}
#   {Version:kustomize/v5.4.2 GitCommit:a1b2c3d4 GoOs:linux GoArch:amd64}
# One brace-wrapped struct per line, fields as `Key:value` separated by a space
# or `, `. Values may themselves contain colons (timestamps, paths), so fields
# are found by scanning for the next `<sep><Identifier>:` boundary rather than
# splitting on ':'. NOT JSON (keys are unquoted) Aje28094Aj the `":` guard keeps any
# real JSON with the json parsers.

# Field-boundary scan shared by detect and extract. Prints `key<TAB>value` per
# field of one struct body (the text between the braces).
_gostruct_fields () {
    printf '%s' "$1" | awk '
    {
        body=$0
        while (match(body, /(^|,?[ \t]+)[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*:/)) {
            # key starts after the separator, ends at the colon
            seg=substr(body, RSTART, RLENGTH)
            sub(/^,?[ \t]+/, "", seg)
            key=substr(seg, 1, length(seg)-1)
            rest=substr(body, RSTART+RLENGTH)
            # value runs until the next `<sep><Identifier>:` boundary (or EOL)
            if (match(rest, /,?[ \t]+[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*:/)) {
                val=substr(rest, 1, RSTART-1); body=substr(rest, RSTART)
            } else { val=rest; body="" }
            sub(/,[ \t]*$/, "", val)
            gsub(/^"|"$/, "", val)
            if (key!="" && val!="") printf "%s\t%s\n", key, val
        }
    }'
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="brace-wrapped Key:value struct lines (Go %+v)"

    # Quoted keys mean JSON, not a Go struct dump.
    [[ "$text" == *'":'* ]] && return 1

    local nonblank=0 structs=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        [[ $nonblank -gt 5 ]] && return 1   # a banner, not a document
        # optional `pkg.Type` prefix, then {...} spanning the rest of the line
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z0-9_.]*\{(.+)\}[[:space:]]*$ ]] || return 1
        local body="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" nf
        # a leading `Key:` plus the scanner finding >=2 fields
        [[ "$body" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*: ]] || return 1
        nf="$(_gostruct_fields " $body" | grep -c .)"
        [[ "$nf" -ge 2 ]] || return 1
        structs=$((structs + 1))
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $structs -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    # Count struct lines first: one struct is a kv snapshot (plain `key value`
    # pairs -> one wide row); several are records (entry<N>.<key> groups).
    local lines=() _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        lines+=("$_l")
    done <<< "$text"

    local result="" entry=0 li kv k v
    for ((li = 0; li < ${#lines[@]}; li++)); do
        [[ "${lines[$li]}" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z0-9_.]*\{(.+)\}[[:space:]]*$ ]] || continue
        local body=" ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        while IFS=$'\t' read -r k v; do
            [[ -z "$k" ]] && continue
            k="${k//./_}"
            if [[ ${#lines[@]} -eq 1 ]]; then result+="${k} ${v}"$'\n'
            else result+="entry${entry}.${k} ${v}"$'\n'; fi
        done <<< "$(_gostruct_fields "$body")"
    done
    [[ ${#lines[@]} -gt 1 && $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/structured/grafana-alerts.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=56c9909c9134bfce2cd4cd1e67f895e32c024ce61cf2fb09f07dca4ec4d39b26===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: grafana-alerts
## Description: Extract alert information from Grafana alert list output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 25
## Sample: samples/grafana-alerts/sample1.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Grafana alert list (CLI output) has columns like ID, TITLE, STATE, HEALTH
    local first_line=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        first_line="$_line"
        break
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ "$first_line" == *"ID"* && "$first_line" == *"TITLE"* && "$first_line" == *"STATE"* ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    # Also match Grafana alerting rule format with labels
    local has_alertname=0
    local has_state=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"alertname"* ]] && has_alertname=1
        [[ "$line" == *"firing"* || "$line" == *"pending"* || "$line" == *"inactive"* ]] && has_state=1
        if [[ $has_alertname -eq 1 && $has_state -eq 1 ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local alert_n=0
    local past_header=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Table format header
        if [[ "$line" == *"ID"* && "$line" == *"TITLE"* && "$line" == *"STATE"* ]]; then
            past_header=1
            continue
        fi
        # Skip separator lines
        [[ "$line" == "---"* || "$line" == "==="* ]] && continue

        [[ $past_header -eq 0 ]] && continue

        read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#_arr[@]} -lt 3 ]] && continue

        alert_n=$((alert_n + 1))
        local prefix="alert${alert_n}"

        local id="${_arr[0]}"
        result+="${prefix}.id ${id}"$'\n'

        # State is typically the last or second-to-last token
        local state=""
        local health=""
        local i
        for ((i=1; i<${#_arr[@]}; i++)); do
            case "${_arr[$i]}" in
                firing|pending|inactive|normal|alerting|ok|paused|no_data|error)
                    if [[ -z "$state" ]]; then
                        state="${_arr[$i]}"
                    else
                        health="${_arr[$i]}"
                    fi
                    ;;
            esac
        done

        # Title is tokens between ID and state keywords
        local title=""
        for ((i=1; i<${#_arr[@]}; i++)); do
            case "${_arr[$i]}" in
                firing|pending|inactive|normal|alerting|ok|paused|no_data|error) break ;;
                *)
                    if [[ -z "$title" ]]; then
                        title="${_arr[$i]}"
                    else
                        title="${title}_${_arr[$i]}"
                    fi
                    ;;
            esac
        done

        [[ -n "$title" ]] && result+="${prefix}.title ${title}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$state" ]] && result+="${prefix}.state ${state}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$health" ]] && result+="${prefix}.health ${health}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/grouped-rows.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=179540903e36db5353a1dcc966a00f9d34351b8e8d6f8d9c9a132e074f9a99ce===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: grouped-rows
## Description: Group-header lines over indented tabular rows Aje28094Aj the group keys carried down onto each leaf row
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 41
## Sample: samples/grouped-rows/basic.txt

# The nested-records shape: an outer GROUP line establishing context, then
# INDENTED tabular rows that belong to it Aje28094Aj possibly through two levels:
#
#   Region: us-east-1                COMMAND=nginx  PID=1201  USER=www-data
#     AZ: us-east-1a                   FD   TYPE   DEVICE   NAME
#       i-0a11  m5.large  running      cwd  DIR    8,1      /
#       i-0a12  t3.micro  running      0u   CHR    1,3      /dev/null
#
# The lossless tidy carries each group's key(s) down onto its leaf rows:
# (region, az, A, B, C) / (command, pid, user, fd, type, device, name). A group
# line is either `Label: value` (one simple-token label) or a run of KEY=value
# tokens; a leaf row is TABULAR Aje28094Aj >=2 whitespace tokens that are NOT themselves
# `key: value` pairs (a kv block under a header is a hierarchy/yaml, not a
# grouped table, and stays with those parsers). A digit-free first leaf row over
# digit-bearing ones names the leaf columns (`Product Units Revenue`,
# `FD TYPE DEVICE NAME`); otherwise columns are synthesised. Subtotal/total
# leaf rows are data, per the corpus-wide convention.

# Classify a line. Sets:
#   _GR_KIND   group|leaf|blank|other
#   _GR_IND    leading-space count
#   _GR_KEYS   for a group: TAB-separated key=value pairs (label lowercased)
_gr_classify () {
    local l="$1"
    _GR_KIND="other"; _GR_IND=0; _GR_KEYS=""
    [[ -z "${l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && { _GR_KIND="blank"; return; }
    local ind="${l%%[![:space:]]*}"; _GR_IND=${#ind}
    local t="${l#"${l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    while [[ "$t" == *" " || "$t" == *$'\t' ]]; do t="${t%?}"; done
    # group form (b): >=2 KEY=value tokens (lsof-style COMMAND=nginx PID=1201)
    local _tk=() _n_eq=0 _tok
    read -ra _tk <<< "$t"
    for _tok in "${_tk[@]}"; do
        [[ "$_tok" == *=* ]] || continue
        local _k="${_tok%%=*}"
        case "$_k" in ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) ;; *) _n_eq=$((_n_eq + 1)) ;; esac
    done
    if [[ $_n_eq -ge 2 && $_n_eq -eq ${#_tk[@]} ]]; then
        _GR_KIND="group"
        local _kv
        for _tok in "${_tk[@]}"; do
            _kv="${_tok%%=*}"; _kv="$(printf '%s' "$_kv" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
            _GR_KEYS+="${_GR_KEYS:+$'\t'}${_kv}=${_tok#*=}"
        done
        return
    fi
    # group form (e): >=2 colon-terminated labels each followed by a value
    # token (`Filesystem UUID: 3f7a-c2e1  Label: data`) Aje28094Aj keys from the labels
    local _ei _elab=0 _ekeys=""
    for ((_ei = 0; _ei < ${#_tk[@]} - 1; _ei++)); do
        local _et="${_tk[$_ei]}"
        if [[ "$_et" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:$ ]]; then
            local _next="${_tk[$((_ei + 1))]}"
            [[ "$_next" =~ :$ ]] && continue
            _elab=$((_elab + 1))
            _ekeys+="${_ekeys:+$'\t'}$(printf '%s' "${_et%:}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')=${_next}"
        fi
    done
    if [[ $_elab -ge 2 ]]; then
        _GR_KIND="group"; _GR_KEYS="$_ekeys"
        return
    fi
    # group form (a): `Label: value` Aje28094Aj colon followed by whitespace, ONE simple
    # label, value NOT a long sentence (<=3 tokens keeps prose out). The
    # no-space variant (`group:web`) counts ONLY when it is alone on the line Aje28094Aj
    # `worker:w_02  STARTING` is a data row whose first cell contains a colon.
    if [[ "$t" =~ ^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*):[[:space:]]+([^[:space:]].*)$ ]]; then
        local _lab="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" _val="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        local _vt=(); read -ra _vt <<< "$_val"
        if [[ ${#_vt[@]} -le 3 ]]; then
            _GR_KIND="group"
            _GR_KEYS="$(printf '%s' "$_lab" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')=${_val}"
            return
        fi
    fi
    if [[ ${#_tk[@]} -eq 1 && "$t" =~ ^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*):([^[:space:]]+)$ ]]; then
        _GR_KIND="group"
        _GR_KEYS="$(printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        return
    fi
    # group form (c): trailing-colon block opener Aje28094Aj `Node node-01:`, `Videos:`
    # (<=3 tokens, colon only at the very end)
    if [[ "$t" =~ ^([A-Za-z][^:]{0,49}):$ ]]; then
        local _body="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        local _bt=(); read -ra _bt <<< "$_body"
        if [[ ${#_bt[@]} -ge 1 && ${#_bt[@]} -le 3 ]]; then
            _GR_KIND="group"
            if [[ ${#_bt[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
                _GR_KEYS="$(printf '%s' "${_bt[0]}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')=${_body#* }"
            else
                _GR_KEYS="group=${_bt[0]}"
            fi
            return
        fi
    fi
    # group form (d): a single bare token opening an indented block (`Images`,
    # `Documents`) Aje28094Aj classified group here; detection still demands the
    # tabular-leaf structure around it, so a lone word in prose never matters
    if [[ ${#_tk[@]} -eq 1 && "$t" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]]; then
        _GR_KIND="group"
        _GR_KEYS="group=${t}"
        return
    fi
    # a YAML list item is a mapping entry, never a grouped-table row Aje28094Aj treat as
    # unclassifiable so detection walks away from YAML documents entirely
    [[ "$t" == "- "* || "$t" == "-" ]] && return
    # leaf: >=2 tokens, not a kv pair itself
    if [[ ${#_tk[@]} -ge 2 && ! "$t" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
        _GR_KIND="leaf"
        _GR_NTOK=${#_tk[@]}
        return
    fi
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local _l groups=0 leaves=0 last_group_ind=-1 leaf_after_group=0 min_ind=-1
    local _lcounts=()
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        _gr_classify "$_l"
        case "$_GR_KIND" in
            blank) continue ;;
            group)
                # track the outermost indent; groups must live at it (or nested deeper)
                [[ $min_ind -lt 0 || $_GR_IND -lt $min_ind ]] && min_ind=$_GR_IND
                groups=$((groups + 1)); last_group_ind=$_GR_IND ;;
            leaf)
                [[ $min_ind -lt 0 ]] && min_ind=$_GR_IND
                leaves=$((leaves + 1)); _lcounts+=("$_GR_NTOK")
                [[ $last_group_ind -ge 0 && $_GR_IND -gt $last_group_ind ]] && leaf_after_group=$((leaf_after_group + 1)) ;;
            other) return 1 ;;   # prose or unclassifiable line Aje28094Aj not this shape
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    # >=2 groups, >=3 leaves, and most leaves sit deeper than a group
    [[ $groups -ge 2 && $leaves -ge 3 ]] || return 1
    [[ $((leaf_after_group * 3)) -ge $((leaves * 2)) ]] || return 1
    # a grouped TABLE has more rows than group headers Aje28094Aj a kv hierarchy where
    # most lines parse as "groups" (homectl, pgbackrest) is not this shape
    [[ $leaves -ge $groups ]] || return 1
    # leaves must be a table: a modal token count (Ajc2b1Aj1) covering >=70% of rows.
    # Hierarchy attribute lines (ifconfig's inet/ether/RX mix: 9,4,6,7 tokens)
    # vary far too much to qualify.
    local _ma _mb _mk _mbest=0 _modal=0
    for _ma in "${_lcounts[@]}"; do
        _mk=0
        for _mb in "${_lcounts[@]}"; do
            local _md=$(( _ma - _mb )); [[ ${_md#-} -le 1 ]] && _mk=$((_mk + 1))
        done
        [[ $_mk -gt $_mbest ]] && { _mbest=$_mk; _modal=$_ma; }
    done
    [[ $(( _mbest * 100 )) -ge $(( leaves * 70 )) ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=82
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="group headers over indented tabular rows"
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0
    # context stack: parallel arrays of indent + TAB-joined key=value pairs
    local ctx_ind=() ctx_keys=()
    # leaf sub-header per group block; only the FIRST leaf after a group may be
    # one (a later digit-free leaf Aje28094Aj "w_02  STARTING" Aje28094Aj is data)
    local subhdr=() subhdr_valid=0 first_leaf=0
    local _l i
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        _gr_classify "$_l"
        case "$_GR_KIND" in
            blank|other) continue ;;
            group)
                # pop contexts at same or deeper indent
                while [[ ${#ctx_ind[@]} -gt 0 && ${ctx_ind[$(( ${#ctx_ind[@]} - 1 ))]} -ge $_GR_IND ]]; do
                    unset 'ctx_ind[${#ctx_ind[@]}-1]'; unset 'ctx_keys[${#ctx_keys[@]}-1]'
                    ctx_ind=("${ctx_ind[@]}"); ctx_keys=("${ctx_keys[@]}")
                done
                ctx_ind+=("$_GR_IND"); ctx_keys+=("$_GR_KEYS")
                subhdr=(); subhdr_valid=0; first_leaf=1
                ;;
            leaf)
                # a leaf at (or above) a group's indent has LEFT that group Aje28094Aj
                # supervisorctl's trailing ungrouped `scheduler` row must not
                # inherit `group=worker`
                while [[ ${#ctx_ind[@]} -gt 0 && ${ctx_ind[$(( ${#ctx_ind[@]} - 1 ))]} -ge $_GR_IND ]]; do
                    unset 'ctx_ind[${#ctx_ind[@]}-1]'; unset 'ctx_keys[${#ctx_keys[@]}-1]'
                    ctx_ind=("${ctx_ind[@]}"); ctx_keys=("${ctx_keys[@]}")
                done
                local _tk=(); read -ra _tk <<< "${_l#"${_l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
                # a digit-free FIRST leaf right under a group is the sub-table
                # header naming the leaf columns
                if [[ $first_leaf -eq 1 && ! "$_l" =~ [0-9] ]]; then
                    subhdr=("${_tk[@]}"); subhdr_valid=1; first_leaf=0
                    continue
                fi
                first_leaf=0
                entry=$((entry + 1))
                # carried group keys (outermost first)
                local _c _pair
                for ((_c = 0; _c < ${#ctx_keys[@]}; _c++)); do
                    while IFS= read -r -d $'\t' _pair || [[ -n "$_pair" ]]; do
                        # the <<< herestring appends a newline that survives the
                        # tab-delimited read as a ghost pair Aje28094Aj strip and require
                        # a real key=value
                        _pair="${_pair//$'\n'/}"
                        [[ -z "$_pair" || "$_pair" != *=* ]] && continue
                        local _pk="${_pair%%=*}" _pv="${_pair#*=}"
                        _pk="${_pk// /_}"
                        result+="entry${entry}.${_pk} ${_pv}"$'\n'
                    done <<< "${ctx_keys[$_c]}"$'\t'
                done
                # leaf columns
                for ((i = 0; i < ${#_tk[@]}; i++)); do
                    local _name
                    if [[ $subhdr_valid -eq 1 && $i -lt ${#subhdr[@]} ]]; then
                        _name="${subhdr[$i]//./_}"; _name="${_name// /_}"
                    else
                        _name="$(_col_letter $((i + 1)))"
                    fi
                    [[ -z "${_tk[$i]}" ]] && continue
                    result+="entry${entry}.${_name} ${_tk[$i]}"$'\n'
                done
                ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE: extract/strategies/structured/har.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=2a58e7a3bae6967819eb4e4057d1c6082ef4bc7ccd2b0db2b4afa61a27ad6156===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: har
## Description: Extract request/response fields from HTTP Archive (HAR) files
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/har/basic.har

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90

    # Must be JSON
    _is_json "$1" || return 1

    # Must contain "log" and "entries" keys
    [[ "$text" == *'"log"'* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *'"entries"'* ]] || return 1

    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
        _strat_har_extract_jq "$text"
    else
        _strat_har_extract_fallback "$text"
    fi
}

_strat_har_extract_jq () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # Extract log-level fields
    local log_version
    log_version=$(echo "$text" | jq -r '.log.version // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true
    if [[ -n "$log_version" ]]; then
        result+="log.version ${log_version}"$'\n'
    fi

    local creator_name
    creator_name=$(echo "$text" | jq -r '.log.creator.name // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true
    if [[ -n "$creator_name" ]]; then
        local clean="${creator_name}"
        result+="log.creator.name ${clean}"$'\n'
    fi

    local creator_version
    creator_version=$(echo "$text" | jq -r '.log.creator.version // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true
    if [[ -n "$creator_version" ]]; then
        result+="log.creator.version ${creator_version}"$'\n'
    fi

    # Extract per-entry fields
    local entry_count
    entry_count=$(echo "$text" | jq -r '.log.entries | length' 2>/dev/null) || true
    if [[ -n "$entry_count" && "$entry_count" -gt 0 ]] 2>/dev/null; then
        local i=0
        while [[ $i -lt $entry_count ]]; do
            local n=$((i + 1))
            local prefix="entry${n}"

            local method
            method=$(echo "$text" | jq -r ".log.entries[$i].request.method // empty" 2>/dev/null) || true
            if [[ -n "$method" ]]; then
                result+="${prefix}.request.method ${method}"$'\n'
            fi

            local url
            url=$(echo "$text" | jq -r ".log.entries[$i].request.url // empty" 2>/dev/null) || true
            if [[ -n "$url" ]]; then
                local clean_url="${url}"
                result+="${prefix}.request.url ${clean_url}"$'\n'
            fi

            local status
            status=$(echo "$text" | jq -r ".log.entries[$i].response.status // empty" 2>/dev/null) || true
            if [[ -n "$status" ]]; then
                result+="${prefix}.response.status ${status}"$'\n'
            fi

            local status_text
            status_text=$(echo "$text" | jq -r ".log.entries[$i].response.statusText // empty" 2>/dev/null) || true
            if [[ -n "$status_text" ]]; then
                local clean_st="${status_text}"
                result+="${prefix}.response.statusText ${clean_st}"$'\n'
            fi

            local time_val
            time_val=$(echo "$text" | jq -r ".log.entries[$i].time // empty" 2>/dev/null) || true
            if [[ -n "$time_val" ]]; then
                result+="${prefix}.time ${time_val}"$'\n'
            fi

            i=$((i + 1))
        done
    fi

    echo "$result"
}

_strat_har_extract_fallback () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # Fallback: extract key fields using bash pattern matching
    local remaining="$text"
    while [[ "$remaining" == *'"'*':'* ]]; do
        local after_quote="${remaining#*\"}"
        local key="${after_quote%%\"*}"
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && break
        remaining="${after_quote#*\"}"
        remaining="${remaining#*:}"
        while [[ "$remaining" == " "* ]]; do remaining="${remaining# }"; done
        local value=""
        if [[ "$remaining" == '"'* ]]; then
            remaining="${remaining#\"}"
            value="${remaining%%\"*}"
            remaining="${remaining#*\"}"
        elif [[ "$remaining" =~ ^([0-9.eE+-]+) ]]; then
            value="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            remaining="${remaining#"$value"}"
        elif [[ "$remaining" == "true"* ]]; then
            value="true"; remaining="${remaining#true}"
        elif [[ "$remaining" == "false"* ]]; then
            value="false"; remaining="${remaining#false}"
        elif [[ "$remaining" == "null"* ]]; then
            value="null"; remaining="${remaining#null}"
        else
            break
        fi
        if [[ -n "$key" && -n "$value" ]]; then
            result+="${key} ${value}"$'\n'
        fi
    done

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/ini-sections.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=b1402ac6d4df777522bfe7909a87f71ef4157949b577b0d3f1aac2ca641e0792===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: ini-sections
## Description: Multi-section INI/config ([section] + key=value) flattened to (section, key, value) rows
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/ini-sections/basic.ini

# Classic INI / config-dump output Aje28094Aj several [section] blocks, each a run of
# `key = value` (or `key=value`) lines:
#
#     [server]                 [database]
#     host = 10.0.0.1          host = 10.0.0.5
#     port = 8080              port = 5432
#
# The plain `equals` parser flattens every pair into ONE wide record, which
# collides duplicate keys across sections (three `host` columns) and drops the
# section a value belongs to. The correct, lossless tidy is one row per pair with
# its section carried alongside: (section, key, value). We fire only when the
# section names are simple tokens AND distinct Aje28094Aj repeated-section block formats
# (ffprobe `[STREAM]Aje280a6Aj[/STREAM]`) and spaced section names (`[Unit foo.target]`)
# are left to their better-fitting parsers. `toml` (priority 15) still wins real
# TOML (quoted values, dotted/array tables) since it is tried first.
#
# The line classifier is inlined into both detect and extract (rather than a
# shared helper) on purpose: the engine unsets `_strat_*` helper functions
# between the detection sweep and extraction, so a helper would vanish before
# strategy_extract runs.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # INI legitimately begins with '['; only a leading '{' means real JSON here
    # (a bare _is_json check treats the opening [section] as a JSON array).
    case "${text#"${text%%[![:space:]]*}"}" in '{'*) return 1 ;; esac
    local _line l inner k _seen="|" _sec=0 _kv=0 _dup=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        l="$_line"
        while [[ "$l" == " "* || "$l" == $'\t'* ]]; do l="${l#?}"; done
        while [[ "$l" == *" " || "$l" == *$'\t' ]]; do l="${l%?}"; done
        [[ -z "$l" ]] && continue
        case "$l" in '#'*|';'*) continue ;; esac
        if [[ "$l" == "["*"]" ]]; then
            inner="${l#[}"; inner="${inner%]}"
            case "$inner" in
                ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*) ;;
                [A-Za-z]*)
                    _sec=$((_sec + 1))
                    case "$_seen" in *"|${inner}|"*) _dup=1 ;; esac
                    _seen="${_seen}${inner}|"
                    continue ;;
            esac
        fi
        if [[ "$l" == *"="* ]]; then
            k="${l%%=*}"
            while [[ "$k" == *" " || "$k" == *$'\t' ]]; do k="${k%?}"; done
            case "$k" in
                ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) ;;
                *) _kv=$((_kv + 1)) ;;
            esac
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $_sec -ge 2 && $_dup -eq 0 && $_kv -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="multi-section INI ([section] + key=value), distinct section names"
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 _line l inner k value section=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        l="$_line"
        while [[ "$l" == " "* || "$l" == $'\t'* ]]; do l="${l#?}"; done
        while [[ "$l" == *" " || "$l" == *$'\t' ]]; do l="${l%?}"; done
        [[ -z "$l" ]] && continue
        case "$l" in '#'*|';'*) continue ;; esac
        # section header?
        if [[ "$l" == "["*"]" ]]; then
            inner="${l#[}"; inner="${inner%]}"
            case "$inner" in
                ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*) ;;
                [A-Za-z]*) section="$inner"; continue ;;
            esac
        fi
        # key = value?
        [[ "$l" == *"="* ]] || continue
        k="${l%%=*}"
        while [[ "$k" == *" " || "$k" == *$'\t' ]]; do k="${k%?}"; done
        case "$k" in ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) continue ;; esac
        value="${l#*=}"
        while [[ "$value" == " "* || "$value" == $'\t'* ]]; do value="${value#?}"; done
        while [[ "$value" == *" " || "$value" == *$'\t' ]]; do value="${value%?}"; done
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.section ${section}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.key ${k}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$value" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.value ${value}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/inline-kv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=782d9d6909b1cbf883e26d3bee003ce521e572ec462f4ccbd921f53fce949274===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: inline-kv
## Description: Space-separated key=value pairs on a line (id, KEY=v KEY=v ...)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 30
## Sample: samples/inline-kv/id.txt

# Every non-blank line is a record of >=2 space-separated `key=value` tokens Aje28094Aj
# e.g. `id` output (`uid=1000(alice) gid=1000(alice) groups=Aje280a6Aj`). Tidied to one
# row per line with a column per key.

# Tokenize one line into _IKV_TOKS, QUOTE-AWARE: a `"` or `'` opens a protected
# span (spaces inside don't split) only when it starts the token or directly
# follows `=` Aje28094Aj the value-start-only rule the csv/quoted-fields parsers use, so
# a mid-word apostrophe (`don't`) or inch mark stays literal. Without this,
# logfmt (`msg="request done, 200 OK"`) and quoted k=v dumps (`k1="a b"`) shred
# into word fragments and the kv-majority gate below wrongly declines them.
_ikv_split () {
    local line="$1"
    local tok="" i c q="" prev="" n=${#line}
    _IKV_TOKS=()
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${line:$i:1}"
        if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
            tok+="$c"
            [[ "$c" == "$q" ]] && q=""
        elif [[ "$c" == '"' || "$c" == "'" ]]; then
            if [[ -z "$tok" || "$prev" == "=" ]]; then q="$c"; fi
            tok+="$c"
        elif [[ "$c" == ' ' || "$c" == '	' ]]; then
            [[ -n "$tok" ]] && _IKV_TOKS+=("$tok")
            tok=""
        else
            tok+="$c"
        fi
        prev="$c"
    done
    [[ -n "$tok" ]] && _IKV_TOKS+=("$tok")
}

# Gauge-line unwrap: when EVERY non-blank line is wrapped in one outer `[Aje280a6Aj]`
# (aria2c's `[#f1a2b3 512MiB/1.4GiB(36%) CN:8 Aje280a6Aj]`), the brackets are display
# chrome Aje28094Aj strip them so the inner fields parse. Guarded away from JSON: an
# inner starting `"`/`{`/`[` or containing no space is data, not a gauge.
_ikv_body () {
    local text="$1" _l all=1 inner
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$_l" =~ ^\[(.+)\]$ ]]; then
            inner="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            [[ "$inner" == *" "* ]] || { all=0; break; }
            case "$inner" in '"'*|'{'*|'['*) all=0 ;; esac
            [[ $all -eq 0 ]] && break
        else
            all=0; break
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $all -eq 1 ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r _l; do
            if [[ "$_l" =~ ^\[(.+)\]$ ]]; then printf '%s\n' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            else printf '%s\n' "$_l"; fi
        done <<< "$text"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$text"
    fi
}

# Is a token a strict COLON pair (`CN:8`, `DL:12MiB`, `model:Pixel_8`)?
# Exactly one colon, alpha-led label, value with no colon/slash-start Aje28094Aj so
# timestamps (06:00:12), MACs (3c:84:Aje280a6Aj), URLs (http://Aje280a6Aj) and ratios never
# qualify.
_ikv_colon_tok () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^:/[:space:]][^:]*$ ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    text="$(_ikv_body "$text")"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    local nonblank=0 kvlines=0 clines=0 _l
    local clabels="" cuniform=1
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        local toks; toks=()
        _ikv_split "$_l"; toks=("${_IKV_TOKS[@]}")
        local n=${#toks[@]} kv=0 ckv=0 t clab=""
        for t in "${toks[@]}"; do
            [[ "$t" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*=.+ ]] && kv=$((kv + 1))
            _ikv_colon_tok "$t" && { ckv=$((ckv + 1)); clab+="${t%%:*} "; }
        done
        # A leading `label:` token (blkid's `/dev/sda1:`) is the record's NAME,
        # not a failed pair Aje28094Aj don't let it count against the kv majority.
        [[ $n -ge 2 && "${toks[0]}" == *: && ! "${toks[0]}" == *=* ]] && n=$((n - 1))
        [[ $n -ge 2 && $kv -ge 2 && $(( kv * 100 / n )) -ge 60 ]] && kvlines=$((kvlines + 1))
        # COLON flavor: >=2 strict colon pairs and a colon-pair majority.
        # Riskier than `=` (colons appear in free text), so detection also
        # demands the SAME label set on every line (aria2c's CN/DL/ETA,
        # adb's product/model/device) Aje28094Aj checked across the loop.
        if [[ $n -ge 2 && $ckv -ge 2 && $(( ckv * 100 / n )) -ge 60 ]]; then
            clines=$((clines + 1))
            [[ -z "$clabels" ]] && clabels="$clab"
            [[ "$clab" != "$clabels" ]] && cuniform=0
        fi
        [[ $nonblank -ge 40 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    # Every non-blank line must be inline-kv (so we don't claim prose that
    # happens to contain one `a=b`).
    if [[ $nonblank -ge 1 && $kvlines -eq $nonblank ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ $nonblank -ge 2 && $clines -eq $nonblank && $cuniform -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    text="$(_ikv_body "$text")"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local toks; toks=()
        _ikv_split "$_l"; toks=("${_IKV_TOKS[@]}")
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        # A leading `label:` token names the record (blkid's `/dev/sda1:`) Aje28094Aj
        # emit it as a `name` column so the device/label isn't dropped.
        # ansible-recap style spells it as two tokens (`web01 : ok=12 Aje280a6Aj`).
        if [[ "${toks[0]:-}" == *: && ! "${toks[0]:-}" == *=* ]]; then
            local _nm="${toks[0]%:}"
            [[ -n "$_nm" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.name ${_nm}"$'\n'
            toks=("${toks[@]:1}")
        elif [[ "${toks[1]:-}" == ":" && ! "${toks[0]:-}" == *=* ]]; then
            result+="entry${entry}.name ${toks[0]}"$'\n'
            toks=("${toks[@]:2}")
        fi
        # COLON flavor (aria2c's `#id 512MiB/1.4GiB(36%) CN:8 DL:12MiB ETA:1m14s`):
        # when the line has no `=` pairs but >=2 strict colon pairs, emit the
        # colon pairs as fields and the leading UNLABELED run as positional
        # columns (A, B, Aje280a6Aj) so the id/progress cells aren't dropped.
        local _has_eq=0 t
        for t in "${toks[@]}"; do
            [[ "$t" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*=.+ ]] && { _has_eq=1; break; }
        done
        if [[ $_has_eq -eq 0 ]]; then
            local _cn=0
            for t in "${toks[@]}"; do _ikv_colon_tok "$t" && _cn=$((_cn + 1)); done
            if [[ $_cn -ge 2 ]]; then
                local _letters=(A B C D E F G H I J K L M) _li=0
                for t in "${toks[@]}"; do
                    if _ikv_colon_tok "$t"; then
                        result+="entry${entry}.${t%%:*} ${t#*:}"$'\n'
                    else
                        result+="entry${entry}.${_letters[$_li]:-Z} ${t}"$'\n'
                        _li=$((_li + 1))
                    fi
                done
                continue
            fi
        fi
        for t in "${toks[@]}"; do
            [[ "$t" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
            local k="${BASH_REMATCH[1]//./_}" v="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            # A value the tokenizer protected as one fully-quoted span carries
            # field-encoding quotes, not data Aje28094Aj strip the matching outer pair
            # (`msg="request done, 200 OK"` Aje28692Aj `request done, 200 OK`).
            if [[ ${#v} -ge 2 ]]; then
                case "$v" in
                    '"'*'"') v="${v#\"}"; v="${v%\"}" ;;
                    "'"*"'") v="${v#\'}"; v="${v%\'}" ;;
                esac
            fi
            result+="entry${entry}.${k} ${v}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/json-array.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=99995e6d269d62699865ae84b85a3e1f2cd5f0e9d54613f56854f241ca51e6a9===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: json-array
## Description: Top-level JSON array of objects Aje28094Aj one record per element (az/gcloud/aws list, docker inspect)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/json-array/basic.txt

# A top-level JSON ARRAY of objects is a list of records; parsing it as one
# blob (the `json` strategy's 0.field/1.field flatten) buries that. This
# parser emits one record per array element with its top-level scalar
# fields Aje28094Aj the natural tidy shape for every `<cli> list --format=json` and
# `docker inspect` style output. Nested objects/arrays inside an element are
# skipped (their scalars are not top-level fields of the record).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Structural: first non-space char is '[', the next non-space char is '{'
    # (an array of OBJECTS Aje28094Aj not a bracketed log line, not "[PHP Modules]",
    # not a Haskell tuple list), and at least one "key": field exists.
    local t="${text#"${text%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    [[ "$t" == '['* ]] || return 1
    t="${t#\[}"
    t="${t#"${t%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    [[ "$t" == '{'* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" =~ \"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\"[[:space:]]*: ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    # Full input as one record so we can scan across newlines Aje28094Aj handles both
    # pretty-printed objects (one field per line) and compact one-object-per-
    # line arrays (`[{"a":1,"b":2},{...}]`, the shape rclone/shellcheck/most
    # `--format json` tools emit).
    printf '%s' "$1" | awk '
        # Index of the char closing the {...} or [...] opened at "start".
        function findmatch(s, start,   i,n,c,instr,esc,d) {
            n=length(s); d=0; instr=0; esc=0
            for (i=start; i<=n; i++) {
                c=substr(s,i,1)
                if (instr) { if (esc) esc=0; else if (c=="\\") esc=1; else if (c=="\"") instr=0; continue }
                if (c=="\"") { instr=1; continue }
                if (c=="{" || c=="[") d++
                else if (c=="}" || c=="]") { d--; if (d==0) return i }
            }
            return n
        }
        function clean(v) {
            gsub(/^[ \t\r\n]+/,"",v); gsub(/[ \t\r\n,]+$/,"",v)
            if (substr(v,1,1)=="\"") { v=substr(v,2); sub(/"$/,"",v) }
            gsub(/[ \t\r\n]+/,"_",v)
            return v
        }
        # Emit scalar "key": value pairs at the object top level (obj includes
        # its outer braces). Nested objects/arrays as values are skipped.
        function emit(obj, e,   n,i,c,instr,esc,key,val,ve,vc) {
            n=length(obj); instr=0; esc=0; i=2   # skip opening {
            while (i<=n) {
                c=substr(obj,i,1)
                if (c=="\"") {                    # a key
                    key=""; i++
                    while (i<=n) { c=substr(obj,i,1)
                        if (c=="\\") { i+=2; continue }
                        if (c=="\"") { i++; break }
                        key=key c; i++ }
                    while (i<=n && substr(obj,i,1) ~ /[ \t\r\n]/) i++
                    if (substr(obj,i,1) != ":") continue
                    i++
                    while (i<=n && substr(obj,i,1) ~ /[ \t\r\n]/) i++
                    c=substr(obj,i,1)
                    if (c=="{" || c=="[") { i=findmatch(obj,i)+1; continue }   # nested: skip
                    # scalar value: read to next top-level , or }
                    val=""
                    if (c=="\"") { val="\""; i++
                        while (i<=n) { vc=substr(obj,i,1); val=val vc
                            if (vc=="\\") { i++; val=val substr(obj,i,1) }
                            else if (vc=="\"") { i++; break }
                            i++ }
                    } else {
                        while (i<=n) { vc=substr(obj,i,1); if (vc=="," || vc=="}") break; val=val vc; i++ }
                    }
                    if (key != "") print "entry" e "." key " " clean(val)
                } else i++
            }
        }
        { buf = buf $0 "\n" }
        END {
            s=buf; n=length(s); instr=0; esc=0; ad=0; od=0; e=0; i=1
            while (i<=n) {
                c=substr(s,i,1)
                if (instr) { if (esc) esc=0; else if (c=="\\") esc=1; else if (c=="\"") instr=0; i++; continue }
                if (c=="\"") { instr=1; i++; continue }
                if (c=="[") { ad++; i++; continue }
                if (c=="]") { ad--; i++; continue }
                if (c=="{") {
                    if (ad==1 && od==0) {           # a top-level array element
                        end=findmatch(s,i); e++
                        emit(substr(s,i,end-i+1), e)
                        i=end+1; continue
                    }
                    od++; i++; continue
                }
                if (c=="}") { od--; i++; continue }
                i++
            }
            if (e>0) print "total_entries " e
        }
    '
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/json.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=cfa556d3bdbc508248c04239095233e75354efb95af32825fe9f30dc66de9fbe===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: json
## Description: Extract key/value pairs from JSON input, flattening nested objects with dot notation
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 10
## Sample: samples/json/benchmark.json

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=95
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="input starts with { or ["
    # Apply if input looks like JSON (starts with { or [, possibly with leading whitespace)
    local trimmed="$text"
    while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* || "$trimmed" == $'\t'* || "$trimmed" == $'\n'* ]]; do
        trimmed="${trimmed#?}"
    done
    # Trailing whitespace/newlines too, so we can check the closing bracket.
    while [[ "$trimmed" == *" " || "$trimmed" == *$'\t' || "$trimmed" == *$'\n' ]]; do
        trimmed="${trimmed%?}"
    done
    # Must open AND close like JSON. This rejects bracket-prefixed logs such as
    # dmesg ("[    0.000000] Linux version Aje280a6Aj") which open with '[' but do not
    # close with ']'/'}'.
    [[ "$trimmed" == "{"* || "$trimmed" == "["* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$trimmed" == *"}" || "$trimmed" == *"]" ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Try jq first (most reliable), fall back to awk-based parser. Pipe the flat
    # key/value pairs through _list_explode so a single indexed list-of-records
    # (avro `fields`, amtool `Peers`) becomes one tidy row per element instead of
    # a wide `fields.0.* fields.1.*` row whose duplicate leaf names collide.
    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
        _strat_json_extract_jq "$text" | _list_explode
    else
        _strat_json_extract_fallback "$text" | _list_explode
    fi
}

_strat_json_extract_jq () {
    local text="$1"

    # Use jq to flatten and extract all leaf key/value pairs
    # Outputs "path value" for each leaf node
    # Uses path(.. | select()) for jq 1.8+ compatibility
    echo "$text" | jq -r '
        path(.. | select(type == "number" or type == "string" or type == "boolean" or type == "null")) as $p |
        ($p | map(if type == "number" then tostring else . end) | join(".")) + " " +
        (getpath($p) | tostring)
    ' 2>/dev/null || true
}

_strat_json_extract_fallback () {
    local text="$1"

    # Simple fallback: extract "key": value patterns with bash
    # Limitations: processes line-by-line, so multi-line JSON strings are broken.
    # This won't handle deeply nested structures as well as jq
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        # Match patterns like "key": "value" or "key": 123 or "key": true
        local remaining="$_line"
        while [[ "$remaining" == *'"'*':'* ]]; do
            # Find the next "key":
            local after_quote="${remaining#*\"}"
            local key="${after_quote%%\"*}"
            [[ -z "$key" ]] && break
            # Move past the key and colon
            remaining="${after_quote#*\"}"
            remaining="${remaining#*:}"
            # Trim spaces
            while [[ "$remaining" == " "* ]]; do remaining="${remaining# }"; done
            # Extract value
            local value=""
            if [[ "$remaining" == '"'* ]]; then
                # String value
                remaining="${remaining#\"}"
                value="${remaining%%\"*}"
                remaining="${remaining#*\"}"
            elif [[ "$remaining" =~ ^([0-9.eE+-]+) ]]; then
                value="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                remaining="${remaining#"$value"}"
            elif [[ "$remaining" == "true"* ]]; then
                value="true"
                remaining="${remaining#true}"
            elif [[ "$remaining" == "false"* ]]; then
                value="false"
                remaining="${remaining#false}"
            elif [[ "$remaining" == "null"* ]]; then
                value="null"
                remaining="${remaining#null}"
            else
                break
            fi
            [[ -n "$key" && -n "$value" ]] && echo "$key $value"
        done
    done <<< "$text"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: jsonl
## Description: Extract key/value pairs from JSON Lines (one JSON object per line)
## Version: 1.1
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/jsonl/basic.jsonl
##
## Priority 9 places JSON Lines ahead of the single-document `json` strategy
## (p10): a `.jsonl` file is NOT one JSON document, and `json` would flatten its
## objects into a wide row with duplicate columns. `jsonl`'s detector requires
## 2+ lines that are each a complete `{...}` object, so single-line or
## pretty-printed JSON (whose lines are not standalone objects) is left to json.
## Each line is emitted as a `line<N>.<field>` group so the capture tidy melt
## renders one row per record.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90

    # Must have 2+ lines, each looking like a JSON object
    local line_count=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -n "$_line" ]] && line_count=$((line_count + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $line_count -lt 2 ]] && return 1

    # Check first 3 non-empty lines are JSON objects
    local json_lines=0
    local checked=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        checked=$((checked + 1))
        local trimmed="$_line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* || "$trimmed" == $'\t'* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed#?}"; done
        if [[ "$trimmed" == "{"*"}" ]]; then
            json_lines=$((json_lines + 1))
        fi
        [[ $checked -ge 3 ]] && break
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $json_lines -ge 2 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local line_num=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        line_num=$((line_num + 1))

        # Try jq first, fall back to regex
        if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
            local fields
            fields=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '
                to_entries[] | "\(.key) \(.value)"
            ' 2>/dev/null)
            if [[ -n "$fields" ]]; then
                while IFS= read -r field_line; do
                    [[ -z "$field_line" ]] && continue
                    read -ra _arr <<< "$field_line"
                    local fname="${_arr[0]}"
                    local fval="${field_line#"$fname" }"
                    result+="line${line_num}.${fname} ${fval}"$'\n'
                done <<< "$fields"
            fi
        else
            # Fallback: simple extraction of "key": value patterns
            local remaining="$line"
            while [[ "$remaining" == *'"'*':'* ]]; do
                local after_quote="${remaining#*\"}"
                local fname="${after_quote%%\"*}"
                [[ -z "$fname" ]] && break
                remaining="${after_quote#*\"}"
                remaining="${remaining#*:}"
                while [[ "$remaining" == " "* ]]; do remaining="${remaining# }"; done
                local fval=""
                if [[ "$remaining" == '"'* ]]; then
                    remaining="${remaining#\"}"
                    fval="${remaining%%\"*}"
                    remaining="${remaining#*\"}"
                elif [[ "$remaining" =~ ^([0-9.eE+-]+) ]]; then
                    fval="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    remaining="${remaining#"$fval"}"
                elif [[ "$remaining" == "true"* ]]; then
                    fval="true"; remaining="${remaining#true}"
                elif [[ "$remaining" == "false"* ]]; then
                    fval="false"; remaining="${remaining#false}"
                elif [[ "$remaining" == "null"* ]]; then
                    fval="null"; remaining="${remaining#null}"
                else
                    break
                fi
                [[ -n "$fname" && -n "$fval" ]] && result+="line${line_num}.${fname} ${fval}"$'\n'
            done
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
