===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/key-value.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=424dcfb80b8c1a6deb67a21d3f76e252ca8db3400556e29be6eefe508b4aa030===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: key-value
## Description: Generic aligned "Label:   value" listings (lscpu, hwinfo, tool --status output) as a two-column key/value table
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 11
## Sample: samples/key-value/basic.txt

# Many tools print a flat/indented list of "Label:   value" pairs with the
# value column whitespace-aligned (lscpu, hwinfo, `systemctl show`-ish, various
# `--status`/`--info` dumps). Rather than a bespoke strategy per command, this
# captures ANY such listing as indexed key/value row groups
# (entry<N>.key / entry<N>.value) so the capture tidy melt renders a clean
# two-column table Aje28094Aj one row per property Aje28094Aj instead of one unreadable wide
# record. Wrapped continuation lines (no colon) fold into the previous value.
#
# Detection deliberately targets *aligned* human-readable output (2+ spaces
# after the colon, and/or multi-word labels) and rejects YAML list/documents,
# so it does not steal compact `key: value` YAML/config or JSON.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80
    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    local nonempty=0 kv=0 aligned=0 spacey=0 listmark=0
    local line t key after
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # strip leading whitespace
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && continue
        nonempty=$((nonempty + 1))

        # YAML list items / document markers disqualify the whole input.
        case "$t" in
            '- '*|'-'|'---'*|'...'*) listmark=$((listmark + 1)); continue ;;
        esac

        [[ "$t" == *:* ]] || continue
        key="${t%%:*}"
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        kv=$((kv + 1))

        after="${t#*:}"
        # Aligned value column (2+ spaces after the colon) or a bare section
        # header (nothing after the colon) Aje28094Aj the hallmark of tool display output.
        if [[ "$after" == "  "* || -z "${after//[[:space:]]/}" ]]; then
            aligned=$((aligned + 1))
        fi
        [[ "$key" == *" "* ]] && spacey=$((spacey + 1))
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $listmark -gt 0 ]] && return 1
    [[ $kv -lt 5 ]] && return 1
    # Most non-empty lines must be key:value (wrapped continuations are the rest).
    (( kv * 2 < nonempty )) && return 1
    # Require BOTH an aligned value column AND several multi-word labels Aje28094Aj the
    # signature of human-readable tool dumps (lscpu, hwinfo, `systemctl show`).
    # This deliberately leaves single-word-key formats (/proc/meminfo) and
    # compact YAML/config to their own strategies.
    if (( aligned >= 3 && spacey >= 3 )); then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local -a K V
    local n=0
    local line t key value cont

    # `_await_val` is set after a BARE label line (`webpage:` with nothing
    # after the colon). The reviewer's rule: the value then sits on the line(s)
    # below, so the next non-blank line is that value VERBATIM Aje28094Aj its own colons
    # are data, not a new key (`https://busybox.net/`, `so:libc.muslAje280a6Aj`,
    # `cmd:busybox=1.36.1-r5`). Without this the URL's `https:` became a spurious
    # key and the real value was lost (apk info -a).
    # A line is STRUCTURAL kv when a colon is followed by an aligned value
    # (2+ spaces) or the line is a bare label (colon at end). A URL
    # (`https://Aje280a6Aj`), a `so:libAje280a6Aj` / `cmd:pkg=Aje280a6Aj` token Aje28094Aj colon NOT followed by a
    # space Aje28094Aj is NOT structural, so it folds as a value below its label.
    # Structural = a label, a colon, then WHITESPACE or end-of-line
    # (`Containers: 12`, `Client:`, `Byte Order:  Little`). A URL
    # (`https://Aje280a6Aj` Aje28094Aj colon then `/`), a `so:libcAje280a6Aj` / `cmd:pkg=Aje280a6Aj` token
    # (colon then a non-space) is NOT structural, so it folds as a value.
    _kv_structural () {
        [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z][^:]*:([[:space:]]|$) ]]
    }
    local _await_val=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        t="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # strip leading whitespace
        [[ -z "$t" ]] && { _await_val=0; continue; }   # blank ends a value block

        # A below-the-line value: fold it Aje28094Aj UNLESS it is itself a structural
        # kv line, which means the bare label above it was a SECTION HEADER
        # (aide-check's `Summary:` over `Total Aje280a6Aj:  184203`), not a label
        # awaiting a value.
        if [[ $_await_val -eq 1 ]] && ! _kv_structural "$t"; then
            cont="${t%"${t##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            if [[ -n "${V[$n]}" ]]; then V[$n]="${V[$n]} ${cont}"; else V[$n]="$cont"; fi
            continue
        fi
        _await_val=0

        if [[ "$t" == *:* ]]; then
            key="${t%%:*}"
            value="${t#*:}"
            key="${key%"${key##*[![:space:]]}"}"                 # trim key trailing ws
            value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"           # trim value leading ws
            value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"           # trim value trailing ws
            [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
            n=$((n + 1))
            K[$n]="$key"
            V[$n]="$value"
            # a bare label opens a below-the-line value block
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && _await_val=1
        elif (( n > 0 )); then
            # Wrapped continuation line Aje28094Aj fold into the previous value.
            cont="${t%"${t##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            if [[ -n "${V[$n]}" ]]; then
                V[$n]="${V[$n]} ${cont}"
            else
                V[$n]="$cont"
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    # NOTE: bare section-header labels (aide-check's `Summary:`, lscpu's
    # `Caches (sum of all):`) are still emitted as empty-value rows. Dropping
    # them blindly loses GROUP context where the "header" actually
    # disambiguates repeated keys (sensors' `Core 0:` / `Core 1:` over the
    # same temp keys, docker's `Client:` / `Server:` over `Version`) Aje28094Aj that
    # is the kv-under-group shape, deferred to a dedicated pivot round rather
    # than a blunt drop here.
    local result="" i
    for ((i=1; i<=n; i++)); do
        result+="entry${i}.key ${K[$i]}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "${V[$i]}" ]] && result+="entry${i}.value ${V[$i]}"$'\n'
    done
    (( n > 0 )) && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/kv-pairs.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=b5d7de419cce39aa5d4b509b28e0f4ceaa7c792252d30d42825e35ff4746daa3===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: kv-pairs
## Description: Inline key=value records Aje28094Aj each line is a set of key=value pairs (a table row)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 13
## Sample: samples/kv-pairs/basic.txt

# Lines like:
#   a=1, b=2, c=3
#   a=5, b=6, c=7
# are records: each line is a set of `key=value` pairs (comma- and/or
# whitespace-separated) sharing the same keys. Emitted as entry<N>.<key> groups
# so the capture-side tidy melt turns them into one row per line with the keys
# as columns. Distinct from the `equals`/`toml`/config strategies, which handle
# ONE pair per line; this targets MULTIPLE pairs per line (priority 13, ahead of
# csv/tsv at 14 so `a=1, b=2` is not mistaken for a CSV header + data row).

# A token is a key=value pair: an identifier, '=', then a (possibly empty) value.
_KVP_TOKEN_RE='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*='

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="lines of comma/space-separated key=value pairs"

    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    local _records=0 _nonempty=0 _line _tok _pairs _ok
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        # trim
        _line="${_line#"${_line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        _line="${_line%"${_line##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        _nonempty=$((_nonempty + 1))
        # split on commas and/or whitespace; every token must be key=value and
        # there must be at least two (a single pair per line is another strategy).
        _pairs=0; _ok=1
        local _oldifs="$IFS"; IFS=$', \t'
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        set -- $_line
        IFS="$_oldifs"
        for _tok in "$@"; do
            if [[ "$_tok" =~ $_KVP_TOKEN_RE ]]; then _pairs=$((_pairs + 1)); else _ok=0; break; fi
        done
        [[ "$_ok" -eq 1 && "$_pairs" -ge 2 ]] && _records=$((_records + 1))
    done <<< "$text"

    # Most non-empty lines must be kv records, and there must be at least one.
    [[ $_records -ge 1 && $_records -ge $((_nonempty - _records)) ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    printf '%s\n' "$text" | awk '
        function is_all_kv(s,   a, i, n, p) {
            n = split(s, a, /[ \t,]+/); p = 0
            for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                if (a[i] == "") continue
                if (a[i] ~ /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*=/) p++
                else return 0
            }
            return (p >= 2) ? p : 0
        }
        {
            line = $0
            gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", line)
            if (line == "") next
            if (!is_all_kv(line)) next
            n++
            m = split(line, toks, /[ \t,]+/)
            for (i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
                if (toks[i] == "") continue
                eq = index(toks[i], "=")
                k = substr(toks[i], 1, eq - 1)
                v = substr(toks[i], eq + 1)
                gsub(/ /, "_", v)
                printf "entry%d.%s %s\n", n, k, v
            }
        }
        END { if (n > 0) printf "total_entries %d\n", n }
    '
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/kv-under-group.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=774e62f51e80535da1b6682b3312b8b29734ce2e3ce4be39cf99e9e122d4db1d===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: kv-under-group
## Description: Grouped kv records Aje28094Aj indented key/value runs under repeated group labels (ethtool queues, nvme namespaces, blkid -o full)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 10
## Sample: samples/kv-under-group/basic.txt

# The kv-CARRY-DOWN shape grouped-rows explicitly cannot take (its leaves must
# be a table) and pivot-stats cannot either (no header/values pivot): a GROUP
# label line over an INDENTED run of key/value leaves, the same keys repeating
# group after group:
#
#   NIC statistics for enp3s0:
#     Queue 0:
#        rx_packets: 88213
#        tx_packets: 77120
#     Queue 1:
#        rx_packets: 91002
#   ...
#
# One wide row per LEAF group (the group whose kv lines follow directly):
# `name` = its label, one column per key, and the nearest OUTER group
# (nvme's `Controller nvme0 Aje280a6Aj` over its namespaces, ethtool's NIC title)
# carried down as a `group` column. Leaves take `key: value` (tight or spaced
# colon) and `KEY value` (blkid's indented pairs).
#
# Priority 10 Aje28094Aj it must outrank key-value (11), which flattens these into one
# record with colliding keys. What makes that safe is the detection signature:
# >=2 leaf groups with >=2 leaves each AND >=2 leaf KEYS REPEATED across
# different groups. A single-record kv snapshot has no repeated keys; a
# multi-record one without group labels belongs to block-records. Nothing
# else looks like this.

# Leaf-kv shape: sets _KUG_KEY/_KUG_VAL, returns 0/1. Forms: `key: value`,
# `key : value`, `KEY value` (bare label token).
_kug_leaf () {
    local line="$1"
    _KUG_KEY=""; _KUG_VAL=""
    local -a tk=(); read -ra tk <<< "$line"
    [[ ${#tk[@]} -lt 2 ]] && return 1
    local k="${tk[0]}"
    if [[ "$k" == *: && "$k" != : ]]; then
        _KUG_KEY="${k%:}"
        _KUG_VAL="${tk[*]:1}"
    elif [[ "${tk[1]:-}" == ":" ]]; then
        [[ ${#tk[@]} -lt 3 ]] && return 1
        _KUG_KEY="$k"
        _KUG_VAL="${tk[*]:2}"
    elif [[ "$k" =~ ^[A-Z0-9_-]+$ || "$k" =~ ^[a-z0-9_-]+$ ]]; then
        # A colon-less pair's key must be LABEL-shaped Aje28094Aj ALL-CAPS (blkid's
        # UUID/TYPE) or lowercase_snake (rx_packets). A Titlecase English word
        # (`Operating System   UbuntuAje280a6Aj`) is the first word of a MULTI-WORD key,
        # which this parser would truncate Aje28094Aj not a leaf.
        _KUG_KEY="$k"
        _KUG_VAL="${tk[*]:1}"
    else
        return 1
    fi
    [[ -n "$_KUG_KEY" && -n "$_KUG_VAL" ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

_kug_indent () {
    local l="$1" i=0
    while [[ "${l:$i:1}" == ' ' || "${l:$i:1}" == '	' ]]; do i=$((i + 1)); done
    _KUG_IND=$i
}

# Load $1 into _KUG_LINES/_KUG_INDS/_KUG_BODYS (nonblank only) and classify
# each as G (group), L (leaf) or X in _KUG_KIND. A line is a GROUP when its
# last token ends ':' with 1-4 tokens, when it is a single bare token
# (blkid's `/dev/sda1`), or Aje28094Aj lookahead Aje28094Aj when it is NOT a leaf, has 1-6
# tokens, and the next line is deeper-indented (nvme's `Controller nvme0
# (PCIe Aje280a6Aj)` carrier). The group test runs BEFORE the leaf test: `Queue 0:`
# reads as `Queue=0:` to the leaf matcher but IS a group.
_kug_load () {
    local text="$1"
    _KUG_LINES=(); _KUG_INDS=(); _KUG_BODYS=(); _KUG_KIND=()
    local _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _KUG_LINES+=("$_l")
        _kug_indent "$_l"
        _KUG_INDS+=("$_KUG_IND")
        _KUG_BODYS+=("${_l#"${_l%%[![:space:]]*}"}")
    done <<< "$text"
    local i n=${#_KUG_LINES[@]}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        local body="${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}"
        local -a tk=(); read -ra tk <<< "$body"
        local ntk=${#tk[@]}
        local last="${tk[$((ntk - 1))]:-}"
        if [[ $ntk -ge 1 && $ntk -le 4 && "$last" == *: && "$body" =~ [A-Za-z0-9] ]]; then
            _KUG_KIND+=("G"); continue
        fi
        if [[ $ntk -eq 1 && "$body" =~ [A-Za-z0-9] ]]; then
            # a group label must bear an alphanumeric Aje28094Aj a `Aje29480e29480e29480e29480Aj` separator
            # rule (netlify's site cards) is chrome, not a group
            _KUG_KIND+=("G"); continue
        fi
        # An UNINDENTED line over deeper content is a record carrier (nvme's
        # `Controller nvme0 (PCIe Aje280a6Aj)`) even though it also parses as a kv leaf
        # Aje28094Aj test before the leaf rule, but only at indent 0 so real indented
        # leaves are never stolen.
        if [[ ${_KUG_INDS[$i]} -eq 0 && $ntk -le 6 && $((i + 1)) -lt $n \
              && ${_KUG_INDS[$((i + 1))]} -gt 0 ]]; then
            _KUG_KIND+=("G"); continue
        fi
        if _kug_leaf "$body"; then
            _KUG_KIND+=("L"); continue
        fi
        if [[ $ntk -le 6 && $((i + 1)) -lt $n && ${_KUG_INDS[$((i + 1))]} -gt ${_KUG_INDS[$i]} ]]; then
            _KUG_KIND+=("G"); continue
        fi
        _KUG_KIND+=("X")
    done
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="repeated kv keys under group labels (kv carry-down)"
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    _kug_load "$text"
    local n=${#_KUG_LINES[@]} i
    [[ $n -lt 5 || $n -gt 400 ]] && return 1
    # Not ours, whole-input vetoes:
    #  - a `- ` list marker means YAML (kubectl config view, helm values) Aje28094Aj
    #    the yaml parser flattens those losslessly, we would DROP subtrees;
    #  - `{` / `}` block syntax means a CONFIG file (named.conf), not records.
    local braces=0
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        [[ "${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}" == "- "* ]] && return 1
        # YAML anchors/aliases (`defaults: &defaults`, `<<: *defaults`) mark a
        # YAML document even without list items Aje28094Aj the yaml parser flattens it
        # losslessly, this model would mangle the merge keys.
        [[ "${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}" =~ (^|[[:space:]])[\&\*][A-Za-z0-9_] ]] && return 1
        [[ "${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}" == *"{" || "${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}" == "}"* ]] && braces=$((braces + 1))
    done
    [[ $braces -ge 2 ]] && return 1
    local groups_ok=0 cur_ind=-1 cur_leaves=0 classified=0 mangled=0 leaves_total=0 dup_in_group=0
    local -A key_groups=() key_seen_this=()
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        case "${_KUG_KIND[$i]}" in
            L)
                if [[ $cur_ind -ge 0 && ${_KUG_INDS[$i]} -gt $cur_ind ]]; then
                    _kug_leaf "${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}"
                    cur_leaves=$((cur_leaves + 1)); classified=$((classified + 1))
                    leaves_total=$((leaves_total + 1))
                    # a value whose 1st/2nd token ends ':' means the REAL key
                    # was multi-word (`API version: 1.43` Aje28692Aj key API, val
                    # `version: 1.43`) Aje28094Aj we'd truncate every such key
                    local -a _vt=(); read -ra _vt <<< "$_KUG_VAL"
                    [[ "${_vt[0]:-}" == *: || "${_vt[1]:-}" == *: ]] && mangled=$((mangled + 1))
                    if [[ -z "${key_seen_this[$_KUG_KEY]:-}" ]]; then
                        key_seen_this[$_KUG_KEY]=1
                        key_groups[$_KUG_KEY]=$(( ${key_groups[$_KUG_KEY]:-0} + 1 ))
                    else
                        # same key twice INSIDE one group (ifconfig's two RX
                        # lines): these aren't kv keys, a wide row would drop
                        # data
                        dup_in_group=1
                    fi
                else
                    [[ $cur_leaves -ge 2 ]] && groups_ok=$((groups_ok + 1))
                    cur_ind=-1; cur_leaves=0; key_seen_this=()
                fi ;;
            G)
                [[ $cur_leaves -ge 2 ]] && groups_ok=$((groups_ok + 1))
                cur_ind=${_KUG_INDS[$i]}; cur_leaves=0; key_seen_this=()
                classified=$((classified + 1)) ;;
            X)
                [[ $cur_leaves -ge 2 ]] && groups_ok=$((groups_ok + 1))
                cur_ind=-1; cur_leaves=0; key_seen_this=() ;;
        esac
    done
    [[ $cur_leaves -ge 2 ]] && groups_ok=$((groups_ok + 1))

    [[ $groups_ok -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    [[ $dup_in_group -eq 1 ]] && return 1
    # Bare (no-colon) leaves with a uniform >=3-token count are TABLE rows
    # under a group header (lsof's `cwd DIR 8,1 /` under COMMAND=nginx), not
    # kv pairs Aje28094Aj that's grouped-rows' shape; a wide kv row would weld cells.
    local bare3=0 bare_tot=0
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        [[ "${_KUG_KIND[$i]}" == "L" ]] || continue
        local -a bt=(); read -ra bt <<< "${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}"
        [[ "${bt[0]}" == *: || "${bt[1]:-}" == ":" ]] && continue
        bare_tot=$((bare_tot + 1))
        [[ ${#bt[@]} -ge 3 ]] && bare3=$((bare3 + 1))
    done
    [[ $bare_tot -ge 3 && $(( bare3 * 100 / bare_tot )) -ge 70 ]] && return 1
    # mangled multi-word keys dominate Aje28692Aj not safely parseable by this model
    [[ $leaves_total -gt 0 && $(( mangled * 5 )) -gt $leaves_total ]] && return 1
    # >=2 keys repeated under >=2 distinct groups Aje28094Aj THE signature.
    local k rep=0
    for k in "${!key_groups[@]}"; do [[ ${key_groups[$k]} -ge 2 ]] && rep=$((rep + 1)); done
    [[ $rep -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    # the shape must dominate the block
    [[ $(( classified * 100 / n )) -ge 80 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=82
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    _kug_load "$text"
    local n=${#_KUG_LINES[@]} i
    local result="" entry=0
    # Group stack: parallel indent/label arrays. A leaf materializes an entry
    # for the TOP group (once), with the nearest ancestor as `group`.
    local -a st_ind=() st_lab=()
    local emitted=0
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        local ind=${_KUG_INDS[$i]} body="${_KUG_BODYS[$i]}"
        case "${_KUG_KIND[$i]}" in
            G)
                local label="${body%:}"
                # pop groups at same-or-deeper indent
                while [[ ${#st_ind[@]} -gt 0 && ${st_ind[$(( ${#st_ind[@]} - 1 ))]} -ge $ind ]]; do
                    unset "st_ind[$(( ${#st_ind[@]} - 1 ))]"; st_ind=("${st_ind[@]}")
                    unset "st_lab[$(( ${#st_lab[@]} - 1 ))]"; st_lab=("${st_lab[@]}")
                done
                st_ind+=("$ind"); st_lab+=("$label")
                emitted=0 ;;
            L)
                if [[ ${#st_ind[@]} -gt 0 && $ind -gt ${st_ind[$(( ${#st_ind[@]} - 1 ))]} ]]; then
                    _kug_leaf "$body"
                    if [[ $emitted -eq 0 ]]; then
                        entry=$((entry + 1)); emitted=1
                        result+="entry${entry}.name ${st_lab[$(( ${#st_lab[@]} - 1 ))]}"$'\n'
                        if [[ ${#st_lab[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
                            result+="entry${entry}.group ${st_lab[$(( ${#st_lab[@]} - 2 ))]}"$'\n'
                        fi
                    fi
                    local k="${_KUG_KEY//./_}"; k="${k// /_}"
                    result+="entry${entry}.${k} ${_KUG_VAL}"$'\n'
                fi ;;
            X)
                st_ind=(); st_lab=(); emitted=0 ;;
        esac
    done
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/pivot-stats.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=2d20b19fcca60d7986fc78d90c8faca183d5fe8f540b3f5796145fcf1daf389f===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: pivot-stats
## Description: Per-record labeled counter pivots (ip -s link RX:/TX: sub-tables) Aje28094Aj one wide row per record
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 39
## Sample: samples/pivot-stats/basic.txt

# The `ip -s link` shape Aje28094Aj a record header, then LABELED PIVOT pairs where a
# label line names the counters and the NEXT line carries their values:
#
#   2: eth0: <BROADCAST,...> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT
#       link/ether 02:42:ac:11:00:02 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
#       RX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped  overrun  mcast
#       9928374011 8837422  0       12       0        4421
#       TX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped  carrier  collsns
#       5432109876 4321098  0       1        0        0
#
# This is a PIVOT, not a carry-down (grouped-rows' shape): the label line is the
# column header of the single value row that follows. The lossless wide tidy is
# ONE ROW PER RECORD with the label folded into the counter names:
# (name, mtu, qdisc, state, Aje280a6Aj, rx_bytes, rx_packets, Aje280a6Aj, tx_bytes, Aje280a6Aj).
# Record headers also yield generic `word value` pairs (mtu 1500, state UP);
# other attribute lines (link/ether, inet Aje280a6Aj) are per-record detail we skip.

# Pivot header: `LABEL:` + >=2 name tokens (letters/underscores, no digits).
# Sets _PS_LABEL (lowercased) and _PS_NAMES.
_ps_is_pivot_header () {
    local t="$1"
    _PS_LABEL=""; _PS_NAMES=()
    [[ "$t" =~ ^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*):[[:space:]]+(.+)$ ]] || return 1
    local _lab="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" _rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    local _nm=() _n
    read -ra _nm <<< "$_rest"
    [[ ${#_nm[@]} -ge 2 ]] || return 1
    for _n in "${_nm[@]}"; do
        [[ "$_n" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_/-]*$ ]] || return 1
    done
    _PS_LABEL="$(printf '%s' "$_lab" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    _PS_NAMES=("${_nm[@]}")
    return 0
}

# Value row: same token count, every token numeric-ish.
_ps_is_values () {
    local t="$1" want="$2"
    _PS_VALS=()
    local _v=() _x
    read -ra _v <<< "$t"
    [[ ${#_v[@]} -eq $want ]] || return 1
    for _x in "${_v[@]}"; do
        [[ "$_x" =~ ^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?[KMGTkmgt]?$ ]] || return 1
    done
    _PS_VALS=("${_v[@]}")
    return 0
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local _l _prev_hdr=0 _prev_n=0 pivots=0 records=0
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local t="${_l#"${_l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        if [[ $_prev_hdr -eq 1 ]] && _ps_is_values "$t" "$_prev_n"; then
            pivots=$((pivots + 1)); _prev_hdr=0; continue
        fi
        _prev_hdr=0
        if _ps_is_pivot_header "$t"; then _prev_hdr=1; _prev_n=${#_PS_NAMES[@]}; continue; fi
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[^[:space:]] ]] && records=$((records + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    # >=2 pivot pairs and at least one unindented record header
    [[ $pivots -ge 2 && $records -ge 1 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="labeled counter pivots (header line + value line) under record headers"
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0
    local _l pend_label="" pend_names=()
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local t="${_l#"${_l%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        # pending pivot: does this line carry the values?
        if [[ -n "$pend_label" ]] && _ps_is_values "$t" "${#pend_names[@]}"; then
            local i
            for ((i = 0; i < ${#pend_names[@]}; i++)); do
                local _cn="${pend_names[$i]//\//_}"; _cn="${_cn//-/_}"
                result+="entry${entry}.${pend_label}_${_cn} ${_PS_VALS[$i]}"$'\n'
            done
            pend_label=""; pend_names=()
            continue
        fi
        pend_label=""; pend_names=()
        # record header: unindented line opens a new row
        if [[ "$_l" =~ ^[^[:space:]] ]]; then
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            # `N: name: rest` (ip link) -> name; else first token
            local _name="" _rest=""
            if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]+:[[:space:]]+([^:[:space:]]+):[[:space:]]*(.*)$ ]]; then
                _name="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            else
                _name="${t%%[[:space:]]*}"; _rest="${t#*[[:space:]]}"
            fi
            result+="entry${entry}.name ${_name}"$'\n'
            # generic `word value` pairs in the rest (mtu 1500, state UP Aje280a6Aj);
            # <FLAG,LISTS> and bare tokens are skipped
            local _rt=() _ri
            read -ra _rt <<< "$_rest"
            for ((_ri = 0; _ri + 1 < ${#_rt[@]}; _ri++)); do
                local _k="${_rt[$_ri]}" _v="${_rt[$((_ri + 1))]}"
                if [[ "$_k" =~ ^[a-z][a-z_]*$ && ! "$_v" =~ ^[\<] && "$_v" != *:* ]]; then
                    result+="entry${entry}.${_k} ${_v}"$'\n'
                    _ri=$((_ri + 1))
                fi
            done
            continue
        fi
        # indented: pivot header, or per-record detail we skip
        if [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && _ps_is_pivot_header "$t"; then
            pend_label="$_PS_LABEL"; pend_names=("${_PS_NAMES[@]}")
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/prometheus-query.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=49ffbbb4fd425c2a3c4cd2a22e1f01892987744fa181f55848cc2da16440c06f===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: prometheus-query
## Description: Extract metric values from Prometheus query result output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 25
## Sample: samples/prometheus-query/sample1.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Prometheus text output has lines like: metric_name{label="value"} 123.45
    local prom_count=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue
        # Match pattern: name{labels} value Aje28094Aj the braces must hold a real
        # LABEL ASSIGNMENT (`key="value"`) and the line must END in a bare
        # number. Without both, a package list whose `{origin}` braces have no
        # `=` and whose line ends `[installed]` (apk list) or `(license)` false
        # -matches. Only the braced form qualifies here: a bare `name value`
        # is the exposition-format parser's domain, not this one Aje28094Aj matching it
        # would steal proc-vmstat / package lists / any `word number` output.
        if [[ "$line" == *"{"*'="'*'"'*"}"* && "$line" =~ [[:space:]][0-9][0-9.eE+-]*$ ]]; then
            prom_count=$((prom_count + 1))
        fi
        [[ $prom_count -ge 3 ]] && return 0
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local metric_n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Parse HELP and TYPE comments
        if [[ "$line" == "# HELP "* ]]; then
            local help_text="${line#\# HELP }"
            local help_name="${help_text%% *}"
            local help_desc="${help_text#* }"
            result+="meta.${help_name}.help ${help_desc}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi
        if [[ "$line" == "# TYPE "* ]]; then
            local type_text="${line#\# TYPE }"
            local type_name="${type_text%% *}"
            local type_val="${type_text#* }"
            result+="meta.${type_name}.type ${type_val}"$'\n'
            continue
        fi
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue

        # Parse metric lines: metric_name{label1="val1",label2="val2"} value
        if [[ "$line" == *"{"*"}"* ]]; then
            metric_n=$((metric_n + 1))
            local prefix="metric${metric_n}"

            local metric_name="${line%%\{*}"
            local rest="${line#*\{}"
            local labels="${rest%%\}*}"
            local value="${rest#*\} }"

            result+="${prefix}.name ${metric_name}"$'\n'
            result+="${prefix}.value ${value}"$'\n'

            # Parse individual labels
            local remaining="$labels"
            while [[ -n "$remaining" ]]; do
                local pair="${remaining%%,*}"
                if [[ "$remaining" == *","* ]]; then
                    remaining="${remaining#*,}"
                else
                    remaining=""
                fi
                local lkey="${pair%%=*}"
                local lval="${pair#*=}"
                # Strip quotes from value
                lval="${lval#\"}"
                lval="${lval%\"}"
                [[ -n "$lkey" && -n "$lval" ]] && result+="${prefix}.label.${lkey} ${lval}"$'\n'
            done
        elif [[ "$line" =~ ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\  ]]; then
            # Simple metric without labels: metric_name value
            metric_n=$((metric_n + 1))
            local prefix="metric${metric_n}"
            read -ra _arr <<< "$line"
            result+="${prefix}.name ${_arr[0]}"$'\n'
            result+="${prefix}.value ${_arr[1]}"$'\n'
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/protobuf-text.sh===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: protobuf-text
## Description: Extract field/value pairs from Protocol Buffers text format output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/protobuf-text/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80

    # Must NOT be JSON
    _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Must NOT look like YAML (no --- markers)
    local _nl=$'\n'
    local _re_yaml="(^|${_nl})---"
    [[ "$text" =~ $_re_yaml ]] && return 1

    # Must have { and } block nesting
    [[ "$text" == *"{"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"}"* ]] || return 1

    # Must have field: value pattern (word followed by colon and space)
    local _re_field="(^|${_nl})[[:space:]]*[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*:[[:space:]]"
    [[ "$text" =~ $_re_field ]] || return 1

    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    local result=""
    # Track prefix stack (pipe-delimited)
    local prefix_stack=""
    local depth=0
    # Track repeated field counts (pipe-delimited "name:count" pairs)
    local repeated_counts=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Skip empty lines
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Strip leading whitespace
        local trimmed="$line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* || "$trimmed" == "	"* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed#?}"; done

        # Skip comment lines
        case "$trimmed" in
            '#'*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Handle closing brace
        if [[ "$trimmed" == "}" || "$trimmed" == "},"* ]]; then
            if [[ $depth -gt 0 ]]; then
                depth=$((depth - 1))
                if [[ "$prefix_stack" == *"|"* ]]; then
                    prefix_stack="${prefix_stack%|*}"
                else
                    prefix_stack=""
                fi
            fi
            continue
        fi

        # Check for field: { (block opening)
        if [[ "$trimmed" == *"{"* && "$trimmed" == *":"* ]]; then
            local block_name="${trimmed%%:*}"
            # Trim whitespace
            while [[ "$block_name" == " "* || "$block_name" == "	"* ]]; do block_name="${block_name#?}"; done
            while [[ "$block_name" == *" " || "$block_name" == *"	" ]]; do block_name="${block_name%?}"; done

            # Check for repeated field Aje28094Aj count occurrences
            local count
            count=$(_strat_pb_get_count "$block_name")
            count=$((count + 1))
            _strat_pb_set_count "$block_name" "$count"

            # Use numbered prefix for repeated fields (count > 1)
            local numbered_name="${block_name}${count}"

            if [[ -z "$prefix_stack" ]]; then
                prefix_stack="$numbered_name"
            else
                prefix_stack="${prefix_stack}|${numbered_name}"
            fi
            depth=$((depth + 1))
            continue
        fi

        # Check for simple block opening (just "name {" without colon)
        if [[ "$trimmed" == *" {"* && "$trimmed" != *":"* ]]; then
            local block_name="${trimmed%% \{*}"
            while [[ "$block_name" == " "* || "$block_name" == "	"* ]]; do block_name="${block_name#?}"; done
            while [[ "$block_name" == *" " || "$block_name" == *"	" ]]; do block_name="${block_name%?}"; done

            local count
            count=$(_strat_pb_get_count "$block_name")
            count=$((count + 1))
            _strat_pb_set_count "$block_name" "$count"

            local numbered_name="${block_name}${count}"

            if [[ -z "$prefix_stack" ]]; then
                prefix_stack="$numbered_name"
            else
                prefix_stack="${prefix_stack}|${numbered_name}"
            fi
            depth=$((depth + 1))
            continue
        fi

        # Check for field: value pair
        if [[ "$trimmed" == *":"* ]]; then
            local key="${trimmed%%:*}"
            local value="${trimmed#*:}"

            # Trim whitespace from key
            while [[ "$key" == " "* || "$key" == "	"* ]]; do key="${key#?}"; done
            while [[ "$key" == *" " || "$key" == *"	" ]]; do key="${key%?}"; done

            # Trim whitespace from value
            while [[ "$value" == " "* || "$value" == "	"* ]]; do value="${value#?}"; done
            while [[ "$value" == *" " || "$value" == *"	" ]]; do value="${value%?}"; done

            # Skip if key or value is empty
            [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

            # Strip quotes from string values
            case "$value" in
                '"'*) value="${value#\"}"; value="${value%\"}" ;;
            esac

            # Replace spaces in key and value with underscores
            key="${key// /_}"

            # Skip if value is empty after stripping
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

            # Build full prefix from stack
            local full_prefix=""
            if [[ -n "$prefix_stack" ]]; then
                local old_ifs="$IFS"
                IFS="|"
                for entry in $prefix_stack; do
                    if [[ -z "$full_prefix" ]]; then
                        full_prefix="$entry"
                    else
                        full_prefix="${full_prefix}.${entry}"
                    fi
                done
                IFS="$old_ifs"
            fi

            if [[ -n "$full_prefix" ]]; then
                result+="${full_prefix}.${key} ${value}"$'\n'
            else
                result+="${key} ${value}"$'\n'
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

# Helper: get repeated field count
_strat_pb_get_count () {
    local name="$1"
    local old_ifs="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for entry in $repeated_counts; do
        local entry_name="${entry%%:*}"
        local entry_count="${entry#*:}"
        if [[ "$entry_name" == "$name" ]]; then
            IFS="$old_ifs"
            echo "$entry_count"
            return
        fi
    done
    IFS="$old_ifs"
    echo "0"
}

# Helper: set repeated field count
_strat_pb_set_count () {
    local name="$1"
    local new_count="$2"
    local new_counts=""
    local found=0
    local old_ifs="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for entry in $repeated_counts; do
        local entry_name="${entry%%:*}"
        if [[ "$entry_name" == "$name" ]]; then
            entry="${name}:${new_count}"
            found=1
        fi
        if [[ -z "$new_counts" ]]; then
            new_counts="$entry"
        else
            new_counts="${new_counts}|${entry}"
        fi
    done
    IFS="$old_ifs"
    if [[ $found -eq 0 ]]; then
        if [[ -z "$new_counts" ]]; then
            new_counts="${name}:${new_count}"
        else
            new_counts="${new_counts}|${name}:${new_count}"
        fi
    fi
    repeated_counts="$new_counts"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/psql-expanded.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=66f3859c95f7458edf63cae635377e17f6b949df39960b2dfc5c8cb8508da514===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: psql-expanded
## Description: psql \x expanded output Aje28094Aj one record per -[ RECORD N ] block of key | value lines
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/psql-expanded/basic.txt

# psql's expanded display (\x on, any query):
#   -[ RECORD 1 ]---------+------------------------------
#   datname               | orders
#   state                 | active
#   -[ RECORD 2 ]---------+------------------------------
#   datname               | metrics
#   ...
# One entry per RECORD block; each `key | value` line becomes entryN.key.
# This is a FORMAT parser: it keys on the `-[ RECORD N ]` separator psql
# always prints in expanded mode, never on any table's column names.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"-[ RECORD 1 ]"* ]] || return 1
    # Require at least one `key | value` body line so a stray marker in a log
    # can't trigger a whole-file parse.
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]*\| ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line key val entry=0 fields=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # `-[ RECORD N ]---+---` opens the next record.
        if [[ "$line" == *"-[ RECORD"* ]]; then
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            continue
        fi
        [[ $entry -eq 0 ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]?(.*)$ ]] || continue
        key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        val="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        val="${val%"${val##*[![:space:]]}"}"   # rtrim
        val="${val//$'\t'/_}"
        result+="entry${entry}.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
        fields=$((fields + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $fields -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: snmp-output
## Description: Extract OID/type/value records from snmpget and snmpwalk output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/snmp-output/basic.txt

# snmpget and snmpwalk print the same line shape Aje28094Aj `MIB::name.N = TYPE: value` Aje28094Aj
# and want the same record output (oid/type/value per line). They were previously
# two strategies split only by a detect heuristic (get = scalar `.0` instances,
# walk = a subtree with non-`.0` indices); that distinction changes nothing about
# the output, so a single parser covers both.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local snmp=0 _line
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$_line" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+::[^[:space:]=]+[[:space:]]+=[[:space:]]+[^:]+:[[:space:]] ]]; then
            snmp=$((snmp + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $snmp -ge 1 ]] && { _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86; return 0; }
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"::"*" = "*": "* ]] || continue
        local oid="${line%% = *}"
        local rhs="${line#* = }"
        local type="${rhs%%: *}"
        local val="${rhs#*: }"

        n=$((n + 1))
        local p="entry${n}."
        result+="${p}oid ${oid}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}type ${type}"$'\n'
        result+="${p}value ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: toml
## Description: Extract key/value pairs from TOML format with section and array table support
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 15
## Sample: samples/toml/basic.toml

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85

    # Must NOT look like JSON
    local first_nonblank=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        [[ -z "$_line" ]] && continue
        local _trimmed="$_line"
        while [[ "$_trimmed" == " "* || "$_trimmed" == "	"* ]]; do _trimmed="${_trimmed#?}"; done
        [[ -z "$_trimmed" ]] && continue
        first_nonblank="$_trimmed"
        break
    done <<< "$text"
    case "$first_nonblank" in
        '{'*|'['*) ;;
    esac

    # Check for actual JSON start
    case "$first_nonblank" in
        '{'*) return 1 ;;
    esac

    # 1. [[array]] table headers
    if [[ "$text" == *$'\n'"[["* || "$text" == "[["* ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # 2. [dotted.section] headers
    if [[ "$text" =~ (^|$'\n')\[[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\. ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # 3. key = "quoted_value" pattern (TOML uses = with spaces, not :)
    if [[ "$text" =~ (^|$'\n')[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*[\ ]*=[\ ]*\" ]]; then
        # Also must have [section] to distinguish from env-vars / equals
        if [[ "$text" == *$'\n'"["* || "$text" == "["* ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
        # Or [[array]] tables
        if [[ "$text" == *"[["* ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
        # Accept if we have key = "value" at top level AND [section] somewhere
        local section_count=0
        while IFS= read -r _line; do
            [[ "$_line" == "["* ]] && section_count=$((section_count + 1))
        done <<< "$text"
        [[ $section_count -ge 1 ]] && return 0
    fi

    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    local result=""
    local current_section=""
    # Track array table counts using pipe-delimited "name:count" pairs
    local array_table_counts=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Skip empty lines
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Skip comment lines
        case "$line" in
            '#'*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Check for array table header [[name]]
        if [[ "$line" == "[["* ]]; then
            local array_name="${line#\[\[}"
            array_name="${array_name%%\]\]*}"
            # Trim whitespace
            while [[ "$array_name" == " "* || "$array_name" == "	"* ]]; do array_name="${array_name#?}"; done
            while [[ "$array_name" == *" " || "$array_name" == *"	" ]]; do array_name="${array_name%?}"; done

            # Get and increment the counter for this array table
            local count
            count=$(_strat_toml_get_array_count "$array_name")
            _strat_toml_set_array_count "$array_name" $((count + 1))

            current_section="${array_name}.${count}"
            continue
        fi

        # Check for section header [name] or [dotted.name]
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^\[[a-zA-Z] ]]; then
            current_section="${line#\[}"
            current_section="${current_section%%\]*}"
            # Trim whitespace
            while [[ "$current_section" == " "* || "$current_section" == "	"* ]]; do current_section="${current_section#?}"; done
            while [[ "$current_section" == *" " || "$current_section" == *"	" ]]; do current_section="${current_section%?}"; done
            continue
        fi

        # Check for key = value lines
        if [[ "$line" == *"="* ]]; then
            local key value

            # Extract key (before first =)
            key="${line%%=*}"
            # Trim whitespace from key
            while [[ "$key" == " "* || "$key" == "	"* ]]; do key="${key#?}"; done
            while [[ "$key" == *" " || "$key" == *"	" ]]; do key="${key%?}"; done

            # Extract value (after first =)
            value="${line#*=}"
            # Trim leading whitespace
            while [[ "$value" == " "* || "$value" == "	"* ]]; do value="${value#?}"; done

            # Skip if key is empty
            [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue

            # Strip quotes from string values
            case "$value" in
                '"'*) value="${value#\"}"; value="${value%\"}" ;;
                "'"*) value="${value#\'}"; value="${value%\'}" ;;
            esac
            # Trim trailing whitespace
            while [[ "$value" == *" " || "$value" == *"	" ]]; do value="${value%?}"; done

            # Skip if value is empty
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

            # Replace spaces in key and value with underscores
            key="${key// /_}"

            # Prefix with section if we have one
            if [[ -n "$current_section" ]]; then
                result+="${current_section}.${key} ${value}"$'\n'
            else
                result+="${key} ${value}"$'\n'
            fi
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

# Helper: get array table count for a given name
_strat_toml_get_array_count () {
    local name="$1"
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for entry in $array_table_counts; do
        local entry_name entry_count
        entry_name="${entry%%:*}"
        entry_count="${entry#*:}"
        if [[ "$entry_name" == "$name" ]]; then
            IFS="$IFS_OLD"
            echo "$entry_count"
            return
        fi
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"
    echo "0"
}

# Helper: set array table count for a given name
_strat_toml_set_array_count () {
    local name="$1"
    local new_count="$2"
    local new_counts=""
    local found=0
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for entry in $array_table_counts; do
        local entry_name
        entry_name="${entry%%:*}"
        if [[ "$entry_name" == "$name" ]]; then
            entry="${name}:${new_count}"
            found=1
        fi
        if [[ -z "$new_counts" ]]; then
            new_counts="$entry"
        else
            new_counts="${new_counts}|${entry}"
        fi
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"
    if [[ $found -eq 0 ]]; then
        if [[ -z "$new_counts" ]]; then
            new_counts="${name}:${new_count}"
        else
            new_counts="${new_counts}|${name}:${new_count}"
        fi
    fi
    array_table_counts="$new_counts"
}

===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/tree-view.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=ffe37eef3c33a34a443502b393747c6ee78a9192b1d8f37e6355dd04b0b57d3a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: tree-view
## Description: Tree-structured output (tree, pstree, npm ls) Aje28094Aj one row per node
## Version: 1.1
## Priority: 38
## Sample: samples/tree-view/basic.txt

# Priority 38 (was 50): the engine dispatches in priority order, first-match
# wins, so a genuine glyph tree must be tried BEFORE the generic block-records
# (40) and indented-hierarchy (50) parsers Aje28094Aj otherwise those grab the preamble
# or the first `label:` line and collapse the tree to a single record. The
# detect gate (>=60% of non-blank lines carry a Aje2949cAj/Aje29494Aj/Aje294acAj branch marker, and no
# ALL-CAPS columnar header) is specific enough that only real trees flip here.

# A single generic strategy for the many commands that draw a hierarchy with
# box-drawing branch characters: `tree`, `pstree`, `npm ls`, `cargo tree`,
# `pnpm ls`, etc. Rather than a bespoke strategy per command, this captures ANY
# such listing as indexed node row groups (entry<N>.depth / entry<N>.name) so
# the capture tidy melt renders one clean row per node with two columns
# (depth, name) instead of one unreadable wide record.
#
# A "node line" is any line carrying a branch marker: the Unicode connectors
# Aje2949cAj (U+251C), Aje29494Aj (U+2514) or Aje294acAj (U+252C), or the ASCII variants `|--`, `\--`,
# `+--`. The bare root line that some tools print on its own (tree's `.`, the
# `pkg@ver /path` header from `npm ls`) has no branch marker and is treated as
# the implicit depth-0 parent Aje28094Aj it is not emitted as its own row. Depth is the
# indentation level (0-based) measured from the leading box-drawing cells.

# Byte sequences of the box-drawing chars (works regardless of locale Aje28094Aj both the
# literals here and the sampled input are the same UTF-8 bytes).
_TV_VERT='Aje29482Aj'        # U+2502
_TV_BRANCH='Aje2949cAj'      # U+251C
_TV_LAST='Aje29494Aj'        # U+2514
_TV_HORZ='Aje29480Aj'        # U+2500
_TV_TDOWN='Aje294acAj'       # U+252C

# Does this line carry a branch marker?
_tv_is_node () {
    local t="$1"
    case "$t" in
        *"$_TV_BRANCH"*|*"$_TV_LAST"*|*"$_TV_TDOWN"*) return 0 ;;
        *'|--'*|*'\--'*|*'+--'*)                      return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    local line nonblank=0 nodes=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        _tv_is_node "$line" && nodes=$((nodes + 1))
    done <<< "$text"

    # Need a few real branch lines, and a strong majority of the non-blank lines
    # must carry a marker (root + trailing summary lines are the only allowance).
    [[ $nodes -lt 2 ]] && return 1
    (( nodes * 10 < nonblank * 6 )) && return 1

    # NUMBERED-HOP decline: `mtr` / `traceroute` draw `1.|-- host Aje280a6Aj` Aje28094Aj the
    # `|--` is a hop-number connector, not tree indentation, and every line
    # carries a columnar `Loss% Snt Last Aje280a6Aj` record. A real tree never prefixes
    # its branch marker with `N.`. When most node lines match `^ *NN.|--`,
    # this is a numbered report Aje28692Aj decline so aligned-columns reads the columns.
    local _hop=0 _hl
    while IFS= read -r _hl; do
        [[ "$_hl" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.\|?[[:space:]]*[|\\+]?-- ]] && _hop=$((_hop + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    (( _hop * 2 >= nodes )) && return 1

    # Decline columnar tables that merely use tree chars in their first column
    # (e.g. findmnt): if the first non-blank line is not itself a node and looks
    # like an ALL-CAPS column header, this belongs to aligned-columns, not here.
    local first; first="$(printf '%s\n' "$text" | sed -n '/[^[:space:]]/{p;q}')"
    if ! _tv_is_node "$first"; then
        local _ft; _ft=(); read -ra _ft <<< "$first"
        local _up=0 _t
        for _t in "${_ft[@]}"; do [[ "$_t" =~ ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_/-]*$ ]] && _up=$((_up + 1)); done
        [[ ${#_ft[@]} -ge 2 && $_up -ge 2 ]] && return 1
    fi

    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

# Depth = number of 4-column indentation cells before the node label.
# Continuation cells are "Aje29482Aj   " or four spaces; the marker cell is "Aje2949ce29480e29480Aj "/"Aje29494e29480e29480Aj ".
_tv_depth () {
    local s="$1" depth=0
    # Drop a small cosmetic left-margin (some tools indent the whole tree a few
    # spaces) so it is not mistaken for a depth level.
    while [[ "$s" == '  '* && "$s" != '    '* ]]; do s="${s#'  '}"; done
    while true; do
        case "$s" in
            # A VERTICAL-BAR indent cell: the connector plus its trailing
            # spaces up to the next glyph, however many (`Aje29482Aj   `, `Aje29482Aj  `, `Aje29482Aj `,
            # ASCII `|  `, `|   `). Consume the bar then any run of spaces.
            "$_TV_VERT"*)
                s="${s#"$_TV_VERT"}"
                while [[ "$s" == ' '* ]]; do s="${s# }"; done
                depth=$((depth + 1)) ;;
            '|'*)
                # ASCII bar, but NOT the `|--`/`|  |--` branch marker itself.
                if [[ "$s" == '|--'* ]]; then depth=$((depth + 1)); break; fi
                s="${s#'|'}"
                while [[ "$s" == ' '* ]]; do s="${s# }"; done
                depth=$((depth + 1)) ;;
            # 4- / 2-column blank indent cells.
            '    '*)           s="${s#'    '}";                        depth=$((depth + 1)) ;;
            '  '*)             s="${s#'  '}";                          depth=$((depth + 1)) ;;
            # Branch markers of any dash count (Aje2949ce29480e29480Aj/Aje2949ce29480Aj/Aje29494e29480Aj/Aje2949ce29480e294acAj), then the label.
            "$_TV_BRANCH"*|"$_TV_LAST"*) depth=$((depth + 1)); break ;;
            '\--'*|'+--'*|'`--'*)        depth=$((depth + 1)); break ;;
            *) break ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s' "$depth"
}

# Strip tree glyphs and leading connector debris but PRESERVE internal spacing,
# so a trailing `   1.2 kB` value gap survives for the value split. (`_tv_name`
# collapses runs; this variant does not.)
_tv_label_raw () {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s//$_TV_VERT/ }"; s="${s//$_TV_BRANCH/ }"; s="${s//$_TV_LAST/ }"
    s="${s//$_TV_HORZ/ }"; s="${s//$_TV_TDOWN/ }"; s="${s//|/ }"; s="${s//\\/ }"
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    while [[ "$s" == '+'* || "$s" == '`'* || "$s" == '-'* ]]; do s="${s#?}"; done
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

# Strip all box-drawing chars (and the ASCII `|`,`\` connectors) to a space,
# then collapse runs of whitespace and trim. ASCII hyphens are preserved so
# names like "dbus-daemon" survive.
_tv_name () {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s//$_TV_VERT/ }"
    s="${s//$_TV_BRANCH/ }"
    s="${s//$_TV_LAST/ }"
    s="${s//$_TV_HORZ/ }"
    s="${s//$_TV_TDOWN/ }"
    s="${s//|/ }"
    s="${s//\\/ }"
    # Strip a LEADING ASCII branch marker (`+---`, `` `-- ``, leading dashes left
    # by the box-glyph pass) so the name isn't prefixed with connector debris.
    # Only leading runs are removed Aje28094Aj an internal hyphen (dbus-daemon) survives.
    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
    while [[ "$s" == '+'* || "$s" == '`'* || "$s" == '-'* ]]; do s="${s#?}"; done
    # collapse + trim via word-splitting
    local -a parts
    read -r -a parts <<< "$s"
    printf '%s' "${parts[*]}"
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local line nm d

    # ANCESTOR tracking: a tree is only tidy if each node carries its context.
    # A depth-keyed stack holds the name at each level so every row gets its
    # immediate `parent` (the reviewer's "the thing one level up") Aje28094Aj turning a
    # flat depth/name dump into a navigable parent -> child edge list. A
    # trailing metric on the label (broot's `main.rs   1.2 kB`, a size after a
    # 2+-space gap) is split off into a `value` column so the number isn't
    # welded to the name. The implicit depth-0 root (the bare first line) is
    # seeded as the parent of depth-1 nodes.
    local -a _stack=()
    local _root=""
    local _first; _first="$(printf '%s\n' "$text" | sed -n '/[^[:space:]]/{p;q}')"
    if ! _tv_is_node "$_first"; then
        _root="$(_tv_name "$_first")"
        _stack[0]="$_root"
    fi

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _tv_is_node "$line" || continue

        d="$(_tv_depth "$line")"
        # Split a trailing value off the RAW (uncollapsed) label so the 2+-space
        # gap before a metric survives (broot's `main.rs   1.2 kB`).
        local _raw _val=""
        _raw="$(_tv_label_raw "$line")"
        if [[ "$_raw" =~ ^(.*[^[:space:]])[[:space:]][[:space:]]+([0-9].*)$ ]]; then
            _raw="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _val="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        fi
        # collapse the (value-stripped) label to the clean name
        local _np; read -r -a _np <<< "$_raw"; nm="${_np[*]}"
        [[ -z "$nm" ]] && continue

        # parent = the name recorded at the level just above this node.
        local _parent="${_stack[$((d - 1))]:-$_root}"
        _stack[$d]="$nm"
        # a deeper level's stale entries can't be this node's ancestors
        local _si
        for _si in "${!_stack[@]}"; do [[ $_si -gt $d ]] && unset '_stack[$_si]'; done

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.depth ${d}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$_parent" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.parent ${_parent}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${nm}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$_val" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.value ${_val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/tsv.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=32270d5edd05dcd7d92286b5ec1b5d5e52d7d5f3a46be67c72acb4d42ed7de3a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: tsv
## Description: Extract field names and values from TSV files (tab-delimited with header row)
## Version: 2.0
## Priority: 14
## Sample: samples/tsv/basic.tsv

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90

    # Must have at least 2 lines
    local line_count=0
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        line_count=$((line_count + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $line_count -lt 2 ]] && return 1

    # First line must contain tabs
    local first_line=""
    IFS= read -r first_line <<< "$text"
    [[ "$first_line" != *"	"* ]] && return 1

    # Tab count should be consistent between header and first data row
    local header_tabs=0 data_tabs=0
    local _tmp="$first_line"
    while [[ "$_tmp" == *"	"* ]]; do
        header_tabs=$((header_tabs + 1))
        _tmp="${_tmp#*	}"
    done

    # Get second line
    local _line_num=0 second_line=""
    while IFS= read -r _line; do
        _line_num=$((_line_num + 1))
        if [[ $_line_num -eq 2 ]]; then
            second_line="$_line"
            break
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    _tmp="$second_line"
    while [[ "$_tmp" == *"	"* ]]; do
        data_tabs=$((data_tabs + 1))
        _tmp="${_tmp#*	}"
    done

    local diff=$(( header_tabs - data_tabs ))
    [[ ${diff#-} -le 1 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

# Split one TSV line into _TSV_FIELDS, QUOTE-AWARE (the csv treatment with a
# tab delimiter): a '"' is structural only at FIELD START Aje28094Aj it protects any
# tabs inside the field (`"a<TAB>b"` is ONE cell, not two) and is consumed;
# a mid-field quote is literal data. A protected tab becomes a single space in
# the emitted value Aje28094Aj the tidy output is itself TSV, so a literal tab inside a
# cell would shear every column after it.
#
# Empty fields are DROPPED (a run of tabs counts as one separator, leading tabs
# are stripped) Aje28094Aj matching the `IFS=tab read -ra` semantics this replaced. Tools
# pad with extra tabs for display alignment (ldd's leading tab, proc-cpuinfo's
# `flags<TAB><TAB>: Aje280a6Aj`), and preserving those as empty cells would shift every
# later column's name and orphan values into phantom columns.
_tsv_split () {
    local line="$1"
    local field="" i c in_q=0 n=${#line}
    _TSV_FIELDS=()
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${line:$i:1}"
        if [[ $in_q -eq 1 ]]; then
            if [[ "$c" == '"' ]]; then in_q=0
            elif [[ "$c" == '	' ]]; then field+=' '
            else field+="$c"; fi
        elif [[ "$c" == '"' && -z "$field" ]]; then
            in_q=1
        elif [[ "$c" == '	' ]]; then
            [[ -n "$field" ]] && _TSV_FIELDS+=("$field")
            field=""
        else
            field+="$c"
        fi
    done
    [[ -n "$field" ]] && _TSV_FIELDS+=("$field")
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    # Parse header row for field names
    local header=""
    IFS= read -r header <<< "$text"

    # Split header into fields on tabs (quote-aware Aje28094Aj see _tsv_split)
    local headers; headers=()
    _tsv_split "$header"; headers=("${_TSV_FIELDS[@]}")

    # Headerless TSV: synthesise A,B,CAje280a6Aj names and treat every line as a record
    # when row 1 is already DATA Aje28094Aj so `du` output (size <tab> path) stays one row
    # per line instead of eating row 1 as a header. Trigger (long-standing): row
    # 1 bears a digit anywhere Aje28094Aj a header of pure labels does not.
    local headerless=0 _hf
    for _hf in "${headers[@]}"; do [[ "$_hf" =~ [0-9] ]] && { headerless=1; break; }; done
    # Aje280a6Ajbut a digit-BEARING row 1 can still be a genuine header whose LABELS embed
    # digits (`C1`, `C6`, `Avg_MHz`). Distinguish by comparing row 1 to the first
    # data row, column by column: if some column is a non-numeric label in row 1
    # yet a numeric value in row 2, row 1 is a header after all Aje28094Aj keep it (so
    # turbostat -q's 20-wide table keeps every column name instead of collapsing
    # to AAje280a6AjT). This override only ever fires when row 1 already looked headerless,
    # so nothing that used a header before changes. Gated to >=3 columns: a
    # 2-column tsv is a key/value or pair LIST (`wg show` pubkey<tab>time,
    # colon-value KV dumps) where the value column legitimately mixes text and
    # numbers row to row Aje28094Aj never a wide table whose header needs rescuing.
    if [[ $headerless -eq 1 && ${#headers[@]} -ge 3 ]]; then
        local _second="" _ln=0
        while IFS= read -r _hf; do _ln=$((_ln + 1)); [[ $_ln -eq 2 ]] && { _second="$_hf"; break; }; done <<< "$text"
        if [[ -n "$_second" ]]; then
            local -a _d2=(); _tsv_split "$_second"; _d2=("${_TSV_FIELDS[@]}")
            local _i _h _v
            for ((_i=0; _i<${#headers[@]}; _i++)); do
                _h="${headers[$_i]}"; _h="${_h#"${_h%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
                _v="${_d2[$_i]:-}"; _v="${_v#"${_v%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
                if [[ "$_h" != [0-9]* && "$_h" != -[0-9]* ]] \
                   && { [[ "$_v" == [0-9]* ]] || [[ "$_v" == -[0-9]* ]]; }; then
                    headerless=0; break
                fi
            done
        fi
        # Second rescue: row 1's fields form a NUMBERED SERIES Aje28094Aj >=2 adjacent
        # labels with one shared alpha prefix and integer suffixes ascending by
        # 1 (`col1 col2 col3`, `q1 q2 q3 q4`). That's a header-labeling idiom;
        # a data row essentially never enumerates itself like that.
        if [[ $headerless -eq 1 ]]; then
            local _run=1 _prevp="" _prevn=-1 _p _num
            for _hf in "${headers[@]}"; do
                if [[ "$_hf" =~ ^([A-Za-z_]+)([0-9]+)$ ]]; then
                    _p="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _num="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    if [[ "$_p" == "$_prevp" && "$_num" -eq $((_prevn + 1)) ]]; then
                        _run=$((_run + 1))
                        [[ $_run -ge 2 ]] && { headerless=0; break; }
                    else
                        _run=1
                    fi
                    _prevp="$_p"; _prevn="$_num"
                else
                    _run=1; _prevp=""; _prevn=-1
                fi
            done
        fi
    fi
    if [[ $headerless -eq 1 ]]; then
        local _n=${#headers[@]} _i
        headers=()
        for ((_i = 1; _i <= _n; _i++)); do headers+=("$(_col_letter "$_i")"); done
    fi

    # CELL-SPLIT pre-pass. Two shapes hide multiple fields inside ONE tab
    # cell, recognisable only across the whole column:
    #  * datetime-prefix (`Thu Jul 10 18:00:00 2026 a deploy` Aje28094Aj at/atq):
    #    every row's cell opens with a full ctime-style stamp followed by a
    #    UNIFORM number of trailing tokens Aje28692Aj stamp column + one column per
    #    trailing token.
    #  * constant multi-word prefix (`nice run-parts /etc/cron.daily` Aje28094Aj
    #    anacrontab): every row shares the same >=2-token prefix with a
    #    non-empty remainder Aje28692Aj prefix column + remainder column.
    local _cs_rows=() _cs_l _cs_rn=0
    while IFS= read -r _cs_l; do
        _cs_rn=$((_cs_rn + 1))
        [[ $_cs_rn -eq 1 && $headerless -eq 0 ]] && continue
        [[ -z "$_cs_l" ]] && continue
        _cs_rows+=("$_cs_l")
    done <<< "$text"
    local _dt_split=() _cp_split=() _cp_pref=() _dt_ntok=()
    local _dt_re='^([A-Z][a-z]{2}[[:space:]]+[A-Z][a-z]{2}[[:space:]]+[0-9]{1,2}[[:space:]]+[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[[:space:]]+[0-9]{4})[[:space:]]+(.+)$'
    if [[ ${#_cs_rows[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
        local _cs_j _cs_r
        for ((_cs_j = 0; _cs_j < ${#headers[@]}; _cs_j++)); do
            local _dt_all=1 _dt_n=-1 _cp_all=1 _cp_p=""
            for _cs_r in "${_cs_rows[@]}"; do
                _tsv_split "$_cs_r"
                local _cs_v="${_TSV_FIELDS[$_cs_j]:-}"
                if [[ "$_cs_v" =~ $_dt_re ]]; then
                    local _dt_rest=() ; read -ra _dt_rest <<< "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    [[ $_dt_n -lt 0 ]] && _dt_n=${#_dt_rest[@]}
                    [[ ${#_dt_rest[@]} -ne $_dt_n ]] && _dt_all=0
                else
                    _dt_all=0
                fi
                local _cp_tk=() ; read -ra _cp_tk <<< "$_cs_v"
                # The remainder must be ARGUMENT-shaped (a path, flag or
                # number: anacrontab's `/etc/cron.daily`) Aje28094Aj a word remainder
                # means the cell is one multi-word LABEL ("number of
                # samples:" Aje28094Aj bcftools) and must stay whole.
                if [[ ${#_cp_tk[@]} -ge 3 && "${_cp_tk[2]}" =~ ^[/~.0-9-] ]]; then
                    local _cp_this="${_cp_tk[0]} ${_cp_tk[1]}"
                    [[ -z "$_cp_p" ]] && _cp_p="$_cp_this"
                    [[ "$_cp_this" != "$_cp_p" ]] && _cp_all=0
                else
                    _cp_all=0
                fi
            done
            _dt_split[$_cs_j]=0; _cp_split[$_cs_j]=0; _cp_pref[$_cs_j]=""; _dt_ntok[$_cs_j]=0
            if [[ $_dt_all -eq 1 && $_dt_n -ge 1 ]]; then
                _dt_split[$_cs_j]=1; _dt_ntok[$_cs_j]=$_dt_n
            elif [[ $_cp_all -eq 1 && -n "$_cp_p" ]]; then
                _cp_split[$_cs_j]=1; _cp_pref[$_cs_j]="$_cp_p"
            fi
        done
    fi

    # Process each data row as an indexed record group (entry<N>.<column>) so the
    # capture tidy melt renders one row per record Aje28094Aj rather than welding every
    # row's cells into a single wide record with duplicate column names.
    local result=""
    local row_num=0
    local rec=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        row_num=$((row_num + 1))
        [[ $row_num -eq 1 && $headerless -eq 0 ]] && continue  # skip header
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Split on tabs (quote-aware Aje28094Aj see _tsv_split)
        local values; values=()
        _tsv_split "$line"; values=("${_TSV_FIELDS[@]}")

        rec=$((rec + 1))
        local j
        for ((j=0; j<${#headers[@]}; j++)); do
            local name="${headers[$j]}"
            local value="${values[$j]:-}"
            if [[ "${_dt_split[$j]:-0}" -eq 1 && "$value" =~ $_dt_re ]]; then
                local _dt_stamp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" _dt_tail="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                local _dt_tt=() _dt_k
                read -ra _dt_tt <<< "$_dt_tail"
                local _nm0="${name//\"}"; _nm0="${_nm0// /_}"; _nm0="${_nm0//./_}"
                result+="entry${rec}.${_nm0} ${_dt_stamp}"$'\n'
                for ((_dt_k = 0; _dt_k < ${#_dt_tt[@]}; _dt_k++)); do
                    result+="entry${rec}.${_nm0}_$(_col_letter $((_dt_k + 2))) ${_dt_tt[$_dt_k]}"$'\n'
                done
                continue
            fi
            if [[ "${_cp_split[$j]:-0}" -eq 1 ]]; then
                local _cp_rest="${value#"${_cp_pref[$j]}"}"
                _cp_rest="${_cp_rest# }"
                local _nm1="${name//\"}"; _nm1="${_nm1// /_}"; _nm1="${_nm1//./_}"
                result+="entry${rec}.${_nm1} ${_cp_pref[$j]}"$'\n'
                [[ -n "$_cp_rest" ]] && result+="entry${rec}.${_nm1}_b ${_cp_rest}"$'\n'
                continue
            fi
            # Clean up name and value: replace spaces with underscores, remove quotes
            name="${name//\"}"
            name="${name// /_}"
            name="${name#_}"
            name="${name%_}"
            name="${name//./_}"   # '.' would break the tidy melt's group key split
            value="${value//\"}"
            [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
            [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
            result+="entry${rec}.${name} ${value}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $rec -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${rec}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/structured/xml.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=8d23f1fc8126a88b59a431c90f61813e58d85097c116d5630208dc92b8cee8b9===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: xml
## Description: Extract element text content and attribute key/value pairs from XML/HTML
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/xml-elements/basic.xml

# Merges xml-elements and xml-attributes strategies.
# Elements pass:    <tag>content</tag>    -> "tagname content"
# Attributes pass:  <tag attr="value">    -> "tagname.attr value"
# Both passes run sequentially; a single XML file gets both element and attribute fields.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=80

    # Accept if input looks like XML with elements (opening + closing tags)
    if [[ "$text" == *"<"[a-zA-Z]* && "$text" == *"</"[a-zA-Z]* ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Accept if input has tags with attributes: <tagname attr="
    if [[ "$text" =~ \<[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*[[:space:]] ]] && [[ "$text" =~ [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*=\" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # --- Pass 1: element text content ---
    # Match <tag...>content</tag> where content is on the same line
    local elem_matches
    elem_matches=$(echo "$text" | grep -oE '<[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*[^>]*>[^<]+</[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*>' 2>/dev/null) || true

    while IFS= read -r match; do
        [[ -z "$match" ]] && continue

        local tagname="${match#<}"
        tagname="${tagname%% *}"
        tagname="${tagname%%>*}"
        tagname="${tagname%%/*}"

        local content="${match#*>}"
        content="${content%%<*}"

        local trimmed="$content"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* || "$trimmed" == "	"* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed#?}"; done
        while [[ "$trimmed" == *" " || "$trimmed" == *"	" ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed%?}"; done
        [[ -z "$trimmed" ]] && continue

        local clean_content="${trimmed}"
        [[ -z "$tagname" ]] && continue

        result+="${tagname} ${clean_content}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$elem_matches"

    # --- Pass 2: tag attribute key/value pairs ---
    local attr_tags
    attr_tags=$(echo "$text" | grep -oE '<[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*[^>]*>' 2>/dev/null) || true

    while IFS= read -r tag; do
        [[ -z "$tag" ]] && continue

        # Skip XML declarations and comments
        case "$tag" in
            '<?'*|'<!--'*) continue ;;
        esac

        local tagname="${tag#<}"
        tagname="${tagname%% *}"
        tagname="${tagname%%/*}"
        tagname="${tagname%%>*}"

        local attrs
        attrs=$(echo "$tag" | grep -oE '[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*="[^"]*"' 2>/dev/null) || true

        while IFS= read -r attr; do
            [[ -z "$attr" ]] && continue

            local attr_name="${attr%%=*}"
            local attr_value="${attr#*=\"}"
            attr_value="${attr_value%\"}"

            [[ -z "$attr_name" ]] && continue
            [[ -z "$attr_value" ]] && continue

            result+="${tagname}.${attr_name} ${attr_value}"$'\n'
        done <<< "$attrs"
    done <<< "$attr_tags"

    echo "$result"
}
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/strategies/structured/yaml.sh===
