#!/bin/bash
## Name: yaml
## Description: Extract key/value pairs from YAML, flattening nested keys with dot notation
## Version: 1.1
## Priority: 12
## Sample: samples/yaml/basic.yaml

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE_REASON="key: value pattern with indented sub-keys"

    # Must have YAML key pattern: lines starting with word chars followed by colon
    [[ "$text" =~ (^|$'\n')[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*: ]] || return 1

    # Must NOT look like JSON (starts with { or [)
    _is_json "$1" && return 1

    # Repeated top-level keys mean a multi-record output, not a single YAML
    # mapping Aje28094Aj leave it to the dedicated record strategy (see _has_repeated_top_keys).
    _has_repeated_top_keys "$text" && return 1

    # Require a strong majority of non-blank lines to be YAML-shaped Aje28094Aj a `key:`
    # mapping, a `- ` list item, or a `---` document marker. This stops yaml from
    # claiming whitespace-columnar output that merely happens to have a
    # colon-bearing line (e.g. `free` with its `Mem:`/`Swap:` rows, or `sensors`
    # with an `Adapter:` line), which it would otherwise collapse to one record.
    local nonblank=0 yamlish=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        # A key must start with a LETTER, matching the overall gate above Aje28094Aj a
        # purely-numeric label before the colon (`/proc/interrupts`' IRQ rows:
        # `0:`, `16:`) is a table row label, not a YAML key, and would otherwise
        # inflate the yamlish ratio enough to hijack non-YAML numeric tables.
        if [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*:([[:space:]]|$) ]] \
           || [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]] ]] \
           || [[ "$_l" == "---"* ]]; then
            yamlish=$((yamlish + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $nonblank -eq 0 ]] && return 1
    [[ $(( yamlish * 100 / nonblank )) -ge 80 ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"

    local result=""
    # Key stack as indexed array
    local stack_keys=""
    local stack_size=0
    # Array index tracking: stack of counters per depth
    local array_counters=""
    local prev_depth=-1

    # Block scalar state
    local in_block=0
    local block_key=""
    local block_style=""
    local block_min_indent=0
    local block_val=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Handle block scalar accumulation
        if [[ $in_block -eq 1 ]]; then
            # Empty lines are part of the block (literal style preserves them)
            if [[ -z "$line" ]]; then
                if [[ "$block_style" == "|"* ]]; then
                    block_val+="_"
                fi
                continue
            fi

            # Calculate line indent
            local bl_stripped
            bl_stripped="${line#"${line%%[! ]*}"}"
            local bl_indent=${#line}
            bl_indent=$((bl_indent - ${#bl_stripped}))

            if [[ $bl_indent -ge $block_min_indent ]]; then
                # Still in block - accumulate
                local bl_content="$bl_stripped"
                while [[ "$bl_content" == " "* || "$bl_content" == "	"* ]]; do bl_content="${bl_content#?}"; done
                while [[ "$bl_content" == *" " || "$bl_content" == *"	" ]]; do bl_content="${bl_content%?}"; done
                if [[ -n "$block_val" ]]; then
                    if [[ "$block_style" == "|"* ]]; then
                        # Literal: join with underscores (representing newlines)
                        block_val+="_${bl_content}"
                    else
                        # Folded: join with spaces (then underscores for storage)
                        block_val+="_${bl_content}"
                    fi
                else
                    block_val="$bl_content"
                fi
                continue
            fi

            # Block ended - emit accumulated value
            if [[ -n "$block_val" ]]; then
                result+="${block_key} ${block_val}"$'\n'
            fi
            in_block=0
            block_val=""
            # Fall through to process current line normally
        fi

        # Skip empty lines
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Skip comment lines
        case "$line" in
            '#'*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Skip document markers
        [[ "$line" == "---" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "..." ]] && continue

        # Calculate indentation depth (each level = 2 spaces)
        local stripped
        stripped="${line#"${line%%[! ]*}"}"
        local indent=${#line}
        indent=$((indent - ${#stripped}))
        local depth=$((indent / 2))

        # Check if this is an array entry (- item)
        local is_array=0
        local array_value=""
        if [[ "$stripped" == "- "* || "$stripped" == "-	"* ]]; then
            is_array=1
            array_value="${stripped#- }"
            if [[ "$array_value" == "$stripped" ]]; then
                array_value="${stripped#-	}"
            fi
        fi

        if [[ $is_array -eq 1 ]]; then
            # Array entry: use parent key with numeric index
            local counter
            _strat_yaml_get_counter "$depth"
            local counter="$_YAML_COUNTER"
            _strat_yaml_set_counter "$depth" $((counter + 1))

            local full_key
            _strat_yaml_build_key "$depth"
            full_key="${_YAML_KEY}.${counter}"

            local clean_val="$array_value"
            while [[ "$clean_val" == " "* || "$clean_val" == "	"* ]]; do clean_val="${clean_val#?}"; done
            while [[ "$clean_val" == *" " || "$clean_val" == *"	" ]]; do clean_val="${clean_val%?}"; done
            if [[ -n "$clean_val" ]]; then
                result+="${full_key} ${clean_val}"$'\n'
            fi
            continue
        fi

        # Check for key: value or bare key:
        local key value
        if [[ "$stripped" =~ ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*: ]]; then
            key="${stripped%%:*}"
            # Get everything after "key:"
            local after_colon="${stripped#*:}"
            if [[ -z "$after_colon" ]]; then
                value=""
            else
                # Trim leading whitespace
                while [[ "$after_colon" == " "* || "$after_colon" == "	"* ]]; do after_colon="${after_colon#?}"; done
                value="$after_colon"
            fi
        else
            continue
        fi

        # Update the key stack: trim stack to current depth
        _strat_yaml_set_stack "$depth" "$key"

        # Reset array counters for deeper levels when we move to a new key
        _strat_yaml_reset_counters_above "$depth"

        if [[ "$value" == "|" || "$value" == ">" || "$value" == "|+" || "$value" == ">+" || "$value" == "|-" || "$value" == ">-" ]]; then
            # Block scalar: start collecting subsequent indented lines
            in_block=1
            block_style="$value"
            block_min_indent=$((indent + 2))
            block_val=""

            local full_key
            _strat_yaml_build_key "$((depth + 1))"
            full_key="$_YAML_KEY"
            block_key="${full_key// /_}"
        elif [[ -n "$value" ]]; then
            # Emit the full dotted key path with value
            local full_key
            _strat_yaml_build_key "$((depth + 1))"
            full_key="$_YAML_KEY"
            local clean_val="$value"
            while [[ "$clean_val" == " "* || "$clean_val" == "	"* ]]; do clean_val="${clean_val#?}"; done
            while [[ "$clean_val" == *" " || "$clean_val" == *"	" ]]; do clean_val="${clean_val%?}"; done
            local clean_key="${full_key// /_}"
            result+="${clean_key} ${clean_val}"$'\n'
        fi

        prev_depth=$depth
    done <<< "$text"

    # Emit any remaining block scalar
    if [[ $in_block -eq 1 && -n "$block_val" ]]; then
        result+="${block_key} ${block_val}"$'\n'
    fi

    # A single indexed list-of-records (amtool `Peers`, avro-style `fields`)
    # explodes to one tidy row per element with the scalar keys repeated.
    printf '%s' "$result" | _list_explode
}

# Helper: get array counter for a given depth. Result in _YAML_COUNTER.
_strat_yaml_get_counter () {
    local depth="$1"
    local i=0
    local val=""
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for val in $array_counters; do
        if [[ $i -eq $depth ]]; then
            IFS="$IFS_OLD"
            _YAML_COUNTER="${val:-0}"
            return
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"
    _YAML_COUNTER="0"
}

# Helper: set array counter for a given depth
_strat_yaml_set_counter () {
    local depth="$1"
    local new_val="$2"
    local new_counters=""
    local i=0
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"

    # Ensure we have enough slots
    local max=$((depth + 1))
    local current_size=0
    IFS="|"
    for val in $array_counters; do
        current_size=$((current_size + 1))
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"

    # Rebuild with updated value
    IFS="|"
    local found=0
    i=0
    for val in $array_counters; do
        if [[ $i -eq $depth ]]; then
            val="$new_val"
            found=1
        fi
        if [[ -z "$new_counters" ]]; then
            new_counters="$val"
        else
            new_counters="${new_counters}|${val}"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"

    # If depth wasn't reached, pad with zeros and add
    while [[ $i -lt $depth ]]; do
        if [[ -z "$new_counters" ]]; then
            new_counters="0"
        else
            new_counters="${new_counters}|0"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    if [[ $found -eq 0 ]]; then
        if [[ -z "$new_counters" ]]; then
            new_counters="$new_val"
        else
            new_counters="${new_counters}|${new_val}"
        fi
    fi

    array_counters="$new_counters"
}

# Helper: reset array counters above a given depth
_strat_yaml_reset_counters_above () {
    local depth="$1"
    local new_counters=""
    local i=0
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for val in $array_counters; do
        if [[ $i -gt $depth ]]; then
            val="0"
        fi
        if [[ -z "$new_counters" ]]; then
            new_counters="$val"
        else
            new_counters="${new_counters}|${val}"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"
    array_counters="$new_counters"
}

# Helper: set stack key at a given depth, truncating deeper entries
_strat_yaml_set_stack () {
    local depth="$1"
    local key="$2"
    local new_stack=""
    local i=0
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"

    # Copy existing entries up to depth
    IFS="|"
    for val in $stack_keys; do
        if [[ $i -ge $depth ]]; then
            break
        fi
        if [[ -z "$new_stack" ]]; then
            new_stack="$val"
        else
            new_stack="${new_stack}|${val}"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"

    # Pad with empty entries if needed
    while [[ $i -lt $depth ]]; do
        if [[ -z "$new_stack" ]]; then
            new_stack="_"
        else
            new_stack="${new_stack}|_"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done

    # Add the new key at this depth
    if [[ -z "$new_stack" ]]; then
        new_stack="$key"
    else
        new_stack="${new_stack}|${key}"
    fi

    stack_keys="$new_stack"
    stack_size=$((depth + 1))
}

# Helper: build dotted key path from stack up to given depth. Result in _YAML_KEY.
_strat_yaml_build_key () {
    local up_to="$1"
    _YAML_KEY=""
    local i=0
    local IFS_OLD="$IFS"
    IFS="|"
    for val in $stack_keys; do
        if [[ $i -ge $up_to ]]; then
            break
        fi
        if [[ -z "$_YAML_KEY" ]]; then
            _YAML_KEY="$val"
        else
            _YAML_KEY="${_YAML_KEY}.${val}"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    IFS="$IFS_OLD"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: R-version
## Description: Extract version fields from `R --version` banner
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/R-version/basic.txt

# `R --version` opens with 'R version 4.3.2 (2023-10-31) -- "Eye Holes"' and a
# "Platform: <triple> (...)" line, followed by license text. One wide key/value
# record: product, version, date, nickname, platform.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    local first="" line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        first="$line"; break
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ "$first" == "R version "* && "$text" == *"Platform:"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" ver="" date="" nick="" plat=""
    if [[ "$text" =~ R[[:space:]]version[[:space:]]([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*) ]]; then
        ver="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    if [[ "$text" =~ \(([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})\) ]]; then
        date="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    if [[ "$text" =~ \"([^\"]+)\" ]]; then
        nick="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    if [[ "$text" =~ Platform:[[:space:]]*([^[:space:]]+) ]]; then
        plat="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    result+="entry1.product R"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.version ${ver}"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.date ${date}"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.nickname ${nick}"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.platform ${plat}"$'\n'
    result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ansible-inventory-list
## Description: Extract hosts from `ansible-inventory --list` JSON (keys under _meta.hostvars)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/ansible-inventory-list/basic.txt

# `ansible-inventory --list` emits a JSON document whose real inventory of hosts
# lives under `_meta.hostvars` (the top-level group keys like "all"/"webservers"
# are groupings, not hosts). Each direct key of `_meta.hostvars` is a managed
# host; each becomes a single-field record.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Positively identify the ansible inventory JSON by its distinctive
    # _meta.hostvars structure (do not rely on a JSON guard declining).
    case "$text" in
        '{'*) ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
    [[ "$text" == *'"_meta"'* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *'"hostvars"'* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

# Echo the direct child keys of _meta.hostvars, one per line. Tracks brace depth
# so nested hostvar keys (e.g. "ansible_host") are ignored. mawk-safe.
_ansible_inventory_hosts () {
    awk '
    {
        L=$0
        if (capture==1 && d==target) {
            if (match(L, /"[^"]+"[ \t]*:[ \t]*\{[ \t]*$/)) {
                s=substr(L, RSTART, RLENGTH)
                match(s, /"[^"]+"/)
                print substr(s, RSTART+1, RLENGTH-2)
            }
        }
        if (L ~ /"hostvars"[ \t]*:/) { target=d+1; capture=1 }
        o=gsub(/\{/,"x",L); c=gsub(/\}/,"y",L); d=d+o-c
        if (capture==1 && d<target) capture=0
    }'
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 host
    while IFS= read -r host; do
        [[ -z "$host" ]] && continue
        host="${host//[[:space:]]/_}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.hostname ${host}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$(printf '%s\n' "$text" | _ansible_inventory_hosts)"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===META: mode=644 sha256=7cf1a711c639c88c4eab1df5dae2de093631b094ddc4c8d4f4a098c6076830ea===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: ansible-version
## Description: `ansible --version` banner (version + config/path/python key=value block)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/ansible-version/basic.txt

# `ansible --version` prints "ansible [core X.Y.Z]" followed by an indented
# "key = value" block (config file, module search path, python version, ...).
# Generic key/value parsers split on the first "=" but mangle the values that
# themselves contain spaces / "=" (search paths, python banner). This pulls the
# whole snapshot into one wide record.

_ansver_key () {
    local s="$1" out="" c i n=${#1}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${s:i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    while [[ "$out" == *__* ]]; do out="${out//__/_}"; done
    out="${out#_}"; out="${out%_}"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

_ansver_val () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/ }"
    while [[ "$v" == *"  "* ]]; do v="${v//  / }"; done
    v="${v# }"; v="${v% }"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    local first="" line trimmed
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        trimmed="${line//[[:space:]]/}"
        [[ -z "$trimmed" ]] && continue
        first="$line"
        break
    done <<< "$text"

    # Distinctive banner: "ansible [core X.Y.Z]" as the first non-blank line.
    [[ "$first" =~ ^ansible[[:space:]]+\[core[[:space:]] ]] || return 1

    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line trimmed first="" key val
    local seen_first=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        trimmed="${line//[[:space:]]/}"
        [[ -z "$trimmed" ]] && continue

        if [[ $seen_first -eq 0 ]]; then
            seen_first=1
            first="$line"
            # Pull the core version out of "ansible [core 2.16.3]".
            if [[ "$first" =~ \[core[[:space:]]+([^]]+)\] ]]; then
                result+="entry1.core_version $(_ansver_val "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")"$'\n'
            fi
            continue
        fi

        # Indented "key = value" lines.
        [[ "$line" == *" = "* ]] || continue
        key="${line%% = *}"
        val="${line#* = }"
        key="$(_ansver_key "$key")"
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        val="$(_ansver_val "$val")"
        result+="entry1.${key} ${val}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: bcc-funccount
## Description: bcc funccount FUNC/COUNT table Aje28692Aj one tidy row per function
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/bcc-funccount/basic.txt

# bcc's `funccount` prints a "Tracing N functions ..." line, a "^C" interrupt
# marker, a "FUNC   COUNT" header, one row per traced function, then a
# "Detaching..." footer. A function row has exactly two fields whose second
# field (count) is an integer Aje28094Aj that distinguishes it from every non-data line.

_bcc_funccount_is_row () {
    # $1 = field count, $2 = the count token, $3 = the FUNC token
    [[ "$1" -eq 2 && "$2" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$3" != "FUNC" ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"Tracing"* && "$text" == *"FUNC"* && "$text" == *"COUNT"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local toks
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$line"
        _bcc_funccount_is_row "${#toks[@]}" "${toks[1]:-}" "${toks[0]:-}" || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.func ${toks[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.count ${toks[1]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: bpftrace
## Description: bpftrace @map[key]: count output Aje28692Aj one tidy row per key
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/bpftrace/basic.txt

# bpftrace prints an "Attaching N probes..." line, a blank line, then one
# aggregated map entry per line: "@map[key]: count" (or "@[key]: count"). Each
# map line starts with '@' and contains "]:" Aje28094Aj that distinguishes it from the
# attach banner and blanks, so we emit exactly one record per key.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == "@"* && "$line" == *"]:"* ]]; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "@"* && "$line" == *"]:"* ]] || continue
        # key = text between the first '[' and its matching ']'
        local inside="${line#*[}"
        local key="${inside%%]*}"
        # count = text after "]:" with surrounding whitespace stripped
        local rest="${line#*]:}"
        local count="${rest// /}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.key ${key}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.count ${count}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: fossil-status
## Description: Extract status lines from fossil status output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/fossil-status/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # fossil status: "repository:" / "checkout:" kv headers plus file-change
    # lines with verbs like EDITED / ADDED / DELETED.
    local has_repo=0 has_checkout=0 has_change=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "$line" in
            "repository:"*) has_repo=1 ;;
            "checkout:"*)   has_checkout=1 ;;
            EDITED\ *|ADDED\ *|DELETED\ *|MISSING\ *|RENAMED\ *|UPDATED\ *|CONFLICT\ *|EXTRA\ *)
                has_change=1 ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_repo -eq 1 && $has_checkout -eq 1 && $has_change -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local line cleaned
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Emit one record per non-blank status line (skip blanks only).
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        case "$line" in
            *[![:space:]]*) : ;;   # has non-whitespace
            *) continue ;;
        esac

        # Clean: trim ends, collapse internal whitespace runs, spaces -> underscore.
        cleaned="$line"
        cleaned="${cleaned#"${cleaned%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # ltrim
        cleaned="${cleaned%"${cleaned##*[![:space:]]}"}"   # rtrim
        # Collapse runs of whitespace to a single space.
        while [[ "$cleaned" == *"  "* ]]; do
            cleaned="${cleaned//  / }"
        done
        cleaned="${cleaned//$'\t'/ }"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.line ${cleaned}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/system/fossil-timeline.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=13847b86d274852cf2e2a8847bda812cee8813f62efab14bdf87bddea8c492ae===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: fossil-timeline
## Description: Extract checkins from a Fossil `fossil timeline`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/fossil-timeline/basic.txt

# `fossil timeline` groups entries under `=== DATE ===` banners:
#   10:15:42 [a1b2c3d4e5] Add login form validation (user: alice tags: trunk)
# One record per timed checkin; banners and the `--- entry limit ---` footer
# are skipped.

_fossiltl_is_entry () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9][[:space:]]\[ ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line has=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _fossiltl_is_entry "$line" && has=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line timev hash rest message user
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _fossiltl_is_entry "$line" || continue
        timev="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        hash="${line#*[}"
        hash="${hash%%]*}"
        rest="${line#*] }"
        message="${rest%% (user:*}"
        if [[ "$line" == *"(user: "* ]]; then
            user="${line#*(user: }"
            user="${user%% *}"
            user="${user%)}"
        else
            user=""
        fi
        message="${message//$'\t'/_}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.time ${timev}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.hash ${hash}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.message ${message}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.user ${user}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: free
## Description: Extract memory and swap usage from free -h / free -m output
## Version: 2.0
## Priority: 10
## Sample: samples/free/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    # Reject JSON
    _is_json "$1" && return 1
    # Look for header with "total" and "used", followed by "Mem:" or "Swap:" line
    local has_header=0 has_mem_swap=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == *"total"* && "$line" == *"used"* ]]; then
            has_header=1
        fi
        if [[ "$line" == "Mem:"* || "$line" == "Swap:"* ]]; then
            has_mem_swap=1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_header -eq 1 && $has_mem_swap -eq 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # `free` is already a table: a header of column names, then one row per
    # region (`Mem:`, `Swap:`, and `Total:` with `free -t`). Emit it as indexed
    # `entry<N>.<field>` groups Aje28094Aj the same shape ls-l / kv-pairs use Aje28094Aj so the
    # capture-side tidy melt turns it back into one row per region with shared
    # columns (name, total, used, free, shared, buff_cache, available) instead
    # of welding both regions into a single unintelligible wide record.
    local -a cols=()
    local header_seen=0
    local idx=0
    local line

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue

        # Header row: contains the column labels but no leading "Region:" tag.
        # (`buff/cache` is sanitised to `buff_cache` so it is a valid field name;
        # the older `buffers`/`cached` split header is carried through verbatim.)
        if [[ $header_seen -eq 0 && "$line" == *"total"* && "$line" == *"used"* && "$line" != *:* ]]; then
            read -ra _h <<< "$line"
            cols=()
            local c
            for c in "${_h[@]}"; do
                c="${c//\//_}"   # buff/cache -> buff_cache
                cols+=("$c")
            done
            header_seen=1
            continue
        fi

        # Data row: "Region:  v1 v2 v3 ...". The label before ':' names the row.
        if [[ "$line" == *:* ]]; then
            local label="${line%%:*}"
            label="${label// /}"
            [[ -z "$label" ]] && continue
            local after="${line#*:}"
            read -ra _v <<< "$after"
            [[ ${#_v[@]} -eq 0 ]] && continue

            idx=$((idx + 1))
            result+="entry${idx}.name ${label}"$'\n'
            local i col
            for i in "${!_v[@]}"; do
                col="${cols[$i]:-col$((i + 1))}"
                result+="entry${idx}.${col} ${_v[$i]}"$'\n'
            done
            continue
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $idx -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${idx}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

===META: mode=644 sha256=2dd61d1afefecc91101ad10edbd226be8cddde144579d266fc258aa8d11a050a===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: git-branch-vv
## Description: Extract branch rows from `git branch -vv`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/git-branch-vv/basic.txt

# `git branch -vv` prints one line per branch:
#   `* main            a1b2c3d [origin/main] Fix null pointer ...`
#   `  hotfix/urgent   7c6b5a4 Refactor session handling`
# Leading `*` marks the current branch, then the branch name, a 7-hex short SHA,
# an optional `[upstream ...]` tracking block, then the commit subject. Emit ONE
# record per branch (name, sha, upstream). Detection keys narrowly on a
# `<name> <7-hex> [` signature so it declines vmstat/dstat/apt-list/dnf-list.

_gbvv_san () { local v="$1"; v="${v//$'\t'/_}"; printf '%s' "$v"; }

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Require at least one canonical branch line: optional `* `, a branch name,
    # a 7-hex short SHA, then a `[upstream]` tracking block.
    local line hit=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^(\*[[:space:]]|[[:space:]][[:space:]])[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[0-9a-f]{7}[[:space:]]+\[ ]]; then
            hit=1; break
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $hit -eq 1 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" entry=0 line body name sha rest up
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Drop the leading current-branch marker.
        body="$line"
        body="${body#\*}"
        body="${body#"${body%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # ltrim
        name="${body%%[[:space:]]*}"              # branch name
        rest="${body#"$name"}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # ltrim to SHA
        sha="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"
        # Require a 7-hex short SHA to accept the row.
        [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7}$ ]] || continue
        rest="${rest#"$sha"}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"   # ltrim
        up="-"
        if [[ "$rest" == \[* ]]; then
            up="${rest#\[}"; up="${up%%\]*}"      # content inside [...]
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name $(_gbvv_san "$name")"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.sha ${sha}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.upstream $(_gbvv_san "$up")"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: git-log-graph
## Description: Extract commits from `git log --graph --oneline`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/git-log-graph/basic.txt

# `git log --graph --oneline` draws an ASCII graph; commit lines carry a `*`
# node followed by an abbreviated sha and subject:
#   * a1b2c3d Add login form validation
#   | * d4e5f6a Add search indexing
# Pure-glyph lines (|\ , |/ , | ) carry no commit and are skipped.

_gitloggraph_is_commit () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[|/\\\*[:space:]]*\*[[:space:]]+[0-9a-f]+[[:space:]] ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line has=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _gitloggraph_is_commit "$line" && has=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line rest sha message
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _gitloggraph_is_commit "$line" || continue
        # drop everything up to and including the `*` node marker
        rest="${line#*\*}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        sha="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"
        message="${rest#*[[:space:]]}"
        message="${message#"${message%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        message="${message//$'\t'/_}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.commit ${sha}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.message ${message}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: git-log-stat
## Description: Extract per-file diffstat lines from `git log --stat`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 13
## Sample: samples/git-log-stat/basic.txt

# `git log --stat` prints commit blocks; each changed file gets a line:
#   src/login.py         | 24 +++++++++++++++++++----
# The trailing `N files changed, ...` summary carries no `|` and is skipped.
# One record per file-stat line, across all commit blocks.

_gitlogstat_is_file () {

        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi

}

strategy_extract () {

        _gitlogstat_is_file "$line" || continue
        path="${line%%|*}"

#!/bin/bash
## Name: git-worktree-list-porcelain
## Description: Extract worktrees from `git worktree list --porcelain`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/git-worktree-list-porcelain/basic.txt

# Porcelain output is blank-line-separated blocks:
#   worktree /home/user/glean
#   HEAD a1b2c3d4...
#   branch refs/heads/main     (or `detached`)
# One record per worktree block.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line has_wt=0 has_head=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "worktree "* ]] && has_wt=1
        [[ "$line" =~ ^HEAD[[:space:]][0-9a-f]+ ]] && has_head=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_wt -eq 1 && $has_head -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local wt="" head="" branch="" have=0

    _flush () {
        [[ $have -eq 1 ]] || return 0
        local w="${wt//$'\t'/_}"
        local h="${head}"
        local b="${branch}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.worktree ${w}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.head ${h}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.branch ${b}"$'\n'
        wt=""; head=""; branch=""; have=0
    }

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "$line" in
            "worktree "*)
                _flush
                wt="${line#worktree }"; have=1 ;;
            "HEAD "*)
                head="${line#HEAD }" ;;
            "branch "*)
                branch="${line#branch }"
                branch="${branch#refs/heads/}" ;;
            "detached")
                branch="detached" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"
    _flush
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/system/gpg-list-packets.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=92dfea24fc1928d69cf96ce821bd3195b5cdd00710dd26e071df89b4f8614068===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: gpg-list-packets
## Description: Extract packet fields from `gpg --list-packets` into one wide record
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/gpg-list-packets/basic.txt

# `gpg --list-packets` prints `# off=.. ctb=.. tag=..` markers, `:type packet:`
# block headers, and TAB-indented `keyword value` detail lines:
#   \tversion 4, algo 1, created 1699999999, expires 0
#   \tkeyid: A1B2C3D4E5F60718
# Flatten the tab-indented detail lines into ONE wide record (`entry1.<field>
# value`). Repeated keywords are suffixed _2, _3, ... so columns stay unique.

_gpglp_name () {
    local s="$1" out="" c i n=${#1}
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        c="${s:i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9]) out+="$c" ;;
            *) out+="_" ;;
        esac
    done
    while [[ "$out" == *__* ]]; do out="${out//__/_}"; done
    out="${out#_}"; out="${out%_}"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}
_gpglp_san () { local v="$1"; v="${v//$'\t'/_}"; printf '%s' "$v"; }

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"ctb="*"tag="* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *":public key packet:"* || "$text" == *":signature packet:"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" result="" line rest key val san count fields=0
    declare -A seen=()
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Only TAB-indented detail lines carry keyword/value pairs.
        [[ "$line" == $'\t'* ]] || continue
        rest="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"    # ltrim (drops leading tab)
        [[ -n "$rest" ]] || continue
        key="${rest%%[[:space:]]*}"                # first word
        val="${rest#"$key"}"
        val="${val#"${val%%[![:space:]]*}"}"       # ltrim value
        san="$(_gpglp_name "$key")"
        [[ -n "$san" ]] || continue
        count="${seen[$san]:-0}"
        count=$((count + 1))
        seen[$san]=$count
        [[ $count -gt 1 ]] && san="${san}_${count}"
        result+="entry1.${san} $(_gpglp_san "$val")"$'\n'
        fields=$((fields + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $fields -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: iftop
## Description: Extract per-direction connection records from iftop output (host, peer, rates)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/iftop/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Distinctive signature: iftop's cumulative-rate table and totals.
    if [[ "$text" == *"Total send and receive rate"* ]] \
       || { [[ "$text" == *"cumulative"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"=>"* ]] && [[ "$text" == *"<="* ]]; }; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local last_host="" last_peer=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # Skip separator rules and the Total summary lines.
        [[ "$line" == *"Total"* ]] && continue

        local v
        read -ra v <<< "$line"

        local direction="" host="" peer="" r2="" r10="" r40="" cum=""
        if [[ "${v[1]:-}" == "=>" ]]; then
            # "<host> => <peer>  <2s> <10s> <40s> <cumulative>"
            [[ ${#v[@]} -lt 7 ]] && continue
            direction="send"
            host="${v[0]}"; peer="${v[2]}"
            r2="${v[3]}"; r10="${v[4]}"; r40="${v[5]}"; cum="${v[6]}"
            last_host="$host"; last_peer="$peer"
        elif [[ "${v[0]:-}" == "<=" ]]; then
            # "<= <2s> <10s> <40s> <cumulative>" (host/peer from prior => row)
            [[ ${#v[@]} -lt 5 ]] && continue
            direction="recv"
            host="$last_host"; peer="$last_peer"
            r2="${v[1]}"; r10="${v[2]}"; r40="${v[3]}"; cum="${v[4]}"
        else
            continue
        fi

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.host ${host}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.direction ${direction}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.peer ${peer}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.last_2s ${r2}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.last_10s ${r10}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.last_40s ${r40}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.cumulative ${cum}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/system/iotop.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=a14c04548432a32ddfdf04b9e46c18bbc8c76f21da8acd14bc5b6b3efbf31473===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: iotop
## Description: Extract per-process records from iotop output (tid, prio, user, io rates, command)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/iotop/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Distinctive signature: iotop's DISK READ/WRITE totals plus its
    # "TID PRIO USER ... IO> COMMAND" process header.
    if [[ "$text" == *"Total DISK READ"* ]] \
       && [[ "$text" == *"TID"* ]] \
       && [[ "$text" == *"DISK WRITE"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local in_table=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue

        # Skip the Total/Current summary lines.
        [[ "$line" == *"DISK READ"*"|"* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == *"DISK WRITE"*"|"* ]] && continue

        # The TID/PRIO/... row is the process-table header.
        if [[ "$line" == *"TID"* ]] && [[ "$line" == *"COMMAND"* ]]; then
            in_table=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_table -eq 0 ]] && continue

        local v
        read -ra v <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#v[@]} -lt 11 ]] && continue
        [[ "${v[0]}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue

        # Columns: TID PRIO USER  <read val+unit>  <write val+unit>
        #          <swapin val+unit>  <io val+unit>  COMMAND...
        local command="${v[*]:11}"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.tid ${v[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.prio ${v[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.user ${v[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.disk_read ${v[3]} ${v[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.disk_write ${v[5]} ${v[6]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.swapin ${v[7]} ${v[8]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.io ${v[9]} ${v[10]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.command ${command}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: jj-log
## Description: Extract changes from a Jujutsu `jj log` graph
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/jj-log/basic.txt

# `jj log` draws a graph; node lines carry the change id, author, timestamp and
# commit id, e.g.
#   @  qpvuntsm alice@example.com 2026-07-06 10:15:42 a1b2c3d4
# Description continuation lines and the synthetic root() node (no author email)
# are skipped, so only real changes are counted.

_jjlog_is_node () {
    [[ "$1" =~ [^[:space:]]+@[^[:space:]]+\.[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+20[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9][[:space:]] ]]

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line has=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _jjlog_is_node "$line" && has=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local -a a
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _jjlog_is_node "$line" || continue
        read -ra a <<< "$line"
        # a[0]=graph glyph, a[1]=change id, a[2]=author, a[3]=date, last=commit id
        local change="${a[1]}" author="${a[2]}" datev="${a[3]}"
        local commit="${a[$((${#a[@]}-1))]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.change ${change}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.author ${author}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.date ${datev}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.commit ${commit}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: lastb
## Description: Extract failed login attempts from `lastb` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/lastb/basic.txt

# `lastb` prints one row per bad login:
#   user  ssh:notty  1.2.3.4  Mon Jul  6 10:01 - 10:01  (00:00)
# followed by a trailing "btmp begins ..." footer.

_lastb_is_login () {
    [[ "$1" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}[[:space:]]+(Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun)[[:space:]] ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # lastlog's table opens with a "Username Port From Latest" header and its
    # data rows mimic lastb's login lines Aje28094Aj that table belongs to
    # aligned-columns, not lastb (which has no header).
    case "$text" in Username[[:space:]]*) return 1 ;; esac
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if _lastb_is_login "$line"; then
            _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        _lastb_is_login "$line" || continue
        read -ra _a <<< "$line"
        local user="${_a[0]}" terminal="${_a[1]}" host="${_a[2]}"
        # The remainder is "<weekday date time> - <time>  (dur)".
        local rest="${line#*"$host"}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        # duration is the trailing (..) token; when is everything before it.
        local duration="" when="$rest"
        if [[ "$rest" =~ \(([^\)]*)\)[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
            duration="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            when="${rest%(*}"
            when="${when%"${when##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        fi
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.user ${user}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.terminal ${terminal}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.host ${host}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.when ${when}"$'\n'
        [[ -n "$duration" ]] && result+="entry${entry}.duration ${duration}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: lscpu-parse
## Description: Extract per-CPU topology rows from lscpu -p parsable CSV output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/lscpu-parse/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # lscpu -p: "#"-comment preamble then rows like "0,0,0,0,,0,0,0,0"
    # (the empty 5th field / double comma is distinctive).
    local rows=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue
        # A CPU row starts with an integer, is comma-separated, and contains
        # the empty-field ",," produced by lscpu -p.
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+, ]] && [[ "$line" == *",,"* ]]; then
            rows=$((rows + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $rows -ge 2 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == "#"* ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+, ]] || continue

        IFS=',' read -ra c <<< "$line"
        # c[0]=cpu c[1]=core c[2]=socket c[3]=node c[4]=(empty) c[5]=L1d c[6]=L1i c[7]=L2 c[8]=L3
        [[ ${#c[@]} -ge 9 ]] || continue

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.cpu ${c[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.core ${c[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.socket ${c[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.node ${c[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.l1d ${c[5]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.l1i ${c[6]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.l2 ${c[7]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.l3 ${c[8]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: multipath-ll
## Description: Extract per-path rows from `multipath -ll` topology output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 27
## Sample: samples/multipath-ll/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # `multipath -ll` is distinctive: a map line ending `dm-N ...`, a
    # `size=... features=... hwhandler=... wp=rw` line, and `policy='...'` groups.
    local has_wp=0 has_policy=0 has_hwhandler=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == *"wp=rw"* || "$line" == *"wp=ro"* ]] && has_wp=1
        [[ "$line" == *"policy='"* ]] && has_policy=1
        [[ "$line" == *"hwhandler='"* ]] && has_hwhandler=1
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_wp -eq 1 && $has_policy -eq 1 && $has_hwhandler -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Strip the leading tree drawing chars (spaces, |, `, -, +).
        local stripped="${line#"${line%%[!| \`+-]*}"}"
        read -ra f <<< "$stripped"
        # A leaf path row starts with an H:C:I:L tuple, e.g. `6:0:0:0 sdc 8:32 active ready running`
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 6 ]] || continue
        [[ "${f[0]}" =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || continue

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.hcil ${f[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.devnode ${f[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.major_minor ${f[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.dm_status ${f[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.path_status ${f[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.online ${f[5]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: numastat
## Description: Extract per-node memory counters from `numastat` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/numastat/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Distinctive signature: a header row whose every token matches nodeN
    # (node0 node1 ...), followed by "metric val0 val1" rows. df-h.txt's header
    # is "Filesystem Size Used ..." Aje28094Aj no node tokens Aje28094Aj so it declines.
    local line first="" tok ok=0 seen_header=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ $seen_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            seen_header=1
            ok=1
            local ntok=0
            for tok in $line; do
                ntok=$((ntok + 1))
                [[ "$tok" =~ ^node[0-9]+$ ]] || { ok=0; break; }
            done
            [[ $ntok -ge 1 ]] || ok=0
            [[ $ok -eq 1 ]] || return 1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $ok -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line seen_header=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ $seen_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            seen_header=1     # skip the "node0 node1" header row
            continue
        fi
        # metric  node0val  node1val ...
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 2 ]] || continue
        local metric="${f[0]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.metric ${metric}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.node0 ${f[1]}"$'\n'
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 3 ]] && result+="entry${entry}.node1 ${f[2]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: pcp-pmstat
## Description: Extract per-sample rows from `pcp pmstat` / `pmstat` columnar output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/pcp-pmstat/basic.txt

# `pcp pmstat` prints a two-line banner+header:
#    loadavg           memory      swap        io    system         cpu
#    1 min  swpd  free  buff cache  si so  bi bo  in cs  us sy id
# followed by one sample row per line. The leading "loadavg / 1 min" column is a
# single float value (e.g. 0.42), so data rows carry 14 fixed columns. Signature:
# the "loadavg" group banner plus the "1 min" sub-header. Emit ONE record per
# sample row; skip both header lines.

_pcp_sanitize () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *loadavg* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *swpd* ]]    || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"1 min"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line i
    local -a t=()
    local -a fields=(loadavg swpd free buff cache si so bi bo in cs us sy id)
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        # data rows: first token is a float (loadavg), header rows are not
        [[ "${t[0]}" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
        [[ ${#t[@]} -eq ${#fields[@]} ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i=0; i<${#fields[@]}; i++)); do
            result+="entry${entry}.${fields[$i]} $(_pcp_sanitize "${t[$i]}")"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: perf-trace
## Description: perf trace -s syscall summary table Aje28692Aj one tidy row per syscall
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/perf-trace/basic.txt

# `perf trace -s` prints a "Summary of events:" banner, a per-thread line
# (e.g. "mysqld (1843), 88213 events, 42.1%"), a
# "syscall calls errors total (msec) min (msec) avg (msec) max (msec) stddev (%)"
# header, then one row per syscall. A syscall row has 8 whitespace fields whose
# second field (calls) is an integer Aje28094Aj that distinguishes it from the banner,
# the thread line, and the parenthesised header.

_perf_trace_is_row () {
    # $1 = field count, $2 = the calls token
    [[ "$1" -eq 8 && "$2" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"Summary of events:"* && "$text" == *"stddev"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    local toks
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$line"
        _perf_trace_is_row "${#toks[@]}" "${toks[1]:-}" || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.syscall ${toks[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.calls ${toks[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.errors ${toks[2]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.total_msec ${toks[3]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.min_msec ${toks[4]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.avg_msec ${toks[5]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.max_msec ${toks[6]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.stddev_pct ${toks[7]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: php-modules
## Description: Extract module names from `php -m` output (skips [PHP Modules]/[Zend Modules] section headers)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/php-modules/basic.txt

# `php -m` prints bracketed section headers ("[PHP Modules]", "[Zend Modules]")
# followed by one module name per line. The bracket lines and blank separators
# are skipped; every remaining line is a module. Single-column list; a module
# name containing a space (e.g. "Zend OPcache") is joined with an underscore so
# it stays one value.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # NB: no _is_json guard here Aje28094Aj this output legitimately begins with '[',
    # which _is_json treats as JSON. The literal section-header check below is
    # specific enough on its own.
    # Distinctive: the "[PHP Modules]" section header.
    [[ "$text" == *"[PHP Modules]"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Trim surrounding whitespace.
        line="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        line="${line%"${line##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Skip bracketed section headers.
        [[ "$line" =~ ^\[.*\]$ ]] && continue
        # The whole line is the module name value; spaces (e.g. "Zend OPcache")
        # survive because the engine splits each record on its first space only.
        local v="${line}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${v}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'

#!/bin/bash
## Name: pipx-list
## Description: `pipx list` Aje28094Aj one record per installed package (name, version)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/pipx-list/basic.txt

# `pipx list` prints a "venvs are in Aje280a6Aj" / "apps are exposed Aje280a6Aj" preamble, then one
# `   package <name> <version>, installed using Python Aje280a6Aj` line per package, each
# followed by indented `- <app>` lines. Emit one record per package (name,
# version), skipping the preamble and the `- app` sub-lines.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local saw_pkg=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]+package[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]] ]] && { saw_pkg=1; break; }
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $saw_pkg -eq 1 ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ "$_l" =~ ^[[:space:]]+package[[:space:]]+([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+([^[:space:],]+) ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.version ${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'

===META: mode=644 sha256=ff89aaed349bd9da197d49b4a5dcd7011b98c22fda61c0ec59fb92c75b8ce39d===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: pkg-config
## Description: Extract packages from `pkg-config --list-all` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 21
## Sample: samples/pkg-config/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1

    # Decline anything with an all-caps column header (`prlimit`'s
    # "RESOURCE DESCRIPTION SOFT HARD UNITS", ps/who/aws headers). `pkg-config
    # --list-all` never prints a header Aje28094Aj its first line is a package Aje28094Aj so a
    # multi-token ALL-CAPS first line means this is a real table for
    # aligned-columns, not a name/description list.
    local _first="" _fl
    while IFS= read -r _fl; do
        [[ -z "${_fl//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        _first="$_fl"; break
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ "$_first" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*([[:space:]]+[A-Z][A-Z0-9_()%-]*)+[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    # Header smell: a real pkg-config list opens with an entry, so its first
    # line carries the " - " name/description separator. A first line WITHOUT
    # " - " followed by lines WITH it is a headed table (yum/dnf repolist's
    # "repo id  repo name  status") Aje28094Aj decline it for aligned-columns.
    if [[ "$_first" != *" - "* && "$text" == *" - "* ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    # Same smell, Title-Case variant: a first line of 3+ tokens that ALL open
    # with a capital ("Username Port From Latest") is a column header, not a
    # package entry Aje28094Aj package names are effectively never Title-Case runs.
    local _htoks=() _ht _allcap=1
    read -ra _htoks <<< "$_first"
    if [[ ${#_htoks[@]} -ge 3 ]]; then
        for _ht in "${_htoks[@]}"; do
            [[ "$_ht" =~ ^[A-Z] ]] || { _allcap=0; break; }
        done
        [[ $_allcap -eq 1 ]] && return 1
    fi

    # Distinctive: every line is "<package-name>   <prose description>".
    # A package name starts with a letter and is a single token; the remainder
    # is a free-text description (contains an alphabetic word). Reject anything
    # that looks like a sized/percentage table (df) or an arrow map (ldconfig).
    local lines=0 line _cc=() _t _colon=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        # No size/percentage tables, no "=>" maps, no parenthesised version lists.
        [[ "$line" == *"%"* || "$line" == *"=>"* ]] && return 1
        local name="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        # Package name: starts with a letter, package-ish characters only.
        [[ "$name" =~ ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$ ]] || return 1
        local rest="${line#"$name"}"
        rest="${rest#"${rest%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        # Description must be present and contain a real word (2+ letters).
        [[ -n "$rest" && "$rest" =~ [A-Za-z][A-Za-z] ]] || return 1
        # A ` : `-aligned "Label : value" line is a colon key/value block
        # (chage -l, some status dumps) Aje28094Aj colon-fields/colons own those, not a
        # pkg-config name/description list (whose descriptions use ` - `, not ` : `).
        [[ "$line" == *" : "* ]] && _colon=$((_colon + 1))
        _t=(); read -ra _t <<< "$line"; _cc+=("${#_t[@]}")
        lines=$((lines + 1))
    done <<< "$text"
    # Mostly colon key/value lines -> decline (let a colon parser split them).
    [[ $lines -ge 2 && $(( _colon * 100 / lines )) -ge 60 ]] && return 1
    # A consistent multi-column table (dominant modal column count >=3) is a real
    # aligned table for aligned-columns (az/aws/dnf/chage/es-cat listings), not a
    # pkg-config name/description list Aje28094Aj whose description length (and so column
    # count) varies line to line. Decline it so aligned-columns wins instead of
    # cramming every trailing field into `description`.
    if [[ $lines -ge 2 ]]; then
        local _m=0 _best=0 _a _b _k
        for _a in "${_cc[@]}"; do
            _k=0; for _b in "${_cc[@]}"; do [[ "$_b" -eq "$_a" ]] && _k=$((_k + 1)); done
            [[ $_k -gt $_best ]] && { _best=$_k; _m=$_a; }
        done
        [[ $_m -ge 3 && $(( _best * 100 / lines )) -ge 60 ]] && return 1
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local name="${line%%[[:space:]]*}"
        local desc="${line#"$name"}"
        desc="${desc#"${desc%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.description ${desc}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: pmap
## Description: Extract memory mapping rows from `pmap <pid>` output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/pmap/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    # Distinctive signature: a "<pid>:  <command>" banner on line 1, mapping rows
    # whose first token is a hex address and second a size like "148K", and a
    # trailing "total <N>" footer. df-h.txt has none of these.
    local line first="" nmap=0 total=0 n=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        if [[ $n -eq 1 ]]; then
            [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9]+: ]] || return 1
            continue
        fi
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        if [[ "${f[0]}" == "total" ]]; then
            total=1
            continue
        fi
        if [[ "${f[0]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]+$ && "${f[1]}" =~ ^[0-9]+K?$ ]]; then
            nmap=$((nmap + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $nmap -ge 2 && $total -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line n=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        [[ $n -eq 1 ]] && continue                 # skip PID/command banner
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ "${f[0]}" == "total" ]] && continue     # skip footer
        # mapping row: address kbytes mode mapping...  (rss column, if present,
        # sits between kbytes and mode; guard by locating the mode token).
        [[ "${f[0]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]+$ ]] || continue
        [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 3 ]] || continue
        local address="${f[0]}" kbytes="${f[1]}"
        # Find the permission/mode token (chars from rwxsp-). It is either f[2]
        # (no rss column) or f[3] (rss column present).
        local mode="" mapping="" idx=2
        if [[ "${f[2]}" =~ ^[rwxsp-]+$ ]]; then
            mode="${f[2]}"; idx=3
        elif [[ ${#f[@]} -ge 4 && "${f[3]}" =~ ^[rwxsp-]+$ ]]; then
            mode="${f[3]}"; idx=4
        else
            mode="${f[2]}"; idx=3
        fi
        local j="$idx"
        while [[ $j -lt ${#f[@]} ]]; do
            mapping+="${f[$j]} "; j=$((j + 1))
        done
        mapping="${mapping% }"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.address ${address}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.kbytes ${kbytes}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.mode ${mode}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.mapping ${mapping}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    printf '%s' "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: powertop
## Description: powertop tunable/usage table Aje28692Aj one tidy row per process (usage, events, category, description)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/powertop/basic.txt

# powertop's overview prints a discharge/summary preamble then an aligned table:
#     Usage       Events/s    Category       Description
#     45.2 ms/s    142.1       Process        /usr/lib/postgresql/postgres
# The Usage column is a number + unit ("45.2 ms/s"), so plain whitespace splitting
# over-counts columns; parse positionally instead. Tidied to one row per entry.

_pt_is_header () {
    [[ "$1" == *"Events/s"* && "$1" == *"Category"* ]]
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line seen_hdr=0 seen_row=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ $seen_hdr -eq 0 ]]; then
            _pt_is_header "$line" && seen_hdr=1
        else
            [[ -n "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && seen_row=1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $seen_hdr -eq 1 && $seen_row -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line past=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ $past -eq 0 ]]; then
            _pt_is_header "$line" && past=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        local toks; toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$line"
        local n=${#toks[@]}
        # usage(value unit) events category description...  -> need >= 4 tokens
        [[ $n -ge 4 ]] || continue
        local usage="${toks[0]}_${toks[1]}"
        local events="${toks[2]}"
        local category="${toks[3]}"
        local desc="" i
        for ((i = 4; i < n; i++)); do
            [[ -n "$desc" ]] && desc+="_"
            desc+="${toks[$i]}"
        done
        [[ -z "$desc" ]] && desc="-"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.usage ${usage}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.events ${events}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.category ${category}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.description ${desc}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: proc-devices
## Description: Extract registered character/block devices from /proc/devices
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/proc-devices/basic.txt

# /proc/devices has two sections, each a "<major> <name>" list:
#   Character devices:
#     1 mem
#   Block devices:
#     8 sd
# We emit one record per device with its section type, major number and name,
# skipping the section headers and the blank line between them.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"Character devices:"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Block devices:"* ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0 section=""

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        case "$line" in
            "Character devices:") section="character"; continue ;;
            "Block devices:")     section="block";     continue ;;
        esac

        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 2 ]] && continue
        [[ "${f[0]}" == *[!0-9]* ]] && continue      # major must be numeric

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.type ${section}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.major ${f[0]}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.name ${f[1]}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: proc-filesystems
## Description: Extract supported filesystem types from /proc/filesystems
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/proc-filesystems/basic.txt

# /proc/filesystems lists one filesystem per line, tab-separated: an optional
# "nodev" marker then the filesystem name:
#   nodev<TAB>sysfs
#   <TAB>ext4
# We emit one record per line with a nodev flag and the fs name.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"nodev"$'\t'* ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 1 ]] && continue

        local nodev="" name
        if [[ "${f[0]}" == "nodev" && ${#f[@]} -ge 2 ]]; then
            nodev="nodev"
            name="${f[1]}"
        else
            name="${f[0]}"
        fi

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.nodev ${nodev}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.name ${name}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: proc-net-snmp
## Description: Extract per-protocol SNMP counters from /proc/net/snmp
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/proc-net-snmp/basic.txt

# /proc/net/snmp is a sequence of header/value line pairs, one pair per protocol:
#   Ip: Forwarding DefaultTTL InReceives ... OutRequests   <- column names
#   Ip: 2 64 1204832 ... 982341                            <- values
# A header line's first data token is a word; a value line's is numeric. We pair
# each value line with the most recent header for the same protocol label and
# emit one record per value line, columns taken from that paired header.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    local reh='(^|
)[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*:[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z]'
    local rev='(^|
)[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*:[[:space:]]+-?[0-9]'
    [[ "$text" =~ $reh ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" =~ $rev ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0
    declare -A HDR=()

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 2 ]] && continue
        [[ "${f[0]}" == *: ]] || continue

        local label="${f[0]%:}" first="${f[1]}"
        if [[ "$first" == -* || "$first" == [0-9]* ]]; then
            # value line: pair with stored header for this protocol
            local -a hcols=()
            read -ra hcols <<< "${HDR[$label]}"
            n=$((n + 1))
            result+="entry${n}.proto ${label}"$'\n'
            local i
            for ((i = 1; i < ${#f[@]}; i++)); do
                local col="${hcols[$((i - 1))]:-col$i}"
                result+="entry${n}.${col} ${f[$i]}"$'\n'
            done
        else
            # header line: remember its column names for this protocol
            HDR[$label]="${f[*]:1}"
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: proc-net-tcp
## Description: Extract TCP socket table rows from /proc/net/tcp
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/proc-net-tcp/basic.txt

# /proc/net/tcp has a fixed header:
#   sl  local_address rem_address   st tx_queue rx_queue tr tm->when retrnsmt uid timeout inode
# then one hex-encoded record per socket. We keep the named leading columns and
# preserve the remaining trailing fields as col13.. so nothing is dropped.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"local_address"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"rem_address"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"tx_queue"* ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0
    local names="sl local_address rem_address st tx_queue rx_queue tr tm_when retrnsmt uid timeout inode"
    local -a hn=()
    read -ra hn <<< "$names"

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == *"local_address"* ]] && continue   # header

        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 12 ]] && continue
        [[ "${f[0]}" == *: ]] || continue                # data rows are "N:"

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.sl ${f[0]%:}"$'\n'
        local i
        for ((i = 1; i < ${#f[@]}; i++)); do
            local col="${hn[$i]:-col$i}"
            result+="entry${n}.${col} ${f[$i]}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: proc-pagetypeinfo
## Description: Extract per-zone/migrate-type free-page counts from /proc/pagetypeinfo
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/proc-pagetypeinfo/basic.txt

# /proc/pagetypeinfo has a "Free pages count per migrate type at order ..." table:
#   Node    0, zone      DMA, type    Unmovable   0  0  0  1  2 ... 0
# One row per (node, zone, migrate type) with 11 order columns. We skip the
# "Page block order:" / "Pages per block:" banners and the column header line.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *", type"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Free pages count"* ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == Node*", zone"*", type"* ]] || continue

        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        # f: Node <node>, zone <zone>, type <type> <order0> ... <order10>
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 17 ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.node ${node}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.zone ${zone}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${n}.type ${type}"$'\n'
        local i
        for ((i = 0; i <= 10; i++)); do
            result+="entry${n}.order${i} ${f[$((6 + i))]}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"

#!/bin/bash
## Name: proc-schedstat
## Description: Extract per-CPU scheduler statistics from /proc/schedstat
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/proc-schedstat/basic.txt

# /proc/schedstat starts with "version N" and "timestamp N", then per-CPU lines
#   cpu0 0 0 0 0 0 0 <run> <wait> <slices>
# each followed by "domainN ..." rows. We keep one record per cpuN line (its 9
# counters) and skip version/timestamp/domain lines.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    [[ "$text" == *"timestamp "* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"domain0 "* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"cpu0 "* ]] || return 1
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" line n=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        [[ "$line" == cpu[0-9]* ]] || continue

        local -a f=()
        read -ra f <<< "$line"
        # f: cpuN c1 c2 ... c9
        [[ ${#f[@]} -lt 10 ]] && continue

        n=$((n + 1))
        result+="entry${n}.cpu ${f[0]}"$'\n'
        local i
        for ((i = 1; i <= 9; i++)); do
            result+="entry${n}.col${i} ${f[$i]}"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $n -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${n}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"

#!/bin/bash
## Name: rc-status
## Description: Extract service states from OpenRC rc-status output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/rc-status/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # OpenRC rc-status: a "Runlevel:" header and "svc   [  started  ]" lines.
    local has_runlevel=0 svc=0 line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "$line" in
            "Runlevel:"*) has_runlevel=1 ;;
        esac
        if [[ "$line" == *"[ "*" ]"* ]] && { [[ "$line" == *"started"* ]] || [[ "$line" == *"stopped"* ]] || [[ "$line" == *"crashed"* ]]; }; then
            svc=$((svc + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_runlevel -eq 1 && $svc -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local line trimmed service status
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        case "$line" in
            "Runlevel:"*) continue ;;
        esac
        # A service line has a "[ ... ]" status bracket.
        [[ "$line" == *"["*"]"* ]] || continue

        trimmed="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        service="${trimmed%%[[:space:]]*}"
        [[ -n "$service" ]] || continue

        # Status is the text between the brackets, whitespace stripped.
        status="${line#*[}"
        status="${status%%]*}"
        status="${status//[[:space:]]/}"

        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.service ${service}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.status ${status}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: swift-version
## Description: Extract version fields from `swift --version` banner
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/swift-version/basic.txt

# `swift --version` prints "Apple Swift version 5.9.2 (swiftlang-... clang-...)"
# and a "Target: <triple>" line. One wide key/value record: product, version,
# swiftlang, clang, target.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    if [[ "$text" == *"Swift version"* && "$text" == *"Target:"* ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" ver="" slang="" clang="" target=""
    if [[ "$text" =~ Swift[[:space:]]version[[:space:]]([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*) ]]; then
        ver="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    if [[ "$text" =~ swiftlang-([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*) ]]; then
        slang="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    if [[ "$text" =~ clang-([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*) ]]; then
        clang="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    if [[ "$text" =~ Target:[[:space:]]*([^[:space:]]+) ]]; then
        target="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    fi
    result+="entry1.product Swift"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.version ${ver}"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.swiftlang ${slang}"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.clang ${clang}"$'\n'
    result+="entry1.target ${target}"$'\n'
    result+="total_entries 1"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
