===META: mode=644 sha256=b5cdb9b2097ceb66bf2f9f90e0b4aeb7629f3ff6cef85905fe6ab5104d535ff8===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: sysstat
## Description: sysstat tools (mpstat, sar, pidstat) Aje28094Aj banner + timestamped table
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 40
## Sample: samples/sysstat/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"; _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    local line first_seen=0 banner_ok=0 time_ok=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        # Skip blank / whitespace-only lines.
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        if [[ $first_seen -eq 0 ]]; then
            first_seen=1
            # The first non-blank line must be a sysstat banner: begins with a
            # kernel name (a letter) and ends with "(N CPU)".
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[A-Za-z].*\([0-9]+\ CPU\)[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
                banner_ok=1
                continue
            fi
            return 1
        fi
        # A later line whose first token is a HH:MM:SS timestamp.
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9] ]]; then
            time_ok=1
        fi
    done <<< "$text"

    if [[ $banner_ok -eq 1 && $time_ok -eq 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"; local result="" entry=0
    local line first_seen=0 got_header=0
    local -a cols=()

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue

        # First non-blank line is the banner Aje28094Aj skip it.
        if [[ $first_seen -eq 0 ]]; then
            first_seen=1
            continue
        fi

        local -a toks=()
        read -ra toks <<< "$line"
        [[ ${#toks[@]} -eq 0 ]] && continue

        # Leading HH:MM:SS timestamp (optionally followed by AM/PM) is the time.
        local timeval offset
        if [[ "${toks[0]}" =~ ^[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            timeval="${toks[0]}"; offset=1
            if [[ "${toks[1]:-}" == "AM" || "${toks[1]:-}" == "PM" ]]; then
                timeval="${toks[0]} ${toks[1]}"; offset=2
            fi
        else
            continue
        fi

        # First timestamped line is the column header.
        if [[ $got_header -eq 0 ]]; then
            got_header=1
            cols=()
            local i
            for ((i=offset; i<${#toks[@]}; i++)); do
                cols+=("$(_strat_sysstat_sanitize "${toks[$i]}")")
            done
            continue
        fi

        # Data row -> one record.
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.time ${timeval}"$'\n'
        local i ci=0
        for ((i=offset; i<${#toks[@]}; i++)); do
            local col="${cols[$ci]:-col${ci}}"
            result+="entry${entry}.${col} ${toks[$i]}"$'\n'
            ci=$((ci + 1))
        done
    done <<< "$text"

    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

# Sanitise a header token to a field name of letters/digits/underscore only.
# %usr -> pct_usr ; kB_read/s -> kB_read_s ; anything else non-word -> _.
_strat_sysstat_sanitize () {
    local col="$1"
    col="${col//%/pct_}"      # percent sign -> pct_
    col="${col//\//_}"        # slash -> underscore
    col="${col//[^A-Za-z0-9_]/_}"  # any remaining non-word char -> underscore
    echo "$col"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: systemctl-status
## Description: Extract service information from systemctl status output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 19
## Technique: kv_colon
## Sample: samples/systemctl-status/sample1.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # systemctl status output contains "Loaded:" and "Active:" lines
    local has_loaded=0
    local has_active=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        local trimmed="$line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done
        [[ "$trimmed" == "Loaded:"* ]] && has_loaded=1
        [[ "$trimmed" == "Active:"* ]] && has_active=1
        if [[ $has_loaded -eq 1 && $has_active -eq 1 ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""

    # Extract the unit name from the first line (bullet line)
    local unit_name=""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local trimmed="$line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done
        # First line is typically "Aje2978fAj service-name.service - Description"
        if [[ "$trimmed" == *".service"* || "$trimmed" == *".socket"* || "$trimmed" == *".timer"* ]]; then
            # Remove bullet character prefix
            trimmed="${trimmed#*  }"
            while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done
            # Get unit name before " - "
            if [[ "$trimmed" == *" - "* ]]; then
                unit_name="${trimmed%% - *}"
                local desc="${trimmed#* - }"
                result+="unit ${unit_name}"$'\n'
                result+="description ${desc}"$'\n'
            else
                unit_name="$trimmed"
                result+="unit ${unit_name}"$'\n'
            fi
            break
        fi
        break
    done <<< "$text"

    # Extract key: value fields
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        local trimmed="$line"
        while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* ]]; do trimmed="${trimmed# }"; done

        case "$trimmed" in
            "Loaded: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#Loaded: }"
                result+="loaded ${val}"$'\n'
                ;;
            "Active: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#Active: }"
                # Extract the state keyword (active, inactive, failed, etc.)
                local state="${val%% *}"
                result+="active ${state}"$'\n'
                # Extract since timestamp if present
                if [[ "$val" == *"since "* ]]; then
                    local since="${val#*since }"
                    since="${since%;*}"
                    result+="since ${since}"$'\n'
                fi
                ;;
            "Main PID: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#Main PID: }"
                local pid="${val%% *}"
                result+="main_pid ${pid}"$'\n'
                ;;
            "Tasks: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#Tasks: }"
                local tasks="${val%% *}"
                result+="tasks ${tasks}"$'\n'
                ;;
            "Memory: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#Memory: }"
                result+="memory ${val}"$'\n'
                ;;
            "CPU: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#CPU: }"
                result+="cpu ${val}"$'\n'
                ;;
            "CGroup: "*)
                local val="${trimmed#CGroup: }"
                result+="cgroup ${val}"$'\n'
                ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$text"

    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: systemd-analyze-critical-chain
## Description: Extract the boot critical chain from `systemd-analyze critical-chain`
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/systemd-analyze-critical-chain/basic.txt

# `systemd-analyze critical-chain` prints a preamble, then the boot critical
# chain as a tree: one unit per line (Aje29494e29480Ajunit @activation +duration), indented
# with box-drawing connectors. Each unit becomes a record: c1 = unit name,
# c2 = timing (the @activation and optional +duration, spaces -> _).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: units with an "@time" activation stamp (e.g. ".target @14s").
    [[ "$text" == *".target @"* || "$text" == *".service @"* || "$text" == *".socket @"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line s
    local re='^([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+(@[0-9].*)$'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        s="$line"
        # Strip box-drawing glyphs: Aje29482Aj Aje2949cAj Aje29494Aj Aje29480Aj
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x82'/}"
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x9c'/}"
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x94'/}"
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x80'/}"
        # Trim leading whitespace.
        while [[ "$s" == " "* || "$s" == $'\t'* ]]; do s="${s#[$' \t']}"; done
        # Only unit lines match "<unit> @<time>..."; skips preamble prose.
        [[ "$s" =~ $re ]] || continue
        local unit="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        local timing="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${unit}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.B ${timing}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: systemd-cgls
## Description: Extract control-group nodes from `systemd-cgls` tree output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/systemd-cgls/basic.txt

# `systemd-cgls` prints a control-group hierarchy: a "Control group /:" header
# followed by one node per line, indented with box-drawing connectors
# (Aje29482Aj Aje2949ce29480Aj Aje29494e29480Aj Aje29480Aj). Each node line becomes a record whose single field is the line
# with the tree glyphs and leading indentation stripped (spaces -> _).

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: the "Control group" header plus cgroup slice/scope nodes.
    [[ "$text" == *"Control group"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *".slice"* || "$text" == *".scope"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line s
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Skip the "Control group /:" header (root description line).
        [[ "$line" == "Control group"* ]] && continue
        s="$line"
        # Strip box-drawing glyphs: Aje29482Aj Aje2949cAj Aje29494Aj Aje29480Aj
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x82'/}"
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x9c'/}"
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x94'/}"
        s="${s//$'\xe2\x94\x80'/}"
        # Trim leading whitespace left behind by the connectors.
        while [[ "$s" == " "* || "$s" == $'\t'* ]]; do s="${s#[$' \t']}"; done
        [[ -z "$s" ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.A ${s}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: systemd-tmpfiles-cat-config
## Description: Parse `systemd-tmpfiles --cat-config` lines (type path mode user group age arg)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/systemd-tmpfiles-cat-config/basic.txt

# `systemd-tmpfiles --cat-config` concatenates tmpfiles.d fragments. Comment
# lines (starting with '#', e.g. "# /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/systemd.conf") and blank
# lines separate the fragments; each real line is a directive:
#   type path mode user group age argument
# One record per directive.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"tmpfiles.d"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
        {
            if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next
            if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*#/) next
            if (NF < 2) next
            type=$1; path=$2
            mode=(NF>=3?$3:"-"); user=(NF>=4?$4:"-")
            group=(NF>=5?$5:"-"); age=(NF>=6?$6:"-")
            arg=""
            for(i=7;i<=NF;i++) arg=arg (i>7?"_":"") $i
            e++
            print "entry" e ".type " type
            print "entry" e ".path " path
            print "entry" e ".mode " mode
            print "entry" e ".user " user
            print "entry" e ".group " group
            print "entry" e ".age " age
            print "entry" e ".arg " (arg==""?"-":arg)
        }
        END{ if(e>0) print "total_entries " e }
    '
}

===FILE: extract/strategies/system/top-batch.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=f9de968d23f609e1a2a8e3b3c1bd5c62cce63a58eaf7c56a02ab72f47c9bfea7===
#!/bin/bash
## Name: top-batch
## Description: Extract process rows from `top -b -n1` (batch mode) output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 9
## Sample: samples/top-batch/basic.txt

# `top -b -n1` prints a summary block (top/Tasks/%Cpu/Mem/Swap lines), a blank
# line, then a process table:
#     PID USER   PR  NI  VIRT  RES  SHR S %CPU %MEM  TIME+ COMMAND
#    1843 mysql  20   0 ...  S  24.3  8.1 412:07.44 mysqld
# Signature: the "top - HH:MM:SS up" header + "Tasks:" + "%Cpu". Emit ONE record
# per process row; skip the summary block and the column header.

_top_batch_sanitize () {
    local v="$1"
    v="${v//$'\t'/_}"
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"top - "* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"Tasks:"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"%Cpu"* ]]   || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line in_table=0 i
    local -a t=()
    local -a fields=(pid user pr ni virt res shr s cpu mem time command)
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "${line//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        read -ra t <<< "$line"
        if [[ "${t[0]}" == "PID" ]]; then         # process-table header
            in_table=1
            continue
        fi
        [[ $in_table -eq 1 ]] || continue         # still in summary block
        [[ ${#t[@]} -eq ${#fields[@]} ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        for ((i=0; i<${#fields[@]}; i++)); do
            result+="entry${entry}.${fields[$i]} $(_top_batch_sanitize "${t[$i]}")"$'\n'
        done
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
===END===

#!/bin/bash
## Name: ulimit
## Description: Extract resource limits from ulimit -a output
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 20
## Sample: samples/ulimit/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: a description followed by a "(unit, -X)" or "(-X)" group and a value,
    # e.g. "core file size          (blocks, -c) 0" or "open files (-n) 1024".
    local re='\(([a-zA-Z0-9, ]*)-[a-zA-Z]\) +[^ ]+$'
    local hits=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        if [[ "$line" =~ $re ]]; then
            hits=$((hits + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $hits -ge 2 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=88
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result=""
    local entry=0
    local re='^(.*[^ ]) +\(([a-zA-Z0-9, ]*)-([a-zA-Z])\) +([^ ]+)$'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
        # Match: <description> (<unit>, -X) <value>   OR   <description> (-X) <value>
        if [[ "$line" =~ $re ]]; then
            local desc="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            local flag="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
            local value="${BASH_REMATCH[4]}"
            # Normalize description -> resource (spaces to underscores, trim)
            desc="${desc#"${desc%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
            desc="${desc%"${desc##*[![:space:]]}"}"
            local resource="${desc}"
            entry=$((entry + 1))
            result+="entry${entry}.resource ${resource}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.flag ${flag}"$'\n'
            result+="entry${entry}.value ${value}"$'\n'
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: user-groups
## Description: `groups` output Aje28094Aj "user : group1 group2 Aje280a6Aj" Aje28692Aj one row per membership
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 30
## Sample: samples/user-groups/basic.txt

# `groups` (and `groups <user>`) prints a single line: a user, " : ", then a
# space-separated list of the user's groups. Tidied to one row per membership
# with (user, group) columns. The distinctive " : " (space-colon-space) after a
# single token, on a lone line, keys the detection.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0

    local nonblank=0 first="" _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && continue
        nonblank=$((nonblank + 1))
        [[ -z "$first" ]] && first="$_l"
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $nonblank -eq 1 ]] || return 1
    [[ "$first" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+[[:space:]]+:[[:space:]]+[a-zA-Z] ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=85
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local first="" _l
    while IFS= read -r _l; do
        [[ -z "${_l//[[:space:]]/}" ]] && { continue; }
        first="$_l"; break
    done <<< "$text"

    local toks; toks=(); read -ra toks <<< "$first"
    local user="${toks[0]}"
    local result="" entry=0 i seen_sep=0
    for ((i = 1; i < ${#toks[@]}; i++)); do
        if [[ "${toks[$i]}" == ":" && $seen_sep -eq 0 ]]; then seen_sep=1; continue; fi
        [[ $seen_sep -eq 0 ]] && continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.user ${user}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.group ${toks[$i]}"$'\n'
    done
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: vagrant-global-status
## Description: Extract machines from `vagrant global-status` output (skips header/rule/footer)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 26
## Sample: samples/vagrant-global-status/basic.txt

# `vagrant global-status` prints a header ("id name provider state directory"), a
# dashed rule line, one row per known machine, then a trailing explanatory
# paragraph. The header, rule, and footer are noise; each machine row (whose last
# field is its directory path) becomes a record.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    command -v _is_json >/dev/null 2>&1 && _is_json "$text" && return 1
    # Distinctive: the vagrant header columns plus a dashed rule line.
    local line has_header=0 has_rule=0 rows=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$line" == *id*name*provider*state*directory* ]]; then
            has_header=1
            continue
        fi
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^-+[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
            has_rule=1
            continue
        fi
        # A machine row: 5 whitespace fields whose last is an absolute path.
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+/[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then
            rows=$((rows + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$text"
    if [[ $has_header -eq 1 && $has_rule -eq 1 && $rows -ge 1 ]]; then
        _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    local result="" entry=0 line id name provider state directory
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" =~ ^[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+/[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]*$ ]] || continue
        read -r id name provider state directory _ <<< "$line"
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        result+="entry${entry}.id ${id}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.name ${name}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.provider ${provider}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.state ${state}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.directory ${directory}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}

#!/bin/bash
## Name: zypper-packages
## Description: Parse `zypper packages` box table (S | Repository | Name | Version | Arch)
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 22
## Sample: samples/zypper-packages/basic.txt

# `zypper packages` prints a pipe-delimited box table:
#   S | Repository | Name | Version | Arch
#   --+------------+------+---------+-----
#   i | openSUSE-Oss | bash | 5.2.15-1.1 | x86_64
# preceded by "Loading repository data..." style status lines. One record per
# package row; status lines, the header and the "--+--" separator are skipped.

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == *"| Repository"* ]] || return 1
    [[ "$text" == *"| Arch"* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=86
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk -F'|' '
        function trim(s){ gsub(/^[ \t]+/,"",s); gsub(/[ \t]+$/,"",s); gsub(/[ \t]+/,"_",s); return s }
        {
            if ($0 !~ /\|/) next                       # only table rows
            if ($0 ~ /Repository/) next                # header
            if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*-.*\+/) next              # --+-- separator
            if (NF < 5) next
            s=trim($1); repo=trim($2); name=trim($3); ver=trim($4); arch=trim($5)
            e++
            print "entry" e ".s " (s==""?"-":s)
            print "entry" e ".repository " repo
            print "entry" e ".name " name
            print "entry" e ".version " ver
            print "entry" e ".arch " arch
        }
        END{ if(e>0) print "total_entries " e }
    '
}

===META: mode=755 sha256=bdce3f6cc6957535b632c5ed85662501136d96de7755c61fdd0a8ed3a21084ee===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Benchmark: envoy-extract memory profile on large inputs (ENV-042)
##
## Generates a synthetic large input file and times envoy-extract + captures
## peak RSS if /usr/bin/time -v is available. Focuses on streaming mode vs
## batch mode (streaming should use less memory).
##
## Usage:
##   bash bench_memory.sh                 # default: 100MB log
##   bash bench_memory.sh --size 10MB     # smaller for quick check
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
MFE_SCRIPT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/envoy-extract"

SIZE="100MB"
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --size) SIZE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

# Convert size spec to bytes (e.g., 100MB -> 104857600)
size_to_bytes () {
    local spec="$1"
    # Strip the unit part (handle MB / GB / KB)
    local num="${spec%%[GgMmKk]*}"
    local unit
    unit=$(printf '%s' "$spec" | sed 's/^[0-9]*//')
    case "${unit^^}" in
        GB|G)   echo "$(( num * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 ))" ;;
        MB|M)   echo "$(( num * 1024 * 1024 ))" ;;
        KB|K)   echo "$(( num * 1024 ))" ;;
        "")     echo "$num" ;;
        *)      echo "$num" ;;
    esac
}

BYTES=$(size_to_bytes "$SIZE")

echo "Memory benchmark (ENV-042)"
echo "=========================="
echo "Synthetic size: $SIZE ($BYTES bytes)"
echo ""

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t envextract_bench.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Generate a log file: repeated apache-like access lines
# Each line is ~120 bytes; we loop until we hit target bytes.
echo "Generating synthetic input..."
LINE='192.168.1.100 - - [17/Apr/2026:10:22:01 +0000] "GET /api/v1/users/12345 HTTP/1.1" 200 1234 "-" "Mozilla/5.0" 0.042'
python3 -c "
import sys
line = '''$LINE
'''
line_bytes = line.encode('utf-8')
target = $BYTES
n = target // len(line_bytes) + 1
with open('$TMP/big.log', 'wb') as f:
    for _ in range(n):
        f.write(line_bytes)
" || { echo "generation failed"; exit 1; }

actual=$(wc -c <"$TMP/big.log")
echo "  actual bytes: $actual"

# Force input-size ceiling high enough for batch mode
echo ""
echo "Measuring..."
TIMEFORMAT='%R'

# Streaming mode
stream_time=""
stream_rss=""
if command -v /usr/bin/time >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    /usr/bin/time -v -o "$TMP/stream.time" bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" stream --strategy apache-access < "$TMP/big.log" > /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
    stream_time=$(awk -F': ' '/Elapsed \(wall clock\)/ {print $2}' "$TMP/stream.time")
    stream_rss=$(awk -F': ' '/Maximum resident set size/ {print $2}' "$TMP/stream.time")
else
    stream_time=$({ time bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" stream --strategy apache-access < "$TMP/big.log" > /dev/null 2>&1 ; } 2>&1)
fi

echo "  stream mode time: ${stream_time}"
[[ -n "$stream_rss" ]] && echo "  stream mode RSS:  ${stream_rss} KB"

# Regression gate (conservative Aje28094Aj tune after baseline)
BENCH_MAX_RSS_MB="${BENCH_MAX_RSS_MB:-500}"
if [[ -n "$stream_rss" ]]; then
    local_rss_mb=$((stream_rss / 1024))
    if [[ "$local_rss_mb" -gt "$BENCH_MAX_RSS_MB" ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo "FAIL: stream peak RSS ${local_rss_mb}MB exceeds ${BENCH_MAX_RSS_MB}MB gate"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

echo ""
echo "OK"
exit 0
===END===
===FILE: extract/tests/bench_strategy_load.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=f00f3a83821dc28eb1315dc1d9b7c660a20bc3b41e4deb10f4f6a74b460d8279===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Benchmark: strategy-load time for envoy-extract (ENV-017)
##
## Measures cold-start time to discover and read metadata for all shipped
## strategies. Runs several iterations and reports min, median, max.
##
## Usage: bash bench_strategy_load.sh [ITERATIONS]
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
MFE_SCRIPT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/envoy-extract"
ITERATIONS="${1:-10}"

if [[ ! -x "$MFE_SCRIPT" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: envoy-extract not found at $MFE_SCRIPT" >&2
    exit 2
fi

echo "Strategy-load benchmark (ENV-017)"
echo "================================="
echo "Iterations: $ITERATIONS"
echo ""

TIMEFORMAT='%R'
samples=()

for i in $(seq 1 "$ITERATIONS"); do
    t=$({ time bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" list > /dev/null 2>&1 ; } 2>&1)
    samples+=("$t")
    printf "  run %2d: %s s\n" "$i" "$t"
done

# Compute min / median / max via sort
sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${samples[@]}" | sort -n)
min=$(echo "$sorted" | head -1)
max=$(echo "$sorted" | tail -1)
mid_idx=$((ITERATIONS / 2 + 1))
median=$(echo "$sorted" | sed -n "${mid_idx}p")

# Strategy count for context
strategy_count=$(bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" list 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^  ')

echo ""
echo "Results"
echo "-------"
echo "  strategies: $strategy_count"
echo "  min:        $min s"
echo "  median:     $median s"
echo "  max:        $max s"

# Optional regression gate: fail if max exceeds 1s cold.
REGRESSION_MAX="${BENCH_MAX:-1.000}"
over=$(awk -v m="$max" -v r="$REGRESSION_MAX" 'BEGIN{exit !(m>r)}' && echo 1 || echo 0)
if [[ "$over" -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo ""
    echo "FAIL: max time $max s exceeded ${REGRESSION_MAX}s threshold"
    exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "OK: max time $max s under ${REGRESSION_MAX}s threshold"
exit 0
===END===

# Handoff Aje28094Aj EnvoyExtract/tests/golden

## Status: Complete (124 golden output files)

Golden (expected) output files for snapshot regression tests in `test_snapshot_regression.sh`. Each file contains the expected field extraction output for a representative strategy/sample pair. If refactoring changes output, these files are updated to track the new canonical output.

## Contents

One `.txt` file per strategy (124 files), named `<strategy-name>.txt`. Each contains the expected plain-text extraction output when running that strategy against its `basic.*` sample file.

## Usage

The snapshot regression test (`test_snapshot_regression.sh`) runs `envoy-extract --strategy <name> samples/<name>/basic.*` and diffs against the corresponding golden file. Failures indicate unexpected output changes.

To update a golden file after an intentional change:
```bash
bash EnvoyExtract/envoy-extract --strategy <name> samples/<name>/basic.* > tests/golden/<name>.txt
```

## Next Steps

Golden files are updated automatically when strategies are intentionally changed. No pending work.

===FILE: extract/tests/helpers.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=72af492a06ac3cdef8947de45d06603263fefcda64ea45947a1881eb13538acf===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Test Helpers for Envoy:Explore
##
## Provides assertion utilities for testing envoy-extract strategies and engine.
################################################################################

# Absolute path to the mfe script under test
MFE_SCRIPT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/envoy-extract"
SAMPLES_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/samples"
STRATEGIES_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/strategies"

# Test counters
TESTS_RUN=0
TESTS_PASSED=0
TESTS_FAILED=0
FAILED_NAMES=()

# Colors (if terminal supports them)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    RED='\033[0;31m'
    YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
    NC='\033[0m'
else
    GREEN='' RED='' YELLOW='' NC=''
fi

################################################################################
## Assertion functions
##

assert_eq () {
    local expected="$1"
    local actual="$2"
    local msg="${3:-values should be equal}"
    if [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    expected: '$expected'"
        echo "    actual:   '$actual'"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_contains () {
    local haystack="$1"
    local needle="$2"
    local msg="${3:-output should contain string}"
    if [[ "$haystack" == *"$needle"* ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    looking for: '$needle'"
        echo "    in:          '$haystack'"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_not_contains () {
    local haystack="$1"
    local needle="$2"
    local msg="${3:-output should not contain string}"
    if [[ "$haystack" != *"$needle"* ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    should not find: '$needle'"
        echo "    in:              '$haystack'"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_exit_zero () {
    local code="$1"
    local msg="${2:-command should succeed (exit 0)}"
    if [[ "$code" -eq 0 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    exit code: $code"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_exit_nonzero () {
    local code="$1"
    local msg="${2:-command should fail (exit non-zero)}"
    if [[ "$code" -ne 0 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    exit code: $code (expected non-zero)"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_line_count () {
    local text="$1"
    local expected="$2"
    local msg="${3:-line count should match}"
    local actual
    actual=$(echo "$text" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$actual" -eq "$expected" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    expected lines: $expected"
        echo "    actual lines:   $actual"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_match () {
    local actual="$1"
    local pattern="$2"
    local msg="${3:-output should match regex}"
    if [[ "$actual" =~ $pattern ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    pattern: '$pattern'"
        echo "    actual:  '$actual'"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_line_count_ge () {
    local text="$1"
    local min="$2"
    local msg="${3:-line count should be >= $min}"
    local actual
    actual=$(echo "$text" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$actual" -ge "$min" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    minimum expected: $min"
        echo "    actual lines:     $actual"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_line_count_le () {
    local text="$1"
    local max="$2"
    local msg="${3:-line count should be <= $max}"
    local actual
    actual=$(echo "$text" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$actual" -le "$max" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    maximum expected: $max"
        echo "    actual lines:     $actual"
        return 1
    fi
}

assert_json_valid () {
    local text="$1"
    local msg="${2:-output should be valid JSON}"
    # Use jq for real validation if available
    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if echo "$text" | jq . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            return 0
        fi
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    jq validation failed"
        echo "    text: '${text:0:80}'"
        return 1
    fi
    # Fallback: structural bracket check (when jq is not installed)
    local trimmed="$text"
    while [[ "$trimmed" == " "* || "$trimmed" == $'\n'* || "$trimmed" == $'\t'* ]]; do
        trimmed="${trimmed#[  	]}"
    done
    while [[ "$trimmed" == *" " || "$trimmed" == *$'\n' || "$trimmed" == *$'\t' ]]; do
        trimmed="${trimmed%[  	]}"
    done
    case "$trimmed" in
        '{'*'}'|'['*']') return 0 ;;
    esac
    printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
    echo "    text: '${text:0:80}'"
    return 1
}

assert_output_empty () {
    local text="$1"
    local msg="${2:-output should be empty}"
    local trimmed="$text"
    # Strip all whitespace
    trimmed="${trimmed// /}"
    trimmed="${trimmed//$'\n'/}"
    trimmed="${trimmed//$'\t'/}"
    if [[ -z "$trimmed" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}ASSERT FAILED${NC}: $msg"
        echo "    output: '${text:0:80}'"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## run_mfe
##
## Run envoy-extract with given arguments.
##
run_mfe () {
    bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" "$@"
}

################################################################################
## run_test
##
## Runs a test function and tracks results.
## Usage: run_test "test description" test_function_name
##
run_test () {
    local description="$1"
    local func="$2"
    TESTS_RUN=$((TESTS_RUN + 1))

    # `|| result=$?` instead of bare `( ... ); result=$?` so a
    # failing test subshell can't trip the caller's `set -e` before
    # we record the result.
    local result=0
    ( set -e; "$func" ) || result=$?

    if [[ $result -eq 0 ]]; then
        TESTS_PASSED=$((TESTS_PASSED + 1))
        printf '%b\n' "  ${GREEN}PASS${NC}: $description"
    else
        TESTS_FAILED=$((TESTS_FAILED + 1))
        FAILED_NAMES+=("$description")
        printf '%b\n' "  ${RED}FAIL${NC}: $description"
    fi
}

################################################################################
## print_summary
##
## Prints test run summary and exits with appropriate code.
##
print_summary () {
    echo ""
    echo "========================================"
    echo "Results: $TESTS_PASSED/$TESTS_RUN passed, $TESTS_FAILED failed"
    if [[ $TESTS_FAILED -gt 0 ]]; then
        printf '%b\n' "${RED}Failed tests:${NC}"
        for name in "${FAILED_NAMES[@]}"; do
            echo "  - $name"
        done
        echo "========================================"
        return 1
    else
        printf '%b\n' "${GREEN}All tests passed.${NC}"
        echo "========================================"
        return 0
    fi
}

===FILE: extract/tests/run_tests.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=18c12880953989dfcbcbffd744580fc9cd97f455cb5780fa1e9e15d50051966d===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Envoy:Explore Test Runner
##
## Runs all test suites and reports combined results.
##
## Usage: bash run_tests.sh [OPTIONS]
##
## Options:
##   --filter PATTERN   Only run test files matching PATTERN
##   --timing           Show elapsed time per test file
##   --fail-fast        Stop on first test file failure
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
OVERALL_EXIT=0
FILES_RUN=0
FILES_FAILED=0
FAILED_FILES=()
opt_filter=""
opt_timing=0
opt_fail_fast=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --filter)   opt_filter="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --timing)   opt_timing=1; shift ;;
        --fail-fast) opt_fail_fast=1; shift ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

echo "========================================"
echo "Envoy:Explore Test Suite"
echo "========================================"

# Auto-discover all test files
for test_file in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/test_*.sh; do
    [[ -f "$test_file" ]] || continue

    # Apply filter if set
    if [[ -n "$opt_filter" ]]; then
        case "$test_file" in
            *"$opt_filter"*) ;;
            *) continue ;;
        esac
    fi

    FILES_RUN=$((FILES_RUN + 1))

    if [[ $opt_timing -eq 1 ]]; then
        _start=$SECONDS
    fi

    bash "$test_file"
    _rc=$?

    if [[ $opt_timing -eq 1 ]]; then
        _elapsed=$((SECONDS - _start))
        echo "  [timing] $(basename "$test_file"): ${_elapsed}s"
    fi

    if [[ $_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
        OVERALL_EXIT=1
        FILES_FAILED=$((FILES_FAILED + 1))
        FAILED_FILES+=("$(basename "$test_file")")
        if [[ $opt_fail_fast -eq 1 ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "FAIL-FAST: Stopping after $(basename "$test_file")"
            break
        fi
    fi
done

# Run golden output verification (if no filter is set, or filter matches)
if [[ -z "$opt_filter" || "verify_strategy_outputs" == *"$opt_filter"* ]]; then
    FILES_RUN=$((FILES_RUN + 1))
    bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/verify_strategy_outputs.sh" --check
    if [[ $? -ne 0 ]]; then
        OVERALL_EXIT=1
        FILES_FAILED=$((FILES_FAILED + 1))
        FAILED_FILES+=("verify_strategy_outputs.sh")
    fi
fi

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Overall: $((FILES_RUN - FILES_FAILED))/$FILES_RUN test files passed"
if [[ $FILES_FAILED -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "Failed files:"
    for f in "${FAILED_FILES[@]}"; do
        echo "  - $f"
    done
    echo "========================================"
    echo "Some test suites had failures."
else
    echo "========================================"
    echo "All test suites passed."
fi

exit $OVERALL_EXIT
===END===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Batch Mode Tests
##
## Tests for --batch flag: process multiple files in one envoy-extract invocation,
## outputting one JSON Lines record per file.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

MFE_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Batch Mode Tests"
echo "========================================"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic: single file produces a JSON Lines record with correct structure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_single_file () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"name": "project", "version": "1.0"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(echo "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" '"file"' "batch: output should contain file key"
    assert_contains "$output" '"fields"' "batch: output should contain fields key"
    assert_contains "$output" '"name"' "batch: output should contain extracted field name"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two files: produces two JSON Lines records
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_two_files () {
    local tmp1 tmp2 output line_count
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp2=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"host": "server1"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    printf '{"host": "server2"}\n' > "$tmp2"
    output=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$tmp1" "$tmp2" | run_mfe --batch)
    rm -f "$tmp1" "$tmp2"
    assert_line_count "$output" 2 "batch: two input files should produce two output records"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File path is echoed correctly in the output record
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_file_path_in_output () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"key": "val"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(echo "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "$tmpfile" "batch: output should include the input file path"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty fields: file with no extractable content yields {"file":..., "fields":{}}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_empty_fields () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'no extractable content here\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(echo "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Record should still be emitted (with empty fields)
    assert_contains "$output" '"file"' "batch: record emitted even for no-field input"
    assert_contains "$output" '"fields": {}' "batch: empty fields yields {}"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Missing file: warning to stderr, no output record for that file
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_missing_file () {
    local output stderr_out
    output=$(echo "/nonexistent/path/file.json" | run_mfe --batch 2>${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/batch_stderr_test)
    stderr_out=$(cat ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/batch_stderr_test)
    rm -f ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/batch_stderr_test
    assert_not_contains "$output" '"file"' "batch: missing file should not produce output record"
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "not found" "batch: missing file should warn on stderr"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty stdin: warning, no output
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_empty_stdin () {
    local output stderr_out
    output=$(echo "" | run_mfe --batch 2>${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/batch_empty_stderr)
    stderr_out=$(cat ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/batch_empty_stderr)
    rm -f ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/batch_empty_stderr
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "no files processed" "batch: empty stdin should warn"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Works with --strategy to limit extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_with_strategy () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"name": "alpha", "count": 5}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(echo "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch --strategy json)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" '"name"' "batch --strategy: should extract name field"
    assert_contains "$output" '"count"' "batch --strategy: should extract count field"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Works with --rename to rename fields in output
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_with_rename () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"name": "alpha"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(echo "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch --rename "name=project_name")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "project_name" "batch --rename: field should be renamed"
    assert_not_contains "$output" '"name"' "batch --rename: original name should not appear"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Works with --no-dedup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_with_no_dedup () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"key": "val1"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(echo "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch --no-dedup)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" '"file"' "batch --no-dedup: should still produce output"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Blank lines in stdin are ignored
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_blank_lines_ignored () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"host": "server"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(printf '\n%s\n\n' "$tmpfile" | run_mfe --batch)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Should produce exactly one record
    assert_line_count "$output" 1 "batch: blank lines in stdin should be skipped"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conflict: --batch and --stream cannot be used together
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_conflict_stream () {
    local exit_code stderr_out
    stderr_out=$(echo "" | run_mfe --batch --stream --strategy colons 2>&1 >/dev/null || true)
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "cannot be used together" "batch+stream: should error with conflict message"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conflict: --batch and --chain cannot be used together
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_conflict_chain () {
    local stderr_out
    stderr_out=$(echo "" | run_mfe --batch --chain 'colons|json' 2>&1 >/dev/null || true)
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "cannot be used together" "batch+chain: should error with conflict message"
}

# Conflict: --batch and --replay cannot be used together
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_conflict_replay () {
    local stderr_out
    stderr_out=$(echo "" | run_mfe --batch --replay 'json@1.0' 2>&1 >/dev/null || true)
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "cannot be used together" "batch+replay: should error with conflict message"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_conflict_interactive () {
    local stderr_out
    stderr_out=$(echo "" | run_mfe --batch --interactive 2>&1 >/dev/null || true)
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "cannot be used together" "batch+interactive: should error with conflict message"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conflict: --batch with a FILE argument should error
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_conflict_file_argument () {
    local tmpfile stderr_out
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"key": "val"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    stderr_out=$(echo "" | run_mfe --batch "$tmpfile" 2>&1 >/dev/null || true)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "do not specify a FILE" "batch+file: should error when FILE arg given"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output goes to --output file
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_output_to_file () {
    local tmpfile outfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    outfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"name": "test"}\n' > "$tmpfile"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_mixed_content () {

}

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Batch Summary Tests
##
## Tests for --batch-summary flag: after batch processing, emit a summary JSON
## object with totals, strategy usage, common fields, and file lists.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

MFE_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Batch Summary Tests"
echo "========================================"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic: --batch-summary emits summary object after file records
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_basic () {
    local tmp1 tmp2 output last_line
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp2=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"host": "server1", "port": "80"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    printf '{"host": "server2", "version": "2.0"}\n' > "$tmp2"
    output=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$tmp1" "$tmp2" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmp1" "$tmp2"
    # Should have 3 lines: 2 file records + 1 summary
    assert_line_count "$output" 3 "batch-summary: should produce 3 output lines (2 files + summary)"
    last_line=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    assert_contains "$last_line" '"_summary": true' "batch-summary: last line should have _summary marker"
    assert_contains "$last_line" '"total_files": 2' "batch-summary: total_files should be 2"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verify total_files count with three files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_total_files () {
    local tmp1 tmp2 tmp3 output summary
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp2=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp3=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"a": "1"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    printf '{"b": "2"}\n' > "$tmp2"
    printf '{"c": "3"}\n' > "$tmp3"
    output=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$tmp1" "$tmp2" "$tmp3" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmp1" "$tmp2" "$tmp3"
    summary=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    assert_contains "$summary" '"total_files": 3' "batch-summary: total_files should be 3"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"total_fields": 3' "batch-summary: total_fields should be 3"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verify common_fields detection: fields present in all files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_common_fields () {
    local tmp1 tmp2 output summary
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp2=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"name": "alpha", "version": "1.0", "author": "test"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    printf '{"name": "beta", "version": "2.0", "license": "MIT"}\n' > "$tmp2"
    output=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$tmp1" "$tmp2" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmp1" "$tmp2"
    summary=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    # "name" and "version" are common to both files
    assert_contains "$summary" '"name"' "batch-summary: common_fields should include name"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"version"' "batch-summary: common_fields should include version"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error when --batch-summary used without --batch
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_requires_batch () {
    local tmp1 stderr_out exit_code
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"key": "val"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    stderr_out=$(run_mfe --batch-summary "$tmp1" 2>&1 >/dev/null || true)
    rm -f "$tmp1"
    assert_contains "$stderr_out" "requires --batch" "batch-summary: should error without --batch"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty input: summary with zero totals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_empty_input () {
    local output summary
    output=$(echo "" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    summary=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    assert_contains "$summary" '"_summary": true' "batch-summary: empty input should still emit summary"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"total_files": 0' "batch-summary: empty input total_files should be 0"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"total_fields": 0' "batch-summary: empty input total_fields should be 0"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"common_fields": []' "batch-summary: empty input common_fields should be empty"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"files_processed": []' "batch-summary: empty input files_processed should be empty"
    assert_contains "$summary" '"files_failed": []' "batch-summary: empty input files_failed should be empty"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Files with different strategies: strategies_used tracks counts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_strategies_used () {
    local tmp_json tmp_ini output summary
    tmp_json=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp_ini=$(mktemp --suffix=.ini)
    printf '{"host": "server1"}\n' > "$tmp_json"
    printf '[section]\nkey = value\n' > "$tmp_ini"
    output=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$tmp_json" "$tmp_ini" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmp_json" "$tmp_ini"
    summary=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    assert_contains "$summary" '"strategies_used":' "batch-summary: should contain strategies_used"
    # json strategy should appear (the .json file definitely triggers json strategy)
    assert_contains "$summary" '"json":' "batch-summary: json strategy should appear in strategies_used"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# files_failed tracks missing files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_files_failed () {
    local tmp1 output summary
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"key": "val"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    output=$(printf '%s\n/nonexistent/missing.json\n' "$tmp1" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmp1"
    summary=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    assert_contains "$summary" '"total_files": 1' "batch-summary: total_files should be 1 (only successful)"
    assert_contains "$summary" '/nonexistent/missing.json' "batch-summary: files_failed should contain missing file"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# files_processed lists all successfully processed files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_batch_summary_files_processed () {
    local tmp1 tmp2 output summary
    tmp1=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    tmp2=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)
    printf '{"a": "1"}\n' > "$tmp1"
    printf '{"b": "2"}\n' > "$tmp2"
    output=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$tmp1" "$tmp2" | run_mfe batch --batch-summary 2>/dev/null)
    summary=$(echo "$output" | tail -1)
    assert_contains "$summary" "$tmp1" "batch-summary: files_processed should include first file"
    assert_contains "$summary" "$tmp2" "batch-summary: files_processed should include second file"
    rm -f "$tmp1" "$tmp2"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run all tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

run_test "batch-summary: basic output with two files"                  test_batch_summary_basic
run_test "batch-summary: total_files count with three files"           test_batch_summary_total_files
run_test "batch-summary: common_fields detects shared fields"          test_batch_summary_common_fields
run_test "batch-summary: errors without --batch"                       test_batch_summary_requires_batch
run_test "batch-summary: empty input produces zero-count summary"      test_batch_summary_empty_input
run_test "batch-summary: strategies_used tracks different strategies"   test_batch_summary_strategies_used
run_test "batch-summary: files_failed tracks missing files"            test_batch_summary_files_failed
run_test "batch-summary: files_processed lists successful files"       test_batch_summary_files_processed

print_summary

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Chain Data Flow Verification Tests
##
## Verify that --chain actually transforms data between strategies,
## not just that it doesn't crash.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Chain Data Flow Tests"
echo "========================================"

# --- Test 1: colons|equals verifiable transform ---

test_chain_colons_to_equals () {
    # Stage 1 (colons): extracts "Format KEY=val1" and "Type NAME=val2"
    # Chain strips field names, passes "KEY=val1" and "NAME=val2" to stage 2
    # Stage 2 (equals): re-extracts as "KEY val1" and "NAME val2"
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Format: KEY=val1\nType: NAME=val2\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --chain 'colons|equals' -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "KEY val1" "chain should extract KEY from colons values via equals"
    assert_contains "$output" "NAME val2" "chain should extract NAME from colons values via equals"
    assert_contains "$output" "STRAT-chain" "output should have STRAT-chain label"
}

# --- Test 2: chain + --rename applied to final output ---

test_chain_with_rename () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Host: localhost\nPort: 5432\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --chain 'colons' --rename 'Host=Server' -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "Server localhost" "rename should apply to chain output"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Host localhost" "original name should be replaced"
}

# --- Test 3: chain + --sort applied to final output ---

test_chain_with_sort () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Zebra: last\nAlpha: first\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --chain 'colons' --sort -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # After sort, Alpha should come before Zebra
    local alpha_pos zebra_pos
    alpha_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Alpha" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    zebra_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Zebra" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    assert_contains "$output" "Alpha first" "chain+sort should include Alpha"
    assert_contains "$output" "Zebra last" "chain+sort should include Zebra"
    if [[ -n "$alpha_pos" && -n "$zebra_pos" && "$alpha_pos" -lt "$zebra_pos" ]]; then
        assert_eq "ok" "ok" "Alpha should sort before Zebra in chain output"
    else
        assert_eq "Alpha<Zebra" "Alpha=$alpha_pos Zebra=$zebra_pos" "sort order incorrect"
    fi
}

# --- Test 4: chain + --aggregate on repeated values ---

test_chain_with_aggregate () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Score: 10\nScore: 20\nScore: 30\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --chain 'colons' --aggregate -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "Score_count 3" "chain+aggregate should compute count"
    assert_contains "$output" "Score_sum 60" "chain+aggregate should compute sum"
    assert_contains "$output" "Score_avg 20.00" "chain+aggregate should compute avg"
}

# --- Test 5: chain + --count on output ---

test_chain_with_count () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Host: localhost\nPort: 5432\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --chain 'colons' --count "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_eq "$output" "2" "chain+count should count 2 fields"
}

# --- Register all tests ---

run_test "chain: colons|equals data flow" test_chain_colons_to_equals
run_test "chain: --rename on chain output" test_chain_with_rename
run_test "chain: --sort on chain output" test_chain_with_sort
run_test "chain: --aggregate on chain output" test_chain_with_aggregate
run_test "chain: --count on chain output" test_chain_with_count

print_summary
===END===

################################################################################
## Fix #1: clean_text() cache works (no subshell)
##

test_clean_text_cache_works () {
    # Source the modules to get clean_text
    source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_log.sh"
    source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/_helpers.sh"
    _CLEAN_TEXT_CACHE=""
    _CLEAN_TEXT_DONE=0

    local input="Host: server1
Date: Mon 01 12:30:45 2024"

    # First call should compute and cache
    clean_text "$input"
    local result1="$_CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT"
    assert_eq "1" "$_CLEAN_TEXT_DONE" "cache flag should be set after first call"

    # Second call should use cache (verify _CLEAN_TEXT_DONE is still 1)
    clean_text "$input"
    local result2="$_CLEAN_TEXT_RESULT"
    assert_eq "$result1" "$result2" "cached result should match first result"
}

test_source_error_guard () {
    local tmpdir
    tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
    local strat_dir="$tmpdir/strategies"
    mkdir -p "$strat_dir"

    # Create a valid strategy
    cat > "$strat_dir/good.sh" << 'STRAT'
#!/bin/bash
## Name: good
## Description: A valid strategy
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 50
strategy_detect () { _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90; return 0; }
strategy_extract () { echo "key value"; }
STRAT

    # Create a broken strategy (syntax error)
    cat > "$strat_dir/broken.sh" << 'STRAT'
#!/bin/bash
## Name: broken
## Description: A broken strategy
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 10
strategy_detect () {
    this is not valid bash syntax }{}{
}
STRAT

    # Run mfe with the plugin dir -- should not crash
    local output rc=0
    output=$(echo "key: value" | bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" --plugin-dir "$strat_dir" -f plain 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
    # Should succeed (good strategy or built-in strategies should still work)
    # The broken strategy should be skipped, not crash the engine

    rm -rf "$tmpdir"

    # mfe should not have crashed (exit code 0 if fields extracted)
    assert_eq "0" "$rc" "mfe should not crash on broken strategy file"
}

run_test "source error guard: broken strategy skipped, not crashed" test_source_error_guard

test_xstrat_yaml_not_colons () {

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Advanced Deduplication Tests for Envoy:Explore (envoy-extract)
##
## Tests that deduplication works correctly when many strategies match the
## same input, and with large field counts.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Advanced Deduplication Tests"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## Input matching 5+ strategies produces deduplicated output
################################################################################

test_dedup_multi_strategy () {
    # This input has colons, equals, and env-var patterns Aje28094Aj multiple strategies
    # will match and extract overlapping fields.
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Host: localhost\nPort: 5432\nHost=localhost\nPort=5432\nDebug=true\nDB_HOST=localhost\nDB_PORT=5432\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # After dedup, each unique "fieldname value" pair should appear only once
    local host_count
    host_count=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'Host localhost' || true)
    assert_eq "1" "$host_count" "Host localhost should appear exactly once after dedup"
    local port_count
    port_count=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'Port 5432' || true)
    assert_eq "1" "$port_count" "Port 5432 should appear exactly once after dedup"
    # Debug should still appear (unique to equals)
    assert_contains "$output" "Debug true" "Debug (equals-only) should be present"
}

################################################################################
## Dedup count verification (known input -> known field count after dedup)
################################################################################

test_dedup_count () {
    # Create input with 5 unique fields, each duplicated across colons and equals
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\nCity: Boston\nRole: admin\nTeam: ops\n' > "$tmpfile"
    printf 'Name=Alice\nAge=30\nCity=Boston\nRole=admin\nTeam=ops\n' >> "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # After dedup, should have exactly 5 unique field/value pairs (not 10)
    local line_count
    line_count=$(echo "$output" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    # Each unique pair should only appear once
    local unique_count
    unique_count=$(echo "$output" | sed '/^$/d' | awk '{
        idx = index($0, "\t")
        if (idx > 0) print substr($0, idx + 1)
        else print
    }' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    assert_eq "$unique_count" "$line_count" "all lines should be unique after dedup (no duplicates remain)"
}

################################################################################
## Large dedup (100+ fields)
################################################################################

test_dedup_large () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Generate 120 colons fields
    local i
    for ((i=1; i<=120; i++)); do
        printf 'Field%03d: Value%03d\n' "$i" "$i" >> "$tmpfile"
    done
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s colons "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should handle 120+ fields without error"
    # Verify we extracted a large number of fields
    local line_count
    line_count=$(echo "$output" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    # Should have at least 100 fields extracted
    if [[ $line_count -ge 100 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  expected >= 100 fields, got $line_count"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Run all tests
################################################################################

run_test "dedup: multi-strategy overlap produces unique fields" test_dedup_multi_strategy
run_test "dedup: count verification (known input)" test_dedup_count
run_test "dedup: 120+ fields handled correctly" test_dedup_large

print_summary
===END===
