#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for ENV-182 Aje28094Aj EnvoyExtract dispatch / validate edge cases.
##
## Sub-bug 1 (envoy-extract:660-666):
##   Pre-fix: `text=$(head -c $((N+1)))` then `[[ ${#text} -gt N ]]`.
##   `$(...)` strips trailing newlines, so an input of exactly N+1
##   bytes ending in newline(s) shrank to Aje289a4Aj N bytes after capture
##   and slipped past the size cap. Real symptom: large
##   newline-terminated inputs ignored the --max-input-size limit.
##   Fix: stage stdin into a same-FS temp file with `head -c N+2`,
##   measure raw byte count via `wc -c` BEFORE the `$(<file)` strip,
##   and compare against the cap.
##
## Sub-bug 2 (lib/_dispatch.sh:274):
##   `for k in "${!_bs_strategy_counts[@]}"; do Aje280a6Aj` aborts under
##   bash 4.x with `set -u` when the assoc array has no keys.
##   Fix: explicit `declare -A foo=()` initializer plus a
##   `${#arr[@]} -gt 0` guard around the loop.
##
## Sub-bug 3 (lib/_dispatch.sh:447):
##   Replay command was constructed with single-quote splices:
##     local cmd="mfe --replay '${matched_strategies}'"
##   A value containing `'` produced a broken / injection-prone
##   command that pasted into a shell mis-parses or runs unintended
##   code. Fix: shell-quote each piece via `printf '%q'` so the
##   emitted line round-trips through bash word-splitting.
################################################################################

set -u

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# Resolve the engine relative to this test dir (tests/.. == the engine root),
# not via a hardcoded "EnvoyExtract" directory name Aje28094Aj so the suite runs unchanged
# when the tree is vendored elsewhere (e.g. glean/lib/extract/). Matches helpers.sh.
ENGINE_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
EE="$ENGINE_ROOT/envoy-extract"
DISPATCH="$ENGINE_ROOT/lib/_dispatch.sh"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
_pass () { PASS=$((PASS+1)); printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
_fail () { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf '  FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2; if [[ -n "${2:-}" ]]; then printf '    %s\n' "$2" >&2; fi; }

WORK=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/env182_test.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "ENV-182: extract dispatch Aje28094Aj oversize, empty-array, replay-quote"
echo "========================================"

###############################################################################
# Section A Aje28094Aj oversized-input check fires on newline-terminated input
###############################################################################

# Use a tiny cap so we don't blast the test environment.
SMALL_CAP=64

# A1: input of exactly CAP+1 bytes plus trailing newlines.
# Pre-fix `$(head -c CAP+1)` strips the newlines, so ${#text} Aje289a4Aj CAP
# and the cap check missed. Post-fix the cap check uses raw byte
# count and fires.
{
    head -c $((SMALL_CAP + 1)) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x'
    printf '\n\n\n'
} > "$WORK/oversize.in"

err_out=$(bash "$EE" --max-input-size $SMALL_CAP < "$WORK/oversize.in" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?")
if [[ "$err_out" == *"too large"* && "$err_out" == *"rc=1"* ]]; then
    _pass "oversized stdin (CAP+1 bytes + newlines) triggers --max-input-size cap"
else
    _fail "oversized cap missed newline-terminated input" \
          "$(printf '%s' "$err_out" | head -3)"
fi

# A2: input of exactly CAP bytes (no overflow) is accepted, even when
# trailing newlines push the byte count to CAP+2. The cap is
# inclusive Aje28094Aj input <= CAP must NOT trigger the abort. We feed CAP-2
# bytes of payload + 2 trailing newlines for a total of CAP bytes.
{
    head -c $((SMALL_CAP - 2)) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x'
    printf '\n\n'
} > "$WORK/under.in"

err_out=$(bash "$EE" --max-input-size $SMALL_CAP < "$WORK/under.in" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?")
if [[ "$err_out" != *"too large"* ]]; then
    _pass "under-cap input is not rejected"
else
    _fail "under-cap input incorrectly rejected" "$(printf '%s' "$err_out" | head -3)"
fi

# A3: drift Aje28094Aj the new staging-into-tempfile path is wired in.
if grep -qE 'envoy-extract-stage' "$EE" && grep -qE 'wc -c < "\$_raw_stage"' "$EE"; then
    _pass "drift: envoy-extract uses temp-file staging + wc -c byte cap"
else
    _fail "drift: envoy-extract still uses \${#text}-only oversize check"
fi

###############################################################################
# Section B Aje28094Aj empty assoc-array iteration in batch summary
###############################################################################

# B1: source the lib in a fresh shell with `set -u`, declare an empty
# assoc array the same way _dispatch.sh does, and iterate. Pre-fix
# this aborted on bash 4.x; the explicit `=()` initializer is the
# documented fix, so we reproduce that pattern in isolation.
out=$(bash -c 'set -u; declare -A foo=(); for k in "${!foo[@]}"; do echo "$k"; done; echo done' 2>&1)
if [[ "$out" == "done" ]]; then
    _pass "empty assoc array iteration is set -u safe with =() initializer"
else
    _fail "empty assoc array initializer fix didn't hold" "got: $out"
fi

# B2: drift Aje28094Aj _dispatch.sh's declaration uses the empty initializer.
if grep -qE 'declare -A _bs_strategy_counts=\(\)' "$DISPATCH"; then
    _pass "drift: _dispatch.sh uses 'declare -A foo=()' for batch counts"
else
    _fail "drift: _dispatch.sh missing empty-init for _bs_strategy_counts"
fi

# B3: drift Aje28094Aj the iteration is guarded by a size check.
if grep -qE '\$\{#_bs_strategy_counts\[@\]\} -gt 0' "$DISPATCH"; then
    _pass "drift: _dispatch.sh guards iteration with size check"
else
    _fail "drift: _dispatch.sh missing size-guard around assoc iteration"
fi

###############################################################################
# Section C Aje28094Aj replay command shell-quotes each piece
###############################################################################

# C1: drift Aje28094Aj `printf '%q'` is wired in for the cmdline build path.
if grep -qE "_qstrats=\\\$\(printf '%q' \"\\\$matched_strategies\"\)" "$DISPATCH"; then
    _pass "drift: _dispatch.sh quotes matched_strategies via printf %q"
else
    _fail "drift: _dispatch.sh missing printf %q for matched_strategies"
fi
if grep -qE "_qfile=\\\$\(printf '%q' \"\\\$file\"\)" "$DISPATCH"; then
    _pass "drift: _dispatch.sh quotes file via printf %q"
else
    _fail "drift: _dispatch.sh missing printf %q for file"
fi
if grep -qE "_qfields=\\\$\(printf '%q' \"\\\$fields\"\)" "$DISPATCH"; then
    _pass "drift: _dispatch.sh quotes fields via printf %q"
else
    _fail "drift: _dispatch.sh missing printf %q for fields"
fi

# C2: drift Aje28094Aj the legacy single-quote splice is gone.
if grep -nE "cmd=\"mfe --replay '\\\$\{matched_strategies\}'\"" "$DISPATCH" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _fail "drift: _dispatch.sh still has legacy single-quote splice for replay"
else
    _pass "drift: legacy single-quote splice removed from _dispatch.sh replay"
fi

# C3: round-trip Aje28094Aj quoted output round-trips through eval. We
# simulate the dispatch path by mirroring the new construction in
# isolation; if the values come back equal post-eval, the quoting is
# correct.
matched_strategies="strat1,strat2"
file="it's a name.txt"
fields="a,b,c"
_qstrats=$(printf '%q' "$matched_strategies")
_qfile=$(printf '%q' "$file")
_qfields=$(printf '%q' "$fields")
cmd="mfe --replay ${_qstrats} ${_qfile} ${_qfields}"
# Round-trip the cmd through bash word-splitting via `eval set --`.
# After this, $1..$5 contain the parsed argv (mfe / --replay /
# strategies / file / fields). The single-quote in $file must
# survive intact.
eval "set -- $cmd"
if [[ "$#" == "5" \
   && "$1" == "mfe" \
   && "$2" == "--replay" \
   && "$3" == "$matched_strategies" \
   && "$4" == "$file" \
   && "$5" == "$fields" ]]; then
    _pass "replay command with single-quote in filename round-trips through eval"
else
    _fail "replay round-trip wrong" \
          "argc=$# argv1=$1 argv2=$2 argv3=$3 argv4=$4 argv5=$5"
fi

###############################################################################

echo ""
echo "========================================"
printf 'Results: %d/%d passed, %d failed\n' "$PASS" "$((PASS+FAIL))" "$FAIL"
if [[ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "========================================"
    exit 1
fi
echo "All tests passed."
echo "========================================"
===END===
===FILE: extract/tests/test_edge_cases.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=a6327b462f3d7d9274e041f4dc3b7ae08830fd40e0d4dcd5d9f5cad61aa8c785===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Edge Case Tests for envoy-extract
##
## Tests for input size limits, boundary conditions, and error handling.
################################################################################

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/helpers.sh"

TMPDIR_E="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/edge_cases_$$"
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR_E"

################################################################################
## Max input size guard
################################################################################

test_max_input_size_file_rejected () {
    # Create a file that exceeds a small max-input-size
    printf '%0.s.' {1..200} > "$TMPDIR_E/big.txt"
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --max-input-size 100 "$TMPDIR_E/big.txt" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "too large" "should report file too large"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit"; return 1; }
}

test_max_input_size_file_accepted () {
    # Create a small file within limits
    echo '{"name": "test"}' > "$TMPDIR_E/small.json"
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --max-input-size 1000 -s json "$TMPDIR_E/small.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Should succeed without error
    if [[ "$out" == *"too large"* ]]; then
        echo "  unexpected size rejection"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

test_max_input_size_stdin_rejected () {
    # Pipe data that exceeds a small max-input-size
    local out rc=0
    out=$(printf '%0.s.' {1..200} | run_mfe --max-input-size 100 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "too large" "should report stdin input too large"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit"; return 1; }
}

################################################################################
## Empty file (0 bytes)
################################################################################

test_empty_file () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/empty.txt"
    : > "$tmpfile"
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Should not crash; exit 0 with a "No fields" message or exit 1 quietly
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Empty file: verify no spurious output on stdout
################################################################################

test_empty_file_no_spurious_output () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/empty2.txt"
    : > "$tmpfile"
    local stdout_out
    stdout_out=$(run_mfe "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null) || true
    # stdout should be empty (no extracted fields)
    assert_output_empty "$stdout_out" "empty file should produce no stdout output"
}

################################################################################
## Whitespace-only file
################################################################################

test_whitespace_only_file () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/whitespace.txt"
    printf '   \n\t\t\n   \n\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Should not crash; whitespace-only input has no extractable fields
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Whitespace-only file: verify no spurious output on stdout
################################################################################

test_whitespace_only_no_spurious_output () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/whitespace2.txt"
    printf '   \n\t\n  \n' > "$tmpfile"
    local stdout_out
    stdout_out=$(run_mfe "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null) || true
    assert_output_empty "$stdout_out" "whitespace-only file should produce no stdout output"
}

################################################################################
## Very long single line (>64KB)
################################################################################

test_very_long_line () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/longline.txt"
    # Create a line >64KB with key: value pattern
    printf 'Name: ' > "$tmpfile"
    # Append 70000 'A' characters as the value
    python3 -c "print('A' * 70000, end='')" >> "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null || \
        perl -e "print 'A' x 70000" >> "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null || \
        dd if=/dev/zero bs=1 count=70000 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' 'A' >> "$tmpfile"
    printf '\n' >> "$tmpfile"
    local out rc=0
    # Use specific strategy to avoid slow auto-discovery on huge input
    out=$(run_mfe -s colons "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Should not crash or hang; exit code 0 or 1 is acceptable
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## File with only one field
################################################################################

test_single_field_file () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/single.txt"
    printf 'hostname: server01\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe -r -s colons "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "single field file should succeed"
    assert_contains "$out" "hostname" "should extract the single field name"
    assert_contains "$out" "server01" "should extract the single field value"
}

################################################################################
## File with only one field: count should be 1
################################################################################

test_single_field_count () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile="$TMPDIR_E/single_count.txt"
    printf 'version: 2.0\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    assert_eq "$out" "1" "count for single-field file should be 1"
}

################################################################################
## Run all tests
################################################################################

echo "Edge Case Tests"
echo "================"

run_test "max-input-size: file rejected" test_max_input_size_file_rejected
run_test "max-input-size: file accepted" test_max_input_size_file_accepted
run_test "max-input-size: stdin rejected" test_max_input_size_stdin_rejected
run_test "edge: empty file (0 bytes) no crash" test_empty_file
run_test "edge: empty file no spurious stdout" test_empty_file_no_spurious_output
run_test "edge: whitespace-only file no crash" test_whitespace_only_file
run_test "edge: whitespace-only file no spurious stdout" test_whitespace_only_no_spurious_output
run_test "edge: very long single line >64KB" test_very_long_line
run_test "edge: single field extraction" test_single_field_file
run_test "edge: single field count" test_single_field_count

print_summary

# Cleanup
rm -rf "$TMPDIR_E"
===END===
===FILE: extract/tests/test_emit_meta.sh===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## --emit-meta tests (ENV-200)
##
## Verify that a single extract run can surface the winning strategy + its
## confidence on stderr (so callers like `envoy-capture inject` avoid a second
## `explain` pass), while stdout still carries the normal extracted data.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "--emit-meta Tests"
echo "========================================"

test_emit_meta_line_on_stderr () {
    local tmpfile meta
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"a":1,"b":2}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # stdout = data, stderr = meta line.
    meta=$(run_mfe --emit-meta -f tsv --max-strategies 1 "$tmpfile" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$meta" "__EXTRACT_META__" "meta line is emitted to stderr"
    assert_contains "$meta" "json" "meta names the winning strategy"
}

test_emit_meta_keeps_stdout_data () {
    local tmpfile out
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"a":1,"b":2}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    out=$(run_mfe --emit-meta -f tsv --max-strategies 1 "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$out" "a" "stdout still carries the extracted data"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "__EXTRACT_META__" "meta does not leak onto stdout"
}

test_emit_meta_absent_without_flag () {
    local tmpfile both
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"a":1}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    both=$(run_mfe -f tsv --max-strategies 1 "$tmpfile" 2>&1)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_not_contains "$both" "__EXTRACT_META__" "no meta line without --emit-meta"
}

run_test "emit-meta line on stderr"        test_emit_meta_line_on_stderr
run_test "emit-meta keeps stdout data"     test_emit_meta_keeps_stdout_data
run_test "no meta without the flag"        test_emit_meta_absent_without_flag

print_summary
===END===
===FILE: extract/tests/test_encoding.sh===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Encoding Tests for Envoy:Explore (envoy-extract)
##
## Tests that multi-byte / non-ASCII characters are handled without crashing
## or data loss by the engine and relevant strategies.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Encoding Tests"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## UTF-8 multi-byte characters in colons input
################################################################################

test_utf8_colons () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Ren\xc3\xa9\nCity: Z\xc3\xbcrich\nRole: d\xc3\xa9veloppeur\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s colons "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should not crash on UTF-8 colons input"
    assert_contains "$output" "Name" "should extract Name field"
    assert_contains "$output" "City" "should extract City field"
}

################################################################################
## CSV with UTF-8 BOM
################################################################################

test_csv_utf8_bom () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Write UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) followed by CSV content
    printf '\xef\xbb\xbfName,Age,City\nAlice,30,Boston\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s csv "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should not crash on BOM CSV"
    assert_contains "$output" "Name" "should strip BOM and extract Name header"
    assert_contains "$output" "Alice" "should extract value Alice"
    assert_contains "$output" "30" "should extract value 30"
}

################################################################################
## Mixed ASCII/UTF-8 values in equals format
################################################################################

test_utf8_equals () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Greeting=Caf\xc3\xa9\nTemp=25\xc2\xb0C\nStatus=OK\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s equals "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should not crash on UTF-8 equals input"
    assert_contains "$output" "Greeting" "should extract Greeting field"
    assert_contains "$output" "Status" "should extract Status field"
    assert_contains "$output" "OK" "should extract ASCII value OK"
}

################################################################################
## UTF-8 values round-trip through JSON format
################################################################################

test_utf8_json_format () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Server: M\xc3\xbcnchen\nPort: 8080\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -s colons -f json "$tmpfile" 1,2 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should not crash when formatting UTF-8 as JSON"
    assert_contains "$output" '"Server":' "JSON output should contain Server key"
    assert_contains "$output" '"Port":' "JSON output should contain Port key"
}

################################################################################
## Run all tests
################################################################################

run_test "encoding: UTF-8 multi-byte in colons input" test_utf8_colons
run_test "encoding: CSV with UTF-8 BOM stripping" test_csv_utf8_bom
run_test "encoding: mixed ASCII/UTF-8 in equals" test_utf8_equals
run_test "encoding: UTF-8 values in JSON format output" test_utf8_json_format

print_summary
===END===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Error Path Tests for envoy-extract
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Error Path Tests"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## 1. Missing file argument (no stdin, no file)
################################################################################

test_missing_file_argument () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    # When stdin is a tty, mfe reports "No input file provided"
    # Redirect /dev/null to stdin so -t 0 fails, triggering the stdin path
    # which then gets empty data Aje28094Aj but to test the actual "no file" path,
    # we need stdin to be a tty. Use the /dev/null redirect to at least
    # confirm mfe exits non-zero and shows an error.
    output=$(run_mfe 2>&1 </dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero with no input"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "No data received" "should mention no data received"
}

################################################################################
## 2. Non-existent file
################################################################################

test_nonexistent_file () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe /tmp/this_file_does_not_exist_mfe_test.txt 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero for missing file"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "File not found" "should mention file not found"
}

################################################################################
## 3. Empty stdin
################################################################################

test_empty_stdin () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    output=$(echo "" | run_mfe 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero for empty stdin"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "No data received" "should mention no data"
}

################################################################################
## 4. Invalid --format value
################################################################################

test_invalid_format () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe --format bogusformat "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero for invalid format"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "Unknown format" "should mention unknown format"
}

################################################################################
## 5. Invalid --min-confidence (non-numeric)
################################################################################

test_invalid_min_confidence () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe --min-confidence abc "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero for non-numeric min-confidence"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "--min-confidence" "should mention the flag"
}

################################################################################
## 6. Invalid --max-strategies (non-numeric)
################################################################################

test_invalid_max_strategies () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe --max-strategies xyz "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero for non-numeric max-strategies"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "--max-strategies" "should mention the flag"
}

################################################################################
## 7. --stream without --strategy
################################################################################

test_stream_without_strategy () {
    local rc=0
    local output
    output=$(echo "test" | run_mfe --stream 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should exit non-zero for --stream without --strategy"
    assert_contains "$output" "envoy-extract: error:" "should show error message"
    assert_contains "$output" "--stream requires --strategy" "should mention stream requires strategy"
}

################################################################################
## 15. --no-dedup produces duplicates
################################################################################

test_no_dedup () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Write data that both colons and equals strategies can match
    printf "hostname: server01\nhostname=server01\n" > "$tmpfile"

    # With --no-dedup -r, both strategies should produce duplicate hostname fields
    local output_dup
    output_dup=$(run_mfe --no-dedup -r "$tmpfile")
    local dup_count
    dup_count=$(echo "$output_dup" | grep -c "hostname" || true)

    # Without --no-dedup, deduplication should collapse duplicates
    local output_dedup
    output_dedup=$(run_mfe -r "$tmpfile")
    local dedup_count
    dedup_count=$(echo "$output_dedup" | grep -c "hostname" || true)

    rm -f "$tmpfile"

    # With no-dedup, there should be more hostname occurrences than with dedup
    assert_contains "$output_dup" "hostname" "no-dedup output should contain hostname"
    assert_contains "$output_dedup" "hostname" "dedup output should contain hostname"
    if [[ "$dup_count" -gt "$dedup_count" ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --no-dedup should produce more duplicates"
        echo "    no-dedup count: $dup_count"
        echo "    dedup count:    $dedup_count"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## 16. --output FILE writes to file
################################################################################

test_output_file () {
    local tmpdir
    tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
    local outfile="$tmpdir/mfe_output.txt"

    local rc=0
    run_mfe --output "$outfile" -s colons "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?

    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should succeed writing to output file"

    if [[ ! -f "$outfile" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: output file should exist"
        echo "    file: $outfile"
        rm -rf "$tmpdir"
        return 1
    fi

    local content
    content=$(<"$outfile")
    assert_contains "$content" "Name" "output file should contain extracted field"

    rm -rf "$tmpdir"
}

    assert_contains "$output" "binary" "should warn about binary file"

################################################################################

run_test "error: missing file argument" test_missing_file_argument

===FILE: extract/tests/test_field_filter.sh===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for --field-pattern and --exclude-field flags
##
## Covers: regex pattern matching, exact name exclusion, combined usage,
##         edge cases (no matches, invalid regex, multiple excludes)
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/tests/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Field Filter Tests (--field-pattern, --exclude-field)"
echo "========================================"

# Sample JSON input used by most tests
SAMPLE_JSON='{"cpu_user": 42, "cpu_system": 10, "cpu_idle": 48, "hostname": "server1", "mem_total": 8192, "mem_free": 4096, "disk_total": 500, "uptime_seconds": 86400}'

################################################################################
## Test 1: --field-pattern '^cpu' matches cpu_user, cpu_system, cpu_idle
##

test_field_pattern_prefix () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '^cpu' -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should contain cpu_user"
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_system" "should contain cpu_system"
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_idle" "should contain cpu_idle"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not contain hostname"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "mem_total" "should not contain mem_total"
}

run_test "--field-pattern '^cpu' matches cpu_ fields" test_field_pattern_prefix

################################################################################
## Test 2: --field-pattern '.*_total$' matches fields ending in _total
##

test_field_pattern_suffix () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '_total$' -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "mem_total" "should contain mem_total"
    assert_contains "$out" "disk_total" "should contain disk_total"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should not contain cpu_user"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not contain hostname"
}

run_test "--field-pattern '_total\$' matches fields ending in _total" test_field_pattern_suffix

################################################################################
## Test 3: --exclude-field hostname removes exactly that field
##

test_exclude_field_single () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --exclude-field hostname -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not contain hostname"
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should still contain cpu_user"
    assert_contains "$out" "mem_total" "should still contain mem_total"
}

run_test "--exclude-field hostname removes exactly hostname" test_exclude_field_single

################################################################################
## Test 4: Multiple --exclude-field flags
##

test_exclude_field_multiple () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --exclude-field hostname --exclude-field uptime_seconds -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not contain hostname"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "uptime_seconds" "should not contain uptime_seconds"
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should still contain cpu_user"
    assert_contains "$out" "mem_total" "should still contain mem_total"
}

run_test "Multiple --exclude-field flags remove multiple fields" test_exclude_field_multiple

################################################################################
## Test 5: Combined --field-pattern + --exclude-field
##

test_combined_pattern_and_exclude () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '^cpu' --exclude-field cpu_idle -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should contain cpu_user"
    assert_contains "$out" "cpu_system" "should contain cpu_system"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "cpu_idle" "should not contain cpu_idle (excluded)"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not contain hostname (filtered by pattern)"
}

run_test "Combined --field-pattern + --exclude-field" test_combined_pattern_and_exclude

################################################################################
## Test 6: --field-pattern with no matches produces empty/no-fields output
##

test_field_pattern_no_matches () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '^nonexistent' -f json 2>/dev/null)
    # When no fields match, output should be empty JSON or no output
    assert_not_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should not contain cpu_user"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not contain hostname"
}

run_test "--field-pattern with no matches produces empty output" test_field_pattern_no_matches

################################################################################
## Test 7: Invalid regex produces error message
##

test_field_pattern_invalid_regex () {
    local out rc
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '[invalid' -f json 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "${rc:-1}" "should exit non-zero for invalid regex"
    assert_contains "$out" "Invalid regex" "should show invalid regex error"
}

run_test "--field-pattern with invalid regex shows error" test_field_pattern_invalid_regex

################################################################################
## Test 8: --exclude-field with nonexistent field name is a no-op
##

test_exclude_nonexistent_field () {
    local out_without out_with
    out_without=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe -f json 2>/dev/null)
    out_with=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --exclude-field nonexistent_field -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_eq "$out_without" "$out_with" "excluding nonexistent field should not change output"
}

run_test "--exclude-field with nonexistent field is a no-op" test_exclude_nonexistent_field

################################################################################
## Test 9: --field-pattern with dot-star matches all fields
##

test_field_pattern_match_all () {
    local out_all out_pattern
    out_all=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe -f json 2>/dev/null)
    out_pattern=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '.*' -f json 2>/dev/null)
    assert_eq "$out_all" "$out_pattern" "pattern '.*' should match all fields"
}

run_test "--field-pattern '.*' matches all fields" test_field_pattern_match_all

################################################################################
## Test 10: --field-pattern works with --names output mode
##

test_field_pattern_with_names () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '^mem' --names 2>/dev/null)
    assert_contains "$out" "mem_total" "should list mem_total"
    assert_contains "$out" "mem_free" "should list mem_free"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "should not list cpu_user"
    assert_not_contains "$out" "hostname" "should not list hostname"
}

run_test "--field-pattern works with --names output mode" test_field_pattern_with_names

################################################################################
## Test 11: --exclude-field works with --count output mode
##

test_exclude_field_with_count () {
    local count_all count_excluded
    count_all=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --count 2>/dev/null)
    count_excluded=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --exclude-field hostname --count 2>/dev/null)
    # Excluding one field should reduce the count by 1
    local expected=$((count_all - 1))
    assert_eq "$expected" "$count_excluded" "count should be one less after excluding a field"
}

run_test "--exclude-field works with --count output mode" test_exclude_field_with_count

################################################################################
## Test 12: --field-pattern with case-sensitive matching
##

test_field_pattern_case_sensitive () {
    local out
    out=$(echo "$SAMPLE_JSON" | run_mfe --field-pattern '^CPU' -f json 2>/dev/null)
    # Field names are lowercase (cpu_user, etc.), so ^CPU should not match
    assert_not_contains "$out" "cpu_user" "case-sensitive: ^CPU should not match cpu_user"
}

run_test "--field-pattern is case-sensitive" test_field_pattern_case_sensitive

################################################################################
## Summary
##

print_summary
exit $?
===END===
===FILE: extract/tests/test_flag_combinations.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=89905dc2a226a8e6b676d6ce853a01d3b805f7d59d662bf36cceaf060a670556===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Flag Combination Interaction Tests
##
## Verify that combined CLI flags produce correct behavior.
## These test interactions NOT covered by individual flag tests.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Flag Combination Tests"
echo "========================================"

# --- --sort + --names: sorted field names only ---

test_flags_sort_names () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Zebra: last\nAlpha: first\nMiddle: center\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # --names exits before --sort is applied (names at line 1107, sort at line 1117)
    # so field names should appear in extraction order, not sorted
    output=$(run_mfe --names -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Just verify names are present (order depends on pipeline)
    assert_contains "$output" "Zebra" "should output Zebra field name"
    assert_contains "$output" "Alpha" "should output Alpha field name"
    assert_contains "$output" "Middle" "should output Middle field name"
}

# --- --sort + --count: count takes precedence ---

test_flags_sort_count () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\nCity: Portland\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # --count exits at line 1097, before --sort at line 1117
    output=$(run_mfe --sort --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Count should be 3 regardless of sort
    assert_eq "$output" "3" "count should be 3 independent of sort"
}

# --- --rename + --sort: renamed then sorted ---

test_flags_rename_sort () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Alpha: first\nBeta: second\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # Rename Alpha to ZZZ_Alpha, then sort: ZZZ_Alpha should appear after Beta
    output=$(run_mfe --rename 'Alpha=ZZZ_Alpha' --sort -r -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "ZZZ_Alpha first" "should have renamed field"
    # In sorted output, Beta should come before ZZZ_Alpha
    local beta_pos zzz_pos
    beta_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Beta" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    zzz_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "ZZZ_Alpha" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    if [[ -n "$beta_pos" && -n "$zzz_pos" && "$beta_pos" -lt "$zzz_pos" ]]; then
        assert_eq "ok" "ok" "Beta should sort before ZZZ_Alpha"
    else
        assert_eq "Beta before ZZZ_Alpha" "ZZZ_Alpha before Beta" "sort order incorrect after rename"
    fi
}

# --- --rename + --aggregate: aggregated fields use renamed names ---

test_flags_rename_aggregate () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Score: 10\nScore: 20\nScore: 30\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --rename 'Score=Points' --aggregate -r -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "Points_count 3" "aggregated field should use renamed name"
    assert_contains "$output" "Points_sum 60" "aggregated sum should use renamed name"
}

# --- --rename + --names: renamed names in output ---

test_flags_rename_names () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --rename 'Name=FullName' --names -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "FullName" "names should show renamed field"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "Alice" "names should not show values"
}

# --- --rename + --count: count unchanged by rename ---

test_flags_rename_count () {
    local tmpfile output_with output_without
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\nCity: Portland\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output_with=$(run_mfe --rename 'Name=FullName' --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    output_without=$(run_mfe --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_eq "$output_with" "$output_without" "count should be the same with or without rename"
}

# --- --first-match + --min-confidence: confidence filters first ---

test_flags_firstmatch_minconfidence () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Create input that matches both yaml (c90, p12) and colons (c35, p60)
    printf 'server:\n  host: localhost\n  port: 8080\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # With min-confidence 80, colons (c35) is filtered out; yaml (c90) matches first
    output=$(run_mfe --first-match --min-confidence 80 -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # yaml produces dot-notation fields
    assert_contains "$output" "server.host" "high-confidence yaml should match with first-match"
}

# --- --max-strategies + --no-dedup: duplicates preserved ---

test_flags_maxstrategies_nodedup () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Host: localhost\nPort: 5432\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # With no-dedup, if multiple strategies extract the same fields, both kept
    output=$(run_mfe --no-dedup -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Just verify output is non-empty (no-dedup should not cause issues)
    assert_contains "$output" "Host" "no-dedup output should include fields"
}

# --- --aggregate + --sort: aggregated then sorted ---

test_flags_aggregate_sort () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Score: 10\nScore: 20\nScore: 30\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --aggregate --sort -r -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # After aggregate: Score_count, Score_min, Score_max, Score_sum, Score_avg
    # After sort: alphabetical order: Score_avg < Score_count < Score_max < Score_min < Score_sum
    assert_contains "$output" "Score_count 3" "Score_count should be in sorted output"
    assert_contains "$output" "Score_avg" "Score_avg should be in sorted output"
    # Verify sorting: avg should come before count (alphabetical)
    local avg_pos count_pos
    avg_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Score_avg" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    count_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Score_count" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    if [[ -n "$avg_pos" && -n "$count_pos" && "$avg_pos" -lt "$count_pos" ]]; then
        assert_eq "ok" "ok" "Score_avg should sort before Score_count"
    else
        assert_eq "avg<count" "avg=$avg_pos count=$count_pos" "sort order incorrect"
    fi
}

# --- --aggregate + --count: count reflects aggregated lines ---

test_flags_aggregate_count () {
    local tmpfile count_plain count_agg
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Score: 10\nScore: 20\nLevel: 5\n' > "$tmpfile"
    count_plain=$(run_mfe --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    count_agg=$(run_mfe --aggregate --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Plain: 3 fields (Score, Score, Level) -> after dedup: 2 (Score, Level)
    # Aggregated: Level + Score_count + Score_min + Score_max + Score_sum + Score_avg = 6
    # count_agg should be larger than count_plain
    if [[ "$count_agg" -gt "$count_plain" ]]; then
        assert_eq "ok" "ok" "aggregate count should be larger due to stats fields"
    else
        assert_eq "agg>plain" "agg=$count_agg plain=$count_plain" "aggregate should produce more fields"
    fi
}

# --- --quiet + --min-confidence 100: silent no-match ---

test_flags_quiet_minconfidence_high () {
    local tmpfile rc output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\n' > "$tmpfile"
    rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe --quiet --min-confidence 100 "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # With min-confidence 100, no strategy reaches that threshold
    # --quiet means no stderr messages, exit code 1
    assert_eq "$rc" "1" "should exit 1 when no fields pass confidence filter"
    assert_eq "$output" "" "quiet mode should produce no output"
}

# --- --verbose + --first-match: verbose shows 1 matched ---

test_flags_verbose_firstmatch () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"name": "test", "value": 42}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --verbose --first-match -s json "$tmpfile" 2>&1)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "1 matched" "verbose should show 1 matched with first-match"
}

# --- --output FILE + --sort: sorted output in file ---

test_flags_output_sort () {
    local tmpfile outfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    outfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Zebra: last\nAlpha: first\n' > "$tmpfile"
    run_mfe --output "$outfile" --sort -r -s colons "$tmpfile" >/dev/null 2>&1
    output=$(<"$outfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile" "$outfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "Alpha first" "output file should contain Alpha"
    assert_contains "$output" "Zebra last" "output file should contain Zebra"
}

# --- -f csv + --rename: CSV header uses renamed names ---

test_flags_format_csv_rename () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe -f csv --rename 'Name=FullName' -s colons "$tmpfile" 1,2)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "FullName" "CSV header should use renamed field name"
}

# --- -f json + --aggregate: valid JSON with aggregate keys ---

test_flags_format_json_aggregate () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Score: 10\nScore: 20\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe -f json --aggregate -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # JSON output should contain aggregate keys
    assert_contains "$output" "Score_count" "JSON output should have aggregate keys"
    assert_contains "$output" "{" "output should be JSON (has opening brace)"
}

# --- --stream + --rename: streaming output uses renamed names ---

test_flags_stream_rename () {
    # Stream mode processes lines independently and exits before rename pipeline
    # Verify that stream produces output (rename is not applied in stream mode)
    local output
    output=$(printf 'Host: web\nPort: 80\n' | run_mfe --stream --strategy colons)
    assert_contains "$output" '"Host"' "stream JSON should output Host field"
    assert_contains "$output" '"Port"' "stream JSON should output Port field"
}

# --- field-by-name + --sort: filtered and sorted ---

test_flags_field_by_name_sort () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Zebra: last\nAlpha: first\nMiddle: center\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --sort -r -s colons "$tmpfile" -f Name,Alpha,Zebra)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # field-by-name with sort should filter AND sort
    # This tests the interaction: sort applies, then field selection filters
    assert_contains "$output" "Alpha" "should include Alpha field"
}

# --- --no-dedup + --aggregate: aggregation sees duplicates ---

test_flags_nodedup_aggregate () {
    local tmpfile count_dedup count_nodedup
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Score: 10\nScore: 20\n' > "$tmpfile"
    count_dedup=$(run_mfe --aggregate --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    count_nodedup=$(run_mfe --no-dedup --aggregate --count -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # With single strategy, no-dedup shouldn't change anything
    # Both should produce aggregate output
    assert_contains "$count_dedup" "" "dedup aggregate count should be numeric"
    assert_contains "$count_nodedup" "" "no-dedup aggregate count should be numeric"
}

# --- --delimiter with multi-character delimiter '|||' ---

test_flags_delimiter_multichar () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'hostname|||web-server-01\nrole|||load-balancer\nenv|||staging\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe -r --delimiter '|||' "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "hostname" "should extract hostname with ||| delimiter"
    assert_contains "$output" "web-server-01" "should extract value web-server-01"
    assert_contains "$output" "role" "should extract role with ||| delimiter"
    assert_contains "$output" "load-balancer" "should extract value load-balancer"
    assert_contains "$output" "env" "should extract env with ||| delimiter"
    assert_contains "$output" "staging" "should extract value staging"
}

test_flags_delimiter_multichar_coloneq () {

    # Should be valid JSON written to the output file

    assert_contains "$output" "Name" "output file JSON should contain Name field"

    assert_contains "$output" "Age" "output file JSON should contain Age field"

# --- --replay with version mismatch: warns but still works ---

test_flags_replay_version_mismatch () {
    local tmpfile output stderr_output rc
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Host: localhost\nPort: 8080\n' > "$tmpfile"
    # Run with --replay specifying a version that does not match the installed colons strategy
    rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe --replay 'colons@999.0' -r "$tmpfile" 2>"${tmpfile}.err") || rc=$?
    stderr_output=$(<"${tmpfile}.err")
    rm -f "$tmpfile" "${tmpfile}.err"
    # Should still succeed (exit 0) and produce output
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "replay with version mismatch should still exit 0"
    assert_contains "$output" "Host" "replay should still extract Host field"
    assert_contains "$output" "localhost" "replay should still extract localhost value"
    # Stderr should contain a version mismatch warning
    assert_contains "$stderr_output" "version mismatch" "stderr should contain version mismatch warning"
}

test_yaml_quote_empty () {
    _yaml_needs_quote ""
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "empty string requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_colon () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "host:port"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "colon in value requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_hash () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "value#comment"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "hash in value requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_boolean_true () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "true"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "boolean 'true' requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_boolean_false () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "false"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "boolean 'false' requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_null () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "null"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "'null' requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_yes () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "yes"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "'yes' requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_numeric_start () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "42"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "digit-starting value requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_numeric_start_float () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "3.14"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "float value requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_curly_brace () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "{key: val}"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "curly brace requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_double_quote () {
    _yaml_needs_quote 'say "hello"'
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "double quote in value requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_quote_special_chars () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "foo@bar"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "@ character requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_no_quote_plain_word () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "hello"
    assert_eq "0" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "plain word should not require quoting"
}

test_yaml_no_quote_hyphenated () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "server-a"
    assert_eq "0" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "hyphenated identifier should not require quoting"
}

    _yaml_needs_quote "10.0.0.1"
    assert_eq "1" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "IP address (digit-start) requires quoting"
}

test_yaml_no_quote_underscore () {
    _yaml_needs_quote "my_value"
    assert_eq "0" "$_YAML_NEEDS_QUOTE" "underscore-containing value should not require quoting"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# --generic works with --sort
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_generic_with_sort () {
    local tmpfile output
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Zebra: last\nAlpha: first\n' > "$tmpfile"
    output=$(run_mfe --generic --sort -r "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    local alpha_pos zebra_pos
    alpha_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Alpha" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    zebra_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n "Zebra" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    if [[ -n "$alpha_pos" && -n "$zebra_pos" && "$alpha_pos" -lt "$zebra_pos" ]]; then
        assert_eq "ok" "ok" "--generic --sort: Alpha before Zebra"
    else
        assert_eq "Alpha before Zebra" "wrong order" "--generic --sort should sort alphabetically"
    fi
}

test_technique_validate_key () {
    bash -c "
        source \"$MFE_DIR/lib/_helpers.sh\"
        source \"$MFE_DIR/lib/_techniques.sh\"
        _tech_validate_key ''
        [[ \$_TECH_KEY_VALID -eq 0 ]] || exit 1   # empty should be invalid
        _tech_validate_key 'NormalKey'
        [[ \$_TECH_KEY_VALID -eq 1 ]] || exit 1   # normal key should be valid
        long=\$(printf '%0.s_' {1..51})
        _tech_validate_key \"\$long\"
        [[ \$_TECH_KEY_VALID -eq 0 ]] || exit 1   # 51-char key should be invalid
        _tech_validate_key '9digitstart'
        [[ \$_TECH_KEY_VALID -eq 0 ]] || exit 1   # digit-start should be invalid
    "
    assert_exit_zero "$?" "_tech_validate_key should correctly validate keys"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unit test: _tech_split_blocks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_technique_split_blocks () {
    local tmpscript result
    tmpscript=$(mktemp)
    cat > "$tmpscript" <<SCRIPT
source "$MFE_DIR/lib/_helpers.sh"
source "$MFE_DIR/lib/_techniques.sh"
input=\$'block1_line1\nblock1_line2\n\nblock2_line1\nblock2_line2'
_tech_split_blocks "\$input"
count=0
_remaining="\$_TECH_BLOCKS"
while [[ -n "\$_remaining" ]]; do
    _block="\${_remaining%%\$'\\x01'*}"
    [[ "\$_remaining" == *\$'\\x01'* ]] && _remaining="\${_remaining#*\$'\\x01'}" || _remaining=""
    count=\$((count + 1))
done
[[ \$count -eq 2 ]] || exit 1
SCRIPT
    bash "$tmpscript"
    result=$?
    rm -f "$tmpscript"
    assert_exit_zero "$result" "_tech_split_blocks should split into 2 blocks"
}

test_toggle_nth_zero_to_one () {
    local list

    _interactive_toggle_nth "$list" 1

test_toggle_nth_one_to_zero () {
    local list
    list=$'1\n1\n1'
    _interactive_toggle_nth "$list" 0
    local first
    first=$(echo "$_TOGGLE_RESULT" | head -1)
    assert_eq "0" "$first" "toggling index 0 of all-ones should set it to 0"

    third=$(echo "$_TOGGLE_RESULT" | sed -n '3p')

    assert_eq "1" "$third" "toggle should not change non-toggled items (third)"
}

################################################################################
## TTY fallback: mfe --interactive without terminal exits gracefully
################################################################################

test_interactive_no_tty_graceful () {
    # When run without a controlling terminal, mfe -i should exit (not hang).
    # We use timeout to guard against hanging.
    local rc=0
    timeout 3 bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" -i -s colons "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" \
        >/dev/null 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    # Exit code 1 (no output) or 0 (empty selection message) are both acceptable.
    # The critical property is that it exits within 3 seconds (not hung).
    [[ $rc -ne 124 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --interactive hung (timeout)"; return 1; }
}

################################################################################
## Non-TTY fallback behavior
################################################################################

test_interactive_no_tty_fallback_selects_all () {
    # When /dev/tty is unavailable, interactive mode should fall back to
    # selecting all fields and produce output (not just exit silently).
    local output rc=0
    output=$(timeout 3 bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" -i -s colons -f json \
        "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
    # Should not hang (rc 124 = timeout)
    [[ $rc -ne 124 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --interactive hung (timeout)"; return 1; }
    # Should produce JSON output with all fields (fallback selects all)
    if [[ $rc -eq 0 && -n "$output" ]]; then
        assert_contains "$output" "Name" "fallback should include all fields"
    fi
    # rc=0 with output is the ideal; rc=1 with warning is also acceptable
}

test_interactive_no_tty_stderr_warning () {
    # When /dev/tty is unavailable (or broken), stderr should contain a
    # diagnostic message: either the "not a terminal" warning from the code,
    # or the shell's own "No such device" error from /dev/tty redirection.
    local stderr_output rc=0
    stderr_output=$(timeout 3 bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" -i -s colons \
        "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    [[ $rc -ne 124 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --interactive hung (timeout)"; return 1; }
    # Accept either our warning or a shell-level /dev/tty error
    if [[ "$stderr_output" == *"terminal"* ]] || \
       [[ "$stderr_output" == *"/dev/tty"* ]] || \
       [[ "$stderr_output" == *"interactive"* ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    echo "  ASSERT FAILED: non-TTY fallback should warn on stderr"
    echo "    stderr was: '$stderr_output'"
    return 1
}

test_interactive_multiple_files_no_tty () {
    # Interactive mode should work with multiple input files in non-TTY mode.
    # Note: envoy-extract processes one file at a time; multiple files are
    # handled by the caller (or batch mode). This tests that -i doesn't break
    # when a single file is specified alongside strategy.
    local output1 rc1=0
    output1=$(timeout 3 bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" -i -s colons -f json \
        "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" 2>/dev/null) || rc1=$?
    local output2 rc2=0
    output2=$(timeout 3 bash "$MFE_SCRIPT" -i -s json -f json \
        "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>/dev/null) || rc2=$?

    [[ $rc1 -ne 124 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: first file hung"; return 1; }
    [[ $rc2 -ne 124 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: second file hung"; return 1; }

    # Both should succeed (or gracefully fall back)
    if [[ $rc1 -eq 0 && -n "$output1" ]]; then
        assert_contains "$output1" "Name" "first file should extract colons fields"
    fi
    if [[ $rc2 -eq 0 && -n "$output2" ]]; then
        assert_contains "$output2" "name" "second file should extract json fields"
    fi
}

test_interactive_sigint_no_hang () {
    # Send SIGINT to an interactive process and verify it exits promptly.
    # This tests that the process doesn't ignore SIGINT and hang.
    local rc=0
    # Run in background, send SIGINT after a short delay
    timeout 3 bash -c "
        bash \"$MFE_SCRIPT\" -i -s colons \"$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt\" &
        pid=\$!
        sleep 0.3
        kill -INT \$pid 2>/dev/null
        wait \$pid 2>/dev/null
    " >/dev/null 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    # The key property: did not hang (rc=124 means timeout)
    [[ $rc -ne 124 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: process hung after SIGINT"; return 1; }
}

################################################################################

_run_expect_test () {
    local script="$1"
    local desc="$2"
    if [[ $HAS_EXPECT -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf "  %sSKIP%s: %s (expect not installed)\n" "$YELLOW" "$NC" "$desc"
        TESTS_RUN=$((TESTS_RUN + 1))
        TESTS_PASSED=$((TESTS_PASSED + 1))
        return 0
    fi
    local tmpscript
    tmpscript=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/itest_XXXXXX.exp")
    echo "$script" > "$tmpscript"
    local result=0
    expect -f "$tmpscript" >/dev/null 2>&1 || result=1
    rm -f "$tmpscript"
    if [[ $result -eq 0 ]]; then
        TESTS_PASSED=$((TESTS_PASSED + 1))
        printf "  %sPASS%s: %s\n" "$GREEN" "$NC" "$desc"
    else
        TESTS_FAILED=$((TESTS_FAILED + 1))
        FAILED_NAMES+=("$desc")
        printf "  %sFAIL%s: %s\n" "$RED" "$NC" "$desc"
    fi
    TESTS_RUN=$((TESTS_RUN + 1))
}

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Interface Tests for EnvoyExtract v4.2
##
## Tests for subcommand dispatch, smart piped output, interactive non-TTY
## warning, field provenance, and backward compatibility.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Interface Tests (v4.2)"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## Subcommand: list
################################################################################

test_subcommand_list () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe list)
    assert_contains "$output" "Available strategies:" "list subcommand should show header"
    assert_contains "$output" "json" "list subcommand should show json strategy"
    assert_contains "$output" "colons" "list subcommand should show colons strategy"
}

test_subcommand_list_backward_compat () {
    local output_sub output_flag

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Malformed Input Tests for Envoy:Explore (envoy-extract)
##
## Tests that corrupt, truncated, or structurally invalid inputs are handled
## gracefully (no crash, no hang).
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Malformed Input Tests"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## Truncated JSON (no crash, graceful exit)
################################################################################

test_truncated_json () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"name": "test", "version": "1.0", "items": [1, 2,' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -s json "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # jq returns exit code 5 for truncated JSON; the key is it doesn't hang
    # or crash the whole engine catastrophically. Any exit code is acceptable
    # as long as it terminates.
    return 0
}

################################################################################
## CSV with mismatched quotes (graceful handling)
################################################################################

test_csv_mismatched_quotes () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name,City\n"Alice,"New York\nBob,Boston\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -s csv "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Should not hang or crash; mismatched quotes may cause partial data
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Partial CSV (fewer data columns than header)
################################################################################

test_csv_partial_data () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Second data row has one fewer column than the header (3 commas in header, 2 in short row)
    printf 'Name,Age,City,Country\nAlice,30,Boston,US\nBob,25,Denver\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s csv "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "partial CSV should not crash"
    # The full row should still produce all fields
    assert_contains "$output" "Name" "should extract Name header"
    assert_contains "$output" "Alice" "should extract Alice from complete row"
    # The short row should still produce what it can
    assert_contains "$output" "Bob" "should extract Bob from short row"
}

################################################################################
## YAML with tab indentation (doesn't crash)
################################################################################

test_yaml_tab_indentation () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Use tabs instead of spaces for indentation (invalid YAML but common mistake)
    printf 'server:\n\thost: localhost\n\tport: 8080\ndebug: true\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -s yaml "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Should not crash; may extract top-level or nothing
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Malformed TOML (unclosed brackets)
################################################################################

test_malformed_toml_unclosed () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # TOML with unclosed array table bracket and unclosed inline table
    printf '[server]\nhost = "localhost"\nport = 8080\n\n[[items\nname = "broken"\nvalue = {key = "unclosed"\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s toml "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Should not hang or crash
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Malformed TOML: verify partial extraction
################################################################################

test_malformed_toml_partial_extraction () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Valid section header + valid key/value, then a malformed section
    printf '[database]\nhost = "db.example.com"\nport = 5432\n\n[[broken\nname = "item"\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s toml "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # The valid [database] section should still produce output
    assert_contains "$output" "host" "should extract host from valid section"
    assert_contains "$output" "db.example.com" "should extract host value"
}

################################################################################
## Malformed XML (unclosed tags)
################################################################################

test_malformed_xml_unclosed () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # XML with unclosed tags and mismatched nesting
    printf '<root>\n  <name>Alice\n  <age>30</age>\n  <city>Portland\n</root>\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s xml "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Should not hang or crash
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Malformed XML: verify partial extraction of closed tags
################################################################################

test_malformed_xml_partial_extraction () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Mix of well-formed and unclosed tags; the closed tag should still extract
    printf '<data>\n  <name>Bob</name>\n  <email>bob@example.com\n  <age>25</age>\n</data>\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s xml "$tmpfile" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Well-formed elements should still be extracted
    assert_contains "$output" "name" "should extract name from well-formed tag"
    assert_contains "$output" "Bob" "should extract value Bob"
    assert_contains "$output" "age" "should extract age from well-formed tag"
    assert_contains "$output" "25" "should extract value 25"
}

################################################################################

################################################################################

################################################################################

run_test "malformed: truncated JSON (no crash)" test_truncated_json
run_test "malformed: CSV with mismatched quotes (no crash)" test_csv_mismatched_quotes
run_test "malformed: partial CSV fewer data columns than header" test_csv_partial_data
run_test "malformed: YAML with tab indentation (no crash)" test_yaml_tab_indentation
run_test "malformed: TOML unclosed brackets (no crash)" test_malformed_toml_unclosed
run_test "malformed: TOML partial extraction from valid section" test_malformed_toml_partial_extraction
run_test "malformed: XML unclosed tags (no crash)" test_malformed_xml_unclosed
run_test "malformed: XML partial extraction of closed tags" test_malformed_xml_partial_extraction

##
## Tests for strategies that were merged from two or more original strategies.
## Each merged strategy must handle BOTH input styles from its predecessors.
##
## Merged strategies:
##   block-records     (blank-line-records + repeated-blocks)
##   exposition-format (prometheus + openmetrics)
##   pipe-table        (sql-result + markdown-table)
##   network-hops      (traceroute + mtr)
##   xml               (xml-elements + xml-attributes)
##   test-results      (go-test + cargo-test)

################################################################################

test_block_records_blank_line_input () {
    local tmpfile output rc
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Blank-line-separated records with key:value pairs
    printf 'Name: Alice\nAge: 30\nCity: Portland\n\nName: Bob\nAge: 25\nCity: Denver\n' > "$tmpfile"
    rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s block-records "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "block-records should handle blank-line-separated records"
    assert_contains "$output" "Name" "should extract Name field from blank-line records"
    assert_contains "$output" "Alice" "should extract Alice value"
}

test_block_records_repeated_block_input () {
    local tmpfile output rc
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Repeated blocks with key=value pairs separated by blank lines
    printf 'host=web01\nport=80\nstatus=up\n\nhost=web02\nport=443\nstatus=down\n' > "$tmpfile"
    rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s block-records "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "block-records should handle repeated block patterns"
    assert_contains "$output" "host" "should extract host field from repeated blocks"
}

test_exposition_prometheus_input () {

    # Prometheus exposition format
    printf '# HELP http_requests_total The total number of HTTP requests.\n# TYPE http_requests_total counter\nhttp_requests_total{method="post",code="200"} 1027\nhttp_requests_total{method="get",code="200"} 5023\n' > "$tmpfile"
    rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "exposition-format should handle prometheus input"
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total" "should extract prometheus metric name"
}

test_exposition_openmetrics_input () {
    local tmpfile output rc
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)

    rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$tmpfile" 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "exposition-format should handle openmetrics input"
    assert_contains "$output" "process_cpu_seconds" "should extract openmetrics metric"
}

    assert_contains "$output" '{"name":' "JSON should start with opening brace and first key"
    assert_contains "$output" '"version":' "JSON should contain second key"
}

test_csv_format () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -s json -f csv "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 1,2)
    # Should have two lines: header and values
    local line_count
    line_count=$(echo "$output" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    assert_eq "2" "$line_count" "CSV should have 2 lines"
    assert_contains "$output" '"name"' "CSV header should contain field name"
}

test_tsv_format () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -s json -f tsv "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 1,2)
    # TSV horizontal: header row + data row, tab-separated columns
    local line_count
    line_count=$(echo "$output" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    assert_eq "2" "$line_count" "TSV should have 2 lines (header + data)"
    # With 2 fields, each line should have 1 tab
    local header_tabs
    header_tabs=$(echo "$output" | head -1 | tr -cd '\t' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
    assert_eq "1" "$header_tabs" "TSV header should have 1 tab for 2 columns"
}

test_plain_format () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -s json -f plain "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 1)
    assert_contains "$output" "name" "plain should show field name"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "{" "plain should not have JSON braces"
}

## Empty/no-match handling
################################################################################

test_empty_file () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    local rc=0
    run_mfe "$tmpfile" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Should exit 0 (no output, no error)
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "empty file should exit cleanly"
}

################################################################################
## Deduplication
################################################################################

test_dedup_across_strategies () {
    # This file has "Name: John" (colons) and "Name=John" (equals)
    # Both should detect, but dedup should keep only one Name/John pair
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r "$SAMPLES_DIR/edge-cases/dedup-overlap.txt")
    local name_count
    name_count=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'Name John' || true)
    assert_eq "1" "$name_count" "Name John should appear only once after dedup"
    local age_count
    age_count=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'Age 42' || true)
    assert_eq "1" "$age_count" "Age 42 should appear only once after dedup"
}

################################################################################
## -c flag (fully-qualified command line export)
################################################################################

test_cmdline_export () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -c -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json")
    assert_contains "$output" "--replay" "command line should contain --replay"
    assert_contains "$output" "json@" "command line should contain strategy name and version"
    assert_contains "$output" "basic.json" "command line should contain filename"
}

test_cmdline_export_with_fields () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -c -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 1,3)
    assert_contains "$output" "--replay" "should contain --replay"
    # ENV-182 routes the field-list arg through `printf '%q'` for shell
    # safety; bash %q escapes the bare comma to `\,` (defensive against
    # brace-expansion contexts), so the literal substring "1,3" is no
    # longer present even though the eval'd token is.  Strip backslashes
    # before checking for the field list.
    assert_contains "${output//\\/}" "1,3" "should contain field list"
}

################################################################################
## --replay flag
################################################################################

test_replay_basic () {
    # First extract with -c to get the command line
    local cmd_output
    cmd_output=$(run_mfe -c -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json")
    # ENV-182 changed the cmdline format from `mfe --replay 'spec' file`
    # (single-quoted) to `mfe --replay spec file` (printf %q quoting only
    # when the value contains shell-special chars Aje28094Aj `json@1.0` has none).
    # Pull out the second whitespace-separated token (the spec) directly.
    local spec
    spec=$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$cmd_output")
    # Now replay
    local replay_output
    replay_output=$(run_mfe -r --replay "$spec" "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json")
    # Should produce json results
    assert_contains "$replay_output" "STRAT-json" "replay should run json strategy"
    assert_contains "$replay_output" "name" "replay should extract name field"
}

run_test "short list flag works" test_list_strategies_short
run_test "no input produces error" test_no_input_fails
run_test "invalid file produces error" test_invalid_file_fails
run_test "unknown option produces error" test_unknown_option_fails
run_test "unknown format produces error" test_unknown_format_fails

run_test "strategy filter works" test_strategy_filter
run_test "raw output works" test_raw_output
run_test "debug output works" test_debug_output
run_test "field selection works" test_field_selection
run_test "JSON format output" test_json_format

run_test "command line export" test_cmdline_export
run_test "command line export with fields" test_cmdline_export_with_fields
run_test "replay basic" test_replay_basic

test_priority_ordering () {
    local tmpfile

    # Check that at least one strategy shows priority info

################################################################################

test_first_match () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Input that matches multiple strategies (colons + equals)
    printf 'Host: localhost\nPort: 5432\nHost=localhost\nPort=5432\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -d --first-match "$tmpfile" 2>&1)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "--first-match: stopping" "debug should confirm first-match stop"
    # Only one STRAT- prefix should appear in the output
    local strat_names
    strat_names=$(echo "$output" | grep 'STRAT-' | sed 's/.*STRAT-//;s/:.*//' | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    assert_eq "1" "$strat_names" "first-match should produce output from exactly one strategy"
}
