#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Performance Tests for Envoy:Explore (envoy-extract)
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Performance Tests"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## Large input (10K+ lines)
################################################################################

test_large_colons_input () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Generate 10,000 key: value lines
    local i=0
    while [[ $i -lt 10000 ]]; do
        echo "Field_${i}: Value_${i}" >> "$tmpfile"
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    local start_time=$SECONDS
    local rc=0
    run_mfe -s colons "$tmpfile" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    local elapsed=$((SECONDS - start_time))
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "10K lines should complete successfully"
    if [[ $elapsed -gt 60 ]]; then
        echo "  SLOW: took ${elapsed}s (limit 60s)"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_large_json_input () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    # Generate a JSON object with 1000 keys
    echo "{" > "$tmpfile"
    local i=0
    while [[ $i -lt 1000 ]]; do
        if [[ $i -gt 0 ]]; then
            echo "," >> "$tmpfile"
        fi
        printf '  "field_%d": "value_%d"' "$i" "$i" >> "$tmpfile"
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    echo "" >> "$tmpfile"
    echo "}" >> "$tmpfile"
    local start_time=$SECONDS
    local rc=0
    run_mfe -s json "$tmpfile" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    local elapsed=$((SECONDS - start_time))
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "1K JSON keys should complete successfully"
    if [[ $elapsed -gt 30 ]]; then
        echo "  SLOW: took ${elapsed}s (limit 30s)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Strategy scan benchmark
################################################################################

test_list_strategies_performance () {
    local start_time=$SECONDS
    local rc=0
    run_mfe --list-strategies >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    local elapsed=$((SECONDS - start_time))
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "list-strategies should complete successfully"
    if [[ $elapsed -gt 10 ]]; then
        echo "  SLOW: took ${elapsed}s (limit 10s)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Single-strategy fast path benchmark
################################################################################

test_single_strategy_fast_path () {
    local start_time=$SECONDS
    local rc=0
    run_mfe -s colons "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    local elapsed=$((SECONDS - start_time))
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "single strategy should complete successfully"
    if [[ $elapsed -gt 5 ]]; then
        echo "  SLOW: took ${elapsed}s (limit 5s)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Run all tests
################################################################################

run_test "large colons input (10K lines)" test_large_colons_input
run_test "large JSON input (1K keys)" test_large_json_input
run_test "list-strategies scan benchmark" test_list_strategies_performance
run_test "single-strategy fast path" test_single_strategy_fast_path

print_summary

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Plugin Directory Tests for envoy-extract
##
## Tests that --plugin-dir correctly loads strategy plugins from a custom
## directory, including detection, extraction, listing, and edge cases.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Plugin Directory Tests"
echo "========================================"

TMPDIR_P="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/plugin_dir_tests_$$"
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR_P"

################################################################################
## Helper: create a minimal plugin strategy file
################################################################################

_create_plugin () {
    local dir="$1" name="$2" marker="$3" field_name="$4" field_value="$5"
    cat > "$dir/${name}.sh" <<STRAT
#!/bin/bash
## Name: ${name}
## Description: Test plugin strategy for ${name}
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 50

strategy_detect () {
    local text="\$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=90
    echo "\$text" | grep -q '${marker}' 2>/dev/null
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="\$1"
    echo "${field_name} ${field_value}"
}
STRAT
}

################################################################################
## Plugin loaded and used for extraction
################################################################################

test_plugin_dir_basic_extraction () {
    local plugin_dir="$TMPDIR_P/basic"
    mkdir -p "$plugin_dir"
    _create_plugin "$plugin_dir" "my-plugin" "PLUGIN_BASIC" "plugin_key" "plugin_val"

    local tmpfile="$TMPDIR_P/basic_input.txt"
    printf 'PLUGIN_BASIC\nsome data\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r --plugin-dir "$plugin_dir" "$tmpfile")
    assert_contains "$output" "plugin_key" "should extract field from plugin strategy"
    assert_contains "$output" "plugin_val" "should extract value from plugin strategy"
}

################################################################################
## Plugin appears in --list-strategies output
################################################################################

test_plugin_dir_list_strategies () {
    local plugin_dir="$TMPDIR_P/list"
    mkdir -p "$plugin_dir"
    _create_plugin "$plugin_dir" "list-test-plugin" "LIST_MARKER" "f" "v"

    local output
    output=$(run_mfe --list-strategies --plugin-dir "$plugin_dir")
    assert_contains "$output" "list-test-plugin" "plugin should appear in strategy list"
}

################################################################################
## Plugin with high confidence overrides built-in strategies
################################################################################

test_plugin_dir_high_confidence () {
    local plugin_dir="$TMPDIR_P/highconf"
    mkdir -p "$plugin_dir"
    # Create a plugin that detects "Name:" patterns (same as colons) but with
    # high confidence (95) and a unique field name
    cat > "$plugin_dir/override-colons.sh" <<'STRAT'
#!/bin/bash
## Name: override-colons
## Description: Override colons with high confidence
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 5

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=95
    echo "$text" | grep -q ':' 2>/dev/null
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1"
    echo "override_field override_value"
}
STRAT

    local tmpfile="$TMPDIR_P/highconf_input.txt"

}

===FILE: extract/tests/test_progress.sh===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: ENV-135 progress indicator in envoy-extract.
##
## Pins the contract from the ticket:
##   * `--progress` forces ticks even on a non-TTY (line-per-tick).
##   * On a TTY the ticks are `\r`-rewritten in place.
##   * `--no-progress` and `ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1` suppress ticks entirely.
##   * `ENVOY_QUIET=1` and `NO_COLOR=1` suppress ticks.
##   * Stdout payload is byte-identical with vs. without progress.
##   * Below the 20-strategy threshold, default mode emits no progress
##     even on a TTY (uses the explicit `--strategy` filter to limit).
##
## We synthesise a TTY for the relevant tests via the helper's
## `ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1` test hook so the suite stays portable
## across CI environments that don't ship `script(1)` or `expect(1)`.
################################################################################
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

EE="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)/envoy-extract"
SAMPLE_INPUT='user=alice host=localhost path=/foo'

################################################################################
## --progress on a non-TTY produces line-per-tick on stderr
################################################################################

test_progress_emits_lines_on_non_tty () {
    local out err rc=0
    err=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" | bash "$EE" --progress 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "extract should still succeed with --progress"
    if ! grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\] [A-Za-z0-9_/-]+' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --progress should emit '[n/N] strategy-name' lines"
        echo "  stderr (first 200): $(printf '%s' "$err" | head -c 200)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## TTY path uses `\r` for in-place updates
################################################################################

test_progress_uses_carriage_return_on_tty () {
    local err rc=0
    # `ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1` is the documented test hook.
    err=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" \
        | ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 bash "$EE" --progress 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "extract should still succeed with TTY-forced progress"
    if [[ "$err" != *$'\r'* ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: TTY progress should contain a CR for in-place updates"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Suppression knobs
################################################################################

test_no_progress_flag_suppresses () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" \
        | ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 bash "$EE" --no-progress 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "extract should still succeed with --no-progress"
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --no-progress should suppress all '[n/N]' ticks"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_envoy_no_progress_env_suppresses () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" \
        | ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1 bash "$EE" --progress 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "extract should still succeed under ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1"
    # ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS beats --progress.
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1 should suppress ticks even with --progress"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_envoy_quiet_suppresses () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" \
        | ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 ENVOY_QUIET=1 bash "$EE" 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    # ENVOY_QUIET propagates through the suite-quiet contract.
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: ENVOY_QUIET=1 should suppress progress ticks"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_no_color_suppresses () {
    local err rc=0
    err=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" \
        | ENVOY_PROGRESS_FORCE_TTY=1 NO_COLOR=1 bash "$EE" --progress 2>&1 >/dev/null) || rc=$?
    if grep -qE '^\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]' <<< "$err"; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: NO_COLOR=1 should suppress progress (decorative output)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Stdout payload is byte-identical with / without progress
################################################################################

test_progress_does_not_alter_stdout () {
    local with without
    with=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" | bash "$EE" --progress 2>/dev/null)
    without=$(printf '%s' "$SAMPLE_INPUT" | bash "$EE" --no-progress 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ "$with" != "$without" ]]; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --progress changed stdout payload"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## --help advertises the flags
################################################################################

test_help_documents_progress () {
    local out
    out=$(bash "$EE" --help 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "--progress" "--help must advertise --progress"
    assert_contains "$out" "--no-progress" "--help must advertise --no-progress"
}

run_test "ENV-135 --progress emits [n/N] lines on stderr (non-TTY)" test_progress_emits_lines_on_non_tty
run_test "ENV-135 TTY progress uses carriage return for in-place" test_progress_uses_carriage_return_on_tty
run_test "ENV-135 --no-progress suppresses ticks" test_no_progress_flag_suppresses
run_test "ENV-135 ENVOY_NO_PROGRESS=1 beats --progress" test_envoy_no_progress_env_suppresses
run_test "ENV-135 ENVOY_QUIET=1 suppresses progress" test_envoy_quiet_suppresses
run_test "ENV-135 NO_COLOR=1 suppresses progress" test_no_color_suppresses
run_test "ENV-135 --progress does not alter stdout payload" test_progress_does_not_alter_stdout
run_test "ENV-135 --help advertises --progress / --no-progress" test_help_documents_progress

print_summary
===END===
===FILE-ESC: extract/tests/test_quote_json_glob_sed.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=301cb5dccc0a823cf65a74580a6ce08674d4cedd3a6f4f9649120506e71e01bb===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for ENV-172 Aje28094Aj EnvoyExtract: _quote_arg backslash, JSON key/value
##                     escape consistency, --chain/--rename glob expansion,
##                     sed-escape gaps in apply_renames.
##
## Sub-bug 1: _build.sh:267. The `_quote_arg` double-quote branch had
##   `case "$ch" in '\'*) ... esac` Aje28094Aj a multi-character pattern that
##   never matched the single-character $ch. Backslashes leaked through
##   unescaped, so the produced double-quoted shell-replay string then
##   re-interpreted whatever followed the backslash on replay.
##
## Sub-bug 2: _build.sh:121-132 vs 159-179. The JSON decoder translated
##   `\n` `\t` `\r` (and `\\` `\"` etc.) inside string values, but the
##   in_key branch just appended `_ch` after `_in_escape=1` Aje28094Aj keys with
##   escape sequences ended up holding the raw backslash + char pair.
##
## Sub-bug 3: _discovery.sh:198 and _postprocess.sh:65. `for cs in
##   $_OPT_chain` and `for pair in $renames` were unquoted. With
##   `IFS='|'` (or `,`) the variable word-split correctly, but bash
##   ALSO glob-expanded the unquoted variable against CWD before the
##   loop iterated Aje28094Aj `--chain '*.sh'` resolved to whatever `*.sh`
##   files were sitting in the cwd.
##
## Sub-bug 4: _postprocess.sh:71. The pattern-side bracket class
##   `[.[\/*^$]` missed `]` (would close the class). The replacement-
##   side class `[\/&]` missed `\`. A field name containing `]` or a
##   replacement containing a literal backslash produced a malformed
##   sed script and aborted the pipeline.
##
## We pin:
##   - _quote_arg over a string that contains both `'` and `\` produces
##     a double-quoted form where backslashes are escaped, so the
##     replay round-trip preserves the original byte sequence.
##   - JSON decoder treats `"a\nb"` identically as a key and as a value
##     (both yield 3-char string `a<NL>b`).
##   - --chain '*.sh' invocation does NOT glob-expand against CWD
##     (the chain list contains literal `*.sh` rather than filenames).
##   - --rename with a name containing `]` produces a valid sed script
##     and the pipeline doesn't abort.
##   - drift guards on each fix.
################################################################################

set -u

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
EX_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
EX_DISCOVERY="$EX_DIR/lib/_discovery.sh"
EX_POSTPROCESS="$EX_DIR/lib/_postprocess.sh"

PASS=0
FAIL=0
_pass () { PASS=$((PASS+1)); printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
_fail () { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf '  FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2; if [[ -n "${2:-}" ]]; then printf '    %s\n' "$2" >&2; fi; }

WORK=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/env172_test.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "ENV-172: extract glob + sed escape"
echo "========================================"

###############################################################################
# Section C Aje28094Aj --chain glob expansion
###############################################################################

# Drop a sentinel `*.sh` file in WORK then run envoy-extract with
# `--chain '*.sh'`. Pre-fix the loop would have iterated over each
# matched filename; post-fix the chain list contains the LITERAL
# `*.sh` (which won't match any real strategy and so produces a
# clean "strategy not found" path).
mkdir -p "$WORK/cwd"
touch "$WORK/cwd/sentinel.sh" "$WORK/cwd/another.sh"
EX_BIN="$EX_DIR/envoy-extract"
out=$(cd "$WORK/cwd" && bash "$EX_BIN" --chain '*.sh' /dev/null 2>&1) || true
# Pre-fix the chain would have contained "sentinel.sh" / "another.sh"
# expansions. Post-fix the chain only contains the literal `*.sh`.
if grep -qE 'sentinel\.sh|another\.sh' <<< "$out"; then
    _fail "drift: --chain '*.sh' was glob-expanded against CWD" "$out"
else
    _pass "--chain '*.sh' is taken literally (no CWD glob expansion)"
fi

# Drift: live code uses `read -r -a` for chain split, not `for cs in
# $_OPT_chain`.
if grep -qE 'read -r -a _chain_arr' "$EX_DISCOVERY"; then
    _pass "drift: _discovery.sh uses read -r -a for the chain split"
else
    _fail "drift: _discovery.sh missing read -r -a for chain"
fi

###############################################################################
# Section D Aje28094Aj --rename sed-escape with `]` in field name
###############################################################################

# We exercise apply_renames directly. It requires the input on stdin-like
# stream Aje28094Aj the function takes `input` and `renames` strings and returns
# the rewritten table on stdout. Define _OPT_rename or simulate via
# sourcing.
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$EX_POSTPROCESS"
input=$'header\nSTRAT-x\tname[bracket] hello\nSTRAT-x\tnormal world\n'
out=$(apply_renames "$input" 'name[bracket]=plain')
if grep -qF 'plain hello' <<< "$out"; then
    _pass "apply_renames: field name with ']' is escaped + renamed correctly"
else
    _fail "apply_renames: ']' in field name didn't round-trip" "$out"
fi

# Drift: pattern class lists `]` first.
if grep -qE "sed 's/\\[\\]\\.\\[" "$EX_POSTPROCESS"; then
    _pass "drift: _postprocess.sh pattern-side class lists ] first"
else
    _fail "drift: pattern-side ']'-first form missing"
fi

# Drift: replacement class lists \\.
if grep -qE "sed 's/\\[\\\\\\\\/&\\]/" "$EX_POSTPROCESS"; then
    _pass "drift: _postprocess.sh replacement-side class includes \\\\"
else
    _fail "drift: replacement-side \\\\ inclusion missing"
fi

# Drift: rename loop uses read -r -a.
if grep -qE 'read -r -a _renames_arr' "$EX_POSTPROCESS"; then
    _pass "drift: _postprocess.sh uses read -r -a for renames split"
else
    _fail "drift: _postprocess.sh missing read -r -a"
fi

###############################################################################

echo ""
echo "========================================"
printf 'Results: %d/%d passed, %d failed\n' "$PASS" "$((PASS+FAIL))" "$FAIL"
if [[ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "========================================"
    exit 1
fi
echo "All tests passed."
echo "========================================"
===END===

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Replay Tests for Envoy:Explore (envoy-extract)
##
## Tests the --replay flag and -c (command line export) round-tripping
## including error handling for malformed and empty replay specs.
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Replay Tests"
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## Non-existent strategy in replay spec
################################################################################

test_replay_nonexistent_strategy () {
    # Replaying a strategy that doesn't exist should produce no output (exits 0)
    # because the strategy loop simply skips it when it's not in the sorted list.
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r --replay 'nonexistent_strategy@1.0' "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Should not crash; exit 0 with no output is acceptable
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Malformed spec (no @version)
################################################################################

test_replay_malformed_no_version () {
    # A replay spec without @version should still work; the sed strips @...
    # leaving just the strategy name which gets matched in the loop.
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r --replay 'json' "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "replay without @version should not crash"
    # The strategy name 'json' should still be recognized
    assert_contains "$output" "STRAT-json" "should still run the json strategy"
}

################################################################################
## Empty spec
################################################################################

test_replay_empty_spec () {
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe --replay '' "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Empty spec means no strategies match the replay filter; should exit cleanly
    if [[ $rc -le 1 ]]; then
        return 0
    else
        echo "  exit code was $rc (expected 0 or 1)"
        return 1
    fi
}

################################################################################
## Round-trip -c -> --replay identity
################################################################################

test_replay_roundtrip () {
    # Run once with -c to get the export command
    local cmd_output
    cmd_output=$(run_mfe -c -s colons "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt")
    # Extract the replay spec Aje28094Aj third whitespace-separated token after
    # `mfe --replay`.  ENV-182 dropped the legacy single-quotes in favour
    # of printf %q, which leaves single-token specs like `colons@1.0`
    # unquoted; the old sed pattern relied on the quotes and silently
    # passed the entire cmdline through as the "spec".
    local spec
    spec=$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$cmd_output")
    # Run original extraction with raw output
    local original
    original=$(run_mfe -r -s colons "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt")
    # Run replay with same spec
    local replay_output
    replay_output=$(run_mfe -r --replay "$spec" "$SAMPLES_DIR/colons/basic.txt")
    # Both should extract the same field names
    local orig_fields replay_fields
    orig_fields=$(echo "$original" | sed '/^$/d' | awk '{
        idx = index($0, "\t")
        if (idx > 0) print substr($0, idx + 1)
        else print
    }' | sort)
    replay_fields=$(echo "$replay_output" | sed '/^$/d' | awk '{
        idx = index($0, "\t")
        if (idx > 0) print substr($0, idx + 1)
        else print
    }' | sort)
    assert_eq "$orig_fields" "$replay_fields" "replay should produce same fields as original"
}

################################################################################
## Replay version enforcement
################################################################################

test_replay_matching_version () {
    # Replay with the correct version should produce no warning
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r --replay 'json@1.0' "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Should NOT contain version mismatch warning
    if [[ "$output" == *"version mismatch"* ]]; then
        echo "  unexpected version mismatch warning"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

test_replay_mismatched_version () {
    # Replay with a wrong version should warn on stderr
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r --replay 'json@9.9' "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$output" "version mismatch" "should warn about version mismatch"
    assert_contains "$output" "requested: 9.9" "should show requested version"
    assert_contains "$output" "installed: 1.0" "should show installed version"
}

test_replay_no_version_in_spec () {
    # Replay without version should produce no warning
    local output rc=0
    output=$(run_mfe -r --replay 'json' "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    if [[ "$output" == *"version mismatch"* ]]; then
        echo "  unexpected version mismatch warning"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

################################################################################
## Run all tests
################################################################################

run_test "replay: non-existent strategy in spec" test_replay_nonexistent_strategy
run_test "replay: malformed spec without @version" test_replay_malformed_no_version
run_test "replay: empty spec" test_replay_empty_spec
run_test "replay: round-trip -c -> --replay identity" test_replay_roundtrip
run_test "replay: matching version (no warning)" test_replay_matching_version
run_test "replay: mismatched version (warning)" test_replay_mismatched_version
run_test "replay: no version in spec (no warning)" test_replay_no_version_in_spec

print_summary

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: envoy-extract search subcommand (ENV-016)
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "=== Search Subcommand Tests (ENV-016) ==="

test_search_finds_json () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe search json 2>&1 || true)
    assert_contains "$out" "json" "should find json strategies"
    assert_contains "$out" "structured" "should show json's category"
}

test_search_case_insensitive_default () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe search JSON 2>&1 || true)
    assert_contains "$out" "json" "uppercase JSON should still find json strategy (case-insensitive default)"
}

test_search_case_sensitive_flag_requires_exact_case () {
    # Without --case-sensitive, JSONL (uppercase) matches the jsonl strategy.
    # With --case-sensitive, JSONL should only match strategies whose metadata
    # literally contains the uppercase substring.
    local insensitive_has_jsonl sensitive_has_jsonl
    insensitive_has_jsonl=$(run_mfe search JSONL 2>&1 || true)
    sensitive_has_jsonl=$(run_mfe search --case-sensitive JSONL 2>&1 || true)
    # Sanity: case-insensitive run finds jsonl
    if ! echo "$insensitive_has_jsonl" | grep -q "^  structured     jsonl "; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: case-insensitive JSONL search should find jsonl strategy"
        return 1
    fi
    # With --case-sensitive, jsonl (lowercase strategy name) should NOT match
    # because no metadata field literally contains uppercase "JSONL".
    if echo "$sensitive_has_jsonl" | grep -q "^  structured     jsonl "; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --case-sensitive JSONL should not match lowercase jsonl strategy"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_search_category_narrows_results () {
    local out
    # Search for csv, without category restriction vs with "structured" restriction
    local all_out struct_out
    all_out=$(run_mfe search csv 2>&1 || true)
    struct_out=$(run_mfe search --category structured csv 2>&1 || true)
    # Both should contain the structured/csv strategy
    assert_contains "$struct_out" "csv" "category-filtered search should include csv"
    # Filtered output should have <= lines as unfiltered (narrowed set)
    local all_lines struct_lines
    all_lines=$(echo "$all_out" | wc -l)
    struct_lines=$(echo "$struct_out" | wc -l)
    [[ "$struct_lines" -le "$all_lines" ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: --category should narrow results"; return 1; }
}

test_search_multiple_keywords_and_semantics () {
    local out
    # Find strategies with both "docker" and "stats" in metadata (AND)
    out=$(run_mfe search docker stats 2>&1 || true)
    assert_contains "$out" "docker-stats" "AND of docker+stats should find docker-stats"
    # "docker ps" strategy lacks "stats" Aje28094Aj should not appear
    if echo "$out" | grep -q "^  container      docker-ps "; then
        echo "  ASSERT FAILED: docker-ps should not match 'docker stats' (AND semantics)"
        return 1
    fi
}

test_search_no_args_lists_all () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe search 2>&1 || true)
    # Should have header + many rows (at least 50)
    local lines
    lines=$(echo "$out" | grep -c "^  ")
    [[ "$lines" -ge 50 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: empty search should list all strategies (got $lines rows)"; return 1; }
}

test_search_no_match_exits_1 () {
    local rc=0
    run_mfe search xyzzy-nonexistent-strategy >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    [[ "$rc" -eq 1 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: no-match should exit 1 (got $rc)"; return 1; }
}

test_search_match_exits_0 () {
    local rc=0
    run_mfe search json >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
    [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: match should exit 0 (got $rc)"; return 1; }
}

run_test "search: finds json strategies" test_search_finds_json
run_test "search: case-insensitive by default" test_search_case_insensitive_default
run_test "search: --case-sensitive requires exact case" test_search_case_sensitive_flag_requires_exact_case
run_test "search: --category narrows results" test_search_category_narrows_results
run_test "search: multiple keywords use AND semantics" test_search_multiple_keywords_and_semantics
run_test "search: no args lists all strategies" test_search_no_args_lists_all
run_test "search: no match exits 1" test_search_no_match_exits_1
run_test "search: match exits 0" test_search_match_exits_0

print_summary

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: envoy-extract validate-strategies (ENV-018)
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "=== Strategy Self-Validation Tests (ENV-018) ==="

test_self_validate_single_strategy_passes () {
    # json strategy has a real sample file and a very high-confidence detector.
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe validate-strategies -s json 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "json" "should mention the json strategy"
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS" "json should pass at threshold 75"
    [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: single-strategy PASS should exit 0 (got $rc)"; return 1; }
}

test_self_validate_threshold_flag () {
    # At threshold 100, json (conf ~95) should fall below.
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe validate-strategies --threshold 100 -s json 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "BELOW" "json should be BELOW at threshold 100"
    [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: below-threshold should exit nonzero"; return 1; }
}

test_self_validate_missing_sample_reported () {
    # Find a strategy whose sample file is missing (there are many in the
    # scientific/hpc/etc. folders). We pick one and verify the report.
    local out rc=0
    # Any of the scientific strategies without sample files work; try fits-header.
    out=$(run_mfe validate-strategies -s fits-header 2>&1) || rc=$?
    if echo "$out" | grep -q "MISSING"; then
        # Good Aje28094Aj confirms MISSING detection
        :
    else
        # If fits-header's sample has been added since, skip rather than fail;
        # the machinery itself is tested by other assertions.
        return 0
    fi
    [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: missing sample should cause nonzero exit"; return 1; }
}

test_self_validate_all_prints_summary () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe validate-strategies 2>&1 || true)
    assert_contains "$out" "Self-validation:" "should print summary header"
    assert_contains "$out" "pass" "summary line should include pass count"
    assert_contains "$out" "below threshold" "summary line should include below-threshold count"
}

test_self_validate_unknown_strategy_filter () {
    # Filter to a non-existent strategy name: nothing to validate.
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe validate-strategies -s zzz_nonexistent 2>&1) || rc=$?
    # Summary should show 0 total
    assert_contains "$out" "0 total" "unknown filter should show 0 total"
    [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: 0 total should exit 0"; return 1; }
}

run_test "self-validate: single strategy passes at threshold 75" test_self_validate_single_strategy_passes
run_test "self-validate: --threshold 100 puts most strategies below" test_self_validate_threshold_flag
run_test "self-validate: missing sample file reported" test_self_validate_missing_sample_reported
run_test "self-validate: overall summary is printed" test_self_validate_all_prints_summary
run_test "self-validate: unknown -s filter yields 0 total, exit 0" test_self_validate_unknown_strategy_filter

print_summary

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Snapshot Regression Tests for envoy-extract
##
## Runs mfe against representative samples and verifies exact output.
## This is a safety net for refactoring -- if any output changes unexpectedly,
## these tests will catch it.
################################################################################

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/helpers.sh"

# Generate a snapshot: run mfe with raw output (-r) and a specific strategy (-s)
# to get deterministic, reproducible output.
snapshot () {
    local strategy="$1"
    local sample="$2"
    run_mfe -r -s "$strategy" "$SAMPLES_DIR/$sample" 2>/dev/null
}

################################################################################
## Structured formats
################################################################################

test_snapshot_json () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot json json/basic.json)
    assert_contains "$out" "name " "json: should have name field"
    assert_contains "$out" "version " "json: should have version field"
    # Verify field count is stable
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "json: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}

test_snapshot_yaml () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot yaml yaml/basic.yaml)
    assert_contains "$out" "name " "yaml: should have name field"
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "yaml: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}

test_snapshot_csv () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot csv csv/basic.csv)
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "csv: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}


test_snapshot_toml () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot toml toml/basic.toml)
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "toml: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}

################################################################################
## Delimited formats
################################################################################

test_snapshot_colons () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot colons colons/basic.txt)
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "colons: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}

test_snapshot_equals () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot equals equals/basic.txt)
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "equals: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}


################################################################################
## Benchmark formats
################################################################################



################################################################################
## System formats
################################################################################


################################################################################
## Network/container formats
################################################################################

test_snapshot_nmap () {
    local out
    out=$(snapshot nmap nmap/basic.txt)
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "nmap: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}

## Logging format
################################################################################

    local out
    out=$(snapshot syslog syslog/basic.txt)
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    [[ $count -gt 0 ]] || { echo "syslog: no fields extracted"; return 1; }
}

################################################################################
## Output format tests (same input, different output formats)
################################################################################

test_snapshot_json_format () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe -s json --format json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>/dev/null)
    assert_json_valid "$out" "json format should produce valid JSON"
}

test_snapshot_csv_format () {
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe -s json --format csv "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>/dev/null)

test_aligned_columns_ps () {

    output=$(run_mfe -r -s aligned-columns "$SAMPLES_DIR/aligned-columns/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "PID" "should extract PID column"
    assert_contains "$output" "USER" "should extract USER column"
    assert_contains "$output" "CPU" "should extract CPU column"
    assert_contains "$output" "MEM" "should extract MEM column"
    assert_contains "$output" "COMMAND" "should extract COMMAND column"
    assert_contains "$output" "123" "should extract PID value 123"
    assert_contains "$output" "root" "should extract USER value root"
}

# v2.0: each data line is an indexed row group (entry<N>.<field>) so the
# capture tidy melt turns it into one row per line, not a single wide record.
test_aligned_columns_row_groups () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s aligned-columns "$SAMPLES_DIR/aligned-columns/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.PID 123" "row 1 grouped under entry1"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.USER www" "row 2 grouped under entry2"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry3.COMMAND postgres" "row 3 grouped under entry3"
    assert_contains "$output" "total_entries 3" "three rows"
}

################################################################################
## df-style output extraction
################################################################################

test_aligned_columns_df () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Filesystem  Size  Used  Avail  Use%%  Mounted\n/dev/sda1   50G   30G   20G    60%%  /\ntmpfs       4G    0G    4G     0%%   /tmp\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s aligned-columns "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "Filesystem" "should extract Filesystem column"
    assert_contains "$output" "Size" "should extract Size column"
    assert_contains "$output" "/dev/sda1" "should extract filesystem value"
    assert_contains "$output" "50G" "should extract size value"
}

################################################################################
## Not detected for JSON
################################################################################

test_aligned_columns_not_json () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s aligned-columns "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "aligned-columns should not apply to JSON"
}

################################################################################
## Run all tests
################################################################################

run_test "aligned-columns: ps-style extraction" test_aligned_columns_ps
run_test "aligned-columns: indexed row groups" test_aligned_columns_row_groups
run_test "aligned-columns: df-style extraction" test_aligned_columns_df

    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s block-records "$SAMPLES_DIR/blank-line-records/basic.txt")

    assert_contains "$output" "record1.IP 10.0.0.1" "should extract record1 IP"

test_csv_quoted_fields () {

    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Name,City\n"Smith, John","New York"\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s csv "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "Name" "should extract Name"
    assert_contains "$output" "Smith, John" "should handle quoted commas"

    output=$(run_mfe -d -s csv "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "csv should not apply to JSON"
}

test_csv_trims_whitespace_after_comma () {
    # Values after a ", " delimiter must be trimmed like the header fields are Aje28094Aj
    # the leading space must not become a leading underscore (`_b=6`).
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'a=1, b=2, c=3\na=5, b=6, c=7\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s csv "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "a=1 a=5" "value should be clean"
    assert_contains "$output" "b=2 b=6" "value after ', ' must not gain a leading underscore"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "_b=6" "no leading underscore from the delimiter space"
}

# v2.0: each data row is an indexed record group (entry<N>.<col>) so the capture
# tidy melt renders one row per record Aje28094Aj not one wide row with duplicate columns.
test_csv_rows_are_indexed_records () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s csv "$SAMPLES_DIR/csv/employees.csv")
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.name Alice Johnson" "row 1 under entry1"

#!/bin/bash

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

test_equals_basic () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s equals "$SAMPLES_DIR/equals/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "USER" "should extract USER"
    assert_contains "$output" "jdoe" "should extract value jdoe"
    assert_contains "$output" "HOME" "should extract HOME"
    assert_contains "$output" "SHELL" "should extract SHELL"
}

test_equals_field_selection () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -s equals "$SAMPLES_DIR/equals/basic.txt" 1,2)
    assert_contains "$output" "USER" "should contain USER"
    assert_contains "$output" "HOME" "should contain HOME"
}

test_equals_skips_comparisons () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf "NAME=test\nif x == y then\na += b\nx != y\n" > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s equals "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "NAME" "should extract NAME"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "==" "should skip comparisons"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "+=" "should skip augmented assignments"
}

test_equals_json_format () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -s equals -f json "$SAMPLES_DIR/equals/basic.txt" 1,2)
    assert_contains "$output" '"USER":' "JSON should have USER key"
    assert_contains "$output" '"HOME":' "JSON should have HOME key"
}

run_test "equals: basic extraction" test_equals_basic
run_test "equals: field selection" test_equals_field_selection
run_test "equals: skips comparisons" test_equals_skips_comparisons
run_test "equals: JSON format output" test_equals_json_format

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Strategy Tests: exposition-format
## Consolidates tests from: prometheus, openmetrics
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Strategy Tests: exposition-format"
echo "========================================"

# --- prometheus cases ---

test_ef_prometheus_basic () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$SAMPLES_DIR/prometheus/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.name http_requests_total" "should extract first metric name"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.value 1027" "should extract first metric value"
    assert_contains "$output" 'metric1.labels method="post",code="200"' "should extract labels"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric2.name http_requests_total" "should extract second metric name"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric2.value 3" "should extract second metric value"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric3.name process_cpu_seconds_total" "should extract bare metric name"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric3.value 0.52" "should extract bare metric value"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric4.name go_goroutines" "should extract gauge metric name"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric4.value 33" "should extract gauge metric value"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "metric3.labels" "bare metric should not have labels"
}

test_ef_prometheus_metadata () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$SAMPLES_DIR/prometheus/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total.help The total number of HTTP requests." "should extract help text"
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total.type counter" "should extract type"
    assert_contains "$output" "process_cpu_seconds_total.type counter" "should extract cpu type"
    assert_contains "$output" "go_goroutines.type gauge" "should extract gauge type"
    assert_contains "$output" "go_goroutines.help Number of goroutines that currently exist." "should extract goroutines help"
}

# --- openmetrics cases ---

test_ef_openmetrics_basic () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$SAMPLES_DIR/openmetrics/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total.type counter" "should extract type"
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total.unit requests" "should extract unit"
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total.help Total HTTP requests" "should extract help"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.name http_requests_total" "should extract metric1 name"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.value 1234" "should extract metric1 value"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric4.name process_cpu_seconds_total" "should extract process cpu metric"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric4.value 456.78" "should extract process cpu value"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric8.name http_request_duration_seconds_count" "should extract histogram count"
}

# --- rejection tests ---

test_ef_not_detected_for_json () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"key": "value", "count": 42}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s exposition-format "$tmpfile" 2>&1)
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "exposition-format should not apply to JSON"
}

test_ef_detects_prometheus_format () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '# TYPE http_requests_total counter\nhttp_requests_total 100\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "http_requests_total.type counter" "should detect and extract Prometheus format"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.name http_requests_total" "should extract metric name"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.value 100" "should extract metric value"
}

test_ef_detects_openmetrics_eof () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '# TYPE requests counter\nrequests_total 42\n# EOF\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s exposition-format "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "requests.type counter" "should extract type from OpenMetrics"
    assert_contains "$output" "metric1.value 42" "should extract metric value"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "# EOF" "should not emit EOF line as a field"
}

run_test "exposition-format: Prometheus basic extraction" test_ef_prometheus_basic
run_test "exposition-format: Prometheus help/type metadata" test_ef_prometheus_metadata
run_test "exposition-format: OpenMetrics basic extraction" test_ef_openmetrics_basic
run_test "exposition-format: not detected for JSON" test_ef_not_detected_for_json
run_test "exposition-format: detects Prometheus format" test_ef_detects_prometheus_format
run_test "exposition-format: detects OpenMetrics EOF" test_ef_detects_openmetrics_eof

===FILE: extract/tests/test_strategy_free.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=bd0aec621c2359c0c8a800bbe72a1cfddbd928ba94dad9802497ddb7b607321c===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Strategy Tests: free
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Strategy Tests: free"
echo "========================================"

test_detect () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s free "$SAMPLES_DIR/free/basic.txt" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "detected as applicable" "free should detect free -h output"
}

test_extract () {
    # v2.0: `free` is emitted as indexed row groups (entry<N>.<field>) so the
    # capture-side tidy melt turns it into one row per region with shared
    # columns, rather than one wide Mem_*/Swap_* record.
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s free "$SAMPLES_DIR/free/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.name Mem" "row 1 is the Mem region"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.total 15Gi" "Mem total"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.used 8.2Gi" "Mem used"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.free 1.5Gi" "Mem free"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.shared 512Mi" "Mem shared"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.buff_cache 5.8Gi" "Mem buff/cache -> buff_cache field"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.available 6.5Gi" "Mem available"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.name Swap" "row 2 is the Swap region"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.total 4.0Gi" "Swap total"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.used 1.2Gi" "Swap used"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.free 2.8Gi" "Swap free"
    assert_contains "$output" "total_entries 2" "two regions"
}

test_field_selection () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s free "$SAMPLES_DIR/free/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.total" "should have a total field"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.free" "should have a Swap free field"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "buffers" "should not have raw buffers field"
}

# Swap has no shared/buff_cache/available columns; those must not be
# fabricated for the Swap region.
test_swap_has_no_trailing_columns () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s free "$SAMPLES_DIR/free/basic.txt")
    assert_not_contains "$output" "entry2.shared" "Swap row must not invent a shared value"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "entry2.available" "Swap row must not invent an available value"
}

run_test "free: detection" test_detect
run_test "free: extraction" test_extract
run_test "free: field selection" test_field_selection
run_test "free: swap has no trailing columns" test_swap_has_no_trailing_columns

print_summary
===END===

    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"host": "web-01", "status": "up"}\n{"host": "web-02", "status": "down"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s jsonl "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    assert_contains "$output" "host" "should extract host field"
    assert_contains "$output" "web-01" "should extract value web-01"
    assert_contains "$output" "status" "should extract status field"
    assert_contains "$output" "up" "should extract value up"
    assert_contains "$output" "web-02" "should extract value web-02"
}

################################################################################
## Multiple fields per line
################################################################################

test_jsonl_multiple_fields () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf '{"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "city": "Boston"}\n{"name": "Bob", "age": 25, "city": "NYC"}\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s jsonl "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # JSONL strategy prefixes with lineN.fieldname
    assert_contains "$output" "line1.name" "should prefix line1 for first record"
    assert_contains "$output" "line2.name" "should prefix line2 for second record"
    assert_contains "$output" "Alice" "should extract Alice"
    assert_contains "$output" "Bob" "should extract Bob"
    assert_contains "$output" "city" "should extract city field"
}

################################################################################

################################################################################

test_jsonl_not_for_json_object () {

    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "jsonl should not apply to regular JSON object"
}

test_jsonl_not_for_plain_text () {

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Strategy Tests: key-value (generic aligned "Label:  value" listings)
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Strategy Tests: key-value"
echo "========================================"

test_detect () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s key-value "$SAMPLES_DIR/key-value/basic.txt" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "detected as applicable" "key-value should detect aligned Label: value listings"
}

# Each pair becomes an indexed row group (entry<N>.key / entry<N>.value) so the
# capture tidy melt renders a two-column key/value table Aje28094Aj one row per property.
test_extract () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s key-value "$SAMPLES_DIR/key-value/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.key Architecture" "first key"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.value x86_64" "first value"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.key CPU op-mode(s)" "multi-word key preserved"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry8.value AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor" "value with spaces preserved"
    assert_contains "$output" "total_entries 15" "fifteen properties"
}

# Wrapped continuation lines (no colon) fold into the previous value.
test_wrapped_value () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s key-value "$SAMPLES_DIR/key-value/basic.txt")
    assert_contains "$output" "entry12.value fpu vme de pse" "Flags value starts correctly"
    assert_contains "$output" "clflush mmx fxsr sse sse2" "wrapped continuation folded into the value"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "entry13.key pge" "continuation line must not become its own key"
}

# A value that itself contains a colon splits on the FIRST colon only.
test_value_with_colon () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Spec rstack overflow:      Vulnerable: Safe RET, no microcode\n' > "$tmp"
    printf 'Model name:                AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor\n' >> "$tmp"
    printf 'Byte Order:                Little Endian\n' >> "$tmp"
    printf 'Vendor ID:                 AuthenticAMD\n' >> "$tmp"
    printf 'CPU family:                25\n' >> "$tmp"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s key-value "$tmp")
    rm -f "$tmp"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.key Spec rstack overflow" "key stops at first colon"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.value Vulnerable: Safe RET, no microcode" "value keeps its inner colon"
}

# Must NOT steal compact YAML or JSON (those go to their own strategies).
test_not_yaml () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s key-value "$SAMPLES_DIR/yaml/basic.yaml" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "key-value should not match compact YAML"
}

test_not_json () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s key-value "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "key-value should not match JSON"
}

run_test "key-value: detection" test_detect
run_test "key-value: extraction" test_extract
run_test "key-value: wrapped continuation values" test_wrapped_value
run_test "key-value: value with inner colon" test_value_with_colon
run_test "key-value: not confused with YAML" test_not_yaml
run_test "key-value: not confused with JSON" test_not_json

print_summary

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Strategy Tests: kv-pairs
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "Strategy Tests: kv-pairs"
echo "========================================"

test_kv_pairs_comma_separated () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s kv-pairs "$SAMPLES_DIR/kv-pairs/basic.txt")
    # Each line is a record -> entry<N>.<key> groups (which the capture-side
    # tidy melt later turns into one row per line).
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.a 1" "record 1, key a"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.b 2" "record 1, key b"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.a 5" "record 2, key a"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.c 7" "record 2, key c"
    assert_contains "$output" "total_entries 2" "two records"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "_b" "no leading underscore from the ', ' delimiter"
}

test_kv_pairs_space_separated () {
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf 'x=10 y=20 z=30\nx=40 y=50 z=60\n' > "$tmp"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -r -s kv-pairs "$tmp")
    rm -f "$tmp"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry1.x 10" "space-separated pairs parse"
    assert_contains "$output" "entry2.z 60" "second record"
}

test_kv_pairs_not_single_pair_lines () {
    # One pair per line is a different shape (config/.env) Aje28094Aj must not match.
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf 'a=1\nb=2\nc=3\n' > "$tmp"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s kv-pairs "$tmp" 2>&1)
    rm -f "$tmp"
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "single pair per line should not match kv-pairs"
}

test_kv_pairs_not_plain_csv () {
    # Bare CSV (no '=') is not kv-pairs.
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -d -s kv-pairs "$SAMPLES_DIR/csv/basic.csv" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$output" "not applicable" "plain CSV should not match kv-pairs"
}

run_test "kv-pairs: comma-separated records" test_kv_pairs_comma_separated
run_test "kv-pairs: space-separated records" test_kv_pairs_space_separated
run_test "kv-pairs: single-pair lines not matched" test_kv_pairs_not_single_pair_lines
run_test "kv-pairs: plain CSV not matched" test_kv_pairs_not_plain_csv

print_summary

===FILE-ESC: extract/tests/test_streaming_multiline.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=7e7b226f3093ac6439d854d5657bd4f803a365258a4fc267044ad19e35a9244c===
#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for: streaming multi-line records (ENV-019)
##
## Exercises stream mode against inputs where records span multiple lines:
## multi-line JSON objects, stack traces, multi-line SQL. Uses --record-boundary
## to opt into multi-line record assembly.
################################################################################
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo "=== Streaming Multi-Line Record Tests (ENV-019) ==="

# Multi-line JSON objects, 2 records.
test_multiline_json_via_record_boundary () {
    local input='{
  "user": "alice",
  "action": "login"
}
{
  "user": "bob",
  "action": "logout"
}'
    local out
    # Use opening brace at column 0 as the record boundary.
    out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | run_mfe stream --strategy json --record-boundary '^\{$')
    # Expect 2 JSON-Lines output records
    local count
    count=$(echo "$out" | grep -c '"user"' || echo 0)
    [[ "$count" -eq 2 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: expected 2 records, got $count (out=$out)"; return 1; }
    # Both users present
    assert_contains "$out" "alice" "alice should appear in streamed output"
    assert_contains "$out" "bob" "bob should appear in streamed output"
}

# Without --record-boundary, multi-line JSON degrades to line-per-record.
# Each line is passed to strategy_extract separately, so the output is
# garbled for multi-line objects Aje28094Aj that's the motivation for ENV-019. This
# test just pins that the invocation still produces *some* valid JSON Lines
# output and does not crash, so callers don't rely on accidental behavior.
test_multiline_json_without_boundary_emits_something () {
    local input='{
  "user": "alice"
}'
    local out rc=0
    out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | run_mfe stream --strategy json 2>&1) || rc=$?
    [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: stream mode should exit 0"; return 1; }
    # Output should contain at least one JSON Lines record (one `{`)
    local lines
    lines=$(echo "$out" | grep -c '^{' || echo 0)
    [[ "$lines" -ge 1 ]] || { echo "  ASSERT FAILED: expected at least one JSON-Lines row, got $lines"; return 1; }
}

# Single-record pipeline should still work cleanly when --record-boundary does not match.
test_single_record_with_unused_boundary () {
    local input='{"user":"carol","action":"login"}'
    local out
    out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | run_mfe stream --strategy json --record-boundary '^NOT_PRESENT$')
    assert_contains "$out" "carol" "single-line record should still be processed"
}

# Flush-on-EOF: a record without a trailing boundary should still be emitted.
test_record_flushed_on_eof () {
    local input='{
  "user": "dave"
}'
    local out
    out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | run_mfe stream --strategy json --record-boundary '^\{$')
    assert_contains "$out" "dave" "EOF should flush the buffered record"
}

run_test "multi-line JSON via --record-boundary emits 2 records" test_multiline_json_via_record_boundary
run_test "default stream mode emits valid output (no crash regression)" test_multiline_json_without_boundary_emits_something
run_test "single-record input with unused boundary still works" test_single_record_with_unused_boundary
run_test "buffered record at EOF is flushed" test_record_flushed_on_eof

print_summary
===END===

################################################################################

source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/helpers.sh"

TMPDIR_TEST="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/envoy_tools_test_$$"
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR_TEST"

cleanup () {
    rm -rf "$TMPDIR_TEST"
    # Clean up any scaffolded test strategies
    rm -rf "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/strategies/misc/test-tool-scaffold.sh"
    rm -rf "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/samples/test-tool-scaffold"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

################################################################################

test_new_strategy_help () {

    assert_contains "$out" "--name" "help should mention --name"
    assert_contains "$out" "--category" "help should mention --category"
    assert_contains "$out" "--sample" "help should mention --sample"
}

    bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should fail without args"
}

    local rc=0
    bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" --name foo --category misc --sample /nonexistent/file 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should fail with missing sample file"
}

test_new_strategy_invalid_name () {
    printf "data\n" > "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample.txt"
    local rc=0
    bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" --name "Bad Name" --category misc --sample "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample.txt" 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should fail with invalid name"
}

test_new_strategy_creates_files () {
    printf "key1: value1\nkey2: value2\n" > "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample.txt"
    local out
    out=$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" --name test-tool-scaffold --category misc --sample "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample.txt" 2>&1)
    local extract_dir
    extract_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

    # Check strategy file was created
    local strat_file="$extract_dir/strategies/misc/test-tool-scaffold.sh"
    [[ -f "$strat_file" ]]
    assert_exit_zero $? "strategy file should exist"

    # Check sample directory was created
    local sample_dir="$extract_dir/samples/test-tool-scaffold"
    [[ -d "$sample_dir" ]]
    assert_exit_zero $? "sample directory should exist"

    [[ -f "$sample_dir/sample1.txt" ]]
    assert_exit_zero $? "sample file should be copied"

    # Check strategy file has proper headers
    local content
    content=$(cat "$strat_file")
    assert_contains "$content" "## Name: test-tool-scaffold" "should have Name header"
    assert_contains "$content" "## Version: 1.0" "should have Version header"
    assert_contains "$content" "## Priority: 50" "should have Priority header"
    assert_contains "$content" "## Sample:" "should have Sample header"
    assert_contains "$content" "strategy_detect" "should have strategy_detect stub"
    assert_contains "$content" "strategy_extract" "should have strategy_extract stub"
}

test_new_strategy_force_overwrite () {
    printf "data\n" > "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample2.txt"
    # Should fail without --force
    local rc=0
    bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" --name test-tool-scaffold --category misc --sample "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample2.txt" 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    assert_exit_nonzero "$rc" "should fail without --force on existing"

    # Should succeed with --force
    rc=0
    bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" --name test-tool-scaffold --category misc --sample "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample2.txt" --force 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
    assert_exit_zero "$rc" "should succeed with --force"
}

test_new_strategy_custom_priority () {
    printf "data\n" > "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample3.txt"
    bash "$TOOLS_DIR/new_strategy.sh" --name test-tool-scaffold --category misc --sample "$TMPDIR_TEST/sample3.txt" --priority 15 --force 2>/dev/null

}

    assert_not_contains "$output" "John" "names should not include values"

################################################################################
## --sort flag
################################################################################

test_sort_basic () {
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    printf 'Zebra: last\nAlpha: first\nMid: middle\n' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe --sort -r -s colons "$tmpfile")
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
    # Alpha should appear before Mid, Mid before Zebra
    local alpha_pos mid_pos zebra_pos
    alpha_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n 'Alpha' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    mid_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n 'Mid' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    zebra_pos=$(echo "$output" | grep -n 'Zebra' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
    [[ "$alpha_pos" -lt "$mid_pos" && "$mid_pos" -lt "$zebra_pos" ]] || {
        echo "ASSERT FAILED: fields not sorted alphabetically"
        echo "  Alpha at line $alpha_pos, Mid at $mid_pos, Zebra at $zebra_pos"
        return 1
    }
}

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for v3.4 features: YAML/XML formats, auto-tune, interactive
################################################################################

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/helpers.sh"

echo ""
echo "========================================"

################################################################################
## YAML output format
################################################################################

test_yaml_format_basic () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f yaml -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json")
    assert_contains "$output" ": " "YAML output should contain key: value pairs"
    assert_not_contains "$output" "{" "YAML output should not contain JSON braces"
}

test_yaml_special_char_quoting () {
    # Create temp file with colons in values
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    echo 'time: 12:30:00' > "$tmpfile"
    echo 'note: hello' >> "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f yaml -s colons "$tmpfile")
    # The value "12:30:00" contains colons, so it should be quoted
    assert_contains "$output" '"' "YAML should quote values with colons"
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
}

test_yaml_keyword_quoting () {
    # Create temp file where values are YAML keywords
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    echo 'enabled: true' > "$tmpfile"
    echo 'active: false' >> "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f yaml -s colons "$tmpfile")
    # "true" and "false" are YAML keywords and should be quoted
    assert_contains "$output" '"true"' "YAML should quote boolean keywords"
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
}

test_yaml_format_with_field_selection () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f yaml -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 1)
    # Should output exactly one YAML key: value line
    local line_count
    line_count=$(echo "$output" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    assert_eq "1" "$line_count" "field selection should return single line"
    assert_contains "$output" ": " "should be YAML format"
}

################################################################################
## XML output format
################################################################################

test_xml_format_basic () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f xml -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json")
    assert_contains "$output" '<?xml version="1.0"' "should have XML declaration"
    assert_contains "$output" '<fields>' "should have root element"
    assert_contains "$output" '</fields>' "should have closing root element"
    assert_contains "$output" '<field name=' "should have field elements"
}

test_xml_escaping () {
    # Create temp file with values that need XML escaping
    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    echo 'formula: 1<2 & 3>0' > "$tmpfile"
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f xml -s colons "$tmpfile")
    assert_contains "$output" '&lt;' "should escape < in XML"
    assert_contains "$output" '&amp;' "should escape & in XML"
    assert_contains "$output" '&gt;' "should escape > in XML"
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
}

test_xml_format_with_field_selection () {
    local output
    output=$(run_mfe -f xml -s json "$SAMPLES_DIR/json/basic.json" 1)
    assert_contains "$output" '<fields>' "should have root element"
    # Count field elements Aje28094Aj should be exactly 1
    local field_count
    field_count=$(echo "$output" | grep -c '<field name=' || true)
    assert_eq "1" "$field_count" "field selection should return single field"
}

#!/bin/bash
################################################################################
## Tests for strategy validation tooling (--validate-strategy, --validate-all)
################################################################################

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/helpers.sh"

TMPDIR_V="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/validation_$$"
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR_V"

################################################################################
## --validate-strategy tests
################################################################################

test_validate_valid_strategy () {
    # Pick a known good strategy
    local out
    out=$(run_mfe --validate-strategy "$STRATEGIES_DIR/structured/json.sh" 2>&1)
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS: Has ## Name: header" "should pass Name check"
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS: Has ## Description: header" "should pass Description check"
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS: Has strategy_detect function" "should pass detect check"
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS: Has strategy_extract function" "should pass extract check"
}

test_validate_missing_function () {
    # Create a strategy missing strategy_detect
    cat > "$TMPDIR_V/no-detect.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
## Name: no-detect
## Description: Test strategy missing detect
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 50
## Sample: json/basic.json

strategy_extract () {
    echo "field value"
}
EOF
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --validate-strategy "$TMPDIR_V/no-detect.sh" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Missing strategy_detect function" "should fail on missing detect"
    assert_contains "$out" "PASS: Has strategy_extract function" "should pass extract check"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit code"; return 1; }
}

test_validate_missing_headers () {
    # Create a strategy with no metadata headers
    cat > "$TMPDIR_V/bare.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
strategy_detect () { return 0; }
strategy_extract () { echo "field value"; }
EOF
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --validate-strategy "$TMPDIR_V/bare.sh" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Missing ## Name: header" "should fail on missing Name"
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Missing ## Description: header" "should fail on missing Description"
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Missing ## Version: header" "should fail on missing Version"
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Missing ## Priority: header" "should fail on missing Priority"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit code"; return 1; }
}

test_validate_bad_version_format () {
    cat > "$TMPDIR_V/bad-version.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
## Name: bad-version
## Description: Test bad version
## Version: abc
## Priority: 50

strategy_detect () { return 0; }
strategy_extract () { echo "field value"; }
EOF
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --validate-strategy "$TMPDIR_V/bad-version.sh" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Version format should be N.N" "should fail on bad version"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit code"; return 1; }
}

test_validate_name_mismatch () {
    cat > "$TMPDIR_V/actual-name.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
## Name: different-name
## Description: Test name mismatch
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 50

strategy_extract () { echo "field value"; }
EOF
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --validate-strategy "$TMPDIR_V/actual-name.sh" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: Filename 'actual-name' does not match ## Name: 'different-name'" "should fail on name mismatch"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit code"; return 1; }
}

test_validate_file_not_found () {
    local out rc=0
    out=$(run_mfe --validate-strategy "$TMPDIR_V/nonexistent.sh" 2>&1) || rc=$?
    assert_contains "$out" "FAIL: File not found" "should fail on missing file"
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || { echo "expected non-zero exit code"; return 1; }
}
