===FILE-ESC: tests/corpus/run.sh===
===META: mode=755 sha256=363ac3050c7ca7dc3a69924aabf22207b3197dc056f9b2a9273dd1bf271b37ba===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/corpus/run.sh Aje28094Aj batch tidy-coverage harness for common tool outputs.
#
# For every input under inputs/, run the extract engine in --generic mode (only
# the fundamental parsers) and, when needed, full mode (all strategies), melt the
# result to tidy TSV, and report whether each tool's output comes out tidy.
#
# The point of the corpus: prove that a MINIMAL set of generic strategies can
# tidy the common Linux tool outputs, without a bespoke strategy per tool.
# Generic mode = the format-level parsers (strategies/delimited/ + structured/)
# plus declarative hint rows (extract/hints.tsv). Coverage distinguishes:
#   Aje29c85Aj  tidied by a generic parser via auto-detection (no per-tool anything)
#   Aje29c85cab0Aj tidied by a generic parser routed by a hints.tsv data row
#   Aje29c85e1b587Aj tidied only in full mode by a bespoke per-tool strategy script
#
# Modes:
#   run.sh                 report table + summary (development view)
#   run.sh --coverage      markdown coverage table (regenerates COVERAGE.md)
#   run.sh --golden        regression: diff generic tidy output vs expected/<name>.tsv
#   run.sh --update-golden (re)write expected/<name>.tsv from current generic output
#
# Speed: each tool is processed in parallel (job pool sized to the CPU count),
# and each engine invocation uses --emit-meta so the wide output (stdout) and the
# winning-strategy meta (stderr) come from ONE call. Full mode is only run for the
# report/coverage views that need it.
set -u

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
ENGINE="$ROOT/extract/envoy-extract"
IN="$HERE/inputs"
EXP="$HERE/expected"
MANIFEST="$HERE/expected.tsv"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "$ROOT/transform/melt.sh"

mode="${1:-report}"
[[ "$mode" == "--golden" ]] && mode="golden"
[[ "$mode" == "--update-golden" ]] && mode="update"
[[ "$mode" == "--coverage" ]] && mode="coverage"
[[ "$mode" == "update" ]] && mkdir -p "$EXP"

# Full mode is only needed to show the full-mode winner (report) or bespoke
# coverage (coverage). Skip it for golden/update to halve the engine calls.
need_full=0
[[ "$mode" == "report" || "$mode" == "coverage" ]] && need_full=1

JOBS="${GLEAN_CORPUS_JOBS:-$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 4)}"
WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/glean-corpus.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# Melt a wide extract and echo "<cols> <rows>".
_melt_dims () {
    local t; t="$(_core_melt_tidy "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local c r
    c="$(printf '%s\n' "$t" | head -1 | awk -F'\t' '{print NF}')"; [[ -z "$c" ]] && c=0
    r=$(( $(printf '%s\n' "$t" | grep -c .) - 1 )); [[ $r -lt 0 ]] && r=0
    printf '%s %s' "$c" "$r"
}

# Worker: process one input, write a result record + its generic tidy output.
_worker () {
    local f="$1" name; name="$(basename "$f" .txt)"
    local em="$WORK/$name.err"

    # One generic call: wide on stdout, meta on stderr.
    local gwide gstrat gconf
    gwide="$(env -u GIT_DIR bash "$ENGINE" --generic --emit-meta -f tsv --max-strategies 1 "$f" 2>"$em")"
    gstrat="$(awk -F'\t' '/^__EXTRACT_META__/{s=$2;c=$3} END{print s}' "$em")"; [[ -z "$gstrat" ]] && gstrat="(none)"
    gconf="$(awk -F'\t' '/^__EXTRACT_META__/{c=$3} END{print c+0}' "$em")"
    local gtidy; gtidy="$(_core_melt_tidy "$gwide" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    printf '%s\n' "$gtidy" > "$WORK/$name.tidy"
    local gc gr; read -r gc gr <<< "$(_melt_dims "$gwide")"

    # Optional full-mode call.
    local fstrat="(none)" fconf=0 fc=0 fr=0
    if [[ $need_full -eq 1 ]]; then
        local fwide
        fwide="$(env -u GIT_DIR bash "$ENGINE" --emit-meta -f tsv --max-strategies 1 "$f" 2>"$em")"
        fstrat="$(awk -F'\t' '/^__EXTRACT_META__/{s=$2} END{print s}' "$em")"; [[ -z "$fstrat" ]] && fstrat="(none)"
        fconf="$(awk -F'\t' '/^__EXTRACT_META__/{c=$3} END{print c+0}' "$em")"
        read -r fc fr <<< "$(_melt_dims "$fwide")"
    fi

    # Manifest expectation.
    local exp ekind erows emin
    exp="$(awk -F'\t' -v n="$name" '$1==n{print $2"\t"$3"\t"$4; exit}' "$MANIFEST")"
    ekind="$(printf '%s' "$exp" | cut -f1)"; erows="$(printf '%s' "$exp" | cut -f2)"; emin="$(printf '%s' "$exp" | cut -f3)"

    local gtidy_ok=0 ftidy_ok=0 want
    # `text`'s min-col bound was silently ignored (hardcoded >=2 regardless of
    # the manifest's recorded `emin`) -- a garbled parse that happened to clear
    # 2 columns passed even when the manifest asked for many more. Honor emin
    # here too (falling back to the >=2 floor only when the manifest genuinely
    # has no column expectation, i.e. emin=='-' -- free text like ASCII art).
    _ok () { # $1=cols $2=rows
        if [[ "$ekind" == "table" ]]; then [[ "$2" -eq "$erows" && "$1" -ge "$emin" ]]
        elif [[ "$ekind" == "kv" ]]; then [[ "$2" -ge 1 && "$1" -ge "$emin" ]]
        elif [[ "$emin" != "-" ]]; then [[ "$1" -ge "$emin" && "$2" -ge 1 ]]
        else [[ "$1" -ge 2 && "$2" -ge 1 ]]; fi
    }
    case "$ekind" in
        table) want="=${erows}r,>=${emin}c" ;;
        kv)    want=">=1r,>=${emin}c" ;;
        *)     if [[ "$emin" != "-" ]]; then want=">=1r,>=${emin}c"; else want="(unlisted)"; fi ;;
    esac
    _ok "$gc" "$gr" && gtidy_ok=1
    _ok "$fc" "$fr" && ftidy_ok=1

    # Result record (tab-separated).
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$name" "$gstrat" "$gconf" "$gc" "$gr" "$fstrat" "$fconf" "$fc" "$fr" \
        "$gtidy_ok" "$ftidy_ok" > "$WORK/$name.rec"
    printf '%s\n' "$want" >> "$WORK/$name.rec"
}

# --- fan out over inputs with a bounded job pool ---------------------------
for f in "$IN"/*.txt; do
    _worker "$f" &
    while [[ "$(jobs -r | wc -l)" -ge "$JOBS" ]]; do wait -n 2>/dev/null || break; done
done
wait

# --- aggregate + render (deterministic order) ------------------------------
pass=0; fail=0; total=0; relies=0; besp=0; hint=0; skip=0
declare -a FAILED

# Coverage is the queryable record: write it to COVERAGE.md (and still echo to
# the terminal) so the committed file can never silently drift from the live
# result Aje28094Aj `run.sh --coverage` alone regenerates it, no manual redirect needed.
if [[ "$mode" == "coverage" ]]; then exec > >(tee "$HERE/COVERAGE.md"); fi

if [[ "$mode" == "report" ]]; then
    printf '%-16s %-18s %-18s %6s %-6s %s\n' 'TOOL' 'FULL(conf)' 'GENERIC(conf)' 'CxR' 'TIDY' 'NOTE'
    printf '%s\n' "--------------------------------------------------------------------------------"
elif [[ "$mode" == "coverage" ]]; then
    echo "# glean Aje28094Aj common-tool tidy coverage"; echo
    echo "Generated by \`tests/corpus/run.sh --coverage\`. Aje29c85Aj = tidied by a **generic**"
    echo "parser (auto-detected, no per-tool rule); Aje29c85cab0Aj = tidied by a generic parser"
    echo "routed by a **hint row** (one data line in \`extract/hints.tsv\`); Aje29c85e1b587Aj ="
    echo "tidied by a **bespoke** strategy script; Aje28fb3Aj = not yet tidy."; echo
    echo "| Tool | Covered | Parser |"; echo "|---|:---:|---|"
fi

# Map hint tool names -> target strategy (for the Aje29c85cab0Aj tier in coverage mode).
HINTS_TSV="$ROOT/extract/hints.tsv"
_hint_target () { # $1=winner name; echoes target strategy or nothing
    [[ -f "$HINTS_TSV" ]] || return 0
    awk -F'\t' -v n="$1" '$1==n && $1 !~ /^#/ {print $4; exit}' "$HINTS_TSV"
}

for rec in "$WORK"/*.rec; do
    [[ -f "$rec" ]] || continue
    total=$((total + 1))
    IFS=$'\t' read -r name gstrat gconf gc gr fstrat fconf fc fr gtidy_ok ftidy_ok < "$rec"
    want="$(sed -n '2p' "$rec")"
    note=""
    [[ "$fstrat" != "$gstrat" && "$fstrat" != "(none)" ]] && { note="full uses bespoke '$fstrat'"; relies=$((relies + 1)); }

    case "$mode" in
      update)
        if [[ "$gtidy_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then cp "$WORK/$name.tidy" "$EXP/$name.tsv"; echo "golden: $name ($gc col x $gr row)"
        else rm -f "$EXP/$name.tsv"; echo "skip (not tidy yet): $name"; fi ;;
      golden)
        if [[ ! -f "$EXP/$name.tsv" ]]; then skip=$((skip + 1))
        elif diff -q "$WORK/$name.tidy" "$EXP/$name.tsv" >/dev/null 2>&1; then pass=$((pass + 1))
        else echo "FAIL $name Aje28094Aj differs from golden"; fail=$((fail + 1)); FAILED+=("$name"); fi ;;
      report)
        local_mark="FAIL"; if [[ "$gtidy_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then local_mark="tidy"; pass=$((pass + 1)); else fail=$((fail + 1)); FAILED+=("$name"); fi
        [[ -n "$note" ]] && note="want $want | $note" || note="want $want"
        printf '%-16s %-18s %-18s %6s %-6s %s\n' "$name" "$fstrat($fconf)" "$gstrat($gconf)" "${gc}x${gr}" "$local_mark" "$note" ;;
      coverage)
        if [[ "$gtidy_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then
            htarget="$(_hint_target "$gstrat")"
            if [[ -n "$htarget" ]]; then mark="Aje29c85cab0Aj"; parser="$htarget (hint: $gstrat)"; hint=$((hint + 1))
            else mark="Aje29c85Aj"; parser="$gstrat"; pass=$((pass + 1)); fi
        elif [[ "$ftidy_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then mark="Aje29c85e1b587Aj"; parser="$fstrat (bespoke)"; besp=$((besp + 1))
        else mark="Aje28fb3Aj"; parser="Aje28094Aj"; fail=$((fail + 1)); FAILED+=("$name"); fi
        printf '| %s | %s | %s |\n' "$name" "$mark" "$parser" ;;
    esac
done

echo
case "$mode" in
  update)   echo "wrote goldens to expected/ ($total tools processed)" ;;
  golden)   echo "golden regression: $pass passed, $fail failed, $skip not-yet-covered of $total" ;;
  report)   echo "generic-tidy: $pass/$total pass, $fail fail   |   $relies tool(s) currently rely on a bespoke strategy in full mode"
            [[ $fail -gt 0 ]] && echo "not tidy under --generic: ${FAILED[*]}" ;;
  coverage) echo "**Coverage: $((pass + hint + besp)) / $total** Aje28094Aj Aje29c85Aj $pass via a generic parser, Aje29c85cab0Aj $hint via a hint row, Aje29c85e1b587Aj $besp via a bespoke strategy."
            [[ $fail -gt 0 ]] && echo "Aje28fb3Aj not yet tidy: ${FAILED[*]}" ;;
esac
[[ "${fail:-0}" -eq 0 ]]
===END===

===FILE-ESC: tests/corpus/text-inputs/README.md===
===META: mode=644 sha256=de29ba0739a1eeb8c6493dbcd4be008d2dd28da3e1246c356b521e1f4861c2eb===
# text-inputs Aje28094Aj free-form output glean intentionally does NOT parse

These captures are **prose / free text**, not tabular or record-structured data
(version banners, status narratives, config displays that read as sentences).
glean's job is to tidy *structured* command output; forcing a parser onto text
like this only invents fake columns.

They are kept here Aje28094Aj **out of `tests/corpus/inputs/`** Aje28094Aj so the coverage harness
(`run.sh`) and its manifest/goldens never treat them as things-to-tidy. They
carry **no `expected.tsv` row, no golden, and no test**. Move an input here (and
drop its manifest row + `expected/<name>.tsv`) whenever review decides it is
"just text."
===END===

===FILE-ESC: tests/python/test_launcher.py===
===META: mode=644 sha256=3923c12ff61979f58e7633df247f27b706f2ebdf2b99e1d4934208762aa35364===
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Martin Gallagher
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only

"""Unit tests for the glean_data launcher Aje28094Aj run via `python -m pytest`.

Coverage of glean_data is enforced at 100% (branch coverage included) by the
pytest/coverage configuration in pyproject.toml.
"""

import os
import runpy
import shutil
import sys

import pytest

import glean_data


def test_bundle_dir_is_inside_package():
    d = glean_data.bundle_dir()
    assert os.path.isabs(d)
    assert os.path.basename(d) == "_bundle"
    assert os.path.dirname(d) == os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(glean_data.__file__))


def test_glean_script_is_in_bundle_dir():
    s = glean_data.glean_script()
    assert os.path.dirname(s) == glean_data.bundle_dir()
    assert os.path.basename(s) == "glean"


def test_main_execs_bash_with_bundled_script(monkeypatch):
    calls = {}
    monkeypatch.setattr(os.path, "isfile", lambda p: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(shutil, "which", lambda cmd: "/bin/bash")

        os, "execv", lambda path, args: calls.update(path=path, args=args)
    )
    assert glean_data.main(["show", "df"]) is None
    assert calls["path"] == "/bin/bash"
    assert calls["args"] == ["/bin/bash", glean_data.glean_script(), "show", "df"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Phase-1 smoke test: inject Aje28692Aj ls Aje28692Aj show end-to-end in a throwaway workspace.
set -euo pipefail

# Hermetic: test THIS repo's bundled extract/analyze/transform trees, never a
# stale engine a developer happens to have in their global store. glean resolves
# its engine from $GLEAN_HOME first (see _find_engine), so an old ~/.glean/extract
# would otherwise shadow the bundled one and misclassify inputs. Clear every GLEAN_*
# knob the caller's shell may carry, then set only what the test needs.
unset GLEAN_HOME GLEAN_MIN_CONFIDENCE GLEAN_RECONCILE_OVERLAP GLEAN_QUIET GLEAN_MAX_INPUT
# Capture is async BY DEFAULT now; the bulk of these checks assert on the
# synchronous "Aje28692Aj dataset" result, so pin the foreground path for determinism
# (exactly how a script that needs the result inline would invoke glean). The
# dedicated async block below overrides this with GLEAN_ASYNC=1 / --async.
export GLEAN_ASYNC=0

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
GLEAN="$HERE/../glean"
WS="$(mktemp -d)/.glean"
export GLEAN_WORKSPACE="$WS"

pass=0; fail=0
check () { # desc, expected-substring, actual
    # Here-string, not `printf | grep -q`: grep -q exits on the first match and
    # closes the pipe mid-write, which under `set -o pipefail` flakily surfaces
    # as a SIGPIPE ("Broken pipe") and fails the check.
    if grep -qF -- "$2" <<< "$3"; then
        echo "  ok   $1"; pass=$((pass+1))
    else
        echo "  FAIL $1"; echo "       want substring: $2"; echo "       got: $3"; fail=$((fail+1))
    fi
}

free_out="$(printf '              total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available\nMem:           15943        2456        9876         123        3610       13234\nSwap:           2047           0        2047\n' | "$GLEAN" 2>&1)"
check "free injects into 'free'" "dataset 'free'" "$free_out"
check "first free sample gets row index #1" "#1.." "$free_out"

# second same-schema sample should append with fresh global indices (#3..#4)
free_out2="$(printf '              total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available\nMem:           16000        3050        8500         120        4330       12800\nSwap:           2047           0        2047\n' | "$GLEAN" 2>&1)"
check "second free sample gets new global indices (#3..)" "#3.." "$free_out2"

# provenance: row #3 maps back to the 2nd free sample's source

# schema reconciliation: a trimmed same-type capture (>=60% column overlap)
# unions into the base dataset instead of splitting to free.v2
RWS="$(mktemp -d)/.recon"
GLEAN_WORKSPACE="$RWS" "$GLEAN" run printf '              total   used   free   shared   buff/cache   available\nMem:  15943   2456   9876   123   3610   13234\n' >/dev/null 2>&1
GLEAN_WORKSPACE="$RWS" "$GLEAN" run printf '              total   used   free\nMem:  16000   3050   8500\n' >/dev/null 2>&1

#!/bin/bash
## Name: frames
## Description: smoke-test plugin strategy Aje28094Aj '@@frame N status' lines
## Version: 1.0
## Priority: 10
## Sample: samples/frames/basic.txt

strategy_detect () {
    local text="$1"
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=0
    [[ "$text" == "@@frame "* ]] || return 1
    _STRATEGY_CONFIDENCE=95
    return 0
}

strategy_extract () {
    local text="$1" entry=0 line f2 f3 result=""
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        [[ "$line" == "@@frame "* ]] || continue
        entry=$((entry + 1))
        f2="${line#@@frame }"; f3="${f2#* }"; f2="${f2%% *}"
        result+="entry${entry}.frame ${f2}"$'\n'
        result+="entry${entry}.status ${f3}"$'\n'
    done <<< "$text"
    [[ $entry -gt 0 ]] && result+="total_entries ${entry}"$'\n'
    echo "$result"
}
EOS

===META: mode=644 sha256=036f201305adf1c4992253bf2fee7a678a670b5ca15874d1498cc68fa73bc5a3===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# glean/transform/melt.sh Aje28094Aj the extract-output transform (tidy melt + schema-union
# helpers). First-party glean code; edit it here.
#
# Functions: _core_melt_tidy, _core_union_header, _core_align_rows.
# Originally imported from EnvoyCapture/lib/_core.sh
# @ 8639a6ef54fe5867aba8bee81171c5abd344adb3 (2026-07-05); maintained locally since.

# Union of two TSV header lines, by column name: all of $1's columns in order,
# then any of $2's columns not already present. Prints the tab-joined header.
_core_union_header () {
    awk -v old="$1" -v new="$2" 'BEGIN{
        n1=split(old,a,"\t"); n2=split(new,b,"\t"); m=0
        for(i=1;i<=n1;i++) if(!(a[i] in seen)){out[++m]=a[i]; seen[a[i]]=1}
        for(j=1;j<=n2;j++) if(!(b[j] in seen)){out[++m]=b[j]; seen[b[j]]=1}
        s=""; for(k=1;k<=m;k++) s=s (k>1?"\t":"") out[k]; print s
    }'
}

# Re-map data rows (read from stdin, no header) from a source header's column
# order to a target header's, matching by NAME and blanking columns the source
# lacks. Prints the aligned data rows (no header). This keeps a dataset
# rectangular across schema changes Aje28094Aj added, removed, or reordered columns.
_core_align_rows () {
    awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' -v sh="$1" -v th="$2" '
        BEGIN{ ns=split(sh,sc,"\t"); for(i=1;i<=ns;i++) sidx[sc[i]]=i; nt=split(th,tc,"\t") }
        {
            line=""
            for(j=1;j<=nt;j++){ v=(tc[j] in sidx)?$(sidx[tc[j]]):""; line=line (j>1?OFS:"") v }
            print line
        }'
}

# Reshape a wide extract (header + one data row) into tidy long form when its
# columns are a single repeating group named `<prefix><N>.<field>` (e.g.
# entry1.permissions, entry2.permissions, Aje280a6Aj, as emitted by table strategies like
# tar-listing / pipe-table). Emits one row per record with a `capture` group id
# ($2) and an `n` index, the shared fields, and any non-repeating scalar columns
# (repeated per row). Anything that is NOT a single clean repeating table Aje28094Aj
# plain scalars (`a b`), or multiple record prefixes Aje28094Aj is passed through
# unchanged, so this only reshapes table-shaped output.
#
# One exception: a single-column, single-row wide (one key/value observation Aje28094Aj
# the shape of a version banner or one-line status) is emitted in long form
# (`field`/`value` columns), the canonical tidy layout for a lone observation
# of a lone variable. Multi-column snapshots keep their wide layout.
_core_melt_tidy () {
    local tsv="$1" capid="${2:-}"
    printf '%s\n' "$tsv" | awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' -v cap="$capid" '
        { L[NR]=$0 }
        NR==1 { nf=NF; for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) H[i]=$i }
        NR==2 { for(i=1;i<=nf;i++) V[i]=$i }
        END {
          if (NR!=2) { for(r=1;r<=NR;r++) print L[r]; exit }   # only header+1row is meltable
          np=0; nfld=0; nidx=0; nsc=0
          for(i=1;i<=nf;i++){
            h=H[i]; d=index(h,"."); isgroup=0
            if (d>1){
              left=substr(h,1,d-1); field=substr(h,d+1)
              if (match(left,/[0-9]+$/)){
                num=substr(left,RSTART)+0; pref=substr(left,1,RSTART-1)
                if (pref!=""){
                  isgroup=1
                  if(!(pref in seenp)){seenp[pref]=1; np++}
                  key=num SUBSEP field; cell[key]=V[i]
                  if(!(num in seenix)){seenix[num]=1; idxs[++nidx]=num}
                  if(!(field in seenf)){seenf[field]=1; flds[++nfld]=field}
                }
              }
            }
            if(!isgroup) scalidx[++nsc]=i
          }
          if (np!=1 || nfld==0){
            # lone key/value observation -> long form (see header comment)
            if (nf==1 && H[1]!="" && V[1]!=""){ print "field" OFS "value"; print H[1] OFS V[1]; exit }
            print L[1]; print L[2]; exit                          # not a single table
          }
          for(a=1;a<=nidx;a++) for(b=a+1;b<=nidx;b++) if(idxs[b]<idxs[a]){t=idxs[a];idxs[a]=idxs[b];idxs[b]=t}
          hdr=(cap!=""?"capture" OFS:"") "n"
          for(k=1;k<=nfld;k++) hdr=hdr OFS flds[k]
          for(s=1;s<=nsc;s++) hdr=hdr OFS H[scalidx[s]]
          print hdr
          for(a=1;a<=nidx;a++){ ix=idxs[a]; row=(cap!=""?cap OFS:"") ix
            for(k=1;k<=nfld;k++){key=ix SUBSEP flds[k]; row=row OFS ((key in cell)?cell[key]:"")}
            for(s=1;s<=nsc;s++) row=row OFS V[scalidx[s]]
            print row }
        }'
}
===END===
===FILE: transform/tests/test_melt.sh===
===META: mode=644 sha256=33abd4058d3925e1872e7965ec72dc4f2c6444543e8a8a1c2fb38f79dd8ea352===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Unit test for the imported transform module (glean/transform/melt.sh):
# _core_melt_tidy, _core_union_header, _core_align_rows. Mirrors the tidy-melt
# assertions from EnvoyCapture tests/test_run.sh, exercised directly on the
# functions rather than through the capture pipeline.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "$HERE/../melt.sh"

pass=0; fail=0
# Use a here-string, not `printf | grep -q`: grep -q exits on the first match and
# closes the pipe while printf is still writing, which under `set -o pipefail`
# surfaces as a SIGPIPE ("write error: Broken pipe") and flakily fails the check.
check () { if grep -qF -- "$2" <<< "$3"; then echo "  ok   $1"; pass=$((pass+1))
           else echo "  FAIL $1"; echo "       want: $2"; echo "       got: $3"; fail=$((fail+1)); fi; }
refute () { if grep -qF -- "$2" <<< "$3"; then echo "  FAIL $1 (unexpected: $2)"; fail=$((fail+1))
            else echo "  ok   $1"; pass=$((pass+1)); fi; }

# 1. A repeating entry<N>.<field> table melts to one row per record.
wide="$(printf 'entry1.name\tentry1.used\tentry2.name\tentry2.used\ttotal_entries\nMem\t10\tSwap\t20\t2\n')"
melted="$(_core_melt_tidy "$wide")"
check  "melt: header carries the n index"        $'n\tname\tused' "$melted"
check  "melt: one row per record (Mem)"          "1"$'\t'"Mem"  "$melted"
check  "melt: one row per record (Swap)"         "2"$'\t'"Swap" "$melted"
check  "melt: scalar column repeated per row"    "total_entries" "$melted"
refute "melt: no wide entry1.* remains"          "entry1"      "$melted"

# 2. Non-table scalar output passes through unchanged (opt-out).
scalar="$(printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n')"
check  "melt: plain scalar passes through"       "1"$'\t'"2"   "$(_core_melt_tidy "$scalar")"

# 2b. A lone key/value observation goes to long form (field/value).
lone="$(_core_melt_tidy "$(printf 'distrobox\n1.7.2.1\n')")"
check  "melt: lone pair gets field/value header" $'field\tvalue' "$lone"
check  "melt: lone pair kept as one long row"    "distrobox"$'\t'"1.7.2.1" "$lone"

# 3. Header union + row alignment (the schema-reconcile helpers).
uni="$(_core_union_header $'#\tname\tused\tfree' $'#\tname\tused')"
check  "union: keeps all old columns"            $'#\tname\tused\tfree' "$uni"
aligned="$(printf '2\tSwap\t5\n' | _core_align_rows $'#\tname\tused' "$uni")"
check  "align: blank-fills a missing column"     "2"$'\t'"Swap"$'\t'"5"$'\t' "$aligned"

echo "melt: $pass passed, $fail failed"
[[ $fail -eq 0 ]]
===END===
